nodes.description: A group G has unique products if for any two non-empty finite subsets A, B ⊆ G, there is an element g ∈ A B that can be written uniquely as a product of an element of A and an element of B. We call the formalization this property UniqueProds. Since the condition requires no property of the group operation, we define it for a Type simply satisfying Mul. We also introduce the analogous "additive" companion, UniqueSums, and link the two so that to_additive converts UniqueProds into UniqueSums.

Given functors F₁₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₁₂, G : C₁₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄, F : C₁ ⥤ C₂₃ ⥤ C₄, G₂₃ : C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₂₃ equipped with an isomorphism associator : bifunctorComp₁₂ F₁₂ G ≅ bifunctorComp₂₃ F G₂₃ (which informally means that we have natural isomorphisms G(F₁₂(X₁, X₂), X₃) ≅ F(X₁, G₂₃(X₂, X₃))), we define an isomorphism mapBifunctorAssociator from mapBifunctor (mapBifunctor K₁ K₂ F₁₂ c₁₂) K₃ G c₄ to...

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.BifunctorFlip
nodes.descriptionTitle: Action of the flip of a bifunctor on homological complexes
nodes.description: Given K₁ : HomologicalComplex C₁ c₁, K₂ : HomologicalComplex C₂ c₂, a bifunctor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ D, and a complex shape c with [TotalComplexShape c₁ c₂ c] and [TotalComplexShape c₂ c₁ c], we define an isomorphism mapBifunctor K₂ K₁ F.flip c ≅ mapBifunctor K₁ K₂ F c under the additional assumption [TotalComplexShapeSymmetry c₁ c₂ c].

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.BifunctorHomotopy

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.BifunctorShift
nodes.descriptionTitle: Behavior of the action of a bifunctor on cochain complexes with respect to shifts
nodes.description: In this file, given cochain complexes K₁ : CochainComplex C₁ ℤ, K₂ : CochainComplex C₂ ℤ and a functor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ D, we define an isomorphism of cochain complexes in D: mapBifunctor (K₁⟦x⟧) K₂ F ≅ (mapBifunctor K₁ K₂ F)⟦x⟧ for x : ℤ. mapBifunctor K₁ (K₂⟦y⟧) F ≅ (mapBifunctor K₁ K₂ F)⟦y⟧ for y : ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ComplexShape
nodes.description: We define a structure ComplexShape ι for describing the shapes of homological complexes indexed by a type ι. This is intended to capture chain complexes and cochain complexes, indexed by either ℕ or ℤ, as well as more exotic examples.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Signs in constructions on homological complexes

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ConcreteCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homology of complexes in concrete categories
nodes.description: The homology of short complexes in concrete categories was studied in Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ConcreteCategory.lean. In this file, we introduce specific definitions and lemmas for the homology of homological complexes in concrete categories. In particular, we give a computation of the connecting homomorphism of the homology sequence in terms of (co)cycles.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derived category of an abelian category
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the derived category DerivedCategory C of an abelian category C. It is equipped with a triangulated structure.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: An exact functor induces a functor on derived categories
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ is an exact functor between abelian categories, then there is an induced triangulated functor F.mapDerivedCategory : DerivedCategory C₁ ⥤ DerivedCategory C₂.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category (with C : Type u and Category.{v} C). In this file, we introduce the assumption HasExt.{w} C which asserts that morphisms between single complexes in arbitrary degrees in the derived category of C are w-small. Under this assumption, we define Ext.{w} X Y n : Type w as shrunk versions of suitable types of morphisms in the derived category. In particular, when C has enough projectives or enough injectives, the property HasExt.{v} C shall hold.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.EnoughInjectives
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smallness of Ext-groups from the existence of enough injectives
nodes.description: Let C : Type u be an abelian category (Category.{v} C) that has enough injectives. If C is locally w-small, i.e. the type of morphisms in C are Small.{w}, then we show that the condition HasExt.{w} holds, which means that for X and Y in C, and n : ℕ, we may define Ext X Y n : Type w. In particular, this holds for w = v.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.EnoughProjectives
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smallness of Ext-groups from the existence of enough projectives
nodes.description: Let C : Type u be an abelian category (Category.{v} C) that has enough projectives. If C is locally w-small, i.e. the type of morphisms in C are Small.{w}, then we show that the condition HasExt.{w} holds, which means that for X and Y in C, and n : ℕ, we may define Ext X Y n : Type w. In particular, this holds for w = v.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.ExactSequences
nodes.description: In this file, we obtain the covariant long exact sequence of Ext when n₀ + 1 = n₁: Ext X S.X₁ n₀ → Ext X S.X₂ n₀ → Ext X S.X₃ n₀ → Ext X S.X₁ n₁ → Ext X S.X₂ n₁ → Ext X S.X₃ n₁ when S is a short exact short complex in an abelian category C, n₀ + 1 = n₁ and X : C. Similarly, if Y : C, there is a contravariant long exact sequence : Ext S.X₃ Y n₀ → Ext S.X₂ Y n₀ → Ext S.X₁ Y n₀ → Ext S.X₃ Y n₁ → Ext S.X₂ Y n₁ → Ext S.X₁ Y n₁.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.ExtClass
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Ext class of a short exact sequence
nodes.description: In this file, given a short exact short complex S : ShortComplex C in an abelian category, we construct the associated class in Ext S.X₃ S.X₁ 1.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.Linear
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if C is an R-linear abelian category, then there is an R-module structure on the groups Ext X Y n for X and Y in C and n : ℕ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.Map
nodes.descriptionTitle: Map between Ext groups induced by an exact functor
nodes.description: In this file, we define the map Ext^k (M, N) → Ext^k (F(M), F(N)), where F is an exact functor between abelian categories.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.MapBijective
nodes.description: In this file, we show that the maps between Ext induced by a fully faithful exact functor F : C ⥤ D are bijective when either 1. F preserves projective objects and C has enough projectives, or 2. F preserves injective objects and C has enough injectives.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Ext.TStructure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphisms between bounded complexes are small
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category. Assuming HasExt.{w} C, we show that if two cochain complexes K and L are cohomologically in a single degree, then the type of morphisms from K to L⟦n⟧ in the derived category is w-small for any n : ℤ, which we phrase here by saying that HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w} (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ _) ℤ K L hold.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Fractions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Calculus of fractions in the derived category
nodes.description: We obtain various consequences of the calculus of left and right fractions for HomotopyCategory.quasiIso C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) as lemmas about factorizations of morphisms f : Q.obj X ⟶ Q.obj Y (where X and Y are cochain complexes). These f can be factored as a right fraction inv (Q.map s) ≫ Q.map g or as a left fraction Q.map g ≫ inv (Q.map s), with s a quasi-isomorphism (to X or from Y). When strict bounds are known on X or Y, certain bounds may also be ensured on the auxiliary object appearing in the fraction.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.FullyFaithful
nodes.descriptionTitle: The fully faithful embedding of the abelian category in its derived category
nodes.description: In this file, we show that for any n : ℤ, the functor singleFunctor C n : C ⥤ DerivedCategory C is fully faithful.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.HomologySequence
nodes.description: In this file, we construct homologyFunctor C n : DerivedCategory C ⥤ C for all n : ℤ, show that they are homological functors which form a shift sequence, and construct the long exact homology sequences associated to distinguished triangles in the derived category.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.KInjective
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphisms to K-injective complexes in the derived category
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if L : CochainComplex C ℤ is K-injective, then for any K : HomotopyCategory C (.up ℤ), the functor DerivedCategory.Qh induces a bijection from the type of morphisms K ⟶ (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj L) (i.e. homotopy classes of morphisms of cochain complexes) to the type of morphisms in the derived category. We obtain that a morphism between K-injective cochain complexes is a quasi-isomorphism iff it is a homotopy equivalence.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.KProjective
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphisms from K-projective complexes in the derived category
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if K : CochainComplex C ℤ is K-projective, then for any L : HomotopyCategory C (.up ℤ), the functor DerivedCategory.Qh induces a bijection from the type of morphisms (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj K) ⟶ L (i.e. homotopy classes of morphisms of cochain complexes) to the type of morphisms in the derived category. We obtain that a morphism between K-projective cochain complexes is a quasi-isomorphism iff it is a homotopy equivalence.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.SmallShiftedHom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cohomology of HomComplex and morphisms in the derived category
nodes.description: Let K and L be two cochain complexes in an abelian category C. Given a class x : HomComplex.CohomologyClass K L n, we construct an element in the type SmallShiftedHom (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso C (.up ℤ)) K L n, and compute its image as a morphism Q.obj K ⟶ (Q.obj L)⟦n⟧ in the derived category when x is given as the class of a cocycle.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.DifferentialObject

nodes.description: We verify that a HomologicalComplex indexed by an AddCommGroup is essentially the same thing as a differential graded object.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Double
nodes.descriptionTitle: A homological complex lying in two degrees
nodes.description: Given c : ComplexShape ι, distinct indices i₀ and i₁ such that hi₀₁ : c.Rel i₀ i₁, we construct a homological complex double f hi₀₁ for any morphism f : X₀ ⟶ X₁. It consists of the objects X₀ and X₁ in degrees i₀ and i₁, respectively, with the differential X₀ ⟶ X₁ given by f, and zero everywhere else.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.AreComplementary
nodes.description: Given two embeddings e₁ : c₁.Embedding c and e₂ : c₂.Embedding c of complex shapes, we introduce a property e₁.AreComplementary e₂ saying that the image subsets of the indices of c₁ and c₂ form a partition of the indices of c.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.Basic
nodes.description: Given two complex shapes c : ComplexShape ι and c' : ComplexShape ι', an embedding from c to c' (e : c.Embedding c') consists of the data of an injective map f : ι → ι' such that for all i₁ i₂ : ι, c.Rel i₁ i₂ implies c'.Rel (e.f i₁) (e.f i₂). We define a type class e.IsRelIff to express that this implication is an equivalence. Other type classes e.IsTruncLE and e.IsTruncGE are introduced in order to formalize truncation functors.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.Boundary
nodes.descriptionTitle: Boundary of an embedding of complex shapes
nodes.description: In the file Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/Embedding/Basic.lean, given p : ℤ, we have defined an embedding embeddingUpIntGE p of ComplexShape.up ℕ in ComplexShape.up ℤ which sends n : ℕ to p + n. The (canonical) truncation (≥ p) of K : CochainComplex C ℤ shall be defined as the extension to ℤ (see Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/Embedding/Extend.lean) of a certain cochain complex indexed by ℕ:

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.CochainComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Truncations on cochain complexes indexed by the integers.
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce abbreviations for the canonical truncations CochainComplex.truncLE, CochainComplex.truncGE of cochain complexes indexed by ℤ, as well as the conditions CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE, CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE, CochainComplex.IsLE, and CochainComplex.IsGE.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.Connect
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connecting a chain complex and a cochain complex
nodes.description: Given a chain complex K: ... ⟶ K.X 2 ⟶ K.X 1 ⟶ K.X 0, a cochain complex L: L.X 0 ⟶ L.X 1 ⟶ L.X 2 ⟶ ..., a morphism d₀ : K.X 0 ⟶ L.X 0 satisfying the identifies K.d 1 0 ≫ d₀ = 0 and d₀ ≫ L.d 0 1 = 0, we construct a cochain complex indexed by ℤ of the form ... ⟶ K.X 2 ⟶ K.X 1 ⟶ K.X 0 ⟶ L.X 0 ⟶ L.X 1 ⟶ L.X 2 ⟶ ..., where K.X 0 lies in degree -1 and L.X 0 in degree 0.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.Extend
nodes.descriptionTitle: The extension of a homological complex by an embedding of complex shapes
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : Embedding c c' of complex shapes, and K : HomologicalComplex C c, we define K.extend e : HomologicalComplex C c', and this leads to a functor e.extendFunctor C : HomologicalComplex C c ⥤ HomologicalComplex C c'.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.ExtendHomology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homology of the extension of a homological complex
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : c.Embedding c' and K : HomologicalComplex C c, we shall compute the homology of K.extend e. In degrees that are not in the image of e.f, the homology is obviously zero. When e.f j = j, we construct an isomorphism (K.extend e).homology j' ≅ K.homology j.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.ExtendHomotopy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The extension functor on the homotopy categories
nodes.description: Given an embedding of complex shapes e : c.Embedding c' and a preadditive category C, we define a fully faithful functor e.extendHomotopyFunctor C : HomotopyCategory C c ⥤ HomotopyCategory C c'.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.HomEquiv
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : Embedding c c' of complex shapes satisfying e.IsRelIff, we obtain a bijection e.homEquiv between the type of morphisms K ⟶ L.extend e (with K : HomologicalComplex C c' and L : HomologicalComplex C c) and the subtype of morphisms φ : K.restriction e ⟶ L which satisfy a certain condition e.HasLift φ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.IsSupported
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : c.Embedding c' of complex shapes, we say that K : HomologicalComplex C c' is supported (resp. strictly supported) on e if K is exact in degree i' (resp. K.X i' is zero) whenever i' is not of the form e.f i. This defines two typeclasses K.IsSupported e and K.IsStrictlySupported e.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.Restriction
nodes.descriptionTitle: The restriction functor of an embedding of complex shapes
nodes.description: Given c and c' complex shapes on two types, and e : c.Embedding c' (satisfying [e.IsRelIff]), we define the restriction functor e.restrictionFunctor C : HomologicalComplex C c' ⥤ HomologicalComplex C c.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.RestrictionHomology
nodes.description: Under favourable circumstances, we may relate the homology of K : HomologicalComplex C c' in degree j' and that of K.restriction e in degree j when e : Embedding c c' is an embedding of complex shapes. See restriction.sc'Iso and restriction.hasHomology.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.StupidTrunc
nodes.descriptionTitle: The stupid truncation of homological complexes
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : c.Embedding c' of complex shapes, we define a functor stupidTruncFunctor : HomologicalComplex C c' ⥤ HomologicalComplex C c' which sends K to K.stupidTrunc e which is defined as (K.restriction e).extend e.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.TruncGE
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : Embedding c c' of complex shapes which satisfies e.IsTruncGE and K : HomologicalComplex C c', we define K.truncGE' e : HomologicalComplex C c and K.truncGE e : HomologicalComplex C c' which are the canonical truncations of K relative to e.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.TruncGEHomology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homology of a canonical truncation
nodes.description: Given an embedding of complex shapes e : Embedding c c', we relate the homology of K : HomologicalComplex C c' and of K.truncGE e : HomologicalComplex C c'.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.TruncLE
nodes.description: Given an embedding e : Embedding c c' of complex shapes which satisfies e.IsTruncLE and K : HomologicalComplex C c', we define K.truncGE' e : HomologicalComplex C c and K.truncLE e : HomologicalComplex C c' which are the canonical truncations of K relative to e.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Embedding.TruncLEHomology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homology of a canonical truncation
nodes.description: Given an embedding of complex shapes e : Embedding c c', we relate the homology of K : HomologicalComplex C c' and of K.truncLE e : HomologicalComplex C c'.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.EulerCharacteristic
nodes.description: The Euler characteristic is defined using the ComplexShape.EulerCharSigns typeclass, which provides the alternating signs for each index. This allows the definition to work uniformly for chain complexes, cochain complexes, and complexes with other index types.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ExactSequence
nodes.description: A sequence of n composable arrows S : ComposableArrows C (i.e. a functor S : Fin (n + 1) ⥤ C) is said to be exact (S.Exact) if the composition of two consecutive arrows are zero (S.IsComplex) and the diagram is exact at each i for 1 ≤ i < n.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ExactSequenceFour
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is ComposableArrows.Exact.cokerIsoKer: given an exact sequence S (involving at least four objects), this is the isomorphism from the cokernel of S.map' k (k + 1) to the kernel of S.map' (k + 2) (k + 3). This is intended to be used for exact sequences in abelian categories, but the construction works for preadditive balanced categories.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Factorizations.Basic
nodes.description: We define the class of morphisms degreewiseEpiWithInjectiveKernel : MorphismProperty (CochainComplex C ℤ) in the category of cochain complexes in an abelian category C.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Factorizations.CM5a
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if f : K ⟶ L is a morphism between bounded below cochain complexes in an abelian category with enough injectives, there exists a factorization ι ≫ π = f with ι : K ⟶ K' a monomorphism that is also a quasimorphism and π : K' ⟶ L a morphism which degreewise is an epimorphism with an injective kernel, while K' is also bounded below (with precise bounds depending on the available bounds for K and L): this is CochainComplex.Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.cm5a.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Factorizations.CM5b
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category with enough injectives. We show that any morphism f : K ⟶ L between bounded below cochain complexes in C can be factored as i ≫ p where i : K ⟶ L' is a monomorphism (with L' bounded below) and p : L' ⟶ L a quasi-isomorphism that is an epimorphism with a degreewise injective kernel. (This is part of the factorization axiom CM5 for a model category structure on bounded below cochain complexes (TODO @joelriou).)

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Functor
nodes.description: We can view a complex valued in a functor category T ⥤ V as a functor from T to complexes valued in V.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.GrothendieckAbelian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homological complexes in a Grothendieck abelian category
nodes.description: Let c : ComplexShape ι be a complex shape with no loop, and such that Small.{w} ι. Then, if C is a Grothendieck abelian category (with IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C), the category HomologicalComplex C c is Grothendieck abelian.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HasNoLoop
nodes.description: Let c : ComplexShape ι. We define a type class c.HasNoLoop which expresses that ¬ c.Rel i i for all i : ι.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalBicomplex
nodes.description: Given a category C with zero morphisms and two complex shapes c₁ : ComplexShape I₁ and c₂ : ComplexShape I₂, we define the type of bicomplexes HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂ as an abbreviation for HomologicalComplex (HomologicalComplex C c₂) c₁. In particular, if K : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂, then for each i₁ : I₁, K.X i₁ is a column of K.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalComplex
nodes.description: A HomologicalComplex V c with a "shape" controlled by c : ComplexShape ι has chain groups X i (objects in V) indexed by i : ι, and a differential d i j whenever c.Rel i j.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalComplexAbelian
nodes.descriptionTitle: THe category of homological complexes is abelian
nodes.description: If C is an abelian category, then HomologicalComplex C c is an abelian category for any complex shape c : ComplexShape ι.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalComplexBiprod
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if two homological complex K and L in a preadditive category are such that for all i : ι, the binary biproduct K.X i ⊞ L.X i exists, then K ⊞ L exists, and there is an isomorphism biprodXIso K L i : (K ⊞ L).X i ≅ (K.X i) ⊞ (L.X i).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalComplexLimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits in the category of homological complexes
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if a category C has (co)limits of shape J, then it is also the case of the categories HomologicalComplex C c, and the evaluation functors eval C c i : HomologicalComplex C c ⥤ C commute to these.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologicalComplexLimitsEventuallyConstant
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits of degreewise eventually constant systems
nodes.description: Let F : J ⥤ HomologicalComplex C c be a functor from a cofiltered category such that for any degree q, the functor F ⋙ eval C c q : J ⥤ C is eventually constant. Let cF be a limit cone for F. For a given degree q, we show that for suitable j : J, the map (cF.π.app j).f q is an isomorphism, and that cf.π.app j is a quasi-isomorphism in degree q.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologySequence
nodes.description: If 0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0 is a short exact sequence in a category of complexes HomologicalComplex C c in an abelian category (i.e. S is a short complex in that category and satisfies hS : S.ShortExact), then whenever i and j are degrees such that hij : c.Rel i j, then there is a long exact sequence : ... ⟶ S.X₁.homology i ⟶ S.X₂.homology i ⟶ S.X₃.homology i ⟶ S.X₁.homology j ⟶ ....

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomologySequenceLemmas
nodes.description: Given a morphism φ : S₁ ⟶ S₂ between two short exact sequences of homological complexes in an abelian category, we show the naturality of the homology sequence of S₁ and S₂ with respect to φ (see HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.δ_naturality).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Homotopy
nodes.description: We define chain homotopies, and prove that homotopic chain maps induce the same map on homology.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory
nodes.description: HomotopyCategory V c gives the category of chain complexes of shape c in V, with chain maps identified when they are homotopic.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.Acyclic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The triangulated subcategory of acyclic complex in the homotopy category
nodes.description: In this file, we define the triangulated subcategory HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic C of the homotopy category of cochain complexes in an abelian category C. In the lemma HomotopyCategory.quasiIso_eq_subcategoryAcyclic_W we obtain that the class of quasiisomorphisms HomotopyCategory.quasiIso C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) consists of morphisms whose cone belongs to the triangulated subcategory HomotopyCategory.subcategoryAcyclic C of acyclic complexes.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.DegreewiseSplit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Degreewise split exact sequences of cochain complexes
nodes.description: The main result of this file is the lemma HomotopyCategory.distinguished_iff_iso_trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit which asserts that a triangle in HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) is distinguished iff it is isomorphic to the triangle attached to a degreewise split short exact sequence of cochain complexes.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The cochain complex of homomorphisms between cochain complexes
nodes.description: If F and G are cochain complexes (indexed by ℤ) in a preadditive category, there is a cochain complex of abelian groups whose 0-cocycles identify to morphisms F ⟶ G. Informally, in degree n, this complex shall consist of cochains of degree n from F to G, i.e. arbitrary families for morphisms F.X p ⟶ G.X (p + n). This complex shall be denoted HomComplex F G.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomComplexCohomology
nodes.description: Given ℤ-indexed cochain complexes K and L, and n : ℤ, we introduce a type HomComplex.CohomologyClass K L n which is the quotient of HomComplex.Cocycle K L n which identifies cohomologous cocycles. We construct this type of cohomology classes instead of using the homology API because Cochain K L can be considered both as a complex of abelian groups or as a complex of R-modules when the category is R-linear.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomComplexInduction
nodes.description: Let K and L be cochain complexes in a preadditive category C. We provide an API to construct a cochain in Cochain K L d in the following situation. Assume that X n : Set (Cochain K L d) is a sequence of subsets of Cochain K L d, and φ n : X n → X (n + 1) is a sequence of maps such that for a certain p₀ : ℕ and any x : X n, φ n x and x coincide up to the degree p₀ + n, then we construct a cochain InductionUp.limitSequence in Cochain K L d which coincides with the nth-iteration of φ evaluated on x₀ up to the degre...

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomComplexShift
nodes.description: Let C be a preadditive category. Given two cochain complexes (indexed by ℤ), the type of cochains HomComplex.Cochain K L n of degree n was introduced in Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/HomComplex.lean. In this file, we study how these cochains behave with respect to the shift on the complexes K and L.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomComplexSingle
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cochains from or to single complexes
nodes.description: We introduce constructors Cochain.fromSingleMk and Cocycle.fromSingleMk for cochains and cocycles from a single complex. We also introduce similar definitions for cochains and cocycles to a single complex.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.HomologicalFunctor
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if C is an abelian category, then homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n is a homological functor HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ C. As distinguished triangles in the homotopy category can be characterized in terms of degreewise split short exact sequences of cochain complexes, this follows from the homology sequence associated to a short exact sequence of homological complexes.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.KInjective
nodes.description: We define the notion of K-injective cochain complex in an abelian category, and show that bounded below complexes of injective objects are K-injective.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.KProjective
nodes.description: We define the notion of K-projective cochain complex in an abelian category, and show that bounded above complexes of projective objects are K-projective.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.MappingCocone
nodes.description: Given a morphism φ : K ⟶ L of cochain complexes, the mapping cone allows to obtain a triangle K ⟶ L ⟶ mappingCone φ ⟶ .... In this file, we define the mapping cocone, which fits in a rotated triangle: mappingCocone φ ⟶ K ⟶ L ⟶ ....

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.MappingCone
nodes.descriptionTitle: The mapping cone of a morphism of cochain complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we study the homotopy cofiber HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber of a morphism φ : F ⟶ G of cochain complexes indexed by ℤ. In this case, we redefine it as CochainComplex.mappingCone φ. The API involves definitions

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.Plus
nodes.descriptionTitle: The triangulated subcategory of bounded below cochain complexes up to homotopy
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the triangulated full subcategory HomotopyCategory.Plus C of HomotopyCategory C (.up ℤ) consisting of bounded below cochain complexes.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.Pretriangulated
nodes.descriptionTitle: The pretriangulated structure on the homotopy category of complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we define the pretriangulated structure on the homotopy category HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) of an additive category C. The distinguished triangles are the triangles that are isomorphic to the image in the homotopy category of the standard triangle K ⟶ L ⟶ mappingCone φ ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ for some morphism of cochain complexes φ : K ⟶ L.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.Shift
nodes.descriptionTitle: The shift on cochain complexes and on the homotopy category
nodes.description: In this file, we show that for any preadditive category C, the categories CochainComplex C ℤ and HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) are equipped with a shift by ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.ShiftSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compatibilities of the homology functor with the shift
nodes.description: This file studies how homology of cochain complexes behaves with respect to the shift: there is a natural isomorphism (K⟦n⟧).homology a ≅ K.homology a when n + a = a'. This is summarized by instances (homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).ShiftSequence ℤ in the CochainComplex and HomotopyCategory namespaces.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.ShortExact
nodes.descriptionTitle: The mapping cone of a monomorphism, up to a quasi-isomorphism
nodes.description: If S is a short exact short complex of cochain complexes in an abelian category, we construct a quasi-isomorphism descShortComplex S : mappingCone S.f ⟶ S.X₃.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.SingleFunctors
nodes.descriptionTitle: Single functors from the homotopy category
nodes.description: Let C be a preadditive category with a zero object. In this file, we put together all the single functors C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℤ along with their compatibilities with shifts into the definition CochainComplex.singleFunctors C : SingleFunctors C (CochainComplex C ℤ) ℤ. Similarly, we define HomotopyCategory.singleFunctors C : SingleFunctors C (HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.SpectralObject
nodes.descriptionTitle: The spectral object with values in the homotopy category
nodes.description: Let C be an additive category. In this file, we show that the mapping cone defines a spectral object with values in the homotopy category of ℤ-indexed cochain complexes C that is indexed by the category CochainComplex C ℤ. (It follows that to any functor ι ⥤ CochainComplex C ℤ (e.g. a filtered complex), there is an associated spectral object indexed by ι.)

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.Triangulated
nodes.descriptionTitle: The triangulated structure on the homotopy category of complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we show that for any additive category C, the pretriangulated category HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) is triangulated.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCofiber
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy cofiber of a morphism of homological complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the homotopy cofiber of a morphism φ : F ⟶ G between homological complexes in HomologicalComplex C c. In degree i, it is isomorphic to (F.X j) ⊞ (G.X i) if there is a j such that c.Rel i j, and G.X i otherwise. (This is also known as the mapping cone of φ. Under the name CochainComplex.mappingCone, a specific API shall be developed for the case of cochain complexes indexed by ℤ.)

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.HomotopyFiber
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy fiber of a morphism of homological complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the homotopy fiber of a morphism φ : F ⟶ G between homological complexes. Moreover, we dualise the definition of the cylinder (which is a particular case of a homotopy cofiber) in order to define the path object of a homological complex.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ImageToKernel
nodes.description: Whenever f : A ⟶ B and g : B ⟶ C satisfy w : f ≫ g = 0, we have image_le_kernel f g w : imageSubobject f ≤ kernelSubobject g (assuming the appropriate images and kernels exist).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.LeftResolution.Basic
nodes.description: Given a fully faithful functor ι : C ⥤ A to an abelian category, we introduce a structure Abelian.LeftResolution ι which gives a functor F : A ⥤ C and a natural epimorphism π.app X : ι.obj (F.obj X) ⟶ X for all X : A. This is used in order to construct a resolution functor LeftResolution.chainComplexFunctor : A ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.LeftResolution.Reduced
nodes.descriptionTitle: Left resolutions which preserve the zero object
nodes.description: The structure LeftResolution allows to define a functorial resolution of an object (see LeftResolution.chainComplexFunctor in the file Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/LeftResolution/Basic.lean). In order to extend this resolution to complexes, we not only need the functoriality but also that zero morphisms are sent to zero.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.LeftResolution.Transport
nodes.description: If ι : C ⥤ A is equipped with Λ : LeftResolution ι and ι' : C' ⥤ A' is a functor which corresponds to ι via equivalences of categories A' ≌ A and C' ≌ C, we define Λ.transport .. : LeftResolution ι'.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Linear
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of homological complexes is linear
nodes.description: In this file, we define the instance Linear R (HomologicalComplex C c) when the category C is R-linear.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.LocalCohomology
nodes.description: This file defines the i-th local cohomology module of an R-module M with support in an ideal I of R, where R is a commutative ring, as the direct limit of Ext modules:

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Localization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of homological complexes up to quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.description: Given a category C with homology and any complex shape c, we define the category HomologicalComplexUpToQuasiIso C c which is the localized category of HomologicalComplex C c with respect to quasi-isomorphisms. When C is abelian, this will be the derived category of C in the particular case of the complex shape ComplexShape.up ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ModelCategory.Injective
nodes.descriptionTitle: The model category structure on bounded below complexes
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category with enough injectives. In this file, we define a model category structure on the category CochainComplex.Plus C of bounded below cochain complexes in C. The cofibrations are monomorphisms, the weak equivalences are quasi-isomorphisms and the fibrations are those morphisms that are degreewise epimorphisms with an injective kernel. The ModelCategory instance is scoped in the namespace CochainComplex.Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ModelCategory.Lifting
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category. Consider a commutative diagram in the category CochainComplex C ℤ. Assume that there exists a degreewise lifting B.X n ⟶ X.X n for any n : ℤ, that Q is a cokernel of i, and K is a kernel of p. In this situation, we construct a cocycle in Cocycle Q K 1 and show that there exists a lifting B ⟶ X if this cocycle is a coboundary.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The monoidal category structure on homological complexes
nodes.description: Let c : ComplexShape I with I an additive monoid. If c is equipped with the data and axioms c.TensorSigns, then the category HomologicalComplex C c can be equipped with a monoidal category structure if C is a monoidal category such that C has certain coproducts and both left/right tensoring commute with these.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Opposite
nodes.description: Given a preadditive category V, the opposite of its category of chain complexes is equivalent to the category of cochain complexes of objects in Vᵒᵖ. We define this equivalence, and another analogous equivalence (for a general category of homological complexes with a general complex shape).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Precylinder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Precylinder and pre-path objects in the category of homological complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we upgrade the definitions HomologicalComplex.cylinder and HomologicalComplex.pathObject to pre-cylinder objects and pre-path objects in the sense of homotopical algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.QuasiIso
nodes.description: A chain map is a quasi-isomorphism if it induces isomorphisms on homology.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Refinements
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about "refinements" that are specific to the study of the homology of HomologicalComplex. General lemmas about refinements and the case of ShortComplex appear in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Refinements.lean.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Ab
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homology and exactness of short complexes of abelian groups
nodes.description: In this file, the homology of a short complex S of abelian groups is identified with the quotient of AddMonoidHom.ker S.g by the image of the morphism S.abToCycles : S.X₁ →+ AddMonoidHom.ker S.g induced by S.f.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Abelian
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that all short complexes S in abelian categories have terms of type S.HomologyData.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the category ShortComplex C of diagrams X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ such that the composition is zero.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ConcreteCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Exactness of short complexes in concrete abelian categories
nodes.description: If an additive concrete category C has an additive forgetful functor to Ab which preserves homology, then a short complex S in C is exact if and only if it is so after applying the functor forget₂ C Ab.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Exact
nodes.description: When S : ShortComplex C, this file defines a structure S.Exact which expresses the exactness of S, i.e. there exists a homology data h : S.HomologyData such that h.left.H is zero. When [S.HasHomology], it is equivalent to the assertion IsZero S.homology.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ExactFunctor
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that additive functors which preserves homology also preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.FunctorEquivalence
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if J and C are two categories (such that C has zero morphisms), then there is an equivalence of categories ShortComplex.functorEquivalence J C : ShortComplex (J ⥤ C) ≌ J ⥤ ShortComplex C.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.HomologicalComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The short complexes attached to homological complexes
nodes.description: In this file, we define a functor shortComplexFunctor C c i : HomologicalComplex C c ⥤ ShortComplex C. By definition, the image of a homological complex K by this functor is the short complex K.X (c.prev i) ⟶ K.X i ⟶ K.X (c.next i).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Homology
nodes.description: In this file, we shall define the homology of short complexes S, i.e. diagrams f : X₁ ⟶ X₂ and g : X₂ ⟶ X₃ such that f ≫ g = 0. We shall say that [S.HasHomology] when there exists h : S.HomologyData. A homology data for S consists of compatible left/right homology data left and right. The left homology data left involves an object left.H that is a cokernel of the canonical map S.X₁ ⟶ K where K is a kernel of g.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.LeftHomology
nodes.description: Given a short complex S : ShortComplex C, which consists of two composable maps f : X₁ ⟶ X₂ and g : X₂ ⟶ X₃ such that f ≫ g = 0, we shall define here the "left homology" S.leftHomology of S. For this, we introduce the notion of "left homology data". Such an h : S.LeftHomologyData consists of the data of morphisms i : K ⟶ X₂ and π : K ⟶ H such that i identifies K with the kernel of g : X₂ ⟶ X₃, and that π identifies H with the cokernel of the induced map f' : X₁ ⟶ K.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits in the category of short complexes
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown if a category C with zero morphisms has limits of a certain shape J, then it is also the case of the category ShortComplex C.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Linear
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if C is an R-linear category, then ShortComplex C is an R-linear category. Various homological notions are also shown to be linear.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ModuleCat
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homology and exactness of short complexes of modules
nodes.description: In this file, the homology of a short complex S of abelian groups is identified with the quotient of LinearMap.ker S.g by the image of the morphism S.moduleCatToCycles : S.X₁ →ₗ[R] LinearMap.ker S.g induced by S.f.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Preadditive
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if C is a preadditive category, then ShortComplex C is a preadditive category.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.PreservesHomology
nodes.description: If F : C ⥤ D is a functor between categories with zero morphisms, we shall say that F preserves homology when F preserves both kernels and cokernels. This typeclass is named [F.PreservesHomology], and is automatically satisfied when F preserves both finite limits and finite colimits.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.QuasiIso
nodes.description: This file introduces the typeclass QuasiIso φ for a morphism φ : S₁ ⟶ S₂ of short complexes (which have homology): the condition is that the induced morphism homologyMap φ in homology is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Retract
nodes.descriptionTitle: Quasi-isomorphisms of short complexes are stable under retracts
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.Retract.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.RightHomology
nodes.description: In this file, we define the dual notions to those defined in Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.LeftHomology. In particular, if S : ShortComplex C is a short complex consisting of two composable maps f : X₁ ⟶ X₂ and g : X₂ ⟶ X₃ such that f ≫ g = 0, we define h : S.RightHomologyData to be the datum of morphisms p : X₂ ⟶ Q and ι : H ⟶ Q such that Q identifies to the cokernel of f and H to the kernel of the induced map g' : Q ⟶ X₃.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ShortExact
nodes.description: A short complex S : ShortComplex C is short exact (S.ShortExact) when it is exact, S.f is a mono and S.g is an epi.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.SnakeLemma
nodes.description: The snake lemma is a standard tool in homological algebra. The basic situation is when we have a diagram as follows in an abelian category C, with exact rows:

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Single
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homological complexes supported in a single degree
nodes.description: We define single V j c : V ⥤ HomologicalComplex V c, which constructs complexes in V of shape c, supported in degree j.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SingleHomology
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctorSingleIso which is a natural isomorphism single C c j ⋙ homologyFunctor C c j ≅ 𝟭 C.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the category SpectralObject C ι of spectral objects in an abelian category C indexed by the category ι.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.Cycles
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kernel and cokernel of the differential of a spectral object
nodes.description: Let X be a spectral object indexed by the category ι in the abelian category C. In this file, we introduce the kernel X.cycles and the cokernel X.opcycles of X.δ. These are defined when f and g are composable morphisms in ι and for any integer n. In the documentation, the kernel X.cycles n f g of δ : H^n(g) ⟶ H^{n+1}(f) shall be denoted Z^n(f, g), and the cokernel X.opcycles n f g of δ : H^{n-1}(g) ⟶ H^n(f) shall be denoted opZ^n(f, g).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.Differentials
nodes.description: Let X be a spectral object in an abelian category C indexed by a category ι. In this file, we construct the differentials d : E^{n}(f₃, f₄, f₅) ⟶ E^{n+1}(f₁, f₂, f₃) that are attached to families of five composable morphisms f₁, f₂, f₃, f₄, f₅ in ι. We show that d ≫ d = 0. The homology of these differentials is computed in the file Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/SpectralObject/Homology.lean.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Induced morphisms that are epi or mono
nodes.description: Given a spectral object in an abelian category, we show that certain morphisms E^n(f₁, f₂, f₃) ⟶ E^n(f₁', f₂', f₃') are monomorphisms, epimorphisms or isomorphisms.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.FirstPage
nodes.descriptionTitle: The first page of the spectral sequence of a spectral object
nodes.description: Let ι be a preordered type, X a spectral object in an abelian category indexed by ι. Let data : SpectralSequenceDataCore ι c r₀. Assume that X.HasSpectralSequence data holds. In this file, we introduce a property data.HasFirstPageComputation which allows to "compute" the objects of the r₀th page of the spectral sequence attached to X in terms of objects of the form X.H, and we compute the differential on the first page in terms of X.δ, see spectralSequence_first_page_d_eq.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.HasSpectralSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Shapes of spectral sequences obtained from a spectral object
nodes.description: This file prepares for the construction of the spectral sequence of a spectral object in an abelian category which shall be conducted in the file Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/SpectralObject/SpectralSequence.lean.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.Homology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homology of the differentials of a spectral object
nodes.description: Let X be a spectral object indexed by a category ι in an abelian category C. Assume we have seven composable arrows f₁, f₂, f₃, f₄, f₅, f₆, f₇ in ι. In this file, we compute the homology of the differentials, i.e. the homology of the short complex E^{n - 1}(f₅, f₆, f₇) ⟶ E^n(f₃, f₄, f₅) ⟶ E^{n + 1}(f₁, f₂, f₃). The main definition for this is dHomologyData which is a homology data for this short complex where:

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.Page
nodes.description: Let X be a spectral object index by the category ι in the abelian category C. The purpose of this file is to introduce the homology X.E of the short complex X.shortComplex (X.H n₀).obj (mk₁ f₃) ⟶ (X.H n₁).obj (mk₁ f₂) ⟶ (X.H n₂).obj (mk₁ f₁) when f₁, f₂ and f₃ are composable morphisms in ι and the equalities n₀ + 1 = n₁ and n₁ + 1 = n₂ hold (both maps in the short complex are given by X.δ).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject.SpectralSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: The spectral sequence of a spectral object
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is Abelian.SpectralObject.spectralSequence. Assume that X is a spectral object indexed by ι in an abelian category C, and that we have data : SpectralSequenceDataCore ι c r₀ for a family of complex shapes c : ℤ → ComplexShape κ for a type κ and r₀ : ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralSequence.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define the category SpectralSequence C c r₀ of spectral sequences in an abelian category C with Eᵣ-pages defined from r₀ : ℤ having differentials given by complex shapes c : ℤ → ComplexShape κ, where κ is the index type for the objects on each page (e.g. κ := ℤ × ℤ or κ := ℕ × ℕ). A spectral sequence is defined as the data of a sequence of homological complexes (the pages) and a sequence of isomorphisms between the homology of a page and the next page.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.SpectralSequence.ComplexShape
nodes.descriptionTitle: Complex shapes for pages of spectral sequences
nodes.description: In this file, we define complex shapes which correspond to pages of spectral sequences: is the complex shape on ℕ × ℕ corresponding to differentials of ComplexShape.up' u : ComplexShape (ℤ × ℤ) with source and target in ℕ × ℕ. (With u := (r, 1 - r), this will apply to the rth-page of first quadrant E₂ cohomological spectral sequence). this is a similar definition as ComplexShape.spectralSequenceNat but for ℤ × Fin l (identified as a subset of ℤ × ℤ).

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.Square
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relation between pullback/pushout squares and kernel/cokernel sequences
nodes.description: This file is the bundled counterpart of Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/CommSq.lean. The same results are obtained here for squares sq : Square C where C is an additive category.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.TotalComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The total complex of a bicomplex
nodes.description: Given a preadditive category C, two complex shapes c₁ : ComplexShape I₁, c₂ : ComplexShape I₂, a bicomplex K : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂, and a third complex shape c₁₂ : ComplexShape I₁₂ equipped with [TotalComplexShape c₁ c₂ c₁₂], we construct the total complex K.total c₁₂ : HomologicalComplex C c₁₂.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.TotalComplexShift
nodes.descriptionTitle: Behaviour of the total complex with respect to shifts
nodes.description: There are two ways to shift objects in HomologicalComplex₂ C (up ℤ) (up ℤ): which corresponds to the shift by ℤ on CochainComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ) ℤ.

nodes.label: Algebra.Homology.TotalComplexSymmetry
nodes.descriptionTitle: The symmetry of the total complex of a bicomplex
nodes.description: Let K : HomologicalComplex₂ C c₁ c₂ be a bicomplex. If we assume both [TotalComplexShape c₁ c₂ c] and [TotalComplexShape c₂ c₁ c], we may form the total complex K.total c and K.flip.total c.

nodes.label: Algebra.IsPrimePow
nodes.description: This file deals with prime powers: numbers which are positive integer powers of a single prime.

nodes.label: Algebra.Jordan.Basic
nodes.description: Let A be a non-unital, non-associative ring. Then A is said to be a (commutative, linear) Jordan ring if the multiplication is commutative and satisfies a weak associativity law known as the Jordan Identity: for all a and b in A, i.e. the operators of multiplication by a and a^2 commute.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Abelian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Trivial Lie modules and Abelian Lie algebras
nodes.description: The action of a Lie algebra L on a module M is trivial if ⁅x, m⁆ = 0 for all x ∈ L and m ∈ M. In the special case that M = L with the adjoint action, triviality corresponds to the concept of an Abelian Lie algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.AdjointAction.Basic
nodes.description: Theorems about the adjoint action LieAlgebra.ad on associative algebras.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.AdjointAction.Derivation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjoint action of a Lie algebra on itself
nodes.description: This file defines the adjoint action of a Lie algebra on itself, and establishes basic properties.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.AdjointAction.JordanChevalley
nodes.descriptionTitle: Jordan–Chevalley decomposition and the adjoint action
nodes.description: This file contains results about the interaction between the adjoint action LieAlgebra.ad and the Jordan–Chevalley decomposition.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.BaseChange
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extension and restriction of scalars for Lie algebras and Lie modules
nodes.description: Lie algebras and their representations have a well-behaved theory of extension and restriction of scalars.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines Lie rings and Lie algebras over a commutative ring together with their modules, morphisms and equivalences, as well as various lemmas to make these definitions usable.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Basis
nodes.description: In this file we define bases of semisimple Lie algebras. Given an indexing type ι, a basis of a Lie algebra consists of a non-degenerate matrix of integers A indexed by ι × ι and generators h i, e i, f i indexed by ι, each forming an sl₂ triple, and satisfying the Chevalley-Serre relations:

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.CartanCriterion
nodes.description: The two Cartan criteria characterise solvability and semisimplicity of finite-dimensional Lie algebras over fields of characteristic zero in terms of the Killing form: solvability via its vanishing on L × ⁅L, L⁆, semisimplicity via its non-degeneracy.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.CartanExists
nodes.description: In this file we prove existence of Cartan subalgebras in finite-dimensional Lie algebras, following [barnes1967].

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.CartanMatrix
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.CartanSubalgebra
nodes.description: Cartan subalgebras are one of the most important concepts in Lie theory. We define them here. The standard example is the set of diagonal matrices in the Lie algebra of matrices.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Character
nodes.description: A character of a Lie algebra L over a commutative ring R is a morphism of Lie algebras L → R, where R is regarded as a Lie algebra over itself via the ring commutator. For an Abelian Lie algebra (e.g., a Cartan subalgebra of a semisimple Lie algebra) a character is just a linear form.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Classical
nodes.description: This file is the place to find definitions and basic properties of the classical Lie algebras:

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Cochain
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie algebra cohomology in low degree
nodes.description: This file defines low degree cochains of Lie algebras with coefficients given by a module. They are useful in the construction of central extensions, so we treat these easier cases separately from the general theory of Lie algebra cohomology.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Derivation.BaseChange
nodes.descriptionTitle: LieDerivations of a Lie algebra created through BaseChange
nodes.description: When, given an R-algebra A and an R-Lie algebra L the (Lie algebra) basechange A ⊗[R] L, both derivations of A and Lie derivations of L induce Lie derivations of A ⊗[R] L. Moreover, both these procedures are Lie algebra homomorphisms themselves.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Derivation.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines Lie derivations and establishes some basic properties.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Derivation.Killing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivations of finite-dimensional Killing Lie algebras
nodes.description: This file establishes that all derivations of finite-dimensional Killing Lie algebras are inner.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.DirectSum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Direct sums of Lie algebras and Lie modules
nodes.description: Direct sums of Lie algebras and Lie modules carry natural algebra and module structures.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Engel
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of Engel's theorem providing necessary and sufficient conditions for Lie algebras and Lie modules to be nilpotent.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.EngelSubalgebra
nodes.description: This file defines Engel subalgebras of a Lie algebra and provides basic related properties.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Extension
nodes.description: This file defines extensions of Lie algebras, given by short exact sequences of Lie algebra homomorphisms. They are implemented in two ways: IsExtension is a Prop-valued class taking two homomorphisms as parameters, and Extension is a structure that includes the middle Lie algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Free
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring R and a type X we construct the free Lie algebra on X with coefficients in R together with its universal property.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Graded
nodes.description: This file defines typeclasses SetLike.GradedBracket and GradedLieAlgebra, for working with Lie algebras that are graded by a collection ℒ of submodules.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Ideal
nodes.description: This file defines Lie ideals, which are Lie submodules of a Lie algebra over itself. They are defined as a special case of LieSubmodule, and inherit much of their structure from it.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.IdealOperations
nodes.description: Given a Lie module M over a Lie algebra L, there is a natural action of the Lie ideals of L on the Lie submodules of M. In the special case that M = L with the adjoint action, this provides a pairing of Lie ideals which is especially important. For example, it can be used to define solvability / nilpotency of a Lie algebra via the derived / lower-central series.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.InvariantForm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie algebras with non-degenerate invariant bilinear forms are semisimple
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field is semisimple if it does not have non-trivial abelian ideals and it admits a non-degenerate reflexive invariant bilinear form. Here a form is invariant if it is invariant under the Lie bracket in the sense that ⁅x, Φ⁆ = 0 for all x or equivalently, Φ ⁅x, y⁆ z = Φ x ⁅y, z⁆.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Killing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie algebras with non-degenerate Killing forms.
nodes.description: In characteristic zero, the following three conditions are equivalent: 1. The solvable radical of a Lie algebra is trivial 2. A Lie algebra is a direct sum of its simple ideals 3. A Lie algebra has non-degenerate Killing form

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.LieTheorem
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie's theorem for Solvable Lie algebras.
nodes.description: Lie's theorem asserts that Lie modules of solvable Lie algebras over fields of characteristic 0 have a common eigenvector for the action of all elements of the Lie algebra. This result is named LieModule.exists_forall_lie_eq_smul_of_isSolvable.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Loop
nodes.descriptionTitle: Loop Lie algebras and their central extensions
nodes.description: Given a Lie algebra L, the loop algebra is the Lie algebra of maps from a circle into L. This can mean many different things, e.g., continuous maps, smooth maps, polynomial maps. In this file, we consider the simplest case of polynomial maps, meaning we take a base change with the ring of Laurent polynomials.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Matrix
nodes.description: An important class of Lie algebras are those arising from the associative algebra structure on square matrices over a commutative ring. This file provides some very basic definitions whose primary value stems from their utility when constructing the classical Lie algebras using matrices.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Nilpotent
nodes.description: Like groups, Lie algebras admit a natural concept of nilpotency. More generally, any Lie module carries a natural concept of nilpotency. We define these here via the lower central series.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.NonUnitalNonAssocAlgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie algebras as non-unital, non-associative algebras
nodes.description: The definition of Lie algebras uses the Bracket typeclass for multiplication whereas we have a separate Mul typeclass used for general algebras.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Normalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: The normalizer of Lie submodules and subalgebras.
nodes.description: Given a Lie module M over a Lie subalgebra L, the normalizer of a Lie submodule N ⊆ M is the Lie submodule with underlying set { m | ∀ (x : L), ⁅x, m⁆ ∈ N }.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.OfAssociative
nodes.description: This file defines the Lie algebra structure that arises on an associative algebra via the ring commutator.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Prod
nodes.description: This file defines the Lie algebra structure the Product of two Lie algebras

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Quotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: Quotients of Lie algebras and Lie modules
nodes.description: Given a Lie submodule of a Lie module, the quotient carries a natural Lie module structure. In the special case that the Lie module is the Lie algebra itself via the adjoint action, the submodule is a Lie ideal and the quotient carries a natural Lie algebra structure.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Rank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rank of a Lie algebra and regular elements
nodes.description: Let L be a Lie algebra over a nontrivial commutative ring R, and assume that L is finite free as R-module. Then the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of ad R L x are polynomial in x. The rank of L is the smallest n for which the n-th coefficient is not the zero polynomial.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.SemiDirect
nodes.description: This file defines the semi-direct sum of Lie algebras. These are the infinitesimal counterpart of semidirect products of (Lie) groups. Given two Lie algebras K and L over R as well as a Lie algebra homomorphism ψ : L → LieDerivation R K K, the underlying set of the semidirect sum is K × L, however the bracket is twisted by ψ. In this file we show that SemiDirectSum K L ψ is itself a Lie algebra and that it fits into an exact sequence H → (SemiDirectSum K L ψ) → L, i.e. forms an extension of L.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Semisimple.Basic
nodes.description: The famous Cartan-Dynkin-Killing classification of semisimple Lie algebras renders them one of the most important classes of Lie algebras. In this file we prove basic results about simple and semisimple Lie algebras.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Semisimple.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define simple and semisimple Lie algebras, together with related concepts.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Semisimple.Lemmas
nodes.description: This file is a home for lemmas about semisimple and reductive Lie algebras.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.SerreConstruction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Serre construction of Lie algebras from Cartan matrices
nodes.description:
This file provides the Serre construction of Lie algebras from Cartan matrices. Given a Cartan matrix A, we construct a Lie algebra as a quotient of the free Lie algebra on generators {H_i, E_i, F_i} by the Serre relations: $$  egin{align} [H_i, H_j] &= 0\ [E_i, F_i] &= H_i\ [E_i, F_j] &= 0 \quad	ext{if $i 
e j$}\ [H_i, E_j] &= A_{ij}E_j\ [H_i, F_j] &= -A_{ij}F_j\ ad(E_i)^{1 - A_{ij}}(E_j) &= 0 \quad	ext{if $i 
e j$}\ ad(F_i)^{1 - A_{ij}}(F_j) &= 0 \quad	ext{if $i 
e j$}\ \end{align} $$

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.SkewAdjoint
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie algebras of skew-adjoint endomorphisms of a bilinear form
nodes.description: When a module carries a bilinear form, the Lie algebra of endomorphisms of the module contains a distinguished Lie subalgebra: the skew-adjoint endomorphisms. Such subalgebras are important because they provide a simple, explicit construction of the so-called classical Lie algebras.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Sl2
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Lie algebra sl₂ and its representations
nodes.description: The Lie algebra sl₂ is the unique simple Lie algebra of minimal rank, 1, and as such occupies a distinguished position in the general theory. This file provides some basic definitions and results about sl₂.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Solvable
nodes.description: Like groups, Lie algebras admit a natural concept of solvability. We define this here via the derived series and prove some related results. We also define the radical of a Lie algebra and prove that it is solvable when the Lie algebra is Noetherian.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Subalgebra
nodes.description: This file defines Lie subalgebras of a Lie algebra and provides basic related definitions and results.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Submodule
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie submodules of a Lie algebra
nodes.description: In this file we define Lie submodules, we construct the lattice structure on Lie submodules and we use it to define various important operations, notably the Lie span of a subset of a Lie module.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.TensorProduct
nodes.description: Tensor products of Lie modules carry natural Lie module structures.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.TraceForm
nodes.descriptionTitle: The trace and Killing forms of a Lie algebra.
nodes.description: Let L be a Lie algebra with coefficients in a commutative ring R. Suppose M is a finite, free R-module and we have a representation φ : L → End M. This data induces a natural bilinear form B on L, called the trace form associated to M; it is defined as B(x, y) = Tr (φ x) (φ y).

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.UniversalEnveloping
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring R and a Lie algebra L over R, we construct the universal enveloping algebra of L, together with its universal property.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weight spaces of Lie modules of nilpotent Lie algebras
nodes.description: Just as a key tool when studying the behaviour of a linear operator is to decompose the space on which it acts into a sum of (generalised) eigenspaces, a key tool when studying a representation M of Lie algebra L is to decompose M into a sum of simultaneous eigenspaces of x as x ranges over L. These simultaneous generalised eigenspaces are known as the weight spaces of M.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.Cartan
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weights and roots of Lie modules and Lie algebras with respect to Cartan subalgebras
nodes.description: Given a Lie algebra L which is not necessarily nilpotent, it may be useful to study its representations by restricting them to a nilpotent subalgebra (e.g., a Cartan subalgebra). In the particular case when we view L as a module over itself via the adjoint action, the weight spaces of L restricted to a nilpotent subalgebra are known as root spaces.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.Chain
nodes.description: Given roots α and β of a Lie algebra, together with elements x in the α-root space and y in the β-root space, it follows from the Leibniz identity that ⁅x, y⁆ is either zero or belongs to the α + β-root space. Iterating this operation leads to the study of families of roots of the form k • α + β. Such a family is known as the α-chain through β (or sometimes, the α-string through β) and the study of the sum of the corresponding root spaces is an important technique.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.IsSimple
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie ideals, invariant root submodules, and simple Lie algebras
nodes.description: Given a semisimple Lie algebra, the lattice of ideals is order isomorphic to the lattice of Weyl-group-invariant submodules of the corresponding root system. In this file we provide LieIdeal.toInvtRootSubmodule, which constructs the invariant submodule associated to an ideal, and LieAlgebra.IsKilling.invtSubmoduleToLieIdeal, which constructs the ideal associated to an invariant submodule.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.Killing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Roots of Lie algebras with non-degenerate Killing forms
nodes.description: The file contains definitions and results about roots of Lie algebras with non-degenerate Killing forms.

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.Linear
nodes.description: Given a Lie module M over a nilpotent Lie algebra L with coefficients in R, one frequently studies M via its weights. These are functions χ : L → R whose corresponding weight space LieModule.genWeightSpace M χ, is non-trivial. If L is Abelian or if R has characteristic zero (and M is finite-dimensional) then such χ are necessarily R-linear. However in general non-linear weights do exist. For example if we take:

nodes.label: Algebra.Lie.Weights.RootSystem
nodes.descriptionTitle: The root system associated with a Lie algebra
nodes.description: We show that the roots of a finite-dimensional splitting semisimple Lie algebra over a field of characteristic 0 form a root system. We achieve this by studying root chains.

nodes.label: Algebra.LieRinehartAlgebra.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines Lie-Rinehart algebras and their morphisms. It also shows that the derivations of a commutative algebra over a commutative Ring form such a Lie-Rinehart algebra. Lie-Rinehart algebras appear in differential geometry as section spaces of Lie algebroids and singular foliations. The typical Cartan calculus of differential geometry can be restated fully in terms of the Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra of a Lie-Rinehart algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.LinearRecurrence
nodes.description: Informally, a "linear recurrence" is an assertion of the form ∀ n : ℕ, u (n + d) = a 0 u n + a 1 u (n+1) + ... + a (d-1) u (n+d-1), where u is a sequence, d is the order of the recurrence and the a i are its coefficients.

nodes.label: Algebra.ModEq
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Algebra.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Basic
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Algebra.Module.Basic.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.BigOperators
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite sums over modules over a ring
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Algebra.Module.BigOperators.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Bimodule
nodes.description: One frequently encounters situations in which several sets of scalars act on a single space, subject to compatibility condition(s). A distinguished instance of this is the theory of bimodules: one has two rings R, S acting on an additive group M, with R acting covariantly ("on the left") and S acting contravariantly ("on the right"). The compatibility condition is just: (r • m) • s = r • (m • s) for all r : R, s : S, m : M.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Card
nodes.description: This file proves that the cardinality of a module without zero divisors is at least the cardinality of its base ring.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.CharacterModule
nodes.description: For commutative ring R and an R-module M and an injective module D, its character module M⋆ is defined to be R-linear maps M ⟶ D.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Congruence.Defs
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Algebra.Module.Congruence.Defs.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.DedekindDomain
nodes.description: Over a Dedekind domain, an I-torsion module is the internal direct sum of its p i ^ e i-torsion submodules, where I = ∏ i, p i ^ e i is its unique decomposition in prime ideals. Therefore, as any finitely generated torsion module is I-torsion for some I, it is an internal direct sum of its p i ^ e i-torsion submodules for some prime ideals p i and numbers e i.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Defs
nodes.description: Semiring R if for r : R and x : M their "scalar multiplication" r • x : M is defined, and the operation • satisfies some natural associativity and distributivity axioms similar to those on a ring.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.End
nodes.description: In this file, we define Module.toAddMonoidEnd, which is (•) as a monoid homomorphism. We use this to prove some results on scalar multiplication by integers.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Equiv.Opposite
nodes.description: This file contains definitions that build on top of the group action definitions in Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Opposite.lean.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.FinitePresentation
nodes.description: finite set s and the kernel of the presentation Rˢ → M is also finitely generated.

nodes.description: Given an R-algebra A graded by 𝓐, a graded A-module M is expressed as DirectSum.Decomposition 𝓜 and SetLike.GradedSMul 𝓐 𝓜. Then ⨁ i, 𝓜 i is an A-module and is isomorphic to M.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Hom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bundled Hom instances for module and multiplicative actions
nodes.description: This file defines instances for Module on bundled Hom types.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Injective
nodes.description: map descends to a linear map to Q, i.e. in the following diagram, if f is injective then there is an R-linear map h : Y ⟶ Q such that g = h ∘ f Ideal R extends to an R-linear map R ⟶ Q

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.Lattice
nodes.description: Let A be an R-algebra and V an A-module. Then an R-submodule M of V is a lattice, if M is finitely generated and spans V as an A-module.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Basic
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Basic.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Defs
nodes.description: σ is a RingHom from R to R₂ and an f : M →ₛₗ[σ] M₂ satisfies f (c • x) = (σ c) • (f x). We recover plain linear maps by choosing σ to be RingHom.id R. This is denoted by M →ₗ[R] M₂. We also add the notation M →ₗ⋆[R] M₂ for star-linear maps.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.DivisionRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some lemmas about linear functionals on division rings
nodes.description: This file proves some results on linear functionals on division semirings.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.End
nodes.description: In this file we define the type of linear endomorphisms of a module over a ring (Module.End). We set up the basic theory, including the action of Module.End on the module we are considering endomorphisms of.

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.FiniteRange
nodes.descriptionTitle: HasFiniteRange predicate on linear maps, and the associated equivalence relation
nodes.description: In this file, we define:

nodes.label: Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Polynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characteristic polynomials of linear families of endomorphisms
nodes.description: The coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of a linear family of endomorphisms are homogeneous polynomials in the parameters. This result is used in Lie theory to establish the existence of regular elements and Cartan subalgebras, and ultimately a well-defined notion of rank for Lie algebras.

The order compatibility allows for a treatment of the R((z))-module structure on (z ^ s) V((z)) for an R-module V, using the formalism of Hahn series. In the multiplicative case, a standard example is the action of non-negative rationals on an ordered field.

nodes.label: Algebra.Order.Archimedean.Class
nodes.descriptionTitle: Archimedean classes of a linearly ordered group
nodes.description: This file defines archimedean classes of a given linearly ordered group. Archimedean classes measure to what extent the group fails to be Archimedean. For additive group, elements a and b in the same class are "equivalent" in the sense that there exist two natural numbers m and n such that |a| ≤ m • |b| and |b| ≤ n • |a|. An element a in a higher class than b is "infinitesimal" to b in the sense that n • |a| < |b| for all natural numbers n.

nodes.label: Algebra.Order.Ring.Star
nodes.descriptionTitle: Commutative star-ordered rings are ordered rings
nodes.description: A noncommutative star-ordered ring is generally not an ordered ring. Indeed, in a star-ordered ring, nonnegative elements are self-adjoint, but the product of self-adjoint elements is self-adjoint if and only if they commute. Therefore, a necessary condition for a star-ordered ring to be an ordered ring is that all nonnegative elements commute. Consequently, if a star-ordered ring is spanned by it nonnegative elements (as is the case for C⋆-algebras) and it is also an ordered ring, then it is commutative.

The nonsingular affine points on W can be given negation and addition operations defined by a secant-and-tangent process. nonsingular point of intersection between W and the vertical line through P. Explicitly, if P is (x, y), then -P is (x, -y - a₁x - a₃). negation of the unique third nonsingular point of intersection between W and the line L through P and Q. Explicitly, let P be (x₁, y₁) and let Q be (x₂, y₂).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Affine.Point
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nonsingular points and the group law in affine coordinates
nodes.description: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field F given by a Weierstrass equation W(X, Y) = 0 in affine coordinates. The type of nonsingular points in affine coordinates is an inductive, consisting of the unique point at infinity 𝓞 and nonsingular affine points (x, y). It can be endowed with a group law, with 𝓞 as the identity nonsingular point, which is uniquely determined by the formulae in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Formula.lean.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.DivisionPolynomial.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines certain polynomials associated to division polynomials of Weierstrass curves. These are defined in terms of the auxiliary sequences for normalised elliptic divisibility sequences (EDS) as defined in Mathlib/NumberTheory/EllipticDivisibilitySequence.lean.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.DivisionPolynomial.Degree
nodes.description: This file computes the leading terms of certain polynomials associated to division polynomials of Weierstrass curves defined in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/DivisionPolynomial/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.IsomOfJ
nodes.descriptionTitle: Elliptic curves with same j-invariants are isomorphic
nodes.description: same j-invariants defined over a separably closed field, then there exists a change of variables over that field which change E into E'.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Jacobian.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weierstrass equations and the nonsingular condition in Jacobian coordinates
nodes.description: A point on the projective plane over a commutative ring R with weights (2, 3, 1) is an equivalence class [x : y : z] of triples (x, y, z) ≠ (0, 0, 0) of elements in R such that (x, y, z) ∼ (x', y', z') if there is some unit u in Rˣ with (x, y, z) = (u²x', u³y', uz').

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Jacobian.Formula
nodes.descriptionTitle: Negation and addition formulae for nonsingular points in Jacobian coordinates
nodes.description: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field F. The nonsingular Jacobian points on W can be given negation and addition operations defined by an analogue of the secant-and-tangent process in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Formula.lean, but the polynomials involved are (2, 3, 1)-homogeneous, so any instances of division become multiplication in the Z-coordinate. Most computational proofs are immediate from their analogous proofs for affine coordinates.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Jacobian.Point
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nonsingular points and the group law in Jacobian coordinates
nodes.description: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field F.
