The nonsingular Jacobian points of W can be endowed with a group law, which is uniquely determined by the formulae in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Jacobian/Formula.lean and follows from an equivalence with the nonsingular points in affine coordinates.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.LFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: The L-function of a Weierstrass curve
nodes.description: In this file, we define the L-function of a Weierstrass curve.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.ModelsWithJ
nodes.descriptionTitle: Models of elliptic curves with prescribed j-invariant
nodes.description: This file defines the Weierstrass equation over a field with prescribed j-invariant, proved that it is an elliptic curve, and that its j-invariant is equal to the given value. It is a modification of [silverman2009], Chapter III, Proposition 1.4 (c).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.NormalForms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some normal forms of elliptic curves
nodes.description: This file defines some normal forms of Weierstrass equations of elliptic curves.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Projective.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weierstrass equations and the nonsingular condition in projective coordinates
nodes.description: A point on the unweighted projective plane over a commutative ring R is an equivalence class [x : y : z] of triples (x, y, z) ≠ (0, 0, 0) of elements in R such that (x, y, z) ∼ (x', y', z') if there is some unit u in Rˣ with (x, y, z) = (ux', uy', uz').

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Projective.Formula
nodes.descriptionTitle: Negation and addition formulae for nonsingular points in projective coordinates
nodes.description: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field F. The nonsingular projective points on W can be given negation and addition operations defined by an analogue of the secant-and-tangent process in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Formula.lean, but the polynomials involved are homogeneous, so any instances of division become multiplication in the Z-coordinate. Most computational proofs are immediate from their analogous proofs for affine coordinates.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Projective.Point
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nonsingular points and the group law in projective coordinates
nodes.description: Let W be a Weierstrass curve over a field F. The nonsingular projective points of W can be endowed with a group law, which is uniquely determined by the formulae in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Projective/Formula.lean and follows from an equivalence with the nonsingular points in affine coordinates.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Reduction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Reduction of Weierstrass curves over local fields
nodes.description: This file defines reduction of Weierstrass curves over local fields, or more generally, fraction fields of discrete valuation rings.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.VariableChange
nodes.descriptionTitle: Change of variables of Weierstrass curves
nodes.description: This file defines admissible linear change of variables of Weierstrass curves.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.EllipticCurve.Weierstrass
nodes.description: This file defines the structure of an elliptic curve as a nonsingular Weierstrass curve given by a Weierstrass equation, which is mathematically accurate in many cases but also good for computation.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Fiber
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicGeometry.Fiber.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.FunctionField
nodes.description: We define the function field of an irreducible scheme as the stalk of the generic point. This is a field when the scheme is integral.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.GammaSpecAdjunction
nodes.description: We define the adjunction ΓSpec.adjunction : Γ ⊣ Spec by defining the unit (toΓSpec, in multiple steps in this file) and counit (done in Spec.lean) and checking that they satisfy the left and right triangle identities. The constructions and proofs make use of maps and lemmas defined and proved in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/StructureSheaf.lean extensively.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define the basic interface for properties like geometrically reduced, geometrically irreducible, geometrically connected etc. In this file we treat an abstract property of schemes P and derive the general properties that are shared by all of these variants.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Connected
nodes.description: In this file we define geometrically connected morphisms of schemes. A morphism f : X ⟶ Y is geometrically connected if for all Spec K ⟶ Y with K a field, X ×[Y] Spec K is connected. In the case where Y = Spec K for some field K this recovers the standard definition of a geometrically connected scheme over a field.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Integral
nodes.description: We say that morphism f : X ⟶ Y is geometrically integral if for all Spec K ⟶ Y with K a field, X ×[Y] Spec K is integral. We also provide the fact that this is stable under base change (by infer_instance) A scheme is geometrically integral over S iff the fibers of all s : S are geometrically integral. If X is geometrically integral, flat, and universally open (e.g. when over a field), over an integral locally noetherian scheme, then X is also integral.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Irreducible
nodes.description: We say that morphism f : X ⟶ Y is geometrically irreducible if for all Spec K ⟶ Y with K a field, X ×[Y] Spec K is irreducible. We also provide the fact that this is stable under base change (by infer_instance) A scheme is geometrically irreducible over S iff the fibers of all s : S are geometrically irreducible. If X is geometrically irreducible and universally open (e.g. when flat + finite presentation), over an irreducible scheme, then X is also irreducible.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Reduced
nodes.description: We say that morphism f : X ⟶ Y is geometrically reduced if for all Spec K ⟶ Y with K a field, X ×[Y] Spec K is reduced. We also provide the fact that this is stable under base change (by infer_instance) A scheme is geometrically reduced over S iff the fibers of all s : S are geometrically reduced. If X is geometrically reduced and flat over a reduced and locally noetherian scheme, then X is also reduced.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Gluing
nodes.description: Given a family of gluing data of schemes, we may glue them together. Also see the section about "locally directed" gluing, which is a special case where the conditions are easier to check.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.GluingOneHypercover
nodes.description: In this file, given D : Scheme.GlueData, we construct a 1-hypercover D.openHypercover of the scheme D.glued in the big Zariski site. We use this 1-hypercover in order to define a constructor D.sheafValGluedMk for sections over D.glued of a sheaf of types over the big Zariski site.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Abelian
nodes.description: A proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Smooth
nodes.description: If G is a group scheme over a field k that is geometrically reduced and locally of finite type, then G is smooth over k.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Basic
nodes.description: We define ideal sheaves of schemes and provide various constructors for it.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Functorial
nodes.description: We define the pullback and pushforward of ideal sheaves in this file.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.IrreducibleComponent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Subscheme structure on an irreducible component
nodes.description: We define the subscheme structure on an irreducible component of a Noetherian scheme. Typically, one takes the reduced induced subscheme structure, but this will throw away information if the irreducible component is not already reduced. Instead, we take the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of the restriction to the complement of the union of the other irreducible components. For example, if X is irreducible then this will give back the original scheme X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Subscheme
nodes.descriptionTitle: Subscheme associated to an ideal sheaf
nodes.description: We construct the subscheme associated to an ideal sheaf.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Limits
nodes.description: We construct various limits and colimits in the category of schemes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitsOver
nodes.description: We show that if P is a morphism property in Scheme that is local at the source, then colimits in P.Over ⊤ X for X : Scheme of locally directed diagrams of open immersions exist and agree with the colimit in Scheme.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Presheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of presheaves of modules over a scheme
nodes.description: In this file, given a scheme X, we define the category of presheaves of modules over X. As categories of presheaves of modules are defined for presheaves of rings (and not presheaves of commutative rings), we also introduce a definition X.ringCatSheaf for the underlying sheaf of rings of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of sheaves of modules over a scheme
nodes.description: In this file, we define the abelian category of sheaves of modules X.Modules over a scheme X, and study its basic functoriality.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Tilde
nodes.description: Given any commutative ring R and R-module M, we construct the sheaf M^~ of 𝒪_SpecR-modules such that M^~(U) is the set of dependent functions that are locally fractions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Affine
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is affine if the preimage of an arbitrary affine open subset of Y is affine.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.AffineAnd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Affine morphisms with additional ring hom property
nodes.description: In this file we define a constructor affineAnd Q for affine target morphism properties of schemes from a property of ring homomorphisms Q: A morphism f : X ⟶ Y with affine target satisfies affineAnd Q if it is an affine morphism (i.e. X is affine) and the induced ring map on global sections satisfies Q.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Basic
nodes.description: We provide the basic framework for talking about properties of morphisms between Schemes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.ClosedImmersion
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is a closed immersion if the underlying map of topological spaces is a closed immersion and the induced morphisms of stalks are all surjective.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Constructors
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructors for properties of morphisms between schemes
nodes.description: This file provides some constructors to obtain morphism properties of schemes from other morphism properties:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Descent
nodes.description: Let P and P' be morphism properties. In this file we show some results to deduce that P descends along P' from a codescent property of ring homomorphisms.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Etale
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is étale if for each affine U ⊆ Y and V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U, the induced map Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is étale.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Finite
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is finite if the preimage of an arbitrary affine open subset of Y is affine and the induced ring map is finite.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FinitePresentation
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is locally of finite presentation if for each affine U ⊆ Y and V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U, The induced map Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is of finite presentation.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FiniteType
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is locally of finite type if for each affine U ⊆ Y and V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U, The induced map Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is of finite type.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is flat if for each affine U ⊆ Y and V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U, the induced map Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is flat. This is equivalent to asking that all stalk maps are flat (see AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FlatDescent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of morphisms satisfying fpqc descent
nodes.description: In this file we show some global properties satisfy fpqc descent.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FlatMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Flat monomorphisms of finite presentation are open immersions
nodes.description: We show the titular result AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.of_flat_of_mono by fpqc descent.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FlatRank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rank of a finite flat morphism of schemes
nodes.description: In this file we define the rank AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finrank of a finite flat morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y. It is locally constant and is characterized by the condition that the rank of Spec S ⟶ Spec R at some prime p of R is the rank of S as an R-algebra at p.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FormallyUnramified
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is formally unramified if for each affine U ⊆ Y and V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U, the induced map Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is formally unramified.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Immersion
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is an immersion if the underlying map of topological spaces is a locally closed embedding, and the induced morphisms of stalks are all surjective. This is true if and only if it can be factored into a closed immersion followed by an open immersion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Integral
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is integral if the preimage of an arbitrary affine open subset of Y is affine and the induced ring map is integral.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.IsIso
nodes.descriptionTitle: Being an isomorphism is local at the target
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.IsIso.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.LocalClosure
nodes.description: We define the source local closure of a property P w.r.t. a morphism property W and show it inherits stability properties from P.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.LocalFlatDescent
nodes.description: In this file we provide instances that show that the following local properties satisfy fpqc descent:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.LocalIso
nodes.description: A local isomorphism of schemes is a morphism that is source-locally an open immersion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.OpenImmersion
nodes.description: A morphism is an open immersion if the underlying map of spaces is an open embedding f : X ⟶ U ⊆ Y, and the sheaf map Y(V) ⟶ f _ X(V) is an iso for each V ⊆ U.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Preimmersion
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is a preimmersion if the underlying map of topological spaces is an embedding and the induced morphisms of stalks are all surjective. This is not a concept seen in the literature but it is useful for generalizing results on immersions to other maps including Spec 𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ X and inclusions of fibers κ(x) ×ₓ Y ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Proper
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes is proper if it is separated, universally closed and (locally) of finite type. Note that we don't require quasi-compact, since this is implied by universally closed.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiCompact
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes is quasi-compact if the preimages of quasi-compact open sets are quasi-compact.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiFinite
nodes.description: We say that a morphism f : X ⟶ Y is locally quasi finite if Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V) is quasi-finite (in the mathlib sense) for every pair of affine opens that f maps one into the other.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiSeparated
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is quasi-separated if the diagonal morphism X ⟶ X ×[Y] X is quasi-compact.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.RingHomProperties
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of morphisms from properties of ring homs.
nodes.description: We provide the basic framework for talking about properties of morphisms that come from properties of ring homs. For P a property of ring homs, we have two ways of defining a property of scheme morphisms:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.SchemeTheoreticallyDominant
nodes.description: In this file, we define scheme-theoretically dominant morphisms as morphisms with trivial kernel.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Separated
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes is separated if its diagonal morphism is a closed immersion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Smooth
nodes.description: In this file we define smooth morphisms. The main definitions are:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.SmoothFiber
nodes.description: finite presentation and smooth fibers is smooth.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.SurjectiveOnStalks
nodes.description: We define the class of morphisms between schemes that are surjective on stalks. We show that this class is stable under composition and base change.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UnderlyingMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties on the underlying functions of morphisms of schemes
nodes.description: This file includes various results on properties of morphisms of schemes that come from properties of the underlying map of topological spaces, including

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyClosed
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is universally closed if X ×[Y] Y' ⟶ Y' is a closed map for all base change Y' ⟶ Y. This implies that f is topologically proper (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isProperMap).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyInjective
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is universally injective if X ×[Y] Y' ⟶ Y' is injective for all base changes Y' ⟶ Y. This is equivalent to the diagonal morphism being surjective (AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyInjective.iff_diagonal).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UniversallyOpen
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes f : X ⟶ Y is universally open if X ×[Y] Y' ⟶ Y' is an open map for all base change Y' ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.WeaklyEtale
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes is weakly étale if it is flat and its diagonal is flat. As the name suggests any étale morphism is weakly étale and every weakly étale morphism of finite presentation is étale.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Noetherian
nodes.description: We introduce the concept of (locally) Noetherian schemes, giving definitions, equivalent conditions, and basic properties.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Normalization
nodes.description: Given a qcqs morphism f : X ⟶ Y, we define the relative normalization f.normalization, along with the maps that f factor into:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.OpenImmersion
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicGeometry.OpenImmersion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Over
nodes.description: We define these as thin wrappers around CategoryTheory/Comma/OverClass.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.PointsPi
nodes.description: We show that the canonical map X(Π Rᵢ) ⟶ Π X(Rᵢ) (AlgebraicGeometry.pointsPi) is injective and surjective under various assumptions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of the scheme Proj A
nodes.description: The scheme Proj 𝒜 for a graded ring 𝒜 is constructed in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Scheme.lean. In this file we provide basic properties of the scheme.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Functor
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Functor.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proper
nodes.description: We show that Proj 𝒜 is proper over Spec 𝒜₀.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Scheme
nodes.description: This file is to prove that Proj is a scheme.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.StructureSheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: The structure sheaf on ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜.
nodes.description: In Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Topology.lean, we have given a topology on ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜; in this file we will construct a sheaf on ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Topology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective spectrum of a graded ring
nodes.description: The projective spectrum of a graded commutative ring is the subtype of all homogeneous ideals that are prime and do not contain the irrelevant ideal. It is naturally endowed with a topology: the Zariski topology.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Properties
nodes.description: We provide some basic properties of schemes

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.PullbackCarrier
nodes.descriptionTitle: Underlying topological space of fibre product of schemes
nodes.description: Let f : X ⟶ S and g : Y ⟶ S be morphisms of schemes. In this file we describe the underlying topological space of pullback f g, i.e. the fiber product X ×[S] Y.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
nodes.description: In this file we construct the fibred product of schemes via gluing. We roughly follow [har77] Theorem 3.3.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiAffine
nodes.description: A scheme X is quasi-affine if it is quasi-compact and X ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤) is an immersion. This actually implies that X ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤) is an open immersion. Any quasi-compact locally closed subscheme of a quasi-affine scheme is quasi-affine.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.RationalMap
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in AlgebraicGeometry.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeGluing
nodes.description: In this file we show a relative gluing lemma (see https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LH): If {Uᵢ} is a locally directed open cover of S and we have a compatible family of Xᵢ over Uᵢ, the Xᵢ glue to a morphism f : X ⟶ S such that Xᵢ ≅ f⁻¹ Uᵢ.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ResidueField
nodes.description: The following are in the AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme namespace:

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Restrict
nodes.description: The map X.restrict f ⟶ X is AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ofRestrict. U : X.Opens has a coercion to Scheme and U.ι is a shorthand for X.restrict U.open_embedding : U ⟶ X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
nodes.description: A scheme is a locally ringed space such that every point is contained in some open set where there is an isomorphism of presheaves between the restriction to that open set, and the structure sheaf of Spec R, for some commutative ring R.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Affine
nodes.descriptionTitle: Small affine site induced by a morphism property
nodes.description: Let P be a morphism property of schemes and S be a scheme. In this file we study the small affine P-site of S: its objects are rings R with a structure morphism Spec R ⟶ S that satisfies P.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.AffineEtale
nodes.description: In this file we define the small affine étale site of a scheme S. The underlying category is the category of commutative rings R equipped with an étale structure morphism Spec R ⟶ S. We show that this category is essentially small, that it is a dense subsite of the small étale site, and that it is 1-hypercover dense, which allows to show that if S : Scheme.{u}, then we can sheafify étale presheaves with values in Type u, AddCommGrpCat.{u}, etc.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.BigZariski
nodes.descriptionTitle: The big Zariski site of schemes
nodes.description: In this file, we define the Zariski topology, as a Grothendieck topology on the category Scheme.{u}: this is Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u}. If X : Scheme.{u}, the Zariski topology on Over X can be obtained as Scheme.zariskiTopology.over X (see CategoryTheory.Sites.Over.).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.ConstantSheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sheaf of continuous maps associated to topological space
nodes.description: Given a topological space T, we consider the presheaf on Scheme given by U ↦ C(U, T) and show that it is a Zariski sheaf (TODO: show that it is a fpqc sheaf). When T is discrete, this is the constant sheaf associated to T (TODO).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.ElladicCohomology
nodes.description: Let X be a scheme and ℓ be a prime number. In this file we define the sheaf associated to the topological group ℤ_[ℓ] on the pro-étale site of X. Its cohomology groups are the ℓ-adic cohomology groups of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Etale
nodes.description: In this file we define the big étale site, i.e. the étale topology as a Grothendieck topology on the category of schemes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Fpqc
nodes.description: In this file we define the fpqc topology and show it is subcanonical. It is the quasi-compact topology for flat morphisms.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Site defined by a morphism property
nodes.description: Given a multiplicative morphism property P that is stable under base change, we define the associated precoverage on the category of schemes, where coverings are given by jointly surjective families of morphisms satisfying P.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Pretopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Grothendieck topology defined by a morphism property
nodes.description: Given a multiplicative morphism property P that is stable under base change, we define the associated (pre)topology on the category of schemes, where coverings are given by jointly surjective families of morphisms satisfying P.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Proetale
nodes.description: In this file we define the big and small pro-étale site. The big pro-étale site is the category of schemes equipped with the pro-étale topology, which is the topology generated by fpqc covers of weakly étale morphisms.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.QuasiCompact
nodes.description: In this file we define the quasi-compact precoverage. A cover is covering in the quasi-compact precoverage if it is a quasi-compact cover, i.e., if every affine open of the base can be covered by a finite union of images of quasi-compact opens of the components.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
nodes.descriptionTitle: Representability of schemes is a local property
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a sheaf of types F on Sch is representable if it is locally representable.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.SheafQuasiCompact
nodes.description: In this file we show that a presheaf is a sheaf in the AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.propQCTopology if and only if it is a sheaf in the Zariski topology and a sheaf on single object P-coverings of affine schemes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Small
nodes.description: In this file we define the small sites associated to morphism properties and give generating pretopologies.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.SmallAffineZariski
nodes.description: X.AffineZariskiSite is the small affine Zariski site of X, whose elements are affine open sets of X, and whose arrows are basic open sets D(f) ⟶ U for any f : Γ(X, U).

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Spec
nodes.descriptionTitle: $Spec$ as a functor to locally ringed spaces.
nodes.description: We define the functor $Spec$ from commutative rings to locally ringed spaces.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.SpreadingOut
nodes.description: Under certain conditions, a morphism on stalks Spec 𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ Spec 𝒪_{Y, y} can be spread out into a neighborhood of x.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.Stalk
nodes.description: exactly the ys that specialize to x. Given a local ring R and scheme X, morphisms Spec R ⟶ X corresponds to pairs (x, f) where x : X and f : 𝒪_{X, x} ⟶ R is a local ring homomorphism.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: The structure sheaf on PrimeSpectrum R.
nodes.description: We define the structure sheaf on TopCat.of (PrimeSpectrum R), for an R-module M and prove basic properties about it. We define this as a subsheaf of the sheaf of dependent functions into the localizations, cut out by the condition that the function must be locally equal to a quotient of an element of M by an element of R.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCriterion
nodes.description: A morphism is universally closed if and only if it is quasi-compact and satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion. A morphism is separated if and only if it is quasi-separated and satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion. A morphism is proper if and only if it is qcqs and of finite type and satisfies the valuative criterion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskisMainTheorem
nodes.description: In this file we prove Grothendieck's reformulation of Zariski's main theorem, namely if f : X ⟶ Y is separated and of finite type, then the map from the quasi-finite locus U ⊆ X of f to the relative normalization X' of Y in X is an open immersion.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The alternating face map complex of a simplicial object in a preadditive category
nodes.description: We construct the alternating face map complex, as a functor alternatingFaceMapComplex : SimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ for any preadditive category C. For any simplicial object X in C, this is the homological complex ... → X_2 → X_1 → X_0 where the differentials are alternating sums of faces.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.CechNerve
nodes.description: This file provides a definition of the Čech nerve associated to an arrow, provided the base category has the correct wide pullbacks.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Compatibility
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tools for compatibilities between Dold-Kan equivalences
nodes.description: The purpose of this file is to introduce tools which will enable the construction of the Dold-Kan equivalence SimplicialObject C ≌ ChainComplex C ℕ for a pseudoabelian category C from the equivalence Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) ≌ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) and the two equivalences SimplicialObject C ≌ Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) and ChainComplex C ℕ ≌ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Decomposition
nodes.description: In this file, we obtain a lemma decomposition_Q which expresses explicitly the projection (Q q).f (n+1) : X _⦋n+1⦌ ⟶ X _⦋n+1⦌ (X : SimplicialObject C with C a preadditive category) as a sum of terms which are postcompositions with degeneracies.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Degeneracies
nodes.descriptionTitle: Behaviour of P_infty with respect to degeneracies
nodes.description: For any X : SimplicialObject C where C is an abelian category, the projector PInfty : K[X] ⟶ K[X] is supposed to be the projection on the normalized subcomplex, parallel to the degenerate subcomplex, i.e. the subcomplex generated by the images of all X.σ i.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Equivalence
nodes.description: The Dold-Kan correspondence states that for any abelian category A, there is an equivalence between the category of simplicial objects in A and the category of chain complexes in A (with degrees indexed by ℕ and the homological convention that the degree is decreased by the differentials).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.EquivalenceAdditive
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Dold-Kan equivalence for additive categories.
nodes.description: This file defines Preadditive.DoldKan.equivalence which is the equivalence of categories Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) ≌ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.EquivalencePseudoabelian
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Dold-Kan correspondence for pseudoabelian categories
nodes.description: In this file, for any idempotent complete additive category C, the Dold-Kan equivalence Idempotents.DoldKan.Equivalence C : SimplicialObject C ≌ ChainComplex C ℕ is obtained. It is deduced from the equivalence Preadditive.DoldKan.Equivalence between the respective idempotent completions of these categories using the fact that when C is idempotent complete, then both SimplicialObject C and ChainComplex C ℕ are idempotent complete.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Faces
nodes.descriptionTitle: Study of face maps for the Dold-Kan correspondence
nodes.description: In this file, we obtain the technical lemmas that are used in the file Projections.lean in order to get basic properties of the endomorphisms P q : K[X] ⟶ K[X] with respect to face maps (see Homotopies.lean for the role of these endomorphisms in the overall strategy of proof).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.FunctorGamma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of the inverse functor of the Dold-Kan equivalence
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the functor Γ₀ : ChainComplex C ℕ ⥤ SimplicialObject C which shall be the inverse functor of the Dold-Kan equivalence in the case of abelian categories, and more generally pseudoabelian categories.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.FunctorN
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of functors N for the Dold-Kan correspondence
nodes.description: In this file, we construct functors N₁ : SimplicialObject C ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) and N₂ : Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) for any preadditive category C. (The indices of these functors are the number of occurrences of Karoubi at the source or the target.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.GammaCompN
nodes.descriptionTitle: The counit isomorphism of the Dold-Kan equivalence
nodes.description: The purpose of this file is to construct natural isomorphisms N₁Γ₀ : Γ₀ ⋙ N₁ ≅ toKaroubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) and N₂Γ₂ : Γ₂ ⋙ N₂ ≅ 𝟭 (Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ)).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Homotopies
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of homotopies for the Dold-Kan correspondence
nodes.description: (The general strategy of proof of the Dold-Kan correspondence is explained in Equivalence.lean.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.HomotopyEquivalence
nodes.descriptionTitle: The normalized Moore complex and the alternating face map complex are homotopy equivalent
nodes.description: In this file, when the category A is abelian, we obtain the homotopy equivalence homotopyEquivNormalizedMooreComplexAlternatingFaceMapComplex between the normalized Moore complex and the alternating face map complex of a simplicial object in A.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.NCompGamma
nodes.descriptionTitle: The unit isomorphism of the Dold-Kan equivalence
nodes.description: In order to construct the unit isomorphism of the Dold-Kan equivalence, we first construct natural transformations Γ₂N₁.natTrans : N₁ ⋙ Γ₂ ⟶ toKaroubi (SimplicialObject C) and Γ₂N₂.natTrans : N₂ ⋙ Γ₂ ⟶ 𝟭 (SimplicialObject C). It is then shown that Γ₂N₂.natTrans is an isomorphism by using that it becomes an isomorphism after the application of the functor N₂ : Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) which reflects isomorphisms.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.NReflectsIso
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that the functors N₁ : SimplicialObject C ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) and N₂ : Karoubi (SimplicialObject C) ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ) reflect isomorphisms for any preadditive category C.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Normalized
nodes.descriptionTitle: Comparison with the normalized Moore complex functor
nodes.description: In this file, we show that when the category A is abelian, there is an isomorphism N₁_iso_normalizedMooreComplex_comp_toKaroubi between the functor N₁ : SimplicialObject A ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex A ℕ) defined in FunctorN.lean and the composition of normalizedMooreComplex A with the inclusion ChainComplex A ℕ ⥤ Karoubi (ChainComplex A ℕ).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Notations
nodes.description: This file defines the notation K[X] : ChainComplex C ℕ for the alternating face map complex of (X : SimplicialObject C) where C is a preadditive category, as well as N[X] for the normalized subcomplex in the case C is an abelian category.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.PInfty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of the projection PInfty for the Dold-Kan correspondence
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the projection PInfty : K[X] ⟶ K[X] by passing to the limit the projections P q defined in Projections.lean. This projection is a critical tool in this formalisation of the Dold-Kan correspondence, because in the case of abelian categories, PInfty corresponds to the projection on the normalized Moore subcomplex, with kernel the degenerate subcomplex.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Projections
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of projections for the Dold-Kan correspondence
nodes.description: In this file, we construct endomorphisms P q : K[X] ⟶ K[X] for all q : ℕ. We study how they behave with respect to face maps with the lemmas HigherFacesVanish.of_P, HigherFacesVanish.comp_P_eq_self and comp_P_eq_self_iff.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.SplitSimplicialObject
nodes.descriptionTitle: Split simplicial objects in preadditive categories
nodes.description: In this file we define a functor nondegComplex : SimplicialObject.Split C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ when C is a preadditive category with finite coproducts, and get an isomorphism toKaroubiNondegComplexFunctorIsoN₁ : nondegComplex ⋙ toKaroubi _ ≅ forget C ⋙ DoldKan.N₁.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ExtraDegeneracy
nodes.descriptionTitle: Augmented simplicial objects with an extra degeneracy
nodes.description: In simplicial homotopy theory, in order to prove that the connected components of a simplicial set X are contractible, it suffices to construct an extra degeneracy as it is defined in Simplicial Homotopy Theory by Goerss-Jardine p. 190. It consists of a series of maps π₀ X → X _⦋0⦌ and X _⦋n⦌ → X _⦋n+1⦌ which behave formally like an extra degeneracy σ (-1). It can be thought as a datum associated to the augmented simplicial set X → π₀ X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.Basic
nodes.description: Given a topological space X, we can define the fundamental groupoid of X to be the category with objects being points of X, and morphisms x ⟶ y being paths from x to y, quotiented by homotopy equivalence. With this, the fundamental group of X based at x is just the automorphism group of x.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.FundamentalGroup
nodes.description: Given a topological space X and a basepoint x, the fundamental group is the automorphism group of x i.e. the group with elements being loops based at x (quotiented by homotopy equivalence).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.InducedMaps
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homotopic maps induce naturally isomorphic functors
nodes.description: between the induced functors f : π(X) ⥤ π(Y) and g : π(X) ⥤ π(Y), given a homotopy H : f ∼ g

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.PUnit
nodes.description: The fundamental groupoid of punit is naturally isomorphic to CategoryTheory.Discrete PUnit

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.Product
nodes.description: In this file, we give the following definitions/theorems:

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.SimplyConnected
nodes.description: This file defines simply connected spaces. A topological space is simply connected if its fundamental groupoid is equivalent to Unit.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Basic
nodes.description: We introduce a typeclass ModelCategory C expressing that C is equipped with classes of morphisms named "fibrations", "cofibrations" and "weak equivalences" which satisfy the axioms of (closed) model categories as they appear for example in Simplicial Homotopy Theory by Goerss and Jardine. We also provide an alternate constructor ModelCategory.mk' which uses a formulation of the axioms using weak factorization systems.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Bifibrant
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the full subcategories CofibrantObject C, FibrantObject C and BifibrantObject C of a model category C which respectively consist of cofibrant objects, fibrant objects, and bifibrant objects, where "bifibrant" means both cofibrant and fibrant.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.BifibrantObjectHomotopy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy category of bifibrant objects
nodes.description: We construct the homotopy category BifibrantObject.HoCat C of bifibrant objects in a model category C and show that the functor BifibrantObject.toHoCat : BifibrantObject C ⥤ BifibrantObject.HoCat C is a localization functor with respect to weak equivalences.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.BrownLemma
nodes.descriptionTitle: The factorization lemma by K. S. Brown
nodes.description: In a model category, any morphism f : X ⟶ Y between cofibrant objects can be factored as i ≫ p with i a cofibration and p a trivial fibration which has a section s that is a cofibration. In order to state this, we introduce a structure CofibrantBrownFactorization f with the data of such morphisms i, p and s with the expected properties, and show it is nonempty. Moreover, if f is a weak equivalence, then all the morphisms i, p and s are weak equivalences.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.CategoryWithCofibrations
nodes.descriptionTitle: Categories with classes of fibrations, cofibrations, weak equivalences
nodes.description: We introduce typeclasses CategoryWithFibrations, CategoryWithCofibrations and CategoryWithWeakEquivalences to express that a category C is equipped with classes of morphisms named "fibrations", "cofibrations" or "weak equivalences".

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.CofibrantObjectHomotopy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy category of cofibrant objects
nodes.description: Let C be a model category. By using the right homotopy relation, we introduce the homotopy category CofibrantObject.HoCat C of cofibrant objects in C, and we define a cofibrant resolution functor CofibrantObject.HoCat.resolution : C ⥤ CofibrantObject.HoCat C.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Cylinder
nodes.description: We introduce a notion of cylinder for an object A : C in a model category. It consists of an object I, a weak equivalence π : I ⟶ A equipped with two sections i₀ and i₁. This notion shall be important in the definition of "left homotopies" in model categories.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.DerivabilityStructureCofibrant
nodes.descriptionTitle: The left derivability structure attached to a model category
nodes.description: We show that the inclusion of the full subcategory of cofibrant objects in a model category is a left derivability structure. This is the dual to Corollaire 10.10 in the paper by Kahn and Maltsiniotis.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.DerivabilityStructureFibrant
nodes.descriptionTitle: The right derivability structure attached to a model category
nodes.description: We show that the inclusion of the full subcategory of fibrant objects in a model category is a right derivability structure. This is Corollaire 10.10 in the paper by Kahn and Maltsiniotis.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.FibrantObjectHomotopy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy category of fibrant objects
nodes.description: Let C be a model category. By using the left homotopy relation, we introduce the homotopy category FibrantObject.HoCat C of fibrant objects in C, and we define a fibrant resolution functor FibrantObject.HoCat.resolution : C ⥤ FibrantObject.HoCat C.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.FundamentalLemma
nodes.descriptionTitle: The fundamental lemma of homotopical algebra
nodes.description: Let C be a model category. Let L : C ⥤ H be a localization functor with respect to weak equivalences in C. We obtain the fundamental lemma of homotopical algebra: if X is cofibrant and Y fibrant, the map (X ⟶ Y) → (L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y) identifies L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y to the quotient of X ⟶ Y by the homotopy relation (in this case, the left and right homotopy relations coincide).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Homotopy
nodes.description: In this file, we relate left and right homotopies between morphisms X ⟶ Y in model categories. In particular, if X is cofibrant and Y is fibrant, these notions coincide (for arbitrary choices of good cylinders or good path objects).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Instances
nodes.description: In this file, we deduce basic properties of fibrations, cofibrations, and weak equivalences from the axioms of model categories.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.IsCofibrant
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fibrant and cofibrant objects in a model category
nodes.description: Once a category C has been endowed with a CategoryWithCofibrations C instance, it is possible to define the property IsCofibrant X for any X : C as an abbreviation for Cofibration (initial.to X : ⊥_ C ⟶ X). (Fibrant objects are defined similarly.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.JoyalTrick
nodes.description: In order to construct a model category, we may sometimes have basically proven all the axioms with the exception of the left lifting property of cofibrations with respect to trivial fibrations. A trick by Joyal allows to obtain this lifting property under suitable assumptions, namely that cofibrations are stable under composition and cobase change. (The dual result is also formalized.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.LeftHomotopy
nodes.description: We introduce the types Precylinder.LeftHomotopy and Cylinder.LeftHomotopy of homotopies between morphisms X ⟶ Y relative to a (pre)cylinder of X. Given two morphisms f and g, we introduce the relation LeftHomotopyRel f g asserting the existence of a cylinder object P and a left homotopy P.LeftHomotopy f g, and we define the quotient type LeftHomotopyClass X Y. We show that if X is a cofibrant object in a model category, then LeftHomotopyRel is an equivalence relation on X ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite of a model category structure
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Opposite.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: The model category structure on Over categories
nodes.description: Let C be a model category. For any S : C, we define a model category structure on the category Over S: a morphism X ⟶ Y in Over S is a cofibration (resp. a fibration, a weak equivalence) if the underlying morphism f.left : X.left ⟶ Y.left is. (Apart from the existence of (finite) limits from Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Basic, the verification of the axioms is straightforward.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.PathObject
nodes.description: We introduce a notion of path object for an object A : C in a model category. It consists of an object P, a weak equivalence ι : A ⟶ P equipped with two retractions p₀ and p₁. This notion shall be important in the definition of "right homotopies" in model categories.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.RightHomotopy
nodes.description: We introduce the types PrepathObject.RightHomotopy and PathObject.RightHomotopy of homotopies between morphisms X ⟶ Y relative to a (pre)path object of Y. Given two morphisms f and g, we introduce the relation RightHomotopyRel f g asserting the existence of a path object P and a right homotopy P.RightHomotopy f g, and we define the quotient type RightHomotopyClass X Y. We show that if Y is a fibrant object in a model category, then RightHomotopyRel is an equivalence relation on X ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory.Transport
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transport a model category via an equivalence
nodes.description: Given an equivalence of categories e : C ≌ D, we transport a model category structure on D in order to obtain a model category structure on C. More precisely, we assume that C has been equipped with notions of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences and that these properties of morphisms are the inverse images of the corresponding properties of morphisms by the functor e.functor : C ⥤ D. Under these assumptions, we show that the model category axioms for C hold if they hold for D.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.MooreComplex
nodes.description: We construct the normalized Moore complex, as a functor SimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ, for any abelian category C.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define quasicategories, a common model of infinity categories. We show that every Kan complex is a quasicategory.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.InnerFibration
nodes.description: Inner fibrations of simplicial sets are the morphisms in SSet which have the right lifting property with respect to all inner horn inclusions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.Nerve
nodes.descriptionTitle: The nerve of a category is a quasicategory
nodes.description: In AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.StrictSegal, we show that any strict Segal simplicial set is a quasicategory. In AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StrictSegal, we show that the nerve of a category satisfies the strict Segal condition.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.StrictBicategory
nodes.description: In this file we define a strict bicategory QCat.strictBicategory whose objects are quasicategories.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.StrictSegal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Strict Segal simplicial sets are quasicategories
nodes.description: In AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StrictSegal, we define the strict Segal condition on a simplicial set X. We say that X is strict Segal if its simplices are uniquely determined by their spine.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.TwoTruncated
nodes.description: We define 2-truncated quasicategories Quasicategory₂ by three horn-filling properties, and the left and right homotopy relations HomotopicL and HomotopicR on the edges in a 2-truncated simplicial set.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.RelativeCellComplex.AttachCells
nodes.description: Given a family of morphisms g a : A a ⟶ B a and a morphism f : X₁ ⟶ X₂, we introduce a structure AttachCells g f which expresses that X₂ is obtained from X₁ by attaching cells of the form g a. It means that there is a pushout diagram of the form In other words, the morphism f is a pushout of coproducts of morphisms of the form g a : A a ⟶ B a, see nonempty_attachCells_iff.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.RelativeCellComplex.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define a structure RelativeCellComplex which expresses that a morphism f : X ⟶ Y is a transfinite composition of morphisms, all of which consist in attaching cells. Here, we allow a different family of authorized cells at each step. For example, (relative) CW-complexes are defined in the file Mathlib/Topology/CWComplex/Abstract/Basic.lean by requiring that at the nth step, we attach n-disks along their boundaries.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Augmented.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the AugmentedSimplexCategory as the category obtained by adding an initial object to SimplexCategory (using CategoryTheory.WithInitial).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Augmented.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monoidal structure on the augmented simplex category
nodes.description: This file defines a monoidal structure on AugmentedSimplexCategory. The tensor product of objects is characterized by the fact that the initial object star is also the unit, and the fact that ⦋m⦌ ⊗ ⦋n⦌ = ⦋m + n + 1⦌ for n m : ℕ.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of the simplex category
nodes.description: In Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplexCategory/Defs.lean, we define the simplex category with objects ℕ and morphisms n ⟶ m the monotone maps from Fin (n + 1) to Fin (m + 1).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Defs
nodes.description: We construct a skeletal model of the simplex category, with an object ⦋n⦌ for each n : ℕ, and morphisms ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌ identify to monotone maps from Fin (n + 1) to Fin (m + 1).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.DeltaZeroIter
nodes.description: This file introduces morphisms δ₀Iter i and σ₀Iter i in the simplex category: they are obtained as the ith iteration of δ 0 or σ 0.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.GeneratorsRelations.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Presentation of the simplex category by generators and relations.
nodes.description: We introduce SimplexCategoryGenRel as the category presented by generating morphisms δ i : [n] ⟶ [n + 1] and σ i : [n + 1] ⟶ [n] and subject to the simplicial identities, and we provide induction principles for reasoning about objects and morphisms in this category.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.GeneratorsRelations.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Epi-mono factorization in the simplex category presented by generators and relations
nodes.description: This file aims to establish that there is a nice epi-mono factorization in SimplexCategoryGenRel. More precisely, we introduce two morphism properties P_δ and P_σ that single out morphisms that are compositions of δ i (resp. σ i).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.GeneratorsRelations.NormalForms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normal forms for morphisms in SimplexCategoryGenRel.
nodes.description: In this file, we establish that P_δ and P_σ morphisms in SimplexCategoryGenRel each admits a normal form.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of morphisms in the simplex category
nodes.description: In this file, we show that morphisms in the simplex category are generated by faces and degeneracies. This is stated by saying that if W : MorphismProperty SimplexCategory is multiplicative, and contains faces and degeneracies, then W = ⊤. This statement is deduced from a similar statement for the category SimplexCategory.Truncated d.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Rev
nodes.descriptionTitle: The covariant involution of the simplex category
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the functor rev : SimplexCategory ⥤ SimplexCategory which, via the equivalence between the simplex category and the category of nonempty finite linearly ordered types, corresponds to the covariant functor which sends a type α to αᵒᵈ.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.SemiSimplexCategory
nodes.description: We define a category SemiSimplexCategory so that semi-simplicial objects can be defined (TODO) as functors from SemiSimplexCategoryᵒᵖ similarly as simplicial objects are functors from SimplexCategory.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.ToMkOne
nodes.description: We define a bijective map SimplexCategory.toMk₁ : Fin (n + 2) → ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌. This is used in the file Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StdSimplexOne in the study of simplices in the simplicial set Δ[1].

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplexCategory.Truncated
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of the truncated simplex category
nodes.description: We prove that for n > 0, the inclusion functor from the n-truncated simplex category to the untruncated simplex category, and the inclusion functor from the n-truncated to the m-truncated simplex category, for n ≤ m are initial.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialCategory.Basic
nodes.description: A simplicial category is a category C that is enriched over the category of simplicial sets in such a way that morphisms in C identify to the 0-simplices of the enriched hom.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialCategory.SimplicialObject
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of simplicial objects is simplicial
nodes.description: In CategoryTheory.Functor.FunctorHom, it was shown that a category of functors C ⥤ D is enriched over a suitable category C ⥤ Type _ of functors to types.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialComplex.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define abstract simplicial complexes. An abstract simplicial complex is a downwards-closed collection of nonempty finite sets containing every singleton. These are defined first defining PreAbstractSimplicialComplex, which does not require the presence of singletons, and then defining AbstractSimplicialComplex as an extension.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialNerve
nodes.descriptionTitle: The simplicial nerve of a simplicial category
nodes.description: This file defines the simplicial nerve (sometimes called homotopy coherent nerve) of a simplicial category.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.Basic
nodes.description: A simplicial object in a category C is a C-valued presheaf on SimplexCategory. (Similarly, a cosimplicial object is a functor SimplexCategory ⥤ C.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.ChainHomotopy
nodes.description: Given a simplicial homotopy between morphisms of simplicial objects in a preadditive category, we construct a chain homotopy between the induced morphisms on the alternating face map complexes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.Coskeletal
nodes.description: The identity natural transformation exhibits a simplicial object X as a right extension of its restriction along (Truncated.inclusion n).op recorded by rightExtensionInclusion X n.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.DeltaZeroIter
nodes.description: This file introduces morphisms δ₀Iter i and σ₀Iter i for simplicial objects: they are obtained as the ith iteration of δ 0 or σ 0.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.Homotopy
nodes.description: This file defines the notion of a combinatorial simplicial homotopy between two morphisms of simplicial objects.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.II
nodes.descriptionTitle: A construction by Gabriel and Zisman
nodes.description: In this file, we construct a cosimplicial object SimplexCategory.II in SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, i.e. a functor SimplexCategory ⥤ SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ. If we identify SimplexCategory with the category of finite nonempty linearly ordered types, this functor could be interpreted as the contravariant functor which sends a finite nonempty linearly ordered type T to T →o Fin 2 (with f ≤ g ↔ ∀ i, g i ≤ f i, which turns out to be a linear order); in particular, it sends Fin (n + 1) to a linearly ordered type which is isomorphic...

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.Op
nodes.descriptionTitle: The covariant involution of the category of simplicial objects
nodes.description: In this file, we define the covariant involution SimplicialObject.opFunctor of the category of simplicial objects that is induced by the covariant involution SimplexCategory.rev : SimplexCategory ⥤ SimplexCategory.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialObject.Split
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the notion of split simplicial object. If C is a category that has finite coproducts, a splitting s : Splitting X of a simplicial object X in C consists of the datum of a sequence of objects s.N : ℕ → C (which we shall refer to as "nondegenerate simplices") and a sequence of morphisms s.ι n : s.N n → X _⦋n⦌ that have the property that a certain canonical map identifies X _⦋n⦌ with the coproduct of objects s.N i indexed by all possible epimorphisms ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋i⦌ in SimplexCategory.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Basic
nodes.description: Anodyne extensions form a property of morphisms in the category of simplicial sets. It contains horn inclusions and it is closed under coproducts, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Inner.Basic
nodes.description: Much of this file is mirrored from Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Basic.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.IsUniquelyCodimOneFace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Simplices that are uniquely codimensional one faces
nodes.description: Let X be a simplicial set. If x : X _⦋d⦌ and y : X _⦋d + 1⦌, we say that x is uniquely a 1-codimensional face of y if there exists a unique i : Fin (d + 2) such that X.δ i y = x. In this file, we extend this to a predicate IsUniquelyCodimOneFace involving two terms in the type X.S of simplices of X. This is used in the file Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/AnodyneExtensions/Pairing.lean for the study of strong (inner) anodyne extensions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Op
nodes.description: Let A be a subcomplex of a simplicial set X. If P is a pairing of A, we construct a pairing P.op for the subcomplex A.op of X.op.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Pairing
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the definition of a pairing for a subcomplex A of a simplicial set X, following the ideas by Sean Moss, Another approach to the Kan-Quillen model structure, who gave a complete combinatorial characterization of strong (inner) anodyne extensions. Strong (inner) anodyne extensions are transfinite compositions of pushouts of coproducts of (inner) horn inclusions, i.e. this is similar to (inner) anodyne extensions but without the stability property under retracts.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.PairingCore
nodes.descriptionTitle: Helper structure in order to construct pairings
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce a helper structure Subcomplex.PairingCore in order to construct a pairing for a subcomplex of a simplicial set. The main difference with Subcomplex.Pairing are that we provide an index type ι and a function dim : ι → ℕ which allow to parametrize type (II) and (I) simplices in such a way that, definitionally, their dimensions are respectively dim s or dim s + 1 for s : ι.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.Rank
nodes.description: We introduce types of (weak) rank functions for a pairing P of a subcomplex A of a simplicial set X. These are functions f : P.II → α such that P.AncestralRel x y implies f x < f y (in the weak case, we require this only under the additional condition that x and y are of the same dimension). Such rank functions are used in order to show that the ancestrality relation on P.II is well founded, i.e. that P is regular (when we already know P is proper).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.RankNat
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of a rank function to natural numbers
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if P : A.Pairing is a regular pairing of subcomplex A of a simplicial set X, then there exists a rank function for P with values in ℕ.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.AnodyneExtensions.RelativeCellComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The relative cell complex attached to a rank function for a pairing
nodes.description: Let A be a subcomplex of a simplicial set X. Let P : A.Pairing be a proper pairing (in the sense of Moss) and f : P.RankFunction ι be a rank function. We show that the inclusion A.ι is a relative cell complex with basic cells given by horn inclusions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Basic
nodes.description: A simplicial set is just a simplicial object in Type, i.e. a Type-valued presheaf on the simplex category.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Boundary
nodes.descriptionTitle: The boundary of the standard simplex
nodes.description: We introduce the boundary ∂Δ[n] of the standard simplex Δ[n]. (These notations become available by doing open Simplicial.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.CategoryWithFibrations
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cofibrations and fibrations in the category of simplicial sets
nodes.description: We endow SSet with CategoryWithCofibrations and CategoryWithFibrations instances. Cofibrations are monomorphisms, and fibrations are morphisms having the right lifting property with respect to horn inclusions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.CompStruct
nodes.description: Given a simplicial set X, we introduce two types: which is the type of 1-simplices with faces x₁ and x₀ respectively; e₀₂ : Edge x₀ x₂, a structure CompStruct e₀₁ e₁₂ e₀₂ which records the data of a 2-simplex with faces e₁₂, e₀₂ and e₀₁ respectively. This data will allow to obtain relations in the homotopy category of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.CompStructTruncated
nodes.descriptionTitle: Edges and "triangles" in truncated simplicial sets
nodes.description: Given a 2-truncated simplicial set X, we introduce two types: which is the type of 1-simplices with faces x₁ and x₀ respectively; e₀₂ : Edge x₀ x₂, a structure CompStruct e₀₁ e₁₂ e₀₂ which records the data of a 2-simplex with faces e₁₂, e₀₂ and e₀₁ respectively. This data will allow to obtain relations in the homotopy category of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Coskeletal
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that if X is StrictSegal then X is 2-coskeletal, i.e. X ≅ (cosk 2).obj X. In particular, nerves of categories are 2-coskeletal.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Degenerate
nodes.description: Given a simplicial set X and n : ℕ, we define the sets X.degenerate n and X.nonDegenerate n of degenerate or non-degenerate simplices of dimension n.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Dimension
nodes.description: For a simplicial set X and d : ℕ, we introduce a typeclass X.HasDimensionLT d saying that the dimension of X is < d, i.e. all nondegenerate simplices of X are of dimension < d.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Finite
nodes.description: A simplicial set is finite (SSet.Finite) if it has finitely many nondegenerate simplices.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.FiniteColimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite colimits of finite simplicial sets are finite
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.FiniteColimits.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.FiniteProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: A binary product of finite simplicial sets is finite
nodes.description: If X₁ and X₂ are respectively of dimensions ≤ d₁ and ≤ d₂, then X₁ ⊗ X₂ has dimension ≤ d₁ + d₂.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.HoFunctorMonoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy category functor is monoidal
nodes.description: Given 2-truncated simplicial sets X and Y, we introduce ad operation Truncated.Edge.tensor : Edge x x' → Edge y y' → Edge (x, y) (x', y'). We use this in order to construct an equivalence of categories (X ⊗ Y).HomotopyCategory ≌ X.HomotopyCategory × Y.HomotopyCategory.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Homology.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define the homology of simplicial sets. For any preadditive category C with coproducts of size w and any object R : C, the simplicial chain complex of a simplicial set X is denoted X.chainComplex R, and its homology in degree n : ℕ is X.homology R n.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Homology.HomologyZero
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homology of simplicial sets in degree 0
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is SSet.homology₀Iso which is an isomorphism X.homology R 0 ≅ ∐ (fun (_ : π₀ X) ↦ R) for any simplicial set X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Homology.HomotopyInvariance
nodes.description: This file proves that homotopic morphisms of simplicial sets induce the same maps on singular homology (with coefficients in an object R of a preadditive category C with coproducts).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Homology.Nondegenerate
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the normalized chain complex X.normalizedChainComplex R of a simplicial set X with coefficients in R (where R is an object of a preadditive category C with coproducts). The n-chains of this complex identify to the coproduct of copies of R indexed by the nondegenerate n-simplices of X. In particular, we deduce that the homology is zero in degree ≥ d when X has dimension < d.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Homotopy
nodes.description: In this file, we define the notion of homotopy (SSet.Homotopy) between morphisms f : X ⟶ Y and g : X ⟶ Y of simplicial sets: it involves a morphism X ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ Y inducing both f and g. (This definition is a particular case of SSet.RelativeMorphism.Homotopy that is defined in the file Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/RelativeMorphism.lean).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.HomotopyCat
nodes.descriptionTitle: The homotopy category of a simplicial set
nodes.description: The homotopy category of a simplicial set is defined as a quotient of the free category on its underlying reflexive quiver (equivalently its one truncation). The quotient imposes an additional hom relation on this free category, asserting that f ≫ g = h whenever f, g, and h are respectively the 2nd, 0th, and 1st faces of a 2-simplex.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Horn
nodes.description: This file introduces horns Λ[n, i].

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.HornColimits
nodes.description: In this file, we express horns as colimits: simplex of dimension n-1 (a dedicated API is provided for inner horns in Δ[3]).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.KanComplex
nodes.description: In this file, the abbreviation KanComplex is introduced for fibrant objects in the category SSet which is equipped with Kan fibrations.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.KanComplex.MulStruct
nodes.description: Given a simplicial set X, n : ℕ and x : X _⦋0⦌, we introduce the type X.PtSimplex n x of morphisms Δ[n] ⟶ X which send ∂Δ[n] to x. We introduce structures PtSimplex.RelStruct and PtSimplex.MulStruct which will be used in the definition of homotopy groups of Kan complexes.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The monoidal category structure on simplicial sets
nodes.description: This file defines an instance of chosen finite products for the category SSet. It follows from the fact the SSet if a category of functors to the category of types and that the category of types have chosen finite products. As a result, we obtain a monoidal category structure on SSet.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Monomorphisms
nodes.description: In this file, we show that the class of monomorphisms in SSet is stable under coproducts, pushouts, filtered colimits and transfinite compositions.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Nerve
nodes.description: This file provides the definition of the nerve of a category C, which is a simplicial set nerve C (see [goerss-jardine-2009], Example I.1.4). By definition, the type of n-simplices of nerve C is ComposableArrows C n, which is the category Fin (n + 1) ⥤ C.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.NerveAdjunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: The adjunction between the nerve and the homotopy category functor
nodes.description: We define an adjunction nerveAdjunction : hoFunctor ⊣ nerveFunctor between the functor that takes a simplicial set to its homotopy category and the functor that takes a category to its nerve.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.NerveNondegenerate
nodes.descriptionTitle: The nondegenerate simplices in the nerve of a partially ordered type
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if X is a partially ordered type, then an n-simplex s of the nerve is nondegenerate iff the monotone map s.obj : Fin (n + 1) → X is strictly monotone.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.NonDegenerateSimplices
nodes.descriptionTitle: The partially ordered type of non degenerate simplices of a simplicial set
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the partially ordered type X.N of non degenerate simplices of a simplicial set X. We obtain an embedding X.orderEmbeddingN : X.N ↪o X.Subcomplex which sends a non degenerate simplex to the subcomplex of X it generates.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.NonDegenerateSimplicesSubcomplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The type of nondegenerate simplices not in a subcomplex
nodes.description: In this file, given a subcomplex A of a simplicial set X, we introduce the type A.N of nondegenerate simplices of X that are not in A.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Nonempty
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Nonempty.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Nonsingular
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce a typeclass SSet.Nonsingular for a simplicial set X : SSet: it says that for any non-degenerate simplex x : X _⦋n⦌, the corresponding morphism Δ[n] ⟶ X is a monomorphism. This notion is useful in the context of the study of the subdivision functor (TODO @joelriou).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Op
nodes.descriptionTitle: The covariant involution of the category of simplicial sets
nodes.description: In this file, we define the covariant involution opFunctor : SSet ⥤ SSet of the category of simplicial sets that is induced by the covariant involution SimplexCategory.op : SimplexCategory ⥤ SimplexCategory. We use an abbreviation X.op for opFunctor.obj X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Path
nodes.description: A path in a simplicial set X of length n is a directed path comprised of n + 1 0-simplices and n 1-simplices, together with identifications between 0-simplices and the sources and targets of the 1-simplices. We define this construction first for truncated simplicial sets in SSet.Truncated.Path. A path in a simplicial set X is then defined as a 1-truncated path in the 1-truncation of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.PiZero
nodes.description: In this file, we define the type π₀ X of connected components of a simplicial sets. We also introduce typeclasses IsPreconnected X and IsConnected X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Presentable
nodes.description: In this file, we show that finite simplicial sets are finitely presentable, which will allow the use of the small object argument in SSet.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.ProdStdSimplex
nodes.description: In this file, we show that Δ[p] ⊗ Δ[q] identifies to the nerve of ULift (Fin (p + 1) × Fin (q + 1)). We relate the n-simplices of Δ[p] ⊗ Δ[q] to order preserving maps Fin (n + 1) →o Fin (p + 1) × Fin (q + 1), Via this bijection, a simplex in Δ[p] ⊗ Δ[q] is nondegenerate iff the corresponding monotone map Fin (n + 1) →o Fin (p + 1) × Fin (q + 1) is injective (or a strict mono).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.ProdStdSimplexOne
nodes.description: In this file, we define a bijection SSet.prodStdSimplex.nonDegenerateEquiv₁ between Fin (p + 1) and the type of nondegenerate (p + 1)-simplices of Δ[p] ⊗ Δ[1].

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.PushoutProduct
nodes.description: Results about pushout-products and pullback-homs in the category of simplicial sets.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.RegularEpi
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of simplicial sets is a regular epi category
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.RegularEpi.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.RelativeMorphism
nodes.description: Given two simplicial sets X and Y, and subcomplexes A of X, and B of Y, we introduce a type RelativeMorphism A B φ of morphisms X ⟶ Y which induce a given morphism of simplicial sets A ⟶ B. We define homotopies between these relative morphisms and introduce the quotient type of homotopy classes. This is used in the file Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/Homotopy.lean in order to define homotopies (SSet.Homotopy) between morphisms in the category of simplicial sets.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Simplices
nodes.descriptionTitle: The preordered type of simplices of a simplicial set
nodes.description: In this file, we define the type X.S of simplices of a simplicial set X, where a simplex consists of the data of dim : ℕ and simplex : X _⦋dim⦌. We endow this type with a preorder defined by x ≤ y ↔ Subcomplex.ofSimplex x.simplex ≤ Subcomplex.ofSimplex y.simplex. In particular, as a preordered type, X.S is a category, but this is not what is called "the category of simplices of X" in the literature (and which is X.Elementsᵒᵖ in mathlib).

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Skeleton
nodes.descriptionTitle: The skeleton of a simplicial set
nodes.description: In this file, we define the skeleton X.skeleton : ℕ →o X.Subcomplex of a simplicial set X. For any n : ℕ, X.skeleton n is the subcomplex of X that is generated by (non-degenerate) simplices of dimension < n.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Splitting
nodes.descriptionTitle: The splitting of a simplicial set
nodes.description: Let X be a simplicial set. The fact that any simplex x : X _⦋n⦌ can be written in a unique way as X.map f.op y for an epimorphism f : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌ and a nondegenerate simplex y : X _⦋m⦌ is translated in this file as the data of a splitting of X.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StdSimplex
nodes.description: We define the standard simplices Δ[n] as simplicial sets. See files SimplicialSet.Boundary and SimplicialSet.Horn for their boundaries ∂Δ[n] and horns Λ[n, i]. (The notations are available via open Simplicial.)

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StdSimplexOne
nodes.description: We define a bijection SSet.stdSimplex.objMk₁ between Fin (n + 2) and Δ[1] _⦋n⦌ for any n : ℕ.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StrictSegal
nodes.description: A simplicial set X satisfies the StrictSegal condition if for all n, the map X.spine n : X _⦋n⦌ → X.Path n is an equivalence, with equivalence inverse spineToSimplex {n : ℕ} : Path X n → X _⦋n⦌.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Subcomplex
nodes.description: Given a simplicial set X, this file defines the type X.Subcomplex of subcomplexes of X as an abbreviation for Subfunctor X. It also introduces a coercion from X.Subcomplex to SSet.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.SubcomplexColimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Colimits involving subcomplexes of a simplicial set
nodes.description: If X is a simplicial set, and we have subcomplexes A, U i (for i : ι) and V i j which satisfy Subcomplex.MulticoequalizerDiagram A U V (an abbreviation for CompleteLattice.MulticoequalizerDiagram), we show that the simplicial sset corresponding to A is the multicoequalizer of the U i along the V i j.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.SubcomplexEvaluation
nodes.description: We define an evaluation functor SSet.Subcomplex.evaluation : X.Subcomplex ⥤ Set (X.obj j) when X : SSet and j : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ. We use it to show that the functor Subcomplex.toSSetFunctor : X.Subcomplex ⥤ SSet preserves filtered colimits.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.SubcomplexOp
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.SubcomplexOp.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.Subdivision
