nodes.description: In this file, we define the subdivision functor sd : SSet ⥤ SSet and its right adjoint ex.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.TopAdj
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce some API in order to study the geometric realization functor (and its right adjoint the singular simplicial set functor): realization of Δ[n] and stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (n + 1)); the morphism corresponding to toTopObjIsoI.hom by adjunction.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SingularHomology.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define the singular chain complex and singular homology of a topological space. We also calculate the homology of a totally disconnected space as an example.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SingularHomology.HomologyZero
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is TopCat.singularHomology₀Iso which is an isomorphism ((singularHomologyFunctor C 0).obj R).obj X ≅ ∐ (fun (_ : ZerothHomotopy X) ↦ R) for any X : TopCat.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SingularHomology.HomotopyInvariance
nodes.description: In this file, we show that for any homotopy H : TopCat.Homotopy f g between two morphisms f : X ⟶ Y and g : X ⟶ Y in TopCat, the corresponding morphisms on the singular chain complexes are homotopic, and in particular the induced morphisms on singular homology are equal.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SingularHomology.HomotopyInvarianceTopCat
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.SingularSet
nodes.descriptionTitle: The singular simplicial set of a topological space and geometric realization of a simplicial set
nodes.description: The singular simplicial set TopCat.toSSet.obj X of a topological space X has n-simplices which identify to continuous maps stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (n + 1)) → X, where stdSimplex ℝ (Fin (n + 1)) is the standard topological n-simplex, defined as the subtype of Fin (n + 1) → ℝ consisting of functions f such that 0 ≤ f i for all i and ∑ i, f i = 1.

nodes.label: AlgebraicTopology.TopologicalSimplex
nodes.description: We define the natural functor from SimplexCategory to TopCat sending ⦋n⦌ to the topological n-simplex. This is used to define TopCat.toSSet in AlgebraicTopology.SingularSet.

nodes.label: Analysis.AbsoluteValue.Equivalence
nodes.description: Two absolute values v₁, v₂ : AbsoluteValue R ℝ are equivalent if there exists a positive real number c such that v₁ x ^ c = v₂ x for all x : R.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Basic
nodes.description: A function is analytic in one dimension around 0 if it can be written as a converging power series Σ pₙ zⁿ. This definition can be extended to any dimension (even in infinite dimension) by requiring that pₙ is a continuous n-multilinear map. In general, pₙ is not unique (in two dimensions, taking p₂ (x, y) (x', y') = x y' or y x' gives the same map when applied to a vector (x, y) (x, y)).

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Binomial
nodes.description: This file introduces the binomial series: $$ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \; \binom{a}{k} \; x^k = 1 + a x + \frac{a(a-1)}{2!} x^2 + \frac{a(a-1)(a-2)}{3!} x^3 + \cdots $$ where $a$ is an element of a normed field $\mathbb{K}$, and $x$ is an element of a normed algebra over $\mathbb{K}$.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.CPolynomial
nodes.description: We expand the API around continuously polynomial functions. Notably, we show that this class is stable under the usual operations (addition, subtraction, negation).

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.CPolynomialDef
nodes.description: Let p be a formal multilinear series from E to F, i.e., p n is a multilinear map on E^n for n : ℕ, and let f be a function from E to F.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.ChangeOrigin
nodes.descriptionTitle: Changing origin in a power series
nodes.description: If a function is analytic in a disk D(x, R), then it is analytic in any disk contained in that one. Indeed, one can write $$ f (x + y + z) = \sum_{n} p_n (y + z)^n = \sum_{n, k} \binom{n}{k} p_n y^{n-k} z^k = \sum_{k} \Bigl(\sum_{n} \binom{n}{k} p_n y^{n-k}\Bigr) z^k. $$ The corresponding power series has thus a k-th coefficient equal to $\sum_{n} \binom{n}{k} p_n y^{n-k}$.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Composition
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the composition of analytic functions is analytic.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Various ways to combine analytic functions
nodes.description: We show that the following are analytic:

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.ConvergenceRadius
nodes.descriptionTitle: Radius of convergence of a power series
nodes.description: This file introduces the notion of the radius of convergence of a power series.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Inverse
nodes.description: We construct the left and right inverse of a formal multilinear series with invertible linear term, we prove that they coincide and study their properties (notably convergence). We deduce that the inverse of an analytic open partial homeomorphism is analytic.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.IsolatedZeros
nodes.description: This file proves the fact that the zeros of a non-constant analytic function of one variable are isolated. It also introduces a little bit of API in the HasFPowerSeriesAt namespace that is useful in this setup.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.IteratedFDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: The iterated derivative of an analytic function
nodes.description: If a function is analytic, written as f (x + y) = ∑ pₙ (y, ..., y) then its n-th iterated derivative at x is given by (v₁, ..., vₙ) ↦ ∑ pₙ (v_{σ (1)}, ..., v_{σ (n)}) where the sum is over all permutations of {1, ..., n}. In particular, it is symmetric.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Linear
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a ContinuousLinearMap defines an analytic function with the formal power series f x = f a + f (x - a). We also prove similar results for bilinear maps.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.OfScalars
nodes.description: This file contains API for analytic functions ∑ cᵢ • xⁱ defined in terms of scalars c₀, c₁, c₂, ….

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Order
nodes.description: This file defines the order of vanishing of an analytic function f at a point z₀, as an element of ℕ∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.Polynomial
nodes.description: This file combines the analysis and algebra libraries and shows that evaluation of a polynomial is an analytic function.

nodes.label: Analysis.Analytic.RadiusLiminf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Representation of FormalMultilinearSeries.radius as a liminf
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the radius of convergence of a FormalMultilinearSeries is equal to $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt[n]{‖p n‖}}$. This lemma can't go to Analysis.Analytic.Basic because this would create a circular dependency once we redefine exp using FormalMultilinearSeries.

nodes.label: Analysis.Asymptotics.Theta

nodes.description: In this file we prove basic properties of the equivalence relation given by f =Θ[l] g ↔ f =O[l] g ∧ g =O[l] f.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoundedVariation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Almost everywhere differentiability of functions with locally bounded variation
nodes.description: In this file we show that a bounded variation function is differentiable almost everywhere. This implies that Lipschitz functions from the real line into finite-dimensional vector space are also differentiable almost everywhere.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrals of Riemann, Henstock-Kurzweil, and McShane
nodes.description: In this file we define the integral of a function over a box in ℝⁿ. The same definition works for Riemann, Henstock-Kurzweil, and McShane integrals.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Box.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define rectangular boxes in ℝⁿ. As usual, we represent ℝⁿ as the type of functions ι → ℝ (usually ι = Fin n for some n). When we need to interpret a box [l, u] as a set, we use the product {x | ∀ i, l i < x i ∧ x i ≤ u i} of half-open intervals (l i, u i]. We exclude l i because this way boxes of a partition are disjoint as sets in ℝⁿ.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Box.SubboxInduction
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following induction principle for BoxIntegral.Box, see BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on. Let p be a predicate on BoxIntegral.Box ι, let I be a box. Suppose that the following two properties hold true.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.DivergenceTheorem
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Divergence Theorem for a Henstock-Kurzweil style integral. The theorem says the following. Let f : ℝⁿ → Eⁿ be a function differentiable on a closed rectangular box I with derivative f' x : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] Eⁿ at x ∈ I. Then the divergence fun x ↦ ∑ k, f' x eₖ k, where eₖ = Pi.single k 1 is the k-th basis vector, is integrable on I, and its integral is equal to the sum of integrals of f over the faces of I taken with appropriate signs.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Integrability
nodes.description: In this file we prove that any Bochner integrable function is McShane integrable (hence, it is Henstock and GP integrable) with the same integral. The proof is based on Russel A. Gordon, The integrals of Lebesgue, Denjoy, Perron, and Henstock.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Additive
nodes.description: We say that a function f : Box ι → M from boxes in ℝⁿ to a commutative additive monoid M is box additive on subboxes of I₀ : WithTop (Box ι) if for any box J, ↑J ≤ I₀, and a partition π of J, f J = ∑ J' ∈ π.boxes, f J'. We use I₀ : WithTop (Box ι) instead of I₀ : Box ι to use the same definition for functions box additive on subboxes of a box and for functions box additive on all boxes.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Partitions of rectangular boxes in ℝⁿ
nodes.description: In this file we define (pre)partitions of rectangular boxes in ℝⁿ. A partition of a box I in ℝⁿ (see BoxIntegral.Prepartition and BoxIntegral.Prepartition.IsPartition) is a finite set of pairwise disjoint boxes such that their union is exactly I. We use boxes : Finset (Box ι) to store the set of boxes.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Filter
nodes.description: First we define a structure BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams. This structure will be used as an argument in the definition of BoxIntegral.integral in order to use the same definition for a few well-known definitions of integrals based on partitions of a rectangular box into subboxes (Riemann integral, Henstock-Kurzweil integral, and McShane integral).

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Measure
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few simple facts about rectangular boxes, partitions, and measures:

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Split
nodes.descriptionTitle: Split a box along one or more hyperplanes
nodes.description: A hyperplane {x : ι → ℝ | x i = a} splits a rectangular box I : BoxIntegral.Box ι into two smaller boxes. If a ∉ Ioo (I.lower i, I.upper i), then one of these boxes is empty, so it is not a box in the sense of BoxIntegral.Box.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.SubboxInduction
nodes.description: In this file we prove (see BoxIntegral.Box.exists_taggedPartition_isHenstock_isSubordinate_homothetic) that for every box I in ℝⁿ and a function r : ℝⁿ → ℝ positive on I there exists a tagged partition π of I such that

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.Partition.Tagged
nodes.description: A tagged (pre)partition is a (pre)partition π enriched with a tagged point for each box of π. For simplicity we require that the function BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.tag is defined on all boxes J : Box ι but use its values only on boxes of the partition. Given π : BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition I, we require that each BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition π J belongs to BoxIntegral.Box.Icc I. If for every J ∈ π, π.tag J belongs to J.Icc, then π is called a Henstock partition.

nodes.label: Analysis.BoxIntegral.UnitPartition
nodes.description: Fix n a positive integer. BoxIntegral.unitPartition.box are boxes in ι → ℝ obtained by dividing the unit box uniformly into boxes of side length 1 / n and translating the boxes by vectors ν : ι → ℤ.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ApproximateUnit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nonnegative contractions in a C⋆-algebra form an approximate unit
nodes.description: This file shows that the collection of positive contractions (of norm strictly less than one) in a possibly non-unital C⋆-algebra form a directed set. The key step uses the continuous functional calculus applied with the functions fun x : ℝ≥0, 1 - (1 + x)⁻¹ and fun x : ℝ≥0, x (1 - x)⁻¹, which are inverses on the interval {x : ℝ≥0 | x < 1}.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Basic
nodes.description: A normed star group is a normed group with a compatible star which is isometric.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.CStarMatrix
nodes.descriptionTitle: Matrices with entries in a C⋆-algebra
nodes.description: This file creates a type copy of Matrix m n A called CStarMatrix m n A meant for matrices with entries in a C⋆-algebra A. Its action on C⋆ᵐᵒᵈ (n → A) (via Matrix.mulVec) gives it the operator norm, and this norm makes CStarMatrix n n A a C⋆-algebra.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Classes
nodes.description: This file defines classes for complex C⋆-algebras. These are (unital or non-unital, commutative or noncommutative) Banach algebra over ℂ with an antimultiplicative conjugate-linear involution (star) satisfying the C⋆-identity ∥star x x∥ = ∥x∥ ^ 2.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.CompletelyPositiveMap
nodes.description: A linear map φ : A₁ →ₗ[ℂ] A₂ (where A₁ and A₂ are C⋆-algebras) is called completely positive (CP) if CStarMatrix.map (Fin k) (Fin k) φ (i.e. applying φ to all entries of a k × k matrix) is also positive for every k : ℕ.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we construct the continuousFunctionalCalculus for a normal element a of a (unital) C⋆-algebra over ℂ. This is a star algebra equivalence C(spectrum ℂ a, ℂ) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] elemental ℂ a which sends the (restriction of) the identity map ContinuousMap.id ℂ to the (unique) preimage of a under the coercion of elemental ℂ a to A.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Commute
nodes.descriptionTitle: Commuting with applications of the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file shows that if an element b commutes with both a and star a, then it commutes with cfc f a (or cfcₙ f a). In the case where a is selfadjoint, we may reduce the hypotheses.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Continuity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuity of the continuous functional calculus in each variable
nodes.description: The continuous functional calculus is a map which takes a pair a : A (A is a C⋆-algebra) and a function f : C(spectrum R a, R) where a satisfies some predicate p, depending on R and returns another element of the algebra A. This is the map cfcHom. The class ContinuousFunctionalCalculus declares that cfcHom is a continuous map from C(spectrum R a, R) to A.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Instances
nodes.descriptionTitle: Instances of the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: selfadjoint elements in a ℂ-algebra with a continuous functional calculus for normal elements and where every element has compact spectrum. In particular, this includes unital C⋆-algebras over ℂ. elements in an ℝ-algebra with a continuous functional calculus for selfadjoint elements, where every element has compact spectrum, and where nonnegative elements have nonnegative spectrum. In particular, this includes unital C⋆-algebras over ℝ.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrals and the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file gives results about integrals of the form ∫ x, cfc (f x) a. Most notably, we show that the integral commutes with the continuous functional calculus under appropriate conditions.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Isometric
nodes.description: This file adds a class for an isometric continuous functional calculus. This is separate from the usual ContinuousFunctionalCalculus class because we prefer not to require a metric (or a norm) on the algebra for reasons discussed in the module documentation for that file.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.NonUnital
nodes.descriptionTitle: The continuous functional calculus for non-unital algebras
nodes.description: This file defines a generic API for the continuous functional calculus in non-unital algebras which is suitable in a wide range of settings. The design is intended to match as closely as possible that for unital algebras in Mathlib/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/ContinuousFunctionalCalculus/Unital.lean. Changes to either file should be mirrored in its counterpart whenever possible. The underlying reasons for the design decisions in the unital case apply equally in the non-unital case.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Documentation concerning the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: A library note giving advice on developing and using the continuous functional calculus, as well as the organizational structure within Mathlib.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Facts about star-ordered rings that depend on the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file contains various basic facts about star-ordered rings (i.e. mainly C⋆-algebras) that depend on the continuous functional calculus.

nodes.descriptionTitle: The continuous functional calculus on product types

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Unique
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniqueness of the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: Let s : Set 𝕜 be compact where 𝕜 is either ℝ or ℂ. By the Stone-Weierstrass theorem, the (star) subalgebra generated by polynomial functions on s is dense in C(s, 𝕜). Moreover, this star subalgebra is generated by X : 𝕜[X] (i.e., ContinuousMap.restrict s (.id 𝕜)) alone. Consequently, any continuous star 𝕜-algebra homomorphism with domain C(s, 𝕜), is uniquely determined by its value on X : 𝕜[X].

nodes.descriptionTitle: The exponential map from selfadjoint to unitary
nodes.description: In this file, we establish various properties related to the map fun a ↦ NormedSpace.exp ℂ A (I • a) between the subtypes selfAdjoint A and unitary A.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Extreme
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extreme points of the closed unit ball in C⋆-algebras
nodes.description: This file contains results on the extreme points of the closed unit ball in (unital) C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Fuglede
nodes.description: Let A be a C⋆-algebra, and let a b x : A. The Fuglede–Putnam–Rosenblum theorem states that if a and b are normal and x intertwines a and b (i.e., SemiconjBy x a b, that is, x a = b x), then x also intertwines star a and star b. Fuglede's original result [fuglede1950] was for a = b (i.e., if x commutes with a, then x also commutes with star a), and Putnam [putnam1951] extended it to intertwining elements.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.GelfandDuality
nodes.description: The gelfandTransform is an algebra homomorphism from a topological 𝕜-algebra A to C(characterSpace 𝕜 A, 𝕜). In the case where A is a commutative complex Banach algebra, then the Gelfand transform is actually spectrum-preserving (spectrum.gelfandTransform_eq). Moreover, when A is a commutative C⋆-algebra over ℂ, then the Gelfand transform is a surjective isometry, and even an equivalence between C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.GelfandNaimarkSegal
nodes.description: This file contains the constructions and definitions that produce a ⋆-homomorphism from an arbitrary C⋆-algebra into the algebra of bounded linear operators on an appropriately constructed Hilbert space.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Hom
nodes.description: Here we collect properties of C⋆-algebra homomorphisms.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Matrix
nodes.descriptionTitle: Analytic properties of the star operation on matrices
nodes.description: This transports the operator norm on EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m to Matrix m n 𝕜. See the file Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix.lean for many other matrix norms.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Module.Constructions
nodes.description: In this file we define the following constructions of CStarModules where A denotes a C⋆-algebra. For some of the types listed below, the instance is declared on the type synonym WithCStarModule E (with the notation C⋆ᵐᵒᵈ E), instead of on E itself; we explain the reasoning behind each decision below.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Module.Defs
nodes.description: A Hilbert C⋆-module is a complex module E together with a right A-module structure, where A is a C⋆-algebra, and with an A-valued inner product. This inner product satisfies the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and induces a norm that makes E a normed vector space over ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Module.Synonym
nodes.descriptionTitle: Type synonym for types with a CStarModule structure
nodes.description: It is often the case that we want to construct a CStarModule instance on a type that is already endowed with a norm, but this norm is not the one associated to its CStarModule structure. For this reason, we create a type synonym WithCStarModule which is endowed with the requisite CStarModule instance. We also introduce the scoped notation C⋆ᵐᵒᵈ for this type synonym.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Multiplier
nodes.description: Define the multiplier algebra of a C⋆-algebra as the algebra (over 𝕜) of double centralizers, for which we provide the localized notation 𝓜(𝕜, A). A double centralizer is a pair of continuous linear maps L R : A →L[𝕜] A satisfying the intertwining condition R x y = x L y.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.PositiveLinearMap
nodes.description: This file develops the API for positive linear maps over C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Projection
nodes.description: Here we collect results about projections specific to C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.SpecialFunctions.PosPart
nodes.descriptionTitle: C⋆-algebraic facts about a⁺ and a⁻.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Spectrum
nodes.description: In this file, we establish various properties related to the spectrum of elements in C⋆-algebras. In particular, we show that the spectrum of a unitary element is contained in the unit circle in ℂ, the spectrum of a selfadjoint element is real, the spectral radius of a selfadjoint element or normal element is its norm, among others.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Unitary.Connected
nodes.descriptionTitle: The unitary group in a unital C⋆-algebra is locally path connected
nodes.description: When A is a unital C⋆-algebra and u : unitary A is a unitary element whose distance to 1 is less that 2, the spectrum of u is contained in the slit plane, so the principal branch of the logarithm is continuous on the spectrum of u (or equivalently, Complex.arg is continuous on the spectrum). The continuous functional calculus can then be used to define a selfadjoint element x such that u = exp (I • x).

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Unitary.Maps
nodes.description: This file defines some basic maps by unitaries in C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Unitary.Span
nodes.description: combination of four unitary elements, and the norm of each coefficient does not exceed ‖x‖ / 2.

nodes.label: Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Unitization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The minimal unitization of a C⋆-algebra
nodes.description: This file shows that when E is a C⋆-algebra (over a densely normed field 𝕜), that the minimal Unitization is as well. In order to ensure that the norm structure is available, we must first show that every C⋆-algebra is a RegularNormedAlgebra.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.AbsolutelyMonotone
nodes.description: A function f : ℝ → ℝ is absolutely monotone on a set s if its iterated derivatives are all nonnegative on s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.AddTorsor.AffineMap

nodes.description: A smooth bump function is an infinitely smooth function f : E → ℝ supported on a ball that is equal to 1 on a ball of smaller radius.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Convolution
nodes.description: In this file we prove lemmas about convolutions (φ.normed μ ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, μ] g) x₀, where φ : ContDiffBump 0 is a smooth bump function.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.FiniteDimension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bump functions in finite-dimensional vector spaces
nodes.description: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space. We show that any open set s in E is exactly the support of a smooth function taking values in [0, 1], in IsOpen.exists_contDiff_support_eq.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.InnerProduct
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smooth bump functions in inner product spaces
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a real inner product space has smooth bump functions, see hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed
nodes.description: In this file we define ContDiffBump.normed f μ to be the bump function f normalized so that ∫ x, f.normed μ x ∂μ = 1 and prove some properties of this function.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.SmoothApprox
nodes.descriptionTitle: Density of smooth functions in the space of continuous functions
nodes.description: In this file we prove that smooth functions are dense in the set of continuous functions from a real finite-dimensional vector space to a Banach space, see ContinuousMap.dense_setOf_contDiff. We also prove several unbundled versions of this statement.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Conformal.InnerProduct
nodes.descriptionTitle: Conformal maps between inner product spaces
nodes.description: A function between inner product spaces which has a derivative at x is conformal at x iff the derivative preserves inner products up to a scalar multiple.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Conformal.NormedSpace
nodes.description: A continuous linear map between real normed spaces X and Y is ConformalAt some point x if it is real differentiable at that point and its differential is a conformal linear map.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Basic
nodes.description: This file continues the development of the API for ContDiff, ContDiffAt, etc, covering constants, products, composition with linear maps, etc.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds
nodes.description: norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le gives the bound n! C D ^ n for the n-th derivative of g ∘ f assuming that the derivatives of g are bounded by C and the i-th derivative of f is bounded by D ^ i.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.CPolynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Higher smoothness of continuously polynomial functions
nodes.description: We prove that continuously polynomial functions are C^∞. In particular, this is the case of continuous multilinear maps.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Comp
nodes.description: We prove that the composition of C^n functions is C^n. We also expand the API around C^n functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Convolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of a convolution of functions
nodes.description: Criteria for a convolution of functions to be differentiable.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
nodes.description: A function is C^1 on a domain if it is differentiable there, and its derivative is continuous. By induction, it is C^n if it is C^{n-1} and its (n-1)-th derivative is C^1 there or, equivalently, if it is C^1 and its derivative is C^{n-1}. It is C^∞ if it is C^n for all n. Finally, it is C^ω if it is analytic (as well as all its derivative, which is automatic if the space is complete).

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Deriv
nodes.description: The general theory of higher derivatives in Mathlib is developed using the Fréchet derivative fderiv; but for maps defined on the field, the one-dimensional derivative deriv is often easier to use. In this file, we reformulate some higher smoothness results in terms of deriv.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.FTaylorSeries
nodes.description: In this file, we define iteratively the n+1-th derivative of a function as the derivative of the n-th derivative. It is called iteratedFDeriv 𝕜 n f x where 𝕜 is the field, n is the number of iterations, f is the function and x is the point, and it is given as an n-multilinear map. We also define a version iteratedFDerivWithin relative to a domain. Note that, in domains, there may be several choices of possible derivative, so we make some arbitrary choice in the definition.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.FaaDiBruno
nodes.description: The Faa di Bruno formula gives the iterated derivative of g ∘ f in terms of those of g and f. It is expressed in terms of partitions I of {0, ..., n-1}. For such a partition, denote by k its number of parts, write the parts as I₀, ..., Iₖ₋₁ ordered so that max I₀ < ... < max Iₖ₋₁, and let iₘ be the number of elements of Iₘ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Polynomial

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.DSlope
nodes.description: Given a function f : 𝕜 → E from a nontrivially normed field to a normed space over this field, dslope f a b is defined as slope f a b = (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b - f a) for a ≠ b and as deriv f a for a = b.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Darboux
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the derivative of a differentiable function on an interval takes all intermediate values. The proof is based on the Wikipedia) page about this theorem.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Abs
nodes.description: This file compiles basic derivability properties of the absolute value, and is largely inspired from Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Calculus.lean, which is the analogous file for norms derived from an inner product space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Add
nodes.description: In this file we prove formulas about derivatives of f + g, -f, f - g, and ∑ i, f i x for functions from the base field to a normed space over this field.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.AffineMap
nodes.description: In this file we prove formulas for one-dimensional derivatives of affine maps f : 𝕜 →ᵃ[𝕜] E. We also specialise some of these results to AffineMap.lineMap because it is useful to transfer MVT from dimension 1 to a domain in higher dimension.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the derivative of a function f : 𝕜 → F where 𝕜 is a normed field and F is a normed space over this field. The derivative of such a function f at a point x is given by an element f' : F.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Comp
nodes.descriptionTitle: One-dimensional derivatives of compositions of functions
nodes.description: In this file we prove the chain rule for the following cases:

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.CompMul
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the derivative of fun x ↦ f (c x) equals c times the derivative of f evaluated at c x.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Inv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of x ↦ x⁻¹ and f x / g x
nodes.description: In this file we prove (x⁻¹)' = -1 / x ^ 2, ((f x)⁻¹)' = -f' x / (f x) ^ 2, and (f x / g x)' = (f' x g x - f x g' x) / (g x) ^ 2 for different notions of derivative.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Inverse
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inverse function theorem - the easy half
nodes.description: In this file we prove that g' (f x) = (f' x)⁻¹ provided that f is strictly differentiable at x, f' x ≠ 0, and g is a local left inverse of f that is continuous at f x. This is the easy half of the inverse function theorem: the harder half states that g exists.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Linear
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of continuous linear maps from the base field
nodes.description: In this file we prove that f : 𝕜 →L[𝕜] E (or f : 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] E) has derivative f 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
nodes.description: In this file we prove Cauchy's and Lagrange's mean value theorems, and deduce some corollaries.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Mul
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative of f x g x
nodes.description: In this file we prove formulas for (f x g x)' and (f x • g x)'.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Pi
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Pi.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
nodes.description: In this file we prove that derivatives of polynomials in the analysis sense agree with their derivatives in the algebraic sense.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Pow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative of (f x) ^ n, n : ℕ
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the Fréchet derivative of fun x => f x ^ n, where n is a natural number, is n f x ^ (n - 1) f'. Additionally, we prove the case for non-commutative rings (with primed names like deriv_pow'), where the result is instead ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f x ^ (n.pred - i) f' f x ^ i.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Prod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of functions taking values in product types
nodes.description: In this file we prove lemmas about derivatives of functions f : 𝕜 → E × F and of functions f : 𝕜 → (Π i, E i).

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Shift
nodes.descriptionTitle: Invariance of the derivative under translation
nodes.description: We show that if a function f has derivative f' at a point a + x, then f (a + ·) has derivative f' at x. Similarly for x + a.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Slope
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative as the limit of the slope
nodes.description: In this file we relate the derivative of a function with its definition from a standard undergraduate course as the limit of the slope (f y - f x) / (y - x) as y tends to 𝓝[≠] x. Since we are talking about functions taking values in a normed space instead of the base field, we use slope f x y = (y - x)⁻¹ • (f y - f x) instead of division.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Star
nodes.description: This file contains the usual formulas (and existence assertions) for the derivative of the star operation.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Support
nodes.descriptionTitle: Support of the derivative of a function
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the (topological) support of a function includes the support of its derivative. As a corollary, we show that the derivative of a function with compact support has compact support.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.ZPow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of x ^ m, m : ℤ
nodes.description: In this file we prove theorems about (iterated) derivatives of x ^ m, m : ℤ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.DerivativeTest
nodes.description: We prove the first-derivative test from calculus, in the strong form given on Wikipedia.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.DiffContOnCl
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions differentiable on a domain and continuous on its closure
nodes.description: Many theorems in complex analysis assume that a function is complex differentiable on a domain and is continuous on its closure. In this file we define a predicate DiffContOnCl that expresses this property and prove basic facts about this predicate.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.DifferentialForm.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Exterior derivative of a differential form on a normed space
nodes.description: In this file we define the exterior derivative of a differential form on a normed space. Under certain smoothness assumptions, we prove that this operation is linear in the form and the second exterior derivative of a form is zero.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.DifferentialForm.VectorField
nodes.descriptionTitle: Evaluation of the derivative of differential forms on vector fields
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following formula and its corollaries. If ω is a differentiable k-form and V i are k + 1 differentiable vector fields, then

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Add
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Affine
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of continuous affine maps
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Analytic
nodes.description: A function expressible as a power series at a point has a Fréchet derivative there. Also the special case in terms of deriv when the domain is 1-dimensional.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
nodes.description: Let E and F be normed spaces, f : E → F, and f' : E →L[𝕜] F a continuous 𝕜-linear map, where 𝕜 is a non-discrete normed field. Then

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Bilinear
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of bounded bilinear maps
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Comp
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of a composition (chain rule)
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.CompCLM
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Congr
nodes.description: Lemmas about congruence properties of the Fréchet derivative under change of function, set, etc.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Const
nodes.description: This file contains the usual formulas (and existence assertions) for the derivative of constant functions, including various special cases such as the functions 0, 1, Nat.cast n, Int.cast z, and other numerals.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.ContinuousAlternatingMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of operations on continuous alternating maps
nodes.description: In this file we prove formulas for the derivatives of

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.ContinuousMultilinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of operations on continuous multilinear maps
nodes.description: depending on a parameter x : E.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Defs
nodes.description: Let E and F be normed spaces, f : E → F, and f' : E →L[𝕜] F a continuous 𝕜-linear map, where 𝕜 is a non-discrete normed field. Then

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Equiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of a linear equivalence
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Extend
nodes.description: We investigate how differentiable functions inside a set extend to differentiable functions on the boundary. For this, it suffices that the function and its derivative admit limits there. A general version of this statement is given in hasFDerivWithinAt_closure_of_tendsto_fderiv.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Linear
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of bounded linear maps
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Measurable
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the derivative of any function with complete codomain is a measurable function. Namely, we prove:

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Mul
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Norm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of the norm in a real normed vector space
nodes.description: This file provides basic results about the differentiability of the norm in a real vector space. Most are of the following kind: if the norm has some differentiability property (DifferentiableAt, ContDiffAt, HasStrictFDerivAt, HasFDerivAt) at x, then so it has at t • x when t ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.OfCompLeft
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the following theorem. Consider three functions f : F → G, g : E → F, and h : E → G, together with "candidate derivatives" f' : F →L[𝕜] G, g' : E →L[𝕜] F, and h' : E →L[𝕜] G. Suppose that

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Partial
nodes.description: Results in this file relate the partial derivatives of a bivariate function to its differentiability in the product space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Pi
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Pi.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Pow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fréchet Derivative of f x ^ n, n : ℕ
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the Fréchet derivative of fun x => f x ^ n, where n is a natural number, is n • f x ^ (n - 1)) • f'. Additionally, we prove the case for non-commutative rings (with primed names like fderiv_pow'), where the result is instead ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, f x ^ (n.pred - i) •> f' <• f x ^ i.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Prod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative of the Cartesian product of functions
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.RestrictScalars
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of the scalar restriction of a linear map
nodes.description: For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Star
nodes.description: This file contains the usual formulas (and existence assertions) for the Fréchet derivative of the star operation. For detailed documentation of the Fréchet derivative, see the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric
nodes.description: We show that, over the reals, the second derivative is symmetric.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.WithLp
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.WithLp.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.FormalMultilinearSeries
nodes.description: In this file we define FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F to be a family of n-multilinear maps for all n, designed to model the sequence of derivatives of a function. In other files we use this notion to define C^n functions (called contDiff in mathlib) and analytic functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
nodes.description: Let f be a function from a Hilbert Space F to 𝕜 (𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ), x be a point in F and f' be a vector in F. Then

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Implicit
nodes.description: We prove three versions of the implicit function theorem. First we define a structure ImplicitFunctionData that holds arguments for the most general version of the implicit function theorem, see ImplicitFunctionData.implicitFunction and ImplicitFunctionData.hasStrictFDerivAt_implicitFunction. This version allows a user to choose a specific implicit function but provides only a little convenience over the inverse function theorem.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ImplicitContDiff
nodes.description: In this file, we apply the generalised implicit function theorem to the more familiar case and show that the implicit function preserves the smoothness class of the implicit equation.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ImplicitFunction.Bivariate
nodes.description: This specialization of the implicit function theorem applies to a curried bivariate function f : E₁ → E₂ → F and assumes continuity of both its partial derivatives at u : E₁ × E₂ as well as invertibility of f₂ u.1 u.2 : E₂ →L[𝕜] F its partial derivative with respect to the second argument.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ImplicitFunction.ProdDomain
nodes.descriptionTitle: Implicit function theorem — domain a product space
nodes.description: This specialization of the implicit function theorem applies to an uncurried bivariate function f : E₁ × E₂ → F and assumes strict differentiability of f at u : E₁ × E₂ as well as invertibility of f₂u : E₂ →L[𝕜] F its partial derivative with respect to the second argument.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.Analytic
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.Analytic.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.ApproximatesLinearOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Non-linear maps close to affine maps
nodes.description: In this file we study a map f such that ‖f x - f y - f' (x - y)‖ ≤ c ‖x - y‖ on an open set s, where f' : E →L[𝕜] F is a continuous linear map and c is suitably small. Maps of this type behave like f a + f' (x - a) near each a ∈ s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.ContDiff
nodes.description: In this file we specialize the inverse function theorem to C^r-smooth functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.Deriv
nodes.description: In this file we prove a version of the inverse function theorem for maps f : 𝕜 → 𝕜. We use ContinuousLinearEquiv.unitsEquivAut to translate HasStrictDerivAt f f' a and f' ≠ 0 into HasStrictFDerivAt f (_ : 𝕜 ≃L[𝕜] 𝕜) a.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.FDeriv
nodes.description: In this file we prove the inverse function theorem. It says that if a map f : E → F has an invertible strict derivative f' at a, then it is locally invertible, and the inverse function has derivative f' ⁻¹.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.InverseFunctionTheorem.FiniteDimensional
nodes.descriptionTitle: A lemma about ApproximatesLinearOn that needs FiniteDimensional
nodes.description: In this file we prove that in a real vector space, a function f that approximates a linear equivalence on a subset s can be extended to a homeomorphism of the whole space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.ConvergenceOnBall
nodes.descriptionTitle: Taylor series converges to function on whole ball
nodes.description: In this file we prove that if a function f is analytic on the ball of convergence of its Taylor series, then the series converges to f on this ball.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.Defs
nodes.description: We define the n-th derivative of a function f : 𝕜 → F as a function iteratedDeriv n f : 𝕜 → F, as well as a version on domains iteratedDerivWithin n f s : 𝕜 → F, and prove their basic properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.FaaDiBruno
nodes.description: In this file we specialize Faà di Bruno's formula to one-dimensional domain to deduce formulae for iteratedDerivWithin k (g ∘ f) s x for k = 2 and k = 3.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.Lemmas
nodes.description: This file contains a number of further results on iteratedDerivWithin that need more imports than are available in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.IteratedDeriv.WithinZpow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of x ^ m, m : ℤ within an open set
nodes.description: In this file we prove theorems about iterated derivatives of x ^ m, m : ℤ within an open set.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LHopital
nodes.description: In this file, we prove several forms of "L'Hôpital's rule" for computing 0/0 indeterminate forms. The proof of HasDerivAt.lhopital_zero_right_on_Ioo is based on the one given in the corresponding Wikibooks chapter, and all other statements are derived from this one by composing by carefully chosen functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LagrangeMultipliers
nodes.description: In this file we formalize the Lagrange multipliers method of solving conditional extremum problems: if a function φ has a local extremum at x₀ on the set f ⁻¹' {f x₀}, f x = (f₀ x, ..., fₙ₋₁ x), then the differentials of fₖ and φ are linearly dependent. First we formulate a geometric version of this theorem which does not rely on the target space being ℝⁿ, then restate it in terms of coordinates.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.Basic
nodes.description: We define the line derivative of a function f : E → F, at a point x : E along a vector v : E, as the element f' : F such that f (x + t • v) = f x + t • f' + o (t) as t tends to 0 in the scalar field 𝕜, if it exists. It is denoted by lineDeriv 𝕜 f x v.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integration by parts for line derivatives
nodes.description: Let f, g : E → ℝ be two differentiable functions on a real vector space endowed with a Haar measure. Then ∫ f g' = - ∫ f' g, where f' and g' denote the derivatives of f and g in a given direction v, provided that f g, f' g and f g' are all integrable.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.Measurable
nodes.description: We prove in measurable_lineDeriv that the line derivative of a function (with respect to a locally compact scalar field) is measurable, provided the function is continuous.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.QuadraticMap
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a quadratic form is line differentiable, with the line derivative given by the polar bilinear form. Note that this statement does not need topology on the domain. In particular, it applies to discontinuous quadratic forms on infinite-dimensional spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.Basic
nodes.description: In a real normed space E we define posTangentConeAt (s : Set E) (x : E). This would be the same as tangentConeAt ℝ≥0 s x if we had a theory of normed semifields. This set is used in the proof of Fermat's Theorem (see below), and can be used to formalize Lagrange multipliers and/or Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.LineDeriv
nodes.description: If f has a local extremum at a point, then the derivative at this point is zero. In this file we prove several versions of this fact for line derivatives.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.Polynomial
nodes.description: In this file we use Rolle's Theorem to relate the number of real roots of a real polynomial and its derivative. Namely, we prove the following facts.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.Rolle
nodes.description: In this file we prove Rolle's Theorem. The theorem says that for a function f : ℝ → ℝ such that

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LogDeriv
nodes.description: We define the logarithmic derivative of a function f as deriv f / f. We then prove some basic facts about this, including how it changes under multiplication and composition.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.LogDerivUniformlyOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Logarithmic derivative of an infinite product
nodes.description: We show that if we have an infinite product of functions f that is locally uniformly convergent, then the logarithmic derivative of the product is the sum of the logarithmic derivatives of the individual functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: The mean value inequality and equalities
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following facts:

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Monotone
nodes.description: We show that a monotone function f : ℝ → ℝ is differentiable almost everywhere, in Monotone.ae_differentiableAt. (We also give a version for a function monotone on a set, in MonotoneOn.ae_differentiableWithinAt.)

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ParametricIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of integrals depending on parameters
nodes.description: A parametric integral is a function with shape f = fun x : H ↦ ∫ a : α, F x a ∂μ for some F : H → α → E, where H and E are normed spaces and α is a measured space with measure μ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.ParametricIntervalIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of interval integrals depending on parameters
nodes.description: In this file we restate theorems about derivatives of integrals depending on parameters for interval integrals.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Rademacher
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rademacher's theorem: a Lipschitz function is differentiable almost everywhere
nodes.description: This file proves Rademacher's theorem: a Lipschitz function between finite-dimensional real vector spaces is differentiable almost everywhere with respect to the Lebesgue measure. This is the content of LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt. Versions for functions which are Lipschitz on sets are also given (see LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt).

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.SmoothSeries
nodes.description: We show that series of functions are differentiable, or smooth, when each individual function in the series is and additionally suitable uniform summable bounds are satisfied.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of tangent cones and sets with unique differentiability property
nodes.description: In this file we prove basic lemmas about tangentConeAt, UniqueDiffWithinAt, and UniqueDiffOn.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Defs
nodes.description: In this file, we define two predicates UniqueDiffWithinAt 𝕜 s x and UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s ensuring that, if a function has two derivatives, then they have to coincide. As a direct definition of this fact (quantifying on all target types and all functions) would depend on universes, we use a more intrinsic definition: if all the possible tangent directions to the set s at the point x span a dense subset of the whole subset, it is easy to check that the derivative has to be unique.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.DimOne
nodes.descriptionTitle: Unique differentiability property of a set in the base field
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a set in the base field has the unique differentiability property at x iff x is an accumulation point of the set, see uniqueDiffWithinAt_iff_accPt.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Pi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Indexed product of sets with unique differentiability property
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the indexed product of a family sets with unique differentiability property has the same property, see UniqueDiffOn.pi and UniqueDiffOn.univ_pi.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Prod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Product of sets with unique differentiability property
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the product of two sets with unique differentiability property has the same property, see UniqueDiffOn.prod.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.ProperSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tangent cone in a proper space
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the tangent cone of a set in a proper normed space at an accumulation point of this set is nontrivial.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: Unique differentiability property in real normed spaces
nodes.description: In this file we prove that

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.TangentCone.Seq
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tangent cone points as limits of sequences
nodes.description: This file contains a few ways to describe tangentConeAt as the set of limits of certain sequences.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.Taylor
nodes.description: This file defines the Taylor polynomial of a real function f : ℝ → E, where E is a normed vector space over ℝ and proves Taylor's theorem, which states that if f is sufficiently smooth, then f can be approximated by the Taylor polynomial up to an explicit error term.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.UniformLimitsDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Swapping limits and derivatives via uniform convergence
nodes.description: The purpose of this file is to prove that the derivative of the pointwise limit of a sequence of functions is the pointwise limit of the functions' derivatives when the derivatives converge _uniformly_. The formal statement appears as hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.

nodes.label: Analysis.Calculus.VectorField
nodes.description: We study functions of the form V : E → E on a vector space, thinking of these as vector fields. We define several notions in this context, with the aim to generalize them to vector fields on manifolds.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.AbelLimit
nodes.description: If a real or complex power series for a function has radius of convergence 1 and the series is only known to converge conditionally at 1, Abel's limit theorem gives the value at 1 as the limit of the function at 1 from the left. "Left" for complex numbers means within a fixed cone opening to the left with angle less than π.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.AbsMax
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the maximum modulus principle. There are several statements that can be called "the maximum modulus principle" for maps between normed complex spaces. They differ by assumptions on the domain (any space, a nontrivial space, a finite dimensional space), assumptions on the codomain (any space, a strictly convex space), and by conclusion (either equality of norms or of the values of the function).

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Angle
nodes.description: This file relates the Euclidean geometric notion of angle between complex numbers to the argument of their quotient.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Arg
nodes.description: This file links the definition SameRay ℝ x y with the equality of arguments of complex numbers, the usual way this is considered.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Asymptotics
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about asymptotics and the natural embedding ℝ → ℂ
nodes.description: In this file we prove several trivial lemmas about Asymptotics.IsBigO etc. and (↑) : ℝ → ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Basic
nodes.description: This file gathers basic facts of analytic nature on the complex numbers.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.BorelCaratheodory
nodes.description: This file proves the Borel-Carathéodory theorem: for any function f analytic on the open ball |z| < R such that Re(f z) < M for all |z| < R, we have ‖f z‖ ≤ 2 M ‖z‖ / (R - ‖z‖) + ‖f 0‖ (R + ‖z‖) / (R - ‖z‖)

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.BranchLogRoot
nodes.descriptionTitle: Branches of logarithm and nth root on simply connected domains
nodes.description: In this file we prove that for a function g : X → ℂ defined on a locally path connected space that is continuous on an open simply connected set U and 0 ∉ g '' U, there exist continuous branches of log (g z) and ⁿ√(g z) on U.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.CanonicalDecomposition
nodes.description: If a function f is meromorphic on a compact set U, then it has only finitely many zeros and poles on the disk, and the theorem MeromorphicOn.extract_zeros_poles can be used to re-write f as (∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ divisor f U u) • g, where g is analytic without zeros on U. In case where U is a disk, one consider a similar decomposition, called Canonical Decomposition or Blaschke Product that replaces the factors (· - u) by canonical factors that take only values of norm one on the boundary of the circle.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Cardinality
nodes.descriptionTitle: The cardinality of the complex numbers
nodes.description: This file shows that the complex numbers have cardinality continuum, i.e. #ℂ = 𝔠.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.CauchyIntegral
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Cauchy-Goursat theorem and the Cauchy integral formula for integrals over circles. Most results are formulated for a function f : ℂ → E that takes values in a complex Banach space with second countable topology.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Circle
nodes.description: This file defines Circle to be the metric sphere (Metric.sphere) in ℂ centred at 0 of radius 1. We equip it with the following structure:

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Conformal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Conformal maps between complex vector spaces
nodes.description: We prove the sufficient and necessary conditions for a real-linear map between complex vector spaces to be conformal.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Convex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Theorems about convexity on the complex plane
nodes.description: We show that the open and closed half-spaces in ℂ given by an inequality on either the real or imaginary part are all convex over ℝ. We also prove some results on star-convexity for the slit plane.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.CoveringMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Covering maps involving the complex plane
nodes.description: In this file, we show that Complex.exp and (· ^ n) (for n ≠ 0) are a covering map on {0}ᶜ. We also show that any complex polynomial is a covering map on the set of regular values.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Exponential
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions of the real and complex exponential function.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bounds on specific values of the exponential
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Hadamard
nodes.description: In this file we present a proof of Hadamard's three-lines Theorem.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.HalfPlane
nodes.description: We state that open left, right, upper and lower half-planes in the complex numbers are open sets, where the bounding value of the real or imaginary part is given by an EReal x. So this includes the full plane and the empty set for x = ⊤/x = ⊥.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.Analytic
nodes.description: If f : ℂ → ℝ is harmonic at x, we show that ∂f/∂1 - I • ∂f/∂I is complex-analytic at x. If f is harmonic on an open ball, then it is the real part of a function F : ℂ → ℂ that is holomorphic on the ball. This implies in particular that harmonic functions are real-analytic.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.Liouville
nodes.descriptionTitle: Liouville's Theorem for Harmonic Functions on the Complex Plane
nodes.description: A bounded harmonic function on the complex plane is constant.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.MeanValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Mean Value Property of Harmonic Functions on the Complex Plane
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.MeanValue.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Harmonic.Poisson
nodes.description: This file establishes several versions of the Poisson Integral Formula for harmonic functions on arbitrary disks in the complex plane, formulated with the real part of the Herglotz–Riesz kernel of integration and with the Poisson kernel, respectively.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.HasPrimitives
nodes.description: In this file, we give conditions under which holomorphic functions have primitives. The main goal is to prove that holomorphic functions on simply connected domains have primitives. As a first step, we prove that holomorphic functions on disks have primitives. The approach is based on Morera's theorem, that a continuous function (on a disk) whose integral round a rectangle vanishes on all rectangles contained in the disk has a primitive.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.IntegerCompl
nodes.description: We define the complement of the integers in the complex plane and give some basic lemmas about it. We also show that the upper half plane embeds into the integer complement.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.IsIntegral
nodes.description: This file proves that Complex.I is integral over ℤ and ℚ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Isometry
nodes.description: The lemma linear_isometry_complex states the classification of isometries in the complex plane. Specifically, isometries with rotations but without translation. The proof involves: 1. creating a linear isometry g with two fixed points, g(0) = 0, g(1) = 1 2. applying linear_isometry_complex_aux to g

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.JensenFormula
nodes.description: If a function g : ℂ → ℂ is analytic without zero on the closed ball with center c and radius R, then log ‖g ·‖ is harmonic, and the mean value theorem of harmonic functions asserts that the circle average circleAverage (log ‖g ·‖) c R equals log ‖g c‖. Note that g c equals meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt g c and see AnalyticOnNhd.circleAverage_log_norm_of_ne_zero for the precise statement.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Liouville
nodes.description: In this file we prove Liouville's theorem: if f : E → F is complex differentiable on the whole space and its range is bounded, then the function is a constant. Various versions of this theorem are formalized in Differentiable.apply_eq_apply_of_bounded, Differentiable.exists_const_forall_eq_of_bounded, and Differentiable.exists_eq_const_of_bounded.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.LocallyUniformLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: This file gathers some results about locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions on an open subset of the complex plane.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.MeanValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Mean Value Property of Complex Differentiable Functions
nodes.description: This file established the classic mean value properties of complex differentiable functions, computing the value of a function at the center of a circle as a circle average. It also provides generalized versions that computing the value of a function at arbitrary points of a disk as circle averages over suitable weighted functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Norm
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Complex.Norm.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.OpenMapping
nodes.descriptionTitle: The open mapping theorem for holomorphic functions
nodes.description: This file proves the open mapping theorem for holomorphic functions, namely that an analytic function on a preconnected set of the complex plane is either constant or open. The main step is to show a local version of the theorem that states that if f is analytic at a point z₀, then either it is constant in a neighborhood of z₀ or it maps any neighborhood of z₀ to a neighborhood of its image f z₀. The results extend in higher dimension to g : E → ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.OperatorNorm
nodes.descriptionTitle: The basic continuous linear maps associated to ℂ
nodes.description: The continuous linear maps Complex.reCLM (real part), Complex.imCLM (imaginary part), Complex.conjCLE (conjugation), and Complex.ofRealCLM (inclusion of ℝ) were introduced in Analysis.Complex.Basic. This file contains a few calculations requiring more imports: the operator norm and (for Complex.conjCLE) the determinant.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Order
nodes.descriptionTitle: The partial order on the complex numbers
nodes.description: This order is defined by z ≤ w ↔ z.re ≤ w.re ∧ z.im = w.im.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Periodic
nodes.description: We show that if f : ℂ → ℂ satisfies f (z + h) = f z, for some nonzero real h, then there is a function F such that f z = F (exp (2 π I z / h)) for all z; and if f is holomorphic at some z, then F is holomorphic at exp (2 π I z / h).

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.PhragmenLindelof
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the Phragmen-Lindelöf principle, a version of the maximum modulus principle for an unbounded domain.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Poisson
nodes.description: We present two versions of the Poisson Integral Formula for ℂ-differentiable functions on arbitrary disks in the complex plane, formulated with the real part of the Herglotz–Riesz kernel of integration and with the Poisson kernel, respectively.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.Basic
nodes.description: This file proves that every nonconstant complex polynomial has a root using Liouville's theorem.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.GaussLucas
nodes.description: In this file we prove Gauss-Lucas Theorem: the roots of the derivative of a nonconstant complex polynomial are included in the convex hull of the roots of the polynomial.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.UnitTrinomial
nodes.description: Develop more theory (e.g., it suffices to check that aeval z p ≠ 0 for z = 0 and z a root of unity).

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Positivity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nonnegativity of values of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: We show that if f is holomorphic on an open disk B(c,r) and all iterated derivatives of f at c are nonnegative real, then f z ≥ 0 for all z ≥ c in the disk; see DifferentiableOn.nonneg_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg. We also provide a variant Differentiable.nonneg_of_iteratedDeriv_nonneg for entire functions and versions showing f z ≥ f c when all iterated derivatives except f itself are nonnegative.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ReImTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Closure, interior, and frontier of preimages under re and im
nodes.description: In this fact we use the fact that ℂ is naturally homeomorphic to ℝ × ℝ to deduce some topological properties of Complex.re and Complex.im.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.RealDeriv
nodes.description: HasDerivAt.real_of_complex expresses that, if a function on ℂ is differentiable (over ℂ), then its restriction to ℝ is differentiable over ℝ, with derivative the real part of the complex derivative.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.RemovableSingularity
nodes.description: In this file we prove Riemann's removable singularity theorem: if f : ℂ → E is complex differentiable in a punctured neighborhood of a point c and is bounded in a punctured neighborhood of c (or, more generally, $f(z) - f(c)=o((z-c)^{-1})$), then it has a limit at c and the function update f c (limUnder (𝓝[≠] c) f) is complex differentiable in a neighborhood of c.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.RiemannMapping
nodes.description: This file contains partial results towards Riemann Mapping Theorem. A complete proof is available at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/33505, though it may fail to compile with the latest Mathlib.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Schwarz
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the Schwarz lemma.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Spectrum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some lemmas on the spectrum and quasispectrum of elements and positivity on ℂ
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Complex.Spectrum.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.SqrtDeriv
nodes.description: This file proves that Complex.sqrt is differentiable on the slit plane Complex.slitPlane and computes its derivative.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.SummableUniformlyOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of uniformly convergent series sums of functions
nodes.description: We collect some results about the differentiability of infinite sums.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.TaylorSeries
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convergence of Taylor series of holomorphic functions
nodes.description: We show that the Taylor series around some point c : ℂ of a function f that is complex differentiable on the open ball of radius r around c converges to f on that open ball; see Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_on_ball and Complex.taylorSeries_eq_on_ball for versions (in terms of HasSum and tsum, respectively) for functions to a complete normed space over ℂ, and Complex.taylorSeries_eq_on_ball' for a variant when f : ℂ → ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Tietze
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite-dimensional topological vector spaces over ℝ satisfy the Tietze extension property
nodes.description: There are two main results here:

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.Trigonometric
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions of the sine, cosine, tangent, hyperbolic sine, hyperbolic cosine, and hyperbolic tangent functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UnitDisc.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define Complex.UnitDisc to be the unit disc in the complex plane. We also introduce some basic operations on this disc.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines UpperHalfPlane to be the upper half plane in ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Exp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Exp on the upper half plane
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the exponential function on the upper half plane. Useful for q-expansions of modular forms.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.FixedPoints
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fixed points of isometries of the upper half-plane
nodes.description: In this file we show that the scalar multiplication by an element g : GL (Fin 2) ℝ has the following set of fixed points, depending on g.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.FunctionsBoundedAtInfty
nodes.description: For complex-valued functions on the upper half plane, this file defines the filter UpperHalfPlane.atImInfty required for defining when functions are bounded at infinity and zero at infinity. Both of which are relevant for defining modular forms.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Manifold
nodes.descriptionTitle: Manifold structure on the upper half plane.
nodes.description: In this file we define the complex manifold structure on the upper half-plane, and show it is invariant under Moebius transformations. We also calculate the derivative, and give an explicit formula for its Jacobian determinant over ℝ (used in proving that the action preserves a suitable measure).

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Measure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Invariant measure on the upper half-plane
nodes.description: We equip the upper half-plane with a measure, defined as the restriction of the usual measure on ℂ weighted by the function 1 / (im z) ^ 2. We show that this measure is invariant under the action of GL(2, ℝ).

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Metric
nodes.description: In this file we define a MetricSpace structure on the UpperHalfPlane. We use hyperbolic (Poincaré) distance given by dist z w = 2 arsinh (dist (z : ℂ) w / (2 √(z.im w.im))) instead of the induced Euclidean distance because the hyperbolic distance is invariant under holomorphic automorphisms of the upper half-plane. However, we ensure that the projection to TopologicalSpace is definitionally equal to the induced topological space structure.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.MoebiusAction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Group action on the upper half-plane
nodes.description: We equip the upper half-plane with the structure of a GL (Fin 2) ℝ action by fractional linear transformations (composing with complex conjugation when needed to extend the action from the positive-determinant subgroup, so that !![-1, 0; 0, 1] acts as z ↦ -conj z.)

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.ProperAction
nodes.description: We show that the actions of SL(2, ℝ) and GL(2, ℝ) on the upper half-plane are jointly continuous, and the action of SL(2, ℝ) is proper. (These results require more imports than in UpperHalfPlane.Topology, because they use the topology on the group as well)

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Topology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on the upper half plane
nodes.description: In this file we introduce a TopologicalSpace structure on the upper half plane and provide various instances.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.Cartan
nodes.description: This file will, in the future, establish Cartan's classic formula, describing the characteristic function characteristic f ⊤ r as a sum of two circle averages,

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.CharacteristicFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Characteristic Function of Value Distribution Theory
nodes.description: This file defines the "characteristic function" attached to a meromorphic function defined on the complex plane. Also known as "Nevanlinna Height", this is one of the three main functions used in Value Distribution Theory.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.FirstMainTheorem
nodes.descriptionTitle: The First Main Theorem of Value Distribution Theory
nodes.description: The First Main Theorem of Value Distribution Theory is a two-part statement, establishing invariance of the characteristic function characteristic f ⊤ under modifications of f.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.LogCounting.Asymptotic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Asymptotic Behavior of the Logarithmic Counting Function
nodes.description: If f is meromorphic over a field 𝕜, we show that the logarithmic counting function for the poles of f is asymptotically bounded if and only if f has only removable singularities. See Page 170f of Lang, Introduction to Complex Hyperbolic Spaces for a detailed discussion.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.LogCounting.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Logarithmic Counting Function of Value Distribution Theory
nodes.description: For nontrivially normed fields 𝕜, this file defines the logarithmic counting function of a meromorphic function defined on 𝕜. Also known as the Nevanlinna counting function, this is one of the three main functions used in Value Distribution Theory.

nodes.label: Analysis.Complex.ValueDistribution.Proximity.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Proximity Function of Value Distribution Theory
nodes.description: This file defines the "proximity function" attached to a meromorphic function defined on the complex plane. Also known as the Nevanlinna Proximity Function, this is one of the three main functions used in Value Distribution Theory.

nodes.label: Analysis.ConstantSpeed
nodes.description: This file defines the notion of constant (and unit) speed for a function f : ℝ → E with pseudo-emetric structure on E with respect to a set s : Set ℝ and "speed" l : ℝ≥0, and shows that if f has locally bounded variation on s, it can be obtained (up to distance zero, on s), as a composite φ ∘ (variationOnFromTo f s a), where φ has unit speed and a ∈ s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.AmpleSet
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ample subsets of real vector spaces
nodes.description: In this file we study ample sets in real vector spaces. A set is ample if all its connected component have full convex hull. Ample sets are an important ingredient for defining ample differential relations.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Approximation
nodes.description: In this file we show that a convex lower-semicontinuous function is the upper envelope of a family of continuous affine linear functions. We follow the proof in N. Bourbaki, Topological vector spaces, Chapter II, §5.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Basic
nodes.description: In a 𝕜-vector space, we define the following property:

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Between
nodes.description: This file defines notions of a point in an affine space being between two given points.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.BetweenList
nodes.description: This file defines notions of lists of points in an affine space being in order on a line.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Birkhoff
nodes.description: combination of permutation matrices. of the permutation matrices. the set of permutation matrices.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Body
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of the type ConvexBody V consisting of convex, compact, nonempty subsets of a real topological vector space V.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Caratheodory
nodes.description: Convex hull can be regarded as a refinement of affine span. Both are closure operators but whereas convex hull takes values in the lattice of convex subsets, affine span takes values in the much coarser sublattice of affine subspaces.
