nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Combination
nodes.description: This file defines convex combinations of points in a vector space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.Basic
nodes.description: We define a proper cone as a closed, pointed cone. Proper cones are used in defining conic programs which generalize linear programs. A linear program is a conic program for the positive cone. We then prove Farkas' lemma for conic programs following the proof in the reference below. Farkas' lemma is equivalent to strong duality. So, once we have the definitions of conic and linear programs, the results from this file can be used to prove duality theorems.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.Closure
nodes.description: We define the closures of convex and pointed cones. This construction is primarily needed for defining maps between proper cones. The current API is basic and should be extended as necessary.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.Dual
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topological dual of a cone and Farkas' lemma
nodes.description: Given a continuous bilinear pairing p between two R-modules M and N and a set s in M, we define ProperCone.dual p C to be the proper cone in N consisting of all points y such that 0 ≤ p x y for all x ∈ s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.Extension
nodes.description: We prove two extension theorems: M. Riesz extension theorem says that if s is a convex cone in a real vector space E, p is a submodule of E such that p + s = E, and f is a linear function p → ℝ which is nonnegative on p ∩ s, then there exists a globally defined linear function g : E → ℝ that agrees with f on p, and is nonnegative on s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.InnerDual
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inner dual cone of a set
nodes.description: We define the inner dual cone of a set s in an inner product space to be the proper cone consisting of all points y such that 0 ≤ ⟪x, y⟫ for all x ∈ s.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Cone.TensorProduct
nodes.description: This file proves that the minimal and maximal tensor products of pointed cones in finite-dimensional real vector spaces are equal when one cone is simplicial and generating and the other is proper (pointed and closed).

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Continuous
nodes.description: This file proves that a convex function from a finite-dimensional real normed space to ℝ is continuous.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.ContinuousLinearEquiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Pre)images of strict convex sets under continuous linear equivalences
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the (pre)image of a strict convex set under a continuous linear equivalence is a strict convex set.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Contractible
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a (star) convex set in a real topological vector space is a contractible topological space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Deriv
nodes.description: Here we relate convexity of functions ℝ → ℝ to properties of their derivatives.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.DoublyStochasticMatrix
nodes.description: or right multiplication by the vector of all 1s gives the vector of all 1s. Equivalently, all row and column sums are equal to 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.EGauge
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Minkowski functional, normed field version
nodes.description: In this file we define (egauge 𝕜 s ·) to be the Minkowski functional (gauge) of the set s in a topological vector space E over a normed field 𝕜, as a function E → ℝ≥0∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Exposed
nodes.description: This file defines exposed sets and exposed points for sets in a real vector space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Extrema
nodes.descriptionTitle: Minima and maxima of convex functions
nodes.description: We show that if a function f : E → β is convex, then a local minimum is also a global minimum, and likewise for concave functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Extreme
nodes.description: This file defines extreme sets and extreme points for sets in a module.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Function
nodes.description: This file defines convex and concave functions in vector spaces and proves the finite Jensen inequality. The integral version can be found in Analysis.Convex.Integral.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.FunctionTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological properties of the set of convex/concave functions
nodes.description: We prove the following facts:

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Gauge
nodes.description: This file defines the Minkowski functional, aka gauge.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.GaugeRescale
nodes.description: Given two convex von Neumann bounded neighbourhoods of the origin in a real topological vector space, we construct a homeomorphism gaugeRescaleHomeomorph that sends the interior, the closure, and the frontier of one set to the interior, the closure, and the frontier of the other set.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Hull
nodes.description: This file defines the convex hull of a set s in a module. convexHull 𝕜 s is the smallest convex set containing s. In order theory speak, this is a closure operator.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Independent
nodes.description: This file defines convex independent families of points.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Integral
nodes.description: In this file we prove several forms of Jensen's inequality for integrals.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Intrinsic
nodes.description: This file defines the intrinsic frontier, interior and closure of a set in a normed additive torsor. These are also known as relative frontier, interior, closure.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Jensen
nodes.descriptionTitle: Jensen's inequality and maximum principle for convex functions
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the finite Jensen inequality and the finite maximum principle for convex functions. The integral versions are to be found in Analysis.Convex.Integral.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Join
nodes.description: This file defines the convex join of two sets. The convex join of s and t is the union of the segments with one end in s and the other in t. This is notably a useful gadget to deal with convex hulls of finite sets.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.KreinMilman
nodes.description: This file proves the Krein-Milman lemma and the Krein-Milman theorem.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.LinearIsometry
nodes.description: In this file we prove some basic lemmas about (strict) convexity and linear isometries.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Measure
nodes.description: Let E be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let μ be a Haar measure on E, let s be a convex set in E. Then the frontier of s has measure zero (see Convex.addHaar_frontier), hence s is a NullMeasurableSet (see Convex.nullMeasurableSet).

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.MetricSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convex spaces with compatible metric structure
nodes.description: A convex space has a compatible metric structure if dist(∑ tᵢ xᵢ, ∑ tᵢ yᵢ) ≤ ∑ tᵢ dist(xᵢ, yᵢ). This is what one would expect from the triangle inequality.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Mul
nodes.description: This file proves that the product of convex functions is convex, provided they monovary.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.NNReal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Specific lemmas about convexity over ℝ≥0
nodes.description: This file collects some specific results about convexity over the ring ℝ≥0. Expand as needed.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.PartitionOfUnity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Partition of unity and convex sets
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following lemma, see exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local. Let X be a normal paracompact topological space (e.g., any extended metric space). Let E be a topological real vector space. Let t : X → Set E be a family of convex sets. Suppose that for each point x : X, there exists a neighborhood U ∈ 𝓝 X and a function g : X → E that is continuous on U and sends each y ∈ U to a point of t y. Then there exists a continuous map g : C(X, E) such that g x ∈ t x for all x.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.PathConnected
nodes.descriptionTitle: Segment between 2 points as a bundled path
nodes.description: In this file we define Path.segment a b : Path a b to be the path going from a to b along the straight segment with constant velocity b - a.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Piecewise
nodes.description: This file proves convex and concave theorems for piecewise functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Quasiconvex
nodes.description: This file defines quasiconvexity, quasiconcavity and quasilinearity of functions, which are generalizations of unimodality and monotonicity. Convexity implies quasiconvexity, concavity implies quasiconcavity, and monotonicity implies quasilinearity.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Radon
nodes.description: Radon's theorem states that any affine dependent set can be partitioned into two sets whose convex hulls intersect nontrivially.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Segment
nodes.description: In a 𝕜-vector space, we define the following objects and properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Side
nodes.description: This file defines notions of two points being on the same or opposite sides of an affine subspace.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.SimplicialComplex.AffineIndependentUnion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Simplicial complexes from affinely independent points
nodes.description: This file provides constructions for simplicial complexes where the vertices are affinely independent.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.SimplicialComplex.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define simplicial complexes over 𝕜-modules. A (pre-) abstract simplicial complex is a downwards-closed collection of nonempty finite sets, and a simplicial complex is such a collection identified with simplices closed by inclusion (of vertices) and intersection (of underlying sets) whose convex hulls "glue nicely", each finite set and its convex hull corresponding respectively to the vertices and the underlying set of a simplex.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Slope
nodes.description: This file relates convexity/concavity of functions in a linearly ordered field and the monotonicity of their slopes.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the following functions are convex or strictly convex:

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Deriv
nodes.description: In this file we prove that certain specific functions are strictly convex, including the following:

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Pow
nodes.description: We prove basic convexity properties of the rpow function. The proofs are elementary and do not require calculus, and as such this file has only moderate dependencies.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Star
nodes.description: This file defines star-convex sets (aka star domains, star-shaped set, radially convex set).

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.StdSimplex
nodes.description: In this file, given an ordered semiring 𝕜 and a finite type ι, we define stdSimplex : Set (ι → 𝕜) as the set of vectors with non-negative coordinates with total sum 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.StoneSeparation
nodes.description: This file proves Stone's separation theorem. This tells us that any two disjoint convex sets can be separated by a convex set whose complement is also convex.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Strict
nodes.description: This file defines strictly convex sets.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Strict.Extreme
nodes.description: This file collects some results of extreme points of (strictly convex) sets.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.StrictCombination
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convex combinations in strictly convex sets and spaces.
nodes.description: This file proves lemmas about convex combinations of points in strictly convex sets and strictly convex spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.StrictConvexBetween
nodes.descriptionTitle: Betweenness in affine spaces for strictly convex spaces
nodes.description: This file proves results about betweenness for points in an affine space for a strictly convex space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.StrictConvexSpace
nodes.description: This file defines strictly convex spaces. A normed space is strictly convex if all closed balls are strictly convex. This does not mean that the norm is strictly convex (in fact, it never is).

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Strong
nodes.description: In this file, we define uniformly convex functions and strongly convex functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Topology
nodes.description: We prove the following facts:

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.TotallyBounded
nodes.descriptionTitle: Totally Bounded sets and Convex Hulls
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Convex.TotallyBounded.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Uniform
nodes.description: This file defines uniformly convex spaces, which are real normed vector spaces in which for all strictly positive ε, there exists some strictly positive δ such that ε ≤ ‖x - y‖ implies ‖x + y‖ ≤ 2 - δ for all x and y of norm at most than 1. This means that the triangle inequality is strict with a uniform bound, as opposed to strictly convex spaces where the triangle inequality is strict but not necessarily uniformly (‖x + y‖ < ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ for all x and y not in the same ray).

nodes.label: Analysis.Convex.Visible
nodes.description: This file defines the relation of visibility with respect to a set, and lower bounds how many elements of a set a point sees in terms of the dimension of that set.

nodes.label: Analysis.Convolution
nodes.description: This file defines the convolution on two functions, i.e. x ↦ ∫ f(t)g(x - t) ∂t. In the general case, these functions can be vector-valued, and have an arbitrary (additive) group as domain. We use a continuous bilinear operation L on these function values as "multiplication". The domain must be equipped with a Haar measure μ (though many individual results have weaker conditions on μ).

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.AEEqOfIntegralContDiff
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions which vanish as distributions vanish as functions
nodes.description: In a finite-dimensional normed real vector space endowed with a Borel measure, consider a locally integrable function whose integral against all compactly supported smooth functions vanishes. Then the function is almost everywhere zero. This is proved in ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.ContDiffMapSupportedIn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuously differentiable functions supported in a given compact set
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of bundled n-times continuously differentiable functions with support contained in a given compact set.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.DerivNotation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Type classes for derivatives and the Laplacian
nodes.description: In this file we define notation type classes for line derivatives, also known as partial derivatives, and for the Laplacian.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.Distribution
nodes.description: Let E be a real finite-dimensional normed space, Ω an open subset of E, and F a real locally convex topological vector space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.FourierMultiplier
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fourier multiplier on Schwartz functions and tempered distributions
nodes.description: We define a Fourier multiplier as continuous linear maps on Schwartz functions and tempered distributions. The multiplier function is throughout assumed to have temperate growth.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.FourierSchwartz
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.SchwartzSpace
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.SchwartzSpace.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the Schwartz space. Usually, the Schwartz space is defined as the set of smooth functions $f : ℝ^n → ℂ$ such that there exists $C_{αβ} > 0$ with $$|x^α ∂^β f(x)| < C_{αβ}$$ for all $x ∈ ℝ^n$ and for all multiindices $α, β$. In mathlib, we use a slightly different approach and define the Schwartz space as all smooth functions f : E → F, where E and F are real normed vector spaces such that for all natural numbers k and n we have uniform bounds ‖x‖ ^ k ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n f x‖ < C.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.SchwartzSpace.Deriv
nodes.description: In this file we define the various notions of derivatives of Schwartz functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.SchwartzSpace.Fourier
nodes.description: This file constructs the Fourier transform as a continuous linear map acting on Schwartz functions, in fourierTransformCLM. It is also given as a continuous linear equiv, in fourierTransformCLE.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.Sobolev
nodes.description: In this file we define Sobolev spaces on normed vector spaces via the Fourier transform. These spaces are also known as Bessel potential spaces. The Bessel potential operator besselPotential is the Fourier multiplier with the symbol x ↦ (1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) and a tempered distribution u belongs to the Sobolev space H ^ {s, p} if besselPotential E F s u can be represented by a Lp function, informally this is written as 𝓕⁻ (fun x ↦ (1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2) ^ (s / 2)) 𝓕 u ∈ Lp.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.Support
nodes.description: We define the support of a distribution, dsupport u, as the intersection of all closed sets for which u vanishes on the complement. For this we also define a predicate IsVanishingOn that asserts that a map f : F → V vanishes on s : Set α if for all u : F with tsupport u ⊆ s it follows that f u = 0.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.TemperateGrowth
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions and measures of temperate growth
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Distribution.TemperateGrowth.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.TemperedDistribution
nodes.description: convergence topology. distribution. tempered distribution. map. linear map.

nodes.label: Analysis.Distribution.TestFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuously differentiable functions with compact support
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of bundled n-times continuously differentiable functions with compact support contained in some open set Ω. More explicitly, given normed spaces E and F, an open set Ω : Opens E and n : ℕ∞, we are interested in the space 𝓓^{n}(Ω, F) of maps f : E → F such that:

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.AddCircle
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fourier analysis on the additive circle
nodes.description: This file contains basic results on Fourier series for functions on the additive circle AddCircle T = ℝ / ℤ • T.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.AddCircleMulti
nodes.description: In this file we define the Fourier series of an L² function on the d-dimensional unit circle, and show that it converges to the function in the L² norm. We also prove uniform convergence of the Fourier series if f is continuous and the sequence of its Fourier coefficients is summable.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.BoundedContinuousFunctionChar
nodes.description: Definition and basic properties of BoundedContinuousFunction.char he hL w := fun v ↦ e (L v w), where e is a continuous additive character and L : V →ₗ[ℝ] W →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ is a continuous bilinear map.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.Convolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Fourier transform of the convolution
nodes.description: In this file we calculate the Fourier transform of a convolution.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.FiniteAbelian.Orthogonality
nodes.descriptionTitle: Orthogonality of characters of a finite abelian group
nodes.description: This file proves that characters of a finite abelian group are orthogonal, and in particular that there are at most as many characters as there are elements of the group.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.FiniteAbelian.PontryaginDuality
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pontryagin duality for finite abelian groups
nodes.description: This file proves the Pontryagin duality in case of finite abelian groups. This states that any finite abelian group is canonically isomorphic to its double dual (the space of complex-valued characters of its space of complex-valued characters).

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.FourierTransform
nodes.description: We set up the Fourier transform for complex-valued functions on finite-dimensional spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.FourierTransformDeriv
nodes.description: In this file we compute the Fréchet derivative of the Fourier transform of f, where f is a function such that both f and v ↦ ‖v‖ ‖f v‖ are integrable. Here the Fourier transform is understood as an operator (V → E) → (W → E), where V and W are normed ℝ-vector spaces and the Fourier transform is taken with respect to a continuous ℝ-bilinear pairing L : V × W → ℝ and a given reference measure μ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.Inversion
nodes.description: In a finite-dimensional real inner product space, we show the Fourier inversion formula, i.e., 𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) v = f v if f and 𝓕 f are integrable, and f is continuous at v. This is proved in MeasureTheory.Integrable.fourier_inversion. See also Continuous.fourier_inversion giving 𝓕⁻ (𝓕 f) = f under an additional continuity assumption for f.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.LpSpace
nodes.description: In this file we define the Fourier transform on $L^2$ as a linear isometry equivalence.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.Notation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Type classes for the Fourier transform
nodes.description: In this file we define type classes for the Fourier transform and the inverse Fourier transform. We introduce the notation 𝓕 and 𝓕⁻ in these classes to denote the Fourier transform and the inverse Fourier transform, respectively.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.PoissonSummation
nodes.description: We prove Poisson's summation formula ∑ (n : ℤ), f n = ∑ (n : ℤ), 𝓕 f n, where 𝓕 f is the Fourier transform of f, under the following hypotheses: See Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier for this formulation.

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.RiemannLebesgueLemma
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma, for functions on finite-dimensional real vector spaces V: if f is a function on V (valued in a complete normed space E), then the Fourier transform of f, viewed as a function on the dual space of V, tends to 0 along the cocompact filter. Here the Fourier transform is defined by

nodes.label: Analysis.Fourier.ZMod
nodes.description: Basic definitions and properties of the discrete Fourier transform for functions on ZMod N (taking values in an arbitrary ℂ-vector space).

nodes.label: Analysis.FunctionalSpaces.SobolevInequality
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality. This states that for compactly supported C¹-functions between finite-dimensional vector spaces, we can bound the L^p-norm of u by the L^q norm of the derivative of u. The bound is up to a constant that is independent of the function u. Let n be the dimension of the domain.

nodes.label: Analysis.Hofer
nodes.description: This is an elementary lemma about complete metric spaces. It is motivated by an application to the bubbling-off analysis for holomorphic curves in symplectic topology. We are very far away from having these applications, but the proof here is a nice example of a proof needing to construct a sequence by induction in the middle of the proof.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjoint of operators on Hilbert spaces
nodes.description: Given an operator A : E →L[𝕜] F, where E and F are Hilbert spaces, its adjoint adjoint A : F →L[𝕜] E is the unique operator such that ⟪x, A y⟫ = ⟪adjoint A x, y⟫ for all x and y.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Affine
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normed affine spaces over an inner product space
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Affine.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
nodes.description: This file proves many basic properties of inner product spaces (real or complex).

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the inner product and square of the norm in an inner space are infinitely ℝ-smooth. In order to state these results, we need a NormedSpace ℝ E instance. Though we can deduce this structure from InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E, this instance may be not definitionally equal to some other “natural” instance. So, we assume [NormedSpace ℝ E].

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.CanonicalTensor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Canonical tensors in real inner product spaces
nodes.description: Given an InnerProductSpace ℝ E, this file defines two canonical tensors.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Coalgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite-dimensional inner product space with a (co)algebra structure
nodes.description: This file proves that a finite-dimensional inner product space has a coalgebra structure if it has an algebra structure, where the comultiplication and counit maps are given by taking adjoints of the multiplication and algebra linear maps, respectively. This is implemented by providing a linear equivalence between the inner product space and an algebra.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Completion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Completion of an inner product space
nodes.description: We show that the separation quotient and the completion of an inner product space are inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ConformalLinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Conformal maps between inner product spaces
nodes.description: In an inner product space, a map is conformal iff it preserves inner products up to a scalar factor.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Continuous
nodes.description: We show that the inner product is continuous, continuous_inner.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Convex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convexity properties of inner product spaces
nodes.description: inner product space, Hilbert space, norm

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines inner product spaces. Hilbert spaces can be obtained using the set of assumptions [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E]. For convenience, a variable alias HilbertSpace is provided so that one can write variable? [HilbertSpace 𝕜 E] and get this as a suggestion.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Dual
nodes.description: We consider an inner product space E over 𝕜, which is either ℝ or ℂ. We define toDualMap, a conjugate-linear isometric embedding of E into its dual, which maps an element x of the space to fun y => ⟪x, y⟫.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.EuclideanDist
nodes.descriptionTitle: Euclidean distance on a finite-dimensional space
nodes.description: When we define a smooth bump function on a normed space, it is useful to have a smooth distance on the space. Since the default distance is not guaranteed to be smooth, we define toEuclidean to be an equivalence between a finite-dimensional topological vector space and the standard Euclidean space of the same dimension. Then we define Euclidean.dist x y = dist (toEuclidean x) (toEuclidean y) and provide some definitions (Euclidean.ball, Euclidean.closedBall) and simple lemmas about this distance.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.GramMatrix
nodes.description: This file defines Gram matrices and proves their positive semidefiniteness. Results require RCLike 𝕜.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.GramSchmidtOrtho
nodes.description: In this file we introduce Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization and Orthonormalization.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines harmonic functions on real, finite-dimensional, inner product spaces E.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.Constructions
nodes.description: This file constructs examples of harmonic functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Harmonic.HarmonicContOnCl
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions Harmonic on a Domain and Continuous on Its Closure
nodes.description: Many theorems in harmonic analysis assume that a function is harmonic on a domain and is continuous on its closure. In this file we define a predicate HarmonicContOnCl that expresses this property and prove basic facts about this predicate.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.JointEigenspace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Joint eigenspaces of commuting symmetric operators
nodes.description: This file collects various decomposition results for joint eigenspaces of commuting symmetric operators on a finite-dimensional inner product space.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Laplacian
nodes.description: This file defines the Laplacian for functions f : E → F on real, finite-dimensional, inner product spaces E. In essence, we define the Laplacian of f as the second derivative, applied to the canonical covariant tensor of E, as defined and discussed in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.CanonicalTensor.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.LaxMilgram
nodes.description: We consider a Hilbert space V over ℝ equipped with a bounded bilinear form B : V →L[ℝ] V →L[ℝ] ℝ.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.LinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Linear maps on inner product spaces
nodes.description: This file studies linear maps on inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.LinearPMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Partially defined linear operators on Hilbert spaces
nodes.description: We will develop the basics of the theory of unbounded operators on Hilbert spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.MeanErgodic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Von Neumann Mean Ergodic Theorem in a Hilbert Space
nodes.description: In this file we prove the von Neumann Mean Ergodic Theorem for an operator in a Hilbert space. It says that for a contracting linear self-map f : E →ₗ[𝕜] E of a Hilbert space, the Birkhoff averages converge to the orthogonal projection of x to the subspace of fixed points of f, see ContinuousLinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_orthogonalProjection.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.MulOpposite
nodes.description: This file defines the inner product space structure on Hᵐᵒᵖ where we define the inner product naturally. We also define OrthonormalBasis.mulOpposite.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormPow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties about the powers of the norm
nodes.description: In this file we prove that x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ p is continuously differentiable for an inner product space and for a real number p > 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.OfNorm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inner product space derived from a norm
nodes.description: This file defines an InnerProductSpace instance from a norm that respects the parallelogram identity. The parallelogram identity is a way to express the inner product of x and y in terms of the norms of x, y, x + y, x - y.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orientation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Orientations of real inner product spaces.
nodes.description: This file provides definitions and proves lemmas about orientations of real inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orthogonal
nodes.description: In this file, the orthogonal complement of a submodule K is defined, and basic API established. We make duplicates for Submodule and ClosedSubmodule. Some of the more subtle results about the orthogonal complement are delayed to Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Orthonormal
nodes.description: This file defines orthonormal sets in inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
nodes.descriptionTitle: L² inner product space structure on finite products of inner product spaces
nodes.description: The L² norm on a finite product of inner product spaces is compatible with an inner product $$ \langle x, y\rangle = \sum \langle x_i, y_i \rangle. $$ This is recorded in this file as an inner product space instance on PiLp 2.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Positive
nodes.description: In this file we define when an operator in a Hilbert space is positive. We follow Bourbaki's choice of requiring self adjointness in the definition.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
nodes.descriptionTitle: L² inner product space structure on products of inner product spaces
nodes.description: The L² norm on product of two inner product spaces is compatible with an inner product $$ \langle x, y\rangle = \langle x_1, y_1 \rangle + \langle x_2, y_2 \rangle. $$ This is recorded in this file as an inner product space instance on WithLp 2 (E × F).

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Basic
nodes.description: Given a nonempty subspace K of an inner product space E such that K admits an orthogonal projection, this file constructs K.orthogonalProjection : E →L[𝕜] K, the orthogonal projection of E onto K. This map satisfies: for any point u in E, the point v = K.orthogonalProjection u in K minimizes the distance ‖u - v‖ to u.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.FiniteDimensional
nodes.description: This file contains results about orthogonal projections in finite-dimensional spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Minimal
nodes.description: This file shows the existence of minimizers (also known as the Hilbert projection theorem). This is the key tool that is used to define Submodule.orthogonalProjection in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Reflection
nodes.description: A linear isometry equivalence K.reflection : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E in constructed, by choosing for each u : E, K.reflection u = 2 • K.starProjection u - u.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Submodule
nodes.description: Here, the orthogonal projection is used to prove a series of more subtle lemmas about the orthogonal complement of subspaces of E (the orthogonal complement itself was defined in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Orthogonal.lean) such that they admit orthogonal projections; the lemma Submodule.sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection, stating that for a subspace K of E such that K admits an orthogonal projection we have K ⊔ Kᗮ = ⊤, is a typical example.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Rayleigh
nodes.description: The Rayleigh quotient of a self-adjoint operator T on an inner product space E is the function fun x ↦ ⟪T x, x⟫ / ‖x‖ ^ 2.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Reproducing
nodes.description: This file defines vector-valued reproducing Kernel Hilbert spaces, which are Hilbert spaces of functions, as well as characterizing these spaces in terms of infinite-dimensional positive semidefinite matrices.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Semisimple
nodes.descriptionTitle: Semisimple operators on inner product spaces
nodes.description: This file is a place to gather results related to semisimplicity of linear operators on inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.SingularValues
nodes.descriptionTitle: Singular values for finite-dimensional linear maps
nodes.description: For a linear map T between finite-dimensional inner product spaces E and F, we define the singular values, which are the square roots of the eigenvalues of T.adjoint ∘ₗ T, arranged in descending order and repeated according to their multiplicity.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Spectrum
nodes.description: This file covers the spectral theory of self-adjoint operators on an inner product space.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.StandardSubspace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Standard subspaces of a Hilbert space
nodes.description: This files defines standard subspaces of a complex Hilbert space: a standard subspace S of H is a closed real subspace S such that S ⊓ i S = ⊥ and S ⊔ i S = ⊤. For a standard subspace, one can define a closable operator x + i y ↦ x - i y and develop an analogue of the Tomita-Takesaki modular theory for von Neumann algebras. By considering inclusions of standard subspaces, one can obtain unitary representations of various Lie groups.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.StarOrder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous linear maps on a Hilbert space are a StarOrderedRing
nodes.description: In this file we show that the continuous linear maps on a complex Hilbert space form a StarOrderedRing. Note that they are already equipped with the Loewner partial order. We also prove that, with respect to this partial order, a map is positive if every element of the real spectrum is nonnegative. Consequently, when H is a Hilbert space, then H →L[ℂ] H is equipped with all the usual instances of the continuous functional calculus.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Subspace
nodes.description: This file defines the inner-product structure on a subspace of an inner-product space, and proves some theorems about orthogonal families of subspaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Symmetric
nodes.descriptionTitle: Symmetric linear maps in an inner product space
nodes.description: This file defines and proves basic theorems about symmetric not necessarily bounded operators on an inner product space, i.e linear maps T : E → E such that ∀ x y, ⟪T x, y⟫ = ⟪x, T y⟫.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TensorProduct
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inner product space structure on tensor product spaces
nodes.description: This file provides the inner product space structure on tensor product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Trace
nodes.description: This file contains various results about traces of linear operators in inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.TwoDim
nodes.descriptionTitle: Oriented two-dimensional real inner product spaces
nodes.description: This file defines constructions specific to the geometry of an oriented two-dimensional real inner product space E.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.WeakOperatorTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The weak operator topology in Hilbert spaces
nodes.description: This file gives a few properties of the weak operator topology that are specific to operators on Hilbert spaces. This mostly involves using the Fréchet-Riesz representation to convert between applications of elements of the dual and inner products with vectors in the space.

nodes.label: Analysis.InnerProductSpace.l2Space
nodes.descriptionTitle: Hilbert sum of a family of inner product spaces
nodes.description: Given a family (G : ι → Type) [Π i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (G i)] of inner product spaces, this file equips lp G 2 with an inner product space structure, where lp G 2 consists of those dependent functions f : Π i, G i for which ∑' i, ‖f i‖ ^ 2, the sum of the norms-squared, is summable. This construction is sometimes called the Hilbert sum of the family G. By choosing G to be ι → 𝕜, the Hilbert space ℓ²(ι, 𝕜) may be seen as a special case of this construction.

nodes.label: Analysis.LConvolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convolution of functions using the Lebesgue integral
nodes.description: In this file we define and prove properties about the convolution of two functions using the Lebesgue integral.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.AbsConvex
nodes.description: A set s in a commutative monoid E is called absolutely convex or disked if it is convex and balanced. The importance of absolutely convex sets comes from the fact that every locally convex topological vector space has a basis consisting of absolutely convex sets.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.AbsConvexOpen
nodes.description: A set s in a commutative monoid E equipped with a topology is said to be an absolutely convex open set if it is absolutely convex and open. When E is a topological additive group, the topology coincides with the topology induced by the family of seminorms arising as gauges of absolutely convex open neighborhoods of zero.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.BalancedCoreHull
nodes.description: The balanced core and hull are implemented differently: for the core we take the obvious definition of the union over all balanced sets that are contained in s, whereas for the hull, we take the union over r • s, for r the scalars with ‖r‖ ≤ 1. We show that balancedHull has the defining properties of a hull in Balanced.balancedHull_subset_of_subset and subset_balancedHull. For the core we need slightly stronger assumptions to obtain a characterization as an intersection, this is balancedCore_eq_iInter.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Barrelled
nodes.descriptionTitle: Barrelled spaces and the Banach-Steinhaus theorem / Uniform Boundedness Principle
nodes.description: This file defines barrelled spaces over a NontriviallyNormedField, and proves the Banach-Steinhaus theorem for maps from a barrelled space to a space equipped with a family of seminorms generating the topology (i.e. WithSeminorms q for some family of seminorms q).

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines absorbent and balanced sets.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Bounded
nodes.description: This file defines natural or von Neumann bounded sets and proves elementary properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.ContinuousOfBounded
nodes.description: This file proves that for two topological vector spaces E and F over nontrivially normed fields, if E is first countable, then every locally bounded linear map E →ₛₗ[σ] F is continuous (this is LinearMap.continuous_of_locally_bounded).

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Montel
nodes.description: A Montel space is a topological vector space E that has the Heine-Borel property: every closed and (von Neumann) bounded set is compact.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.PointwiseConvergence
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topology of pointwise convergence is locally convex
nodes.description: We prove that the topology of pointwise convergence is induced by a family of seminorms and that it is locally convex in the topological sense

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Polar
nodes.description: In this file we define the polar set. There are different notions of the polar, we will define the absolute polar. The advantage over the real polar is that we can define the absolute polar for any bilinear form B : E →ₗ[𝕜] F →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜, where 𝕜 is a normed commutative ring and E and F are modules over 𝕜.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.SeparatingDual
nodes.description: We introduce a typeclass SeparatingDual R V, registering that the points of the topological module V over R can be separated by continuous linear forms.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.Separation
nodes.description: In this file we prove the geometric Hahn-Banach theorem. For any two disjoint convex sets, there exists a continuous linear functional separating them, geometrically meaning that we can intercalate a plane between them.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.StrongTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Local convexity of the strong topology
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the strong topology on E →L[ℝ] F is locally convex provided that F is locally convex.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.WeakDual
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weak Dual in Topological Vector Spaces
nodes.description: We prove that the weak topology induced by a bilinear form B : E →ₗ[𝕜] F →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜 is locally convex and we explicitly give a neighborhood basis in terms of the family of seminorms fun x => ‖B x y‖ for y : F.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.WeakOperatorTopology
nodes.description: This file defines a type copy of E →L[𝕜] F (where E and F are topological vector spaces) which is endowed with the weak operator topology (WOT) rather than the topology of bounded convergence (which is the usual one induced by the operator norm in the normed setting). The WOT is defined as the coarsest topology such that the functional fun A => y (A x) is continuous for any x : E and y : StrongDual 𝕜 F.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.WeakSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Closures of convex sets in locally convex spaces
nodes.description: This file contains the standard result that if E is a vector space with two locally convex topologies, then the closure of a convex set is the same in either topology, provided they have the same collection of continuous linear functionals. In particular, the weak closure of a convex set in a locally convex space coincides with the closure in the original topology. Of course, we phrase this in terms of linear maps between locally convex spaces, rather than creating two separate topologies on the same space.

nodes.label: Analysis.LocallyConvex.WithSeminorms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology induced by a family of seminorms
nodes.description: bounded by a finite number of seminorms in E. (existing) topology on E is induced by the seminorms p. by some family of 𝕜-seminorms. If 𝕜 is RCLike, this is equivalent to LocallyConvexSpace 𝕜 E. The terminology is inspired by N. Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques. However, unlike Bourbaki, we do not ask seminorms to be ultrametric when 𝕜 is ultrametric.

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.Hermitian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Hermitian matrices over ℝ and ℂ
nodes.description: This file proves that Hermitian matrices over ℝ and ℂ are exactly the ones whose corresponding linear map is self-adjoint.

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.HermitianFunctionalCalculus
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous Functional Calculus for Hermitian Matrices
nodes.description: This file defines an instance of the continuous functional calculus for Hermitian matrices over an RCLike field 𝕜.

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.LDL
nodes.description: This file proves the LDL-decomposition of matrices: Any positive definite matrix S can be decomposed as S = LDLᴴ where L is a lower-triangular matrix and D is a diagonal matrix.

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.Order

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.PosDef

nodes.label: Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum

nodes.label: Analysis.MeanInequalities
nodes.description: In this file we prove several inequalities for finite sums, including AM-GM inequality, HM-GM inequality, Young's inequality, Hölder inequality, and Minkowski inequality. Versions for integrals of some of these inequalities are available in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/MeanInequalities.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.MeanInequalitiesPow
nodes.description: In this file we prove several mean inequalities for finite sums. Versions for integrals of some of these inequalities are available in MeasureTheory.MeanInequalities.

nodes.label: Analysis.MellinInversion
nodes.description: We derive the Mellin inversion formula as a consequence of the Fourier inversion formula.

nodes.label: Analysis.MellinTransform
nodes.description: We define the Mellin transform of a locally integrable function on Ioi 0, and show it is differentiable in a suitable vertical strip.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.Divisor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Divisor of a meromorphic function
nodes.description: This file defines the divisor of a meromorphic function and proves the most basic lemmas about those divisors. The lemma MeromorphicOn.divisor_restrict guarantees compatibility between restrictions of divisors and of meromorphic functions to subsets of their domain of definition.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.FactorizedRational
nodes.description: This file discusses functions 𝕜 → 𝕜 of the form ∏ᶠ u, (· - u) ^ d u, where d : 𝕜 → ℤ is integer-valued. We show that these "factorized rational functions" are meromorphic in normal form, with divisor equal to d.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.IsolatedZeros
nodes.descriptionTitle: Principles of Isolated Zeros and Identity Principles for Meromorphic Functions
nodes.description: In line with results in Mathlib.Analysis.Analytic.IsolatedZeros and Mathlib.Analysis.Analytic.Uniqueness, this file establishes principles of isolated zeros and identity principles for meromorphic functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.NormalForm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normal form of meromorphic functions and continuous extension
nodes.description: If a function f is meromorphic on U and if g differs from f only along a set that is codiscrete within U, then g is likewise meromorphic. The set of meromorphic functions is therefore huge, and =ᶠ[codiscreteWithin U] defines an equivalence relation.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.Order
nodes.description: This file defines the order of a meromorphic function f at a point z₀, as an element of ℤ ∪ {∞}.

nodes.label: Analysis.Meromorphic.TrailingCoefficient
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Trailing Coefficient of a Meromorphic Function
nodes.description: This file defines the trailing coefficient of a meromorphic function. If f is meromorphic at a point x, the trailing coefficient is defined as the (unique!) value g x for a presentation of f in the form (z - x) ^ order • g z with g analytic at x.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Affine.AddTorsor

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Affine.Ceva

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Affine.ContinuousAffineMap

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Group.Quotient

If S is closed, we provide NormedAddCommGroup (M ⧸ S) (regardless of whether M itself is separated). The two main properties of these structures are the underlying topology is the quotient topology and the projection is a normed group homomorphism which is norm non-increasing (better, it has operator norm exactly one unless S is dense in M).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Group.Tannery
nodes.description: Tannery's theorem gives a sufficient criterion for the limit of an infinite sum (with respect to an auxiliary parameter) to equal the sum of the pointwise limits. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tannery%27s_theorem. It is a special case of the dominated convergence theorem (with the measure chosen to be the counting measure); but we give here a direct proof, in order to avoid some unnecessary hypotheses that appear when specialising the general measure-theoretic result.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Group.ZeroAtInfty
nodes.description: In this file we give a characterization of the predicate zero_at_infty from ZeroAtInftyContinuousMapClass. A continuous map f is zero at infinity if and only if for every ε > 0 there exists a r : ℝ such that for all x : E with r < ‖x‖ it holds that ‖f x‖ < ε.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Lp.LpEquiv
nodes.description: In this file we collect a variety of equivalences among various $L^p$ spaces. In particular, when α is a Fintype, given E : α → Type u and p : ℝ≥0∞, if all E i for i : α are normed, additive commutative groups, there is a natural linear isometric equivalence lpPiLpₗᵢ : lp E p ≃ₗᵢ PiLp p E. In addition, when α is a discrete topological space, the bounded continuous functions α →ᵇ β correspond exactly to lp (fun _ ↦ β) ∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Lp.PiLp
nodes.descriptionTitle: L^p distance on finite products of metric spaces
nodes.description: Given finitely many metric spaces, one can put the max distance on their product, but there is also a whole family of natural distances, indexed by a parameter p : ℝ≥0∞, that also induce the product topology. We define them in this file. For 0 < p < ∞, the distance on Π i, α i is given by $$ d(x, y) = \left(\sum d(x_i, y_i)^p\right)^{1/p}. $$, whereas for p = 0 it is the cardinality of the set ${i | d (x_i, y_i) ≠ 0}$. For p = ∞ the distance is the supremum of the distances.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Lp.ProdLp
nodes.descriptionTitle: L^p distance on products of two metric spaces
nodes.description: Given two metric spaces, one can put the max distance on their product, but there is also a whole family of natural distances, indexed by a parameter p : ℝ≥0∞, that also induce the product topology. We define them in this file. For 0 < p < ∞, the distance on α × β is given by $$ d(x, y) = \left(d(x_1, y_1)^p + d(x_2, y_2)^p\right)^{1/p}. $$ For p = ∞ the distance is the supremum of the distances and p = 0 the distance is the cardinality of the elements that are not equal.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Lp.SmoothApprox

nodes.description: In this file, we prove that Lp functions can be approximated by smooth compactly supported functions for p < ∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Complemented

nodes.description: A submodule p of a topological module E over R is called complemented if there exists a continuous linear projection f : E →ₗ[R] p, ∀ x : p, f x = x. We prove that for a closed subspace of a normed space this condition is equivalent to existence of a closed subspace q such that p ⊓ q = ⊥, p ⊔ q = ⊤. We also prove that a subspace of finite codimension is always a complemented subspace.

nodes.description: In this file we define the inclusion of a normed space into its double strong dual, prove that it is an isometry (for 𝕜 = ℝ or 𝕜 = ℂ), and use the corresponding weak-topology embedding together with Banach–Alaoglu to transfer compactness from the weak-star bidual back to the weak topology.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Dual
nodes.descriptionTitle: Polar sets in the strong dual of a normed space
nodes.description: In this file we study polar sets in the strong dual StrongDual of a normed space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.ENormedSpace
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Extr
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following lemma, see IsMaxFilter.norm_add_sameRay. If f : α → E is a function such that norm ∘ f has a maximum along a filter l at a point c and y is a vector on the same ray as f c, then the function fun x => ‖f x + y‖ has a maximum along l at c.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite-dimensional normed spaces over complete fields
nodes.description: Over a complete nontrivially normed field, in finite dimension, all norms are equivalent and all linear maps are continuous. Moreover, a finite-dimensional subspace is always complete and closed.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.HahnBanach
nodes.description: In this file we prove the analytic Hahn-Banach theorem. For any continuous linear function on a subspace, we can extend it to a function on the entire space without changing its norm.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.MStructure
nodes.description: A projection P on a normed space X is said to be an L-projection (IsLprojection) if, for all x in X, $\|x\| = \|P x\| + \|(1 - P) x\|$.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Multilinear.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Operator norm on the space of continuous multilinear maps
nodes.description: When f is a continuous multilinear map in finitely many variables, we define its norm ‖f‖ as the smallest number such that ‖f m‖ ≤ ‖f‖ ∏ i, ‖m i‖ for all m.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Multilinear.Curry
nodes.descriptionTitle: Currying and uncurrying continuous multilinear maps
nodes.description: We associate to a continuous multilinear map in n+1 variables (i.e., based on Fin n.succ) two curried functions, named f.curryLeft (which is a continuous linear map on E 0 taking values in continuous multilinear maps in n variables) and f.curryRight (which is a continuous multilinear map in n variables taking values in continuous linear maps on E (last n)). The inverse operations are called uncurryLeft and uncurryRight.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.MultipliableUniformlyOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniform convergence of products of functions
nodes.description: We gather some results about the uniform convergence of infinite products, in particular those of the form ∏' i, (1 + f i x) for a sequence f of complex-valued functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Normalize
nodes.description: Function that returns unit length vector that points in the same direction (if the given vector is nonzero vector) or returns zero vector (if the given vector is zero vector).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.PiTensorProduct.InjectiveSeminorm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Injective seminorm on the tensor of a finite family of normed spaces.
nodes.description: Let 𝕜 be a nontrivially normed field and E be a family of normed 𝕜-vector spaces Eᵢ, indexed by a finite type ι. We define a seminorm on ⨂[𝕜] i, Eᵢ, which we call the "injective seminorm". It is chosen to satisfy the following property: for every normed 𝕜-vector space F, the linear equivalence MultilinearMap 𝕜 E F ≃ₗ[𝕜] (⨂[𝕜] i, Eᵢ) →ₗ[𝕜] F expressing the universal property of the tensor product induces an isometric linear equivalence ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 E F ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] (⨂[𝕜] i, Eᵢ) →L[𝕜] F.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.PiTensorProduct.ProjectiveSeminorm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective seminorm on the tensor of a finite family of normed spaces.
nodes.description: Let 𝕜 be a normed field and E be a family of normed 𝕜-vector spaces Eᵢ, indexed by a finite type ι. We define a seminorm on ⨂[𝕜] i, Eᵢ, which we call the "projective seminorm". For x an element of ⨂[𝕜] i, Eᵢ, its projective seminorm is the infimum over all expressions of x as ∑ j, ⨂ₜ[𝕜] mⱼ i (with the mⱼ ∈ Π i, Eᵢ) of ∑ j, Π i, ‖mⱼ i‖.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.RCLike.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normed spaces over R or C
nodes.description: This file is about results on normed spaces over the fields ℝ and ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.RCLike.Extend
nodes.descriptionTitle: Norm properties of the extension of continuous ℝ-linear functionals to 𝕜-linear functionals
nodes.description: This file shows that StrongDual.extendRCLike preserves the norm of the functional.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.RCLike.Real
nodes.description: In this file we prove some theorems about (semi)normed spaces over real numbers.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Ray
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rays in a real normed vector space
nodes.description: In this file we prove some lemmas about the SameRay predicate in case of a real normed space. In this case, for two vectors x y in the same ray, the norm of their sum is equal to the sum of their norms and ‖y‖ • x = ‖x‖ • y.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.RieszLemma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Applications of the Hausdorff distance in normed spaces
nodes.description: Riesz's lemma, stated for a normed space over a normed field: for any closed proper subspace F of E, there is a nonzero x such that ‖x - F‖ is at least r ‖x‖ for any r < 1. This is riesz_lemma.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Shrink
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfer normed algebraic structures from α to Shrink α
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Normed.Module.Shrink.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.Span
nodes.descriptionTitle: The span of a single vector
nodes.description: The equivalence of 𝕜 and 𝕜 • x for x ≠ 0 are defined as continuous linear equivalence and isometry.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.TransferInstance
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfer normed algebraic structures across Equivs
nodes.description: In this file, we transfer a (semi-)normed (additive) commutative group and normed space structures across an equivalence. This continues the pattern set in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/TransferInstance.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Module.WeakDual
nodes.description: Let E be a normed space over a field 𝕜. This file is concerned with properties of the weak-\ topology on the dual of E. By the dual, we mean either of the type synonyms StrongDual 𝕜 E or WeakDual 𝕜 E, depending on whether it is viewed as equipped with its usual operator norm topology or the weak-\ topology.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.MulAction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas for IsBoundedSMul over normed additive groups
nodes.description: Lemmas which hold only in NormedSpace α β are provided in another file.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Asymptotics
nodes.descriptionTitle: Asymptotic statements about the operator norm
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about how operator norm on continuous linear maps interacts with IsBigO.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Banach
nodes.description: This file contains the Banach open mapping theorem, i.e., the fact that a bijective bounded linear map between Banach spaces has a bounded inverse.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.BanachSteinhaus
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Banach-Steinhaus theorem: Uniform Boundedness Principle
nodes.description: Herein we prove the Banach-Steinhaus theorem for normed spaces: any collection of bounded linear maps from a Banach space into a normed space which is pointwise bounded is uniformly bounded.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Operator norm on the space of continuous linear maps
nodes.description: Define the operator (semi)-norm on the space of continuous (semi)linear maps between (semi)-normed spaces, and prove its basic properties. In particular, show that this space is itself a semi-normed space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Bilinear
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas concerning operator norm as applied to bilinear maps E × F → G, interpreted as linear maps E → F → G as usual (and similarly for semilinear variants).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.BoundedLinearMaps
nodes.description: This file defines a class stating that a map between normed vector spaces is (bi)linear and continuous. Instead of asking for continuity, the definition takes the equivalent condition (because the space is normed) that ‖f x‖ is bounded by a multiple of ‖x‖. Hence the "bounded" in the name refers to ‖f x‖/‖x‖ rather than ‖f x‖ itself.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define compact linear operators between two topological vector spaces (TVS).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.FiniteDimension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compact operators and finite dimensional spaces
nodes.description: This file contains results linking IsCompactOperator with FiniteDimensional.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Compact.FredholmAlternative
nodes.description: This file develops the spectral theory of compact operators on Banach spaces. The main result is the Fredholm alternative for compact operators.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.CompleteCodomain
nodes.descriptionTitle: Completeness of spaces of linear and multilinear maps
nodes.description: If E is a nontrivial normed space over a nontrivially normed field 𝕜, and E has a separating dual, then for any normed space F, the completeness of the space of continuous linear maps from E to F is equivalent to the completeness of F.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Completeness
nodes.description: This file contains statements about norms of operators on complete normed spaces, such as a version of the Banach-Alaoglu theorem (ContinuousLinearMap.isCompact_image_coe_closedBall).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Conformal
nodes.description: A continuous linear map between R-normed spaces X and Y IsConformalMap if it is a nonzero multiple of a linear isometry.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousAlgEquiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous (star-)algebra equivalences between continuous endomorphisms are (isometrically) inner
nodes.description: This file shows that continuous (star-)algebra equivalences between continuous endomorphisms are (isometrically) inner. See Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/GeneralLinearGroup/AlgEquiv.lean for the non-continuous version. The proof follows the same idea as the non-continuous version.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousLinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructions of continuous linear maps between (semi-)normed spaces
nodes.description: A fundamental fact about (semi-)linear maps between normed spaces over sensible fields is that continuity and boundedness are equivalent conditions. That is, for normed spaces E, F, a LinearMap f : E →ₛₗ[σ] F is the coercion of some ContinuousLinearMap f' : E →SL[σ] F, if and only if there exists a bound C such that for all x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C ‖x‖.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Extend
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extension of continuous linear maps on Banach spaces
nodes.description: In this file we provide two different ways to extend a continuous linear map defined on a dense subspace to the entire Banach space.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.LinearIsometry
nodes.description: In this file we define LinearIsometry σ₁₂ E E₂ (notation: E →ₛₗᵢ[σ₁₂] E₂) to be a semilinear isometric embedding of E into E₂ and LinearIsometryEquiv (notation: E ≃ₛₗᵢ[σ₁₂] E₂) to be a semilinear isometric equivalence between E and E₂. The notation for the associated purely linear concepts is E →ₗᵢ[R] E₂, E ≃ₗᵢ[R] E₂, and E →ₗᵢ⋆[R] E₂, E ≃ₗᵢ⋆[R] E₂ for the star-linear versions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Mul
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about operator norms in normed algebras
nodes.description: This file (split off from OperatorNorm.lean) contains results about the operator norm of multiplication and scalar-multiplication operations in normed algebras and normed modules.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.NNNorm
nodes.description: Operator norm as an NNNorm, i.e. taking values in non-negative reals.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.NormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Operator norm for maps on normed spaces
nodes.description: This file contains statements about operator norm for which it really matters that the underlying space has a norm (rather than just a seminorm).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Operator.Prod
nodes.description: Interaction of operator norm with Cartesian products.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Order.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define classes for fields and groups that are both normed and ordered. These are mostly useful to avoid diamonds during type class inference.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Order.Hom.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines constructions that upgrade (Comm)Group to (Semi)Normed(Comm)Group using a Group(Semi)normClass when the codomain is the reals.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Order.Hom.Ultra
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing nonarchimedean (ultrametric) normed groups from nonarchimedean normed homs
nodes.description: This file defines constructions that upgrade Add(Comm)Group to (Semi)NormedAdd(Comm)Group using an AddGroup(Semi)normClass when the codomain is the reals and the hom is nonarchimedean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Order.Lattice
nodes.description: Motivated by the theory of Banach Lattices, we then define NormedLatticeAddCommGroup as a lattice with a covariant normed group addition satisfying the solid axiom.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Order.UpperLower
nodes.description: The topological closure and interior of an upper/lower/order-connected set is an upper/lower/order-connected set (with the notable exception of the closure of an order-connected set).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define (semi)normed rings. We also prove some theorems about these definitions.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite order elements in normed rings.
nodes.description: A finite order element in a normed ring has norm 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.InfiniteProd
nodes.description: This file proves a dominated convergence theorem for infinite products of terms of the form (1 + f n k) in a complete normed commutative ring, by reducing to the additive version (Tannery's theorem) via the formal expansion ∏ (1 + f i) = ∑ₛ ∏ᵢ∈ₛ f i.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.InfiniteSum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multiplying two infinite sums in a normed ring
nodes.description: In this file, we prove various results about (∑' x : ι, f x) (∑' y : ι', g y) in a normed ring. There are similar results proven in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/Ring.lean (e.g. tsum_mul_tsum), but in a normed ring we get summability results which aren't true in general.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Int
nodes.description: This file contains basic facts about the integers as normed ring.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Lemmas
nodes.description: In this file we continue building the theory of (semi)normed rings.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.TransferInstance
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfer normed algebraic structures across Equivs
nodes.description: In this file, we transfer a (semi-)normed ring structure across an equivalence. This continues the pattern set in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/TransferInstance.lean.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Ultra
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ultrametric norms on rings where the norm of one is one
nodes.description: This file contains results on the behavior of norms in ultrametric normed rings. The norm must send one to one.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.Units
nodes.descriptionTitle: The group of units of a complete normed ring
nodes.description: This file contains the basic theory for the group of units (invertible elements) of a complete normed ring (Banach algebras being a notable special case).

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Ring.WithAbs
nodes.description: WithAbs v is a copy of the semiring R with the same underlying ring structure, but assigned v-dependent instances (such as NormedRing) where v is an absolute value on R.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.AlgebraNorm
nodes.description: We define algebra norms and multiplicative algebra norms.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.FiniteExtension
nodes.description: In this file, we prove BGR, Lemma 3.2.1./3 : if K is a normed field with a nonarchimedean power-multiplicative norm and L/K is a finite extension, then there exists at least one power-multiplicative K-algebra norm on L extending the norm on K.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.InvariantExtension
nodes.description: Let K be a nonarchimedean normed field and L/K be a finite algebraic extension. In the comments, ‖ ⬝ ‖ denotes any power-multiplicative K-algebra norm on L extending the norm on K.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.IsPowMulFaithful
nodes.description: In this file, we prove BGR, Proposition 3.1.5/1: if R is a normed commutative ring and f₁ and f₂ are two power-multiplicative R-algebra norms on S, then if f₁ and f₂ are equivalent on every subring R[y] for y : S, it follows that f₁ = f₂.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.RingSeminorm
nodes.description: This file defines seminorms and norms on rings. These definitions are useful when one needs to consider multiple (semi)norms on a given ring.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.SeminormFromBounded
nodes.description: In this file, we prove BGR, Proposition 1.2.1/2 : given a nonzero additive group seminorm on a commutative ring R such that for some c : ℝ and every x y : R, the inequality f (x y) ≤ c f x f y) is satisfied, we create a ring seminorm on R.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.SeminormFromConst
nodes.description: In this file, we prove BGR, Proposition 1.3.2/2 : starting from a power-multiplicative seminorm on a commutative ring R and a nonzero c : R, we create a new power-multiplicative seminorm for which c is multiplicative.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.SmoothingSeminorm
nodes.description: In this file, we prove BGR, Proposition 1.3.2/1: if μ is a nonarchimedean seminorm on a commutative ring R, then iInf (fun (n : PNat), (μ(x ^ (n : ℕ))) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) is a power-multiplicative nonarchimedean seminorm on R.

nodes.label: Analysis.Normed.Unbundled.SpectralNorm
nodes.descriptionTitle: The spectral norm and the norm extension theorem
nodes.description: This file shows that if K is a nonarchimedean normed field and L/K is an algebraic extension, then there is a natural extension of the norm on K to a K-algebra norm on L, the so-called spectral norm. The spectral norm of an element of L only depends on its minimal polynomial over K, so for K ⊆ L ⊆ M two extensions of K, the spectral norm on M restricts to the spectral norm on L. This work can be used to uniquely extend the p-adic norm on ℚ_[p] to an algebraic closure of ℚ_[p], for example.
