nodes.label: Analysis.ODE.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral curves of vector fields on a normed vector space
nodes.description: Let E be a normed vector space and v : ℝ → E → E be a time-dependent vector field on E. An integral curve of v is a function γ : ℝ → E such that the derivative of γ at t equals v t (γ t). The integral curve may only be defined for all t within some subset of ℝ.

nodes.label: Analysis.ODE.DiscreteGronwall
nodes.description: Various forms of the discrete Grönwall inequality, bounding solutions to recurrence inequalities u (n+1) ≤ c n u n + b n and u (n+1) ≤ (1 + c n) u n + b n.

nodes.label: Analysis.ODE.Gronwall
nodes.description: The main technical result of this file is the Grönwall-like inequality norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le. It states that if f : ℝ → E satisfies ‖f a‖ ≤ δ and ∀ x ∈ [a, b), ‖f' x‖ ≤ K ‖f x‖ + ε, then for all x ∈ [a, b] we have ‖f x‖ ≤ δ exp (K x) + (ε / K) (exp (K x) - 1).

nodes.label: Analysis.ODE.PicardLindelof
nodes.description: We prove the (local) existence of integral curves and flows to time-dependent vector fields.

nodes.label: Analysis.ODE.Transform
nodes.descriptionTitle: Translation and scaling of integral curves
nodes.description: New integral curves may be constructed by translating or scaling the domain of an existing integral curve.

nodes.label: Analysis.Oscillation
nodes.description: In this file we define the oscillation of a function f: E → F at a point x of E. (E is required to be a TopologicalSpace and F a PseudoEMetricSpace.) The oscillation of f at x is defined to be the infimum of diam f '' N for all neighborhoods N of x. We also define oscillationWithin f D x, which is the oscillation at x of f restricted to D.

nodes.label: Analysis.PSeries
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the series ∑' k in ℕ, 1 / k ^ p converges if and only if p > 1. The proof is based on the Cauchy condensation test: ∑ k, f k converges if and only if so does ∑ k, 2 ^ k f (2 ^ k). We prove this test in NNReal.summable_condensed_iff and summable_condensed_iff_of_nonneg, then use it to prove summable_one_div_rpow. After this transformation, a p-series turns into a geometric series.

nodes.label: Analysis.PSeriesComplex
nodes.description: Here we show convergence of ∑ n : ℕ, 1 / n ^ p for complex p. This is done in a separate file rather than in Analysis.PSeries in order to keep the prerequisites of the former relatively light.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits related to polynomial and rational functions
nodes.description: This file proves basic facts about limits of polynomial and rational functions. The main result is Polynomial.isEquivalent_atTop_lead, which states that for any polynomial P of degree n with leading coefficient a, the corresponding polynomial function is equivalent to a x^n as x goes to +∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.CauchyBound
nodes.description: The bound is given by Polynomial.cauchyBound, which for a_n x^n + a_(n-1) x^(n - 1) + ⋯ + a_0 is 1 + max_(0 ≤ i < n) a_i / a_n.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.Factorization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Factorization of monic polynomials of given degree
nodes.description: This file contains two main results:

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.Fourier
nodes.description: We define an algebra map from ℂ[X] to the MeasureTheory.Lp (with p := 2) space on the additive circle and show that it sends monomials to the Fourier basis. From this, we derive that polynomial coefficients match Fourier coefficients and prove Parseval's identity for polynomials.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.MahlerMeasure
nodes.description: In this file we define the Mahler measure of a polynomial over ℂ[X] and prove some basic properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.Norm
nodes.description: In this file we define the sup norm on Polynomials based on their coefficients as well as several basic results about this norm. We note that this is often called the _(naive) height_ of the polynomial in the literature.

nodes.label: Analysis.Polynomial.Order
nodes.description: This file proves that a polynomial has a fixed sign beyond its largest or smallest root.

nodes.label: Analysis.Quaternion
nodes.description: In this file we define the following structures on the space ℍ := ℍ[ℝ] of quaternions:

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: RCLike: a typeclass for ℝ or ℂ
nodes.description: This file defines the typeclass RCLike intended to have only two instances: ℝ and ℂ. It is meant for definitions and theorems which hold for both the real and the complex case, and in particular when the real case follows directly from the complex case by setting re to id, im to zero and so on. Its API follows closely that of ℂ.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.BoundedContinuous
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results on bounded continuous functions with RCLike values
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.RCLike.BoundedContinuous.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.ContinuousMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Mapping C(X, ℝ) to C(X, 𝕜) and back
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions for ContinuousMap.realToRCLike and ContinuousMap.rclikeToReal, which map C(X, ℝ) to C(X, 𝕜) and back for any RCLike 𝕜.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.Extend
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extending an ℝ-linear functional to a 𝕜-linear functional
nodes.description: In this file we provide a way to extend a (optionally, continuous) ℝ-linear map to a (continuous) 𝕜-linear map in a way that bounds the norm by the norm of the original map, when 𝕜 is either ℝ (the extension is trivial) or ℂ. We formulate the extension uniformly, by assuming RCLike 𝕜.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.Inner
nodes.descriptionTitle: L2 inner product of finite sequences
nodes.description: This file defines the weighted L2 inner product of functions f g : ι → R where ι is a fintype as ∑ i, conj (f i) g i. This convention (conjugation on the left) matches the inner product coming from RCLike.innerProductSpace.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.Lemmas
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.RCLike.Lemmas.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.Sqrt
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions Complex.sqrt and RCLike.sqrt and builds basic API.

nodes.label: Analysis.RCLike.TangentCone
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relationships between unique differentiability over ℝ and ℂ
nodes.description: A set of unique differentiability for ℝ is also a set of unique differentiability for ℂ (or for a general field satisfying IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜).

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Cardinality
nodes.description: This file shows that the real numbers have cardinality continuum, i.e. #ℝ = 𝔠.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Hyperreal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction of the hyperreal numbers as an ultraproduct of real sequences
nodes.description: We define the Hyperreal numbers as quotients of sequences ℕ → ℝ by an ultrafilter. These form a field, and we prove some of their basic properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.OfDigits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Representation of reals in positional system
nodes.description: This file defines Real.ofDigits and Real.digits functions which allows to work with the representations of reals as sequences of digits in positional system.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Pi.Bounds
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas which establish bounds on Real.pi. Notably, these include pi_gt_sqrtTwoAddSeries and pi_lt_sqrtTwoAddSeries, which bound π using series; numerical bounds on π such as pi_gt_d2 and pi_lt_d2 (more precise versions are given, too).

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Pi.Chudnovsky
nodes.description: This file defines the infinite sum in Chudnovsky's formula for computing π⁻¹. It does not (yet!) contain a proof; anyone is welcome to adopt this problem, but at present we are a long way off.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Pi.Irrational
nodes.description: The main result of this file is irrational_pi.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Pi.Leibniz
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Real.Pi.Leibniz.

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Pi.Wallis
nodes.description: This file establishes the Wallis product for π (Real.tendsto_prod_pi_div_two). Our proof is largely about analyzing the behaviour of the sequence ∫ x in 0..π, sin x ^ n as n → ∞. See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallis_product

nodes.label: Analysis.Real.Spectrum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some lemmas on the spectrum and quasispectrum of elements and positivity
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.Real.Spectrum.

nodes.label: Analysis.Seminorm
nodes.description: This file defines seminorms.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Arcosh
nodes.description: In this file we define an inverse of cosh as a function from $[0, ∞)$ to $[1, ∞)$.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ArithmeticGeometricMean
nodes.description: Starting with two nonnegative real numbers, repeatedly replace them with their arithmetic and geometric means. By the AM-GM inequality, the smaller number (geometric mean) will monotonically increase and the larger number (arithmetic mean) will monotonically decrease.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Arsinh
nodes.description: In this file we prove that sinh is bijective and hence has an inverse, arsinh.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Artanh
nodes.description: In this file we define an inverse of tanh as a function from ℝ to (-1, 1).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Bernstein
nodes.description: We prove that the Bernstein approximations for a continuous function f : C([0,1], E) taking values in a locally convex vector space converge uniformly to f as n tends to infinity. This statement directly applies to the cases when the codomain is a (semi)normed space or, more generally, has a topology defined by a family of seminorms.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.BinaryEntropy
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of Shannon q-ary entropy and binary entropy functions
nodes.description: The binary entropy function binEntropy p := - p log p - (1 - p) log (1 - p) is the Shannon entropy of a Bernoulli random variable with success probability p.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Choose
nodes.description: This file proves asymptotic theorems for binomial coefficients and factorial variants.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.CompareExp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Growth estimates on x ^ y for complex x, y
nodes.description: Let l be a filter on ℂ such that Complex.re tends to infinity along l and Complex.im z grows at a subexponential rate compared to Complex.re z. Then

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Analytic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Various complex special functions are analytic
nodes.description: log, and cpow are analytic, since they are differentiable.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Arctan
nodes.description: This file defines the complex arctangent Complex.arctan as $$\arctan z = -\frac i2 \log \frac{1 + zi}{1 - zi}$$ and shows that it extends Real.arctan to the complex plane. Its Taylor series expansion $$\arctan z = \frac{(-1)^n}{2n + 1} z^{2n + 1},\ |z|<1$$ is proved in Complex.hasSum_arctan.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Arg
nodes.descriptionTitle: The argument of a complex number.
nodes.description: We define arg : ℂ → ℝ, returning a real number in the range $(-π, π]$, such that for x ≠ 0, sin (arg x) = x.im / x.abs and cos (arg x) = x.re / x.abs, while arg 0 defaults to 0

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Circle
nodes.description: In this file we prove some basic lemmas about Circle.exp and the restriction of Complex.arg to the unit circle. These two maps define a partial equivalence between Circle and ℝ, see Circle.argPartialEquiv and Circle.argEquiv, that sends the whole circle to (-π, π].

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.CircleAddChar
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additive characters valued in the unit circle
nodes.description: This file defines additive characters, valued in the unit circle, from either

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.CircleMap
nodes.description: This file defines the circle map $θ ↦ c + R e^{θi}$, a parametrization of a circle.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Log
nodes.description: Basic properties, relationship with exp.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.LogBounds
nodes.description: We show that log (1+z) differs from its Taylor polynomial up to degree n by at most ‖z‖^(n+1)/((n+1)(1-‖z‖)) when ‖z‖ < 1; see Complex.norm_log_sub_logTaylor_le.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.LogDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of the complex log function
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.LogDeriv.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Abs
nodes.descriptionTitle: Absolute value defined via the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file defines the absolute value via the non-unital continuous functional calculus and provides basic API.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.ExpLog
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.ExpLog.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The exponential and logarithm based on the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file defines the logarithm via the continuous functional calculus (CFC) and builds its API. This allows one to take logs of matrices, operators, elements of a C⋆-algebra, etc.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.ExpLog.Order
nodes.descriptionTitle: Order properties of the operator logarithm
nodes.description: This file shows that the logarithm is operator monotone and concave, i.e. that CFC.log is monotone and concave on the strictly positive elements of a unital C⋆-algebra.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.PosPart.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The positive (and negative) parts of a selfadjoint element in a C⋆-algebra
nodes.description: This file defines the positive and negative parts of a selfadjoint element in a C⋆-algebra via the continuous functional calculus and develops the basic API, including the uniqueness of the positive and negative parts.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.PosPart.Isometric
nodes.descriptionTitle: Facts about CFC.posPart and CFC.negPart involving norms
nodes.description: This file collects various facts about the positive and negative parts of elements of a C⋆-algebra that involve the norm.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Real powers defined via the continuous functional calculus
nodes.description: This file defines real powers via the continuous functional calculus (CFC) and builds its API. This allows one to take real powers of matrices, operators, elements of a C⋆-algebra, etc. The square root is also defined via the non-unital CFC.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.ConjSqrt
nodes.descriptionTitle: Conjugating by the square root of a positive element in a C⋆-algebra
nodes.description: This file defines conjSqrt c a as sqrt c a sqrt c, and develops API for this operation.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.IntegralRepresentation
nodes.description: This file contains an integral representation of the rpow function between 0 and 1: we show that there exists a measure on ℝ such that x ^ p = ∫ t, rpowIntegrand₀₁ p t x ∂μ for the integrand rpowIntegrand₀₁ p t x := t ^ p (t⁻¹ - (t + x)⁻¹).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.Isometric
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of rpow and sqrt over an algebra with an isometric CFC
nodes.description: This file collects results about CFC.rpow, CFC.nnrpow and CFC.sqrt that use facts that rely on an isometric continuous functional calculus.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.Order
nodes.description: This file shows that a ↦ a ^ p is monotone for p ∈ [0, 1], where a is an element of a C⋆-algebra. The proof makes use of the integral representation of rpow in Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.IntegralRepresentation.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.RingInverseOrder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Order properties of Ring.inverse in C⋆-algebras
nodes.description: This file shows that Ring.inverse is convex on strictly positive operators.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Elliptic.Weierstrass
nodes.description: The summands of ℘ sums to ℘ locally uniformly.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exp
nodes.description: In this file we prove continuity of Complex.exp and Real.exp. We also prove a few facts about limits of Real.exp at infinity.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ExpDeriv
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Complex.exp and Real.exp are analytic functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exponential
nodes.descriptionTitle: Calculus results on exponential in a Banach algebra
nodes.description: In this file, we prove basic properties about the derivative of the exponential map exp in a Banach algebra 𝔸 over a field 𝕂. We keep them separate from the main file Analysis.Normed.Algebra.Exponential in order to minimize dependencies.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the Γ function (of a real or complex variable s). We define this by Euler's integral Γ(s) = ∫ x in Ioi 0, exp (-x) x ^ (s - 1) in the range where this integral converges (i.e., for 0 < s in the real case, and 0 < re s in the complex case).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Beta
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Beta function, and further properties of the Gamma function
nodes.description: In this file we define the Beta integral, relate Beta and Gamma functions, and prove some refined properties of the Gamma function using these relations.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.BohrMollerup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convexity properties of the Gamma function
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that Gamma and log ∘ Gamma are convex functions on the positive real line. We then prove the Bohr-Mollerup theorem, which characterises Gamma as the unique positive-real-valued, log-convex function on the positive reals satisfying f (x + 1) = x f x and f 1 = 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Deligne
nodes.description: In the theory of L-series one frequently encounters the following functions (of a complex variable s) introduced in Deligne's landmark paper Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales:

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Deriv
nodes.description: This file shows that the (complex) Γ function is complex-differentiable at all s : ℂ with s ∉ {-n : n ∈ ℕ}, as well as the real counterpart.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Digamma
nodes.description: This file defines the digamma function as the logarithmic derivative of the Gamma function and proves some basic properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gaussian.FourierTransform
nodes.description: We prove that the Fourier transform of the Gaussian function is another Gaussian:

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gaussian.GaussianIntegral
nodes.description: We prove various versions of the formula for the Gaussian integral: ∫ x:ℝ, exp (-b x^2) = (π / b) ^ (1 / 2).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gaussian.PoissonSummation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Poisson summation applied to the Gaussian
nodes.description: In Real.tsum_exp_neg_mul_int_sq and Complex.tsum_exp_neg_mul_int_sq, we use Poisson summation to prove the identity

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ImproperIntegrals
nodes.description: This file contains some integrability results, and evaluations of integrals, over ℝ or over half-infinite intervals in ℝ.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrability.Basic
nodes.description: This file establishes basic facts about the interval integrability of special functions, including powers and the logarithm.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrability.LogMeromorphic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrability for Logarithms of Meromorphic Functions
nodes.description: We establish integrability for functions of the form log ‖meromorphic‖. In the real setting, these functions are interval integrable over every interval of the real line. This implies in particular that logarithms of trigonometric functions are interval integrable. In the complex setting, the functions are circle integrable over every circle in the complex plane.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrals.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains proofs of the integrals of various specific functions. This includes: Wallis product for pi)

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrals.LogTrigonometric
nodes.description: This file computes special values of the integral of log ∘ sin. Given that the indefinite integral involves the dilogarithm, this can be seen as computing special values of Li₂.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrals.PosLogEqCircleAverage
nodes.descriptionTitle: Representation of log⁺ as a Circle Average
nodes.description: If a is any complex number, circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_posLog represents log⁺ a as the circle average of log ‖· - a‖ over the unit circle.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.JapaneseBracket
nodes.description: In this file, we show that Japanese bracket $(1 + \|x\|^2)^{1/2}$ can be estimated from above and below by $1 + \|x\|$. The functions $(1 + \|x\|^2)^{-r/2}$ and $(1 + |x|)^{-r}$ are integrable provided that r is larger than the dimension.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Base
nodes.description: In this file we define Real.logb to be the logarithm of a real number in a given base b. We define this as the division of the natural logarithms of the argument and the base, so that we have a globally defined function with logb b 0 = 0, logb b (-x) = logb b x, logb 0 x = 0, and logb (-b) x = logb b x.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define Real.log to be the logarithm of a real number. As usual, we extend it from its domain (0, +∞) to a globally defined function. We choose to do it so that log 0 = 0 and log (-x) = log x.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative and series expansion of real logarithm
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Real.log is infinitely smooth at all nonzero x : ℝ. We also prove that the series ∑' n : ℕ, x ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1) converges to (-Real.log (1 - x)) for all x : ℝ, |x| < 1.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.ENNRealLog
nodes.description: We define log as an extension of the logarithm of a positive real to the extended nonnegative reals ℝ≥0∞. The function takes values in the extended reals EReal, with log 0 = ⊥ and log ⊤ = ⊤.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.ENNRealLogExp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of the extended logarithm and exponential
nodes.description: We prove that log and exp define order isomorphisms between ℝ≥0∞ and EReal.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.ERealExp
nodes.description: We define exp as an extension of the exponential of a real to the extended reals EReal. The function takes values in the extended nonnegative reals ℝ≥0∞, with exp ⊥ = 0 and exp ⊤ = ⊤.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.InvLog
nodes.description: We prove properties of the function x ↦ (log x)⁻¹.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Monotone
nodes.description: In this file we describe the tonality of the logarithm function when multiplied by functions of the form x ^ a.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.NegMulLog
nodes.descriptionTitle: The functions x ↦ x log x and x ↦ - x log x
nodes.description: The purpose of this file is to record basic analytic properties of

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.PosLog
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Positive Part of the Logarithm
nodes.description: This file defines the function Real.posLog = r ↦ max 0 (log r) and introduces the notation log⁺. For a finite length-n sequence f i of reals, it establishes the following standard estimates.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.RpowTendsto
nodes.descriptionTitle: The logarithm as a limit of powers
nodes.description: This file shows that the logarithm can be expressed as a limit of powers, namely that p⁻¹ (x ^ p - 1) tends to log x as p tends to zero for positive x.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Summable
nodes.description: We give conditions under which the logarithms of a summable sequence are summable. We also use this to relate summability of f to multipliability of 1 + f.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.MulExpNegMulSq
nodes.description: mulExpNegMulSq is the mapping fun (ε : ℝ) (x : ℝ) => x Real.exp (- (ε x x)). By composition, it can be used to transform a function g : E → ℝ into a bounded function mulExpNegMulSq ε ∘ g : E → ℝ = fun x => g x Real.exp (-ε g x g x) with useful boundedness and convergence properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.MulExpNegMulSqIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of the integral of mulExpNegMulSq
nodes.description: The mapping mulExpNegMulSq can be used to transform a function g : E → ℝ into a bounded function mulExpNegMulSq ε ∘ g : E → ℝ = fun x => g x Real.exp (-ε g x g x). This file contains results on the integral of mulExpNegMulSq g ε with respect to a finite measure P.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.NonIntegrable
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the derivative of a function that tends to infinity is not interval integrable, see not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_filter and not_intervalIntegrable_of_tendsto_norm_atTop_of_deriv_isBigO_punctured. Then we apply the latter lemma to prove that the function fun x => x⁻¹ is integrable on a..b if and only if a = b or 0 ∉ [a, b].

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.OrdinaryHypergeometric
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ordinary hypergeometric function in a Banach algebra
nodes.description: In this file, we define ordinaryHypergeometric, the _ordinary_ or _Gaussian_ hypergeometric function in a topological algebra 𝔸 over a field 𝕂 given by: $$ _2\mathrm{F}_1(a\ b\ c : \mathbb{K}, x : \mathbb{A}) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(a)_n(b)_n}{(c)_n} \frac{x^n}{n!} \,, $$ with $(a)_n$ is the ascending Pochhammer symbol (see ascPochhammer).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pochhammer
nodes.description: This file proves analysis theorems for Pochhammer polynomials.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.PolarCoord
nodes.description: We define polar coordinates, as an open partial homeomorphism in ℝ^2 between ℝ^2 - (-∞, 0] and (0, +∞) × (-π, π). Its inverse is given by (r, θ) ↦ (r cos θ, r sin θ).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.PolynomialExp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits of P(x) / e ^ x for a polynomial P
nodes.description: In this file we prove that $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{P(x)}{e^x}=0$ for any polynomial P.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Asymptotics
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and asymptotics of power functions at +∞
nodes.description: This file contains results about the limiting behaviour of power functions at +∞. For convenience some results on asymptotics as x → 0 (those which are not just continuity statements) are also located here.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Complex
nodes.description: We construct the power functions x ^ y, where x and y are complex numbers.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Continuity
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about continuity of the power functions on ℂ, ℝ, ℝ≥0, and ℝ≥0∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Deriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of power function on ℂ, ℝ, ℝ≥0, and ℝ≥0∞
nodes.description: We also prove differentiability and provide derivatives for the power functions x ^ y.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: The integral of the real power of a nonnegative function
nodes.description: In this file, we give a common application of the layer cake formula --- a representation of the integral of the p:th power of a nonnegative function f: ∫ f(ω)^p ∂μ(ω) = p ∫ t^(p-1) μ {ω | f(ω) ≥ t} dt.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.NNReal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Power function on ℝ≥0 and ℝ≥0∞
nodes.description: We construct the power functions x ^ y where

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.NthRootLemmas
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Nat.nthRoot n a is indeed the floor of ⁿ√a.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
nodes.description: We construct the power functions x ^ y, where x and y are real numbers.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sigmoid
nodes.description: In this file we define the sigmoid function x : ℝ ↦ (1 + exp (-x))⁻¹ and prove some of its analytic properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.SmoothTransition
nodes.description: In this file we construct two infinitely smooth functions with properties that an analytic function cannot have:

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Sqrt
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Real.sqrt is infinitely smooth at all points x ≠ 0 and provide some dot-notation lemmas.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Stirling
nodes.description: This file proves Stirling's formula for the factorial. It states that $n!$ grows asymptotically like $\sqrt{2\pi n}(\frac{n}{e})^n$.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Angle
nodes.description: In this file we define Real.Angle to be the quotient group ℝ/2πℤ and prove a few simple lemmas about trigonometric functions and angles.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Arctan
nodes.description: Inequalities, identities and Real.tan as an OpenPartialHomeomorph between (-(π / 2), π / 2) and the whole line.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.ArctanDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of the tan and arctan functions.
nodes.description: Continuity and derivatives of the tangent and arctangent functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of π.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Bounds
nodes.description: This file contains upper and lower bounds for real trigonometric functions in terms of polynomials. See Trigonometric.Basic for more elementary inequalities, establishing the ranges of these functions, and their monotonicity in suitable intervals.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Analysis.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multiple angle formulas in terms of Chebyshev polynomials
nodes.description: This file gives the trigonometric characterizations of Chebyshev polynomials, for the real (Real.cos) and complex (Complex.cos) cosine and the real (Real.cosh) and complex (Complex.cosh) hyperbolic cosine.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.ChebyshevGauss
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chebyshev polynomials over the reals: Chebyshev–Gauss
nodes.description: The Chebyshev–Gauss property calculates an integral of a polynomial of degree < 2 n with respect to the weight function √(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹ supported on [-1, 1] by a sum over appropriate evaluations of the polynomial.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.Extremal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chebyshev polynomials over the reals: some extremal properties
nodes.description: following proof in https://math.stackexchange.com/a/978145/1277

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.Orthogonality
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chebyshev polynomials over the reals: orthogonality
nodes.description: Chebyshev T polynomials are orthogonal with respect to √(1 - x ^ 2)⁻¹.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Chebyshev.RootsExtrema
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chebyshev polynomials over the reals: roots and extrema
nodes.description: Show that the bound on T_n^{(k)} (x) is achieved only at x = ±1

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Complex
nodes.description: Basic facts and derivatives for the complex trigonometric functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.ComplexDeriv
nodes.description: Basic facts and derivatives for the complex trigonometric functions.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Cotangent
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the cotangent function, including useful series expansions. In particular, we prove that π cot (π z) = π I - 2 π I ∑' n : ℕ, Complex.exp (2 π I z) ^ n as well as the infinite sum representation of cotangent (also known as the Mittag-Leffler expansion): π cot (π z) = 1 / z + ∑' n : ℕ+, (1 / (z - n) + 1 / (z + n)).

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Deriv
nodes.description: The differentiability of the usual trigonometric functions is proved, and their derivatives are computed.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.DerivHyp
nodes.description: The differentiability of the hyperbolic trigonometric functions is proved, and their derivatives are computed.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.EulerSineProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Euler's infinite product for the sine function
nodes.description: This file proves the infinite product formula

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Inverse
nodes.description: See also Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Arctan for the inverse tan function. (This is delayed as it is easier to set up after developing complex trigonometric functions.)

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.InverseDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: derivatives of the inverse trigonometric functions
nodes.description: Derivatives of arcsin and arccos.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Meromorphic
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Meromorphic.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Series
nodes.descriptionTitle: Trigonometric functions as sums of infinite series
nodes.description: In this file we express trigonometric functions in terms of their series expansion.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Sinc
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of the sinc function and some of its properties.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.ArithmeticGeometric
nodes.description: An arithmetic-geometric sequence is a sequence defined by the recurrence relation u (n + 1) = a u n + b.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: A collection of specific limit computations
nodes.description: This file, by design, is independent of NormedSpace in the import hierarchy. It contains important specific limit computations in metric spaces, in ordered rings/fields, and in specific instances of these such as ℝ, ℝ≥0 and ℝ≥0∞.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.Fibonacci
nodes.descriptionTitle: The ratio of consecutive Fibonacci numbers
nodes.description: We prove that the ratio of consecutive Fibonacci numbers tends to the golden ratio.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.FloorPow
nodes.description: We state several auxiliary results pertaining to sequences of the form ⌊c^n⌋₊.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.Normed
nodes.descriptionTitle: A collection of specific limit computations
nodes.description: This file contains important specific limit computations in (semi-)normed groups/rings/spaces, as well as such computations in ℝ when the natural proof passes through a fact about normed spaces.

nodes.label: Analysis.SpecificLimits.RCLike
nodes.descriptionTitle: A collection of specific limit computations for RCLike
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Analysis.SpecificLimits.RCLike.

nodes.label: Analysis.Subadditive
nodes.description: A subadditive sequence u : ℕ → ℝ is a sequence satisfying u (m + n) ≤ u m + u n for all m, n. We define this notion as Subadditive u, and prove in Subadditive.tendsto_lim that, if u n / n is bounded below, then it converges to a limit (that we denote by Subadditive.lim for convenience). This result is known as Fekete's lemma in the literature.

nodes.label: Analysis.SumIntegralComparisons
nodes.description: It is often the case that error terms in analysis can be computed by comparing an infinite sum to the improper integral of an antitone function. This file will eventually enable that.

nodes.label: Analysis.SumIntegralExpDecay
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bounds for sums and integrals of x ^ k exp (-c x)
nodes.description: We bound the integral and sums of x ^ k exp (-c x) by k ! / c ^ (k + 1), using the Gamma function.

nodes.label: Analysis.SumOverResidueClass
nodes.description: We consider infinite sums over functions f on ℕ, restricted to a residue class mod m.

nodes.label: Analysis.VonNeumannAlgebra.Basic
nodes.description: We give the "abstract" and "concrete" definitions of a von Neumann algebra. We still have a major project ahead of us to show the equivalence between these definitions!

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines some of the Grothendieck Axioms for abelian categories, and proves basic facts about them.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Colim
nodes.description: In this file, we shall study exactness properties of colimits. First, we translate the assumption that colim : (J ⥤ C) ⥤ C preserves monomorphisms (resp. preserves epimorphisms, resp. is exact) into statements involving arbitrary cocones instead of the ones given by the colimit API. We also show that when an inductive system involves only monomorphisms, then the "inclusion" morphism into the colimit is also a monomorphism (assuming J is filtered and C satisfies AB5).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Connected
nodes.description: If c is a cocone over a functor J ⥤ C and f : X ⟶ c.pt, then for every j : J we can take the pullback of c.ι.app j and f. This gives a new cocone with cone point X. We show that if c is a colimit cocone, then this is again a colimit cocone as long as J is connected and C has exact colimits of shape J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.FunctorCategory
nodes.description: This file proves that, when the relevant limits and colimits exist, exactness of limits and colimits carries over from A to the functor category C ⥤ A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Indization
nodes.descriptionTitle: AB axioms in the category of ind-objects
nodes.description: We show that Ind C satisfies Grothendieck's axiom AB5 if C has finite limits and deduce that Ind C is Grothendieck abelian if C is small and abelian.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Sheaf
nodes.description: If J is a Grothendieck topology on a small category C : Type v, and A : Type u₁ (with Category.{v} A) is a Grothendieck abelian category, then Sheaf J A is a Grothendieck abelian category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Types
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of types satisfies Grothendieck's AB5 axiom
nodes.description: This is of course just the well-known fact that filtered colimits commute with finite limits in the category of types.

nodes.description: Let C be a Grothendieck abelian category. In this file, we formalize the theorem by Grothendieck that C has enough injectives.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.HasExt
nodes.description: Let C : Type u be an abelian category (with Category.{v} C). If C is a Grothendieck abelian category relatively to a universe w, the morphisms in C must be w-small, and as C has enough injectives, the Ext-groups are also w-small. If C is a nonzero category, it is possible to show that any w-small type T injects into a type of morphisms in C (consider the various inclusions X ⟶ ∐ (fun (_ : T) ↦ X) for a nonzero object X : C).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.ModuleEmbedding.GabrielPopescu
nodes.description: We prove the following Gabriel-Popescu theorem: if C is a Grothendieck abelian category and G is a separator, then the functor preadditiveCoyonedaObj G : C ⥤ ModuleCat (End G)ᵐᵒᵖ sending X to Hom(G, X) is fully faithful and has an exact left adjoint.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.ModuleEmbedding.Opposite
nodes.description: If C is Grothendieck abelian and F : D ⥤ Cᵒᵖ is a functor from a small category, we construct an object G : Cᵒᵖ such that preadditiveCoyonedaObj G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat (End G)ᵐᵒᵖ is faithful and exact and its precomposition with F is full if F is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.Monomorphisms
nodes.description: In this file, we show that in a Grothendieck abelian category, monomorphisms are stable under transfinite composition.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckCategory.Subobject
nodes.description: We study the complete lattice of subobjects of X : C when C is a Grothendieck abelian category. In particular, for a functor F : J ⥤ MonoOver X from a filtered category, we relate the colimit of F (computed in C) and the supremum of the subobjects corresponding to the objects in the image of F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Images
nodes.description: In an abelian category we usually want the image of a morphism f to be defined as kernel (cokernel.π f), and the coimage to be defined as cokernel (kernel.ι f).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Indization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of ind-objects is abelian
nodes.description: We show that if C is a small abelian category, then Ind C is an abelian category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Injective.Dimension
nodes.description: In an abelian category C, we shall say that X : C has Injective dimension < n if all Ext Y X i vanish when n ≤ i. This defines a type class HasInjectiveDimensionLT X n. We also define a type class HasInjectiveDimensionLE X n as an abbreviation for HasInjectiveDimensionLT X (n + 1). (Note that the fact that X is a zero object is equivalent to the condition HasInjectiveDimensionLT X 0, but this cannot be expressed in terms of HasInjectiveDimensionLE.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Injective.Ext

It is a descent in the sense that I.ι intertwines the descent and the original morphism, see CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.desc_commutes. object are homotopy equivalent. construct a functor injectiveResolutions C : C ⥤ HomotopyCategory C.

nodes.description: In mathlib, we define an abelian category as a preadditive category with finite products, kernels and cokernels, and in which every monomorphism and epimorphism is normal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Preradical.Basic
nodes.description: A preradical on an abelian category C is a monomorphism in the functor category C ⥤ C with codomain 𝟭 C, i.e. an element of MonoOver (𝟭 C).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Preradical.Colon
nodes.description: Given preradicals Φ and Ψ on an abelian category C, this file defines their colon Φ : Ψ in the sense of Stenström. Following Stenström, one can realize the colon object r : s evaluated at X : C as the pullback of X ⟶ X / r X along s (X / r X) ⟶ X / r X. We encode this categorically by constructing Φ : Ψ as a pullback in the category of endofunctors of the canonical projection Φ.π : 𝟭 C ⟶ Φ.quotient along Φ.quotient.whiskerLeft Ψ.ι ≫ Φ.quotient.rightUnitor.hom : Φ.quotient ⋙ Ψ.r ⟶ Φ.quotient.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Preradical.Radical
nodes.description: In this file we define what it means for a preradical Φ : Preradical C on an abelian category C to be radical, and we define Radical C as the full subcategory of Preradical C consisting of radicals.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Projective.Basic
nodes.description: In an abelian category, an object P is projective iff the functor preadditiveCoyonedaObj P preserves finite colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Projective.Dimension
nodes.description: In an abelian category C, we shall say that X : C has projective dimension < n if all Ext X Y i vanish when n ≤ i. This defines a type class HasProjectiveDimensionLT X n. We also define a type class HasProjectiveDimensionLE X n as an abbreviation for HasProjectiveDimensionLT X (n + 1). (Note that the fact that X is a zero object is equivalent to the condition HasProjectiveDimensionLT X 0, but this cannot be expressed in terms of HasProjectiveDimensionLE.)

nodes.descriptionTitle: Computing Ext using a projective resolution
nodes.description: Given a projective resolution R of an object X in an abelian category C, we provide an API in order to construct elements in Ext X Y n in terms of the complex R.complex and to make computations in the Ext-group.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Projective.Extend
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective resolutions as cochain complexes indexed by the integers
nodes.description: Given a projective resolution R of an object X in an abelian category C, we define R.cochainComplex : CochainComplex C ℤ, which is the extension of R.complex : ChainComplex C ℕ, and the quasi-isomorphism R.π' : R.cochainComplex ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj X.

It is a lifting in the sense that P.ι intertwines the lift and the original morphism, see CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution.lift_commutes. object are homotopy equivalent. construct a functor projectiveResolutions C : C ⥤ HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.down ℕ).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Pseudoelements
nodes.description: A pseudoelement of an object X in an abelian category C is an equivalence class of arrows ending in X, where two arrows are considered equivalent if we can find two epimorphisms with a common domain making a commutative square with the two arrows. While the construction shows that pseudoelements are actually subobjects of X rather than "elements", it is possible to chase these pseudoelements through commutative diagrams in an abelian category to prove exactness properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Refinements
nodes.description: In order to prove injectivity/surjectivity/exactness properties for diagrams in the category of abelian groups, we often need to do diagram chases. Some of these can be carried out in more general abelian categories: for example, a morphism X ⟶ Y in an abelian category C is a monomorphism if and only if for all A : C, the induced map (A ⟶ X) → (A ⟶ Y) of abelian groups is a monomorphism, i.e. injective.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived
nodes.description: We define the right-derived functors F.rightDerived n : C ⥤ D for any additive functor F out of a category with injective resolutions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.SerreClass.Basic
nodes.description: For any abelian category C, we introduce a type class IsSerreClass C for Serre classes in C (also known as "Serre subcategories"). A Serre class is a property P : ObjectProperty C of objects in C which holds for a zero object, and is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.SerreClass.Bousfield
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bousfield localizations with respect to Serre classes
nodes.description: If G : D ⥤ C is an exact functor between abelian categories, with a fully faithful right adjoint F, then G identifies C to the localization of D with respect to the class of morphisms G.kernel.isoModSerre, i.e. D is the localization of C with respect to the Serre class G.kernel consisting of the objects in D that are sent to a zero object by G. (We also translate this in terms of a left Bousfield localization.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.SerreClass.Localization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Localization with respect to a Serre class
nodes.description: The main definition in this file is ObjectProperty.SerreClassLocalization.abelian which shows that if L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor with respect to the class of morphisms P.isoModSerre for a Serre class P : ObjectProperty C in the abelian category C, then D is an abelian category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.SerreClass.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: The class of isomorphisms modulo a Serre class
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category and P : ObjectProperty C a Serre class. We define P.isoModSerre : MorphismProperty C, which is the class of morphisms f such that kernel f and cokernel f satisfy P. We show that P.isoModSerre is multiplicative, satisfies the two out of three property and is stable under retracts. (Similarly, we define P.monoModSerre and P.epiModSerre.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Subcategory
nodes.description: Let C be an abelian category. Given P : ObjectProperty C which contains zero, is closed under kernels, cokernels and finite products, we show that the full subcategory defined by P is abelian.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Abelian.Yoneda

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Action
nodes.descriptionTitle: Actions as functors and as categories
nodes.description: From a multiplicative action M ↻ X, we can construct a functor from M to the category of types, mapping the single object of M to X and an element m : M to the map X → X given by multiplication by m. This functor induces a category structure on X -- a special case of the category of elements. A morphism x ⟶ y in this category is simply a scalar m : M such that m • x = y. In the case where M is a group, this category is a groupoid -- the action groupoid.

nodes.description: This file shows that for a functor G : D ⥤ C the data of an initial object in each StructuredArrow category on G is equivalent to a left adjoint to G, as well as the dual.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.CompositionIso
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compatibilities for left adjoints from compatibilities satisfied by right adjoints
nodes.description: In this file, given isomorphisms between compositions of right adjoint functors, we obtain isomorphisms between the corresponding compositions of the left adjoint functors, and show that the left adjoint functors satisfy properties similar to the left/right unitality and the associativity of pseudofunctors if the right adjoint functors satisfy the corresponding properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Evaluation

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.FullyFaithfulLimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of colimits and reflective adjunctions
nodes.description: Let adj : F ⊣ G be an adjunction with G : D ⥤ C full and faithful. We show that if colimits of shape J exist in C, then a functor H : D ⥤ E preserves colimits of shape J iff F ⋙ H does.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Parametrized
nodes.description: Given bifunctors F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ and G : C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₂, this file introduces the notation F ⊣₂ G for the adjunctions with a parameter (in C₁) between F and G.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.ParametrizedLimits
nodes.description: Given bifunctors F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃, G : C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₂ and a paremetrized adjunction adj₂ : F ⊣₂ G, we show that for any X₃ : C₃, the functor G.flip.obj X₃ : C₁ᵒᵖ ⥤ C₃ preserves limits of shape J if for any X₂ : C₂, the functor F.flip.obj X₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₃ preserves colimits of shape Jᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.PartialAdjoint
nodes.descriptionTitle: Domain of definition of the partial left adjoint
nodes.description: Given a functor F : D ⥤ C, we define a functor F.partialLeftAdjoint : F.PartialLeftAdjointSource ⥤ D which is defined on the full subcategory of C consisting of those objects X : C such that F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op X) : D ⥤ Type _ is corepresentable. For X : F.PartialLeftAdjointSource and Y : D, we have a natural bijection (F.partialLeftAdjoint.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X.obj ⟶ F.obj Y) that is similar to what we would expect for the image of the object X by the left adjoint of F, if such an adjoint existed.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Quadruple
nodes.description: This file concerns adjoint quadruples L ⊣ F ⊣ G ⊣ R of functors L G : C ⥤ D, F R : D ⥤ C. We bundle the adjunctions in a structure Quadruple L F G R and make the two triples Triple L F G and Triple F G R accessible as Quadruple.leftTriple and Quadruple.rightTriple.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Reflective
nodes.description: Basic properties of reflective functors, especially those relating to their essential image.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Restrict
nodes.description: Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful shows that an adjunction can be restricted along fully faithful inclusions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Triple
nodes.description: This file concerns adjoint triples F ⊣ G ⊣ H of functors F H : C ⥤ D, G : D ⥤ C. We first prove that F is fully faithful iff H is, and then prove results about the two special cases where G is fully faithful or F and H are.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Unique
nodes.description: This file shows that adjoints are unique up to natural isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Whiskering
nodes.descriptionTitle: Given categories C D E, functors F : D ⥤ E and G : E ⥤ D with an adjunction

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Balanced
nodes.description: A category is called balanced if any morphism that is both monic and epic is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Adjunction.Adj
nodes.descriptionTitle: The bicategory of adjunctions in a bicategory
nodes.description: Given a bicategory B, we construct a bicategory Adj B that has essentially the same objects as B but whose 1-morphisms are adjunctions (in the same direction as the left adjoints), and 2-morphisms are tuples of mate maps between the left and right adjoints (where the map between right adjoints is in the opposite direction).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Adjunction.Basic
nodes.description: For 1-morphisms f : a ⟶ b and g : b ⟶ a in a bicategory, an adjunction between f and g consists of a pair of 2-morphisms η : 𝟙 a ⟶ f ≫ g and ε : g ≫ f ⟶ 𝟙 b satisfying the triangle identities. The 2-morphism η is called the unit and ε is called the counit.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Adjunction.Cat
nodes.description: We show that adjunctions in the bicategory Cat correspond to adjunctions between functors in the usual categorical sense.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.CatEnriched
nodes.descriptionTitle: The strict bicategory associated to a Cat-enriched category
nodes.description: If C is a type with an EnrichedCategory Cat C structure, then it has hom-categories, whose objects define 1-dimensional arrows on C and whose morphisms define 2-dimensional arrows between these. The enriched category axioms equip this data with the structure of a strict bicategory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Coherence
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the coherence theorem for bicategories, stated in the following form: the free bicategory over any quiver is locally thin.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Extension
nodes.description: We introduce the concept of extensions and lifts within the bicategorical framework. These concepts are defined by commutative diagrams in the (1-)categorical context. Within the bicategorical framework, commutative diagrams are replaced by 2-morphisms. Depending on the orientation of the 2-morphisms, we define both left and right extensions (likewise for lifts). The use of left and right here is a common one in the theory of Kan extensions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Free
nodes.description: We define the free bicategory over a quiver. In this bicategory, the 1-morphisms are freely generated by the arrows in the quiver, and the 2-morphisms are freely generated by the formal identities, the formal unitors, and the formal associators modulo the relation derived from the axioms of a bicategory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Functor.Cat

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Functor.Cat.ObjectProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects in target categories of a pseudofunctor to Cat
nodes.description: Given F : Pseudofunctor B Cat, we introduce a type F.ObjectProperty which consists of properties P of objects for all categories F.obj X for X : B. The typeclass P.IsClosedUnderMapObj expresses that this property is preserved by the application of the functors F.map: this allows to define a sub-pseudofunctor P.fullsubcategory : Pseudofunctor B Cat.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Functor.Pseudofunctor
nodes.description: A pseudofunctor is an oplax (or lax) functor whose mapId and mapComp are isomorphisms. We provide several constructors for pseudofunctors: map₂_whiskerRight instead of naturality of mapComp.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.InducedBicategory
nodes.description: In this file we develop API for constructing a full sub-bicategory of a bicategory C, given a map F : B → C. The objects of the induced bicategory are the objects of B, while the 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms are taken as all corresponding morphisms in C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Kan.Adjunction
nodes.description: We show that adjunctions are realized as Kan extensions or Kan lifts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Kan.HasKan
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of Kan extensions and Kan lifts in bicategories
nodes.description: We provide the propositional typeclass HasLeftKanExtension f g, which asserts that there exists a left Kan extension of g along f. See CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Kan.IsKan for the definition of left Kan extensions. Under the assumption that HasLeftKanExtension f g, we define the left Kan extension lan f g by using the axiom of choice.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Kan.IsKan
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kan extensions and Kan lifts in bicategories
nodes.description: The left Kan extension of a 1-morphism g : a ⟶ c along a 1-morphism f : a ⟶ b is the initial object in the category of left extensions LeftExtension f g. The universal property can be accessed by the following definition and lemmas: compositions with each unit are equal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.LocallyDiscrete
nodes.description: A category C can be promoted to a strict bicategory LocallyDiscrete C. The objects and the 1-morphisms in LocallyDiscrete C are the same as the objects and the morphisms, respectively, in C, and the 2-morphisms in LocallyDiscrete C are the equalities between 1-morphisms. In other words, the category consisting of the 1-morphisms between each pair of objects X and Y in LocallyDiscrete C is defined as the discrete category associated with the type X ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.LocallyGroupoid
nodes.description: A bicategory B is said to be locally groupoidal (or a (2,1)-category) if for every pair of objects x, y, the Hom-category x ⟶ y is a groupoid (which is expressed using the CategoryTheory.IsGroupoid typeclass).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Modification.Lax
nodes.descriptionTitle: Modifications between transformations of lax functors

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Modification.Oplax

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Modification.Pseudo
nodes.description: In this file we define modifications of strong transformations of pseudofunctors. They are defined similarly to modifications of transformations of oplax functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Monad.Basic
nodes.description: We define comonads in a bicategory B as comonoid objects in an endomorphism monoidal category. We show that this is equivalent to oplax functors from the trivial bicategory to B. From this, we show that comonads in B form a bicategory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.NaturalTransformation.Lax
nodes.description: Just as there are natural transformations between functors, there are transformations between lax functors. The equality in the naturality condition of a natural transformation gets replaced by a specified 2-morphism. Now, there are three possible types of transformations (between lax functors):

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Opposites

nodes.description: We define the bicategory instance on B × C when B and C are bicategories.

nodes.description: A bicategory is called Strict if the left unitors, the right unitors, and the associators are isomorphisms given by equalities.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.Adjunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjunctions related to Cat, the category of categories
nodes.description: The embedding typeToCat: Type ⥤ Cat, mapping a type to the corresponding discrete category, is left adjoint to the functor Cat.objects, which maps a category to its set of objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.AsSmall
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functorially embedding Cat into the category of small categories

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.CartesianClosed
nodes.description: The category of small categories is Cartesian closed, with the exponential at a category C defined by the functor category mapping out of C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.Colimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of small categories has all small colimits.
nodes.description: In this file, the existence of colimits in Cat is deduced from the existence of colimits in the category of simplicial sets. Indeed, Cat identifies to a reflective subcategory of the category of simplicial sets (see AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.NerveAdjunction), so that colimits in Cat can be computed by passing to nerves, taking the colimit in SSet and finally applying the homotopy category functor SSet ⥤ Cat.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.Limit
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of small categories has all small limits.
nodes.description: An object in the limit consists of a family of objects, which are carried to one another by the functors in the diagram. A morphism between two such objects is a family of morphisms between the corresponding objects, which are carried to one another by the action on morphisms of the functors in the diagram.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.Op
nodes.description: We define a (strict) functor opFunctor and an equivalence assigning opposite categories to categories. We then show that this functor is strictly involutive and that it induces an equivalence on Cat.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Category.Cat.Terminal
nodes.description: We prove that a category is terminal if its underlying type has a Unique structure and the category has an IsDiscrete instance.

Specifically, for functors L : A ⥤ T and R : B ⥤ T, an object in Comma L R is a morphism hom : L.obj left ⟶ R.obj right for some objects left : A and right : B, and a morphism in Comma L R between hom : L.obj left ⟶ R.obj right and hom' : L.obj left' ⟶ R.obj right' is a commutative square

nodes.description: We define the category Dial of the Dialectica interpretation, after [dialectica1989].

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Dialectica.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Dialectica category is symmetric monoidal
nodes.description: We show that the category Dial has a symmetric monoidal category structure.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.DifferentialObject
nodes.description: A differential object in a category with zero morphisms and a shift is an object X equipped with a morphism d : obj ⟶ obj⟦1⟧, such that d^2 = 0.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.DinatTrans
nodes.description: Dinatural transformations are special kinds of transformations between functors F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ C ⥤ D which depend both covariantly and contravariantly on the same category (also known as difunctors).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Discrete.Basic
nodes.description: We define Discrete α as a structure containing a term a : α for any type α, and use this type alias to provide a SmallCategory instance whose only morphisms are the identities.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Discrete.StructuredArrow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Structured arrows when the target category is discrete
nodes.description: When T is a type with a unique element t, we show that if F : C ⥤ Discrete T, then the categories StructuredArrow (Discrete.mk t) F and CostructuredArrow (Discrete.mk t) F are equivalent to C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Discrete.SumsProducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sums and products of discrete categories.
nodes.description: This file shows that binary products and binary sums of discrete categories are also discrete, both in the form of explicit equivalences and through the IsDiscrete typeclass.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Distributive.Cartesian
nodes.description: A category C with finite products and binary coproducts is called distributive if the canonical distributivity morphism (X ⨯ Y) ⨿ (X ⨯ Z) ⟶ X ⨯ (Y ⨿ Z) is an isomorphism for all objects X, Y, and Z in C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Distributive.Monoidal
nodes.description: A monoidal category C with binary coproducts is left distributive if the left tensor product preserves binary coproducts. This means that, for all objects X, Y, and Z in C, the cogap map (X ⊗ Y) ⨿ (X ⊗ Z) ⟶ X ⊗ (Y ⨿ Z) can be promoted to an isomorphism. We refer to this isomorphism as the left distributivity isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Basic
nodes.description: We define the notion of effective epimorphism and effective epimorphic family of morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Comp
nodes.description: This file provides EffectiveEpi instances for certain compositions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Coproduct
nodes.description: This file proves that an effective epimorphic family induces an effective epi from the coproduct if the coproduct exists, and the converse under some more conditions on the coproduct (that it interacts well with pullbacks).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Enough
nodes.descriptionTitle: Effectively enough objects in the image of a functor
nodes.description: We define the class F.EffectivelyEnough on a functor F : C ⥤ D which says that for every object in D, there exists an effective epi to it from an object in the image of F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Extensive
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preserving and reflecting effective epis on extensive categories
nodes.description: We prove that a functor between FinitaryPreExtensive categories preserves (resp. reflects) finite effective epi families if it preserves (resp. reflects) effective epis.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.Preserves
nodes.description: This file concerns functors which preserve and/or reflect effective epimorphisms and effective epimorphic families.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.RegularEpi
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Elements
nodes.description: This file defines the category of elements, also known as (a special case of) the Grothendieck construction.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Elementwise
nodes.descriptionTitle: Use the elementwise attribute to create applied versions of lemmas.
nodes.description: Usually we would use @[elementwise] at the point of definition, however some early parts of the category theory library are imported by Tactic.Elementwise, so we need to add the attribute after the fact.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Algebra
nodes.description: This file defines (co)algebras of an endofunctor, and provides the category instance for them. It also defines the forgetful functor from the category of (co)algebras. It is shown that the structure map of the initial algebra of an endofunctor is an isomorphism. Furthermore, it is shown that for an adjunction F ⊣ G the category of algebras over F is equivalent to the category of coalgebras over G.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Endomorphism
nodes.description: Definition and basic properties of endomorphisms and automorphisms of an object in a category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Basic
nodes.description: We set up the basic theory of V-enriched categories, for V an arbitrary monoidal category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.EnrichedCat
nodes.description: We define the bicategory EnrichedCat V of (bundled) V-enriched categories for a fixed monoidal category V.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.FunctorCategory
nodes.description: If C is a V-enriched ordinary category, then J ⥤ C is also both a V-enriched ordinary category and a J ⥤ V-enriched ordinary category, provided C has suitable limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.HomCongr
nodes.description: Recall that when C is both a category and a V-enriched category, we say it is an EnrichedOrdinaryCategory if it comes equipped with a sufficiently compatible equivalence between morphisms X ⟶ Y in C and morphisms 𝟙_ V ⟶ (X ⟶[V] Y) in V.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalLimits
nodes.description: This file contains different statements about the (non-constructive) existence of conical limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalProducts
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalProducts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalPullbacks
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalPullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalTerminal
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Enriched.Limits.HasConicalTerminal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite category of an enriched category
nodes.description: When a monoidal category V is braided, we may define the opposite V-category of a V-category. The symmetry map is required to define the composition morphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Enriched.Ordinary.Basic
nodes.description: If V is a monoidal category, a V-enriched category C does not need to be a category. However, when we have both Category C and EnrichedCategory V C, we may require that the type of morphisms X ⟶ Y in C identify to 𝟙_ V ⟶ EnrichedCategory.Hom X Y. This data shall be packaged in the typeclass EnrichedOrdinaryCategory V C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EpiMono
nodes.description: The definitions of Epi and Mono are in CategoryTheory.Category, since they are used by some lemmas for Iso, which is used everywhere.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EqToHom
nodes.description: When working categorically, sometimes one encounters an equation h : X = Y between objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Equivalence
nodes.description: An equivalence of categories C and D is a pair of functors F : C ⥤ D and G : D ⥤ C such that η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G and ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 D. In many situations, equivalences are a better notion of "sameness" of categories than the stricter isomorphism of categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.Symmetry
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functoriality of the symmetry of equivalences
nodes.description: Using the calculus of mates in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Mates, we prove that passing to the symmetric equivalence defines an equivalence between C ≌ D and (D ≌ C)ᵒᵖ, and provides the definition of the functor that takes an equivalence to its inverse.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EssentialImage
nodes.description: The essential image essImage of a functor consists of the objects in the target category which are isomorphic to an object in the image of the object function. This, for instance, allows us to talk about objects belonging to a subcategory expressed as a functor rather than a subtype, preserving the principle of equivalence. For example this lets us define exponential ideals.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall
nodes.description: A category given by (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] is w-essentially small if there exists a SmallModel C : Type w equipped with [SmallCategory (SmallModel C)] and an equivalence C ≌ SmallModel C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Extensive
nodes.description: coproducts, and binary coproducts are van Kampen.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ExtremalEpi
nodes.description: An extremal epimorphism p : X ⟶ Y is an epimorphism which does not factor through any proper subobject of Y. In case the category has equalizers, we show that a morphism p : X ⟶ Y which does not factor through any proper subobject of Y is automatically an epimorphism, and also an extremal epimorphism. We also show that a strong epimorphism is an extremal epimorphism, and that both notions coincide when the category has pullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.BasedCategory
nodes.description: In this file we define the type BasedCategory 𝒮, and give it the structure of a strict bicategory. Given a category 𝒮, we define the type BasedCategory 𝒮 as the type of categories 𝒳 equipped with a functor 𝒳.p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.Cartesian
nodes.description: This file defines Cartesian resp. strongly Cartesian morphisms with respect to a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.Cocartesian
nodes.description: This file defines co-Cartesian resp. strongly co-Cartesian morphisms with respect to a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.Fiber
nodes.description: In this file we define, for a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴, the fiber categories Fiber p S for every S : 𝒮 as follows

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.Fibered
nodes.description: This file defines what it means for a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮 to be (pre)fibered.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.Grothendieck
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Grothendieck construction gives a fibered category
nodes.description: In this file we show that the Grothendieck construction applied to a pseudofunctor F gives a fibered category over the base category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.HasFibers
nodes.description: In this file we introduce a typeclass HasFibers for a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮, consisting of:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FiberedCategory.HomLift
nodes.description: Given a functor p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮, this file provides API for expressing the fact that p(φ) = f for given morphisms φ and f. The reason this API is needed is because, in general, p.map φ = f does not make sense when the domain and/or codomain of φ and f are not definitionally equal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Basic
nodes.description: A category is filtered if every finite diagram admits a cocone. We give a simple characterisation of this condition as 1. for every pair of objects there exists another object "to the right", 2. for every pair of parallel morphisms there exists a morphism to the right so the compositions are equal, and 3. there exists some object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Connected
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Filtered.Connected.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.CostructuredArrow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inferring Filteredness from Filteredness of Costructured Arrow Categories
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Filtered.CostructuredArrow.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Final
nodes.description: If C is a filtered category, then the usual equivalent conditions for a functor F : C ⥤ D to be final can be restated. We show:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.FinallySmall
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if C is a filtered finally small category that is locally small, there exists a final functor D ⥤ C from a small filtered category. The dual result is also obtained.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Flat
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pulling back filteredness along representably flat functors
nodes.description: We show that if F : C ⥤ D is a representably coflat functor between two categories, filteredness of D implies filteredness of C. Dually, if F is representably flat, cofilteredness of D implies cofilteredness of C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Grothendieck
nodes.description: We show that if F : C ⥤ Cat is such that C is filtered and F.obj c is filtered for all c : C, then Grothendieck F is filtered.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.OfColimitCommutesFiniteLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: If colimits of shape K commute with finite limits, then K is filtered.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Filtered.OfColimitCommutesFiniteLimit.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Filtered.Small
nodes.descriptionTitle: A functor from a small category to a filtered category factors through a small filtered category
nodes.description: A consequence of this is that if C is filtered and finally small, then C is also "finally filtered-small", i.e., there is a final functor from a small filtered category to C. This is occasionally useful, for example in the proof of the recognition theorem for ind-objects (Proposition 6.1.5 in [Kashiwara2006]).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FinCategory.AsType
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite categories are equivalent to categories in Type 0.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.FinCategory.AsType.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FinCategory.Basic
nodes.description: A category is finite in this sense if it has finitely many objects, and finitely many morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.FintypeCat
nodes.description: We define the category of finite types, denoted FintypeCat as the full subcategory of types with a Finite instance.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
nodes.description: Defines a functor between categories, extending a Prefunctor between quivers.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Category
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of functors and natural transformations between two fixed categories.
nodes.description: We provide the category instance on C ⥤ D, with morphisms the natural transformations.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Const
nodes.description: const J : C ⥤ (J ⥤ C) is the functor that sends an object X : C to the functor J ⥤ C sending every object in J to X, and every morphism to 𝟙 X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Currying
nodes.description: We define curry : ((C × D) ⥤ E) ⥤ (C ⥤ (D ⥤ E)) and uncurry : (C ⥤ (D ⥤ E)) ⥤ ((C × D) ⥤ E), and verify that they provide an equivalence of categories currying : (C ⥤ (D ⥤ E)) ≌ ((C × D) ⥤ E).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.CurryingThree
nodes.descriptionTitle: Currying of functors in three variables
nodes.description: We study the equivalence of categories currying₃ : (C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ E) ≌ C₁ × C₂ × C₃ ⥤ E.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Derived.Adjunction
nodes.description: Assume that functors G : C₁ ⥤ C₂ and F : C₂ ⥤ C₁ are part of an adjunction adj : G ⊣ F, that we have localization functors L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁ and L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂ with respect to classes of morphisms W₁ and W₂, and that G admits a left derived functor G' : D₁ ⥤ D₂ and F a right derived functor F' : D₂ ⥤ D₁. We show that there is an adjunction G' ⊣ F' under the additional assumption that F' and G' are absolute derived functors, i.e.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Derived.LeftDerived
nodes.description: In this file, given a functor F : C ⥤ H, and L : C ⥤ D that is a localization functor for W : MorphismProperty C, we define F.totalLeftDerived L W : D ⥤ H as the right Kan extension of F along L: it is defined if the type class F.HasLeftDerivedFunctor W asserting the existence of a right Kan extension is satisfied. (The name totalLeftDerived is to avoid name-collision with Functor.leftDerived which are the left derived functors in the context of abelian categories.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Derived.PointwiseLeftDerived
