nodes.description: We define pointwise left derived functors using the notion of pointwise right Kan extensions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Derived.PointwiseRightDerived
nodes.description: We define pointwise right derived functors using the notion of pointwise left Kan extensions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Derived.RightDerived
nodes.description: In this file, given a functor F : C ⥤ H, and L : C ⥤ D that is a localization functor for W : MorphismProperty C, we define F.totalRightDerived L W : D ⥤ H as the left Kan extension of F along L: it is defined if the type class F.HasRightDerivedFunctor W asserting the existence of a left Kan extension is satisfied. (The name totalRightDerived is to avoid name-collision with Functor.rightDerived which are the right derived functors in the context of abelian categories.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation and reflection of monomorphisms and epimorphisms
nodes.description: We provide typeclasses that state that a functor preserves or reflects monomorphisms or epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Flat
nodes.description: We define representably flat functors as functors such that the category of structured arrows over X is cofiltered for each X. This concept is also known as flat functors as in [Elephant] Remark C2.3.7, and this name is suggested by Mike Shulman in https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/2011/06/flat_functors_and_morphisms_of.html to avoid confusion with other notions of flatness (e.g. see the notion of flat type-valued functor in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/TypeValuedFlat.lean).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful
nodes.description: We define typeclasses Full and Faithful, decorating functors. These typeclasses carry no data. However, we also introduce a structure Functor.FullyFaithful which contains the data of the inverse map (F.obj X ⟶ F.obj Y) ⟶ (X ⟶ Y) of the map induced on morphisms by a functor F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.FunctorHom
nodes.description: Given functors F G : C ⥤ D, define a functor functorHom F G from C to Type max v' v u, which is a proxy for the "internal hom" functor Hom(F ⊗ coyoneda(-), G). This is used to show that the functor category C ⥤ D is enriched over C ⥤ Type max v' v u. This is also useful for showing that C ⥤ Type max w v u is monoidal closed.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Functorial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Unbundled functors, as a typeclass decorating the object-level function.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Functor.Functorial.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Hom
nodes.descriptionTitle: The hom functor, sending (X, Y) to the type X ⟶ Y.
nodes.description: The hom functor, sending (X, Y) to the type X ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Adjunction
nodes.description: Given a functor L : C ⥤ D, we define the left Kan extension functor L.lan : (C ⥤ H) ⥤ (D ⥤ H) which sends a functor F : C ⥤ H to its left Kan extension along L. This is defined if all F have such a left Kan extension. It is shown that L.lan is the left adjoint to the functor (D ⥤ H) ⥤ (C ⥤ H) given by the precomposition with L (see Functor.lanAdjunction).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Basic
nodes.description: The basic definitions for Kan extensions of functors are introduced in this file. Part of API is parallel to the definitions for bicategories (see CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Kan.IsKan). (The bicategory API cannot be used directly here because it would not allow the universe polymorphism which is necessary for some applications.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Dense
nodes.description: A functor F : C ⥤ D is dense (F.IsDense) if 𝟭 D is a pointwise left Kan extension of F along itself, i.e. any Y : D is the colimit of all F.obj X for all morphisms F.obj X ⟶ Y (which is the condition F.DenseAt Y). When F is full, we show that this is equivalent to saying that the restricted Yoneda functor D ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type _ is fully faithful (see the lemma Functor.isDense_iff_fullyFaithful_restrictedULiftYoneda).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.DenseAt
nodes.descriptionTitle: Canonical colimits, or functors that are dense at an object
nodes.description: Given a functor F : C ⥤ D and Y : D, we say that F is dense at Y (F.DenseAt Y), if Y identifies to the colimit of all F.obj X for X : C and f : F.obj X ⟶ Y, i.e. Y identifies to the colimit of the obvious functor CostructuredArrow F Y ⥤ D. In some references, it is also said that Y is a canonical colimit relatively to F. While F.DenseAt Y contains data, we also introduce the corresponding property isDenseAt F of objects of D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Pointwise
nodes.description: In this file, we define the notion of pointwise (left) Kan extension. Given two functors L : C ⥤ D and F : C ⥤ H, and E : LeftExtension L F, we introduce a cocone E.coconeAt Y for the functor CostructuredArrow.proj L Y ⋙ F : CostructuredArrow L Y ⥤ H the point of which is E.right.obj Y, and the type E.IsPointwiseLeftKanExtensionAt Y which expresses that E.coconeAt Y is a colimit. When this holds for all Y : D, we may say that E is a pointwise left Kan extension (E.IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.KanExtension.Preserves
nodes.description: Given functors F : A ⥤ B, L : B ⥤ C, and G : B ⥤ D, we introduce a typeclass G.PreservesLeftKanExtension F L which encodes the fact that the left Kan extension of F along L is preserved by the functor G.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors from the category of the ordered set ℕ
nodes.description: In this file, we provide a constructor Functor.ofSequence for functors ℕ ⥤ C which takes as an input a sequence of morphisms f : X n ⟶ X (n + 1) for all n : ℕ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.ReflectsIso.Balanced
nodes.descriptionTitle: Balanced categories and functors reflecting isomorphisms
nodes.description: If a category is C, and a functor out of C reflects epimorphisms and monomorphisms, then the functor reflects isomorphisms. Furthermore, categories that admit a functor that ReflectsIsomorphisms, PreservesEpimorphisms and PreservesMonomorphisms are balanced.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.ReflectsIso.Basic
nodes.description: A functor F reflects isomorphisms if whenever F.map f is an isomorphism, f was too.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.ReflectsIso.Exact
nodes.descriptionTitle: Exactness properties of functors which jointly reflect isomorphisms
nodes.description: Let Fᵢ : C ⥤ Dᵢ be a family of exact functors between abelian categories. Assume that they jointly reflect isomorphisms. We show that a short complex in C is exact (resp. short exact) iff it is so after applying the functor Fᵢ. Similar results are obtained for the detection of quasi-isomorphisms between short complexes or homological complexes in C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.ReflectsIso.Jointly
nodes.descriptionTitle: Families of functors which jointly reflect isomorphisms
nodes.description: Let Fᵢ : C ⥤ Dᵢ be a family of functors. The family is said to jointly reflect isomorphisms (resp. monomorphisms, resp. epimorphisms) if every f : X ⟶ Y in C for which Fᵢ.map f is an isomorphism (resp. monomorphism, resp. epimorphism) for all i is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.ReflectsIso.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Exactness of families of functors which jointly reflect isomorphisms
nodes.description: Let Fᵢ : C ⥤ Dᵢ be a conservative family of functors (i.e. they jointly reflect isomorphisms). Let G : J ⥤ C be a functor that has a limit that is preserved by the functors Fᵢ. In this file, we show that a cone for G is a limit if it is so after applying the functors Fᵢ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.RegularEpi
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of type-valued sheaves is a regular epi category
nodes.description: This file proves that when the target category D is a regular epi category (i.e. every epimorphism is regular) and has pushouts and kernel pairs of epimorphisms, the functor category C ⥤ D is a regular epi category. This is an instance that applies directly when D is Type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.Trifunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Trifunctors obtained by composition of bifunctors
nodes.description: Given two bifunctors F₁₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₁₂ and G : C₁₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄, we define the trifunctor bifunctorComp₁₂ F₁₂ G : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄ which sends three objects X₁ : C₁, X₂ : C₂ and X₃ : C₃ to G.obj ((F₁₂.obj X₁).obj X₂).obj X₃.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.TwoSquare
nodes.description: Given four functors T, L, R and B, a 2-square TwoSquare T L R B consists of a natural transformation w : T ⋙ R ⟶ L ⋙ B:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Functor.TypeValuedFlat
nodes.description: A functor F : C ⥤ Type w is a flat Type-valued functor if the category F.Elements is cofiltered. (This is not equivalent to saying that F is representably flat in the sense of the typeclass RepresentablyFlat defined in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Flat.lean, see also https://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/2011/06/flat_functors_and_morphisms_of.html for a clarification about the differences between these notions.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Action
nodes.descriptionTitle: Induced functor to finite Aut F-sets
nodes.description: Any (fiber) functor F : C ⥤ FintypeCat factors via the forgetful functor from finite Aut F-sets to finite sets. In this file we collect basic properties of the induced functor H : C ⥤ Action FintypeCat (Aut F).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definition and basic properties of Galois categories
nodes.description: We define the notion of a Galois category and a fiber functor as in SGA1, following the definitions in Lenstra's notes (see below for a reference).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Decomposition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Decomposition of objects into connected components and applications
nodes.description: We show that in a Galois category every object is the (finite) coproduct of connected subobjects. This has many useful corollaries, in particular that the fiber of every object is represented by a Galois object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Equivalence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fiber functors induce an equivalence of categories
nodes.description: Let C be a Galois category with fiber functor F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.EssSurj
nodes.description: Let F : C ⥤ FintypeCat be a fiber functor of a Galois category C and denote by H the induced functor C ⥤ Action FintypeCat (Aut F).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Examples
nodes.descriptionTitle: Examples of Galois categories and fiber functors
nodes.description: We show that for a group G the category of finite G-sets is a PreGaloisCategory and that the forgetful functor to FintypeCat is a FiberFunctor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Full
nodes.description: Any (fiber) functor F : C ⥤ FintypeCat factors via the forgetful functor from finite Aut F-sets to finite sets. The induced functor H : C ⥤ Action FintypeCat (Aut F) is faithfully full. The faithfulness follows easily from the faithfulness of F. In this file we show that H is also full.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.GaloisObjects
nodes.description: We define when a connected object of a Galois category C is Galois in a fiber-functor-independent way and show equivalent characterisations.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.IsFundamentalgroup
nodes.description: Let C be a Galois category with fiber functor F. While in informal mathematics, we tend to identify known groups from other contexts (e.g. the absolute Galois group of a field) with the automorphism group Aut F of certain fiber functors F, this causes friction in formalization.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Prorepresentability
nodes.description: We show that any fiber functor is pro-representable, i.e. there exists a pro-object X : I ⥤ C such that F is naturally isomorphic to the colimit of X ⋙ coyoneda.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Galois.Topology
nodes.description: In this file we define a natural topology on the automorphism group of a functor F : C ⥤ FintypeCat: It is defined as the subspace topology induced by the natural embedding of Aut F into ∀ X, Aut (F.obj X) where Aut (F.obj X) carries the discrete topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Abelian
nodes.descriptionTitle: A complete abelian category with enough injectives and a separator has an injective coseparator
nodes.description: that Grothendieck categories have an injective coseparator.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Basic
nodes.description: There are several non-equivalent notions of a generator of a category. Here, we consider two of them:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.HomologicalComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Generators of the category of homological complexes
nodes.description: Let c : ComplexShape ι be a complex shape with no loop. If a category C has a separator, then HomologicalComplex C c has a separating family, and a separator when suitable coproducts exist.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Indization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Separating set in the category of ind-objects
nodes.description: We construct a separating set in the category of ind-objects and conclude that if C is small and additive, then Ind C has a separator.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Preadditive
nodes.description: This file contains characterizations of separating sets and objects that are valid in all preadditive categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Presheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Generators in the category of presheaves
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if A is a category with zero morphisms that has a separator (and suitable coproducts), then the category of presheaves Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A also has a separator.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Sheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Generators in the category of sheaves
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if J : GrothendieckTopology C and A is a preadditive category which has a separator (and suitable coproducts), then Sheaf J A has a separator.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.StrongGenerator
nodes.description: If P : ObjectProperty C, we say that P is a strong generator if it is a generator (in the sense that IsSeparating P holds) such that for any proper subobject A ⊂ X, there exists a morphism G ⟶ X which does not factor through A from an object satisfying P.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Generator.Type
nodes.description: In this file, we show that PUnit is a separator of the category Type u.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GlueData
nodes.description: We define GlueData as a family of data needed to glue topological spaces, schemes, etc. We provide the API to realize it as a multispan diagram, and also state lemmas about its interaction with a functor that preserves certain pullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject
nodes.description: For any type β, a β-graded object over some category C is just a function β → C into the objects of C. We put the "pointwise" category structure on these, as the non-dependent specialization of CategoryTheory.Pi.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Associator
nodes.descriptionTitle: The associator for actions of bifunctors on graded objects
nodes.description: Given functors F₁₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₁₂, G : C₁₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄, F : C₁ ⥤ C₂₃ ⥤ C₄, G₂₃ : C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₂₃ equipped with an isomorphism associator : bifunctorComp₁₂ F₁₂ G ≅ bifunctorComp₂₃ F G₂₃ (which informally means that we have natural isomorphisms G(F₁₂(X₁, X₂), X₃) ≅ F(X₁, G₂₃(X₂, X₃))), a map r : I₁ × I₂ × I₃ → J, and data ρ₁₂ : BifunctorComp₁₂IndexData r and ρ₂₃ : BifunctorComp₂₃IndexData r, then if X₁ : GradedObject I₁ C₁, X₂ : GradedObject I₂ C₂ and X₃ : GradedObject I₃ C₃ satisfy suitable assumptions, we construct...

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Bifunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The action of bifunctors on graded objects
nodes.description: Given a bifunctor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ and types I and J, we construct an obvious functor mapBifunctor F I J : GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject (I × J) C₃. When we have a map p : I × J → K and that suitable coproducts exist, we also get a functor mapBifunctorMap F p : GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject K C₃.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Braiding
nodes.descriptionTitle: The braided and symmetric category structures on graded objects
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the braiding GradedObject.Monoidal.braiding : tensorObj X Y ≅ tensorObj Y X for two objects X and Y in GradedObject I C, when I is a commutative additive monoid (and suitable coproducts exist in a braided category C).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The monoidal category structures on graded objects
nodes.description: Assuming that C is a monoidal category and that I is an additive monoid, we introduce a partially defined tensor product on the category GradedObject I C: given X₁ and X₂ two objects in GradedObject I C, we define GradedObject.Monoidal.tensorObj X₁ X₂ under the assumption HasTensor X₁ X₂ that the coproduct of X₁ i ⊗ X₂ j for i + j = n exists for any n : I.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Single
nodes.descriptionTitle: The graded object in a single degree
nodes.description: In this file, we define the functor GradedObject.single j : C ⥤ GradedObject J C which sends an object X : C to the graded object which is X in degree j and the initial object of C in other degrees.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Trifunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The action of trifunctors on graded objects
nodes.description: Given a trifunctor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄ and types I₁, I₂ and I₃, we define a functor GradedObject I₁ C₁ ⥤ GradedObject I₂ C₂ ⥤ GradedObject I₃ C₃ ⥤ GradedObject (I₁ × I₂ × I₃) C₄ (see mapTrifunctor).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.Unitor
nodes.description: Given a bifunctor F : C ⥤ D ⥤ D, an object X : C such that F.obj X ≅ 𝟭 D and a map p : I × J → J such that hp : ∀ (j : J), p ⟨0, j⟩ = j, we define an isomorphism of J-graded objects for any Y : GradedObject J D. mapBifunctorLeftUnitor F X e p hp Y : mapBifunctorMapObj F p ((single₀ I).obj X) Y ≅ Y. Under similar assumptions, we also obtain a right unitor isomorphism mapBifunctorMapObj F p X ((single₀ I).obj Y) ≅ X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Grothendieck
nodes.description: Given a functor F : C ⥤ Cat, the objects of Grothendieck F consist of dependent pairs (b, f), where b : C and f : F.obj b, and a morphism (b, f) ⟶ (b', f') is a pair β : b ⟶ b' in C, and φ : (F.map β).toFunctor.obj f ⟶ f'

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid
nodes.description: We define Groupoid as a typeclass extending Category, asserting that all morphisms have inverses.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: This file defines a few basic properties of groupoids.
nodes.description: This file defines a few basic properties of groupoids.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.Discrete
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Groupoid.Discrete.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.FreeGroupoid
nodes.description: This file defines the free groupoid on a quiver, the lifting of a prefunctor to its unique extension as a functor from the free groupoid, and proves uniqueness of this extension.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.FreeGroupoidOfCategory
nodes.description: This file defines the free groupoid on a category, the lifting of a functor to its unique extension as a functor from the free groupoid, and proves uniqueness of this extension.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.Grpd.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of the category Grpd of all groupoids. In this category objects are groupoids and morphisms are functors between these groupoids.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.Subgroupoid
nodes.description: This file defines subgroupoids as structures containing the subsets of arrows and their stability under composition and inversion. Also defined are:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.VertexGroup
nodes.description: This file defines the vertex group (aka isotropy group) of a groupoid at a vertex.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.Basic
nodes.description: Given four functors T, L, R and B, a 2-square TwoSquare T L R B consists of a natural transformation w : T ⋙ R ⟶ L ⋙ B:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.HorizontalComposition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Horizontal composition of Guitart exact squares
nodes.description: In this file, we show that the horizontal composition of Guitart exact squares is Guitart exact.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.KanExtension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Guitart exact squares and Kan extensions
nodes.description: Given a Guitart exact square w : T ⋙ R ⟶ L ⋙ B, we show that an extension F' : C₄ ⥤ D of F : C₂ ⥤ D along R is a pointwise left Kan extension at B.obj X₃ iff the composition T ⋙ F' is a pointwise left Kan extension at X₃ of B ⋙ F'.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite of a Guitart exact square
nodes.description: A 2-square is Guitart exact iff the opposite (transposed) 2-square is Guitart exact.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: Guitart exact squares involving Over categories
nodes.description: Let F : C ⥤ D be a functor and X : C. One may consider the commutative square of categories where vertical functors are Over.forget:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.Quotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: Guitart exact squares and quotient categories
nodes.description: Consider a commutative square of categories given by a natural isomorphism e : T ⋙ R ≅ L ⋙ B:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.GuitartExact.VerticalComposition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Vertical composition of Guitart exact squares
nodes.description: In this file, we show that the vertical composition of Guitart exact squares is Guitart exact.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.HomCongr
nodes.description: We define CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr : (X ≅ X₁) → (Y ≅ Y₁) → (X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X₁ ⟶ Y₁), cf. Equiv.arrowCongr, and CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr : (f : X₁ ≅ X₂) → (g : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) → (X₁ ≅ Y₁) ≃ (X₂ ≅ Y₂).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define the notion of idempotent complete categories (also known as Karoubian categories, or pseudoabelian in the case of preadditive categories).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Biproducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Biproducts in the idempotent completion of a preadditive category
nodes.description: In this file, we define an instance expressing that if C is an additive category (i.e. is preadditive and has finite biproducts), then Karoubi C is also an additive category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.FunctorCategories
nodes.description: In this file we define an instance functor_category_isIdempotentComplete expressing that a functor category J ⥤ C is idempotent complete when the target category C is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.FunctorExtension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extension of functors to the idempotent completion
nodes.description: In this file, we construct an extension functorExtension₁ of functors C ⥤ Karoubi D to functors Karoubi C ⥤ Karoubi D. This results in an equivalence karoubiUniversal₁ C D : (C ⥤ Karoubi D) ≌ (Karoubi C ⥤ Karoubi D).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.HomologicalComplex
nodes.description: This file contains simplifications lemmas for categories Karoubi (HomologicalComplex C c) and the construction of an equivalence of categories Karoubi (HomologicalComplex C c) ≌ HomologicalComplex (Karoubi C) c.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Karoubi envelope of a category
nodes.description: In this file, we define the Karoubi envelope Karoubi C of a category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.KaroubiKaroubi
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the equivalence of categories KaroubiKaroubi.equivalence C : Karoubi C ≌ Karoubi (Karoubi C) for any category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Idempotents.SimplicialObject
nodes.descriptionTitle: Idempotent completeness of categories of simplicial objects
nodes.description: In this file, we provide an instance expressing that SimplicialObject C and CosimplicialObject C are idempotent complete categories when the category C is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.InducedCategory
nodes.description: Given a category D and a function F : C → D from a type C to the objects of D, there is an essentially unique way to give C a category structure such that F becomes a fully faithful functor, namely by taking $ Hom_C(X, Y) = Hom_D(FX, FY) $. We call this the category induced from D along F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.IsConnected
nodes.description: Define a connected category as a _nonempty_ category for which every functor to a discrete category is isomorphic to the constant functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Iso
nodes.description: This file defines isomorphisms between objects of a category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.IsomorphismClasses
nodes.descriptionTitle: Objects of a category up to an isomorphism
nodes.description: IsIsomorphic X Y := Nonempty (X ≅ Y) is an equivalence relation on the objects of a category. The quotient with respect to this relation defines a functor from our category to Type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Join.Basic
nodes.description: Given categories C, D, this file constructs a category C ⋆ D. Its objects are either objects of C or objects of D, morphisms between objects of C are morphisms in C, morphisms between objects of D are morphisms in D, and finally, given c : C and d : D, there is a unique morphism c ⟶ d in C ⋆ D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Join.Final
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)Finality of the inclusions in joins of categories
nodes.description: This file records the fact that inclLeft C D : C ⥤ C ⋆ D is initial if C is connected. Dually, inclRight : C ⥤ C ⋆ D is final if D is connected.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Join.Opposites
nodes.description: This file constructs the canonical equivalence of categories (C ⋆ D)ᵒᵖ ≌ Dᵒᵖ ⋆ Cᵒᵖ. This equivalence is characterized in both directions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Join.Pseudofunctor
nodes.description: In this file, we promote the join construction to two pseudofunctors Join.pseudofunctorLeft and Join.pseudofunctorRight, expressing its pseudofunctoriality in each variable.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Join.Sum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Embedding of C ⊕ D into C ⋆ D
nodes.description: This file constructs a canonical functor Join.fromSum from C ⊕ D to C ⋆ D and gives its characterization in terms of the canonical inclusions. We also provide Faithful and EssSurj instances on this functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.Adjunction
nodes.description: In this file, we obtain Adjunction.HasLiftingProperty_iff, which states that when we have an adjunction adj : G ⊣ F between two functors G : C ⥤ D and F : D ⥤ C, then a morphism of the form G.map i has the left lifting property in D with respect to a morphism p if and only the morphism i has the left lifting property in C with respect to F.map p.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the lifting property of two morphisms in a category and shows basic properties of this notion.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.Limits
nodes.description: In this file, we show some consequences of lifting properties in the presence of certain (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.Over
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if sq is a commutative square in a category Over S for S : C, there is a lift for sq if there is a lift for the underlying commutative square in the category C. It follows that if i and p are morphisms in Over S, then i has the left lifting property with respect to p when i.left has the left lifting property with respect to p.left.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.ParametrizedAdjunction
nodes.description: If we have a parametrized adjunction adj₂ : F ⊣₂ G, sq₁₂ : F.PushoutObjObj f₁ f₂ and sq₁₃ : G.PullbackObjObj f₁ f₃, we show that sq₁₂.ι has the left lifting property with respect to f₃ if and only if f₂ has the left lifting property with respect to sq₁₃.π: this is the lemma ParametrizedAdjunction.hasLiftingProperty_iff.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LiftingProperties.PushoutProduct
nodes.description: Various equivalent lifting properties involving pushout-products and pullback-homs. For f : A ⟶ B, g : K ⟶ L, h : X ⟶ Y in a monoidal closed category with pushouts and pullbacks, f □ g lifts against h if and only if g lifts against f ⋔ h.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicones
nodes.description: Given a category J, a walking Bicone J is a category whose objects are the objects of J and two extra vertices Bicone.left and Bicone.right. The morphisms are the morphisms of J and left ⟶ j, right ⟶ j for each j : J such that (· ⟶ j) and (· ⟶ k) commutes with each f : j ⟶ k.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Chosen.End
nodes.description: This file defines typeclasses ChosenCoendsOfShape and ChosenEndsOfShape which contain the data of a chosen coend and end in C for each functor Jᵒᵖ ⥤ J ⥤ C of a fixed shape J. It also provides ChosenCoends and ChosenEnds abbreviations for chosen coends and ends of all shapes.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ColimitLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: The morphism comparing a colimit of limits with the corresponding limit of colimits.
nodes.description: For F : J × K ⥤ C there is always a morphism $\colim_k \lim_j F(j,k) → \lim_j \colim_k F(j, k)$. While it is not usually an isomorphism, with additional hypotheses on J and K it may be, in which case we say that "colimits commute with limits".

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Comma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits in comma categories
nodes.description: We build limits in the comma category Comma L R provided that the two source categories have limits and R preserves them. This is used to construct limits in the arrow category, structured arrow category and under category, and show that the appropriate forgetful functors create limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ConcreteCategory.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Facts about (co)limits of functors into concrete categories
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.ConcreteCategory.Basic.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ConcreteCategory.Filtered
nodes.description: In this file, we provide analogues to some of the API in the CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColimit namespace, for concrete categories for which the forgetful functor preserves filtered colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ConcreteCategory.WithAlgebraicStructures
nodes.description: Let C be a concrete category and F : J ⥤ C a filtered diagram in C. We discuss some results about colimit F when objects and morphisms in C have some algebraic structures.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ConeCategory
nodes.description: This file contains results that stem from the limit API. For the definition and the category instance of Cone, please refer to Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Cones.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones
nodes.description: We define Cone F, a cone over a functor F, and F.cones : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type, the functor associating to X the cones over F with cone point X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Connected
nodes.description: A connected limit is a limit whose shape is a connected category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.BinaryProducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing binary product from pullbacks and terminal object.
nodes.description: The product is the pullback over the terminal objects. In particular, if a category has pullbacks and a terminal object, then it has binary products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relating monomorphisms and epimorphisms to limits and colimits
nodes.description: If F preserves (resp. reflects) pullbacks, then it preserves (resp. reflects) monomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Equalizers
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing equalizers from pullbacks and binary products.
nodes.description: If a category has pullbacks and binary products, then it has equalizers.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.EventuallyConstant
nodes.description: If F : J ⥤ C is a functor from a cofiltered category, and j : J, we introduce a property F.IsEventuallyConstantTo j which says that for any f : i ⟶ j, the induced morphism F.map f is an isomorphism. Under this assumption, it is shown that F admits F.obj j as a limit (Functor.IsEventuallyConstantTo.isLimitCone).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Filtered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing colimits from finite colimits and filtered colimits
nodes.description: We construct colimits of size w from finite colimits and filtered colimits of size w. Since w-sized colimits are constructed from coequalizers and w-sized coproducts, it suffices to construct w-sized coproducts from finite coproducts and w-sized filtered colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.FiniteProductsOfBinaryProducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing finite products from binary products and terminal.
nodes.description: If a category has binary products and a terminal object then it has finite products. If a functor preserves binary products and the terminal object then it preserves finite products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.LimitsOfProductsAndEqualizers
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing limits from products and equalizers.
nodes.description: If a category has all products, and all equalizers, then it has all limits. Similarly, if it has all finite products, and all equalizers, then it has all finite limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Basic
nodes.description: Declare instances for limits in the over category: If C has finite wide pullbacks, Over B has finite limits, and if C has arbitrary wide pullbacks then Over B has limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Connected
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connected limits in the over category
nodes.description: We show that the projection CostructuredArrow K B ⥤ C creates and preserves connected limits, without assuming that C has any limits. In particular, CostructuredArrow K B has any connected limit which C has.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Products
nodes.description: Shows that products in the over category can be derived from wide pullbacks in the base category. The main result is over_product_of_widePullback, which says that if C has J-indexed wide pullbacks, then Over B has J-indexed products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Pullbacks
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing pullbacks from binary products and equalizers
nodes.description: If a category has binary products and equalizers, then it has pullbacks. Also, if a category has binary coproducts and coequalizers, then it has pushouts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.WeaklyInitial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructions related to weakly initial objects
nodes.description: This file gives constructions related to weakly initial objects, namely: initial object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.WidePullbackOfTerminal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of wide pullbacks when the target object is terminal
nodes.description: In this file, we show that the wide pullback of a family of arrows objs j ⟶ B exists when B is terminal and the product of the objects objs j exists.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.ZeroObjects
nodes.description: Binary products and coproducts with a zero object always exist, and pullbacks/pushouts over a zero object are products/coproducts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Creates
nodes.description: We say that F creates limits of K if, given any limit cone c for K ⋙ F (i.e. below), we can lift it to a cone "above", and further that F reflects limits for K.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Elements
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits in the category of elements
nodes.description: We show that if C has limits of shape I and A : C ⥤ Type w preserves limits of shape I, then the category of elements of A has limits of shape I and the forgetful functor π : A.Elements ⥤ C creates them.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relation between mono/epi and pullback/pushout squares
nodes.description: In this file, monomorphisms and epimorphisms are characterized in terms of pullback and pushout squares. For example, we obtain mono_iff_isPullback which asserts that a morphism f : X ⟶ Y is a monomorphism iff the obvious square

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.EssentiallySmall
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits over essentially small indexing categories
nodes.description: If C has limits of size w and J is w-essentially small, then C has limits of shape J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.ExactFunctor
nodes.description: We say that a functor F is left exact if it preserves finite limits, it is right exact if it preserves finite colimits, and it is exact if it is both left exact and right exact.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Filtered
nodes.description: In this file, we show that C is filtered if and only if for every functor F : J ⥤ C from a finite category there is some X : C such that lim Hom(F·, X) is nonempty.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FilteredColimitCommutesFiniteLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Filtered colimits commute with finite limits.
nodes.description: We show that for a functor F : J × K ⥤ Type v, when J is finite and K is filtered, the universal morphism colimitLimitToLimitColimit F comparing the colimit (over K) of the limits (over J) with the limit of the colimits is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FilteredColimitCommutesProduct
nodes.description: Given a family of categories I i (i : α) and a family of functors F i : I i ⥤ C, we consider the diagram pointwiseProduct F : Π i, I i ⥤ C defined by (Xᵢ)ᵢ ↦ ∏ᶜ Xᵢ. Given a cocone cᵢ on Fᵢ for each i, there is a natural cocone on pointwiseProduct F with point ∏ᶜ cᵢ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Final
nodes.description: A functor F : C ⥤ D is final if for every d : D, the comma category of morphisms d ⟶ F.obj c is connected.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Final.Connected
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterization of connected categories using initial/final functors
nodes.description: A category C is connected iff the constant functor C ⥤ Discrete PUnit is final (or initial).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Final.ParallelPair
nodes.descriptionTitle: Conditions for parallelPair to be initial
nodes.description: In this file we give sufficient conditions on a category C and parallel morphisms f g : X ⟶ Y in C so that parallelPair f g becomes an initial functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Final.Type
nodes.descriptionTitle: Action of an initial functor on sections
nodes.description: Given F : C ⥤ D and P : D ⥤ Type w, we define a map sectionsPrecomp F : P.sections → (F ⋙ P).sections and show that it is a bijection when F is initial. As Functor.sections identify to limits of functors to types (at least under suitable universe assumptions), this could be deduced from general results about limits and initial functors, but we provide a more down to earth proof.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FinallySmall
nodes.description: A category given by (J : Type u) [Category.{v} J] is w-finally small if there exists a FinalModel J : Type w equipped with [SmallCategory (FinalModel J)] and a final functor FinalModel J ⥤ J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FintypeCat
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)limits in the category of finite types
nodes.description: We show that finite (co)limits exist in FintypeCat and that they are preserved by the natural inclusion FintypeCat.incl.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproducts
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproducts.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we construct the category of formal coproducts given a category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproducts.Cech
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Cech object for formal coproducts
nodes.description: Let C be a category that has finite products. In this file, we define a functor cechFunctor : FormalCoproduct C ⥤ SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct C) which sends a formal coproduct of objects U j (for j : ι) to the simplicial object which sends ⦋n⦌ to the formal coproduct, indexed by i : Fin (n + 1) → ι, of the products of the objects U (i a) for all a : Fin (n + 1).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproducts.ExtraDegeneracy
nodes.description: Let U : FormalCoproduct C. Let T be a terminal object in C. In this file, we construct an isomorphism from the Cech object U.cech that is defined for objects in FormalCoproduct to the general Cech nerve construction applied to the morphism from U to the terminal object. This isomorphism is used in order to show that, as an augmented object (over T), the Cech object U.cech has an extra degeneracy when there is a morphism T ⟶ U.obj i₀ for some i₀.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Fubini
nodes.description: We prove that $lim_{J × K} G = lim_J (lim_K G(j, -))$ for a functor G : J × K ⥤ C, when all the appropriate limits exist.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FullSubcategory
nodes.description: If a property of objects P is closed under taking limits, then limits in FullSubcategory P can be constructed from limits in C. More precisely, the inclusion creates such limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Basic
nodes.description: We show that if D has limits, then the functor category C ⥤ D also has limits (CategoryTheory.Limits.functorCategoryHasLimits), and the evaluation functors preserve limits (CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluation_preservesLimits) (and similarly for colimits).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.BinaryBiproducts
nodes.description: We show that if C has binary biproducts, then the functor category D ⥤ C also has binary biproducts (CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBiproduct.functorCategoryHasBinaryBiproducts).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monomorphisms and epimorphisms in functor categories
nodes.description: A natural transformation f : F ⟶ G between functors K ⥤ C is a mono (resp. epi) iff for all k : K, f.app k is, at least when C has pullbacks (resp. pushouts), see NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app and NatTrans.epi_iff_epi_app.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Filtered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functor categories have filtered colimits when the target category does
nodes.description: These declarations cannot be in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/FunctorCategory/Basic.lean because that file shouldn't import Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Filtered.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functor categories have finite limits when the target category does
nodes.description: These declarations cannot be in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/FunctorCategory/Basic.lean because that file shouldn't import Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/FiniteProducts.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Images
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of type-valued functors has images
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Images.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Kernels
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Kernels.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Products
nodes.description: Given f : α → D ⥤ C, we prove the isomorphisms (∏ᶜ f).obj d ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun s => (f s).obj d) and (∐ f).obj d ≅ ∐ (fun s => (f s).obj d).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Pullbacks
nodes.description: We prove the isomorphism (pullback f g).obj d ≅ pullback (f.app d) (g.app d).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorCategory.Shapes.Terminal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Initial and terminal objects in the category of functors
nodes.description: We show that if a functor F : C ⥤ D is such that F.obj X is terminal for all X, then F is a terminal object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.FunctorToTypes
nodes.descriptionTitle: Concrete description of (co)limits in functor categories
nodes.description: Some of the concrete descriptions of (co)limits in Type v extend to (co)limits in the functor category K ⥤ Type v.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits
nodes.description: In CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit we defined IsLimit c, the data showing that a cone c is a limit cone.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.IndYoneda
nodes.description: We define limit versions of the yoneda and coyoneda lemmas.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.Category
nodes.description: We define the v-category of Ind-objects of a category C, called Ind C, as well as the functors Ind.yoneda : C ⥤ Ind C and Ind.inclusion C : Ind C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.Equalizers
nodes.description: We show that if a category C has equalizers, then ind-objects are closed under equalizers.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.FilteredColimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ind-objects are closed under filtered colimits
nodes.description: We show that if F : I ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v is a functor such that I is small and filtered and F.obj i is an ind-object for all i, then colimit F is also an ind-object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.IndObject
nodes.description: For a presheaf A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v we define the type IndObjectPresentation A of presentations of A as a small filtered colimit of representable presheaves and define the predicate IsIndObject A asserting that there is at least one such presentation.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.LocallySmall
nodes.descriptionTitle: There are only v-many natural transformations between Ind-objects
nodes.description: We provide the instance LocallySmall.{v} (FullSubcategory (IsIndObject (C := C))), which will serve as the basis for our definition of the category of Ind-objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.ParallelPair
nodes.descriptionTitle: Parallel pairs of natural transformations between ind-objects
nodes.description: We show that if A and B are ind-objects and f and g are natural transformations between A and B, then there is a small filtered category I such that A, B, f and g are commonly presented by diagrams and natural transformations in I ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization.Products
nodes.description: We show that if C admits products indexed by α, then IsIndObject is closed under taking products in Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v indexed by α. This will imply that the functor Ind C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v creates products indexed by α and that the functor C ⥤ Ind C preserves them.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.IsConnected
nodes.description: This file proves two characterizations of connected categories by means of colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit
nodes.description: We set up the general theory of limits and colimits in a category. In this introduction we only describe the setup for limits; it is repeated, with slightly different names, for colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Lattice
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits in lattice categories are given by infimums and supremums.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.Lattice.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.MonoCoprod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Categories where inclusions into coproducts are monomorphisms
nodes.description: If C is a category, the class MonoCoprod C expresses that left inclusions A ⟶ A ⨿ B are monomorphisms when HasCoproduct A B holds. If so, it is shown that right inclusions are also monomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)limits in subcategories of comma categories defined by morphism properties
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.MorphismProperty.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Opposites
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits in C give colimits in Cᵒᵖ.
nodes.description: We construct limits and colimits in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits in the over and under categories
nodes.description: Show that the forgetful functor forget X : Over X ⥤ C creates colimits, and hence Over X has any colimits that C has (as well as the dual that forget X : Under X ⟶ C creates limits).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits in the category of indexed families of objects.
nodes.description: Given a functor F : J ⥤ Π i, C i into a category of indexed families, 1. we can assemble a collection of cones over F ⋙ Pi.eval C i into a cone over F 2. if all those cones are limit cones, the assembled cone is a limit cone, and 3. if we have limits for each of F ⋙ Pi.eval C i, we can produce a HasLimit F instance

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preorder
nodes.description: We provide basic results about (co)limits in the associated category of a preordered type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Presentation
nodes.description: Let J and C be categories and X : C. We define type ColimitPresentation J X that contains the data of objects Dⱼ and natural maps sⱼ : Dⱼ ⟶ X that make X the colimit of the Dⱼ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Basic
nodes.description: There are various distinct notions of "preserving limits". The one we aim to capture here is: A functor F : C ⥤ D "preserves limits" if it sends every limit cone in C to a limit cone in D. Informally, F preserves all the limits which exist in C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Bifunctor
nodes.description: Let G : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C a functor. We introduce a class PreservesLimit₂ K₁ K₂ G that encodes the hypothesis that the curried functor F : C₁ × C₂ ⥤ C preserves limits of the diagram K₁ × K₂ : J₁ × J₂ ⥤ C₁ × C₂. We give a basic API to extract isomorphisms $\lim_{(j_1,j_2)} G(K_1(j_1), K_2(j_2)) \simeq G(\lim K_1, \lim K_2)$ out of this typeclass.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.BifunctorCokernel
nodes.description: Let c₁ (resp. c₂) be a cokernel cofork for a morphism f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁ in a category C₁ (resp. f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂ in C₂). Given a bifunctor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C, we construct a cokernel cofork with point (F.obj c₁.pt).obj c₂.pt for the obvious morphism (F.obj X₁).obj Y₂ ⨿ (F.obj Y₁).obj X₂ ⟶ (F.obj Y₁).obj Y₂, and show that it is a colimit when both coforks are colimit, the cokernel of f₁ is preserved by F.obj c₁.pt and the cokernel of f₂ is preserved by F.flip.obj X₁ and F.flip.obj Y₁.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Creates.Finite
nodes.description: This file defines the classes CreatesFiniteLimits, CreatesFiniteColimits, CreatesFiniteProducts and CreatesFiniteCoproducts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Creates.Opposites
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limit creation properties of Functor.op and related constructions
nodes.description: We formulate conditions about F which imply that F.op, F.unop, F.leftOp and F.rightOp create certain (co)limits and vice versa.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Creates.Pullbacks
nodes.description: We show some lemmas relating creation of (co)limits and pullbacks (resp. pushouts).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Filtered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of filtered colimits and cofiltered limits.
nodes.description: Typically forgetful functors from algebraic categories preserve filtered colimits (although not general colimits). See e.g. Mathlib/Algebra/Category/MonCat/FilteredColimits.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Finite
nodes.description: These functors are also known as left exact (flat) or right exact functors when the categories involved are abelian, or more generally, finitely (co)complete.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.FunctorCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of (co)limits in the functor category
nodes.description: for F : C ⥤ D preserves colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Grothendieck
nodes.descriptionTitle: Colimits on Grothendieck constructions preserving limits
nodes.description: We characterize the condition in which colimits on Grothendieck constructions preserve limits: By preserving limits on the Grothendieck construction's base category as well as on each of its fibers.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Limits
nodes.description: If G preserves limits, and C and D have limits, then for any diagram F : J ⥤ C we have a canonical isomorphism preservesLimitsIso : G.obj (Limit F) ≅ Limit (F ⋙ G). We also show that we can commute IsLimit.lift of a preserved limit with Functor.mapCone: (PreservesLimit.preserves t).lift (G.mapCone c₂) = G.map (t.lift c₂).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Opposites
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limit preservation properties of Functor.op and related constructions
nodes.description: We formulate conditions about F which imply that F.op, F.unop, F.leftOp and F.rightOp preserve certain (co)limits and vice versa.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: Forgetful functor from Over X preserves cofiltered limits
nodes.description: Note that Over.forget X : Over X ⥤ C already preserves all colimits because it is a left adjoint. See Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Comma/Over/Pullback.lean

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Presheaf
nodes.description: In this file we prove that if C is a small finitely cocomplete category and A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u is a presheaf, then CostructuredArrow yoneda A is filtered (equivalently, the category of elements of A is cofiltered) if and only if A preserves finite limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.AbelianImages
nodes.description: If a functor preserves kernels and cokernels, then it preserves abelian images, abelian coimages and coimage-image comparisons.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.BinaryProducts
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving binary products and reflecting binary products to concrete binary fans.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Biproducts
nodes.description: We define the image of a (binary) bicone under a functor that preserves zero morphisms and define classes PreservesBiproduct and PreservesBinaryBiproduct. We then

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Equalizers
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving (co)equalizers and reflecting (co)equalizers to concrete (co)forks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Images
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if a functor preserves spans and cospans, then it preserves images.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Kernels
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving (co)kernels and reflecting (co)kernels to concrete (co)forks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Multiequalizer
nodes.description: Let J : MultispanShape and d : MultispanIndex J C. If F : C ⥤ D, we define d.map F : MultispanIndex J D and an isomorphism of functors (d.map F).multispan ≅ d.multispan ⋙ F (see MultispanIndex.multispanMapIso). If c : Multicofork d, we define c.map F : Multicofork (d.map F) and obtain a bijection IsColimit (F.mapCocone c) ≃ IsColimit (c.map F) (see Multicofork.isColimitMapEquiv).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: If a functor preserves limits, so does the induced functor in the Over or Under category
nodes.description: Suppose we are given categories C and D, and object X : C, and a functor F : C ⥤ D. F induces a functor Over.post F : Over X ⥤ Over (F.obj X). If F preserves limits of a certain shape WithTerminal J, then Over.post F preserves limits of shape J. As a corollary, if F preserves finite limits, or limits of a certain size, so does Over.post F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Preorder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of well order continuous functors
nodes.description: Given a well-ordered type J and a functor G : C ⥤ D, we define a type class PreservesWellOrderContinuousOfShape J G saying that G preserves colimits of shape Set.Iio j for any limit element j : J. It follows that if F : J ⥤ C is well order continuous, then so is F ⋙ G.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Products
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving products and reflecting products to concrete fans.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Pullbacks
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving pullbacks and reflecting pullbacks to concrete pullback cones.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Square
nodes.description: If a functor F : C ⥤ D preserves suitable cospans (resp. spans), and sq : Square C is a pullback square (resp. a pushout square) then so is the square sq.map F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Terminal
nodes.description: Constructions to relate the notions of preserving terminal objects and reflecting terminal objects to concrete objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Zero
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of zero objects and zero morphisms
nodes.description: We define the class PreservesZeroMorphisms and show basic properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.SigmaConst
nodes.description: Given an object R in a category C with coproducts of size w, the functor sigmaConst.obj R : Type w ⥤ C which sends a type T to the coproduct of copies of R indexed by T preserves all colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Ulift
nodes.description: This file shows that uliftFunctor.{v, u} preserves all limits and colimits, including those potentially too big to exist in Type u.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Yoneda
nodes.description: Given a bifunctor F : J ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v, we prove the isomorphism Hom(YX, colim_j F(j, -)) ≅ colim_j Hom(YX, F(j, -)), where Y is the Yoneda embedding.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Presheaf
nodes.description: In this file, We show that every presheaf of types on a category C (with Category.{v₁} C) is a colimit of representables. This result is also known as the density theorem, the co-Yoneda lemma and the Ninja Yoneda lemma. Three formulations are given: for yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁; for uliftYoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type max w v₁, when the presheaf has values in Type max w v₁;

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Set
nodes.descriptionTitle: The functor from Set X to types preserves filtered colimits
nodes.description: Given X : Type u, the functor Set.functorToTypes : Set X ⥤ Type u which sends A : Set X to its underlying type preserves filtered colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryBiproducts
nodes.description: We introduce the notion of binary biproducts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryProducts
nodes.description: We define a category WalkingPair, which is the index category for a binary (co)product diagram. A convenience method pair X Y constructs the functor from the walking pair, hitting the given objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Biproducts
nodes.description: We introduce the notion of (finite) biproducts. Binary biproducts are defined in CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.BinaryBiproducts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.CombinedProducts
nodes.description: We provide constructors for combining (co)fans and show their (co)limit properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.ConcreteCategory
nodes.description: In this file, we combine the description of limits in Types and the API about the preservation of products and pullbacks in order to describe these limits in a concrete category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Connected
nodes.description: In this file we prove that various shapes are connected.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Countable
nodes.description: A typeclass for categories with all countable (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Diagonal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The diagonal object of a morphism.
nodes.description: We provide various API and isomorphisms considering the diagonal object Δ_{Y/X} := pullback f f of a morphism f : X ⟶ Y.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.DisjointCoproduct
nodes.description: Defines disjoint coproducts: coproducts where the intersection is initial and the coprojections are monic. Shows that a category with disjoint coproducts is InitialMonoClass.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.End
nodes.description: In this file, given a functor F : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ J ⥤ C, we define its end end_ F, which is a suitable multiequalizer of the objects (F.obj (op j)).obj j for all j : J. For this shape of limits, cones are named wedges: the corresponding type is Wedge F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Equalizers
nodes.description: This file defines (co)equalizers as special cases of (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Equivalence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transporting existence of specific limits across equivalences
nodes.description: For now, we only treat the case of initial and terminal objects, but other special shapes can be added in the future.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.FiniteLimits
nodes.description: A typeclass for categories with all finite (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.FiniteMultiequalizer
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.FiniteMultiequalizer.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.FiniteProducts
nodes.description: Typeclasses representing categories with (co)products over finite indexing types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.FunctorToTypes
nodes.description: Defines an explicit construction of binary products and coproducts of type-valued functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Grothendieck
nodes.description: fiber of G has a colimit, then so does the fiberwise colimit functor C ⥤ H. then G has a colimit. "fibered colimits", i.e. of applying the colimit to each fiber of the functor. on each fiber shape F.obj X and on the base category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Images
nodes.description: We define the categorical image of f as a factorisation f = e ≫ m through a monomorphism m, so that m factors through the m' in any other such factorisation.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.IsTerminal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Initial and terminal objects in a category.
nodes.description: In this file we define the predicates IsTerminal and IsInitial as well as the class InitialMonoClass.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.KernelPair
nodes.description: This file defines what it means for a parallel pair of morphisms a b : R ⟶ X to be the kernel pair for a morphism f. Some properties of kernel pairs are given, namely allowing one to transfer between the kernel pair of f₁ ≫ f₂ to the kernel pair of f₁. It is also proved that if f is a coequalizer of some pair, and a,b is a kernel pair for f then it is a coequalizer of a,b.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Kernels
nodes.description: In a category with zero morphisms, the kernel of a morphism f : X ⟶ Y is the equalizer of f and 0 : X ⟶ Y. (Similarly the cokernel is the coequalizer.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Multiequalizer
nodes.description: A multiequalizer is an equalizer of two morphisms between two products. Since both products and equalizers are limits, such an object is again a limit. This file provides the diagram whose limit is indeed such an object. In fact, it is well-known that any limit can be obtained as a multiequalizer. The dual construction (multicoequalizers) is also provided.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.MultiequalizerPullback
nodes.description: In this file, we show that a multicoequalizer for I : MultispanIndex (.ofLinearOrder ι) C is also a pushout when ι has exactly two elements.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.NormalMono.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definitions and basic properties of normal monomorphisms and epimorphisms.
nodes.description: A normal monomorphism is a morphism that is the kernel of some other morphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.NormalMono.Equalizers
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normal mono categories with finite products and kernels have all equalizers.
nodes.description: This, and the dual result, are used in the development of abelian categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Opposites.Equalizers
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equalizers and coequalizers in C and Cᵒᵖ
nodes.description: We construct equalizers and coequalizers in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Opposites.Filtered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Filtered colimits and cofiltered limits in C and Cᵒᵖ
nodes.description: We construct filtered colimits and cofiltered limits in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Opposites.Kernels
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kernels and cokernels in C and Cᵒᵖ
nodes.description: We construct kernels and cokernels in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Opposites.Products
nodes.descriptionTitle: Products and coproducts in C and Cᵒᵖ
nodes.description: We construct products and coproducts in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Opposites.Pullbacks
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pullbacks and pushouts in C and Cᵒᵖ
nodes.description: We construct pullbacks and pushouts in the opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.PiProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: A product as a binary product
nodes.description: We write a product indexed by I as a binary product of the products indexed by a subset of I and its complement.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits indexed by preorders
nodes.description: In this file, we obtain the following very basic results about limits and colimits indexed by a preordered type J:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.Fin
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits indexed by Fin
nodes.description: In this file, we show that 0 : Fin (n + 1) is an initial object and Fin.last n is a terminal object. This allows to compute limits and colimits indexed by Fin (n + 1), see limitOfDiagramInitial and colimitOfDiagramTerminal in the file Limits.Shapes.IsTerminal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.HasIterationOfShape
nodes.descriptionTitle: An assumption for constructions by transfinite induction
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the typeclass HasIterationOfShape J C which is an assumption in order to do constructions by transfinite induction indexed by a well-ordered type J in a category C (see CategoryTheory.SmallObject).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.PrincipalSeg
nodes.description: If f : α <i β is a principal segment and F : β ⥤ C, there is a cocone for f.monotone.functor ⋙ F : α ⥤ C the point of which is F.obj f.top.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.TransfiniteCompositionOfShape
nodes.descriptionTitle: A structure to describe transfinite compositions
nodes.description: Given a well-ordered type J and a morphism f : X ⟶ Y in a category, we introduce a structure TransfiniteCompositionOfShape J f expressing that f is a transfinite composition of shape J. This allows to extend this structure in order to require more properties or data for the morphisms F.obj j ⟶ F.obj (Order.succ j) which appear in the transfinite composition. See MorphismProperty.TransfiniteCompositionOfShape in the file MorphismProperty.TransfiniteComposition.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Preorder.WellOrderContinuous
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuity of functors from well-ordered types
nodes.description: Let F : J ⥤ C be a functor from a well-ordered type J. We introduce the typeclass F.IsWellOrderContinuous to say that if m is a limit element, then F.obj m is the colimit of the F.obj j for j < m.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Products
nodes.description: This file defines (co)products as special cases of (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Assoc
nodes.description: This file shows that pullbacks (and pushouts) are associative up to natural isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Categorical.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the basic properties of categorical pullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Categorical.CatCospanTransform
nodes.description: Given F : A ⥤ B, G : C ⥤ B, F' : A' ⥤ B' and G' : C' ⥤ B', this file defines CatCospanTransform F G F' G', the category of "categorical transformations" from the (categorical) cospan F G to the (categorical) cospan F' G'. Such a transformation consists of a diagram

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.ChosenPullback
nodes.description: Given two morphisms f₁ : X₁ ⟶ S and f₂ : X₂ ⟶ S, we introduce a structure ChosenPullback f₁ f₂ which contains the data of pullback of f₁ and f₂.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.CommSq
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Connected
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Connected.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Cospan
nodes.description: We define a category WalkingCospan (resp. WalkingSpan), which is the index category for the given data for a pullback (resp. pushout) diagram. Convenience methods cospan f g and span f g construct functors from the walking (co)span, hitting the given morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Equalizer
nodes.description: Also see CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Equalizers for very similar results.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Equifibered
nodes.description: A natural transformation α : F ⟶ G is equifibered if every commutative square of the following form is a pullback.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.EquifiberedLimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors equifibered over a fixed functor is closed under limits
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.EquifiberedLimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.HasPullback
nodes.description: HasPullback f g and pullback f g provides API for HasLimit and limit in the case of pullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.Basic
nodes.description: We restate some results about pullbacks/pushouts in the language of IsPullback and IsPushout, among which the pasting lemmas

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.BicartesianSq
nodes.description: BicartesianSq f g h i is the proposition that is a pullback square and a pushout square.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.Defs
nodes.description: We provide another API for pullbacks and pushouts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.Kernels
nodes.descriptionTitle: Horizontal maps in a pullback square have the same kernel
nodes.description: Consider a commutative square: is an isomorphism. is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Iso
nodes.description: This file provides some basic results about the pullback (and pushout) of an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Mono
nodes.description: This file provides some results about interactions between pullbacks and monomorphisms, as well as the dual statements between pushouts and epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Pasting
nodes.description: This file proves the pasting lemma for pullbacks. That is, given the following diagram: if the right square is a pullback, then the left square is a pullback iff the big square is a pullback.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.PullbackCone
nodes.description: This file provides API for interacting with cones (resp. cocones) in the case of pullbacks (resp. pushouts).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.PullbackObjObj
nodes.description: Let F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃. Given morphisms f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁ in C₁ and f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂ in C₂, we introduce a structure F.PushoutObjObj f₁ f₂ which contains the data of a pushout of (F.obj Y₁).obj X₂ and (F.obj X₁).obj Y₂ along (F.obj X₁).obj X₂. If sq₁₂ : F.PushoutObjObj f₁ f₂, we have a canonical "inclusion" sq₁₂.ι : sq₁₂.pt ⟶ (F.obj Y₁).obj Y₂.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.Square
nodes.descriptionTitle: Commutative squares that are pushout or pullback squares
nodes.description: In this file, we translate the IsPushout and IsPullback API for the objects of the category Square C of commutative squares in a category C. We also obtain lemmas which state in this language that a pullback of a monomorphism is a monomorphism (and similarly for pushouts of epimorphisms).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Reflexive
nodes.description: This file deals with reflexive pairs, which are pairs of morphisms with a common section.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.RegularMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definitions and basic properties of regular monomorphisms and epimorphisms.
nodes.description: A regular monomorphism is a morphism that is the equalizer of some parallel pair.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.SequentialProduct
nodes.description: Given sequences M N : ℕ → C of objects with morphisms f n : M n ⟶ N n for all n, this file exhibits ∏ M as the limit of the tower

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.SingleObj
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)limits of functors out of SingleObj M
nodes.description: We characterise (co)limits of shape SingleObj M. Currently only in the category of types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.SplitCoequalizer
nodes.description: We define what it means for a triple of morphisms f g : X ⟶ Y, π : Y ⟶ Z to be a split coequalizer: there is a section s of π and a section t of g, which additionally satisfy t ≫ f = π ≫ s.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.SplitEqualizer
nodes.description: We define what it means for a triple of morphisms f g : X ⟶ Y, ι : W ⟶ X to be a split equalizer: there is a retraction r of ι and a retraction t of g, which additionally satisfy t ≫ f = r ≫ ι.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.StrictInitial
nodes.description: This file sets up the basic theory of strict initial objects: initial objects where every morphism to it is an isomorphism. This generalises a property of the empty set in the category of sets: namely that the only function to the empty set is from itself.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.StrongEpi
nodes.description: In this file, we define strong epimorphisms. A strong epimorphism is an epimorphism f which has the (unique) left lifting property with respect to monomorphisms. Similarly, a strong monomorphism is a monomorphism which has the (unique) right lifting property with respect to epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Terminal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Initial and terminal objects in a category.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Terminal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.WideEqualizers
nodes.description: This file defines wide (co)equalizers as special cases of (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.WidePullbacks
nodes.description: We define the category WidePullbackShape, (resp. WidePushoutShape) which is the category obtained from a discrete category of type J by adjoining a terminal (resp. initial) element. Limits of this shape are wide pullbacks (pushouts). The convenience method wideCospan (wideSpan) constructs a functor from this category, hitting the given morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.ZeroMorphisms
nodes.description: A category "has zero morphisms" if there is a designated "zero morphism" in each morphism space, and compositions of zero morphisms with anything give the zero morphism. (Notice this is extra structure, not merely a property.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.ZeroObjects
nodes.description: A category "has a zero object" if it has an object which is both initial and terminal. Having a zero object provides zero morphisms, as the unique morphisms factoring through the zero object; see CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.ZeroMorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Sifted
nodes.description: A category C is sifted if C is nonempty and the diagonal functor C ⥤ C × C is final. Sifted categories can be characterized as those such that the colimit functor (C ⥤ Type) ⥤ Type preserves finite products. We achieve this characterization in this file.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Skeleton
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)limits of the skeleton of a category
nodes.description: The skeleton of a category inherits all (co)limits the category has.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.SmallComplete
nodes.descriptionTitle: Any small complete category is a preorder
nodes.description: We show that any small category which has all (small) limits is a preorder: In particular, we show that if a small category C in universe u has products of size u, then for any X Y : C there is at most one morphism X ⟶ Y. Note that in Lean, a preorder category is strictly one where the morphisms are in Prop, so we instead show that the homsets are subsingleton.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Coequalizers
nodes.description: The coequalizer of a pair of maps (f, g) from X to Y is the quotient of Y by ∀ x : Y, f x ~ g x

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.ColimitType
nodes.descriptionTitle: The colimit type of a functor to types
nodes.description: Given a category J (with J : Type u and [Category.{v} J]) and a functor F : J ⥤ Type w₀, we introduce a type F.ColimitType : Type (max u w₀), which satisfies a certain universal property of the colimit: it is defined as a suitable quotient of Σ j, F.obj j. This universal property is not expressed in a categorical way (as in general Type (max u w₀) is not the same as Type u).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.ColimitTypeFiltered
nodes.description: In this file, given a functor F : J ⥤ Type w₀ from a filtered category J, we compute the equivalence relation generated by F.ColimitTypeRel on (j : J) × (F.obj j). Given c : CoconeTypes F, we deduce a lemma Functor.CoconeTypes.injective_descColimitType_iff_of_isFiltered which gives a concrete condition under which the map F.descColimitType c : F.ColimitType → c.pt is injective, which is an important step when proving c.IsColimit.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Colimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Colimits in the category of types
nodes.description: We show that the category of types has all colimits, by providing the usual concrete models.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Coproducts
