nodes.description: If F : J → Type max v u (with J : Type v), we show that the coproduct of F exists in Type max v u and identifies to the sigma type Σ j, F j. Similarly, the binary coproduct of two types X and Y identifies to X ⊕ Y, and the initial object of Type u if PEmpty.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.End
nodes.description: This file constructs explicit ends and coends in Type and provides ChosenEnds and ChosenCoends instances using these constructions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Equalizers
nodes.description: The equalizer of a pair of maps (g, h) from X to Y is the subtype {x : Y // g x = h x}.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Filtered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Filtered colimits in the category of types.
nodes.description: We give a characterisation of the equality in filtered colimits in Type as a lemma CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColimit.colimit_eq_iff: colimit.ι F i xi = colimit.ι F j xj ↔ ∃ k (f : i ⟶ k) (g : j ⟶ k), F.map f xi = F.map g xj.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Images
nodes.descriptionTitle: Images in the category of types
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that the category of types has categorical images, and that these agree with the range of a function.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits in the category of types.
nodes.description: We show that the category of types has all limits, by providing the usual concrete models.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Multicoequalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multicoequalizers in the category of types
nodes.description: Given J : MultispanShape, d : MultispanIndex J (Type u) and c : d.multispan.CoconeTypes, we obtain a lemma isMulticoequalizer_iff which gives a criteria for c to be a colimit (i.e. a multicoequalizer): it restates in a more explicit manner the injectivity and surjectivity conditions for the map d.multispan.descColimitType c : d.multispan.ColimitType → c.pt.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Multiequalizer
nodes.description: Given J : MulticospanShape and I : MulticospanIndex J (Type u), we define a type I.sections. When c : Multifork I, we show that c is a limit iff the canonical map c.toSections : c.pt → I.sections is a bijection.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Products
nodes.description: We describe arbitrary products in the category of types, as well as binary products, and the terminal object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Pullbacks
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pullbacks in the category of types
nodes.description: In Type, the pullback of f : X ⟶ Z and g : Y ⟶ Z is the subtype { p : X × Y // f p.1 = g p.2 } of the product. We show some additional lemmas for pullbacks in the category of types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Pushouts
nodes.description: We describe the pushout of two maps f : S ⟶ X₁ and g : S ⟶ X₂ in the category of types as the quotient of X₁ ⊕ X₂ by the equivalence relation generated by a relation. We also study the particular case when f is injective (in the file CategoryTheory.Types.Monomorphisms, it is deduced that monomorphisms are stable under cobase change in the category of types).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Shapes
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Yoneda
nodes.description: In this file, we give the natural isomorphism between cones on F with cone point X and the type lim Hom(X, F·), and similarly the natural isomorphism between cocones on F with cocone point X and the type lim Hom(F·, X).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Unit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Discrete PUnit has limits and colimits
nodes.description: Mostly for the sake of constructing trivial examples, we show all (co)cones into Discrete PUnit are (co)limit (co)cones. We also show that such (co)cones exist, and that Discrete PUnit has all (co)limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.VanKampen
nodes.descriptionTitle: Universal colimits and van Kampen colimits
nodes.description: if it is stable under pullbacks. Kampen if for every cocone c' over the pullback of the diagram F' : J ⥤ C', c' is colimiting iff c' is the pullback of c.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Limits.Yoneda
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limit properties relating to the (co)yoneda embedding.
nodes.description: We calculate the colimit of Y ↦ (X ⟶ Y), which is just PUnit. (This is used in characterising cofinal functors.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Linear.Basic
nodes.description: An R-linear category is a category in which X ⟶ Y is an R-module in such a way that composition of morphisms is R-linear in both variables.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Linear.FunctorCategory
nodes.description: If C and D are categories and D is R-linear, then C ⥤ D is also R-linear.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Linear.LinearFunctor
nodes.description: An additive functor between two R-linear categories is called linear if the induced map on hom types is a morphism of R-modules.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Linear.Yoneda
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Yoneda embedding for R-linear categories
nodes.description: The Yoneda embedding for R-linear categories C, sends an object X : C to the ModuleCat R-valued presheaf on C, with value on Y : Cᵒᵖ given by ModuleCat.of R (unop Y ⟶ X).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Adjunction
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if we have an adjunction adj : G ⊣ F such that both functors G : C₁ ⥤ C₂ and F : C₂ ⥤ C₁ induce functors G' : D₁ ⥤ D₂ and F' : D₂ ⥤ D₁ on localized categories, i.e. that we have localization functors L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁ and L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂ with respect to morphism properties W₁ and W₂ respectively, and 2-commutative diagrams [CatCommSq G L₁ L₂ G'] and [CatCommSq F L₂ L₁ F'], then we have an induced adjunction Adjunction.localization L₁ W₁ L₂ W₂ G' F' : G' ⊣ F'.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Bifunctor
nodes.description: In this file, in the context of the localization of categories, we extend the notion of lifting of functors to the case of bifunctors. As the localization of categories behaves well with respect to finite products of categories (when the classes of morphisms contain identities), all the definitions for bifunctors C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ E are obtained by reducing to the case of functors (C₁ × C₂) ⥤ E by using currying and uncurrying.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Bousfield
nodes.description: Given a predicate P : ObjectProperty C on the objects of a category C, we define W.isLocal : MorphismProperty C as the class of morphisms f : X ⟶ Y such that for any Z : C such that P Z, the precomposition with f induces a bijection (Y ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Z).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.BousfieldTransfiniteComposition
nodes.descriptionTitle: ObjectProperty.isLocal is stable under transfinite compositions
nodes.description: If P : ObjectProperty C, then P.isLocal : MorphismProperty C is stable under transfinite compositions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.CalculusOfFractions
nodes.description: Following the definitions by Gabriel and Zisman, given a morphism property W : MorphismProperty C on a category C, we introduce the class W.HasLeftCalculusOfFractions. The main result Localization.exists_leftFraction is that if L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for W, then for any morphism L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y in D, there exists an auxiliary object Y' : C and morphisms g : X ⟶ Y' and s : Y ⟶ Y', with W s, such that the given morphism is a sort of fraction g / s, or more precisely of the form L.map g ≫ (Localizati...

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.CalculusOfFractions.ComposableArrows
nodes.descriptionTitle: Essential surjectivity of the functor induced on composable arrows
nodes.description: Assuming that L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for a class of morphisms W that has a calculus of left or right fractions, we show in this file that the functor L.mapComposableArrows n : ComposableArrows C n ⥤ ComposableArrows D n is essentially surjective for any n : ℕ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.CalculusOfFractions.Fractions
nodes.description: Let W : MorphismProperty C, and objects X and Y in C. In this file, we introduce structures like W.LeftFraction₂ X Y which consists of two left fractions with the "same denominator" which shall be important in the construction of the preadditive structure on the localized category when C is preadditive and W has a left calculus of fractions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.CalculusOfFractions.OfAdjunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: The calculus of fractions deduced from an adjunction
nodes.description: If G ⊣ F is an adjunction, F is fully faithful, and W is a class of morphisms that is inverted by G and such that the morphism adj.unit.app X belongs to W for any object X, then G is a localization functor with respect to W. Moreover, if W is multiplicative, then W has a calculus of left fractions. This holds in particular if W is the inverse image of the class of isomorphisms by G.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.CalculusOfFractions.Preadditive
nodes.descriptionTitle: The preadditive category structure on the localized category
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if W : MorphismProperty C has a left calculus of fractions, and C is preadditive, then the localized category is preadditive, and the localization functor is additive.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Composition
nodes.description: Given two composable functors L₁ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ and L₂ : C₂ ⥤ C₃, it is shown in this file that under some suitable conditions on W₁ : MorphismProperty C₁ W₂ : MorphismProperty C₂ and W₃ : MorphismProperty C₁, then if L₁ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ is a localization functor for W₁, then the composition L₁ ⋙ L₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₃ is a localization functor for W₃ if and only if L₂ : C₂ ⥤ C₃ is a localization functor for W₂. The two implications are the lemmas Functor.IsLocalization.comp and Functor.IsLocalization.of_comp.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Construction
nodes.description: This file constructs the localized category, obtained by formally inverting a class of maps W : MorphismProperty C in a category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.Basic
nodes.description: Let Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂ be a localizer morphism, i.e. W₁ : MorphismProperty C₁, W₂ : MorphismProperty C₂, and Φ.functor : C₁ ⥤ C₂ is a functor which maps W₁ to W₂. Following the definition introduced by Bruno Kahn and Georges Maltsiniotis in Bruno Kahn and Georges Maltsiniotis, Structures de dérivabilité, we say that Φ is a right derivability structure if Φ has right resolutions and the following 2-square is Guitart exact, where L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁ and L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂ are localization functors for W₁ and W₂, and F...

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.Constructor
nodes.description: In this file, we provide a constructor for right and left derivability structures. Assume that W₁ and W₂ are classes of morphisms in categories C₁ and C₂, and that we have a localizer morphism Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂ that is a localized equivalence, i.e. Φ.functor induces an equivalence of categories between the localized categories. Assume moreover that W₂ contains identities.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.Derives
nodes.descriptionTitle: Deriving functors using a derivability structure
nodes.description: Let Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂ be a localizer morphism between classes of morphisms on categories C₁ and C₂. Let F : C₂ ⥤ H. When Φ is a left or right derivability structure, it allows to derive the functor F (with respect to W₂) when Φ.functor ⋙ F : C₁ ⥤ H inverts W₁ (this is the most favorable case when we can apply the lemma hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_iff_of_isRightDerivabilityStructure). We define Φ.Derives F as an abbreviation for W₁.IsInvertedBy (Φ.functor ⋙ F).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.OfFunctorialResolutions
nodes.description: In this file, we provide a constructor for right derivability structures. We assume that Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂ is given by a fully faithful functor Φ.functor : C₁ ⥤ C₂ and that we have a resolution functor ρ : C₂ ⥤ C₁ with a natural transformation i : 𝟭 C₂ ⟶ ρ ⋙ Φ.functor such that W₂ (i.app X₂) for any X₂ : C₂. If we assume that W₁ is induced by W₂, that W₂ is multiplicative and has the two-out-of-three property, then Φ is a right derivability structure.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.OfLocalizedEquivalences
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivability structures deduced from localized equivalences
nodes.description: Assume that we have a diagram of localizer morphisms, in the sense that we have an isomorphism T.functor ⋙ R.functor ≅ L.functor ⋙ B.functor. In this file, we obtain the lemma LocalizerMorphism.isRightDerivabilityStructure_of_isLocalizedEquivalence which shows that if both L and R are localized equivalences (with R.functor essentially surjective), then B is a right derivability structure when T is a right derivability structure, the 2-square above is Guitart exact (and W₂' respects isomorphisms).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.DerivabilityStructure.PointwiseRightDerived
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of pointwise right derived functors via derivability structures
nodes.description: In this file, we show how a right derivability structure can be used in order to construct (pointwise) right derived functors. Let Φ be a right derivability structure from W₁ : MorphismProperty C₁ to W₂ : MorphismProperty C₂. Let F : C₂ ⥤ H be a functor. Then, the lemma hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor_iff_of_isRightDerivabilityStructure says that F has a pointwise right derived functor with respect to W₂ if and only if Φ.functor ⋙ F has a pointwise right derived functor with respect to W₁.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Equivalence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Localization functors are preserved through equivalences
nodes.description: In Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean, the lemma Localization.of_equivalence_target already showed that the predicate of localized categories is unchanged when we replace the target category (i.e. the candidate localized category) by an equivalent category. In this file, we show the same for the source category (Localization.of_equivalence_source). More generally, Localization.of_equivalences shows that we may replace both the source and target categories by equivalent categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.FiniteProducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: The localized category has finite products
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for W : MorphismProperty C and that W is stable under finite products, then D has finite products, and L preserves finite products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.HasLocalization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphism properties equipped with a localized category
nodes.description: If C : Type u is a category (with [Category.{v} C]), and W : MorphismProperty C, then the constructed localized category W.Localization is in Type u (the objects are essentially the same as those of C), but the morphisms are in Type (max u v).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.HomEquiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bijections between morphisms in two localized categories
nodes.description: Given two localization functors L₁ : C ⥤ D₁ and L₂ : C ⥤ D₂ for the same class of morphisms W : MorphismProperty C, we define a bijection Localization.homEquiv W L₁ L₂ : (L₁.obj X ⟶ L₁.obj Y) ≃ (L₂.obj X ⟶ L₂.obj Y) between the types of morphisms in the two localized categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Linear
nodes.description: If L : C ⥤ D is an additive localization functor between preadditive categories, and C is R-linear, we show that D can also be equipped with an R-linear structure such that L is an R-linear functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.LocalizerMorphism
nodes.description: A morphism of localizers consists of a functor F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ between two categories equipped with morphism properties W₁ and W₂ such that F sends morphisms in W₁ to morphisms in W₂.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.LocallySmall
nodes.description: In this file, given W : MorphismProperty C and a universe w, we show that there exists a term in HasLocalization.{w} W if and only if there exists (or for all) localization functors L : C ⥤ D for W, the category D is locally w-small.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be a monoidal category equipped with a class of morphisms W which is compatible with the monoidal category structure: this means W is multiplicative and stable by left and right whiskerings (this is the type class W.IsMonoidal). Let L : C ⥤ D be a localization functor for W. In the file, we construct a monoidal category structure on D such that the localization functor is monoidal. The structure is actually defined on a type synonym LocalizedMonoidal L W ε.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.Braided
nodes.description: Let C be a monoidal category equipped with a class of morphisms W which is compatible with the monoidal category structure. The file Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.Basic constructs a monoidal structure on the localized on D such that the localization functor is monoidal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.Functor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Universal property of localized monoidal categories
nodes.description: This file proves that, given a monoidal localization functor L : C ⥤ D, and a functor F : D ⥤ E to a monoidal category, such that F lifts along L to a monoidal functor G, then F is monoidal. See CategoryTheory.Localization.Monoidal.functorMonoidalOfComp.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.OfQuotient
nodes.description: Let r : HomRel C be a relation on morphisms in a category C and W : MorphismProperty C. We assume that W is inverted by the quotient functor functor r : C ⥤ quotient r. If any relation r f₀ f₁ between morphisms f₀ : X ⟶ Y and f₁ : X ⟶ Y can be "explained" by the use of a homotopy involving a cylinder object (i.e.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Opposite
nodes.description: If a functor L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for W : MorphismProperty C, it is shown in this file that L.op : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ is also a localization functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Pi
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if for all j : J (with J finite), functors L j : C j ⥤ D j are localization functors with respect to a class of morphisms W j : MorphismProperty (C j), then the product functor Functor.pi L : (∀ j, C j) ⥤ ∀ j, D j is a localization functor for the product class of morphisms MorphismProperty.pi W. The proof proceeds by induction on the cardinal of J using the main result of the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Prod.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Preadditive
nodes.descriptionTitle: Localization of natural transformations to preadditive categories
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Localization.Preadditive.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Predicate
nodes.description: In this file, a predicate L.IsLocalization W is introduced for a functor L : C ⥤ D and W : MorphismProperty C: it expresses that L identifies D with the localized category of C with respect to W (up to equivalence).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Prod
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if functors L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁ and L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂ are localization functors for morphisms properties W₁ and W₂, then the product functor C₁ × C₂ ⥤ D₁ × D₂ is a localization functor for W₁.prod W₂ : MorphismProperty (C₁ × C₂), at least if both W₁ and W₂ contain identities. This main result is the instance Functor.IsLocalization.prod.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Quotient
nodes.description: Given a relation homRel : HomRel C on morphisms in a category C and W : MorphismProperty C, we introduce a property homRel.FactorsThroughLocalization W expressing that related morphisms are mapped to the same morphism in the localized category with respect to W. When W is compatible with homRel (i.e. there is a class of morphisms W' such that hW : W = W'.inverseImage (Quotient.functor homRel)), we show that LocalizerMorphism.ofEq hW : LocalizerMorphism W W' induces an equivalence on localized categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Resolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: Resolutions for a morphism of localizers
nodes.description: Given a morphism of localizers Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂ (i.e. W₁ and W₂ are morphism properties on categories C₁ and C₂, and we have a functor Φ.functor : C₁ ⥤ C₂ which sends morphisms in W₁ to morphisms in W₂), we introduce the notion of right resolutions of objects in C₂, for X₂ : C₂. A right resolution consists of an object X₁ : C₁ and a morphism w : X₂ ⟶ Φ.functor.obj X₁ that is in W₂. Then, the typeclass Φ.HasRightResolutions holds when any X₂ : C₂ has a right resolution.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallHom
nodes.description: Given a class of morphisms W : MorphismProperty C, and two objects X and Y, we introduce a type-class HasSmallLocalizedHom.{w} W X Y which expresses that in the localized category with respect to W, the type of morphisms from X to Y is w-small for a certain universe w. Under this assumption, we define SmallHom.{w} W X Y : Type w as the shrunk type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShiftedHom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Shrinking morphisms in localized categories equipped with shifts
nodes.description: If C is a category equipped with a shift by an additive monoid M, and W : MorphismProperty C is compatible with the shift, we define a type-class HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w} W X Y which says that all the types of morphisms from X⟦a⟧ to Y⟦b⟧ in the localized category are w-small for a certain universe.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.StructuredArrow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Induction principles for structured and costructured arrows
nodes.description: Assume that L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for W : MorphismProperty C. Given X : C and a predicate P on StructuredArrow (L.obj X) L, we obtain the lemma Localization.induction_structuredArrow which shows that P holds for all structured arrows if P holds for the identity map 𝟙 (L.obj X), if P is stable by post-composition with L.map f for any f and if P is stable by post-composition with the inverse of L.map w when W w.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Triangulated
nodes.description: If L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor for a class of morphisms W that is compatible with the triangulation on the category C and admits a left calculus of fractions, it is shown in this file that D can be equipped with a pretriangulated category structure, and that it is triangulated.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Localization.Trifunctor
nodes.description: In this file, in the context of the localization of categories, we extend the notion of lifting of functors to the case of trifunctors (see also the file Localization.Bifunctor for the case of bifunctors). The main result in this file is that we can localize "associator" isomorphisms (see the definition Localization.associator).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LocallyCartesianClosed.ChosenPullbacksAlong
nodes.description: ChosenPullbacksAlong f provides the data of a pullback functor Over X ⥤ Over Y as a right adjoint to Over.map f.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LocallyCartesianClosed.ExponentiableMorphism
nodes.description: We define an exponentiable morphism f : I ⟶ J to be a morphism with a functorial choice of pullbacks, given by ChosenPullbacksAlong f, together with a right adjoint to the pullback functor ChosenPullbacksAlong.pullback f : Over J ⥤ Over I. We call this right adjoint the pushforward functor along f.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LocallyCartesianClosed.Over
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cartesian monoidal structure on slices induced by chosen pullbacks
nodes.description: Over X for all objects X : C, induced by chosen pullbacks in the base category C. This is the computable analogue of the noncomputable instance CategoryTheory.Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LocallyCartesianClosed.Sections
nodes.descriptionTitle: The section functor as a right adjoint to the toOver functor
nodes.description: We show that in a cartesian monoidal category C, for any exponentiable object I, the functor toOver I : C ⥤ Over I mapping an object X to the projection snd : X ⊗ I ⟶ I in Over I has a right adjoint sections I : Over I ⥤ C whose object part is the object of sections of X over I.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.LocallyDirected
nodes.description: We say that a diagram of sets is "locally directed" if for any V, W ⊆ U in the diagram, V ∩ W is a union of elements in the diagram. Equivalently, for every x ∈ U in the diagram, the set of elements containing x is directed (and hence the name).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MarkovCategory.Basic
nodes.description: Copy-discard categories where deletion is natural for all morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MarkovCategory.Positive
nodes.description: Markov categories where deletion is natural for all morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Adjunction
nodes.description: We develop the basic relationship between adjunctions and (co)monads.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Algebra
nodes.description: This file defines Eilenberg-Moore (co)algebras for a (co)monad, and provides the category instance for them.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Basic
nodes.description: We construct the categories of monads and comonads, and their forgetful functors to endofunctors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Coequalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Special coequalizers associated to a monad
nodes.description: Associated to a monad T : C ⥤ C we have important coequalizer constructions: Any algebra is a coequalizer (in the category of algebras) of free algebras. Furthermore, this coequalizer is reflexive. In C, this cofork diagram is a split coequalizer (in particular, it is still a coequalizer). This split coequalizer is known as the Beck coequalizer (as it features heavily in Beck's monadicity theorem).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Comonadicity
nodes.description: We prove comonadicity theorems which can establish a given functor is comonadic. In particular, we show three versions of Beck's comonadicity theorem, and the coreflexive (crude) comonadicity theorem:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Equalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Special equalizers associated to a comonad
nodes.description: Associated to a comonad T : C ⥤ C we have important equalizer constructions: Any coalgebra is an equalizer (in the category of coalgebras) of cofree coalgebras. Furthermore, this equalizer is coreflexive. In C, this fork diagram is a split equalizer (in particular, it is still an equalizer). This split equalizer is known as the Beck equalizer (as it features heavily in Beck's comonadicity theorem).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.EquivMon
nodes.descriptionTitle: The equivalence between Monad C and Mon (C ⥤ C).
nodes.description: A monad "is just" a monoid in the category of endofunctors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Kleisli
nodes.description: This file defines the Kleisli category on a monad (T, η_ T, μ_ T) as well as the co-Kleisli category on a comonad (U, ε_ U, δ_ U). It also defines the Kleisli adjunction which gives rise to the monad (T, η_ T, μ_ T) as well as the co-Kleisli adjunction which gives rise to the comonad (U, ε_ U, δ_ U).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits and colimits in the category of (co)algebras
nodes.description: This file shows that the forgetful functor forget T : Algebra T ⥤ C for a monad T : C ⥤ C creates limits and creates any colimits which T preserves. This is used to show that Algebra T has any limits which C has, and any colimits which C has and T preserves. This is generalised to the case of a monadic functor D ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Monadicity
nodes.description: We prove monadicity theorems which can establish a given functor is monadic. In particular, we show three versions of Beck's monadicity theorem, and the reflexive (crude) monadicity theorem:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Products
nodes.description: The functor Y ↦ X ⨿ Y forms a monad, whose category of monads is equivalent to the under category of X. Similarly, Y ↦ X ⨯ Y forms a comonad, whose category of coalgebras is equivalent to the over category of X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monad.Types
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convert from Monad (i.e. Lean's Type-based monads) to CategoryTheory.Monad
nodes.description: This allows us to use these monads in category theory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Action.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Actions from a monoidal category on a category
nodes.description: Given a monoidal category C, and a category D, we define a left action of C on D as the data of an object c ⊙ₗ d of D for every c : C and d : D, as well as the data required to turn - ⊙ₗ - into a bifunctor, along with structure natural isomorphisms (- ⊗ -) ⊙ₗ - ≅ - ⊙ₗ - ⊙ₗ - and 𝟙_ C ⊙ₗ - ≅ -, subject to coherence conditions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Action.End
nodes.descriptionTitle: Actions as monoidal functors to endofunctor categories
nodes.description: In this file, we show that given a right action of a monoidal category C on a category D, the curried action functor C ⥤ D ⥤ D is monoidal. Conversely, given a monoidal functor C ⥤ D ⥤ D, we can define a right action of C on D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Action.LinearFunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors that are linear with respect to an action
nodes.description: Given a monoidal category C acting on the left or on the right on categories D and D', we introduce the following typeclasses on functors F : D ⥤ D' to express compatibility of F with the action of C: μₗ : c ⊙ₗ F.obj d ⟶ F.obj (c ⊙ₗ d). μᵣ : F.obj d ⊙ᵣ c ⟶ F.obj (d ⊙ᵣ c). δₗ : F.obj (c ⊙ₗ d) ⟶ c ⊙ₗ F.obj d. δᵣ : F.obj (d ⊙ᵣ c) ⟶ F.obj d ⊙ᵣ c. an F.OplaxLeftLinear C structure, and that they are compatible, i.e. δₗ F is a left and right inverse to μₗ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Action.Opposites
nodes.descriptionTitle: Actions from the monoidal opposite of a category.
nodes.description: In this file, given a monoidal category C and a category D, we construct a left C-action on D out of the data of a right Cᴹᵒᵖ-action on D. We also construct a right C-action on D from the data of a left Cᴹᵒᵖ-action on D. Conversely, given left/right C-actions on D, we construct a Cᴹᵒᵖ action with the conjugate variance.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Arrow
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monoidal structure on the arrow category of a cartesian closed category.
nodes.description: If C is a braided, cartesian closed category with pushouts and an initial object, then Arrow C has a symmetric monoidal category structure given by the pushout-product (the Leibniz construction given by the tensor product on C).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Bimod
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of bimodule objects over a pair of monoid objects.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Bimod.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Bimon_
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of bimonoids in a braided monoidal category.
nodes.description: We define bimonoids in a braided monoidal category C as comonoid objects in the category of monoid objects in C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Basic
nodes.description: The basic definitions of braided monoidal categories, and symmetric monoidal categories, as well as braided functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Multifunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing braided categories from natural transformations between multifunctors
nodes.description: This file provides an alternative constructor for braided categories, given a braiding β : -₁ ⊗ -₂ ≅ -₂ ⊗ -₁ as a natural isomorphism between bifunctors. The hexagon identities are phrased as equalities of natural transformations between trifunctors (-₁ ⊗ -₂) ⊗ -₃ ⟶ -₂ ⊗ (-₃ ⊗ -₁) and -₁ ⊗ (-₂ ⊗ -₃) ⟶ (-₃ ⊗ -₁) ⊗ -₂.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: If C is braided, so is Cᵒᵖ.
nodes.description: Todo: we should also do Cᵐᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Reflection
nodes.description: Let D be a symmetric monoidal closed category and let C be a reflective subcategory. Day's reflection theorem proves the equivalence of four conditions, which are all of the form that a map obtained by acting on the unit of the reflective adjunction, with the internal hom and tensor functors, is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Transport
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transport a symmetric monoidal structure along an equivalence of categories
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Braided.Transport.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Basic
nodes.description: We introduce a class, CartesianMonoidalCategory, which bundles explicit choices for a terminal object and binary products in a category C. This is primarily useful for categories which have finite products with good definitional properties, such as the category of types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Cat
nodes.description: This file proves that the Cartesian product of a pair of categories agrees with the product in Cat, and provides the associated CartesianMonoidalCategory instance.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.CommGrp_
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.CommGrp_.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.CommMon_
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.CommMon_.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Comon_
nodes.descriptionTitle: Comonoid objects in a Cartesian monoidal category.
nodes.description: The category of comonoid objects in a Cartesian monoidal category is equivalent to the category itself, via the forgetful functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.FunctorCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functor categories have chosen finite products
nodes.description: If C is a category with chosen finite products, then so is J ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Grp
nodes.description: We show that group objects are exactly those whose yoneda presheaf is a presheaf of groups, by constructing the yoneda embedding Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{v} and showing that it is fully faithful and its (essential) image is the representable functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.GrpLimits
nodes.description: We show that Grp C has limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Grp_
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.InfSemilattice
nodes.descriptionTitle: The preorder category of a meet-semilattice with a greatest element is Cartesian monoidal
nodes.description: The preorder category of a meet-semilattice C with a greatest element is Cartesian monoidal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Module objects in cartesian monoidal categories
nodes.description: In this file we study module objects in a cartesian monoidal category C action on itself by ⊗.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mod_
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mon
nodes.description: We show that monoid objects in Cartesian monoidal categories are exactly those whose yoneda presheaf is a presheaf of monoids, by constructing the yoneda embedding Mon C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ MonCat.{v} and showing that it is fully faithful and its (essential) image is the representable functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mon_
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Normal
nodes.description: In this file we define normal subgroups of group objects in a cartesian monoidal category as a predicate on morphisms. A morphism φ : H ⟶ G of group objects is normal if it is mono, a monoid morphism and the conjugation map (g, h) ↦ g h g⁻¹ factors through φ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Over
nodes.description: We provide a CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X) instance via pullbacks, and provide simp lemmas for the induced MonoidalCategory (Over X) instance.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Ring
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Ring.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.ShrinkYoneda
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Yoneda embedding for monoid objects for locally small categories
nodes.description: Let C be a locally w-small category. We define the Yoneda embedding shrinkYonedaMon : Mon C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ MonCat.{w} w and its Grp analogue.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Category
nodes.description: A monoidal category is a category equipped with a tensor product, unitors, and an associator. In the definition, we provide the tensor product as a pair of functions

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Center
nodes.descriptionTitle: Half braidings and the Drinfeld center of a monoidal category
nodes.description: We define Center C to be pairs ⟨X, b⟩, where X : C and b is a half-braiding on X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Basic
nodes.description: Define (right) closed objects and (right) closed monoidal categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Braided
nodes.description: Interactions between monoidal closed and braided category structures.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Cartesian
nodes.description: A cartesian closed category is a category with CartesianMonoidalCategory and MonoidalClosed instances. There used to be a separate definition CartesianClosed, with its own API, but over time this ended up as a duplicate of the former. Now, CartesianClosed and the surrounding API has been deprecated, and the API for MonoidalClosed should be used instead. This file now contains a few basic constructions for cartesian closed categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Enrichment
nodes.descriptionTitle: A closed monoidal category is enriched in itself
nodes.description: From the data of a closed monoidal category C, we define a C-category structure for C. where the hom-object is given by the internal hom (coming from the closed structure).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Functor
nodes.description: Define the exponential comparison morphisms for a functor which preserves binary products, and use them to define a Cartesian closed functor: one which (naturally) preserves exponentials.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.FunctorCategory.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be a monoidal closed category. Let J be a category. In this file, we obtain that the category J ⥤ C is monoidal closed if C has suitable limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.FunctorCategory.Complete
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors into a complete monoidal closed category form a monoidal closed category.
nodes.description: TODO (in progress by Joël Riou): make a more explicit construction of the internal hom in functor categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.FunctorCategory.Groupoid
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors from a groupoid into a monoidal closed category form a monoidal closed category.
nodes.description: (Using the pointwise monoidal structure on the functor category.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.FunctorToTypes
nodes.description: Show that C ⥤ Type max w v u is monoidal closed for C a category in Type u with morphisms in Type v, and w an arbitrary universe.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Ideal
nodes.description: An exponential ideal of a Cartesian closed category C is a subcategory D ⊆ C such that for any B : D and A : C, the exponential A ⟹ B is in D: resembling ring-theoretic ideals. We define the notion here for inclusion functors i : D ⥤ C rather than explicit subcategories to preserve the principle of equivalence.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.InternalCurrying
nodes.descriptionTitle: The currying-uncurrying isomorphism between internal homs of a closed monoidal category
nodes.description: For a closed monoidal category C, we construct the isomorphism of internal hom objects C(x ⊗ y, z) ≅ C(y, C(x, z)) for any triple of objects x y z : C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Transport
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transporting a closed monoidal structure along an equivalence of categories
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Transport.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Types
nodes.description: Show that Type u₁ is Cartesian closed, and C ⥤ Type u₁ is Cartesian closed for C a small category in Type u₁. Note this implies that the category of presheaves on a small category C is Cartesian closed.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Closed.Zero
nodes.descriptionTitle: A Cartesian closed category with zero object is trivial
nodes.description: A Cartesian closed category with zero object is trivial: it is equivalent to the category with one object and one morphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CoherenceLemmas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas which are consequences of monoidal coherence
nodes.description: These lemmas are all proved by coherence.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommComon_
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of commutative comonoids in a braided monoidal category.
nodes.description: We define the category of commutative comonoid objects in a braided monoidal category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommGrp_
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of commutative groups in a Cartesian monoidal category
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommGrp_.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommMon_
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of commutative monoids in a braided monoidal category.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommMon_.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Comon_
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of comonoids in a monoidal category.
nodes.description: We define comonoids in a monoidal category C, and show that they are equivalently monoid objects in the opposite category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Conv
nodes.description: When M : Comon C and N : Mon C, the morphisms M.X ⟶ N.X form a monoid (in Type).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.DayConvolution
nodes.description: Given functors F G : C ⥤ V between two monoidal categories, this file defines a typeclass DayConvolution on functors F G that contains a functor F ⊛ G, as well as the required data to exhibit F ⊛ G as a pointwise left Kan extension of F ⊠ G (see Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/ExternalProduct/Basic.lean for the definition) along the tensor product of C. Such a functor is called a Day convolution of F and G, and although we do not show it yet, this operation defines a monoidal structure on C ⥤ V.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.DayConvolution.Braided
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if C is a braided monoidal category and V also a braided monoidal category, then the Day convolution monoidal structure on C ⥤ V is also braided monoidal. We prove it by constructing an explicit braiding isomorphism whenever sufficient Day convolutions exist, and we prove that it satisfies the forward and reverse hexagon identities.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.DayConvolution.Closed
nodes.description: Given a category V that is monoidal closed, a category C that is monoidal, a functor C ⥤ V, and given the data of suitable day convolutions and suitable ends of profunctors c c₁ c₂ ↦ ihom (F c₁) (·.obj (c₂ ⊗ c)), we prove that the data of the units of the left Kan extensions that define day convolutions and the data of the canonical morphisms to the aforementioned ends can be organised as data that exhibit F as monoidal closed in C ⥤ V for the Day convolution monoidal structure.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.DayConvolution.DayFunctor
nodes.description: In this file, given a monoidal category C and a monoidal category V, we define a basic type synonym DayFunctor C V (denoted C ⊛⥤ D) for the category C ⥤ V and endow it with the monoidal structure coming from Day convolution. Such a setup is necessary as by default, the MonoidalCategory instance on C ⥤ V is the "pointwise" one, where the tensor product of F and G is the functor x ↦ F.obj x ⊗ G.obj x.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Discrete
nodes.description: The discrete category on a monoid is a monoidal category. Multiplicative morphisms induce monoidal functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.End
nodes.description: We give the monoidal category structure on C ⥤ C, and show that when C itself is monoidal, it embeds via a monoidal functor into C ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.ExternalProduct.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: External product of diagrams in a monoidal category
nodes.description: In a monoidal category C, given a pair of diagrams K₁ : J₁ ⥤ C and K₂ : J₂ ⥤ C, we introduce the external product K₁ ⊠ K₂ : J₁ × J₂ ⥤ C as the bifunctor (j₁, j₂) ↦ K₁ j₁ ⊗ K₂ j₂. The notation - ⊠ - is scoped to MonoidalCategory.ExternalProduct.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.ExternalProduct.KanExtension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of pointwise left Kan extensions by external products
nodes.description: We prove that if a functor H' : D' ⥤ V is a pointwise left Kan extension of H : D ⥤ V along L : D ⥤ D', and if K : E ⥤ V is any functor such that for any e : E, the functor tensorRight (K.obj e) commutes with colimits of shape CostructuredArrow L d, then the functor H' ⊠ K is a pointwise left Kan extension of H ⊠ K along L.prod (𝟭 E).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Free.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The free monoidal category over a type
nodes.description: Given a type C, the free monoidal category over C has as objects formal expressions built from (formal) tensor products of terms of C and a formal unit. Its morphisms are compositions and tensor products of identities, unitors and associators.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Free.Coherence
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the monoidal coherence theorem, stated in the following form: the free monoidal category over any type C is thin.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Limits.Cokernels
nodes.description: Let c₁ and c₂ be cokernel coforks for morphisms f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁ and f₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂ in a monoidal preadditive category. We define a cokernel cofork for (X₁ ⊗ Y₂) ⨿ (Y₁ ⊗ X₂) ⟶ Y₁ ⊗ Y₂ with point c₁.pt ⊗ c₂.pt, and show that it is colimit if c₁ and c₂ are colimit, and the cokernels of f₁ and f₂ are preserved by suitable tensor products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Mon
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of monoids in a monoidal category.
nodes.description: We define monoids in a monoidal category C and show that the category of monoids is equivalent to the category of lax monoidal functors from the unit monoidal category to C. We also show that if C is braided, then the category of monoids is naturally monoidal. We use the to_additive attribute in order to generate a parallel API for additive monoids.

nodes.description: This file provides alternative constructors for (op/lax) monoidal functors, given tensorators μ : F - ⊗ F - ⟶ F (- ⊗ -) / δ : F (- ⊗ -) ⟶ F - ⊗ F - as natural transformations between bifunctors. The associativity conditions are phrased as equalities of natural transformations between trifunctors (F - ⊗ F -) ⊗ F - ⟶ F (- ⊗ (- ⊗ -)) / F ((- ⊗ -) ⊗ -) ⟶ F - ⊗ (F - ⊗ F -), and the unitality conditions are phrased as equalities of natural transformation between functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Monoidal.NaturalTransformation
nodes.description: Natural transformations between (lax) monoidal functors must satisfy an additional compatibility relation with the tensorators: F.μ X Y ≫ app (X ⊗ Y) = (app X ⊗ app Y) ≫ G.μ X Y.

nodes.description: If C is a cartesian monoidal category and X : C, we introduce a typeclass RingObj X which says that X is a ring object: it has a commutative additive group structure and a multiplicative monoid structure that is distributive over the additive structure. We also introduce a typeclass CommRingObj X which further requires that the multiplicative law is commutative.

nodes.description: Given functors L : A ⥤ T and R : B ⥤ T and morphism properties P, Q and W on T, A and B respectively, we define the subcategory P.Comma L R Q W of Comma L R where

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.CommaSites
nodes.description: We provide some API for proving properties of P.Over ⊤ X in relation to precoverages. Consider a precoverage K on C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Composition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compatibilities of properties of morphisms with respect to composition
nodes.description: Given P : MorphismProperty C, we define the predicate P.IsStableUnderComposition which means that P f → P g → P (f ≫ g). We also introduce the type classes W.ContainsIdentities, W.IsMultiplicative, and W.HasTwoOutOfThreeProperty.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Concrete
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphism properties defined in concrete categories
nodes.description: In this file, we define the class of morphisms MorphismProperty.injective, MorphismProperty.surjective, MorphismProperty.bijective in concrete categories, and show that it is stable under composition and respects isomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Descent
nodes.description: Given morphism properties P and Q we say that P descends along Q (P.DescendsAlong Q), if whenever Q holds for X ⟶ Z, P holds for X ×[Z] Y ⟶ X implies P holds for Y ⟶ Z. Dually, we define P.CodescendsAlong Q.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Factorization
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce a type-class HasFactorization W₁ W₂, which, given two classes of morphisms W₁ and W₂ in a category C, asserts that any morphism in C can be factored as a morphism in W₁ followed by a morphism in W₂. The data of such factorizations can be packaged in the type FactorizationData W₁ W₂.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.FunctorCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stability properties of morphism properties on functor categories
nodes.description: Given W : MorphismProperty C and a category J, we study the stability properties of W.functorCategory J : MorphismProperty (J ⥤ C).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.HasCardinalLT
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of morphisms that are bounded by a cardinal
nodes.description: Given P : MorphismProperty C and κ : Cardinal, we introduce a predicate P.HasCardinalLT κ saying that the cardinality of P.toSet is < κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Ind
nodes.description: Given a morphism property P, we define a morphism property ind P that is satisfied for f : X ⟶ Y if Y is a filtered colimit of Yᵢ and fᵢ : X ⟶ Yᵢ satisfy P.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsInvertedBy
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphism properties that are inverted by a functor
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the predicate P.IsInvertedBy F which expresses that the morphisms satisfying P : MorphismProperty C are mapped to isomorphisms by a functor F : C ⥤ D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.IsSmall
nodes.description: A class of morphisms W : MorphismProperty C is w-small if the corresponding set in Set (Arrow C) is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.LiftingProperty
nodes.description: Given a morphism property T, we define the left and right lifting property with respect to T.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relation of morphism properties with limits
nodes.description: The following predicates are introduces for morphism properties P: squares, the left map satisfies P if the right map satisfies it. squares, the right map satisfies P if the left map satisfies it.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Local
nodes.description: In this file we define locality conditions on morphism properties in a category. Let K be a precoverage in a category C and P be a morphism property on C that respects isomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.OfObjectProperty
nodes.description: Given two object properties P and Q, we introduce a morphism property ofObjectProperty P Q, given by all morphisms whose source satisfies P and target satisfies Q.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjunction of pushforward and pullback in P.Over Q X

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Quotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: Classes of morphisms induced on quotient categories
nodes.description: Let W : MorphismProperty C and homRel : HomRel C. We assume that homRel is stable under pre- and postcomposition. We introduce a property W.HasQuotient homRel expressing that W induces a property of morphisms on the quotient category, i.e. W f ↔ W g when homRel f g holds. We denote W.quotient homRel : MorphismProperty (Quotient homRel) the induced property of morphisms: a morphism in C satisfies W iff (Quotient.functor homRel).map f does.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Representable
nodes.description: In this file we define and develop basic results about relatively representable morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Retract
nodes.description: Given P : MorphismProperty C, we introduce a typeclass P.IsStableUnderRetracts which is the property that P is stable under retracts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.RetractArgument
nodes.description: Let W₁ and W₂ be classes of morphisms in a category C such that any morphism can be factored as a morphism in W₁ followed by a morphism in W₂ (this is HasFactorization W₁ W₂). If W₁ has the left lifting property with respect to W₂ (i.e. W₁ ≤ W₂.llp, or equivalently W₂ ≤ W₁.rlp), then W₂.llp = W₁ if W₁ is stable under retracts, and W₁.rlp = W₂ if W₂ is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.TransfiniteComposition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Classes of morphisms that are stable under transfinite composition
nodes.description: Given a well-ordered type J, W : MorphismProperty C and a morphism f : X ⟶ Y, we define a structure W.TransfiniteCompositionOfShape J f which expresses that f is a transfinite composition of shape J of morphisms in W. This structures extends CategoryTheory.TransfiniteCompositionOfShape which was defined in the file CategoryTheory.Limits.Shape.Preorder.TransfiniteCompositionOfShape.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.WeakFactorizationSystem
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the notion of weak factorization system, which is a property of two classes of morphisms W₁ and W₂ in a category C. The type class IsWeakFactorizationSystem W₁ W₂ asserts that W₁ is exactly W₂.llp, W₂ is exactly W₁.rlp, and any morphism in C can be factored a i ≫ p with W₁ i and W₂ p.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.NatIso

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.NatTrans

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Noetherian
nodes.description: An Artinian category is a category in which objects do not have infinite decreasing sequences of subobjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects in a category
nodes.description: Given a category C, we introduce an abbreviation ObjectProperty C for predicates C → Prop.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ClosedUnderIsomorphisms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects which are closed under isomorphisms
nodes.description: Given a category C and P : ObjectProperty C (i.e. P : C → Prop), this file introduces the type class P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ClosureShift
nodes.description: In this file, we collect facts relating being stable under shifts with closure properties of object properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ColimitsCardinalClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Closure of a property of objects under colimits of bounded cardinality
nodes.description: In this file, given P : ObjectProperty C and κ : Cardinal.{w}, we introduce the closure P.colimitsCardinalClosure κ of P under colimits of shapes given by categories J such that Arrow J is of cardinality < κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ColimitsClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Closure of a property of objects under colimits of certain shapes
nodes.description: In this file, given a property P of objects in a category C and family of categories J : α → Type _, we introduce the closure P.colimitsClosure J of P under colimits of shapes J a for all a : α, and under certain smallness assumptions, we show that it is essentially small.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ColimitsOfShape
nodes.descriptionTitle: Objects that are colimits of objects satisfying a certain property
nodes.description: Given a property of objects P : ObjectProperty C and a category J, we introduce two properties of objects P.strictColimitsOfShape J and P.colimitsOfShape J. The former contains exactly the objects of the form colimit F for any functor F : J ⥤ C that has a colimit and such that F.obj j satisfies P for any j, while the latter contains all the objects that are isomorphic to these "chosen" objects colimit F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.CompleteLattice
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.CompleteLattice.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ContainsZero
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects which hold for a zero object
nodes.description: Given a category C and P : ObjectProperty C, we define a type class P.ContainsZero expressing that there exists a zero object for which P holds. (We do not require that P holds for all zero objects, as in some applications (e.g. triangulated categories), P may not necessarily be closed under isomorphisms.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects that are closed under subobjects and quotients
nodes.description: Given a category C and P : ObjectProperty C, we define type classes P.IsClosedUnderSubobjects and P.IsClosedUnderQuotients expressing that P is closed under subobjects (resp. quotients).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Equivalence
nodes.description: The inclusion functor P.FullSubcategory ⥤ Q.FullSubcategory induced by an inequality P ≤ Q in ObjectProperty C is an equivalence iff Q ≤ P.isoClosure.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Extensions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects that are closed under extensions
nodes.description: Given a category C and P : ObjectProperty C, we define a type class P.IsClosedUnderExtensions expressing that the property is closed under extensions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FiniteProducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects that are stable under finite products
nodes.description: We introduce typeclasses IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts and IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts expressing that P : ObjectProperty C is closed under binary products or finite products. We introduce a constructor for P.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts assuming P.IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts, P.IsClosedUnderLimitsOfShape (Discrete.{0} PEmpty) and that C has finite products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: The full subcategory associated to a property of objects
nodes.description: Given a category C and P : ObjectProperty C, we define a category structure on the type P.FullSubcategory of objects in C satisfying P.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FunctorCategory.PreservesLimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of limits, as a property of objects in the functor category
nodes.description: We make the typeclass PreservesLimitsOfShape K (resp. PreservesFiniteLimits) a property of objects in the functor category J ⥤ C, and show that it is stable under colimits of shape K' when they commute to limits of shape K (resp. to finite limits).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.HasCardinalLT
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects that are bounded by a cardinal
nodes.description: Given P : ObjectProperty C and κ : Cardinal, we introduce a predicate P.HasCardinalLT κ saying that the cardinality of Subtype P is < κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Ind
nodes.description: Given an object property P, we define an object property ind P that is satisfied for X if X is a filtered colimit of Xᵢ and Xᵢ satisfies P.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.InheritedFromHom
nodes.description: In this file we define the predicates InheritedFromSource and InheritedFromTarget for an object property P along a morphism property Q. P is inherited from the source (resp. target) along Q if for every morphism f : X ⟶ Y with Q f, P X implies P Y (resp. P Y implies P X).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Kernels
nodes.description: Given a morphism property W on a category, we introduce two object properties kernels W and cokernels W, consisting of all (co)kernels of morphisms satisfying W.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.LimitsClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Closure of a property of objects under limits of certain shapes
nodes.description: In this file, given a property P of objects in a category C and a family of categories J : α → Type _, we introduce the closure P.limitsClosure J of P under limits of shapes J a for all a : α, and under certain smallness assumptions, we show that it is essentially small.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.LimitsOfShape
nodes.descriptionTitle: Objects that are limits of objects satisfying a certain property
nodes.description: Given a property of objects P : ObjectProperty C and a category J, we introduce two properties of objects P.strictLimitsOfShape J and P.limitsOfShape J. The former contains exactly the objects of the form limit F for any functor F : J ⥤ C that has a limit and such that F.obj j satisfies P for any j, while the latter contains all the objects that are isomorphic to these "chosen" objects limit F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Local
nodes.descriptionTitle: Objects that are local with respect to a property of morphisms
nodes.description: Given W : MorphismProperty C, we define W.isLocal : ObjectProperty C which is the property of objects Z such that for any f : X ⟶ Y satisfying W, the precomposition with f gives a bijection (Y ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Z). (In the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Bousfield.lean, it is shown that this is part of a Galois connection, with "dual" construction ObjectProperty.isLocal : ObjectProperty C → MorphismProperty C.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite of a property of objects

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Orthogonal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Orthogonal of a property of objects
nodes.description: Let P be a property of objects in a category with zero morphisms. We define P.rightOrthogonal as the property of objects Y such that any map f : X ⟶ Y vanishes when P X holds. Similarly, we define P.leftOrthogonal as the property of objects X such that any map f : X ⟶ Y vanishes when P Y holds.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Retract
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of objects which are stable under retracts

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ShiftAdditive

nodes.description: In this file, we show that if C is a preadditive category equipped with a shift by an additive monoid A, and P : ObjectProperty C is stable under the shift, then the shift functors on the full subcategory associated to P are additive if the shift functors on C are.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.SiteLocal
nodes.description: In this file we define locality conditions on object properties in a category. Let K be a precoverage in a category C and P be an object property that is closed under isomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Small

nodes.description: In this file, given P : ObjectProperty C, we define ObjectProperty.Small.{w} P as an abbreviation for Small.{w} (Subtype P).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Opposites

nodes.description: We define star : C ⥤ Discrete PUnit sending everything to PUnit.star, show that any two functors to Discrete PUnit are naturally isomorphic, and construct the equivalence (Discrete PUnit ⥤ C) ≌ C.
