nodes.label: CategoryTheory.PathCategory.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of morphisms in a path category.
nodes.description: We provide a formulation of induction principles for morphisms in a path category in terms of MorphismProperty. This file is separate from Mathlib/CategoryTheory/PathCategory/Basic.lean in order to reduce transitive imports.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Pi.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Categories of indexed families of objects.
nodes.description: We define the pointwise category structure on indexed families of objects in a category (and also the dependent generalization).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Pi.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The pointwise monoidal structure on the product of families of monoidal categories
nodes.description: Given a family of monoidal categories C i, we define a monoidal structure on Π i, C i where the tensor product is defined pointwise.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.AdditiveFunctor
nodes.description: A functor between two preadditive categories is called additive provided that the induced map on hom types is a morphism of abelian groups.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Basic
nodes.description: A preadditive category is a category in which X ⟶ Y is an abelian group in such a way that composition of morphisms is linear in both variables.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Biproducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic facts about biproducts in preadditive categories.
nodes.description: In (or between) preadditive categories,

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.CommGrp_
nodes.descriptionTitle: Commutative group objects in additive categories.
nodes.description: We construct an inverse of the forgetful functor CommGrp C ⥤ C if C is an additive category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.EilenbergMoore
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preadditive structure on algebras over a monad
nodes.description: If C is a preadditive category and T is an additive monad on C then Algebra T is also preadditive. Dually, if U is an additive comonad on C then Coalgebra U is preadditive as well.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.EndoFunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preadditive structure on algebras over a monad
nodes.description: If C is a preadditive category and F is an additive endofunctor on C then Algebra F is also preadditive. Dually, the category Coalgebra F is also preadditive.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.FunctorCategory
nodes.description: If C and D are categories and D is preadditive, then C ⥤ D is also preadditive.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.HomOrthogonal
nodes.description: A family of objects in a category with zero morphisms is "hom orthogonal" if the only morphism between distinct objects is the zero morphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Indization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of ind-objects is preadditive
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Indization.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Injective.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Injective objects and categories with enough injectives
nodes.description: An object J is injective iff every morphism into J can be obtained by extending a monomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Injective.LiftingProperties
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterization of injective objects in terms of lifting properties
nodes.description: An object I is injective iff the morphism I ⟶ 0 has the right lifting property with respect to monomorphisms, injective_iff_rlp_monomorphisms_zero.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Injective.Preserves
nodes.description: We define a typeclass Functor.PreservesInjectiveObjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Injective.Resolution
nodes.description: An injective resolution I : InjectiveResolution Z of an object Z : C consists of an ℕ-indexed cochain complex I.cocomplex of injective objects, along with a quasi-isomorphism I.ι from the cochain complex consisting just of Z in degree zero to I.cocomplex.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.LeftExact
nodes.descriptionTitle: Left exactness of functors between preadditive categories
nodes.description: We show that a functor is left exact in the sense that it preserves finite limits, if it preserves kernels. The dual result holds for right exact functors and cokernels.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.LiftToFinset
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additional results about the liftToFinset construction
nodes.description: If f is a family of objects of C, then there is a canonical cocone whose cocone point is the coproduct of f and whose legs are given by the inclusions of the finite subcoproducts. If C is preadditive, then we can describe the legs of this cocone as finite sums of projections followed by inclusions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Mat
nodes.description: When C is a preadditive category, Mat_ C is the preadditive category whose objects are finite tuples of objects in C, and whose morphisms are matrices of morphisms from C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.OfBiproducts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing a semiadditive structure from binary biproducts
nodes.description: We show that any category with zero morphisms and binary biproducts is enriched over the category of commutative monoids.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: If C is preadditive, Cᵒᵖ has a natural preadditive structure.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Opposite.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective objects and categories with enough projectives
nodes.description: An object P is called projective if every morphism out of P factors through every epimorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective.Internal
nodes.description: This file defines internal projectivity of objects P in a category C as a class InternallyProjective P. This means that the functor taking internal homs out of P preserves epimorphisms. It also proves that a retract of an internally projective object is internally projective (see InternallyProjective.ofRetract).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective.LiftingProperties
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterization of projective objects in terms of lifting properties
nodes.description: An object P is projective iff the morphism 0 ⟶ P has the left lifting property with respect to epimorphisms, projective_iff_llp_epimorphisms_zero.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective.Preserves
nodes.description: We define a typeclass Functor.PreservesProjectiveObjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective.Resolution
nodes.description: A projective resolution P : ProjectiveResolution Z of an object Z : C consists of an ℕ-indexed chain complex P.complex of projective objects, along with a quasi-isomorphism P.π from C to the chain complex consisting just of Z in degree zero.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Schur
nodes.description: We first prove the part of Schur's Lemma that holds in any preadditive category with kernels, that any nonzero morphism between simple objects is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.SingleObj
nodes.descriptionTitle: SingleObj α is preadditive when α is a ring.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Preadditive.SingleObj.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Transfer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pulling back a preadditive structure along a fully faithful functor
nodes.description: A preadditive structure on a category D transfers to a preadditive structure on C for a given fully faithful functor F : C ⥤ D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Yoneda.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Yoneda embedding for preadditive categories
nodes.description: The Yoneda embedding for preadditive categories sends an object Y to the presheaf sending an object X to the group of morphisms X ⟶ Y. At each point, we get an additional End Y-module structure.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Yoneda.Injective
nodes.descriptionTitle: An object is injective iff the preadditive yoneda functor on it preserves epimorphisms.
nodes.description: An object is injective iff the preadditive yoneda functor on it preserves epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Yoneda.Limits
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Yoneda embedding for preadditive categories preserves limits
nodes.description: The Yoneda embedding for preadditive categories preserves limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Yoneda.Projective
nodes.descriptionTitle: An object is projective iff the preadditive coyoneda functor on it preserves epimorphisms.
nodes.description: An object is projective iff the preadditive coyoneda functor on it preserves epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Adjunction
nodes.description: If adj : F ⊣ G and G is κ-accessible for a regular cardinal κ, then F preserves κ-presentable objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Basic
nodes.description: A functor F : C ⥤ D is κ-accessible (Functor.IsCardinalAccessible) if it commutes with colimits of shape J where J is any κ-filtered category (that is essentially small relative to the universe w such that κ : Cardinal.{w}.). We also introduce another typeclass Functor.IsAccessible saying that there exists a regular cardinal κ such that Functor.IsCardinalAccessible.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.CardinalFilteredPresentation
nodes.description: Let C be a category, a regular cardinal κ and P : ObjectProperty C. We define a predicate P.IsCardinalFilteredGenerator κ saying that P consists of κ-presentable objects and that any object in C is a κ-filtered colimit of objects satisfying P. We show that if this condition is satisfied, then P is a strong generator (see IsCardinalFilteredGenerator.isStrongGenerator). Moreover, if C is locally small, we show that any object in C is presentable (see IsCardinalFilteredGenerator.presentable).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.ColimitPresentation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Presentation of a colimit of objects equipped with a presentation
nodes.description: colimit presentations of the components, this is the colimit presentation over the sigma type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Dense
nodes.descriptionTitle: κ-presentable objects form a dense subcategory
nodes.description: In a κ-accessible category C, the inclusion of the full subcategory of κ-presentable objects is a dense functor. This expresses canonically any object X : C as a colimit of κ-presentable objects, and we show that this is a κ-filtered colimit.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Directed
nodes.description: In this file, we formalize the proof by Deligne (SGA 4 I 8.1.6) that for any (small) filtered category J, there exists a final functor F : α ⥤ J where α is a directed partially ordered set (IsFiltered.exists_directed). The construction applies more generally to κ-filtered categories and κ-directed posets (IsCardinalFiltered.exists_cardinal_directed).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.EssentiallyLarge
nodes.description: If a category C satisfies HasCardinalFilteredGenerator C κ for κ : Cardinal.{w} (e.g. it is locally κ-presentable or κ-accessible), then C is equivalent to a w-large category, i.e. a category whose type of objects is in Type (w + 1) and whose types of morphisms are in Type w.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Finite
nodes.description: We define finitely presentable objects as a synonym for ℵ₀-presentable objects, and link this definition with the preservation of filtered colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.IsCardinalFiltered
nodes.description: If κ is a regular cardinal, we introduce the notion of κ-filtered category J: it means that any functor A ⥤ J from a small category such that Arrow A is of cardinality < κ admits a cocone. This generalizes the notion of filtered category. Indeed, we obtain the equivalence IsCardinalFiltered J ℵ₀ ↔ IsFiltered J. The API is mostly parallel to that of filtered categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Limits
nodes.description: In this file, we show that κ-accessible functors (to the category of types) are stable under limits indexed by a category K such that HasCardinalLT (Arrow K) κ. In particular, κ-presentable objects are stable by colimits indexed by a category K such that HasCardinalLT (Arrow K) κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.LocallyPresentable
nodes.description: In this file, we define the notion of locally presentable and accessible categories. We first define these notions for a category C relative to a fixed regular cardinal κ (typeclasses IsCardinalLocallyPresentable C κ and IsCardinalAccessibleCategory C κ). The existence of such a regular cardinal κ is asserted in the typeclasses IsLocallyPresentable and IsAccessibleCategory. We show that in a locally presentable or accessible category, any object is presentable.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.OrthogonalReflection
nodes.description: Given W : MorphismProperty C (which should be small) and assuming the existence of certain colimits in C, we construct a morphism toSucc W Z : Z ⟶ succ W Z for any Z : C. This morphism belongs to W.isLocal.isLocal and is an isomorphism iff Z belongs to W.isLocal (see the lemma isIso_toSucc_iff).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Presheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Categories of presheaves are locally presentable
nodes.description: If A is a locally κ-presentable category and C is a small category, we show that Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A is also locally κ-presentable, under the additional assumption that A has pullbacks (a condition which should be automatically satisfied (TODO)).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Retracts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Presentable objects are stable under retracts
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Presentable.Retracts.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.StrongGenerator
nodes.descriptionTitle: Locally presentable categories and strong generators
nodes.description: In this file, we show that a category is locally κ-presentable iff it is cocomplete and has a strong generator consisting of κ-presentable objects. This is theorem 1.20 in the book by Adámek and Rosický.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Presentable.Type
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if κ : Cardinal.{u} is a regular cardinal, then X : Type u is κ-presentable in the category of types iff HasCardinalLT X κ holds, i.e. the cardinal number of X is less than κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Products.Associator
nodes.descriptionTitle: The associator functor ((C × D) × E) ⥤ (C × (D × E)) and its inverse form an equivalence.
nodes.description: The associator functor ((C × D) × E) ⥤ (C × (D × E)) and its inverse form an equivalence.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Products.Basic
nodes.description: We define the category instance on C × D when C and D are categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Products.Bifunctor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about functors out of product categories.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Products.Bifunctor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Products.Unitor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The left/right unitor equivalences 1 × C ≌ C and C × 1 ≌ C.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Products.Unitor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Profunctor.Basic
nodes.description: A profunctor from a category C to a category D is a functor from C to a category of presheaves of sets on D. We define this as Profunctor.{w} C D := C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Quotient
nodes.description: Constructs the quotient of a category by an arbitrary family of relations on its hom-sets, by introducing a type synonym for the objects, and identifying homs as necessary.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Quotient.Linear
nodes.description: If r : HomRel C is a congruence on a preadditive category C which satisfies certain compatibilities, we have already defined a preadditive structure on Quotient r in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Quotient/Preadditive.lean such that functor r : C ⥤ Quotient r is an additive functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Quotient.LocallySmall
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Quotient.LocallySmall.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive
nodes.description: If an equivalence relation r : HomRel C on the morphisms of a preadditive category is compatible with the addition, then the quotient category Quotient r is also preadditive.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.RegularCategory.Basic
nodes.description: A regular category is a category with finite limits such that each kernel pair has a coequalizer and such that regular epimorphisms are stable under pullback.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.RepresentedBy
nodes.description: In this file we define the predicate IsRepresentedBy: A presheaf F is represented by X with universal element x : F.obj X if the natural transformation yoneda.obj X ⟶ F induced by x is an isomorphism.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Retract
nodes.description: Defines retracts of objects and morphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Adjunction
nodes.description: Given categories C and D that have shifts by an additive group A, functors F : C ⥤ D and G : C ⥤ D, an adjunction F ⊣ G and a CommShift structure on F, this file constructs a CommShift structure on G. We also do the construction in the other direction: given a CommShift structure on G, we construct a CommShift structure on G; we could do this using opposite categories, but the construction is simple enough that it is not really worth it.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Basic
nodes.description: A Shift on a category C indexed by a monoid A is nothing more than a monoidal functor from A to C ⥤ C. A typical example to keep in mind might be the category of complexes ⋯ → C_{n-1} → C_n → C_{n+1} → ⋯. It has a shift indexed by ℤ, where we assign to each n : ℤ the functor C ⥤ C that re-indexes the terms, so the degree i term of Shift n C would be the degree i+n-th term of C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.CommShift
nodes.description: Let C and D be two categories equipped with shifts by an additive monoid A. In this file, we define the notion of functor F : C ⥤ D which "commutes" with these shifts. The associated type class is [F.CommShift A]. The data consists of commutation isomorphisms F.commShiftIso a : shiftFunctor C a ⋙ F ≅ F ⋙ shiftFunctor D a for all a : A which satisfy a compatibility with the addition and the zero.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.CommShiftTwo
nodes.descriptionTitle: Commutation with shifts of functors in two variables
nodes.description: We introduce a typeclass Functor.CommShift₂Int for a bifunctor G : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ D (with D a preadditive category) as the two variable analogue of Functor.CommShift. We require that G commutes with the shifts in both variables and that the two ways to identify (G.obj (X₁⟦p⟧)).obj (X₂⟦q⟧) to ((G.obj X₁).obj X₂)⟦p + q⟧ differ by the sign (-1) ^ (p + q).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Induced
nodes.descriptionTitle: Shift induced from a category to another
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce a sufficient condition on a functor F : C ⥤ D so that a shift on C by a monoid A induces a shift on D. More precisely, when the functor (D ⥤ D) ⥤ C ⥤ D given by the precomposition with F is fully faithful, and that all the shift functors on C can be lifted to functors D ⥤ D (i.e. we have functors s a : D ⥤ D for all a : A, and isomorphisms F ⋙ s a ≅ shiftFunctor C a ⋙ F), then these functors s a are the shift functors of a term of type HasShift D A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.InducedShiftSequence
nodes.description: When G : C ⥤ A is a functor from a category equipped with a shift by a monoid M, we have defined in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Shift/ShiftSequence.lean a type class G.ShiftSequence M which provides functors G.shift a : C ⥤ A for all a : M, isomorphisms shiftFunctor C n ⋙ G.shift a ≅ G.shift a' when n + a = a', and isomorphisms G.isoShift a : shiftFunctor C a ⋙ G ≅ G.shift a for all a, all of which satisfy good coherence properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Linear
nodes.descriptionTitle: Localization of the linearity of the shift functors
nodes.description: If L : C ⥤ D is a localization functor with respect to W : MorphismProperty C and both C and D have been equipped with R-linear category structures such that L is R-linear and the shift functors on C are R-linear, then the shift functors on D are R-linear.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Localization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The shift induced on a localized category
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a shift by a monoid A. A morphism property W on C satisfies W.IsCompatibleWithShift A when for all a : A, a morphism f is in W iff f⟦a⟧' is. When this compatibility is satisfied, then the corresponding localized category can be equipped with a shift by A, and the localization functor is compatible with the shift.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The (naive) shift on the opposite category
nodes.description: If C is a category equipped with a shift by a monoid A, the opposite category can be equipped with a shift such that the shift functor by n is (shiftFunctor C n).op. This is the "naive" opposite shift, which we shall set on a category OppositeShift C A, which is a type synonym for Cᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Pullback
nodes.descriptionTitle: The pullback of a shift by a monoid morphism
nodes.description: Given a shift by a monoid B on a category C and a monoid morphism φ : A →+ B, we define a shift by A on a category PullbackShift C φ which is a type synonym for C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Quotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: The shift on a quotient category
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped a shift by a monoid A. If we have a relation on morphisms r : HomRel C that is compatible with the shift (i.e. if two morphisms f and g are related, then f⟦a⟧' and g⟦a⟧' are also related for all a : A), then the quotient category Quotient r is equipped with a shift.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.ShiftSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sequences of functors from a category equipped with a shift
nodes.description: Let F : C ⥤ A be a functor from a category C that is equipped with a shift by an additive monoid M. In this file, we define a typeclass F.ShiftSequence M which includes the data of a sequence of functors F.shift a : C ⥤ A for all a : A. For each a : A, we have an isomorphism F.isoShift a : shiftFunctor C a ⋙ F ≅ F.shift a which satisfies some coherence relations. This allows to state results (e.g. the long exact sequence of a homology functor (TODO)) using functors F.shift a rather than shiftFunctor C a ⋙ F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.ShiftedHom
nodes.description: Given a category C endowed with a shift by an additive monoid M and two objects X and Y in C, we consider the types ShiftedHom X Y m defined as X ⟶ Y⟦m⟧ for all m : M, and the composition on these shifted hom.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.ShiftedHomOpposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Shifted morphisms in the opposite category
nodes.description: If C is a category equipped with a shift by ℤ, X and Y are objects of C, and n : ℤ, we define a bijection ShiftedHom.opEquiv : ShiftedHom X Y n ≃ ShiftedHom (Opposite.op Y) (Opposite.op X) n. We also introduce ShiftedHom.opEquiv' which produces a bijection ShiftedHom X Y a' ≃ (Opposite.op (Y⟦a⟧) ⟶ (Opposite.op X)⟦n⟧) when n + a = a'.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.SingleFunctors
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors from a category to a category with a shift
nodes.description: Given a category C, and a category D equipped with a shift by a monoid A, we define a structure SingleFunctors C D A which contains the data of functors functor a : C ⥤ D for all a : A and isomorphisms shiftIso n a a' h : functor a' ⋙ shiftFunctor D n ≅ functor a whenever n + a = a'. These isomorphisms should satisfy certain compatibilities with respect to the shift on D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.SingleFunctorsLift
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lift of a "single functor" to a full subcategory
nodes.description: Let C, D and E be categories. Let A be an additive monoid. Assume that D and E have shifts by A and that we have a fully faithful functor G : D ⥤ A which commutes with shifts. Given F : SingleFunctors C E A, and a family of functors Φ a : C ⥤ D with isomorphisms Φ a ⋙ G ≅ F.functor a for all a : A, we lift F in SingleFunctor C D A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Shift.Twist
nodes.description: Given a category C equipped with a shift by a monoid A, we introduce a structure t : TwistShiftData C A which consists of a collection of invertible elements in the center of the category C (typically, C will be preadditive, and these will be signs), which allow to introduce a type synonym category t.Category with identical shift functors as C but where the isomorphisms shiftFunctorAdd have been modified.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.ShrinkYoneda
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Yoneda functor for locally small categories
nodes.description: Let C be a locally w-small category. We define the Yoneda embedding shrinkYoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w. (See the file CategoryTheory.Yoneda for the other variants yoneda and uliftYoneda.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sigma.Basic
nodes.description: We define the category structure on a sigma-type (disjoint union) of categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Simple
nodes.description: We define simple objects in any category with zero morphisms. A simple object is an object Y such that any monomorphism f : X ⟶ Y is either an isomorphism or zero (but not both).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SingleObj
nodes.description: Single object category with a given monoid of endomorphisms. It is defined to facilitate transferring some definitions and lemmas (e.g., conjugacy etc.) from category theory to monoids and groups.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Abelian
nodes.description: Let C, D be categories and J be a Grothendieck topology on C, when D is abelian and sheafification is possible in C, Sheaf J D is abelian as well (sheafIsAbelian).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Adjunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: In this file, we show that an adjunction G ⊣ F induces an adjunction between
nodes.description: In this file, we show that an adjunction G ⊣ F induces an adjunction between categories of sheaves. We also show that G preserves sheafification.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Canonical
nodes.descriptionTitle: The canonical topology on a category
nodes.description: We define the finest (largest) Grothendieck topology for which a given presheaf P is a sheaf. This is well defined since if P is a sheaf for a topology J, then it is a sheaf for any coarser (smaller) topology. Nonetheless we define the topology explicitly by specifying its sieves: A sieve S on X is covering for finestTopologySingle P iff for any f : Y ⟶ X, P satisfies the sheaf axiom for S.pullback f.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CartesianClosed
nodes.description: ...if the underlying presheaf category is Cartesian closed, the target category has (chosen) finite products, and there exists a sheafification functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CartesianMonoidal
nodes.description: In this file, we put a CartesianMonoidalCategory instance on A-valued sheaves for a GrothendieckTopology whenever A has a CartesianMonoidalCategory instance.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Closed
nodes.description: A natural closure operator on sieves is a closure operator on Sieve X for each X which commutes with pullback. We show that a Grothendieck topology J induces a natural closure operator, and define what the closed sieves are. The collection of J-closed sieves forms a presheaf which is a sheaf for J, and further this presheaf can be used to determine the Grothendieck topology from the sheaf predicate.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Coherent, Regular and Extensive Grothendieck Topologies
nodes.description: This file defines three related Grothendieck topologies on a category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.CoherentSheaves
nodes.description: This file characterises sheaves for the coherent topology

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.CoherentTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Description of the covering sieves of the coherent topology
nodes.description: This file characterises the covering sieves of the coherent topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.Comparison
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connections between the regular, extensive and coherent topologies
nodes.description: This file compares the regular, extensive and coherent topologies.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.Equivalence
nodes.description: This file proves that the coherent and regular topologies transfer nicely along equivalences of categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.ExtensiveColimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Colimits in categories of extensive sheaves
nodes.description: This file proves that J-shaped colimits of A-valued sheaves for the extensive topology are computed objectwise if colim : J ⥤ A ⥤ A preserves finite products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.ExtensiveSheaves
nodes.description: This file characterises sheaves for the extensive topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.ExtensiveTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Description of the covering sieves of the extensive topology
nodes.description: This file characterises the covering sieves of the extensive topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.LocallySurjective
nodes.descriptionTitle: Locally surjective morphisms of coherent sheaves
nodes.description: This file characterises locally surjective morphisms of presheaves for the coherent, regular and extensive topologies.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.ReflectsPrecoherent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Reflecting the property of being precoherent
nodes.description: We prove that given a fully faithful functor F : C ⥤ D which preserves and reflects finite effective epimorphic families, such that for every object X of D there exists an object W of C with an effective epi π : F.obj W ⟶ X, the category C is Precoherent whenever D is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.ReflectsPreregular
nodes.descriptionTitle: Reflecting the property of being preregular
nodes.description: We prove that given a fully faithful functor F : C ⥤ D, with Preregular D, such that for every object X of D there exists an object W of C with an effective epi π : F.obj W ⟶ X, the category C is Preregular.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.RegularSheaves
nodes.description: This file characterises sheaves for the regular topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.RegularTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Description of the covering sieves of the regular topology
nodes.description: This file characterises the covering sieves of the regular topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.SequentialLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits of epimorphisms in coherent topoi
nodes.description: This file proves that a sequential limit of epimorphisms is epimorphic in the category of sheaves for the coherent topology on a preregular finitary extensive category where sequential limits of effective epimorphisms are effective epimorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coherent.SheafComparison
nodes.description: Given a fully faithful functor F : C ⥤ D into a precoherent category, which preserves and reflects finite effective epi families, and satisfies the property F.EffectivelyEnough (meaning that to every object in C there is an effective epi from an object in the image of F), the categories of coherent sheaves on C and D are equivalent (see CategoryTheory.coherentTopology.equivalence).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CompatiblePlus
nodes.descriptionTitle: In this file, we prove that the plus functor is compatible with functors which
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that the plus functor is compatible with functors which preserve the correct limits and colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CompatibleSheafification
nodes.descriptionTitle: In this file, we prove that sheafification is compatible with functors which
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that sheafification is compatible with functors which preserve the correct limits and colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.ConcreteSheafification
nodes.description: We construct the sheafification of a presheaf over a site C with values in D whenever D is a concrete category for which the forgetful functor preserves the appropriate (co)limits and reflects isomorphisms.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.ConstantSheaf
nodes.description: We define the constant sheaf functor (the sheafification of the constant presheaf) constantSheaf : D ⥤ Sheaf J D and prove that it is left adjoint to evaluation at a terminal object (see constantSheafAdj).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Continuous
nodes.description: We define the notion of continuous functor between sites: these are functors F such that the precomposition with F.op preserves sheaves of types (and actually sheaves in any category).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoproductSheafCondition
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sheaf condition and universal coproducts
nodes.description: In this file we show that if { fᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ X } is a family of morphisms and ∐ᵢ Yᵢ is a universal coproduct, then any presheaf F that preserves products is a sheaf for the single object covering { ∐ᵢ Yᵢ ⟶ X } if and only if it is a sheaf for { fᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ X }ᵢ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoverLifting
nodes.description: We define cocontinuous functors between sites as functors that pull covering sieves back to covering sieves. This concept is also known as cover-lifting or cover-reflecting functors. We use the original terminology and definition of SGA 4 III 2.1. However, the notion of cocontinuous functor should not be confused with the general definition of cocontinuous functors between categories as functors preserving small colimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoverPreserving
nodes.description: In order to show that a functor is continuous, we define cover-preserving functors between sites as functors that push covering sieves to covering sieves. Then, a cover-preserving and compatible-preserving functor is continuous.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Coverage
nodes.description: A coverage K on a category C is a set of presieves associated to every object X : C, called "covering presieves". This collection must satisfy a certain "pullback compatibility" condition, saying that whenever S is a covering presieve on X and f : Y ⟶ X is a morphism, then there exists some covering sieve T on Y such that T factors through S along f.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoversTop
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoversTop.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Objects which cover the terminal object
nodes.description: In this file, given a site (C, J), we introduce the notion of a family of objects Y : I → C which "cover the final object": this means that for all X : C, the sieve Sieve.ofObjects Y X is covering for J. When there is a terminal object X : C, then J.CoversTop Y holds iff Sieve.ofObjects Y X is covering for J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.CoversTop.Over
nodes.description: This file contains a transitivity lemma for GrothendieckTopology.CoversTop: if a family X : I → C covers the top for J, and for each i a family Y i covers the top for the induced topology on Over (X i), then the combined family covers the top for J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.DenseSubsite.Basic
nodes.description: We define IsCoverDense functors into sites as functors such that there exists a covering sieve that factors through images of the functor for each object in D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.DenseSubsite.InducedTopology
nodes.description: We say that a functor G : C ⥤ (D, K) is locally dense if for each covering sieve T in D of some X : C, T ∩ mor(C) generates a covering sieve of X in D. A locally dense fully faithful functor then induces a topology on C via { T ∩ mor(C) | T ∈ K }. Note that this is equal to the collection of sieves on C whose image generates a covering sieve. This construction would make C both cover-lifting and cover-preserving.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.DenseSubsite.OneHypercoverDense
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equivalence of categories of sheaves with a dense subsite that is 1-hypercover dense
nodes.description: Let F : C₀ ⥤ C be a functor equipped with Grothendieck topologies J₀ and J. Assume that F is a dense subsite. We introduce a typeclass IsOneHypercoverDense.{w} F J₀ J which roughly says that objects in C admits a 1-hypercover consisting of objects in C₀.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.DenseSubsite.SheafEquiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: The equivalence of categories of sheaves of a dense subsite
nodes.description: If G : C ⥤ D exhibits (C, J) as a dense subsite of (D, K), and A is a category with suitable limits, then the functor G.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K : Sheaf K A ⥤ Sheaf J A is an equivalence of categories. The equivalence of categories can be obtained as sheafEquiv J K G A which is defined in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/DenseSubsite/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.DescentData
nodes.description: In this file, given a pseudofunctor F from LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ to Cat, and a family of maps f i : X i ⟶ S in the category C, we define the category F.DescentData f of objects over the X i equipped with descent data relative to the morphisms f i : X i ⟶ S.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.DescentDataAsCoalgebra
nodes.description: Let F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Adj Cat be a pseudofunctor to the bicategory of adjunctions in Cat. In particular, for any morphism g : X ⟶ Y in C, we have an adjunction (g^, g_) between a pullback functor and a pushforward functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.DescentDataPrime
nodes.descriptionTitle: Descent data when we have pullbacks
nodes.description: In this file, given a pseudofunctor F from LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ to Cat, a family of maps f i : X i ⟶ S in the category C, chosen pullbacks sq and threefold wide pullbacks sq₃ for these morphisms, we define a category F.DescentData' sq sq₃ of objects over the X i equipped with a descent data relative to the morphisms f i : X i ⟶ S, where the data and compatibilities are expressed using the chosen pullbacks.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.IsPrestack
nodes.description: Let C be a category and F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat. Given S : C, and objects M and N in F.obj (.mk (op S)), we define a presheaf of types F.presheafHom M N on the category Over S: its sections on an object T : Over S corresponding to a morphism p : X ⟶ S are the type of morphisms p^ M ⟶ p^ N. We shall say that F satisfies the descent of morphisms for a Grothendieck topology J if these presheaves are all sheaves (typeclass F.IsPrestack J).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.IsStack
nodes.description: Let C be a category with a Grothendieck topology J and F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat. In this file, we define the typeclass F.IsStack J saying that F is a stack for J. (See the terminological note in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/IsPrestack.lean: we do not require that the categories F.obj (.mk (op S)) are groupoids.)

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Descent.Precoverage
nodes.description: Let F : LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat be a pseudofunctor. Assuming F is a prestack for a Grothendieck topology J, we show that if f : X i ⟶ S and f' : X' j ⟶ S are two covering families of morphisms in S such that the sieve generated by f' is contained in the sieve generated by f, then the functor F.DescentData f ⥤ F.DescentData f' is fully faithful. It follows that if the descent is effective for the family f', then it is also effective for the family f.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.EffectiveEpimorphic
nodes.description: We define the notion of effective epimorphic (pre)sieves and provide some API for relating the notion with the notions of effective epimorphism and effective epimorphic family.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.EpiMono
nodes.descriptionTitle: Morphisms of sheaves factor as a locally surjective followed by a locally injective morphism
nodes.description: When morphisms in a concrete category A factor in a functorial manner as a surjective map followed by an injective map, we obtain that any morphism of sheaves in Sheaf J A factors in a functorial manner as a locally surjective morphism (which is epi) followed by a locally injective morphism (which is mono).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.EqualizerSheafCondition
nodes.descriptionTitle: The equalizer diagram sheaf condition for a presieve
nodes.description: In Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/IsSheafFor.lean it is defined what it means for a presheaf to be a sheaf for a particular presieve. In this file we provide equivalent conditions in terms of equalizer diagrams.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Equivalence
nodes.description: Given a site (C, J) and a category D which is equivalent to C, with C and D possibly large and possibly in different universes, we transport the Grothendieck topology J on C to D and prove that the sheaf categories are equivalent.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Finite
nodes.description: In this file we define the finite pretopology on a category, which consists of presieves that contain only finitely many arrows.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.GlobalSections
nodes.description: In this file we define a global sections functor Sheaf.Γ : Sheaf J A ⥤ A and show that it is isomorphic to several other constructions when they exist, most notably evaluation of sheaves on a terminal object and Functor.sectionsFunctor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Grothendieck
nodes.description: Definition and lemmas about Grothendieck topologies. A Grothendieck topology for a category C is a set of sieves on each object X satisfying certain closure conditions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.Homotopy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of 1-hypercovers up to homotopy
nodes.description: In this file we define the category of 1-hypercovers up to homotopy. This is the category of 1-hypercovers, but where morphisms are considered up to existence of a homotopy.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.IsSheaf
nodes.description: In this file, given a Grothendieck topology J on a category C, we define a type J.OneHypercoverFamily of families of 1-hypercovers. When H : J.OneHypercoverFamily, we define a predicate H.IsGenerating which means that any covering sieve contains the sieve generated by the underlying covering of one of the 1-hypercovers in the family. If this holds, we show in OneHypercoverFamily.isSheaf_iff that a presheaf P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A is a sheaf iff for any 1-hypercover E in the family, the multifork E.multifork P is a limit.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.One
nodes.description: Given a Grothendieck topology J on a category C, we define the type of 1-hypercovers of an object S : C. They consist of a covering family of morphisms X i ⟶ S indexed by a type I₀ and, for each tuple (i₁, i₂) of elements of I₀, a "covering Y j of the fibre product of X i₁ and X i₂ over S", a condition which is phrased here without assuming that the fibre product actually exists.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.Saturate
nodes.description: Given a 0-hypercover E, we define a 1-hypercover E.saturate

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.SheafOfTypes
nodes.description: In this file we provide some API for working with 1-hypercovers for sheaves of types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.Subcanonical
nodes.description: In this file we provide API related to covers in subcanonical topologies.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.Zero
nodes.description: Given a coverage J on a category C, we define the type of 0-hypercovers of an object S : C. They consist of a covering family of morphisms X i ⟶ S indexed by a type I₀ such that the induced presieve is in J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Hypercover.ZeroFamily
nodes.description: A precoverage is a condition on all presieves. In some applications, it is practical to instead define a condition on all pre-0-hypercovers. Such a condition for every object is a pre-0-hypercover family if these conditions are invariant under deduplication.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.IsSheafFor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sheaf condition for a presieve
nodes.description: We define what it means for a presheaf P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v to be a sheaf for a particular presieve R on X: R. See FamilyOfElements. and any g₁ : Z ⟶ Y₁ and g₂ : Z ⟶ Y₂ such that g₁ ≫ f₁ = g₂ ≫ f₂, the restriction of x_f₁ along g₁ agrees with the restriction of x_f₂ along g₂. See FamilyOfElements.Compatible. R, the restriction of t on f is x_f. See FamilyOfElements.IsAmalgamation.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.JointlySurjective
nodes.description: In the category of types, the jointly surjective precoverage has the jointly surjective families as coverings. We show that this precoverage is stable under the standard constructions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LeftExact
nodes.description: In this file we show that sheafification commutes with finite limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Limits
nodes.description: We prove that the forgetful functor from Sheaf J D to presheaves creates limits. If the target category D has limits (of a certain shape), this then implies that Sheaf J D has limits of the same shape and that the forgetful functor preserves these limits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LocalProperties
nodes.description: In this file we study properties of sheaves that can be checked on a covering family of objects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Localization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sheaf category as a localized category
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that the category of sheaves Sheaf J A is a localization of the category Presheaf J A with respect to the class J.W of morphisms of presheaves which become isomorphisms after applying the sheafification functor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology J. Let A be a concrete category. In this file, we introduce a type class J.WEqualsLocallyBijective A which says that the class J.W (of morphisms of presheaves which become isomorphisms after sheafification) is the class of morphisms that are both locally injective and locally surjective (i.e. locally bijective). We prove that this holds iff for any presheaf P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, the sheafification map toSheafify J P is locally bijective.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyFullyFaithful
nodes.descriptionTitle: Locally fully faithful functors into sites
nodes.description: A functor G : C ⥤ D is locally full w.r.t. a topology on D if for every f : G.obj U ⟶ G.obj V, the set of G.map fᵢ : G.obj Wᵢ ⟶ G.obj U such that G.map fᵢ ≫ f is in the image of G is a coverage of the topology on D. A functor G : C ⥤ D is locally faithful w.r.t. a topology on D if for every f₁ f₂ : U ⟶ V whose images in D are equal, the set of G.map gᵢ : G.obj Wᵢ ⟶ G.obj U such that gᵢ ≫ f₁ = gᵢ ≫ f₂ is a coverage of the topology on D.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyInjective
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology J, and let D be a concrete category. In this file, we introduce the typeclass Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J φ for a morphism φ : F₁ ⟶ F₂ in the category Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D. This means that φ is locally injective. More precisely, if x and y are two elements of some F₁.obj U such the images of x and y in F₂.obj U coincide, then the equality x = y must hold locally, i.e. after restriction by the maps of a covering sieve.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallySurjective
nodes.description: surjective with respect to a Grothendieck topology if every section in the target is locally in the set-theoretic image, i.e. the image sheaf coincides with the target.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.MayerVietorisSquare
nodes.description: The purpose of this file is to allow the formalization of long exact Mayer-Vietoris sequences in sheaf cohomology. If X₄ is an open subset of a topological space that is covered by two open subsets X₂ and X₃, it is known that there is a long exact sequence ... ⟶ H^q(X₄) ⟶ H^q(X₂) ⊞ H^q(X₃) ⟶ H^q(X₁) ⟶ H^{q+1}(X₄) ⟶ ... where X₁ is the intersection of X₂ and X₃, and H^q are the cohomology groups with values in an abelian sheaf.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monoidal category structure on categories of sheaves
nodes.description: If A is a closed braided category with suitable limits, and J is a Grothendieck topology with HasWeakSheafify J A, then Sheaf J A can be equipped with a monoidal category structure. This is not made an instance as in some cases it may conflict with monoidal structure deduced from chosen finite products.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.MorphismProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: The site induced by a morphism property
nodes.description: Let C be a category with pullbacks and P be a multiplicative morphism property which is stable under base change. Then P induces a pretopology, where coverings are given by presieves whose elements satisfy P.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.NonabelianCohomology.H1
nodes.descriptionTitle: The cohomology of a sheaf of groups in degree 1
nodes.description: In this file, we shall define the cohomology in degree 1 of a sheaf of groups (TODO).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Over
nodes.description: In this file, given a Grothendieck topology J on a category C and X : C, we construct a Grothendieck topology J.over X on the category Over X. In order to do this, we first construct a bijection Sieve.overEquiv Y : Sieve Y ≃ Sieve Y.left for all Y : Over X. Then, as it is stated in SGA 4 III 5.2.1, a sieve of Y : Over X is covering for J.over X if and only if the corresponding sieve of Y.left is covering for J. As a result, the forgetful functor Over.forget X : Over X ⥤ X is both cover-preserving and cover-lifting.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Plus
nodes.description: This file contains the construction of P⁺, for a presheaf P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D where C is endowed with a Grothendieck topology J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology J. In this file, we define the notion of point of the site (C, J), as a structure GrothendieckTopology.Point. Such a Φ : J.Point consists in a functor Φ.fiber : C ⥤ Type w such that the category Φ.fiber.Elements is cofiltered (and initially small) and such that if x : Φ.fiber.obj X and R is a covering sieve of X, then x belongs to the image of some y : Φ.fiber.obj Y by a morphism f : Y ⟶ X which belongs to R.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Category
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of points of a site
nodes.description: We define the category structure on the points of a site (C, J): a morphism between Φ₁ ⟶ Φ₂ between two points consists of a morphism Φ₂.fiber ⟶ Φ₁.fiber (SGA 4 IV 3.2).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Comap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inverse image of a point by a continuous functor
nodes.description: Let F : C ⥤ D be a representably flat continuous functor between sites (C, J) and (D, K). Let Φ be a point of (D, K). Assume hF : CoverPreserving J K F. In this file, we define a point Φ.comap F hF of the site (C, J) and construct an isomorphism (Φ.comap F hF).sheafFiber ≅ F.sheafPullback A J K ⋙ Φ.sheafFiber.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Conservative
nodes.description: Let J be a Grothendieck topology on a category C. Let P : ObjectProperty J.Point be a family of points. We say that P is a conservative family of points if the corresponding fiber functors Sheaf J (Type w) ⥤ Type w jointly reflect isomorphisms. Under suitable assumptions on the coefficient category A, this implies that the fiber functors Sheaf J A ⥤ A corresponding to the points in P jointly reflect isomorphisms, epimorphisms and monomorphisms, and they are also jointly faithful.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.IsMonoidalW
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monoidal structure on sheaves using enough points
nodes.description: Let (C, J) be a site with a conservative family of points. If A is a suitable monoidal category, we show that the class of morphisms J.W : MorphismProperty (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) is stable under tensor products, which allows to check the assumptions of Sheaf.monoidalCategory in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Monoidal.lean, i.e. this can be used in order to construct the monoidal category structure on Sheaf J A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Map
nodes.descriptionTitle: The image of a point by a cocontinuous functor
nodes.description: Let F : C ⥤ D be a cocontinuous functor between sites (C, J) and (D, K). Let Φ be a point of (C, J). In this file, we define a point Φ.map F K of (D, K) and show that there are natural isomorphisms (Φ.map F K).presheafFiber ≅ (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ A).obj F.op ⋙ Φ.presheafFiber and (Φ.map F K).sheafFiber ≅ F.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K ⋙ Φ.sheafFiber (the latter is defined only if F is also continuous).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Monoidal
nodes.description: Let Φ be a point of a site (C, J). Let A be a monoidal category where the tensor product commutes with filtered colimits in both variables. We show that the fiber functors Φ.presheafFiber : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A and Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A are monoidal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.OfIsCofiltered
nodes.description: Let J be a Grothendieck topology on a category C. We provide a constructor Point.ofIsCofiltered for points for J which takes as inputs: any morphism f : p.obj U ⟶ X, there exists a morphism g : Y ⟶ X in R, a morphism q : V ⟶ U in N and a morphism a : p.obj V ⟶ Y such that a ≫ g = p.map q ≫ f. We show that the fiber of a presheaf for the constructed point identifies to a colimit indexed by the category N.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Over
nodes.description: Given a point Φ of a site (C, J), an object X : C, and x : Φ.fiber.obj X, we define a point Φ.over x of the site (Over X, J.over X).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Presheaf
nodes.description: Let C be a category. For the Grothendieck topology ⊥ on C, we know that the category of sheaves with values in A identifies to Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A (see sheafBotEquivalence in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Sheaf.lean). In this file, we show that any X : C defines a point for this site, and that these points form a conservative family of points.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Point.Skyscraper
nodes.description: Let Φ be a point of a site (C, J). In this file, we construct the skyscraper sheaf functor skyscraperSheafFunctor : A ⥤ Sheaf J A and show that it is a right adjoint to Φ.sheafFiber : Sheaf J A ⥤ A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Precoverage
nodes.description: A precoverage K on a category C is a set of presieves associated to every object X : C, called "covering presieves". There are no conditions on this set. Common extensions of a precoverage are:

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.PrecoverageToGrothendieck
nodes.descriptionTitle: Grothendieck topology generated by a precoverage
nodes.description: For any category C, we define the Grothendieck topology generated by a precoverage J on C. It is the smallest Grothendieck topology containing all the sieves generated by the covering presieves of J.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Preserves
nodes.description: We prove that a presheaf which satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to certain presieves preserve "the corresponding products".

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.PreservesLimits
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preservation of (co)limits by the sheaf Yoneda functor
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for CategoryTheory.Sites.PreservesLimits.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.PreservesLocallyBijective
nodes.descriptionTitle: Preserving and reflecting local injectivity and surjectivity
nodes.description: This file proves that precomposition with a cocontinuous functor preserves local injectivity and surjectivity of morphisms of presheaves, and that precomposition with a cover-preserving and cover-dense functor reflects the same properties.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.PreservesSheafification
nodes.description: In this file, given a Grothendieck topology J on C and F : A ⥤ B, we define a type class J.PreservesSheafification F. We say that F preserves the sheafification if whenever a morphism of presheaves P₁ ⟶ P₂ induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves, then the induced map P₁ ⋙ F ⟶ P₂ ⋙ F also induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves. (Note: it suffices to check this property for the map from any presheaf P to its associated sheaf, see GrothendieckTopology.preservesSheafification_iff_of_adjunctions).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Pretopology
nodes.description: Definition and lemmas about Grothendieck pretopologies. A Grothendieck pretopology for a category C is a set of families of morphisms with fixed codomain, satisfying certain closure conditions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.PseudofunctorSheafOver
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sheaves on Over categories, as a pseudofunctor
nodes.description: Given a Grothendieck topology J on a category C and a category A, we define the pseudofunctor J.pseudofunctorOver A : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ) Cat which sends X : C to the category of sheaves on Over X with values in A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Pullback
nodes.description: between sites (for topologies J on C and K on D) such that the functor G.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K : Sheaf K A ⥤ Sheaf J A has a left adjoint, this is the pullback functor defined as a chosen left adjoint.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.RegularEpi
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of type-valued sheaves is a regular epi category
nodes.description: isRegularEpiCategory_sheaf: Let J be a Grothendieck topology on C, and suppose that D is a regular epi category which has pushouts and pullbacks, and that sheafification of D-valued J-sheaves exists. Suppose further that the category Sheaf J D is balanced, and that the underlying morphism of presheaves of every epimorphism in Sheaf J D can be factored as an epimorphism followed by a monomorphism. Then Sheaf J D is a regular epi category.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Sheaf
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sheaves taking values in a category
nodes.description: If C is a category with a Grothendieck topology, we define the notion of a sheaf taking values in an arbitrary category A. We follow the definition in https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VR, noting that the presheaf of sets "defined above" can be seen in the comments between tags 00VQ and 00VR on the page . The advantage of this definition is that we need no assumptions whatsoever on A other than the assumption that the morphisms in C and A live in the same universe.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomology.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology J. We define the cohomology types Sheaf.H F n of an abelian sheaf F on the site (C, J) for all n : ℕ. These abelian groups are defined as the Ext-groups from the constant abelian sheaf with values ℤ (actually ULift ℤ) to F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomology.Cech
nodes.description: Given a family of objects U : ι → C in a category C that has finite products, we define a Cech complex functor cechComplexFunctor : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ CochainComplex A ℕ which sends a presheaf P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A in a preadditive category (where products exist) to the cochain complex which in degree n consists of the product, indexed by i : Fin (n + 1) → ι, of the value of P on the product of the objects U (i a) for a : Fin (n + 1).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomology.MayerVietoris
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence in sheaf cohomology
nodes.description: Let C be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology J. Let S : J.MayerVietorisSquare be a Mayer-Vietoris square for J. Let F be an abelian sheaf on (C, J).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafHom
nodes.description: In this file, given two sheaves F and G on a site (C, J) with values in a category A, we define a sheaf of types sheafHom F G which sends X : C to the type of morphisms between the restrictions of F and G to the categories Over X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafOfTypes
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sheaves of types on a Grothendieck topology
nodes.description: Defines the notion of a sheaf of types (usually called a sheaf of sets by mathematicians) on a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology, as well as a range of equivalent conditions useful in different situations.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Sheafification
nodes.description: Given a site (C, J) we define a typeclass HasSheafify J A saying that the inclusion functor from A-valued sheaves on C to presheaves admits a left exact left adjoint (sheafification).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Sieves
nodes.description: which is closed under left-composition. given by downward-closing. the Yoneda embedding of X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Spaces
nodes.descriptionTitle: Grothendieck topology on a topological space
nodes.description: Define the Grothendieck topology and the pretopology associated to a topological space, and show that the pretopology induces the topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Subcanonical
nodes.description: This file provides some API for the Yoneda embedding into the category of sheaves for a subcanonical Grothendieck topology.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.SubcanonicalOver
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on Over X is subcanonical if the base is
nodes.description: We show that if J is subcanonical, then also J.over X is subcanonical.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Subsheaf
nodes.description: We define the subsheaf of a type-valued presheaf.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Types
nodes.descriptionTitle: Grothendieck Topology and Sheaves on the Category of Types
nodes.description: In this file we define a Grothendieck topology on the category of types, and construct the canonical functor that sends a type to a sheaf over the category of types, and make this an equivalence of categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sites.Whiskering
nodes.descriptionTitle: In this file we construct the functor Sheaf J A ⥤ Sheaf J B between sheaf categories
nodes.description: In this file we construct the functor Sheaf J A ⥤ Sheaf J B between sheaf categories obtained by composition with a functor F : A ⥤ B.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Skeletal
nodes.description: Define skeletal categories as categories in which any two isomorphic objects are equal.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Basic
nodes.description: Let C be a category. A class of morphisms I : MorphismProperty C permits the small object argument (typeclass HasSmallObjectArgument.{w} I where w is an auxiliary universe) if there exists a regular cardinal κ : Cardinal.{w} such that IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument I κ holds. This technical condition is defined in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/SmallObject/IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Construction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construction for the small object argument
nodes.description: Given a family of morphisms f i : A i ⟶ B i in a category C, we define a functor SmallObject.functor f : Arrow S ⥤ Arrow S which sends an object given by arrow πX : X ⟶ S to the pushout functorObj f πX: where the morphism on the left is a coproduct (of copies of maps f i) indexed by a type FunctorObjIndex f πX which parametrizes the diagrams of the form

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cardinals that are suitable for the small object argument
nodes.description: In this file, given a class of morphisms I : MorphismProperty C and a regular cardinal κ : Cardinal.{w}, we define a typeclass IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument I κ which requires certain smallness properties (I is w-small, C is locally w-small), the existence of certain colimits (pushouts, coproducts of size w, and the condition HasIterationOfShape κ.ord.ToType C about the existence of colimits indexed by limit ordinal smaller than or equal to κ.ord), and the technical assumption that if A is the a morphism in I...

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Iteration.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfinite iterations of a successor structure
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the structure SuccStruct on a category C. It consists of the data of an object X₀ : C, a successor map succ : C → C and a morphism toSucc : X ⟶ succ X for any X : C. The map toSucc does not have to be natural in X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Iteration.ExtendToSucc
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extension of a functor from Set.Iic j to Set.Iic (Order.succ j)
nodes.description: Given a linearly ordered type J with SuccOrder J, j : J that is not maximal, we define the extension of a functor F : Set.Iic j ⥤ C as a functor Set.Iic (Order.succ j) ⥤ C when an object X : C and a morphism τ : F.obj ⟨j, _⟩ ⟶ X is given.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Iteration.FunctorOfCocone
nodes.descriptionTitle: The functor from Set.Iic j deduced from a cocone
nodes.description: Given a functor F : Set.Iio j ⥤ C and c : Cocone F, we define an extension of F as a functor Set.Iic j ⥤ C for which the top element is mapped to c.pt.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.Iteration.Nonempty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of the iteration of a successor structure
nodes.description: Given Φ : SuccStruct C, we show by transfinite induction that for any element j in a well-ordered set J, the type Φ.Iteration j is nonempty.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.TransfiniteCompositionLifting
nodes.descriptionTitle: The left lifting property is stable under transfinite composition
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if W : MorphismProperty C, then W.llp.IsStableUnderTransfiniteCompositionOfShape J, i.e. the class of morphisms which have the left lifting property with respect to W is stable under transfinite composition.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.TransfiniteIteration
nodes.descriptionTitle: The transfinite iteration of a successor structure
nodes.description: Given a successor structure Φ : SuccStruct C (see the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/SmallObject/Iteration/Basic.lean) and a well-ordered type J, we define the iteration Φ.iteration J : C. It is defined as the colimit of a functor Φ.iterationFunctor J : J ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallObject.WellOrderInductionData
nodes.descriptionTitle: Limits of inverse systems indexed by well-ordered types
nodes.description: Given a functor F : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v where J is a well-ordered type, we introduce a structure F.WellOrderInductionData which allows to show that the map F.sections → F.obj (op ⊥) is surjective.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.SmallRepresentatives
nodes.description: Given a type Ω : Type w, we construct a structure SmallCategoryOfSet Ω : Type w which consists of the data and axioms that allows to define a category structure such that the type of objects and morphisms identify to subtypes of Ω.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Square
nodes.description: In this file, we define a bundled version of CommSq which allows to consider commutative squares as objects in a category Square C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Basic
nodes.description: We define subfunctors of a type-valued functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Equalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: The equalizer of two morphisms of functors, as a subfunctor
nodes.description: If F₁ and F₂ are type-valued functors, A : Subfunctor F₁, and f and g are two morphisms A.toFunctor ⟶ F₂, we introduce Subcomplex.equalizer f g, which is the subfunctor of F₁ contained in A where f and g coincide.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Subpresheaves that are generated by finitely many sections
nodes.description: Given F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w, G : Subfunctor F, objects X : ι → Cᵒᵖ and sections x : (i : ι) → F.obj (X i), we define a predicate G.IsGeneratedBy x saying that G is the subpresheaf generated by the sections x i. If this holds for a finite index type ι, we say that G is "finite", and this gives a type class G.IsFinite.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Image
nodes.description: Given a morphism of type-valued functors p : F' ⟶ F, we define its range Subfunctor.range p. More generally, if G' : Subfunctor F', we define G'.image p : Subfunctor F as the image of G' by f, and if G : Subfunctor F, we define its preimage G.preimage f : Subfunctor F'.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.OfSection
nodes.descriptionTitle: The subpresheaf generated by a section
nodes.description: Given a presheaf of types F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w and a section x : F.obj X, we define Subfunctor.ofSection x : Subfunctor F as the subpresheaf of F generated by x.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Sieves
nodes.description: Given a subpresheaf G of a presheaf of types F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w and a section s : F.obj U, we define a sieve G.sieveOfSection s : Sieve (unop U) and the associated compatible family of elements with values in G.toFunctor.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subfunctor.Subobject
nodes.descriptionTitle: Comparison between Subfunctor, MonoOver and Subobject
nodes.description: Given a type-valued functor F : C ⥤ Type w, we define an equivalence of categories Subfunctor.equivalenceMonoOver F : Subfunctor F ≌ MonoOver F and an order isomorphism Subfunctor.orderIsoSubject F : Subfunctor F ≃o Subobject F.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.ArtinianObject
nodes.description: We shall say that an object X in a category C is Artinian (type class IsArtinianObject X) if the ordered type Subobject X satisfies the descending chain condition. The corresponding property of objects isArtinianObject : ObjectProperty C is always closed under subobjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Basic
nodes.description: We define Subobject X as the quotient (by isomorphisms) of MonoOver X := {f : Over X // Mono f.hom}.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Classifier.Defs
nodes.description: We define a structure containing the data of a subobject classifier in a category C as CategoryTheory.Subobject.Classifier C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Comma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Subobjects in the category of structured arrows
nodes.description: We compute the subobjects of an object A in the category StructuredArrow S T for T : C ⥤ D and S : D as a subtype of the subobjects of A.right. We deduce that StructuredArrow S T is well-powered if C is.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.FactorThru
nodes.description: The predicate h : P.Factors f, for P : Subobject Y and f : X ⟶ Y asserts the existence of some P.factorThru f : X ⟶ (P : C) making the obvious diagram commute.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.HasCardinalLT
nodes.description: If X ⟶ Y is a monomorphism, and the cardinality of Subobject Y is < κ, then the cardinality of Subobject X is also < κ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Lattice
nodes.description: We provide the SemilatticeInf with OrderTop (Subobject X) instance when [HasPullback C], and the SemilatticeSup (Subobject X) instance when [HasImages C] [HasBinaryCoproducts C].

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Limits
nodes.description: We define equalizerSubobject, kernelSubobject and imageSubobject, which are the subobjects represented by the equalizer, kernel and image of (a pair of) morphism(s) and provide conditions for P.factors f, where P is one of these special subobjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.MonoOver
nodes.description: As preparation for defining Subobject X, we set up the theory for MonoOver X := { f : Over X // Mono f.hom}.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.NoetherianObject
nodes.description: We shall say that an object X in a category C is Noetherian (type class IsNoetherianObject X) if the ordered type Subobject X satisfies the ascending chain condition. The corresponding property of objects isNoetherianObject : ObjectProperty C is always closed under subobjects.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Presheaf
nodes.description: Following Section I.3 of Sheaves in Geometry and Logic, we define the subobjects presheaf Subobject.presheaf C mapping any object X to its type of subobjects Subobject X.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.Types
nodes.description: By building a categorical equivalence MonoOver α ≌ Set α for any α : Type u, we deduce that Subobject α ≃o Set α and that Type u is well-powered.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subobject.WellPowered
nodes.description: A category (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] is [WellPowered.{w} C] if C is locally small relative to w and for every X : C, we have Small.{w} (Subobject X). The most common case is when w = v, in which case, it only involves the condition Small.{v} (Subobject X)

nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subpresheaf.Subobject
