nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Subterminal
nodes.description: Subterminal objects are the objects which can be thought of as subobjects of the terminal object. In fact, the definition can be constructed to not require a terminal object, by defining A to be subterminal iff for any Z, there is at most one morphism Z ⟶ A. An alternate definition is that the diagonal morphism A ⟶ A ⨯ A is an isomorphism. In this file we define subterminal objects and show the equivalence of these three definitions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sums.Associator
nodes.descriptionTitle: Associator for binary disjoint union of categories.
nodes.description: The associator functor ((C ⊕ D) ⊕ E) ⥤ (C ⊕ (D ⊕ E)) and its inverse form an equivalence.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sums.Basic
nodes.description: We define the category instance on C ⊕ D when C and D are categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Sums.Products
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functors out of sums of categories.
nodes.description: This file records the universal property of sums of categories as an equivalence of categories Sum.functorEquiv : A ⊕ A' ⥤ B ≌ (A ⥤ B) × (A' ⥤ B), and characterizes its precompositions with the left and right inclusion as corresponding to the projections on the product side.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Thin
nodes.description: A thin category (also known as a sparse category) is a category with at most one morphism between each pair of objects. Examples include posets, but also some indexing categories (diagrams) for special shapes of (co)limits. To construct a category instance one only needs to specify the CategoryStruct part, as the axioms hold for free. If C is thin, then the category of functors to C is also thin. Further, to show two objects are isomorphic in a thin category, it suffices only to give a morphism in each direction.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Topos.Classifier
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in CategoryTheory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Topos.Sheaf
nodes.description: We define a subobject classifier for categories of sheaves of (large enough) types.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Adjunction
nodes.description: If a functor F : C ⥤ D between pretriangulated categories is triangulated, and if we have an adjunction F ⊣ G, then G is also a triangulated functor. We deduce the symmetric statement (if G is a triangulated functor, then so is F) using opposite categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of triangles in an additive category with an additive shift. It also defines morphisms between these triangles.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Functor
nodes.description: In this file, when C and D are categories equipped with a shift by ℤ and F : C ⥤ D is a functor which commutes with the shift, we define the induced functor F.mapTriangle : Triangle C ⥤ Triangle D on the categories of triangles. When C and D are pretriangulated, a triangulated functor is such a functor F which also sends distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles: this defines the typeclass Functor.IsTriangulated.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Generators
nodes.description: We define the notions of strong and classical generators in (pre)triangulated categories. This is not to be confused with ObjectProperty.IsStrongGenerator defined in CategoryTheory/Generator.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.HomologicalFunctor
nodes.description: In this file, given a functor F : C ⥤ A from a pretriangulated category to an abelian category, we define the type class F.IsHomological, which is the property that F sends distinguished triangles in C to exact sequences in A.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.LocalizingSubcategory
nodes.description: Let C be a pretriangulated category. If A and B are triangulated subcategories of C, we define predicates (typeclasses IsVerdierRightLocalizing and IsVerdierLeftLocalizing) saying that A is right B-localizing (or left B-localizing). When B is closed under isomorphisms, we show that this implies that the functor from the Verdier quotient A/(A ⊓ B) to C/B is fully faithful.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The shift on the opposite category of a pretriangulated category
nodes.description: Let C be a (pre)triangulated category. We already have a shift on Cᵒᵖ given by CategoryTheory.Shift.Opposite, but this is not the shift that we want to make Cᵒᵖ into a (pre)triangulated category. The correct shift on Cᵒᵖ is obtained by combining the constructions in the files CategoryTheory.Shift.Opposite and CategoryTheory.Shift.Pullback.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Functor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Opposites of functors between pretriangulated categories,
nodes.description: If F : C ⥤ D is a functor between pretriangulated categories, we prove that F is a triangulated functor if and only if F.op is a triangulated functor. In order to do this, we first show that a CommShift structure on F naturally gives one on F.op (for the shifts on Cᵒᵖ and Dᵒᵖ defined in CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Basic), and we then prove that F.mapTriangle.op and F.op.mapTriangle correspond to each other via the equivalences (Triangle C)ᵒᵖ ≌ Triangle Cᵒᵖ and (Triangle D)ᵒᵖ ≌ Triangle Dᵒᵖ given by Cate...

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.OpOp
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if C is a pretriangulated category, then the functors opOp C : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ and unopUnop C : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ⥤ C are triangulated. We also show that the unit and counit isomorphisms of the equivalence opOpEquivalence C : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ≌ C are compatible with shifts, which is summarized by the property (opOpEquivalence C).IsTriangulated.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Pretriangulated
nodes.descriptionTitle: The pretriangulated structure on the opposite category
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the pretriangulated structure on the opposite category Cᵒᵖ of a pretriangulated category C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Subcategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite of a triangulated subcategory
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if P : ObjectProperty C is a triangulated subcategory of a pretriangulated category C, then P.op is a triangulated subcategory of Cᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Triangle
nodes.descriptionTitle: Triangles in the opposite category of a (pre)triangulated category
nodes.description: Let C be a (pre)triangulated category. In CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Basic, we have constructed a shift on Cᵒᵖ that will be part of a structure of (pre)triangulated category. In this file, we construct an equivalence of categories between (Triangle C)ᵒᵖ and Triangle Cᵒᵖ, called CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.triangleOpEquivalence. It sends a triangle X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧ in C to the triangle op Z ⟶ op Y ⟶ op X ⟶ (op Z)⟦1⟧ in Cᵒᵖ (without introducing signs).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Triangulated
nodes.descriptionTitle: The opposite of a triangulated category is triangulated
nodes.description: The pretriangulated structure on Cᵒᵖ was constructed in the file CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Opposite.Pretriangulated. Here, we show that Cᵒᵖ is triangulated if C is triangulated.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Orthogonal
nodes.description: Let P be a triangulated subcategory of a pretriangulated category C. We show that P.rightOrthogonal (which consists of objects Y with no nonzero map X ⟶ Y with X satisfying P) is a triangulated subcategory. The dual result for P.leftOrthogonal is also obtained.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Pretriangulated
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of pretriangulated categories and triangulated functors between them.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Rotate
nodes.description: This file adds the ability to rotate triangles and triangle morphisms. It also shows that rotation gives an equivalence on the category of triangles.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.SpectralObject
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the category SpectralObject C ι of spectral objects in a pretriangulated category C indexed by the category ι.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Subcategory
nodes.description: In this file, given a pretriangulated category C and P : ObjectProperty C, we introduce a typeclass P.IsTriangulated to express that P is a triangulated subcategory of C. When P is a triangulated subcategory, we introduce a class of morphisms P.trW : MorphismProperty C consisting of the morphisms whose "cone" belongs to P (up to isomorphisms), and we show that it has both calculus of left and right fractions.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.AbelianSubcategory
nodes.description: Let ι : A ⥤ C be a fully faithful additive functor where A is an additive category and C is a triangulated category. We show that A is an abelian category if the following conditions are satisfied: ι.obj X ⟶ (ι.obj Y)⟦n⟧ when n < 0. we complete ι.obj f₁ in a distinguished triangle ι.obj X₁ ⟶ ι.obj X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (ι.obj X₁)⟦1⟧, there exists objects K and Q, and a distinguished triangle (ι.obj K)⟦1⟧ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (ι.obj Q) ⟶ ....

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.Basic
nodes.description: This file introduces the notion of t-structure on (pre)triangulated categories.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.ETrunc
nodes.description: Let t be a t-structure on a triangulated category C. In this file, we extend the definition of the truncation functors truncLT and truncGE for indices in ℤ to EInt, as t.eTruncLT : EInt ⥤ C ⥤ C and t.eTruncGE : EInt ⥤ C ⥤ C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.Heart
nodes.description: Let t be a t-structure on a triangulated category C. We define the heart of t as a property t.heart : ObjectProperty C. As the the heart is usually identified to a particular category in the applications (e.g. the heart of the canonical t-structure on the derived category of an abelian category A identifies to A), instead of working with the full subcategory defined by t.heart, we introduce a typeclass t.Heart H which says that the additive category H identifies to the full subcategory t.heart.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.Induced
nodes.description: Let t be a t-structure on a pretriangulated category C. If P is a triangulated subcategory of C, we introduce a typeclass P.HasInducedTStructure t which essentially says that up to isomorphisms P is stable by the application of the truncation functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.SpectralObject
nodes.description: Let C be a triangulated category equipped with a t-structure t. We define a functor t.ω₁ : ComposableArrows EInt 1 ⥤ C ⥤ C which sends a map a ⟶ b in EInt (i.e. a ≤ b) to the functor t.eTruncLT.obj b ⋙ t.eTruncGE.obj a.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.TruncLEGT
nodes.description: Let t be a t-structure on a (pre)triangulated category C. In this file, for any n : ℤ, we introduce the truncation functors t.truncLE n : C ⥤ C and t.truncGT n : C ⥤ C, as variants of the functors t.truncLT n : C ⥤ C and t.truncGE n : C ⥤ C introduced in the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Triangulated/TStructure/TruncLTGE.lean.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.TruncLTGE
nodes.description: Let t be a t-structure on a (pre)triangulated category C. In this file, for any n : ℤ, we construct truncation functors t.truncLT n : C ⥤ C, t.truncGE n : C ⥤ C and natural transformations t.truncLTι n : t.truncLT n ⟶ 𝟭 C, t.truncGEπ n : 𝟭 C ⟶ t.truncGE n and t.truncGEδLT n : t.truncGE n ⟶ t.truncLT n ⋙ shiftFunctor C (1 : ℤ) which are part of a distinguished triangle (t.truncLT n).obj X ⟶ X ⟶ (t.truncGE n).obj X ⟶ ((t.truncLT n).obj X)⟦1⟧ for any X : C, with (t.truncLT n).obj X < n and (t.truncGE n).obj X ≥ n.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TriangleShift
nodes.descriptionTitle: The shift on the category of triangles
nodes.description: In this file, it is shown that if C is a preadditive category with a shift by ℤ, then the category of triangles Triangle C is also endowed with a shift. We also show that rotating triangles three times identifies with the shift by 1.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Triangulated
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of triangulated categories, which are pretriangulated categories which satisfy the octahedron axiom.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.Yoneda
nodes.description: Let C be a pretriangulated category. In this file, we show that the functors preadditiveCoyoneda.obj A : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat for A : Cᵒᵖ and preadditiveYoneda.obj B : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat for B : C are homological functors.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Types.Basic
nodes.description: In this section we define a LargeCategory structure on Type u, in such a way that it becomes a ConcreteCategory.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Types.Epimorphisms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stability properties of epimorphisms in Type
nodes.description: In this file, we show that in the category Type u, epimorphisms are stable under base change.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Types.Monomorphisms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stability properties of monomorphisms in Type
nodes.description: In this file, we show that in the category Type u, monomorphisms are stable under cobase change, filtered colimits. After importing Mathlib/CategoryTheory/MorphismProperty/TransfiniteComposition.lean, the fact that monomorphisms are stable under transfinite composition will also be inferred automatically.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Types.Set
nodes.descriptionTitle: The functor from Set X to types
nodes.description: Given X : Type u, we define the functor Set.functorToTypes : Set X ⥤ Type u which sends A : Set X to its underlying type.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.UnivLE
nodes.descriptionTitle: Universe inequalities and essential surjectivity of uliftFunctor.
nodes.description: We show UnivLE.{max u v, v} ↔ EssSurj (uliftFunctor.{u, v} : Type v ⥤ Type max u v).

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Whiskering
nodes.description: Given a functor F : C ⥤ D and functors G H : D ⥤ E and a natural transformation α : G ⟶ H, we can construct a new natural transformation F ⋙ G ⟶ F ⋙ H, called whiskerLeft F α. This is the same as the horizontal composition of 𝟙 F with α.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Widesubcategory
nodes.description: A wide subcategory of a category C is a subcategory containing all the objects of C.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.WithTerminal.Basic
nodes.description: Given a category C, this file constructs two objects: 1. WithTerminal C, the category built from C by formally adjoining a terminal object. 2. WithInitial C, the category built from C by formally adjoining an initial object.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.WithTerminal.Cone
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relations between Cone, WithTerminal and Over
nodes.description: Given categories C and J, an object X : C and a functor K : J ⥤ Over X, it has an obvious lift liftFromOver K : WithTerminal J ⥤ C, namely, send the terminal object to X. These two functors have equivalent categories of cones (coneEquiv). As a corollary, the limit of K is the limit of liftFromOver K, and vice-versa.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.WithTerminal.FinCategory
nodes.descriptionTitle: WithTerminal C and WithInitial C are finite whenever C is
nodes.description: If C has finitely many objects, then so do WithTerminal C and WithInitial C, and likewise if C has finitely many morphisms as well.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.WithTerminal.Lemmas
nodes.description: These lemmas and instances need more imports.

nodes.label: CategoryTheory.Yoneda
nodes.description: Let C : Type u₁ be a category (with Category.{v₁} C). We define the Yoneda embedding as a fully faithful functor yoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁, In addition to yoneda, we also define uliftYoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w v₁) with the additional universe parameter w. When C is locally w-small, one may also use shrinkYoneda.{w} : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w from the file Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ShrinkYoneda.lean.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.AP.Three.Behrend
nodes.description: This file proves Behrend's lower bound on Roth numbers. This says that we can find a subset of {1, ..., n} of size n / exp (O (sqrt (log n))) which does not contain arithmetic progressions of length 3.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.AP.Three.Defs
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sets without arithmetic progressions of length three and Roth numbers
nodes.description: This file defines sets without arithmetic progressions of length three, aka 3AP-free sets, and the Roth number of a set.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.ApproximateSubgroup
nodes.description: This file defines approximate subgroups of a group, namely symmetric sets A such that A A can be covered by a small number of translates of A.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.CauchyDavenport
nodes.description: This file proves a generalisation of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem to arbitrary groups.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Convolution
nodes.description: This file defines convolution of finite subsets A and B of group G as the map A ⋆ B : G → ℕ that maps x ∈ G to the number of distinct representations of x in the form x = ab for a ∈ A, b ∈ B. It is shown how convolution behaves under the change of order of A and B, as well as under the left and right actions on A, B, and the function argument.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Corner.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines corners, namely triples of the form (x, y), (x, y + d), (x + d, y), and the property of being corner-free.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Corner.Roth
nodes.descriptionTitle: The corners theorem and Roth's theorem
nodes.description: This file proves the corners theorem and Roth's theorem on arithmetic progressions of length three.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.CovBySMul
nodes.description: This file defines a predicate for a set to be covered by at most K cosets of another set.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Dissociation
nodes.description: This file defines dissociation and span of sets in groups. These are analogs to the usual linear independence and linear span of sets in a vector space but where the scalars are only allowed to be 0 or ±1. In characteristic 2 or 3, the two pairs of concepts are actually equivalent.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.DoublingConst
nodes.description: This file defines the doubling and difference constants of two finsets in a group.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.ETransform
nodes.description: e-transforms are a family of transformations of pairs of finite sets that aim to reduce the size of the sumset while keeping some invariant the same. This file defines a few of them, to be used as internals of other proofs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Energy
nodes.description: This file defines the additive energy of two finsets of a group. This is a central quantity in additive combinatorics.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.ErdosGinzburgZiv
nodes.description: This file proves the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv theorem as a corollary of Chevalley-Warning. This theorem states that among any (not necessarily distinct) 2 n - 1 elements of ZMod n, we can find n elements of sum zero.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.FreimanHom
nodes.description: In this file, we define Freiman homomorphisms and isomorphisms.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.PluenneckeRuzsa
nodes.description: This file proves Ruzsa's triangle inequality, the Plünnecke-Petridis lemma, and the Plünnecke-Ruzsa inequality.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.Randomisation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Randomising by a function of dissociated support
nodes.description: This file proves that a function from a finite abelian group can be randomised by a function of dissociated support.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.RuzsaCovering
nodes.description: This file proves the Ruzsa covering lemma. This says that, for A, B finsets, we can cover A with at most #(A + B) / #B copies of B - B.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.SmallTripling
nodes.description: This file shows that a set with small tripling has small powers, even in non-abelian groups.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.SubsetSum
nodes.description: This file defines the subset sum of a finite subset of a commutative monoid.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Additive.VerySmallDoubling
nodes.description: For a finset A in a group, its doubling is #(A A) / #A. This file characterises sets with For the converse, use the existing facts from the pointwise API: ∅ ^ 2 = ∅ (Finset.empty_pow), (a • H) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 • H ^ 2 = a ^ 2 • H (smul_pow, coe_set_pow). size strictly less than 3 / 2 #A. constant (depending only on the doubling) number of cosets of a finite subgroup of G.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Colex
nodes.description: We define the colex order for finite sets, and give a couple of important lemmas and properties relating to it.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Compactness
nodes.descriptionTitle: Combinatorial compactness and the Rado selection lemma
nodes.description: This file contains compactness arguments for constructing infinite objects from finite approximations. The main result is a formalization of Rado's selection principle, as an application of compactness to combinatorics.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Configuration
nodes.description: This file introduces abstract configurations of points and lines, and proves some basic properties.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Derangements.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define derangements α, the set of derangements on a type α.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Derangements.Exponential
nodes.description: This file proves that the probability of a permutation on n elements being a derangement is 1/e. The specific lemma is numDerangements_tendsto_inv_e.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Derangements.Finite
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas that describe the cardinality of derangements α when α is a fintype.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Digraph.Basic
nodes.description: This module defines directed graphs on a vertex type V, which is the same notion as a relation V → V → Prop. While this might be too simple of a notion to deserve the grandeur of a new definition, the intention here is to develop relations using the language of graph theory.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Digraph.Orientation
nodes.description: This module introduces conversion operations between Digraphs and SimpleGraphs, by forgetting the edge orientations of Digraph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Bell
nodes.description: For n : ℕ, the nth Bell number is the number of partitions of a set of cardinality n. Here, we define a refinement of these numbers, that count, for any m : Multiset ℕ, the number of partitions of a set of cardinality m.sum whose parts have cardinalities given by m.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Catalan
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Combinatorics.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Catalan.Basic
nodes.description: The Catalan numbers (http://oeis.org/A000108) are probably the most ubiquitous sequence of integers in mathematics. They enumerate several important objects like binary trees, Dyck paths, and triangulations of convex polygons.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Catalan.Tree
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Combinatorics.Enumerative.Catalan.Tree.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Composition
nodes.description: A composition of a natural number n is a decomposition n = i₀ + ... + i_{k-1} of n into a sum of positive integers. Combinatorially, it corresponds to a decomposition of {0, ..., n-1} into non-empty blocks of consecutive integers, where the iⱼ are the lengths of the blocks. This notion is closely related to that of a partition of n, but in a composition of n the order of the iⱼs matters.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.DoubleCounting
nodes.description: This file gathers a few double counting arguments.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.DyckWord
nodes.description: A Dyck word is a sequence consisting of an equal number n of symbols of two types such that for all prefixes one symbol occurs at least as many times as the other. If the symbols are ( and ) the latter restriction is equivalent to balanced brackets; if they are U = (1, 1) and D = (1, -1) the sequence is a lattice path from (0, 0) to (0, 2n) and the restriction requires the path to never go below the x-axis.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.IncidenceAlgebra
nodes.description: Given a locally finite order α the incidence algebra over α is the type of functions from non-empty intervals of α to some algebraic codomain.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.InclusionExclusion
nodes.description: This file proves several variants of the inclusion-exclusion principle.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Partition
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Combinatorics.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Partition.Basic
nodes.description: A partition of a natural number n is a way of writing n as a sum of positive integers, where the order does not matter: two sums that differ only in the order of their summands are considered the same partition. This notion is closely related to that of a composition of n, but in a composition of n the order does matter. A summand of the partition is called a part.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Partition.GenFun
nodes.description: This file defines generating functions related to partitions. Given a character function $f(i, c)$ of a part $i$ and the number of occurrences of the part $c$, the related generating function is $$ G_f(X) = \sum_{n = 0}^{\infty} \left(\sum_{p \in P_{n}} \prod_{i \in p} f(i, \#i)\right) X^n = \prod_{i = 1}^{\infty}\left(1 + \sum_{j = 1}^{\infty} f(i, j) X^{ij}\right) $$ where $P_n$ is all partitions of $n$, $\#i$ is the count of $i$ in the partition $p$.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Partition.Glaisher
nodes.description: This file proves Glaisher's theorem: the number of partitions of an integer $n$ into parts not divisible by $d$ is equal to the number of partitions in which no part is repeated $d$ or more times.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Pentagonal
nodes.description: This file introduces (generalized) pentagonal numbers $k(3k-1)/2$ for integer $k$.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Schroder
nodes.description: The Schröder numbers (https://oeis.org/A006318) are a sequence of integers that appear in various combinatorial contexts.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Enumerative.Stirling
nodes.description: This file defines Stirling numbers of the first and second kinds, proves their fundamental recurrence relations, and establishes some of their key properties and identities.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Extremal.RuzsaSzemeredi
nodes.description: This file proves the lower bound of the Ruzsa-Szemerédi problem. The problem is to find the maximum number of edges that a graph on n vertices can have if all edges belong to at most one triangle.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Graph.Basic
nodes.description: A multigraph is a set of vertices and a set of edges, together with incidence data that associates each edge e with an unordered pair s(x,y) of vertices called the ends of e. The pair of e and s(x,y) is called a link. The vertices x and y may be equal, in which case e is a loop. There may be more than one edge with the same ends.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Graph.Delete
nodes.description: This file defines the deletion of edges and vertices from a graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Graph.Lattice
nodes.description: This file defines the lattice-like structures on graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Graph.Maps
nodes.description: This file defines vertex map between graphs Graph α β. Morphisms between graphs will also be defined in this file in the future.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Graph.Subgraph
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of subgraphs for multigraphs Graph α β: the subgraph relation, standard classes of subgraphs (spanning, induced, closed), and the bottom element ⊥.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.HalesJewett
nodes.description: We prove the Hales-Jewett theorem. We deduce Van der Waerden's theorem and the multidimensional Hales-Jewett theorem as corollaries.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Hall.Basic
nodes.description: Given a list of finite subsets $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ of some given set $S$, P. Hall in [Hall1935] gave a necessary and sufficient condition for there to be a list of distinct elements $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ with $x_i\in X_i$ for each $i$: it is when for each $k$, the union of every $k$ of these subsets has at least $k$ elements.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Hall.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Hall's Marriage Theorem for finite index types
nodes.description: This module proves the basic form of Hall's theorem. In contrast to the theorem described in Combinatorics.Hall.Basic, this version requires that the indexed family t : ι → Finset α have ι be finite. The Combinatorics.Hall.Basic module applies a compactness argument to this version to remove the Finite constraint on ι.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Hindman
nodes.description: We prove Hindman's theorem on finite sums, using idempotent ultrafilters.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.KatonaCircle
nodes.description: This file provides tooling to use the Katona circle method, which is double-counting ways to order n elements on a circle under some condition.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Basic
nodes.description: A Matroid is a structure that combinatorially abstracts the notion of linear independence and dependence; matroids have connections with graph theory, discrete optimization, additive combinatorics and algebraic geometry. Mathematically, a matroid M is a structure on a set E comprising a collection of subsets of E called the bases of M, where the bases are required to obey certain axioms.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Circuit
nodes.description: A 'Circuit' of a matroid M is a minimal set C that is dependent in M. A matroid is determined by its set of circuits, and often the circuits offer a more compact description of a matroid than the collection of independent sets or bases. In matroids arising from graphs, circuits correspond to graphical cycles.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Closure
nodes.description: A flat (IsFlat) of a matroid M is a combinatorial analogue of a subspace of a vector space, and is defined to be a subset F of the ground set of M such that for each basis I for F, every set having I as a basis is contained in F.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Constructions
nodes.description: This file defines some very elementary examples of matroids, namely those with at most one base.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Dual
nodes.description: For a matroid M on ground set E, the collection of complements of the bases of M is the collection of bases of another matroid on E called the 'dual' of M. The map from M to its dual is an involution, interacts nicely with minors, and preserves many important matroid properties such as representability and connectivity.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.IndepAxioms
nodes.description: Matroids in mathlib are defined axiomatically in terms of bases, but can be described just as naturally via their collections of independent sets, and in fact such a description, being more 'verbose', can often be useful. As well as this, the definition of a Matroid uses an unwieldy 'maximality' axiom that can be dropped in cases where there is some finiteness assumption.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Init
nodes.description: This module defines the Matroid Aesop rule set which is used by the aesop_mat tactic. Aesop rule sets only become visible once the file in which they're declared is imported, so we must put this declaration into its own file.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Loop
nodes.description: A 'loop' of a matroid M is an element e satisfying one of the following equivalent conditions:

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Map
nodes.description: This file defines maps and comaps, which move a matroid on one type to a matroid on another using a function between the types. The constructions are (up to isomorphism) just combinations of restrictions and parallel extensions, so are not mathematically difficult.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Minor.Contract
nodes.description: Instead of deleting the elements of X : Set α from M : Matroid α, we can contract them. The contraction of X from M, denoted M ／ X, is the matroid on ground set M.E \ X in which a set I is independent if and only if I ∪ J is independent in M, where J is an arbitrarily chosen basis for X. Contraction corresponds to contracting edges in graphic matroids (hence the name) and corresponds to projecting to a quotient space in the case of linearly representable matroids. It is an important notion in both these settings.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Minor.Delete
nodes.description: For M : Matroid α and X : Set α, the deletion of X from M is the matroid M ＼ X with ground set M.E \ X, in which a subset of M.E \ X is independent if and only if it is independent in M.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Minor.Order
nodes.description: A matroid N = M ／ C ＼ D obtained from a matroid M by a contraction then a delete, (or equivalently, by any number of contractions/deletions in any order) is a minor of M. This gives a partial order on Matroid α that is ubiquitous in matroid theory, and interacts nicely with duality and linear representations.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Minor.Restrict
nodes.description: Given M : Matroid α and R : Set α, the independent sets of M that are contained in R are the independent sets of another matroid M ↾ R with ground set R, called the 'restriction' of M to R. For I ⊆ R ⊆ M.E, I is a basis of R in M if and only if I is a base of the restriction M ↾ R, so this construction relates Matroid.IsBasis to Matroid.IsBase.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Rank.Cardinal
nodes.description: In a finitary matroid, all bases have the same cardinality. In fact, something stronger holds: if each of I and J is a basis for a set X, then #(I \ J) = #(J \ I) and (consequently) #I = #J. This file introduces a typeclass InvariantCardinalRank that applies to any matroid such that this property holds for all I, J and X.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Rank.ENat
nodes.description: If the 'cardinality' of s : Set α is taken to mean the ℕ∞-valued term Set.encard s, then all bases of any M : Matroid α have the same cardinality, and for each X : Set α with X ⊆ M.E, all M-bases for X have the same cardinality. The 'rank' of a matroid is the cardinality of all its bases, and the 'rank' of a set X in a matroid M is the cardinality of each M-basis of X. This file defines these two concepts as a term Matroid.eRank M : ℕ∞ and a function Matroid.eRk M : Set α → ℕ∞ respectively.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Rank.Finite
nodes.description: Matroid.IsRkFinite M X means that every basis of the set X in the matroid M is finite, or equivalently that the restriction of M to X is Matroid.RankFinite. Sets in a matroid with IsRkFinite are the largest class of sets for which one can do nontrivial integer arithmetic involving the rank function.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Matroid.Sum
nodes.description: The sum M of a collection M₁, M₂, .. of matroids is a matroid on the disjoint union of the ground sets of the summands, in which the independent sets are precisely the unions of independent sets of the summands.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Nullstellensatz
nodes.description: This is a formalization of Noga Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz. It follows [Alon_1999].

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Optimization.ValuedCSP
nodes.description: General-Valued CSP is a very broad class of problems in discrete optimization. General-Valued CSP subsumes Min-Cost-Hom (including 3-SAT for example) and Finite-Valued CSP.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Pigeonhole
nodes.description: Given pigeons (possibly infinitely many) in pigeonholes, the pigeonhole principle states that, if there are more pigeons than pigeonholes, then there is a pigeonhole with two or more pigeons.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Arborescence
nodes.description: A quiver V is an arborescence (or directed rooted tree) when we have a root vertex root : V such that for every b : V there is a unique path from root to b.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Basic
nodes.description: This module defines quivers. A quiver on a type V of vertices assigns to every pair a b : V of vertices a type a ⟶ b of arrows from a to b. This is a generalization of Digraph V, which can be thought of as "a proposition a ⟶ b of arrows".

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Cast
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rewriting arrows and paths along vertex equalities
nodes.description: This file defines Hom.cast and Path.cast (and associated lemmas) in order to allow rewriting arrows and paths along equalities of their endpoints.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.ConnectedComponent
nodes.description: For a quiver V, define the type WeaklyConnectedComponent V as the quotient of V by the relation which identifies a with b if there is a path from a to b in Symmetrify V. (These zigzags can be seen as a proof-relevant analogue of EqvGen.)

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Covering
nodes.description: This file defines coverings of quivers as prefunctors that are bijective on the so-called stars and costars at each vertex of the domain.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Path
nodes.description: Given a quiver V, we define the type of paths from a : V to b : V as an inductive family. We define composition of paths and the action of prefunctors on paths.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Path.Decomposition
nodes.description: This section provides lemmas for decomposing non-empty paths and for reasoning about paths that cross the boundary of a given set of vertices S.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Path.Vertices
nodes.description: This file provides lemmas for reasoning about the vertices of a path.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Path.Weight
nodes.description: This file defines the weight of a path in a quiver. The weight of a path is the product of the weights of its edges, where weights are taken from a monoid.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Prefunctor
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Combinatorics.Quiver.Prefunctor.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Push
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pushing a quiver structure along a map
nodes.description: Given a map σ : V → W and a Quiver instance on V, this file defines a Quiver instance on W by associating to each arrow v ⟶ v' in V an arrow σ v ⟶ σ v' in W.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.ReflQuiver
nodes.description: This module defines reflexive quivers. A reflexive quiver, or "refl quiver" for short, extends a quiver with a specified endoarrow on each term in its type of objects.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Schreier
nodes.description: This module defines Schreier graphs as quivers with labelled edges.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.SingleObj
nodes.description: Single object quiver with a given arrows type.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Subquiver
nodes.description: A wide subquiver H of a quiver H consists of a subset of the edge set a ⟶ b for every pair of vertices a b : V. We include 'wide' in the name to emphasize that these subquivers by definition contain all vertices.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Quiver.Symmetric
nodes.description: This file contains constructions related to symmetric quivers:

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Schnirelmann
nodes.description: We define the Schnirelmann density of a set A of natural numbers as $inf_{n > 0} |A ∩ {1,...,n}| / n$. As this density is very sensitive to changes in small values, we must exclude 0 from the infimum, and from the intersection.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.AhlswedeZhang
nodes.description: This file proves the Ahlswede-Zhang identity, which is a nontrivial relation between the size of the "truncated unions" of a set family. It sharpens the Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality Finset.lubell_yamamoto_meshalkin_inequality_sum_card_div_choose, by making explicit the correction term.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Compression.Down
nodes.description: This file defines down-compression.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Compression.UV
nodes.description: This file defines UV-compression. It is an operation on a set family that reduces its shadow.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.FourFunctions
nodes.descriptionTitle: The four functions theorem and corollaries
nodes.description: This file proves the four functions theorem. The statement is that if f₁ a f₂ b ≤ f₃ (a ⊓ b) f₄ (a ⊔ b) for all a, b in a finite distributive lattice, then (∑ x ∈ s, f₁ x) (∑ x ∈ t, f₂ x) ≤ (∑ x ∈ s ⊼ t, f₃ x) (∑ x ∈ s ⊻ t, f₄ x) where s ⊼ t = {a ⊓ b | a ∈ s, b ∈ t}, s ⊻ t = {a ⊔ b | a ∈ s, b ∈ t}.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.HarrisKleitman
nodes.description: This file proves the Harris-Kleitman inequality. This relates #𝒜 #ℬ and 2 ^ card α #(𝒜 ∩ ℬ) where 𝒜 and ℬ are upward- or downcard-closed finite families of finsets. This can be interpreted as saying that any two lower sets (resp. any two upper sets) correlate in the uniform measure.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Intersecting
nodes.description: This file defines intersecting families and proves their basic properties.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Kleitman
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kleitman's bound on the size of intersecting families
nodes.description: An intersecting family on n elements has size at most 2ⁿ⁻¹, so we could naïvely think that two intersecting families could cover all 2ⁿ sets. But actually that's not case because for example none of them can contain the empty set. Intersecting families are in some sense correlated. Kleitman's bound stipulates that k intersecting families cover at most 2ⁿ - 2ⁿ⁻ᵏ sets.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.KruskalKatona
nodes.description: This file proves the Kruskal-Katona theorem. This is a sharp statement about how many sets of size k - 1 are covered by a family of sets of size k, given only its size.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.LYM
nodes.description: This file proves the local LYM and LYM inequalities as well as Sperner's theorem.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Shadow
nodes.description: This file defines shadows of a set family. The shadow of a set family is the set family of sets we get by removing any element from any set of the original family. If one pictures Finset α as a big hypercube (each dimension being membership of a given element), then taking the shadow corresponds to projecting each finset down once in all available directions.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SetFamily.Shatter
nodes.description: This file defines the shattering property and VC-dimension of set families.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
nodes.description: This module introduces acyclic graphs (a.k.a. forests) and trees.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.AdjMatrix
nodes.description: This module defines the adjacency matrix of a graph, and provides theorems connecting graph properties to computational properties of the matrix.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
nodes.description: This module defines simple graphs on a vertex type V as an irreflexive symmetric relation.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Bipartite
nodes.description: This file proves results about bipartite simple graphs, including several double-counting arguments.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Cayley
nodes.description: This file defines and proves several fact about Cayley graphs. A Cayley graph over type M with generators s : Set M is a graph in which two vertices u ≠ v are adjacent if and only if there is some g ∈ s such that u g = v or v g = u. The elements of s are called generators.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Circulant
nodes.description: This file defines and proves several fact about circulant graphs. A circulant graph over type G with jumps s : Set G is a graph in which two vertices u and v are adjacent if and only if u - v ∈ s or v - u ∈ s. The elements of s are called jumps.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
nodes.description: This file defines cliques in simple graphs. A clique is a set of vertices that are pairwise adjacent.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.Constructions
nodes.description: This file defines colorings for some common graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.EdgeLabeling
nodes.description: This module defines labelings of the edges of a graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Coloring.VertexColoring
nodes.description: This module defines colorings of simple graphs (also known as proper colorings in the literature). A graph coloring is the attribution of "colors" to all of its vertices such that adjacent vertices have different colors. A coloring can be represented as a homomorphism into a complete graph, whose vertices represent the colors.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.CompleteMultipartite
nodes.description: A graph is complete multipartite iff non-adjacency is transitive.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected
nodes.description: a walk between a given pair of vertices

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.EdgeConnectivity
nodes.description: This file defines k-edge-connectivity for simple graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Counting walks of a given length
nodes.description: from u to v and common neighbours of u and v. Note that u and v may be the same. This is used to give {p : G.walk u v | p.length = n} a Fintype instance, and it can also be useful as a recursive description of this set when V is finite.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Represents
nodes.descriptionTitle: Representation of components by a set of vertices
nodes.description: components if it contains exactly one vertex from each component.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Subgraph
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connectivity of subgraphs and induced graphs
nodes.description: connectivity predicates via SimpleGraph.Subgraph.coe.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Copy
nodes.description: This file introduces the concept of one simple graph containing a copy of another.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Dart
nodes.description: A Dart or half-edge or bond in a graph is an ordered pair of adjacent vertices, regarded as an oriented edge. This file defines darts and proves some of their basic properties.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.DegreeSum
nodes.description: The degree-sum formula is that the sum of the degrees of the vertices in a finite graph is equal to twice the number of edges. The handshaking lemma, a corollary, is that the number of odd-degree vertices is even.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.DeleteEdges
nodes.description: This file defines operations deleting the edges of a simple graph and proves theorems in the finite case.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Density
nodes.description: This file defines the number and density of edges of a relation/graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Diam
nodes.description: This module defines the eccentricity of vertices, the diameter, and the radius of a simple graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Ends.Defs
nodes.description: This file contains a definition of the ends of a simple graph, as sections of the inverse system assigning, to each finite set of vertices, the connected components of its complement.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Ends.Properties
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of the ends of graphs
nodes.description: This file is meant to contain results about the ends of (locally finite connected) graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Extremal.Basic
nodes.description: This file introduces basic definitions for extremal graph theory, including extremal numbers.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Extremal.Turan
nodes.description: In this file we prove Turán's theorem, the first important result of extremal graph theory, which states that the r + 1-cliquefree graph on n vertices with the most edges is the complete r-partite graph with part sizes as equal as possible (turanGraph n r).

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Extremal.TuranDensity
nodes.description: This file defines the Turán density of a simple graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definitions for finite and locally finite graphs
nodes.description: This file defines finite versions of edgeSet, neighborSet and incidenceSet and proves some of their basic properties. It also defines the notion of a locally finite graph, which is one whose vertices have finite degree.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finsubgraph
nodes.description: This file defines the type of finite subgraphs of a SimpleGraph and proves a compactness result for homomorphisms to a finite codomain.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.FiveWheelLike
nodes.description: This file defines an IsFiveWheelLike structure in a graph, and describes properties of these structures as well as graphs which avoid this structure. These have two key uses: complete-multipartite: colorable_iff_isCompleteMultipartite_of_maximal_cliqueFree. first appeared. We give this proof below, see colorable_of_cliqueFree_lt_minDegree.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Girth
nodes.description: This file defines the girth and the extended girth of a simple graph as the length of its smallest cycle, they give 0 or ∞ respectively if the graph is acyclic.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Hall
nodes.description: This file derives Hall's Marriage Theorem for bipartite graphs from the combinatorial formulation in Mathlib/Combinatorics/Hall/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Hamiltonian
nodes.description: In this file we introduce Hamiltonian paths, cycles and graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Hasse
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Hasse diagram as a graph
nodes.description: This file defines the Hasse diagram of an order (graph of CovBy, the covering relation) and the path graph on n vertices.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.IncMatrix
nodes.descriptionTitle: Incidence matrix of a simple graph
nodes.description: This file defines the unoriented incidence matrix of a simple graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Init
nodes.description: This module defines the SimpleGraph Aesop rule set which is used by the aesop_graph tactic. Aesop rule sets only become visible once the file in which they're declared is imported, so we must put this declaration into its own file.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.LapMatrix
nodes.description: This module defines the Laplacian matrix of a graph, and proves some of its elementary properties.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.LineGraph
nodes.description: and two vertices of the line graph adjacent if the corresponding edges share a vertex in G.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps
nodes.description: This file defines two functions and three structures relating graphs. The structures directly correspond to the classification of functions as injective, surjective and bijective, and have corresponding notation.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Matching
nodes.description: A matching for a simple graph is a set of disjoint pairs of adjacent vertices, and the set of all the vertices in a matching is called its support (and sometimes the vertices in the support are said to be saturated by the matching). A perfect matching is a matching whose support contains every vertex of the graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric
nodes.description: This module defines the SimpleGraph.edist function, which takes pairs of vertices to the length of the shortest walk between them, or ⊤ if they are disconnected. It also defines SimpleGraph.dist which is the ℕ-valued version of SimpleGraph.edist, and SimpleGraph.ball which is the open ball in the graph extended metric.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Operations
nodes.description: This file defines some single-graph operations that modify a finite number of vertices and proves basic theorems about them. When the graph itself has a finite number of vertices we also prove theorems about the number of edges in the modified graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Partition
nodes.description: This module provides an interface for dealing with partitions on simple graphs. A partition of a graph G, with vertices V, is a set P of disjoint nonempty subsets of V such that:

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Paths
nodes.description: same and whose vertices except for the first appear no more than once.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Prod
nodes.description: This file defines the box product of graphs and other product constructions. The box product of G and H is the graph on the product of the vertices such that x and y are related iff they agree on one component and the other one is related via either G or H. For example, the box product of two edges is a square.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Bound
nodes.descriptionTitle: Numerical bounds for Szemerédi Regularity Lemma
nodes.description: This file gathers the numerical facts required by the proof of Szemerédi's regularity lemma.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Chunk
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chunk of the increment partition for Szemerédi Regularity Lemma
nodes.description: In the proof of Szemerédi Regularity Lemma, we need to partition each part of a starting partition to increase the energy. This file defines those partitions of parts and shows that they locally increase the energy.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Energy
nodes.description: This file defines the energy of a partition.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Equitabilise
nodes.description: This file allows to blow partitions up into parts of controlled size. Given a partition P and a b m : ℕ, we want to find a partition Q with a parts of size m and b parts of size m + 1 such that all parts of P are "as close as possible" to unions of parts of Q. By "as close as possible", we mean that each part of P can be written as the union of some parts of Q along with at most m other elements.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Increment
nodes.descriptionTitle: Increment partition for Szemerédi Regularity Lemma
nodes.description: In the proof of Szemerédi Regularity Lemma, we need to partition each part of a starting partition to increase the energy. This file defines the partition obtained by gluing the parts partitions together (the increment partition) and shows that the energy globally increases.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Lemma
nodes.description: In this file, we prove Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma (aka SRL). This is a landmark result in combinatorics roughly stating that any sufficiently big graph behaves like a random graph. This is useful because random graphs are well-behaved in many aspects.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Regularity.Uniform
nodes.description: In this file we define uniformity of a pair of vertices in a graph and uniformity of a partition of vertices of a graph. Both are also known as ε-regularity.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.StronglyRegular
nodes.description: a SimpleGraph satisfying the following conditions:

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Subgraph
nodes.description: A subgraph of a simple graph consists of subsets of the graph's vertices and edges such that the endpoints of each edge are present in the vertex subset. The edge subset is formalized as a sub-relation of the adjacency relation of the simple graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Sum
nodes.description: This file defines the disjoint sum of graphs. The disjoint sum of G : SimpleGraph V and H : SimpleGraph W is a graph on V ⊕ W where u and v are adjacent if and only if they are both in G and adjacent in G, or they are both in H and adjacent in H.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Trails
nodes.description: This module contains additional theory about trails, including Eulerian trails (also known as Eulerian circuits).

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Triangle.Basic
nodes.description: A triangle in a simple graph is a 3-clique, namely a set of three vertices that are pairwise adjacent.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Triangle.Counting
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the triangle counting lemma.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Triangle.Removal
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the triangle removal lemma.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Triangle.Tripartite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Construct a tripartite graph from its triangles
nodes.description: This file contains the construction of a simple graph on α ⊕ β ⊕ γ from a list of triangles (a, b, c) (with a in the first component, b in the second, c in the third).

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Tutte
nodes.description: odd components left after deleting u from G is larger than the number of vertices in u. This certifies non-existence of a perfect matching.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.UnitDistance.Basic
nodes.description: An embedding of a graph into some metric space is _unit-distance_ if the distance between any two adjacent vertices is 1. The space in question is usually the Euclidean plane, but can also be higher-dimensional Euclidean space or the sphere (cf. [Frankl_2020]). We do not require nonadjacent vertices to not be distance 1 apart as [hong2014] does.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.UniversalVerts
nodes.description: This file defines the set of universal vertices: those vertices that are connected to all others. In addition, it describes results when considering connected components of the graph where universal vertices are deleted. This particular graph plays a role in the proof of Tutte's Theorem.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.VertexCover
nodes.description: A vertex cover of a simple graph is a set of vertices such that every edge is incident to at least one of the vertices in the set.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Combinatorics.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Basic
nodes.description: In a simple graph, a walk is a finite sequence of adjacent vertices, and can be thought of equally well as a sequence of directed edges.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Chord
nodes.description: This file defines chords and chordless walks in a simple graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Counting
nodes.descriptionTitle: Counting walks of a given length
nodes.description: from u to v and common neighbours of u and v. Note that u and v may be the same. This is used to give {p : G.walk u v | p.length = n} a Fintype instance, and it can also be useful as a recursive description of this set when V is finite.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Decomp
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Decomp.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Maps
nodes.description: Functions that map walks between different graphs.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Operations
nodes.description: Operations on walks that produce a new walk in the same graph.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Subwalks
nodes.description: We define a relation on walks stating that one walk is the subwalk of another.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walk.Traversal
nodes.description: Functions that help access different parts of a walk.

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Tiling.Tile
nodes.description: This file defines some basic concepts related to individual tiles for tilings in a discrete context (with definitions in a continuous context to be developed separately but analogously).

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Young.SemistandardTableau
nodes.description: A semistandard Young tableau is a filling of a Young diagram by natural numbers, such that the entries are weakly increasing left-to-right along rows (i.e. for fixed i), and strictly-increasing top-to-bottom along columns (i.e. for fixed j).

nodes.label: Combinatorics.Young.YoungDiagram
nodes.description: A Young diagram is a finite set of up-left justified boxes:

nodes.label: Computability.Ackermann
nodes.description: In this file, we define the two-argument Ackermann function ack. Despite having a recursive definition, we show that this isn't a primitive recursive function.

nodes.label: Computability.AkraBazzi.AkraBazzi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Divide-and-conquer recurrences and the Akra-Bazzi theorem
nodes.description: A divide-and-conquer recurrence is a function T : ℕ → ℝ that satisfies a recurrence relation of the form T(n) = ∑_{i=0}^{k-1} a_i T(r_i(n)) + g(n) for sufficiently large n, where r_i(n) is a function such that ‖r_i(n) - b_i n‖ ∈ o(n / (log n)^2) for every i, the coefficients a_i are positive, and the coefficients b_i are real numbers in (0, 1).

nodes.label: Computability.AkraBazzi.GrowsPolynomially
nodes.descriptionTitle: Akra-Bazzi theorem: the polynomial growth condition
nodes.description: This file defines and develops an API for the polynomial growth condition that appears in the statement of the Akra-Bazzi theorem: for the theorem to hold, the function g must satisfy the condition that c₁ g(n) ≤ g(u) ≤ c₂ g(n), for u between bn and n for any constant b ∈ (0,1).

nodes.label: Computability.AkraBazzi.SumTransform
nodes.description: We develop further preliminaries required for the theorem, up to the sum transform.

nodes.label: Computability.ContextFreeGrammar
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of a context-free grammar, which is a grammar that has a single nonterminal symbol on the left-hand side of each rule.

nodes.label: Computability.DFA
nodes.description: A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) is a state machine which decides membership in a particular Language, by following a path uniquely determined by an input string.

nodes.label: Computability.Encoding
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of a (finite) encoding, a map from a type to strings in an alphabet, used in defining computability by Turing machines. It also contains several examples:

nodes.label: Computability.EpsilonNFA
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of an epsilon Nondeterministic Finite Automaton (εNFA), a state machine which determines whether a string (implemented as a list over an arbitrary alphabet) is in a regular set by evaluating the string over every possible path, also having access to ε-transitions, which can be followed without reading a character. Since this definition allows for automata with infinite states, a Fintype instance must be supplied for true εNFA's.

nodes.label: Computability.Halting
nodes.descriptionTitle: Computability theory and the halting problem
nodes.description: A universal partial recursive function, Rice's theorem, and the halting problem.

nodes.label: Computability.Language
nodes.description: This file contains the definition and operations on formal languages over an alphabet. Note that "strings" are implemented as lists over the alphabet.

nodes.label: Computability.MyhillNerode
nodes.description: This file proves the Myhill–Nerode theorem using left quotients.

nodes.label: Computability.NFA
nodes.description: A Nondeterministic Finite Automaton (NFA) is a state machine which decides membership in a particular Language, by following every possible path that describes an input string.

nodes.label: Computability.Partrec
nodes.description: The partial recursive functions are defined similarly to the primitive recursive functions, but now all functions are partial, implemented using the Part monad, and there is an additional operation, called μ-recursion, which performs unbounded minimization: μ f returns the least natural number n for which f n = 0, or diverges if such n doesn't exist.

nodes.label: Computability.PartrecBasis
nodes.descriptionTitle: A simplified basis for partial recursive functions
nodes.description: This file defines Nat.Partrec', an inductive predicate that provides an alternative, structural basis for partial recursive functions using vectors. It establishes the equivalence between this vector-based definition and the standard Partrec definition.

nodes.label: Computability.PartrecCode
nodes.descriptionTitle: Gödel Numbering for Partial Recursive Functions.
nodes.description: This file defines Nat.Partrec.Code, an inductive datatype describing code for partial recursive functions on ℕ. It defines an encoding for these codes, and proves that the constructors are primitive recursive with respect to the encoding.

nodes.label: Computability.PostTuringMachine
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.Primrec
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.Primrec.Basic
nodes.description: The primitive recursive functions are the least collection of functions ℕ → ℕ which are closed under projections (using the pair pairing function), composition, zero, successor, and primitive recursion (i.e. Nat.rec where the motive is C n := ℕ).

nodes.label: Computability.Primrec.List
nodes.description: The primitive recursive functions are defined in Mathlib.Computability.Primrec.Basic. This file contains definitions and theorems about primitive recursive functions that relate to operation on lists.

nodes.label: Computability.RE
nodes.description: This file defines computable (ComputablePred) and recursively enumerable (REPred) predicates. It also provides basic closure properties and Post's theorem on the equivalence of recursive, r.e., and co-r.e. sets.

nodes.label: Computability.RecursiveIn
nodes.description: This file defines oracle computability using partial recursive functions.

nodes.label: Computability.Reduce
nodes.description: This file defines the notions of computable many-one reduction and one-one reduction between sets, and shows that the corresponding degrees form a semilattice.

nodes.label: Computability.RegularExpressions
nodes.description: This file contains the formal definition for regular expressions and basic lemmas. Note these are regular expressions in terms of formal language theory. Note this is different to regexes used in computer science such as the POSIX standard.

nodes.label: Computability.StateTransition
nodes.description: This file contains simple definitions and lemmas for reasoning about state transition systems defined by a function σ → Option σ, where σ is the type of states.

nodes.label: Computability.TMComputable
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.TMConfig
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.TMToPartrec
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.Tape
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringDegree
nodes.description: This file defines Turing reducibility and equivalence, proves that Turing equivalence is an equivalence relation, and defines Turing degrees as the quotient under this relation.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Other.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.Computable
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of a Turing machine with some finiteness conditions (bundling the definition of TM2 in StackTuringMachine.lean), a definition of when a TM gives a certain output (in a certain time), and the definition of computability (in polynomial time or any time function) of a function between two types that have an encoding (as in Encoding.lean).

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.Config
nodes.descriptionTitle: Modelling partial recursive functions using Turing machines
nodes.description: The files Config and ToPartrec define a simplified basis for partial recursive functions, and a Turing.TM2 model Turing machine for evaluating these functions. This amounts to a constructive proof that every Partrec function can be evaluated by a Turing machine.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.PostTuringMachine
nodes.description: The files PostTuringMachine.lean and StackTuringMachine.lean define a sequence of simple machine languages, starting with Turing machines and working up to more complex languages based on Wang B-machines.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.StackTuringMachine
nodes.description: The files PostTuringMachine.lean and StackTuringMachine.lean define a sequence of simple machine languages, starting with Turing machines and working up to more complex languages based on Wang B-machines.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.Tape
nodes.description: This file defines the notion of a Turing machine tape, and the operations on it. A tape is a bidirectional infinite sequence of cells, each of which stores an element of a given alphabet Γ. All but finitely many of the cells are required to hold the blank symbol default : Γ.

nodes.label: Computability.TuringMachine.ToPartrec
nodes.descriptionTitle: Modelling partial recursive functions using Turing machines
nodes.description: The files Config and ToPartrec define a simplified basis for partial recursive functions, and a Turing.TM2 model Turing machine for evaluating these functions. This amounts to a constructive proof that every Partrec function can be evaluated by a Turing machine.

nodes.label: Condensed.AB
nodes.description: This file proves that the category of condensed modules over a ring satisfies Grothendieck's axioms AB5, AB4, and AB4.

nodes.label: Condensed.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the category of condensed objects in a category C, following the work of Clausen-Scholze and Barwick-Haine.

nodes.label: Condensed.CartesianClosed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Condensed sets form a Cartesian closed category
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Condensed.CartesianClosed.

nodes.label: Condensed.Discrete.Basic
nodes.description: Given a category C with sheafification with respect to the coherent topology on compact Hausdorff spaces, we define a functor C ⥤ Condensed C which associates to an object of C the corresponding "discrete" condensed object (see Condensed.discrete).

nodes.label: Condensed.Discrete.Characterization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterizing discrete condensed sets and R-modules.
nodes.description: This file proves a characterization of discrete condensed sets, discrete condensed R-modules over a ring R, discrete light condensed sets, and discrete light condensed R-modules over a ring R. see CondensedSet.isDiscrete_tfae, CondensedMod.isDiscrete_tfae, LightCondSet.isDiscrete_tfae, and LightCondMod.isDiscrete_tfae.

nodes.label: Condensed.Discrete.Colimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: The condensed set given by left Kan extension from FintypeCat to Profinite.
nodes.description: This file provides the necessary API to prove that a condensed set X is discrete if and only if for every profinite set S = limᵢSᵢ, X(S) ≅ colimᵢX(Sᵢ), and the analogous result for light condensed sets.

nodes.label: Condensed.Discrete.LocallyConstant
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sheaf of locally constant maps on CompHausLike P
nodes.description: This file proves that under suitable conditions, the functor from the category of sets to the category of sheaves for the coherent topology on CompHausLike P, given by mapping a set to the sheaf of locally constant maps to it, is left adjoint to the "underlying set" functor (evaluation at the point).

nodes.label: Condensed.Discrete.Module
nodes.description: This file provides the necessary API to prove that a condensed R-module is discrete if and only if the underlying condensed set is (both for light condensed and condensed).

nodes.label: Condensed.EffectiveEpi
nodes.descriptionTitle: The functor from compact Hausdorff spaces to condensed sets preserves effective epimorphisms
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Condensed.EffectiveEpi.

nodes.label: Condensed.Epi
nodes.description: This file characterises epimorphisms of condensed sets and condensed R-modules for any ring R, as those morphisms which are objectwise surjective on Stonean (see CondensedSet.epi_iff_surjective_on_stonean and CondensedMod.epi_iff_surjective_on_stonean).

nodes.label: Condensed.Equivalence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sheaves on CompHaus are equivalent to sheaves on Stonean
nodes.description: The forgetful functor from extremally disconnected spaces Stonean to compact Hausdorff spaces CompHaus has the marvellous property that it induces an equivalence of categories between sheaves on these two sites. This means that whatever works on Option.{u} is hard to transport over to Option.{v}. ULiftable is an attempt at improving the situation.

It applies, until one of the lists is exhausted. For example, zipWith f [0, 1, 2] [6.28, 31] = [f 0 6.28, f 1 31]. zip is zipWith applied to Prod.mk. For example, zip [a₁, a₂] [b₁, b₂, b₃] = [(a₁, b₁), (a₂, b₂)]. unzip undoes zip. For example, unzip [(a₁, b₁), (a₂, b₂)] = ([a₁, a₂], [b₁, b₂]).

nodes.label: Data.Set.Card
nodes.description: We define the cardinality of set s as a term Set.encard s : ℕ∞ and a term Set.ncard s : ℕ. The latter takes the junk value of zero if s is infinite. Both functions are noncomputable, and are defined in terms of ENat.card (which takes a type as its argument); this file can be seen as an API for the same function in the special case where the type is a coercion of a Set, allowing for smoother interactions with the Set API.

nodes.label: Data.Set.MemPartition
nodes.descriptionTitle: Partitions based on membership of a sequence of sets
nodes.description: Let f : ℕ → Set α be a sequence of sets. For n : ℕ, we can form the set of points that are in f 0 ∪ f 1 ∪ ... ∪ f (n-1); then the set of points in (f 0)ᶜ ∪ f 1 ∪ ... ∪ f (n-1) and so on for all 2^n choices of a set or its complement. The at most 2^n sets we obtain form a partition of univ : Set α. We call that partition memPartition f n (the membership partition of f). For n = 0 we set memPartition f 0 = {univ}.

nodes.label: Data.SetLike.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Typeclass for types with a set-like extensionality property
nodes.description: The Membership typeclass is used to let terms of a type have elements. Many instances of Membership have a set-like extensionality property: things are equal iff they have the same elements. The SetLike typeclass provides a unified interface to define a Membership that is extensional in this way.

nodes.label: Data.W.Cardinal
nodes.description: This file proves some theorems about the cardinality of W-types. The main result is cardinalMk_le_max_aleph0_of_finite which says that if for any a : α, β a is finite, then the cardinality of WType β is at most the maximum of the cardinality of α and ℵ₀. This can be used to prove theorems about the cardinality of algebraic constructions such as polynomials. There is a surjection from a WType to MvPolynomial for example, and this surjection can be used to put an upper bound on the cardinality of MvPolynomial.

nodes.label: Data.W.Constructions
nodes.description: We take the view of W types as inductive types. Given α : Type and β : α → Type, the W type determined by this data, WType β, is the inductively with constructors from α and arities of each constructor a : α given by β a.

nodes.label: Dynamics.BirkhoffSum.Average
nodes.description: In this file we define birkhoffAverage f g n x to be $$ \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}g(f^{[k]}(x)), $$ where f : α → α is a self-map on some type α, g : α → M is a function from α to a module over a division semiring R, and R is used to formalize division by n as (n : R)⁻¹ • _.

nodes.description: In this file we define birkhoffSum f g n x to be the sum ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, g (f^[k] x). This sum (more precisely, the corresponding average n⁻¹ • birkhoffSum f g n x) appears in various ergodic theorems saying that these averages converge to the "space average" ⨍ x, g x ∂μ in some sense.

nodes.label: Dynamics.BirkhoffSum.NormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Birkhoff average in a normed space
nodes.description: In this file we prove some lemmas about the Birkhoff average (birkhoffAverage) of a function which takes values in a normed space over ℝ or ℂ.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Birkhoff sum and average for quasi-measure-preserving maps
