nodes.label: Dynamics.Circle.RotationNumber.TranslationNumber
nodes.descriptionTitle: Translation number of a monotone real map that commutes with x ↦ x + 1
nodes.description: Let f : ℝ → ℝ be a monotone map such that f (x + 1) = f x + 1 for all x. Then the limit $$ \tau(f)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{f^n(x)-x}{n} $$ exists and does not depend on x. This number is called the translation number of f. Different authors use different notation for this number: τ, ρ, rot, etc

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Action.Basic
nodes.description: A group action of G on a space α with measure μ is called ergodic, if for any (null) measurable set s, if it is a.e.-invariant under each scalar multiplication (g • ·), g : G, then it is either null or conull.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Action.OfMinimal
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the left shift (a ·) on a compact topological group G is ergodic with respect to the Haar measure if and only if it is minimal, i.e., the powers a ^ n are dense in G.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Action.Regular
nodes.descriptionTitle: Regular action of a group on itself is ergodic
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the left and right actions of a group on itself are ergodic.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.AddCircle
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ergodic maps of the additive circle
nodes.description: This file contains proofs of ergodicity for maps of the additive circle.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.AddCircleAdd
nodes.description: In this file we prove that rotation of AddCircle p by a is ergodic if and only if a has infinite order (in other words, if a / p is irrational).

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Conservative
nodes.description: In this file we define f : α → α to be a conservative system w.r.t. a measure μ if f is non-singular (MeasureTheory.QuasiMeasurePreserving) and for every measurable set s of positive measure at least one point x ∈ s returns back to s after some number of iterations of f. There are several properties that look like they are stronger than this one but actually follow from it:

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Ergodic
nodes.description: Let f : α → α be measure preserving with respect to a measure μ. We say f is ergodic with respect to μ (or μ is ergodic with respect to f) if the only measurable sets s such that f⁻¹' s = s are either almost empty or full.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Extreme
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a finite measure μ is an ergodic measure for a self-map f iff it is an extreme point of the set of invariant measures of f with the same total volume. We also specialize this result to probability measures.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.Function
nodes.description: In this file we prove that an a.e. strongly measurable function g : α → X that is a.e. invariant under a (quasi)ergodic map is a.e. equal to a constant. We prove several versions of this statement with slightly different measurability assumptions. We also formulate a version for MeasureTheory.AEEqFun functions with all a.e. equalities replaced with equalities in the quotient space.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.MeasurePreserving
nodes.description: We say that f : α → β is a measure-preserving map w.r.t. measures μ : Measure α and ν : Measure β if f is measurable and map f μ = ν. In this file we define the predicate MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving and prove its basic properties.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Ergodic.RadonNikodym

nodes.label: Dynamics.Flow

nodes.label: Dynamics.Minimal

nodes.label: Dynamics.Newton

nodes.label: Dynamics.OmegaLimit

nodes.label: Dynamics.PeriodicPts.Defs

nodes.label: Dynamics.SymbolicDynamics.Basic

Throughout the documentation we use the additive notations, which are the most common in symbolic dynamics, although all the notions introduced are defined in the multiplicative notations and adapted to the additive notation.

nodes.label: Dynamics.TopologicalEntropy.DynamicalEntourage
nodes.description: Bowen-Dinaburg's definition of topological entropy of a transformation T in a metric space (X, d) relies on the so-called dynamical balls. These balls are sets B (x, ε, n) = { y | ∀ k < n, d(T^[k] x, T^[k] y) < ε }.

nodes.label: Dynamics.TopologicalEntropy.NetEntropy
nodes.description: We implement Bowen-Dinaburg's definitions of the topological entropy, via nets.

nodes.label: Dynamics.TopologicalEntropy.Semiconj
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological entropy of the image of a set under a semiconjugacy
nodes.description: Consider two dynamical systems (X, S) and (Y, T) together with a semiconjugacy φ:

nodes.label: Dynamics.TopologicalEntropy.Subset
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological entropy of subsets: monotonicity, closure, union
nodes.description: This file contains general results about the topological entropy of various subsets of the same dynamical system (X, T). We prove that: the larger its entropy. the latter property to finite unions.

nodes.label: Dynamics.Transitive
nodes.description: In this file we define an action of a monoid M on a topological space α to be topologically transitive if for any pair of nonempty open sets U and V in α there exists an m : M such that (m • U) ∩ V is nonempty. We also provide an additive version of this definition and prove basic facts about topologically transitive actions.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.AbelRuffini
nodes.description: This file proves one direction of the Abel-Ruffini theorem, namely that if an element is solvable by radicals, then its minimal polynomial has solvable Galois group.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.AbsoluteGaloisGroup
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topological abelianization of the absolute Galois group.
nodes.description: We define the absolute Galois group of a field K and its topological abelianization.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.AlgebraicClosure
nodes.description: In this file we construct the relative algebraic closure of a field extension.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.AxGrothendieck
nodes.description: This file proves that if K is an algebraically closed field, then any injective polynomial map K^n → K^n is also surjective.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.CardinalEmb
nodes.descriptionTitle: Number of embeddings of an algebraic extension of infinite separable degree
nodes.description: of infinite degree, then #(Field.Emb F E) = 2 ^ Module.rank F E. This is in contrast to the case of finite degree, where #(Field.Emb F E) = Module.rank F E.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Cardinality
nodes.description: In this file we show all the possible cardinalities of fields. All infinite cardinals can harbour a field structure, and so can all types with prime power cardinalities, and this is sharp.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.ChevalleyWarning
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of the Chevalley–Warning theorem. Throughout most of this file, K denotes a finite field and q is notation for the cardinality of K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Differential.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the logarithmic derivative Differential.logDeriv and proves properties of it. This is defined algebraically, compared to logDeriv which is analytical.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Differential.Liouville
nodes.description: A proof of Liouville's theorem. Follows Rosenlicht, M. Integration in finite terms.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Extension
nodes.description: IntermediateField.exists_algHom_of_adjoin_splits' is the main result: if E/L/F is a tower of field extensions, K is another extension of F, and f is an embedding of L/F into K/F, such that the minimal polynomials of a set of generators of E/L splits in K (via f), then f extends to an embedding of E/F into K/F.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic results about finite fields. Throughout most of this file, K denotes a finite field and q is notation for the cardinality of K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.Extension
nodes.description: In this file we develop the theory of extensions of finite fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.GaloisField
nodes.description: If p is a prime number, and n a natural number, then GaloisField p n is defined as the splitting field of X^(p^n) - X over ZMod p. It is a finite field with p ^ n elements.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.Polynomial
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for FieldTheory.Finite.Polynomial.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.Trace
nodes.descriptionTitle: The trace and norm maps for finite fields
nodes.description: We state several lemmas about the trace and norm maps for finite fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finite.Valuation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Valuations on an algebra over a finite field.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for FieldTheory.Finite.Valuation.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Finiteness
nodes.descriptionTitle: A module over a division ring is Noetherian if and only if it is finite.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for FieldTheory.Finiteness.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Fixed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fixed field under a group action.
nodes.description: This is the basis of the Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory. Given a (finite) group G that acts on a field F, we define FixedPoints.subfield G F, the subfield consisting of elements of F fixed by every element of G.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.Abelian
nodes.description: In this file, we define the typeclass of abelian extensions and provide some basic API.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define Galois extensions as extensions which are both separable and normal.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.GaloisClosure
nodes.description: In a field extension K/k

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.Infinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Fundamental Theorem of Infinite Galois Theory
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the fundamental theorem of infinite Galois theory and the special case for open subgroups and normal subgroups. We first verify that IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup and IntermediateField.fixedField are inverses of each other between intermediate fields and closed subgroups of the Galois group.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.IsGaloisGroup
nodes.description: Given an action of a group G on an extension of fields L/K, we introduce a predicate IsGaloisGroup G K L saying that G acts faithfully on L with fixed field K. In particular, we do not assume that L is an algebraic extension of K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.NormalBasis
nodes.description: We prove the normal basis theorem IsGalois.normalBasis: every finite Galois extension has a basis that is an orbit under the Galois group action.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.Notation
nodes.description: The Galois group Gal(L/K) is implemented via L ≃ₐ[K] L in mathlib. We provide such a notation in this file.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Galois.Profinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Galois Group as a profinite group
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that given a field extension K/k, there is a continuous isomorphism between Gal(K/k) and the limit of Gal(L/k), where L is a finite Galois intermediate field ordered by inverse inclusion, thus making Gal(K/k) profinite as a limit of finite groups.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Algebra
nodes.description: This file relates IntermediateField.adjoin to Algebra.adjoin.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains many results about adjoining elements to fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we introduce the notion of adjoining elements to fields. This isn't quite the same as adjoining elements to rings. For example, K[x] might not include x⁻¹.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Algebraic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results on finite dimensionality and algebraicity of intermediate fields.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Algebraic.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Basic
nodes.description: Let L / K be a field extension, given as an instance Algebra K L. This file defines the type of fields in between K and L, IntermediateField K L. An IntermediateField K L is a subfield of L which contains (the image of) K, i.e. it is a Subfield L and a Subalgebra K L.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IntermediateField.ExtendRight
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extending intermediate fields to a larger extension
nodes.description: Given a tower of field extensions K ⊆ L ⊆ M and an intermediate field F of L/K, this file defines IntermediateField.extendRight F M, the image of F under the inclusion L ⊆ M, as an intermediate field of M/K. It is canonically isomorphic to F as a K-algebra.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.AlgebraicClosure
nodes.description: In this file we construct the algebraic closure of a field

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define the typeclass for algebraically closed fields and algebraic closures, and prove some of their properties.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.Classification
nodes.description: This file contains results related to classifying algebraically closed fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.Spectrum
nodes.description: This file develops and proves the spectral mapping theorem for polynomials over algebraically closed fields. In particular, if a is an element of a 𝕜-algebra A where 𝕜 is a field, and p : 𝕜[X] is a polynomial, then the spectrum of Polynomial.aeval a p contains the image of the spectrum of a under (fun k ↦ Polynomial.eval k p). When 𝕜 is algebraically closed, these are in fact equal (assuming either that the spectrum of a is nonempty or the polynomial has positive degree), which is the spectral mapping theorem.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsPerfectClosure
nodes.description: This file contains IsPerfectClosure which asserts that L is a perfect closure of K under a ring homomorphism i : K →+ L, as well as its basic properties.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsRealClosed.Basic
nodes.description: A field R is real closed if all of the following hold: 1. R is real (that is, -1 is not a sum of squares in R). 2. for every x in R, one of x or -x is a square. 3. every odd-degree polynomial over R has a root in R.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.IsSepClosed
nodes.description: In this file we define the typeclass for separably closed fields and separable closures, and prove some of their properties.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Isaacs
nodes.descriptionTitle: Algebraic extensions are determined by their sets of minimal polynomials up to isomorphism
nodes.description: Field.nonempty_algHom_of_exists_root says if E/F and K/F are field extensions with E/F algebraic, and if the minimal polynomial of every element of E over F has a root in K, then there exists an F-embedding of E into K. If E/F and K/F have the same set of minimal polynomials, then E and K are isomorphic as F-algebras. As a corollary:

nodes.label: FieldTheory.JacobsonNoether
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of the Jacobson-Noether theorem and some auxiliary lemmas. Here we discuss different cases of characteristics of the noncommutative division algebra D with center k.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.KrullTopology
nodes.description: We define the Krull topology on Gal(L/K) for an arbitrary field extension L/K. In order to do this, we first define a GroupFilterBasis on Gal(L/K), whose sets are E.fixingSubgroup for all intermediate fields E with E/K finite dimensional.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.KummerExtension
nodes.description: Suppose L/K is a finite extension of dimension n, and K contains all n-th roots of unity. Then L/K is cyclic iff L is a splitting field of some irreducible polynomial of the form Xⁿ - a : K[X] iff L = K[α] for some αⁿ ∈ K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.KummerPolynomial
nodes.description: a p-power. This is not true for composite n. For example, x^4+4=(x^2-2x+2)(x^2+2x+2) but -4 is not a 4th power.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Laurent
nodes.description: Implemented as the quotient of two Taylor expansions, over domains. An auxiliary definition is provided first to make the construction of the AlgHom easier, which works on CommRing which are not necessarily domains.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.LinearDisjoint
nodes.description: This file contains basics about the linearly disjoint fields. We adapt the definitions in . See the file Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/LinearDisjoint.lean and Mathlib/RingTheory/LinearDisjoint.lean for details.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the minimal polynomial of an element x of an A-algebra B, under the assumption that x is integral over A, and derives some basic properties such as irreducibility under the assumption B is a domain.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.ConjRootClass
nodes.description: In this file, we define the ConjRootClass of a field extension L / K as the quotient of L by the relation IsConjRoot K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.Field
nodes.descriptionTitle: Minimal polynomials on an algebra over a field
nodes.description: This file specializes the theory of minpoly to the setting of field extensions and derives some well-known properties, amongst which the fact that minimal polynomials are irreducible, and uniquely determined by their defining property.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Minimal polynomials on a finite algebra
nodes.description: This file proves the bound on the degree of a minimal polynomial on an algebra that is finite as a module.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.IsConjRoot
nodes.description: Given two elements x and y of some K-algebra, these two elements are conjugate roots over K if they have the same minimal polynomial over K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.IsIntegrallyClosed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Minimal polynomials over a GCD monoid
nodes.description: This file specializes the theory of minpoly to the case of an algebra over a GCD monoid.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Minpoly.MinpolyDiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about minpoly R x / (X - C x)
nodes.description: We used the contents of this file to describe the dual basis of a power basis under the trace form. See traceForm_dualBasis_powerBasis_eq.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.MvRatFunc.Rank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rank of multivariate rational function field
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for FieldTheory.MvRatFunc.Rank.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Normal.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we prove that for a finite extension, being normal is the same as being a splitting field (Normal.of_isSplittingField and Normal.exists_isSplittingField).

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Normal.Closure
nodes.description: Given field extensions K/F and L/F, the predicate IsNormalClosure F K L says that the minimal polynomial of every element of K over F splits in L, and that L is generated by the roots of such minimal polynomials. These conditions uniquely characterize L/F up to F-algebra isomorphisms (IsNormalClosure.equiv).

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Normal.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define normal field extensions.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.NormalizedTrace
nodes.description: This file defines the normalized trace map; that is, an F-linear map from the algebraic closure of F to F defined as the trace of an element from its adjoin extension divided by its degree.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Perfect
nodes.description: In this file we define perfect fields, together with a generalisation to (commutative) rings in prime characteristic.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PerfectClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: The perfect closure of a characteristic p ring
nodes.description: extension that makes frobenius surjective.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PolynomialGaloisGroup
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce the Galois group of a polynomial p over a field F, defined as the automorphism group of its splitting field. We also provide some results about some extension E above p.SplittingField.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PrimeField
nodes.description: A prime field is a field that does not contain any nontrivial subfield. Prime fields are ℚ in characteristic 0 and ZMod p in characteristic p with p a prime number. Any field K contains a unique prime field: it is the smallest field contained in K.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PrimitiveElement
nodes.description: In this file we prove the primitive element theorem.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic results about purely inseparable extensions
nodes.description: This file contains basic definitions and results about purely inseparable extensions.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Exponent
nodes.descriptionTitle: The exponent of purely inseparable extensions
nodes.description: This file defines the exponent of a purely inseparable extension (if one exists) and some related results.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.PerfectClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic results about relative perfect closure
nodes.description: This file contains basic results about relative perfect closures.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.PurelyInseparable.Tower
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tower law for purely inseparable extensions
nodes.description: This file contains results related to Field.sepDegree, Field.insepDegree and the tower law.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.AsPolynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Generalities on the polynomial structure of rational functions
nodes.description: regarded as an element of the height-one-spectrum.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The field structure of rational functions
nodes.description: Working with rational functions as polynomials:

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.Defs
nodes.description: Files in this folder define the field K⟮X⟯ of rational functions over a field K, show it is the field of fractions of K[X] and provide the main results concerning it. This file contains the basic definition.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.Degree
nodes.description: We define the degree of a rational function, with values in ℤ: natDegree of its numerator and the natDegree of its denominator. In particular, intDegree 0 = 0.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.IntermediateField
nodes.descriptionTitle: Intermediate Fields of Rational Function Fields
nodes.description: Results relating IntermediateField and RatFunc.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.Luroth
nodes.description: This file proves Lüroth's theorem, which says that for every field K, every intermediate field between K and the rational function field K⟮X⟯ is either K or isomorphic to K(X) as an K-algebra, see Luroth.algEquiv. The proof depends on the following lemma on degrees of rational functions:

nodes.label: FieldTheory.RatFunc.Valuation
nodes.description: This file defines the valuation at infinity on the field of rational functions F(t).

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Relrank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relative rank of subfields and intermediate fields
nodes.description: This file contains basics about the relative rank of subfields and intermediate fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Separable
nodes.description: We define a polynomial to be separable if it is coprime with its derivative. We prove basic properties about separable polynomials here.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.SeparableClosure
nodes.description: This file contains basics about the (relative) separable closure of a field extension.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.SeparableDegree
nodes.description: This file contains basics about the separable degree of a field extension.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.SeparablyGenerated
nodes.description: We aim to formalize the following result:

nodes.label: FieldTheory.SplittingField.Construction
nodes.description: In this file we prove the existence and uniqueness of splitting fields.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.SplittingField.IsSplittingField
nodes.description: This file introduces the notion of a splitting field of a polynomial and provides an embedding from a splitting field to any field that splits the polynomial. A polynomial f : K[X] splits over a field extension L of K if it is zero or all of its irreducible factors over L have degree 1. A field extension of K of a polynomial f : K[X] is called a splitting field if it is the smallest field extension of K such that f splits.

nodes.label: FieldTheory.Tower
nodes.description: We prove that given IsScalarTower F K A, if A is finite as a module over F then A is finite over K, and (as long as A is Noetherian over F and torsion-free over K) K is finite over F.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.Basic
nodes.description: In an R-module M, we define a convex cone as a set s such that a • x + b • y ∈ s whenever x, y ∈ s and a, b > 0. We prove that convex cones form a CompleteLattice, and define their images (ConvexCone.map) and preimages (ConvexCone.comap) under linear maps.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.Dual
nodes.descriptionTitle: The algebraic dual of a cone
nodes.description: Given a bilinear pairing p between two R-modules M and N and a set s in M, we define PointedCone.dual p s to be the pointed cone in N consisting of all points y such that 0 ≤ p x y for all x ∈ s.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.DualFinite
nodes.description: This file defines the notion of dually finitely generated cones. A cone is dually finitely generated (or DualFG for short) if it is the dual of a finite set, or equivalently, of a finitely generated cone. In geometric terms, a cone is dually finitely generated if it can be written as the intersection of finitely many halfspaces. This is also known as an H-cone. This is the counterpart to FG (finitely generated) which states that the cone is the conic hull of a finite set, or a V-cone.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.Pointed
nodes.description: A pointed cone is defined to be a submodule of a module where the scalars are restricted to be nonnegative. This is equivalent to saying that, as a set, a pointed cone is a convex cone which contains 0. This is a bundled version of ConvexCone.Pointed. We choose the submodule definition as it allows us to use the Module API to work with convex cones.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.Simplicial
nodes.description: A simplicial cone is a pointed convex cone that equals the conic hull of a finite linearly independent set of vectors. We do not require that the generators span the ambient module. However, when the cone is also generating, its generators linearly span the module.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Cone.TensorProduct
nodes.description: Given ordered modules M and N, there are in general several distinct possible orderings of the tensor product module M ⊗ N. Since the ordering of an ordered module can be represented by its cone of nonnegative elements, there are likewise multiple ways to construct a cone in M ⊗ N from cones in M and N. Such constructions are referred to as tensor products of cones.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.AffineSpace
nodes.description: This file shows that every affine space is a convex space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines convex spaces as an algebraic structure supporting finite convex combinations.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.Module
nodes.description: This file shows that every module over ordered coefficients is a convex space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.ConvexSpace.Prod
nodes.description: This file defines the cartesian product of convex spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Convex.Set
nodes.description: This file defines convex sets in a convex space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Diffeology.Basic
nodes.description: A diffeological space is a concrete sheaf on the site of cartesian spaces ℝⁿ and smooth maps between them, or equivalently a type X with a well-behaved notion of smoothness for functions from the spaces ℝⁿ to X - see https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/diffeological+space. In this file we focus on the latter viewpoint and define some of the basic notions of diffeology, like diffeological spaces and smooth maps between them.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Altitude
nodes.description: This file defines the altitudes of a simplex and their feet.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Bisector
nodes.description: This file proves lemmas relating to bisecting angles.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Incenter
nodes.description: This file proves lemmas relating incenters and excenters of a simplex to angle bisection.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.Affine
nodes.description: This file defines oriented angles in Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines oriented angles in real inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.Projection
nodes.description: This file proves lemmas relating to oriented angles involving orthogonal projections.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.RightAngle
nodes.description: This file proves basic geometric results about distances and oriented angles in (possibly degenerate) right-angled triangles in real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.Rotation
nodes.description: This file defines rotations by oriented angles in real inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Sphere
nodes.description: This file proves results about angles in circles and spheres.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Affine
nodes.description: This file defines unoriented angles in Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines unoriented angles in real inner product spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Conformal
nodes.description: This file proves that conformal maps preserve angles.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.CrossProduct
nodes.description: This file proves InnerProductGeometry.norm_withLpEquiv_crossProduct, relating the norm of the cross-product of two real vectors with their individual norms.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Projection
nodes.description: This file proves lemmas relating to angles involving orthogonal projections.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.RightAngle
nodes.description: This file proves basic geometric results about distances and angles in (possibly degenerate) right-angled triangles in real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.TriangleInequality
nodes.description: This file contains the proof that angles obey the triangle inequality.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Basic
nodes.description: This file makes some definitions and proves very basic geometrical results about real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces. Results about real inner product spaces that involve the norm and inner product but not angles generally go in Analysis.NormedSpace.InnerProduct. Results with longer proofs or more geometrical content generally go in separate files.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Circumcenter
nodes.description: This file proves some lemmas on points equidistant from a set of points, and defines the circumradius and circumcenter of a simplex. There are also some definitions for use in calculations where it is convenient to work with affine combinations of vertices together with the circumcenter.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Congruence
nodes.description: This file proves the classical triangle congruence criteria for (possibly degenerate) triangles in real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces. We prove SSS, SAS, ASA, and AAS congruence.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Incenter
nodes.description: This file defines the insphere and exspheres of a simplex (tangent to the faces of the simplex), and the center and radius of such spheres.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Inversion.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define inversion in a sphere in an affine space. This map sends each point x to the point y such that y -ᵥ c = (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c), where c and R are the center and the radius of the sphere.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Inversion.Calculus
nodes.description: In this file we prove a formula for the derivative of EuclideanGeometry.inversion c R.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Inversion.ImageHyperplane
nodes.descriptionTitle: Image of a hyperplane under inversion
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the inversion with center c and radius R ≠ 0 maps a sphere passing through the center to a hyperplane, and vice versa. More precisely, it maps a sphere with center y ≠ c and radius dist y c to the hyperplane AffineSubspace.perpBisector c (EuclideanGeometry.inversion c R y).

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.MongePoint
nodes.description: This file defines the orthocenter of a triangle, via its n-dimensional generalization, the Monge point of a simplex.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.NinePointCircle
nodes.description: This file defines the nine-point circle of a triangle, and its higher dimension analogue, the 3(n+1)-point sphere of a simplex. Specifically for triangles, we show that it passes through nine specific points as desired.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.PerpBisector
nodes.description: We define AffineSubspace.perpBisector p₁ p₂ to be the perpendicular bisector of the segment [p₁, p₂], as a bundled affine subspace. We also prove that a point belongs to the perpendicular bisector if and only if it is equidistant from p₁ and p₂, as well as a few linear equations that define this subspace.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Projection
nodes.description: This file defines orthogonal projection onto an affine subspace, and reflection of a point in an affine subspace.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.SignedDist
nodes.descriptionTitle: Signed distance to an affine subspace in a Euclidean space.
nodes.description: This file defines the signed distance between two points, in the direction of a given vector, and the signed distance between an affine subspace and a point, in the direction of a given reference point.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Similarity
nodes.description: This file contains theorems about similarity of triangles, including conditions for similarity based on sides and angles.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Simplex
nodes.description: This file defines properties of simplices in a Euclidean space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines and proves basic results about spheres and cospherical sets of points in Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.OrthRadius
nodes.descriptionTitle: Spaces orthogonal to the radius vector in spheres.
nodes.description: This file defines the affine subspace orthogonal to the radius vector at a point.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.Power
nodes.descriptionTitle: Power of a point (intersecting chords and secants)
nodes.description: This file proves basic geometrical results about power of a point (intersecting chords and secants) in spheres in real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.Ptolemy
nodes.description: This file proves Ptolemy's theorem on the lengths of the diagonals and sides of a cyclic quadrilateral.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.SecondInter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Second intersection of a sphere and a line
nodes.description: This file defines and proves basic results about the second intersection of a sphere with a line through a point on that sphere.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Sphere.Tangent
nodes.description: This file defines notions of spheres being tangent to affine subspaces and other spheres.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Triangle
nodes.description: This file proves basic geometrical results about distances and angles in (possibly degenerate) triangles in real inner product spaces and Euclidean affine spaces. More specialized results, and results developed for simplices in general rather than just for triangles, are in separate files. Definitions and results that make sense in more general affine spaces rather than just in the Euclidean case go under LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.

nodes.label: Geometry.Euclidean.Volume.Measure
nodes.description: In this file we introduce a d-dimensional measure for n-dimensional Euclidean affine space, namely MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure d with notation μHE[d]. This is the suitable measure to describe area and volume in an environment of arbitrary dimension. It is characterized by the following properties:

nodes.label: Geometry.Group.Growth.LinearLowerBound
nodes.descriptionTitle: Linear lower bound on the growth of a generating set
nodes.description: This file proves that the growth of a set generating an infinite group is at least linear.

nodes.label: Geometry.Group.Growth.QuotientInter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Growth in the quotient and intersection with a subgroup
nodes.description: For a group G and a subgroup H ≤ G, this file gives upper and lower bounds on the growth of a finset by its growth in H and G ⧸ H.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.LeftInvariantDerivation
nodes.description: In this file we define the concept of left invariant derivations for a Lie group. The concept is analogous to the more classical concept of left invariant vector fields, and it holds that the derivation associated to a vector field is left invariant iff the field is.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.LieGroup
nodes.description: A Lie group is a group that is also a C^n manifold, in which the group operations of multiplication and inversion are C^n maps. Regularity of the group multiplication means that multiplication is a C^n mapping of the product manifold G × G into G.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.Monoid
nodes.description: A C^n monoid is a monoid that is also a C^n manifold, in which multiplication is a C^n map of the product manifold G × G into G.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.SMul
nodes.description: In this file we define Cⁿ actions (e.g. by Lie groups or monoids) on manifolds: we say ContMDiffSMul I I' n G M if G acts multiplicatively on M and the action map fun p : G × M ↦ p.1 • p.2 is Cⁿ. We also provide API for additive actions using @[to_additive].

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.SmoothFunctions
nodes.description: In this file, we define instances of algebraic structures over C^n functions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Algebra.Structures
nodes.description: In this file we define C^n structures that build on Lie groups. We prefer using the term ContMDiffRing instead of Lie mainly because Lie ring has currently another use in mathematics.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Bordism
nodes.description: This file defines the beginnings of unoriented bordism theory. We define singular manifolds, the building blocks of unoriented bordism groups. Future pull requests will define bordisms and the bordism groups of a topological space, and prove these are abelian groups.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.BumpFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smooth bump functions on a smooth manifold
nodes.description: In this file we define SmoothBumpFunction I c to be a bundled smooth "bump" function centered at c. It is a structure that consists of two real numbers 0 < rIn < rOut with small enough rOut. We define a coercion to function for this type, and for f : SmoothBumpFunction I c, the function ⇑f written in the extended chart at c has the following properties:

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ChartedSpace
nodes.description: A smooth manifold is a topological space M locally modelled on a Euclidean space (or a Euclidean half-space for manifolds with boundaries, or an infinite-dimensional vector space for more general notions of manifolds), i.e., the manifold is covered by open subsets on which there are local homeomorphisms (the charts) going to a model space H, and the changes of charts should be smooth maps.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Complex
nodes.description: Thanks to the rigidity of complex-differentiability compared to real-differentiability, there are many results about complex manifolds with no analogue for manifolds over a general normed field. For now, this file contains just two (closely related) such results:

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ConformalGroupoid
nodes.description: In this file we define the groupoid of conformal maps on normed spaces.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiff.Atlas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smoothness of charts and local structomorphisms
nodes.description: We show that the model with corners, charts, extended charts and their inverses are C^n, and that local structomorphisms are C^n with C^n inverses.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiff.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of C^n functions between manifolds
nodes.description: In this file, we show that standard operations on C^n maps between manifolds are C^n : embedding e : M → H, then e is C^n.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiff.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smoothness of standard maps associated to the product of manifolds
nodes.description: This file contains results about smoothness of standard maps associated to products and sums (disjoint unions) of smooth manifolds: C^n, as are Sum.elim, Sum.map and Sum.swap.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiff.Defs
nodes.description: We define Cⁿ functions between manifolds, as functions which are Cⁿ in charts, and prove basic properties of these notions. Here, n can be finite, or ∞, or ω.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiff.NormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equivalence of smoothness with the basic definition for functions between vector spaces
nodes.description: manifold-smoothness is equivalent to usual smoothness.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiffMFDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Interactions between differentiability, smoothness and manifold derivatives
nodes.description: We give the relation between MDifferentiable, ContMDiff, mfderiv, tangentMap and related notions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.ContMDiffMap
nodes.description: In this file we define the type ContMDiffMap of n times continuously differentiable bundled maps.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.DerivationBundle
nodes.description: In this file we define the derivations at a point of a manifold on the algebra of smooth functions. Moreover, we define the differential of a function in terms of derivations.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Diffeomorph
nodes.description: This file implements diffeomorphisms.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.GroupLieAlgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Lie algebra of a Lie group
nodes.description: Given a Lie group, we define GroupLieAlgebra I G as its tangent space at the identity, and we endow it with a Lie bracket, as follows. Given two vectors v, w : GroupLieAlgebra I G, consider the associated left-invariant vector fields mulInvariantVectorField v (given at a point g by the image of v under the derivative of left-multiplication by g) and mulInvariantVectorField w. Then take their Lie bracket at the identity: this is by definition the bracket of v and w.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.HasGroupoid
nodes.descriptionTitle: Charted spaces with a given structure groupoid
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Geometry.Manifold.HasGroupoid.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Immersion
nodes.description: In this file, we define C^n immersions between C^n manifolds. The correct definition in the infinite-dimensional setting differs from the standard finite-dimensional definition (concerning the mfderiv being injective): future pull requests will prove that our definition implies the latter, and that both are equivalent for finite-dimensional manifolds.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Icc
nodes.description: The manifold structure on real intervals is defined in Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Real. We relate it to the manifold structure on the real line, by showing that the inclusion (contMDiff_subtype_coe_Icc) and projection (contMDiffOn_projIcc) are smooth, and showing that a function defined on the interval is smooth iff its composition with the projection is smooth on the interval in ℝ (see contMDiffOn_comp_projIcc_iff and friends).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Quotient
nodes.description: This file contains results about quotients of manifolds by group actions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing examples of manifolds over ℝ
nodes.description: We introduce the necessary bits to be able to define manifolds modelled over ℝ^n, boundaryless or with boundary or with corners. As a concrete example, we construct explicitly the manifold with boundary structure on the real interval [x, y], and prove that its boundary is indeed {x, y} whenever x < y. As a corollary, a product M × [x, y] with a manifold M without boundary has boundary M × {x, y}.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Sphere
nodes.description: This file defines stereographic projection from the sphere in an inner product space E, and uses it to put an analytic manifold structure on the sphere.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Instances.UnitsOfNormedAlgebra
nodes.description: We construct the Lie group structure on the group of units of a complete normed 𝕜-algebra R. The group of units Rˣ has a natural C^n manifold structure modelled on R given by its embedding into R. Together with the smoothness of the multiplication and inverse of its elements, Rˣ forms a Lie group.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IntegralCurve.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral curves of vector fields on a manifold
nodes.description: Let M be a manifold and v : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x be a vector field on M. An integral curve of v is a function γ : ℝ → M such that the derivative of γ at t equals v (γ t). The integral curve may only be defined for all t within some subset of ℝ.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IntegralCurve.ExistUnique
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence and uniqueness of integral curves
nodes.description: $C^1$ vector field. This follows from the existence theorem for solutions to ODEs (exists_forall_hasDerivAt_Ioo_eq_of_contDiffAt). $C^1$ vector field. This follows from the uniqueness theorem for solutions to ODEs (ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_set_Ioo). This requires the manifold to be Hausdorff (T2Space).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IntegralCurve.Transform
nodes.descriptionTitle: Translation and scaling of integral curves
nodes.description: New integral curves may be constructed by translating or scaling the domain of an existing integral curve.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IntegralCurve.UniformTime
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniform time lemma for the global existence of integral curves
nodes.description: integral curve at each point x : M is defined at least on an open interval Ioo (-ε) ε, then every point on M has a global integral curve passing through it.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IsManifold.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: C^n manifolds (possibly with boundary or corners)
nodes.description: A C^n manifold is a manifold modelled on a normed vector space, or a subset like a half-space (to get manifolds with boundaries) for which the changes of coordinates are C^n maps. We define a model with corners as a map I : H → E embedding nicely the topological space H in the vector space E (or more precisely as a structure containing all the relevant properties).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IsManifold.ExtChartAt
nodes.description: In a C^n manifold with corners with the model I on (E, H), the charts take values in the model space H. However, we also need to use extended charts taking values in the model vector space E. These extended charts are not OpenPartialHomeomorph as the target is not open in E in general, but we can still register them as PartialEquivs.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.IsManifold.InteriorBoundary
nodes.descriptionTitle: Interior and boundary of a manifold
nodes.description: Define the interior and boundary of a manifold.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.LocalDiffeomorph
nodes.description: In this file, we define C^n local diffeomorphisms between manifolds.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.LocalInvariantProperties
nodes.descriptionTitle: Local properties invariant under a groupoid
nodes.description: We study properties of a triple (g, s, x) where g is a function between two spaces H and H', s is a subset of H and x is a point of H. Our goal is to register how such a property should behave to make sense in charted spaces modelled on H and H'.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.LocalSourceTargetProperty
nodes.descriptionTitle: Local properties of smooth functions which depend on both the source and target
nodes.description: In this file, we consider local properties of functions between manifolds, which depend on both the source and the target: more precisely, properties P of functions f : M → N such that f has property P if and only if there is a suitable pair of charts on M and N, respectively, such that f read in these charts has a particular form.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.Atlas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of models with corners and (extended) charts
nodes.description: In this file, we analyse the differentiability of charts, models with corners and extended charts. We show that

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of the manifold Fréchet derivative
nodes.description: In this file, we show various properties of the manifold Fréchet derivative, mimicking the API for Fréchet derivatives.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.Defs
nodes.descriptionTitle: The derivative of functions between manifolds
nodes.description: Let M and M' be two manifolds over a field 𝕜 (with respective models with corners I on (E, H) and I' on (E', H')), and let f : M → M'. We define the derivative of the function at a point, within a set or along the whole space, mimicking the API for (Fréchet) derivatives. It is denoted by mfderiv I I' f x, where "m" stands for "manifold" and "f" for "Fréchet" (as in the usual derivative fderiv 𝕜 f x).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.FDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relations between vector space derivative and manifold derivative
nodes.description: The manifold derivative mfderiv, when considered on the model vector space with its trivial manifold structure, coincides with the usual Fréchet derivative fderiv. In this section, we prove this and related statements.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.NormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equivalence of manifold differentiability with the basic definition for functions between
nodes.description: The API in this file is mostly copied from Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/ContMDiff/NormedSpace.lean, providing the same statements for higher smoothness. In this file, we do the same for differentiability.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.SpecificFunctions
nodes.description: In this file, we establish differentiability results for

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.Tangent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivatives of maps in the tangent bundle
nodes.description: This file contains properties of derivatives which need the manifold structure of the tangent bundle. Notably, it includes formulas for the tangent maps to charts, and unique differentiability statements for subsets of the tangent bundle.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.UniqueDifferential
nodes.description: In this file, we prove various properties of unique derivative sets in manifolds. has dense range. If s has the unique differential property, then so does f '' s. pullbacks of extended charts its preimage under the tangent bundle projection also has

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Metrizable
nodes.description: In this file we show that a σ-compact Hausdorff topological manifold over a finite-dimensional real vector space is metrizable.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Notation
nodes.description: This file defines custom elaborators for differential geometry to allow for more compact notation. We introduce a class of elaborators for handling differentiability on manifolds, and the elaborator T% for converting dependent sections of fibre bundles into non-dependent functions into the total space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.PartitionOfUnity
nodes.description: In this file we define two structures, SmoothBumpCovering and SmoothPartitionOfUnity. Both structures describe coverings of a set by a locally finite family of supports of smooth functions with some additional properties. The former structure is mostly useful as an intermediate step in the construction of a smooth partition of unity but some proofs that traditionally deal with a partition of unity can use a SmoothBumpCovering as well.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.PoincareConjecture
nodes.descriptionTitle: Statement of the generalized Poincaré conjecture
nodes.description: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_Poincar%C3%A9_conjecture

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Riemannian.Basic
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold M is a real manifold such that its tangent spaces are endowed with an inner product, depending smoothly on the point, and such that M has an emetric space structure for which the distance is the infimum of lengths of paths.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Riemannian.PathELength
nodes.description: Consider a manifold in which the tangent spaces have an enormed structure. Then one defines pathELength γ a b as the length of the path γ : ℝ → M between a and b, i.e., the integral of the norm of its derivative on Icc a b.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Sheaf.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Generic construction of a sheaf from a LocalInvariantProp on a manifold
nodes.description: This file constructs the sheaf-of-types of functions f : M → M' (for charted spaces M, M') which satisfy the lifted property LiftProp P associated to some locally invariant (in the sense of StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp) property P on the model spaces of M and M'. For example, differentiability and smoothness are locally invariant properties in this sense, so this construction can be used to construct the sheaf of differentiable functions on a manifold and the sheaf of smooth functions on a manifold.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Sheaf.LocallyRingedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Smooth manifolds as locally ringed spaces
nodes.description: This file equips a smooth manifold with the structure of a locally ringed space.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.Sheaf.Smooth
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sheaf of smooth functions on a manifold
nodes.description: The sheaf of 𝕜-smooth functions from a manifold M to a manifold N can be defined as a sheaf of types using the construction StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.sheaf from the file Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/Sheaf/Basic.lean. In this file we write that down (a one-liner), then do the work of upgrading this to a sheaf of [groups]/[abelian groups]/[rings]/[commutative rings] when N carries more algebraic structure.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.SmoothApprox
nodes.descriptionTitle: Approximation of continuous functions by smooth functions
nodes.description: In this file, we deduce from the existence of smooth partitions of unity that any continuous map from a real σ-compact finite dimensional manifold M to a real normed space F can be approximated uniformly by smooth functions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.SmoothEmbedding
nodes.description: In this file, we define C^n embeddings between C^n manifolds. This will be useful to define embedded submanifolds.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.StructureGroupoid
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions and properties of structure groupoids, i.e., sets of open partial homeomorphisms stable under composition and inverse. These are used to define charted spaces (and hence manifolds). See the file Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.ChartedSpace for more details.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines C^n vector bundles over a manifold.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.ContMDiffSection
nodes.description: In this file we define the type ContMDiffSection of n times continuously differentiable sections of a vector bundle over a manifold M and prove that it's a module over the base field.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.CovariantDerivative.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines covariant derivatives (aka Koszul connections) on vector bundles over manifolds.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.CovariantDerivative.Torsion
nodes.description: We define the torsion tensor of an affine connection, i.e. a covariant derivative on the tangent bundle TM of some manifold M.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.FiberwiseLinear
nodes.descriptionTitle: The groupoid of C^n, fiberwise-linear maps
nodes.description: This file contains preliminaries for the definition of a C^n vector bundle: an associated StructureGroupoid, the groupoid of contMDiffFiberwiseLinear functions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Hom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homs of C^n vector bundles over the same base space
nodes.description: Here we show that the bundle of continuous linear maps is a C^n vector bundle. We also show that applying a smooth family of linear maps to a smooth family of vectors gives a smooth result, in several versions.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.LocalFrame
nodes.descriptionTitle: Local frames in a vector bundle
nodes.description: Let V → M be a finite rank smooth vector bundle with standard fiber F. A family of sections s i of V → M is called a C^k local frame on a set U ⊆ M iff each section s i is C^k on U, and the section values s i x form a basis for each x ∈ U. We define a predicate IsLocalFrame for a collection of sections to be a local frame on a set, and define basic notions (such as the coefficients of a section w.r.t. a local frame, and checking the smoothness of t via its coefficients in a local frame).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.MDifferentiable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Differentiability of functions in vector bundles
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.MDifferentiable.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Pullback
nodes.description: This file defines pullbacks of C^n vector bundles over a manifold.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Riemannian
nodes.description: Given a vector bundle over a manifold whose fibers are all endowed with a scalar product, we say that this bundle is Riemannian if the scalar product depends smoothly on the base point.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.SmoothSection
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Geometry.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Tangent
nodes.description: This file defines the tangent bundle as a C^n vector bundle.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorBundle.Tensoriality
nodes.description: Given vector bundles V and W over a manifold M, one can construct a section of the hom-bundle Π x, V x →L[𝕜] W x from a tensorial operation sending sections of V to sections of W. This file provides this construction.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorField.LieBracket
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lie brackets of vector fields on manifolds
nodes.description: We define the Lie bracket of two vector fields, denoted with VectorField.mlieBracket I V W x, as the pullback in the manifold of the corresponding notion in the model space (through extChartAt I x).

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.VectorField.Pullback
nodes.description: We study functions of the form V : Π (x : M) → TangentSpace I x on a manifold, i.e., vector fields.

nodes.label: Geometry.Manifold.WhitneyEmbedding
nodes.description: In this file we prove a version of the Whitney embedding theorem: for any compact real manifold M, for sufficiently large n there exists a smooth embedding M → ℝ^n.

nodes.label: Geometry.Polygon.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines polygons in affine spaces. For the special case n = 3, an interconversion is provided with Affine.Triangle.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.Basic
nodes.description: We introduce the category of ringed spaces, as an alias for SheafedSpace CommRingCat.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.LocallyRingedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of locally ringed spaces
nodes.description: We define (bundled) locally ringed spaces (as SheafedSpace CommRing along with the fact that the stalks are local rings), and morphisms between these (morphisms in SheafedSpace with IsLocalHom on the stalk maps).

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.LocallyRingedSpace.HasColimits
nodes.description: We construct the explicit coproducts and coequalizers of LocallyRingedSpace. It then follows that LocallyRingedSpace has all colimits, and forgetToSheafedSpace preserves them.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.LocallyRingedSpace.ResidueField
nodes.description: Any point x of a locally ringed space X comes with a natural residue field, namely the residue field of the stalk at x. Moreover, for every open subset of X containing x, we have a canonical evaluation map from Γ(X, U) to the residue field of X at x.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.OpenImmersion
nodes.description: We say that a morphism of presheafed spaces f : X ⟶ Y is an open immersion if the underlying map of spaces is an open embedding f : X ⟶ U ⊆ Y, and the sheaf map Y(V) ⟶ f _ X(V) is an iso for each V ⊆ U.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.PresheafedSpace
nodes.description: Introduces the category of topological spaces equipped with a presheaf (taking values in an arbitrary target category C).

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.PresheafedSpace.Gluing
nodes.description: Given a family of gluing data of structured spaces (presheafed spaces, sheafed spaces, or locally ringed spaces), we may glue them together.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.PresheafedSpace.HasColimits
nodes.description: If C has limits, then the category PresheafedSpace C has colimits, and the forgetful functor to TopCat preserves these colimits.

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.SheafedSpace
nodes.description: Introduces the category of topological spaces equipped with a sheaf (taking values in an arbitrary target category C).

nodes.label: Geometry.RingedSpace.Stalks
nodes.description: This file lifts constructions of stalks and pushforwards of stalks to work with the category of presheafed spaces. Additionally, we prove that restriction of presheafed spaces does not change the stalks.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Abelianization.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines the commutator and the abelianization of a group. It furthermore prepares for the result that the abelianization is left adjoint to the forgetful functor from abelian groups to groups, which can be found in Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Abelianization.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The abelianization of a finite group is finite
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for GroupTheory.Abelianization.Finite.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Archimedean
nodes.description: This file proves a few facts about ordered groups which satisfy the Archimedean property, that is: class Archimedean (α) [OrderedAddCommMonoid α] : Prop := (arch : ∀ (x : α) {y}, 0 < y → ∃ n : ℕ, x ≤ n • y)

nodes.label: GroupTheory.ArchimedeanDensely
nodes.descriptionTitle: Archimedean groups are either discrete or densely ordered
nodes.description: This file proves a few additional facts about linearly ordered additive groups which satisfy the Archimedean property -- they are either order-isomorphic and additively isomorphic to the integers, or they are densely ordered.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.ClassEquation
nodes.description: This file establishes the class equation for finite groups.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Commensurable
nodes.description: Two subgroups H and K of a group G are commensurable if H ∩ K has finite index in both H and K.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Commutator.Basic
nodes.description: If G is a group and H₁ H₂ : Subgroup G then the commutator ⁅H₁, H₂⁆ : Subgroup G is the subgroup of G generated by the commutators h₁ h₂ h₁⁻¹ h₂⁻¹.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Commutator.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: The commutator of a finite direct product is contained in the direct product of the commutators.
nodes.description: The commutator of a finite direct product is contained in the direct product of the commutators.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.CommutingProbability
nodes.description: This file introduces the commuting probability of finite groups.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Complement
nodes.description: In this file we define the complement of a subgroup.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Congruence.Basic
nodes.description: This file proves basic properties of the quotient of a type by a congruence relation.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Congruence.BigOperators
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for GroupTheory.Congruence.BigOperators.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Congruence.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines congruence relations: equivalence relations that preserve a binary operation, which in this case is multiplication or addition. The principal definition is a structure extending a Setoid (an equivalence relation), and the inductive definition of the smallest congruence relation containing a binary relation is also given (see ConGen).

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Congruence.Hom
nodes.description: This file contains elementary definitions involving congruence relations and morphisms.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Congruence.Opposite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Congruences on the opposite of a group
nodes.description: This file defines the order isomorphism between the congruences on a group G and the congruences on the opposite group Gᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coprod.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Coproduct (free product) of two monoids or groups
nodes.description: In this file we define Monoid.Coprod M N (notation: M ∗ N) to be the coproduct (a.k.a. free product) of two monoids. The same type is used for the coproduct of two monoids and for the coproduct of two groups.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.CoprodI
nodes.descriptionTitle: The coproduct (a.k.a. the free product) of groups or monoids
nodes.description: Given an ι-indexed family M of monoids, we define their coproduct (a.k.a. free product) Monoid.CoprodI M. As usual, we use the suffix I for an indexed (co)product, leaving Coprod for the coproduct of two monoids.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coset.Basic
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of left and right cosets.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coset.Card
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lagrange's theorem: the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group.
nodes.description: there is an analogous version for additive groups

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coset.Defs
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of left and right cosets.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.CosetCover
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemma of B. H. Neumann on coverings of a group by cosets.
nodes.description: Let the group $G$ be the union of finitely many, let us say $n$, left cosets of subgroups $C₁$, $C₂$, ..., $Cₙ$: $$ G = ⋃_{i = 1}^n C_i g_i. $$

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coxeter.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines Coxeter groups and Coxeter systems.

nodes.label: GroupTheory.Coxeter.Inversion

nodes.label: InformationTheory.KullbackLeibler.ChainRule
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chain rule for the Kullback-Leibler divergence
nodes.description: Suppose that we have two finite joint measures on a product 𝓧 × 𝓨, which can be decomposed as μ ⊗ₘ κ and ν ⊗ₘ η, where μ and ν are measures on 𝓧 and κ and η are Markov kernels from 𝓧 to 𝓨. Then we can express the Kullback-Leibler divergence between these two joint measures as a sum of klDiv μ ν and the conditional Kullback-Leibler divergence between the kernels κ and η, averaged over μ. The resulting equality is most often written as klDiv (μ ⊗ₘ κ) (ν ⊗ₘ η) = klDiv μ ν + μ[fun x ↦ klDiv (κ x) (η x)].

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.Basis
nodes.description: Suppose P is an affine space modelled on the module V over the ring k, and p : ι → P is an affine-independent family of points spanning P. Given this data, each point q : P may be written uniquely as an affine combination: q = w₀ p₀ + w₁ p₁ + ⋯ for some (finitely-supported) weights wᵢ. For each i : ι, we thus have an affine map P →ᵃ[k] k, namely q ↦ wᵢ. This family of maps is known as the family of barycentric coordinates. It is defined in this file.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Adjugate

Using Cramer's rule, we can compute for each matrix A the matrix adjugate A. The entries of the adjugate are the minors of A.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.Chain
nodes.description: Given roots α and β, the α-chain through β is the set of roots of the form α + z • β for an integer z. This is known as a "root chain" and also a "root string". For linearly independent roots in finite crystallographic root pairings, these chains are always unbroken, i.e., of the form: β - q • α, ..., β - α, β, β + α, ..., β + p • α for natural numbers p, q, and the length, p + q is at most 3.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.Finite.CanonicalBilinear
nodes.descriptionTitle: The canonical bilinear form on a finite root pairing
nodes.description: Given a finite root pairing, we define a canonical map from weight space to coweight space, and the corresponding bilinear form. This form is symmetric and Weyl-invariant, and if the base ring is linearly ordered, then the form is root-positive, positive-semidefinite on the weight space, and positive-definite on the span of roots. From these facts, it is easy to show that Coxeter weights in a finite root pairing are bounded above by 4.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.Finite.Nondegenerate
nodes.descriptionTitle: Nondegeneracy of the polarization on a finite root pairing
nodes.description: We show that if the base ring of a finite root pairing is linearly ordered, then the canonical bilinear form is root-positive and positive-definite on the span of roots. From these facts, it is easy to show that Coxeter weights in a finite root pairing are bounded above by 4. Thus, the pairings of roots and coroots in a root pairing are restricted to the interval [-4, 4]. Furthermore, a linearly independent pair of roots cannot have Coxeter weight 4.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.OfBilinear
nodes.descriptionTitle: Root pairings made from bilinear forms
nodes.description: A common construction of root systems is given by taking the set of all vectors in an integral lattice for which reflection yields an automorphism of the lattice. In this file, we generalize this construction, replacing the ring of integers with an arbitrary commutative ring and the integral lattice with an arbitrary reflexive module equipped with a bilinear form.

nodes.description: This file contains basic results on Weyl-invariant inner products for root systems and root data. Given a root pairing we define a structure which contains a bilinear form together with axioms for reflection-invariance, symmetry, and strict positivity on all roots. We show that root-positive forms display the same sign behavior as the canonical pairing between roots and coroots.

nodes.label: LinearAlgebra.RootSystem.WeylGroup
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Weyl group of a root pairing
nodes.description: This file defines the Weyl group of a root pairing as the subgroup of automorphisms generated by reflection automorphisms. This deviates from the existing literature, which typically defines the Weyl group as the subgroup of linear transformations of the weight space generated by linear reflections. However, the automorphism group of a root pairing comes with a permutation representation on the set indexing roots and faithful linear representations on the weight space and coweight space.

For each CommRing R, and function v : Fin n → R the matrix vandermonde v is defined to be Fin n by Fin n matrix V whose ith row is [1, (v i), (v i)^2, ...]. This matrix has determinant equal to the product of v i - v j over all unordered pairs i,j, and therefore is nonsingular if and only if v is injective.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Order

nodes.description: The Borel sigma algebra of a linear order topology is generated by intervals of the given kind. The Borel sigma algebra of a dense linear order topology is generated by intervals of a given kind, with endpoints from dense subsets. A locally finite Borel measure on a second countable conditionally complete linear order is characterized by the measures of intervals of the given kind. A finite Borel measure on a second countable linear order is characterized by the measures of intervals of the given kind.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.ClosedCompactCylinders

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.Cylinders

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.HaarToSphere

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.StronglyMeasurable
nodes.description: In measure theory it is often assumed that some space is a PolishSpace, i.e. a separable and completely metrizable topological space, because it ensures a nice interaction between the topology and the measurable space structure. Moreover a strongly measurable function whose codomain is a metric space is measurable and has a separable range (see stronglyMeasurable_iff_measurable_separable).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.Projective
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective measure families and projective limits
nodes.description: A family of measures indexed by finite sets of ι is projective if, for finite sets J ⊆ I, the projection from ∀ i : I, α i to ∀ i : J, α i maps P I to P J. A measure μ is the projective limit of such a family of measures if for all I : Finset ι, the projection from ∀ i, α i to ∀ i : I, α i maps μ to P I.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Constructions.ProjectiveFamilyContent

nodes.description: Let P be a projective family of measures on a family of measurable spaces indexed by ι. That is, for each finite set I of indices, P I is a measure on Π j : I, α j, and for J ⊆ I, the projection from Π i : I, α i to Π i : J, α i maps P I to P J.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.Besicovitch
nodes.description: The topological Besicovitch covering theorem ensures that, in a nice metric space, there exists a number N such that, from any family of balls with bounded radii, one can extract N families, each made of disjoint balls, covering together all the centers of the initial family.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.BesicovitchVectorSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Satellite configurations for Besicovitch covering lemma in vector spaces
nodes.description: The Besicovitch covering theorem ensures that, in a nice metric space, there exists a number N such that, from any family of balls with bounded radii, one can extract N families, each made of disjoint balls, covering together all the centers of the initial family.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.DensityTheorem
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniformly locally doubling measures and Lebesgue's density theorem
nodes.description: Lebesgue's density theorem states that given a set S in a sigma compact metric space with locally-finite uniformly locally doubling measure μ then for almost all points x in S, for any sequence of closed balls B₀, B₁, B₂, ... containing x, the limit μ (S ∩ Bⱼ) / μ (Bⱼ) → 1 as j → ∞.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.Differentiation
nodes.description: On a second countable metric space with a measure μ, consider a Vitali family (i.e., for each x one has a family of sets shrinking to x, with a good behavior with respect to covering theorems). Consider also another measure ρ. Then, for almost every x, the ratio ρ a / μ a converges when a shrinks to x along the Vitali family, towards the Radon-Nikodym derivative of ρ with respect to μ. This is the main theorem on differentiation of measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.LiminfLimsup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Liminf, limsup, and uniformly locally doubling measures.
nodes.description: This file is a place to collect lemmas about liminf and limsup for subsets of a metric space carrying a uniformly locally doubling measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.OneDim
nodes.descriptionTitle: Covering theorems for Lebesgue measure in one dimension
nodes.description: We have a general theory of covering theorems for doubling measures, developed notably in DensityTheorem.lean. In this file, we expand the API for this theory in one dimension, by showing that intervals belong to the relevant Vitali family.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.Vitali
nodes.description: The topological Vitali covering theorem, in its most classical version, states the following. Consider a family of balls (B (x_i, r_i))_{i ∈ I} in a metric space, with uniformly bounded radii. Then one can extract a disjoint subfamily indexed by J ⊆ I, such that any B (x_i, r_i) is included in a ball B (x_j, 5 r_j).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Covering.VitaliFamily
nodes.description: On a metric space X with a measure μ, consider for each x : X a family of measurable sets with nonempty interiors, called setsAt x. This family is a Vitali family if it satisfies the following property: consider a (possibly non-measurable) set s, and for any x in s a subfamily f x of setsAt x containing sets of arbitrarily small diameter. Then one can extract a disjoint subfamily covering almost all s.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEEqFun
nodes.description: We build a space of equivalence classes of functions, where two functions are treated as identical if they are almost everywhere equal. We form the set of equivalence classes under the relation of being almost everywhere equal, which is sometimes known as the L⁰ space. To use this space as a basis for the L^p spaces and for the Bochner integral, we consider equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions (or, equivalently, of almost everywhere strongly measurable functions.)

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEEqFun.DomAct
nodes.descriptionTitle: Action of DomMulAct and DomAddAct on α →ₘ[μ] β
nodes.description: If M acts on α by measure-preserving transformations, then Mᵈᵐᵃ acts on α →ₘ[μ] β by sending each function f to f ∘ (DomMulAct.mk.symm c • ·). We define this action and basic instances about it.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEEqOfIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: From equality of integrals to equality of functions
nodes.description: This file provides various statements of the general form "if two functions have the same integral on all sets, then they are equal almost everywhere". The different lemmas use various hypotheses on the class of functions, on the target space or on the possible finiteness of the measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEEqOfLIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: From equality of integrals to equality of functions
nodes.description: This file provides various statements of the general form "if two functions have the same integral on all sets, then they are equal almost everywhere". The different lemmas use various hypotheses on the class of functions, on the target space or on the possible finiteness of the measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEMeasurableOrder
nodes.description: Consider a function f : α → ℝ≥0∞. If the level sets {f < p} and {q < f} have measurable supersets which are disjoint up to measure zero when p and q are finite numbers satisfying p < q, then f is almost-everywhere measurable.
