This is proved in ENNReal.aemeasurable_of_exist_almost_disjoint_supersets, and deduced from an analogous statement for any target space which is a complete linear dense order, called MeasureTheory.aemeasurable_of_exist_almost_disjoint_supersets.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AEMeasurableSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sequence of measurable functions associated to a sequence of a.e.-measurable functions
nodes.description: We define here tools to prove statements about limits (infi, supr...) of sequences of AEMeasurable functions. Given a sequence of a.e.-measurable functions f : ι → α → β with hypothesis hf : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (f i) μ, and a pointwise property p : α → (ι → β) → Prop such that we have hp : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x (fun n ↦ f n x), we define a sequence of measurable functions aeSeq hf p and a measurable set aeSeqSet hf p, such that

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.AbsolutelyContinuous
nodes.description: This file defines absolutely continuous functions on a closed interval uIcc a b and proves some basic properties about absolutely continuous functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.AEMeasurable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions a.e. measurable with respect to a sub-σ-algebra
nodes.description: A function f verifies AEStronglyMeasurable[m] f μ if it is μ-a.e. equal to an m-strongly measurable function. This is similar to AEStronglyMeasurable, but the MeasurableSpace structures used for the measurability statement and for the measure are different.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic
nodes.description: We build the conditional expectation of an integrable function f with value in a Banach space with respect to a measure μ (defined on a measurable space structure m₀) and a measurable space structure m with hm : m ≤ m₀ (a sub-sigma-algebra). This is an m-strongly measurable function μ[f|hm] which is integrable and verifies ∫ x in s, μ[f|hm] x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ for all m-measurable sets s. It is unique as an element of L¹.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.CondJensen
nodes.description: This file contains the conditional Jensen's inequality. We follow the proof in [Hytonen_VanNeerven_Veraar_Wies_2016].

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.CondexpL1
nodes.description: This file contains two more steps of the construction of the conditional expectation, which is completed in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean. See that file for a description of the full process.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.CondexpL2
nodes.description: This file contains one step of the construction of the conditional expectation, which is completed in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean. See that file for a description of the full process.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Indicator
nodes.description: This file proves some results about the conditional expectation of an indicator function and as a corollary, also proves several results about the behaviour of the conditional expectation on a restricted measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.LebesgueBochner
nodes.description: For non-negative real functions, we have two versions of the conditional expectation: condExp and condLExp, built from the Bochner and Lebesgue integrals respectively. In this file, we gather results that involve both versions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.PullOut
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pull-out property of the conditional expectation
nodes.description: Let Ω be endowed with a measurable space structure mΩ, and let m : MeasurableSpace Ω such that m ≤ mΩ. Let μ be a measure over Ω. Let B : F →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] G a continuous bilinear map, f : Ω → F and g : Ω → E such that fun ω ↦ B (f ω) (g ω) is integrable, g is integrable and f is AEStronglyMeasurable with respect to m. The pull-out property of the conditional expectation states that almost surely, μ[B f g|m] = B f μ[g|m].

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.RadonNikodym
nodes.description: We express the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the pushforward of measures in terms of the conditional expectation of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the original measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Real
nodes.description: This file proves some results regarding the conditional expectation of real-valued functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Unique
nodes.description: Two Lp functions f, g which are almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to a σ-algebra m and verify ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, g x ∂μ for all m-measurable sets s are equal almost everywhere. This proves the uniqueness of the conditional expectation, which is not yet defined in this file but is introduced in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalLExpectation
nodes.description: We define the conditional expectation of a ℝ≥0∞-valued function using the Lebesgue integral. Given a measure P : Measure[mΩ₀] Ω and a sub-σ-algebra mΩ of mΩ₀ (meaning hm : mΩ ≤ mΩ₀) and a function X : Ω → ℝ≥0∞, if P.trim hm is σ-finite, then the conditional (Lebesgue) expectation P⁻[X|mΩ] of X is the mΩ-measurable function such that for all mΩ-measurable sets s, ∫⁻ ω in s, P⁻[X|mΩ] ω ∂P = ∫⁻ ω in s, X ω ∂P (see setLIntegral_condLExp). This is unique up to P-ae equality (see ae_eq_condLExp).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense
nodes.descriptionTitle: Approximation in Lᵖ by continuous functions
nodes.description: This file proves that bounded continuous functions are dense in Lp E p μ, for p < ∞, if the domain α of the functions is a normal topological space and the measure μ is weakly regular. It also proves the same results for approximation by continuous functions with compact support when the space is locally compact and μ is regular.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInDistribution
nodes.description: We introduce a definition of convergence in distribution of random variables: this is the weak convergence of the laws of the random variables. In Mathlib terms this is a Tendsto in the ProbabilityMeasure type.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInMeasure
nodes.description: We define convergence in measure which is one of the many notions of convergence in probability. A sequence of functions f is said to converge in measure to some function g if for all ε > 0, the measure of the set {x | ε ≤ edist (f i x) (g x)} tends to 0 as i converges along some given filter l.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Egorov
nodes.description: This file contains the Egorov theorem which states that an almost everywhere convergent sequence on a finite measure space converges uniformly except on an arbitrarily small set. This theorem is useful for the Vitali convergence theorem as well as theorems regarding convergence in measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.EssSup
nodes.description: We define the essential supremum and infimum of a function f : α → β with respect to a measure μ on α. The essential supremum is the infimum of the constants c : β such that f x ≤ c almost everywhere.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.FactorsThrough
nodes.descriptionTitle: Factorization of a map from measurability
nodes.description: Consider f : X → Y and g : X → Z and assume that g is measurable with respect to the pullback along f. Then g factors through f, which means that (if Z is nonempty) there exists h : Y → Z such that g = h ∘ f.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Floor
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Int.floor, Int.ceil, Int.fract, Nat.floor, and Nat.ceil are measurable under some assumptions on the (semi)ring.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Holder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous bilinear maps on MeasureTheory.Lp spaces
nodes.description: Given a continuous bilinear map B : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G, we define an associated map ContinuousLinearMap.holder : Lp E p μ → Lp F q μ → Lp G r μ where p q r are a Hölder triple. We bundle this into a bilinear map ContinuousLinearMap.holderₗ and a continuous bilinear map ContinuousLinearMap.holderL under some additional assumptions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Intersectivity
nodes.description: This file proves the Bergelson intersectivity lemma: In a finite measure space, a sequence of events that have measure at least r has an infinite subset whose finite intersections all have positive volume.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Jacobian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Change of variables in higher-dimensional integrals
nodes.description: Let μ be a Lebesgue measure on a finite-dimensional real vector space E. Let f : E → E be a function which is injective and differentiable on a measurable set s, with derivative f'. Then we prove that f '' s is measurable, and its measure is given by the formula μ (f '' s) = ∫⁻ x in s, |(f' x).det| ∂μ (where (f' x).det is almost everywhere measurable, but not Borel-measurable in general). This formula is proved in lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_eq_addHaar_image.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.JacobianOneDim
nodes.descriptionTitle: Change of variable formulas for integrals in dimension 1
nodes.description: We record in this file versions of the general change of variables formula in integrals for functions from ℝ to ℝ. This makes it possible to replace the determinant of the Fréchet derivative with the one-dimensional derivative.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.AEEqFun
nodes.description: In this file we establish an API between Integrable and the space L¹ of equivalence classes of integrable functions, already defined as a special case of L^p spaces for p = 1.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.HasFiniteIntegral
nodes.description: In this file we define the predicate HasFiniteIntegral, which is then used to define the predicate Integrable in the corresponding file.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.L1Space.Integrable
nodes.description: In this file, the predicate Integrable is defined and basic properties of integrable functions are proved.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
nodes.description: If E is an inner product space over 𝕜 (ℝ or ℂ), then Lp E 2 μ (defined in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSpace/Basic.lean) is also an inner product space, with inner product defined as inner f g := ∫ a, ⟪f a, g a⟫ ∂μ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LocallyIntegrable
nodes.description: A function is called locally integrable (MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable) if it is integrable on a neighborhood of every point. More generally, it is locally integrable on s if it is locally integrable on a neighbourhood within s of any point of s.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpOrder
nodes.descriptionTitle: Order related properties of Lp spaces
nodes.description: PosPart.pos and NegPart.neg given by the lattice structure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Basic.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.ChebyshevMarkov
nodes.descriptionTitle: Chebyshev-Markov inequality in terms of Lp seminorms
nodes.description: In this file we formulate several versions of the Chebyshev-Markov inequality in terms of the MeasureTheory.eLpNorm seminorm.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.CompareExp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compare Lp seminorms for different values of p
nodes.description: In this file we compare MeasureTheory.eLpNorm' and MeasureTheory.eLpNorm for different exponents.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Count
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Count.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Defs
nodes.description: This file describes properties of almost everywhere strongly measurable functions with finite p-seminorm, denoted by eLpNorm f p μ and defined for p:ℝ≥0∞ as 0 if p=0, (∫ ‖f a‖^p ∂μ) ^ (1/p) for 0 < p < ∞ and essSup ‖f‖ μ for p=∞.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Indicator
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Indicator.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.LpNorm
nodes.description: This file proves theorems about MeasureTheory.lpNorm, a real-valued version of MeasureTheory.eLpNorm.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Monotonicity
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Monotonicity.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Prod
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Prod.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.SMul
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.SMul.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.TriangleInequality
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the triangle inequality for the Lp seminorm, as well as simple corollaries.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSeminorm.Trim
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lp seminorm with respect to trimmed measure
nodes.description: In this file we prove basic properties of the Lp-seminorm of a function with respect to the restriction of a measure to a sub-σ-algebra.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Basic
nodes.description: This file provides the space Lp E p μ as the subtype of elements of α →ₘ[μ] E (see MeasureTheory.AEEqFun) such that eLpNorm f p μ is finite. For 1 ≤ p, eLpNorm defines a norm and Lp is a complete metric space (the latter is proved at Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSpace/Complete.lean).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Complete
nodes.description: In this file we show that Lp is a complete space for 1 ≤ p, in MeasureTheory.Lp.instCompleteSpace.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.CompleteOfCompleteLp
nodes.descriptionTitle: If an Lp space is complete, so is the target space
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.CompleteOfCompleteLp.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.ContinuousCompMeasurePreserving
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the composition of an L^p function g with a continuous measure-preserving map f is continuous in both arguments.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.ContinuousFunctions
nodes.description: When α is a topological space equipped with a finite Borel measure, there is a bounded linear map from the normed space of bounded continuous functions (α →ᵇ E) to Lp E p μ. We construct this as BoundedContinuousFunction.toLp.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.DomAct.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Action of Mᵈᵐᵃ on Lᵖ spaces
nodes.description: In this file we define action of Mᵈᵐᵃ on MeasureTheory.Lp E p μ If f : α → E is a function representing an equivalence class in Lᵖ(α, E), M acts on α, and c : M, then (.mk c : Mᵈᵐᵃ) • [f] is represented by the function a ↦ f (c • a).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.DomAct.Continuous
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuity of the action of Mᵈᵐᵃ on MeasureSpace.Lp E p μ
nodes.description: In this file we prove that under certain conditions, the action of Mᵈᵐᵃ on MeasureTheory.Lp E p μ is continuous in both variables.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Indicator
nodes.descriptionTitle: Indicator of a set as an element of Lp
nodes.description: For a set s with (hs : MeasurableSet s) and (hμs : μ s c).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.Piecewise
nodes.description: In this file, we prove some results about measurability of functions defined by using IndexedPartition.piecewise.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFunc
nodes.description: A function f from a measurable space to any type is called simple, if every preimage f ⁻¹' {x} is measurable, and the range is finite. In this file, we define simple functions and establish their basic properties; and we construct a sequence of simple functions approximating an arbitrary Borel measurable function f : α → ℝ≥0∞.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFuncDense
nodes.description: Show that each Borel measurable function can be approximated pointwise by a sequence of simple functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFuncDenseLp
nodes.description: Show that each Lᵖ Borel measurable function can be approximated in Lᵖ norm by a sequence of simple functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Arctan
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Arctan.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability of real and complex functions
nodes.description: We show that most standard real and complex functions are measurable, notably exp, cos, sin, cosh, sinh, log, pow, arcsin, arccos.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Inner
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Inner.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.RCLike
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability of the basic RCLike functions
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.RCLike.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Sinc
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability and integrability of the sinc function
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.SpecialFunctions.Sinc.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.AEStronglyMeasurable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Strongly measurable and finitely strongly measurable functions
nodes.description: A function f is said to be almost everywhere strongly measurable if f is almost everywhere equal to a strongly measurable function, i.e. the sequential limit of simple functions. It is said to be almost everywhere finitely strongly measurable with respect to a measure μ if the supports of those simple functions have finite measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Strongly measurable and finitely strongly measurable functions
nodes.description: A function f is said to be strongly measurable if f is the sequential limit of simple functions. It is said to be finitely strongly measurable with respect to a measure μ if the supports of those simple functions have finite measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.ENNReal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finitely strongly measurable functions with value in ENNReal
nodes.description: A measurable function with finite Lebesgue integral can be approximated by simple functions whose support has finite measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Inner
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inner products of strongly measurable functions are strongly measurable.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Inner.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Lemmas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Strongly measurable and finitely strongly measurable functions
nodes.description: This file contains some further development of strongly measurable and finitely strongly measurable functions, started in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/StronglyMeasurable/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Lp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finitely strongly measurable functions in Lp
nodes.description: Functions in Lp for 0 < p < ∞ are finitely strongly measurable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.UnifTight
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions for uniform tightness for a family of Lp functions. It is used as a hypothesis to the version of Vitali's convergence theorem for Lp spaces that works also for spaces of infinite measure. This version of Vitali's theorem is also proved later in the file.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Function.UniformIntegrable
nodes.description: This file contains the definitions for uniform integrability (both in the measure theory sense as well as the probability theory sense). This file also contains the Vitali convergence theorem which establishes a relation between uniform integrability, convergence in measure and Lp convergence.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.AEStabilizer
nodes.description: In this file we define the a.e. stabilizer of a set under a measure-preserving group action.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Action
nodes.description: A measure μ : Measure α is said to be invariant under an action of a group G if scalar multiplication by c : G is a measure-preserving map for all c. In this file we define a typeclass for measures invariant under action of an (additive or multiplicative) group and prove some basic properties of such measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.AddCircle
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measure-theoretic results about the additive circle
nodes.description: The file is a place to collect measure-theoretic results about the additive circle.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Arithmetic
nodes.description: In this file we define classes MeasurableMul etc. and prove dot-style lemmas (Measurable.mul, AEMeasurable.mul etc). For binary operations we define two typeclasses:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Convolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: The multiplicative and additive convolution of measures
nodes.description: In this file we define and prove properties about the convolutions of two measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define typeclasses for measures invariant under (scalar) multiplication.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.FoelnerFilter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Følner sequences and filters - definitions and properties
nodes.description: This file defines Følner sequences and filters for measurable spaces acted on by a group.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.FundamentalDomain
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fundamental domain of a group action
nodes.description: A set s is said to be a fundamental domain of an action of a group G on a measurable space α with respect to a measure μ if

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.GeometryOfNumbers
nodes.description: In this file we prove some of the fundamental theorems in the geometry of numbers, as studied by Hermann Minkowski.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Integral
nodes.description: We develop properties of integrals with a group as domain. This file contains properties about integrability and Bochner integration.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.IntegralConvolution
nodes.description: This file contains results about the Bochner integrals of convolutions of measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.LIntegral
nodes.description: We develop properties of integrals with a group as domain. This file contains properties about Lebesgue integration.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.MeasurableEquiv
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Scalar) multiplication and (vector) addition as measurable equivalences
nodes.description: In this file we define the following measurable equivalences:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Measure
nodes.description: We develop some properties of measures on (topological) groups

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.ModularCharacter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Modular character of a locally compact group
nodes.description: On a locally compact group, there is a natural homomorphism G → ℝ≥0, which for g : G gives the value μ (· g⁻¹) / μ, where μ is an (inner regular) Haar measure. This file defines this homomorphism, called the modular character, and shows that it is independent of the chosen Haar measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Pointwise
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the following fact: if s is a measurable set, then so is a • s. Note that the pointwise product of two measurable sets need not be measurable, so there is no MeasurableSet.mul etc.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Group.Prod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measure theory in the product of groups
nodes.description: In this file we show properties about measure theory in products of measurable groups and properties of iterated integrals in measurable groups.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Asymptotics
nodes.description: We establish integrability of f from f = O(g).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Average
nodes.description: In this file we define MeasureTheory.average μ f (notation: ⨍ x, f x ∂μ) to be the average value of f with respect to measure μ. It is defined as ∫ x, f x ∂((μ univ)⁻¹ • μ), so it is equal to zero if f is not integrable or if μ is an infinite measure. If μ is a probability measure, then the average of any function is equal to its integral.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
nodes.description: The Bochner integral extends the definition of the Lebesgue integral to functions that map from a measure space into a Banach space (complete normed vector space). It is constructed here using the L1 Bochner integral constructed in the file Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/L1.lean.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.ContinuousLinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous linear maps composed with integration
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to prove that integration commutes with continuous linear maps. This holds for simple functions. The general result follows from the continuity of all involved operations on the space L¹. Note that composition by a continuous linear map on L¹ is not just the composition, as we are dealing with classes of functions, but it has already been defined as ContinuousLinearMap.compLp. We take advantage of this construction here.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.FundThmCalculus
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fundamental theorem of calculus for set integrals
nodes.description: This file proves a version of the Fundamental theorem of calculus for set integrals. See Filter.Tendsto.integral_sub_linear_isLittleO_ae and its corollaries.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.L1
nodes.description: The Bochner integral extends the definition of the Lebesgue integral to functions that map from a measure space into a Banach space (complete normed vector space). It is constructed here for L1 functions by extending the integral on simple functions. See the file Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean for the integral of functions and corresponding API.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Set
nodes.description: In this file we prove some properties of ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ. Recall that this notation is defined as ∫ x, f x ∂(μ.restrict s). In integral_indicator we prove that for a measurable function f and a measurable set s this definition coincides with another natural definition: ∫ x, indicator s f x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ, where indicator s f x is equal to f x for x ∈ s and is zero otherwise.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.SumMeasure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral with respect to a sum of measures
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a function f is integrable with respect to a countable sum of measures Measure.sum μ if and only if f is integrable with respect to each μ i and the sequence fun i ↦ ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ∂μ i is summable. We then show that under this integrability condition, ∫ x, f x ∂Measure.sum μ = ∑' i, ∫ f x ∂μ i.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.VitaliCaratheodory
nodes.description: Vitali-Carathéodory theorem asserts the following. Consider an integrable function f : α → ℝ on a space with a regular measure. Then there exists a function g : α → EReal such that f x < g x everywhere, g is lower semicontinuous, and the integral of g is arbitrarily close to that of f. This theorem is proved in this file, as exists_lt_lower_semicontinuous_integral_lt.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.BoundedContinuousFunction
nodes.description: In this file, some results are collected about integrals of bounded continuous functions. They are mostly specializations of results in general integration theory, but they are used directly in this specialized form in some other files, in particular in those related to the topology of weak convergence of probability measures and finite measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CircleAverage
nodes.description: For a function f on the complex plane, this file introduces the definition Real.circleAverage f c R as a shorthand for the average of f on the circle with center c and radius R, equipped with the rotation-invariant measure of total volume one. Like IntervalAverage, this notion exists as a convenience. It avoids notationally inconvenient compositions of f with circleMap and avoids the need to manually eliminate 2 π every time an average is computed.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CircleIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral over a circle in ℂ
nodes.description: In this file we define ∮ z in C(c, R), f z to be the integral $\oint_{|z-c|=|R|} f(z)\,dz$ and prove some properties of this integral. We give definition and prove most lemmas for a function f : ℂ → E, where E is a complex Banach space. For this reason, some lemmas use, e.g., (z - c)⁻¹ • f z instead of f z / (z - c).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CircleTransform
nodes.description: In this file we define the circle integral transform of a function f with complex domain. This is defined as $(2πi)^{-1}\frac{f(x)}{x-w}$ where x moves along a circle. We then prove some basic facts about these functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CompactlySupported
nodes.description: This file contains definitions and lemmas related to integrals of compactly supported continuous functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CurveIntegral.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral of a 1-form along a path
nodes.description: In this file we define the integral of a 1-form along a path indexed by [0, 1] and prove basic properties of this operation.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.CurveIntegral.Poincare
nodes.description: In this file we prove Poincaré lemma for 1-forms for convex sets. Namely, we show that a closed 1-form on a convex subset of a normed space is exact.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Divergence theorem for Bochner integral on a box in ℝⁿ⁺¹ = Fin (n + 1) → ℝ. More precisely, we prove the following theorem.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.DominatedConvergence
nodes.description: This file collects various results related to the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for the Bochner integral.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.ExpDecay
nodes.description: As easy special cases of general theorems in the library, we prove the following test for integrability:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.FinMeasAdditive
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additivity on measurable sets with finite measure
nodes.description: Let T : Set α → E →L[ℝ] F be additive for measurable sets with finite measure, in the sense that for s, t two such sets, Disjoint s t → T (s ∪ t) = T s + T t. T is akin to a bilinear map on Set α × E, or a linear map on indicator functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Gamma
nodes.description: In this file, we collect several integrals over ℝ or ℂ that evaluate in terms of the Real.Gamma function.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Indicator
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about indicator functions, their integrals, and measures
nodes.description: This file has a few measure-theoretic or integration-related results on indicator functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegrableOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Functions integrable on a set and at a filter
nodes.description: We define IntegrableOn f s μ := Integrable f (μ.restrict s) and prove theorems like integrableOn_union : IntegrableOn f (s ∪ t) μ ↔ IntegrableOn f s μ ∧ IntegrableOn f t μ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegralEqImproper
nodes.descriptionTitle: Links between an integral and its "improper" version
nodes.description: In its current state, mathlib only knows how to talk about definite ("proper") integrals, in the sense that it treats integrals over [x, +∞) the same as it treats integrals over [y, z]. For example, the integral over [1, +∞) is not defined to be the limit of the integral over [1, x] as x tends to +∞, which is known as an improper integral.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalAverage
nodes.description: In this file we introduce notation ⨍ x in a..b, f x for the average ⨍ x in Ι a b, f x of f over the interval Ι a b = Set.Ioc (min a b) (max a b) w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure, then prove formulas for this average:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.AbsolutelyContinuousFun
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fundamental theorem of calculus and integration by parts for absolutely continuous functions
nodes.description: This file proves that: uIcc a b, then Fundamental Theorem of Calculus holds for f' on a..b, i.e. ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, deriv f x = f b - f a. Integration by Parts holds for absolutely continuous functions, i.e. if f and g are absolutely continuous on uIcc a b, then ∫ x in a..b, f x deriv g x = f b g b - f a g a - ∫ x in a..b, deriv f x g x.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ to be ∫ x in Ioc a b, f x ∂μ if a ≤ b and -∫ x in Ioc b a, f x ∂μ if b ≤ a.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.ContDiff
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fundamental theorem of calculus for C^1 functions
nodes.description: We give versions of the second fundamental theorem of calculus under the strong assumption that the function is C^1 on the interval. This is restrictive, but satisfied in many situations.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable
nodes.descriptionTitle: f' is interval integrable for certain classes of functions f
nodes.description: This file proves that: integrable on a..b. f' on a..b is in uIcc 0 (f b - f a). then f' is interval integrable on a..b. a..b, then f' is interval integrable on a..b.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DistLEIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Displacement is at most the integral of the speed
nodes.description: In this file we prove several version of the following fact: the displacement (dist (f a) (f b)) is at most the integral of ‖deriv f‖ over [a, b].

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.FundThmCalculus
nodes.description: We prove various versions of the fundamental theorem of calculus for interval integrals in ℝ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.IntegrationByParts
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integration by parts and by substitution
nodes.description: We derive additional integration techniques from FTC-2:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.LebesgueDifferentiationThm
nodes.description: This file proves the interval version of the Lebesgue Differentiation Theorem. There are two versions in this file.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.MeanValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: First mean value theorem for interval integrals
nodes.description: We prove versions of the first mean value theorem for interval integrals.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.Periodic
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the half-open interval Ioc t (t + T) in ℝ is a fundamental domain of the action of the subgroup ℤ ∙ T on ℝ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.Slope
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some properties of the interval integral of fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c), given a constant c : ℝ
nodes.description: This file proves that: where a ≤ b and 0 ≤ c, then fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c) is interval integrable on a..b. where a ≤ b and 0 ≤ c, then fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c) is interval integrable on a..b. where a ≤ b and 0 ≤ c, then the interval integral of fun x ↦ slope f x (x + c) on a..b is at most f (b + c) - f a.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.TrapezoidalRule
nodes.description: This file contains a definition of integration on [[a, b]] via the trapezoidal rule, along with an error bound in terms of a bound on the second derivative of the integrand.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Layercake
nodes.descriptionTitle: The layer cake formula / Cavalieri's principle / tail probability formula
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following layer cake formula.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Add
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monotone convergence theorem and addition of Lebesgue integrals
nodes.description: The monotone convergence theorem (aka Beppo Levi lemma) states that the Lebesgue integral and supremum can be swapped for a pointwise monotone sequence of functions. This file first proves several variants of this theorem, then uses it to show that the Lebesgue integral is additive (assuming one of the functions is at least AEMeasurable) and respects multiplication by a constant.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lower Lebesgue integral for ℝ≥0∞-valued functions
nodes.description: We define the lower Lebesgue integral of an ℝ≥0∞-valued function.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Countable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lebesgue integral over finite and countable types, sets and measures
nodes.description: The lemmas in this file require at least one of the following of the Lebesgue integral:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.DominatedConvergence
nodes.description: Lebesgue's dominated convergence theorem states that the limit and Lebesgue integral of a sequence of (almost everywhere) measurable functions can be swapped if the functions are pointwise dominated by a fixed function. This file provides a few variants of the result.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Map
nodes.descriptionTitle: Behavior of the Lebesgue integral under maps
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Map.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Markov
nodes.description: The classical form of Markov's inequality states that for a nonnegative random variable X and real number ε > 0, P(X ≥ ε) ≤ E(X) / ε. Multiplying both sides by the measure of the space gives the measure-theoretic form: This file proves a few variants of the inequality and other lemmas that depend on it.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Norm
nodes.descriptionTitle: Interactions between the Lebesgue integral and norms
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Norm.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Lebesgue.Sub
nodes.description: In this file we first show that Lebesgue integrals can be subtracted with the expected results – ∫⁻ f - ∫⁻ g ≤ ∫⁻ (f - g), with equality if g ≤ f almost everywhere. Then we prove variants of the monotone convergence theorem that use this subtraction in their proofs.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.LebesgueNormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: A lemma about measurability with density under scalar multiplication in normed spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Integral.LebesgueNormedSpace.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Marginal
nodes.description: In this file, we define a convenient way to compute integrals of multivariate functions, especially if you want to write expressions where you integrate only over some of the variables that the function depends on. This is common in induction arguments involving integrals of multivariate functions. This constructions allows working with iterated integrals and applying Tonelli's theorem and Fubini's theorem, without using measurable equivalences by changing the representation of your space (e.g.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.MeanInequalities
nodes.description: In this file we prove several inequalities on integrals, notably the Hölder inequality and the Minkowski inequality. The versions for finite sums are in Analysis.MeanInequalities.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.MeanValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: First mean value theorem for set integrals
nodes.description: We prove versions of the first mean value theorem for set integrals.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.PeakFunction
nodes.description: A sequence of peak functions is a sequence of functions with average one concentrating around a point x₀. Given such a sequence φₙ, then ∫ φₙ g tends to g x₀ in many situations, with a whole zoo of possible assumptions on φₙ and g. This file is devoted to such results. Such functions are also called approximations of unity, or approximations of identity.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Pi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integration with respect to a finite product of measures
nodes.description: On a finite product of measure spaces, we show that a product of integrable functions each depending on a single coordinate is integrable, in MeasureTheory.integrable_fintype_prod, and that its integral is the product of the individual integrals, in MeasureTheory.integral_fintype_prod_eq_prod.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integration with respect to the product measure
nodes.description: In this file we prove Fubini's theorem.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.Regular
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrals of continuous functions with respect to regular measures
nodes.description: When a measure is regular, one may express the measure of compact sets and of open sets in terms of the integral of continuous functions equal to 1 on the compact set, or to 0 outside of the open set respectively.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.RieszMarkovKakutani.Basic
nodes.description: This file prepares technical definitions and results for the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem on a locally compact T2 space X. As a special case, the statements about linear functionals on bounded continuous functions follows. Actual theorems, depending on the linearity (ℝ, ℝ≥0 or ℂ), are proven in separate files (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/NNReal.lean...)

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.RieszMarkovKakutani.NNReal
nodes.description: This file proves the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem on a locally compact T2 space X for ℝ≥0-linear functionals Λ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.RieszMarkovKakutani.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation theorem for real-linear functionals
nodes.description: The Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation theorem relates linear functionals on spaces of continuous functions on a locally compact space to measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.SetToL1
nodes.descriptionTitle: Extension of a linear function from indicators to L1
nodes.description: Given T : Set α → E →L[ℝ] F with DominatedFinMeasAdditive μ T C, we construct an extension of T to integrable simple functions, which are finite sums of indicators of measurable sets with finite measure, then to integrable functions, which are limits of integrable simple functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Integral.TorusIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral over a torus in ℂⁿ
nodes.description: In this file we define the integral of a function f : ℂⁿ → E over a torus {z : ℂⁿ | ∀ i, z i ∈ Metric.sphere (c i) (R i)}. In order to do this, we define torusMap (c : ℂⁿ) (R θ : ℝⁿ) to be the point in ℂⁿ given by $z_k=c_k+R_ke^{θ_ki}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit, then define torusIntegral f c R as the integral over the cube $[0, (fun _ ↦ 2π)] = \{θ\|∀ k, 0 ≤ θ_k ≤ 2π\}$ of the Jacobian of the torusMap multiplied by f (torusMap c R θ).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Basic
nodes.description: This file provides properties of measurable spaces and the functions and isomorphisms between them. The definition of a measurable space is in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Defs.lean.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Card
nodes.description: If a sigma-algebra is generated by a set of sets s, then the cardinality of the sigma-algebra is bounded by (max #s 2) ^ ℵ₀. This is stated in MeasurableSpace.cardinal_generate_measurable_le and MeasurableSpace.cardinalMeasurableSet_le.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructions for measurable spaces and functions
nodes.description: This file provides several ways to construct new measurable spaces and functions from old ones: Quotient, Subtype, Prod, Pi, etc.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.CountablyGenerated
nodes.description: We say a measurable space is countably generated if it can be generated by a countable set of sets.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines measurable spaces and measurable functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Embedding
nodes.description: A measurable equivalence between measurable spaces is an equivalence which respects the σ-algebras, that is, for which both directions of the equivalence are measurable functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.EventuallyMeasurable
nodes.description: In this file we consider the general notion of measurability modulo a σ-filter. Two important instances of this construction are null-measurability with respect to a measure, where the filter is the collection of co-null sets, and Baire-measurability with respect to a topology, where the filter is the collection of comeager (residual) sets. (not to be confused with measurability with respect to the sigma algebra of Baire sets, which is sometimes also called this.) TODO: Implement the latter.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Instances
nodes.description: This file provides measurable-space instances for a selection of standard countable types, in each case defining the Σ-algebra to be ⊤ (the discrete measurable-space structure).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Invariants
nodes.descriptionTitle: σ-algebra of sets invariant under a self-map
nodes.description: In this file we define MeasurableSpace.invariants (f : α → α) to be the σ-algebra of sets s : Set α such that

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.MeasurablyGenerated
nodes.description: We say that a filter f is measurably generated if every set s ∈ f includes a measurable set t ∈ f. This property is useful, e.g., to extract a measurable witness of Filter.Eventually.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.NCard
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Set.encard and Set.ncard are measurable functions, provided that the ambient space is countable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Pi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bases of the indexed product σ-algebra
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the following lemma:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.PreorderRestrict
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability of the restriction function for functions indexed by a preorder
nodes.description: We prove that the map which restricts a function f : (i : α) → X i to elements ≤ a is measurable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.Prod
nodes.description: This file talks about the measurability of operations on binary functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.AEDisjoint
nodes.description: We say that sets s and t are μ-a.e. disjoint (see MeasureTheory.AEDisjoint) if their intersection has measure zero. This assumption can be used instead of Disjoint in most theorems in measure theory.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.AEMeasurable
nodes.description: A function is almost everywhere measurable if it coincides almost everywhere with a measurable function. This property, called AEMeasurable f μ, is defined in the file MeasureSpaceDef. We discuss several of its properties that are analogous to properties of measurable functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous
nodes.description: We say that μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν, or that μ is dominated by ν, if ν(A) = 0 implies that μ(A) = 0. We denote that by μ ≪ ν.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.AddContent
nodes.description: An additive content m on a set of sets C is a set function with value 0 at the empty set which is finitely additive on C. That means that for any finset I of pairwise disjoint sets in C such that ⋃₀ I ∈ C, m (⋃₀ I) = ∑ s ∈ I, m s.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.CharacteristicFunction
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in MeasureTheory.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.CharacteristicFunction.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characteristic Function of a Finite Measure
nodes.description: This file defines the characteristic function of a finite measure on a topological vector space V.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.CharacteristicFunction.TaylorExpansion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Taylor expansion of the characteristic function
nodes.description: This file provides the Taylor expansion of the characteristic function of a measure at 0.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Comap
nodes.description: In this file we define the pullback MeasureTheory.Measure.comap f μ of a measure μ along an injective map f such that the image of any measurable set under f is a null-measurable set. If f does not have these properties, then we define comap f μ to be zero.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Complex
nodes.description: This file defines a complex measure to be a vector measure with codomain ℂ. Then we prove some elementary results about complex measures. In particular, we prove that a complex measure is always in the form s + it where s and t are signed measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Content
nodes.description: In this file we work with contents. A content λ is a function from a certain class of subsets (such as the compact subsets) to ℝ≥0 that is then λ(K₁ ∪ K₂) = λ(K₁) + λ(K₂);

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.ContinuousPreimage
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuity of the preimage of a set under a measure-preserving continuous function
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the preimage of a null measurable set s : Set Y under a measure-preserving continuous function f : C(X, Y) is continuous in f in the sense that μ ((f a ⁻¹' s) ∆ (g ⁻¹' s)) tends to zero as f a tends to g.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Count
nodes.description: In this file we define the counting measure MeasureTheory.Measure.count as MeasureTheory.Measure.sum MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac and prove basic properties of this measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.Exhaustion
nodes.description: If μ, ν are two measures with ν s-finite, then there exists a set s such that μ is sigma-finite on s, and for all sets t ⊆ sᶜ, either ν t = 0 or μ t = ∞.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.Hahn
nodes.description: This file proves the unsigned version of the Hahn decomposition theorem.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.IntegralRNDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrals of functions of Radon-Nikodym derivatives
nodes.description: is absolutely continuous with respect to ν, then ν.real univ f (μ.real univ / ν.real univ) ≤ ∫ x, f (μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal ∂ν. if f ((μ ⊗ₘ κ).rnDeriv (ν ⊗ₘ η) (a, b)) is integrable, then f (μ.rnDeriv ν a) is integrable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.Lebesgue
nodes.description: This file proves the Lebesgue decomposition theorem. The Lebesgue decomposition theorem states that, given two σ-finite measures μ and ν, there exists a σ-finite measure ξ and a measurable function f such that μ = ξ + fν and ξ is mutually singular with respect to ν.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Decomposition.RadonNikodym
nodes.description: This file proves the Radon-Nikodym theorem. The Radon-Nikodym theorem states that, given measures μ, ν, if HaveLebesgueDecomposition μ ν, then μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν if and only if there exists a measurable function f : α → ℝ≥0∞ such that μ = fν. In particular, we have f = rnDeriv μ ν.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Dirac
nodes.description: In this file we define the Dirac measure MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac a and prove some basic facts about it.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.DiracProba
nodes.descriptionTitle: Dirac deltas as probability measures and embedding of a space into probability measures on it
nodes.description: then the mapping that takes a point x : X to the delta-measure diracProba x is an embedding X ↪ ProbabilityMeasure X.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Doubling
nodes.description: A uniformly locally doubling measure μ on a metric space is a measure for which there exists a constant C such that for all sufficiently small radii ε, and for any centre, the measure of a ball of radius 2 ε is bounded by C times the measure of the concentric ball of radius ε.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.EverywherePos
nodes.descriptionTitle: Everywhere positive sets in measure spaces
nodes.description: A set s in a topological space with a measure μ is everywhere positive (also called self-supporting) if any neighborhood n of any point of s satisfies μ (s ∩ n) > 0.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteMeasure
nodes.description: This file defines the type of finite measures on a given measurable space. When the underlying space has a topology and the measurable space structure (sigma algebra) is finer than the Borel sigma algebra, then the type of finite measures is equipped with the topology of weak convergence of measures. The topology of weak convergence is the coarsest topology w.r.t. which for every bounded continuous ℝ≥0-valued function f, the integration of f against the measure is continuous.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteMeasureExt
nodes.description: The main result is ext_of_forall_mem_subalgebra_integral_eq_of_pseudoEMetric_complete_countable: Let A be a StarSubalgebra of C(E, 𝕜) that separates points and whose elements are bounded. If the integrals of all elements of A with respect to two finite measures P, P' coincide, then the measures coincide. In other words: If a subalgebra separates points, it separates finite measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteMeasurePi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Products of finite measures and probability measures
nodes.description: This file introduces finite products of finite measures and probability measures. The constructions are obtained from special cases of products of general measures. Taking products nevertheless has specific properties in the cases of finite measures and probability measures, notably the fact that the product measures depend continuously on their factors in the topology of weak convergence when the underlying space is metrizable and separable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.FiniteMeasureProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Products of finite measures and probability measures
nodes.description: This file introduces binary products of finite measures and probability measures. The constructions are obtained from special cases of products of general measures. Taking products nevertheless has specific properties in the cases of finite measures and probability measures, notably the fact that the product measures depend continuously on their factors in the topology of weak convergence when the underlying space is metrizable and separable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.GiryMonad
nodes.description: Let X be a measurable space. The collection of all measures on X again forms a measurable space. This construction forms a monad on measurable spaces and measurable functions, called the Giry monad.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we prove the existence of Haar measure for a locally compact Hausdorff topological group.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Disintegration
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pushing a Haar measure by a linear map
nodes.description: We show that the push-forward of an additive Haar measure in a vector space under a surjective linear map is proportional to the Haar measure on the target space, in LinearMap.exists_map_addHaar_eq_smul_addHaar.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.DistribChar
nodes.descriptionTitle: The distributive character of Haar measures
nodes.description: Given a group G acting by additive morphisms on a locally compact additive commutative group A, and an element g : G, one can pull back the Haar measure μ of A along the map (g • ·) : A → A to get another Haar measure μ' on A. By unicity of Haar measures, there exists some nonnegative real number r such that μ' = r • μ. We can thus define a map distribHaarChar : G → ℝ≥0 sending g to its associated real number r.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Extension
nodes.description: In this file, if 1 → A → B → C → 1 is a short exact sequence of topological groups, we construct a Haar measure on B from Haar measures on A and C.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.InnerProductSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Volume forms and measures on inner product spaces
nodes.description: A volume form induces a Lebesgue measure on general finite-dimensional real vector spaces. In this file, we discuss the specific situation of inner product spaces, where an orientation gives rise to a canonical volume form. We show that the measure coming from this volume form gives measure 1 to the parallelepiped spanned by any orthonormal basis, and that it coincides with the canonical volume from the MeasureSpace instance.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.MulEquivHaarChar
nodes.descriptionTitle: Scaling Haar measure by a continuous isomorphism
nodes.description: If G is a locally compact topological group and μ is a regular Haar measure on G, then an isomorphism φ : G ≃ₜ G scales this measure by some positive real constant which we call mulEquivHaarChar φ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.NormedSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of Haar measures on real vector spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.NormedSpace.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.OfBasis
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additive Haar measure constructed from a basis
nodes.description: Given a basis of a finite-dimensional real vector space, we define the corresponding Lebesgue measure, which gives measure 1 to the parallelepiped spanned by the basis.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Quotient
nodes.description: In this file, we consider properties of fundamental domains and measures for the action of a subgroup Γ of a topological group G on G itself. Let μ be a measure on G ⧸ Γ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Unique
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniqueness of Haar measure in locally compact groups
nodes.description: In a locally compact group, we prove that two left-invariant measures μ' and μ which are finite on compact sets coincide, up to a normalizing scalar that we denote with haarScalarFactor μ' μ, in the following sense: integral of continuous compactly supported functions, up to a scalar. compact closure, up to a scalar.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.HasOuterApproxClosed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Spaces where indicators of closed sets have decreasing approximations by continuous functions
nodes.description: In this file we define a typeclass HasOuterApproxClosed for topological spaces in which indicator functions of closed sets have sequences of bounded continuous functions approximating them from above. All pseudo-emetrizable spaces have this property, see instHasOuterApproxClosed.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.HasOuterApproxClosedProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterization of a finite measure by the integrals of products of bounded functions
nodes.description: Given two finite families of Borel spaces (i : ι) → X i and (j : κ) → Y j satisfying HasOuterApproxClosed, a finite measure μ over (Π i, X i) × (Π j, Y j) is determined by the values ∫ p, (Π i, f i (p.1 i)) (Π j, g j (p.2 j)) ∂μ, for f : (i : ι) → X i → ℝ and g : (j : κ) → Y j → ℝ any families of bounded continuous functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Hausdorff
nodes.description: In this file we define the d-dimensional Hausdorff measure on an (extended) metric space X and the Hausdorff dimension of a set in an (extended) metric space. Let μ d δ be the maximal outer measure such that μ d δ s ≤ (ediam s) ^ d for every set of diameter less than δ. Then the Hausdorff measure μH[d] s of s is defined as ⨆ δ > 0, μ d δ s. By Carathéodory's theorem MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory, this is a Borel measure on X.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.IntegralCharFun
nodes.description: This file contains results about integrals of characteristic functions, and lemmas relating the measure of some sets to integrals of characteristic functions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lebesgue measure on the real line and on ℝⁿ
nodes.description: We show that the Lebesgue measure on the real line (constructed as a particular case of additive Haar measure on inner product spaces) coincides with the Stieltjes measure associated to the function x ↦ x. We deduce properties of this measure on ℝ, and then of the product Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ. In particular, we prove that they are translation invariant.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Complex
nodes.description: In this file, we consider the Lebesgue measure on ℂ defined as the push-forward of the volume on ℝ² under the natural isomorphism and prove that it is equal to the measure volume of ℂ coming from its InnerProductSpace structure over ℝ. For that, we consider the two frequently used ways to represent ℝ² in mathlib: ℝ × ℝ and Fin 2 → ℝ, define measurable equivalences (MeasurableEquiv) to both types and prove that both of them are volume preserving (in the sense of MeasureTheory.measurePreserving).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.EqHaar
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relationship between the Haar and Lebesgue measures
nodes.description: We prove that the Haar measure and Lebesgue measure are equal on ℝ and on ℝ^ι, in MeasureTheory.addHaarMeasure_eq_volume and MeasureTheory.addHaarMeasure_eq_volume_pi.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of integration with respect to the Lebesgue measure
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.Integral.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.VolumeOfBalls
nodes.description: Let E be a finite-dimensional normed ℝ-vector space equipped with a Haar measure μ. We prove that μ (Metric.ball 0 1) = (∫ (x : E), Real.exp (- ‖x‖ ^ p) ∂μ) / Real.Gamma (finrank ℝ E / p + 1) for any real number p with 0 < p, see MeasureTheory.measure_unitBall_eq_integral_div_gamma. We also prove the corresponding result to compute μ {x : E | g x < 1} where g : E → ℝ is a function defining a norm on E, see MeasureTheory.measure_lt_one_eq_integral_div_gamma.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.LevyConvergence
nodes.description: This file contains developments related to Lévy's convergence theorem, which links convergence of characteristic functions and convergence in distribution in finite dimensional inner product spaces.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.LevyProkhorovMetric
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Lévy-Prokhorov distance on spaces of finite measures and probability measures
nodes.description: pseudometric on the space of finite measures. pseudometric on the space of probability measures. probability measures is always at least as fine as the topology of convergence in distribution. probability measures on a separable space coincides with the topology of convergence in distribution, and in particular convergence in distribution is then pseudometrizable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.LogLikelihoodRatio
nodes.description: The likelihood ratio between two measures μ and ν is their Radon-Nikodym derivative μ.rnDeriv ν. The logarithm of that function is often used instead: this is the log-likelihood ratio.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Map
nodes.description: In this file we define the pushforward MeasureTheory.Measure.map f μ of a measure μ along an almost everywhere measurable map f. If f is not a.e. measurable, then we define map f μ to be zero.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.MeasureSpace
nodes.description: The definition of a measure and a measure space are in MeasureTheory.MeasureSpaceDef, with only a few basic properties. This file provides many more properties of these objects. This separation allows the measurability tactic to import only the file MeasureSpaceDef, and to be available in MeasureSpace (through MeasurableSpace).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.MeasureSpaceDef
nodes.description: This file defines measure spaces, the almost-everywhere filter and AEMeasurable functions. See MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace for their properties and for extended documentation.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.MeasuredSets
nodes.description: Consider a measure μ on a measurable space. One can define an extended distance on the space of measurable sets, by edist s t := μ (s ∆ t). In this file, we introduce this definition on the type synonym MeasuredSets μ, and we prove that μ is a continuous function on this space.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.MutuallySingular
nodes.description: Two measures μ, ν are said to be mutually singular (MeasureTheory.Measure.MutuallySingular, localized notation μ ⟂ₘ ν) if there exists a measurable set s such that μ s = 0 and ν sᶜ = 0. The measurability of s is an unnecessary assumption (see MeasureTheory.Measure.MutuallySingular.mk) but we keep it because this way rcases (h : μ ⟂ₘ ν) gives us a measurable set and usually it is easy to prove measurability.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.NullMeasurable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Null measurable sets and complete measures
nodes.description: A set s : Set α is called null measurable (MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet) if it satisfies any of the following equivalent conditions:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.OpenPos
nodes.description: In this file we define a typeclass for measures that are positive on nonempty opens, see MeasureTheory.Measure.IsOpenPosMeasure. Examples include (additive) Haar measures, as well as measures that have positive density with respect to a Haar measure. We also prove some basic facts about these measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Portmanteau
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterizations of weak convergence of finite measures and probability measures
nodes.description: This file will provide portmanteau characterizations of the weak convergence of finite measures and of probability measures, i.e., the standard characterizations of convergence in distribution.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.PreVariation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pre-variation of a subadditive set function
nodes.description: Given a σ-subadditive ℝ≥0∞-valued set function f, we define the pre-variation as the supremum over finite measurable partitions of the sum of f on the parts. This construction yields a measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
nodes.description: This file defines the type of probability measures on a given measurable space. When the underlying space has a topology and the measurable space structure (sigma algebra) is finer than the Borel sigma algebra, then the type of probability measures is equipped with the topology of convergence in distribution (weak convergence of measures). The topology of convergence in distribution is the coarsest topology w.r.t.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Prod
nodes.description: In this file we define and prove properties about the binary product measure. If α and β have s-finite measures μ resp. ν then α × β can be equipped with an s-finite measure μ.prod ν that satisfies (μ.prod ν) s = ∫⁻ x, ν {y | (x, y) ∈ s} ∂μ. We also have (μ.prod ν) (s ×ˢ t) = μ s ν t, i.e. the measure of a rectangle is the product of the measures of the sides.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Prokhorov
nodes.description: We prove statements about the compactness of sets of finite measures or probability measures, notably several versions of Prokhorov theorem on tight sets of probability measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving
nodes.description: A map f : α → β is said to be quasi-measure-preserving (a.k.a. non-singular) w.r.t. measures μa and μb if it is measurable and μb s = 0 implies μa (f ⁻¹' s) = 0. That last condition can also be written μa.map f ≪ μb (the map of μa by f is absolutely continuous with respect to μb).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Real
nodes.description: Given a measure μ, we have defined μ.real as the function sending a set s to (μ s).toReal. In this file, we develop a basic API around this notion.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Regular
nodes.description: A measure is OuterRegular if the measure of any measurable set A is the infimum of μ U over all open sets U containing A.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.RegularityCompacts
nodes.description: The main result of this file is InnerRegularCompactLTTop_of_pseudoEMetricSpace_completeSpace_secondCountable: A finite measure μ on a PseudoEMetricSpace E and CompleteSpace E with SecondCountableTopology E is inner regular with respect to compact sets. In other words, a finite measure on such a space is a tight measure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.ResolventTransform
nodes.description: Given a normed algebra A over a normed field 𝕜, and μ : Measure 𝕜, we define the resolvent transform of μ by the formula

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Restrict
nodes.descriptionTitle: Restricting a measure to a subset or a subtype
nodes.description: Given a measure μ on a type α and a subset s of α, we define a measure μ.restrict s as the restriction of μ to s (still as a measure on α).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.SeparableMeasure
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to give a sufficient condition on the measure space (X, μ) and the NormedAddCommGroup E for the space MeasureTheory.Lp E p μ to have SecondCountableTopology when 1 ≤ p < ∞. To do so we define the notion of a MeasureTheory.MeasureDense family and a separable measure (MeasureTheory.IsSeparable). We prove that if X is MeasurableSpace.CountablyGenerated and μ is s-finite, then μ is separable. We then prove that if μ is separable and E is second-countable, then Lp E p μ is second-countable.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Stieltjes
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stieltjes measures on the real line
nodes.description: Consider a function f : ℝ → ℝ which is monotone and right-continuous. Then one can define a corresponding measure, giving mass f b - f a to the interval (a, b]. We implement more generally this notion for f : R → ℝ where R is a conditionally complete dense linear order.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Sub
nodes.description: In this file we define μ - ν to be the least measure τ such that μ ≤ τ + ν. It is equivalent to (μ - ν) ⊔ 0 if μ and ν were signed measures. Compare with ENNReal.instSub. Specifically, note that if you have α = {1,2}, and μ {1} = 2, μ {2} = 0, and ν {2} = 2, ν {1} = 0, then (μ - ν) {1, 2} = 2. However, if μ ≤ ν, and ν univ ≠ ∞, then (μ - ν) + ν = μ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.SubFinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about subtraction of finite measures
nodes.description: The content of this file is not placed in MeasureTheory.Measure.Sub because it uses tools that are not imported in the other file: the Hahn decomposition of finite measures and measures built with withDensity.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Support
nodes.description: This file develops the theory of the support of a measure μ on a topological measurable space. The support is defined as the set of points whose every open neighborhood has positive measure. We give equivalent characterizations, prove basic measure-theoretic properties, and study interactions with sums, restrictions, and absolute continuity. Under various Lindelöf conditions, the support is conull, and various descriptions of the complement of the support are provided.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Tight
nodes.description: A set of measures is tight if for all 0 < ε, there exists a compact set K such that for all measures in the set, the complement of K has measure at most ε.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.TightNormed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tight sets of measures in normed spaces
nodes.description: Criteria for tightness of sets of measures in normed and inner product spaces.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Tilted
nodes.description: The exponential tilting of a measure μ on α by a function f : α → ℝ is the measure with density x ↦ exp (f x) / ∫ y, exp (f y) ∂μ with respect to μ. This is sometimes also called the Esscher transform.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Trim
nodes.descriptionTitle: Restriction of a measure to a sub-σ-algebra
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for MeasureTheory.Measure.Trim.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.Finite
nodes.description: We introduce the following typeclasses for measures:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.NoAtoms
nodes.description: A measure μ has no atoms if the measure of each singleton is zero.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.Probability
nodes.description: We introduce the following typeclasses for measures:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.SFinite
nodes.description: We introduce the following typeclasses for measures:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.Typeclasses.ZeroOne
nodes.description: We introduce the typeclass IsZeroOneMeasure for measures that only take the values 0 and 1.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.WithDensity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measure with a given density with respect to another measure
nodes.description: For a measure μ on α and a function f : α → ℝ≥0∞, we define a new measure μ.withDensity f. On a measurable set s, that measure has value ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Measure.WithDensityFinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: s-finite measures can be written as withDensity of a finite measure
nodes.description: If μ is an s-finite measure, then there exists a finite measure μ.toFinite such that a set is μ-null iff it is μ.toFinite-null. In particular, MeasureTheory.ae μ.toFinite = MeasureTheory.ae μ and μ.toFinite = 0 iff μ = 0. As a corollary, μ can be represented as μ.toFinite.withDensity (μ.rnDeriv μ.toFinite).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Order.Group.Lattice
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability results on groups with a lattice structure.
nodes.description: measurable function, group, lattice operation

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Order.Lattice
nodes.descriptionTitle: Typeclasses for measurability of lattice operations
nodes.description: In this file we define classes MeasurableSup and MeasurableInf and prove dot-style lemmas (Measurable.sup, AEMeasurable.sup etc). For binary operations we define two typeclasses:

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Order.UpperLower
nodes.description: This file proves that order-connected sets in ℝⁿ under the pointwise order are null-measurable. Recall that x ≤ y iff ∀ i, x i ≤ y i, and s is order-connected iff ∀ x y ∈ s, ∀ z, x ≤ z → z ≤ y → z ∈ s.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.AE
nodes.descriptionTitle: The “almost everywhere” filter of co-null sets.
nodes.description: If μ is an outer measure or a measure on α, then MeasureTheory.ae μ is the filter of co-null sets: s ∈ ae μ ↔ μ sᶜ = 0.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Basic
nodes.description: An outer measure is a function μ : Set α → ℝ≥0∞, from the powerset of a type to the extended nonnegative real numbers that satisfies the following conditions: 1. μ ∅ = 0; 2. μ is monotone; 3. μ is countably subadditive. This means that the outer measure of a countable union is at most the sum of the outer measure on the individual sets.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.BorelCantelli
nodes.description: In this file we show one implication of the Borel-Cantelli lemma: if s i is a countable family of sets such that ∑' i, μ (s i) is finite, then a.e. all points belong to finitely many sets of the family.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Caratheodory
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Carathéodory σ-algebra of an outer measure
nodes.description: Given an outer measure m, the Carathéodory-measurable sets are the sets s such that for all sets t we have m t = m (t ∩ s) + m (t \ s). This forms a measurable space.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Defs
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definitions of an outer measure and the corresponding FunLike class
nodes.description: In this file we define MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure α to be the type of outer measures on α.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Induced
nodes.description: We can extend a function defined on a subset of Set α to an outer measure. The underlying function is called extend, and the measure it induces is called inducedOuterMeasure.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.OfAddContent
nodes.description: Let C be a semiring of sets and m an additive content on C, which is sigma-subadditive. Then all sets in the sigma-algebra generated by C are Carathéodory measurable with respect to the outer measure induced by m. The induced outer measure is equal to m on C.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.OfFunction
nodes.description: Given an arbitrary function m : Set α → ℝ≥0∞ that sends ∅ to 0 we can define an outer measure on α that on s is defined to be the infimum of ∑ᵢ, m (sᵢ) for all collections of sets sᵢ that cover s. This is the unique maximal outer measure that is at most the given function.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Operations
nodes.description: In this file we define algebraic operations (addition, scalar multiplication) on the type of outer measures on a type. We also show that outer measures on a type α form a complete lattice.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.PiSystem
nodes.descriptionTitle: Induction principles for measurable sets, related to π-systems and λ-systems.
nodes.description: here as an induction principle induction_on_inter. Suppose s is a collection of subsets of α such that the intersection of two members of s belongs to s whenever it is nonempty. Let m be the σ-algebra generated by s. In order to check that a predicate C holds on every member of m, it suffices to check that C holds on the members of s and that C is preserved by complementation and disjoint countable unions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SetAlgebra
nodes.description: In this file we define the notion of algebra of sets and give its basic properties. An algebra of sets is a family of sets containing the empty set and closed by complement and binary union. It is therefore similar to a σ-algebra, except that it is not necessarily closed by countable unions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SetSemiring
nodes.description: A semi-ring of sets C (in the sense of measure theory) is a family of sets containing ∅, stable by intersection and such that for all s, t ∈ C, t \ s is equal to a disjoint union of finitely many sets in C. Note that a semi-ring of sets may not contain unions.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SpecificCodomains.ContinuousMap
nodes.description: In this file, we collect a few results regarding integrability, on a measure space (X, μ), of a C(Y, E)-valued function, where Y is a compact topological space and E is a normed group.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SpecificCodomains.ContinuousMapZero
nodes.description: In this file, we collect a few results regarding integrability, on a measure space (X, μ), of a C(Y, E)₀-valued function, where Y is a compact topological space with a distinguished 0, and E is a normed group.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SpecificCodomains.Pi
