nodes.description: We prove that f : X → Π i, E i is in Lᵖ if and only if for all i, f · i is in Lᵖ. We do the same for f : X → (E × F).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.SpecificCodomains.WithLp
nodes.description: We prove that f : X → PiLp q E is in Lᵖ if and only if for all i, f · i is in Lᵖ. We do the same for f : X → WithLp q (E × F).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.Topology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Theorems combining measure theory and topology
nodes.description: This file gathers theorems that combine measure theory and topology, and cannot easily be added to the existing files without introducing massive dependencies between the subjects.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.AddContent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructing a vector measure from an additive content
nodes.description: Consider a content defined on a semiring of sets. We investigate in this file whether it is possible to extend it to a (countably additive) vector measure on the whole sigma-algebra. We show that this is possible when the content is dominated by a finite measure, see exists_extension_of_isSetSemiring_of_le_measure_of_generateFrom.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines vector-valued measures, which are σ-additive functions from a set to an additive monoid M such that it maps the empty set and non-measurable sets to zero. In the case that M = ℝ, we called the vector measure a signed measure and write SignedMeasure α. Similarly, when M = ℂ, we call the measure a complex measure and write ComplexMeasure α (defined in MeasureTheory/Measure/Complex).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.BoundedVariation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Vector valued Stieltjes measure associated to a bounded variation function
nodes.description: Let α be a dense linear order with compact segments (e.g. ℝ or ℝ≥0), and f : α → E a bounded variation function taking values in a complete additive normed group. We associate to f a vector measure, called BoundedVariationOn.vectorMeasure. It gives mass f.rightLim b - f.leftLim a to the interval [a, b] (with similar formulas for other types of intervals).

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.Hahn
nodes.description: This file proves the Hahn decomposition theorem (signed version). The Hahn decomposition theorem states that, given a signed measure s, there exist complementary, measurable sets i and j, such that i is positive and j is negative with respect to s; that is, s restricted on i is non-negative and s restricted on j is non-positive.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.Jordan
nodes.description: This file proves the existence and uniqueness of the Jordan decomposition for signed measures. The Jordan decomposition theorem states that, given a signed measure s, there exists a unique pair of mutually singular measures μ and ν, such that s = μ - ν.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.JordanSub
nodes.descriptionTitle: Jordan decomposition from signed measure subtraction
nodes.description: This file develops the Jordan decomposition of the signed measure μ - ν for finite measures μ and ν, expressing it as the pair (μ - ν, ν - μ) of mutually singular finite measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.Lebesgue
nodes.description: This file proves the Lebesgue decomposition theorem for signed measures. The Lebesgue decomposition theorem states that, given two σ-finite measures μ and ν, there exists a σ-finite measure ξ and a measurable function f such that μ = ξ + fν and ξ is mutually singular with respect to ν.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Decomposition.RadonNikodym
nodes.description: This file contains results about Radon-Nikodym derivatives of signed measures that depend both on the Lebesgue decomposition of signed measures and the theory of Radon-Nikodym derivatives of usual measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral of vector-valued function against vector measure
nodes.description: We extend the definition of the Bochner integral (of vector-valued function against ℝ≥0∞-valued measure) to vector measures through a bilinear pairing. Let E, F be normed vector spaces, and G be a Banach space (complete normed vector space). We fix a continuous linear pairing B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] G and an F-valued vector measure μ on a measurable space X.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Variation.Basic
nodes.description: We prove basic properties of variation for μ : VectorMeasure X V in ENormedAddCommMonoid V on MeasurableSpace X. It is defined as the supremum over partitions {Eᵢ} of E, of the quantity ∑ᵢ, ‖μ(Eᵢ)‖. This definition allows one to define the integral against such vector-valued measures.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.Variation.Defs
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of variation for any VectorMeasure in an ENormedAddCommMonoid, in particular, any NormedAddCommGroup.

nodes.label: MeasureTheory.VectorMeasure.WithDensity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Vector measure defined by an integral
nodes.description: Given a measure μ and an integrable function f : α → E, we can define a vector measure v such that for all measurable sets s, v s = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ. This definition is useful for the Radon-Nikodym theorem for signed measures.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Field.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the first-order theory of fields as a theory over the language of rings.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Field.CharP
nodes.description: This file defines the first-order theory of fields of characteristic p as a theory over the language of rings

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Field.IsAlgClosed
nodes.descriptionTitle: The First-Order Theory of Algebraically Closed Fields
nodes.description: This file defines the theory of algebraically closed fields of characteristic p, as well as proving completeness of the theory and the Lefschetz Principle.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Ring.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the first-order language of rings, as well as defining instance of Add, Mul, etc. on terms in the language.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Ring.Definability
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definable Subsets in the language of rings
nodes.description: This file proves that the set of zeros of a multivariable polynomial is a definable subset.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Algebra.Ring.FreeCommRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Making a term in the language of rings from an element of the FreeCommRing
nodes.description: This file defines the function FirstOrder.Ring.termOfFreeCommRing which constructs a Language.ring.Term α from an element of FreeCommRing α.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Arithmetic.Presburger.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the first-order language of Presburger arithmetic as (0,1,+).

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Arithmetic.Presburger.Definability
nodes.description: This file formalizes the classical result that Presburger definable sets are the same as semilinear sets. As an application of this result, we show that the graph of multiplication is not Presburger definable.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Arithmetic.Presburger.Semilinear.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Semilinear sets are closed under intersection, set difference and complement
nodes.description: This file proves that the semilinear sets in any commutative monoid are closed under intersection and set difference. They are also closed under complement if the monoid is finitely generated. We prove these results on ℕ ^ k first (which are private APIs in this file) and then generalize to any commutative monoid.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Arithmetic.Presburger.Semilinear.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines linear and semilinear sets. In an AddCommMonoid, a linear set is a coset of a finitely generated additive submonoid, and a semilinear set is a finite union of linear sets.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines first-order languages and structures in the style of the Flypitch project, as well as several important maps between structures.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Bundled
nodes.description: This file bundles types together with their first-order structure.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Complexity
nodes.description: This file defines quantifier complexity of first-order formulas, and constructs prenex normal forms.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Definability
nodes.description: This file defines what it means for a set over a first-order structure to be definable.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.DirectLimit
nodes.description: This file constructs the direct limit of a directed system of first-order embeddings.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.ElementaryMaps
nodes.description: realizations of formulas. parameters that the structure satisfies. elementary embedding of any structure into a model of its elementary diagram.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.ElementarySubstructures
nodes.description: formula agrees with the realization in the larger model.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Encodings and Cardinality of First-Order Syntax
nodes.description: max ℵ₀ # (α ⊕ Σ i, L.Functions i). Σ n, L.BoundedFormula α n is at most max ℵ₀ (Cardinal.lift.{max u v} #α + Cardinal.lift.{u'} L.card).

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Equivalence
nodes.description: sentences in models of T.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.FinitelyGenerated
nodes.description: This file defines what it means for a first-order (sub)structure to be finitely or countably generated, similarly to other finitely-generated objects in the algebra library.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Fraisse
nodes.description: This file pertains to the ages of countable first-order structures. The age of a structure is the class of all finitely-generated structures that embed into it.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Graph
nodes.description: This file defines first-order languages, structures, and theories in graph theory.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.LanguageMap
nodes.description: Maps between first-order languages in the style of the Flypitch project, as well as several important maps between structures.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Order
nodes.description: This file defines ordered first-order languages and structures, as well as their theories.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.PartialEquiv
nodes.description: This file defines partial isomorphisms between first-order structures.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Quotients
nodes.description: This file defines prestructures and quotients of first-order structures.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Satisfiability
nodes.description: This file deals with the satisfiability of first-order theories, as well as equivalence over them.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Semantics
nodes.description: This file defines the interpretations of first-order terms, formulas, sentences, and theories in a style inspired by the Flypitch project.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Skolem
nodes.description: theorem: If s is a set in an L-structure M and κ an infinite cardinal such that max (#s, L.card) ≤ κ and κ ≤ # M, then M has an elementary substructure containing s of cardinality κ.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Substructures
nodes.description: This file defines substructures of first-order structures in a similar manner to the various substructures appearing in the algebra library.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Syntax
nodes.description: This file defines first-order terms, formulas, sentences, and theories in a style inspired by the Flypitch project.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Topology.Types
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on the space of complete types
nodes.description: This file defines a topological structure on the type CompleteType T α (note that these are types from model theory and not types from type theory). The topology is generated by sets of the form {p : CompleteType T α | ∃ φ, φ ∈ p}.

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Types
nodes.description: This file defines the space of complete types over a first-order theory. (Note that types in model theory are different from types in type theory.)

nodes.label: ModelTheory.Ultraproducts
nodes.description: sentence φ if and only if the set of structures in the product that model φ is in the ultrafilter.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ADEInequality
nodes.description: In this file we classify solutions to the inequality (p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ + r⁻¹ : ℚ) > 1, for positive natural numbers p, q, and r.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.AbelSummation
nodes.description: We prove several versions of Abel's summation formula.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Carmichael
nodes.description: also known as the reduced totient function.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines arithmetic functions, which are functions from ℕ to a specified type that map 0 to 0. In the literature, they are often instead defined as functions from ℕ+. These arithmetic functions are endowed with a multiplication, given by Dirichlet convolution, and pointwise addition, to form the Dirichlet ring.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.LFunction
nodes.description: This file constructs L-functions as formal Dirichlet series.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Liouville
nodes.description: This file defines the Liouville function λ(n).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Misc
nodes.description: This file defines some simple examples of arithmetic functions (functions ℕ → R vanishing at 0, considered as a ring under Dirichlet convolution). Note that the Von Mangoldt and Möbius functions are in separate files.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Moebius
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Möbius function and Möbius inversion
nodes.description: the namespace ArithmeticFunction.Moebius).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.VonMangoldt
nodes.description: In this file we define the von Mangoldt function: the function on natural numbers that returns log p if the input can be expressed as p^k for a prime p.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Zeta
nodes.description: We define ζ to be the arithmetic function with ζ n = 1 for 0 < n (whose Dirichlet series is the Riemann zeta function).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Basic
nodes.description: This file should contain basic results in number theory. So far, it only contains the essential lemma in the construction of the ring of Witt vectors.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Bernoulli
nodes.description: The Bernoulli numbers are a sequence of rational numbers that frequently show up in number theory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.BernoulliPolynomials
nodes.description: The Bernoulli polynomials are an important tool obtained from Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Bertrand
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of Bertrand's postulate: That between any positive number and its double there is a prime.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Chebyshev
nodes.description: This file defines the Chebyshev functions theta and psi. These give logarithmically weighted sums of primes and prime powers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ClassNumber.AdmissibleAbs
nodes.descriptionTitle: Admissible absolute value on the integers
nodes.description: This file defines an admissible absolute value AbsoluteValue.absIsAdmissible which we use to show the class number of the ring of integers of a number field is finite.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ClassNumber.AdmissibleAbsoluteValue
nodes.description: This file defines a structure AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible which we use to show the class number of the ring of integers of a global field is finite.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ClassNumber.AdmissibleCardPowDegree
nodes.description: This file defines an admissible absolute value Polynomial.cardPowDegreeIsAdmissible which we use to show the class number of the ring of integers of a function field is finite.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ClassNumber.Finite
nodes.description: In this file, we use the notion of "admissible absolute value" to prove finiteness of the class group for number fields and function fields.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ClassNumber.FunctionField
nodes.description: This file defines the class number of a function field as the (finite) cardinality of the class group of its ring of integers. It also proves some elementary results on the class number.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Basic
nodes.description: Let A and B be commutative rings with Algebra A B. For S : Set ℕ, we define a class IsCyclotomicExtension S A B expressing the fact that B is obtained from A by adding n-th primitive roots of unity, for all nonzero n ∈ S.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.CyclotomicCharacter
nodes.description: Let L be an integral domain and let n : ℕ+ be a positive integer. If μₙ is the group of nth roots of unity in L then any field automorphism g of L induces an automorphism of μₙ which, being a cyclic group, must be of the form ζ ↦ ζ^j for some integer j = j(g), well-defined in ZMod d, with d the cardinality of μₙ. The function j is a group homomorphism (L ≃+ L) → ZMod d.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Discriminant
nodes.description: We compute the discriminant of a p ^ n-th cyclotomic extension.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.Gal
nodes.description: In this file, we show the relationship between the Galois group of K(ζₙ) and (ZMod n)ˣ; it is always a subgroup, and if the nth cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible, they are isomorphic.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Cyclotomic.PrimitiveRoots
nodes.description: If IsCyclotomicExtension {n} A B, we define an element zeta n A B : B that is a primitive nth-root of unity in B and we study its properties. We also prove related theorems under the more general assumption of just being a primitive root, for reasons described in the implementation details section.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Dioph
nodes.description: Hilbert's tenth problem asked whether there exists an algorithm which for a given integer polynomial determines whether this polynomial has integer solutions. It was answered in the negative in 1970, the final step being completed by Matiyasevic who showed that the power function is Diophantine.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DiophantineApproximation.Basic
nodes.description: The first part of this file gives proofs of various versions of Dirichlet's approximation theorem and its important consequence that when $\xi$ is an irrational real number, then there are infinitely many rationals $x/y$ (in lowest terms) such that $$\left|\xi - \frac{x}{y}\right| < \frac{1}{y^2} \,.$$ The proof is based on the pigeonhole principle.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DiophantineApproximation.ContinuedFractions
nodes.description: There are two versions of Legendre's Theorem.Real.exists_rat_eq_convergent, defined in Mathlib/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/Basic.lean, uses Real.convergent, a simple recursive definition of the convergents that is also defined in that file. This file provides Real.exists_convs_eq_rat, using GenContFract.convs of GenContFract.of ξ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.Basic
nodes.description: Let R be a commutative monoid with zero. A Dirichlet character χ of level n over R is a multiplicative character from ZMod n to R sending non-units to 0. We then obtain some properties of toUnitHom χ, the restriction of χ to a group homomorphism (ZMod n)ˣ → Rˣ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.Bounds
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bounds for values of Dirichlet characters
nodes.description: We consider Dirichlet characters χ with values in a normed field F.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.GaussSum
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.GaussSum.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.Orthogonality
nodes.description: Let n be a positive natural number. The main result of this file is DirichletCharacter.sum_char_inv_mul_char_eq, which says that when a : ZMod n is a unit and b : ZMod n, then the sum ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter R n, χ a⁻¹ χ b vanishes when a ≠ b and has the value n.totient otherwise. This requires R to have enough roots of unity (e.g., R could be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Divisors
nodes.description: This file defines sets of divisors of a natural number. This is particularly useful as background for defining Dirichlet convolution.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.EllipticDivisibilitySequence
nodes.description: This file defines the type of an elliptic divisibility sequence (EDS) and a few examples.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.EulerProduct.Basic
nodes.description: The main result in this file is EulerProduct.eulerProduct_hasProd, which says that if f : ℕ → R is norm-summable, where R is a complete normed commutative ring and f is multiplicative on coprime arguments with f 0 = 0, then ∏' p : Primes, ∑' e : ℕ, f (p^e) converges to ∑' n, f n.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.EulerProduct.DirichletLSeries
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Euler Product for the Riemann Zeta Function and Dirichlet L-Series
nodes.description: The first main result of this file is the Euler Product formula for the Riemann ζ function $$\prod_p \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}} = \lim_{n \to \infty} \prod_{p 1$ ($p$ runs through the primes). riemannZeta_eulerProduct is the second equality above. There are versions riemannZeta_eulerProduct_hasProd and riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod in terms of HasProd and tprod, respectively.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.EulerProduct.ExpLog
nodes.description: We consider f : ℕ →₀ ℂ and show that exp (∑ p in Primes, log (1 - f p)⁻¹) = ∑ n : ℕ, f n under suitable conditions on f. This can be seen as a logarithmic version of the Euler product for f.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FLT.Basic
nodes.description: This file states Fermat's Last Theorem. We provide a statement over a general semiring with specific exponent, along with the usual statement over the naturals.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FLT.Four
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fermat's Last Theorem for the case n = 4
nodes.description: There are no non-zero integers a, b and c such that a ^ 4 + b ^ 4 = c ^ 4.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FLT.MasonStothers
nodes.description: This file states and proves the Mason-Stothers theorem, which is a polynomial version of the ABC conjecture. For (pairwise) coprime polynomials a, b, c (over a field) with a + b + c = 0, we have max {deg(a), deg(b), deg(c)} + 1 ≤ deg(rad(abc)) or a' = b' = c' = 0.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FLT.Polynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fermat's Last Theorem for polynomials over a field
nodes.description: This file states and proves the Fermat's Last Theorem for polynomials over a field. For n ≥ 3 not divisible by the characteristic of the coefficient field k and (pairwise) nonzero coprime polynomials a, b, c (over a field) with a ^ n + b ^ n = c ^ n, all polynomials must be constants.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FLT.Three
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fermat Last Theorem in the case n = 3
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to prove Fermat's Last Theorem in the case n = 3.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FactorisationProperties
nodes.description: This file defines abundant, pseudoperfect, deficient, and weird numbers and formalizes their relations with prime and perfect numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Fermat
nodes.description: The Fermat numbers are a sequence of natural numbers defined as Nat.fermatNumber n = 2^(2^n) + 1, for all natural numbers n.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FermatPsp
nodes.description: In this file we define Fermat pseudoprimes: composite numbers that pass the Fermat primality test. A natural number n passes the Fermat primality test to base b (and is therefore deemed a "probable prime") if n divides b ^ (n - 1) - 1. n is a Fermat pseudoprime to base b if n is a composite number that passes the Fermat primality test to base b and is coprime with b.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FrobeniusNumber
nodes.description: In this file we first define a predicate for Frobenius numbers, then solve the 2-variable variant of this problem. We also show the Frobenius number exists for any set of coprime natural numbers that doesn't contain 1. This is closely related to the fact that all ideals of ℕ are finitely generated, which we also prove in this file.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.FunctionField
nodes.description: This file defines a function field and the ring of integers corresponding to it.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.GaussSum
nodes.description: We define the Gauss sum associated to a multiplicative and an additive character of a finite field and prove some results about them.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.Bounds
nodes.descriptionTitle: This file proves $\log(n + 1) \le H_n \le 1 + \log(n)$ for all natural numbers $n$.
nodes.description: This file proves $\log(n + 1) \le H_n \le 1 + \log(n)$ for all natural numbers $n$.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.Defs
nodes.descriptionTitle: This file defines the harmonic numbers.
nodes.description: This file defines the harmonic numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.EulerMascheroni
nodes.description: We define the constant γ, and give upper and lower bounds for it.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.GammaDeriv
nodes.descriptionTitle: Derivative of Γ at positive integers
nodes.description: We prove the formula for the derivative of Real.Gamma at a positive integer:

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.Int
nodes.descriptionTitle: The nth Harmonic number is not an integer. We formalize the proof using
nodes.description: The nth Harmonic number is not an integer. We formalize the proof using 2-adic valuations. This proof is due to Kürschák.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Harmonic.ZetaAsymp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Asymptotics of ζ s as s → 1
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to evaluate the limit of ζ s - 1 / (s - 1) as s → 1.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Height.Basic
nodes.description: This is an attempt at formalizing some basic properties of height functions.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Height.MvPolynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Height bounds for linear and polynomial maps
nodes.description: We prove an upper bound for the height of the image of a tuple under a linear map.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Height.Northcott
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results on the Northcott property for heights
nodes.description: Assume that K is a field with a family of admissible absolute values that satisfies the Northcott property for mulHeight₁. We provide instances showing that K also satisfies the Northcott property

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Height.NumberField
nodes.description: We provide an instance of Height.AdmissibleAbsValues for algebraic number fields and set up some API.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Height.Projectivization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Heights of points in projective space
nodes.description: We define the multiplicative (Projectivization.mulHeight) and the logarithmic (Projectivization.logHeight) height of a point in a (finite-dimensional) projective space over a field that has a Height.AdmissibleAbsValues instance.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.JacobiSum.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the Jacobi sum of two multiplicative characters χ and ψ on a finite commutative ring R with values in another commutative ring R':

nodes.label: NumberTheory.KummerDedekind
nodes.description: This file proves the Kummer-Dedekind theorem on the splitting of prime ideals in an extension of the ring of integers. This states the following: assume we are given

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.AbstractFuncEq
nodes.descriptionTitle: Abstract functional equations for Mellin transforms
nodes.description: This file formalises a general version of an argument used to prove functional equations for zeta and L-functions.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Basic
nodes.description: Given a sequence f: ℕ → ℂ, we define the corresponding L-series.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Convergence
nodes.description: We define LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv f (as an EReal) to be the infimum of all real numbers x such that the L-series of f converges for complex arguments with real part x and provide some results about it.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Convolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: Dirichlet convolution of sequences and products of L-series
nodes.description: We define the Dirichlet convolution f ⍟ g of two sequences f g : ℕ → R with values in a semiring R by (f ⍟ g) n = ∑ (k m = n), f k g m when n ≠ 0 and (f ⍟ g) 0 = 0. Technically, this is done by transporting the existing definition for ArithmeticFunction R; see LSeries.convolution. We show that these definitions agree (LSeries.convolution_def).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Deriv
nodes.description: the abscissa of absolute convergence of f (LSeries.hasDerivAt) and that its derivative there is the negative of the LSeries of the point-wise product log f (LSeries.deriv).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Dirichlet
nodes.descriptionTitle: L-series of Dirichlet characters and arithmetic functions
nodes.description: We collect some results on L-series of specific (arithmetic) functions, for example, the Möbius function μ or the von Mangoldt function Λ. In particular, we show that L ↗Λ is the negative of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta function on re s > 1; see LSeries_vonMangoldt_eq_deriv_riemannZeta_div.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.DirichletContinuation
nodes.description: We show that if χ is a Dirichlet character ZMod N → ℂ, for a positive integer N, then the L-series of χ has analytic continuation (away from a pole at s = 1 if χ is trivial), and similarly for completed L-functions.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.HurwitzZeta
nodes.description: This file gives the definition and properties of the following two functions:

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.HurwitzZetaEven
nodes.description: In this file we study the functions on ℂ which are the meromorphic continuation of the following series (convergent for 1 < re s), where a ∈ ℝ is a parameter:

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.HurwitzZetaOdd
nodes.description: In this file we study the functions on ℂ which are the analytic continuation of the following series (convergent for 1 < re s), where a ∈ ℝ is a parameter:

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.HurwitzZetaValues
nodes.descriptionTitle: Special values of Hurwitz and Riemann zeta functions
nodes.description: This file gives the formula for ζ (2 k), for k a non-zero integer, in terms of Bernoulli numbers. More generally, we give formulae for any Hurwitz zeta functions at any (strictly) negative integer in terms of Bernoulli polynomials.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Injectivity
nodes.descriptionTitle: A converging L-series determines its coefficients
nodes.description: We show that two functions f and g : ℕ → ℂ whose L-series agree and both converge somewhere must agree on all nonzero arguments. See LSeries_eq_iff_of_abscissaOfAbsConv_lt_top and LSeries_injOn.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Linearity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Linearity of the L-series of f as a function of f
nodes.description: We show that the LSeries of f : ℕ → ℂ is a linear function of f (assuming convergence of both L-series when adding two functions).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.MellinEqDirichlet
nodes.description: Here we prove general results of the form "the Mellin transform of a power series in exp (-t) is a Dirichlet series".

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Nonvanishing
nodes.descriptionTitle: The L-function of a Dirichlet character does not vanish on Re(s) ≥ 1
nodes.description: The main result in this file is DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re: if χ is a Dirichlet character, s ∈ ℂ with 1 ≤ s.re, and either χ is nontrivial or s ≠ 1, then the L-function of χ does not vanish at s.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.Positivity
nodes.description: The main results of this file are as follows.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.PrimesInAP
nodes.descriptionTitle: Dirichlet's Theorem on primes in arithmetic progression
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to prove Dirichlet's Theorem: If q is a positive natural number and a : ZMod q is invertible, then there are infinitely many prime numbers p such that (p : ZMod q) = a.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta
nodes.descriptionTitle: Definition of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.description: Λ(s) = π ^ (-s / 2) Γ(s / 2) ζ(s) (away from the poles of Γ(s / 2)). Λ₀(s) = Λ(s) + 1 / (s - 1) - 1 / s wherever the RHS is defined.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.SumCoeff
nodes.descriptionTitle: Partial sums of coefficients of L-series
nodes.description: We prove several results involving partial sums of coefficients (or norm of coefficients) of L-series.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.ZMod
nodes.descriptionTitle: L-series of functions on ZMod N
nodes.description: We show that if N is a positive integer and Φ : ZMod N → ℂ, then the L-series of Φ has analytic continuation (away from a pole at s = 1 if ∑ j, Φ j ≠ 0) and satisfies a functional equation. We also define completed L-functions (given by multiplying the naive L-function by a Gamma-factor), and prove analytic continuation and functional equations for these too, assuming Φ is either even or odd.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LSeries.ZetaZeros
nodes.descriptionTitle: Discreteness of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.description: We show that the zeros of the Riemann zeta function form a discrete subset of ℂ, so that in particular any compact subset of ℂ contains only finitely many zeros.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.AddCharacter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additive characters of finite rings and fields
nodes.description: This file collects some results on additive characters whose domain is (the additive group of) a finite ring or field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains results about Legendre symbols.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.Complex
nodes.description: We construct a primitive additive character on a finite field F with values in ℂ. This file is kept separate from Mathlib.NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.AddCharacter to avoid importing the fundamental theorem of algebra and Bochner integral into that file.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.GaussEisensteinLemmas
nodes.description: This file contains the Lemmas of Gauss and Eisenstein on the Legendre symbol. The main results are ZMod.gauss_lemma and ZMod.eisenstein_lemma.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.JacobiSymbol
nodes.description: We define the Jacobi symbol and prove its main properties.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticChar.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the quadratic character on a finite field F and proves some basic statements about it.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticChar.GaussSum
nodes.description: Further facts relying on Gauss sums.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.QuadraticReciprocity
nodes.description: We prove the law of quadratic reciprocity, see legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity and legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity', as well as the interpretations in terms of existence of square roots depending on the congruence mod 4, ZMod.exists_sq_eq_prime_iff_of_mod_four_eq_one and ZMod.exists_sq_eq_prime_iff_of_mod_four_eq_three.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LegendreSymbol.ZModChar
nodes.description: This file defines some quadratic characters on the rings ℤ/4ℤ and ℤ/8ℤ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LocalField.Basic
nodes.description: Given a topological field K equipped with an equivalence class of valuations (a ValuativeRel), we say that it is a non-archimedean local field if the topology comes from the given valuation, and it is locally compact and non-discrete.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LucasLehmer
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Lucas-Lehmer test for Mersenne primes
nodes.description: We define lucasLehmerResidue : Π p : ℕ, ZMod (2^p - 1), and prove lucasLehmerResidue p = 0 ↔ Prime (mersenne p).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.LucasPrimality
nodes.description: This file implements the Lucas test for primes (not to be confused with the Lucas-Lehmer test for Mersenne primes). A number a witnesses that n is prime if a has order n-1 in the multiplicative group of integers mod n. This is checked by verifying that a^(n-1) = 1 (mod n) and a^d ≠ 1 (mod n) for any divisor d | n - 1. This test is the basis of the Pratt primality certificate.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.MahlerMeasure
nodes.description: The main purpose of this file is to prove some facts about the Mahler measure of integer polynomials, in particular Northcott's Theorem for the Mahler measure.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.MaricaSchoenheim
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Marica-Schönheim special case of Graham's conjecture
nodes.description: Graham's conjecture states that if $0 < a_1 < \dots a_n$ are integers, then $\max_{i, j} \frac{a_i}{\gcd(a_i, a_j)} \ge n$. This file proves the conjecture when the $a_i$ are squarefree as a corollary of the Marica-Schönheim inequality.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Modular
nodes.descriptionTitle: The action of the modular group SL(2, ℤ) on the upper half-plane
nodes.description: We define the action of SL(2,ℤ) on ℍ (via restriction of the SL(2,ℝ) action in Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane). We then define the standard fundamental domain (ModularGroup.fd, 𝒟) for this action and show (ModularGroup.exists_smul_mem_fd) that any point in ℍ can be moved inside 𝒟.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.ArithmeticSubgroups
nodes.description: We define a subgroup of GL (Fin 2) ℝ to be arithmetic if it is commensurable with the image of SL(2, ℤ).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines modular forms and proves some basic properties about them. Including constructing the graded ring of modular forms.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.BoundedAtCusp
nodes.description: We define the notions of "bounded at c" and "vanishing at c" for functions on ℍ, where c is an element of OnePoint ℝ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Bounds
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bounds for the norm of a modular form
nodes.description: We prove bounds for the norm of a modular form f τ in terms of im τ, and deduce polynomial bounds for its q-expansion coefficients. The main results are

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.CongruenceSubgroups
nodes.description: This defines congruence subgroups of SL(2, ℤ) such as Γ(N), Γ₀(N) and Γ₁(N) for N a natural number.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.CuspFormSubmodule
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cusp form submodule and IsCuspForm predicate
nodes.description: This file defines the inclusion of cusp forms into modular forms as a linear map, the cusp form submodule of modular forms, and the IsCuspForm predicate. It also provides a direct constructor ModularForm.toCuspForm for building cusp forms from modular forms with vanishing constant q-expansion coefficient (for 𝒮ℒ).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Cusps
nodes.description: We define the cusps of a subgroup of GL(2, ℝ) as the fixed points of parabolic elements.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.DedekindEta
nodes.description: η(z) = q ^ 1/24 ∏' (1 - q ^ (n + 1)) where q = e ^ (2πiz) and z is in the upper half-plane. The product is taken over all non-negative integers n. We then show it is non-vanishing and differentiable on the upper half-plane. Lastly, we compute its logarithmic derivative and show that it is a multiple of the Eisenstein series E2.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Delta
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Derivative
nodes.description: This file defines normalized derivative $D = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \frac{d}{dz}$ and serre dervative $\partial_k := D - \frac{k}{12} E_2$ of modular forms.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.DimensionFormulas.LevelOne
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Discriminant
nodes.description: This file defines the modular discriminant Δ(z) = η(z) ^ 24, where η is the Dedekind eta function, and proves its key properties including invariance under the generators of SL(2, ℤ).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.Basic
nodes.description: We show that Eisenstein series of weight k and level Γ(N) with congruence condition a : Fin 2 → ZMod N are Modular Forms.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.Defs
nodes.description: ∑' v : (Fin 2 → ℤ), (1 / (v 0 z + v 1) ^ k), where z : ℍ and v ranges over all pairs of coprime integers congruent to a fixed pair (a, b) modulo N. Note that by using (Fin 2 → ℤ) instead of ℤ × ℤ we can state all of the required equivalences using matrices and vectors, which makes working with them more convenient.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.E2.Defs
nodes.description: We define the Eisenstein series E2 of weight 2 and level 1 as a limit of partial sums over non-symmetric intervals.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.E2.MDifferentiable
nodes.descriptionTitle: MDifferentiability of the weight 2 Eisenstein series
nodes.description: We show that the weight 2 Eisenstein series E2 is MDifferentiable (i.e. holomorphic as a function ℍ → ℂ). The proof uses the relation between E2 and the logarithmic derivative of the Dedekind eta function.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.E2.Summable
nodes.description: We collect here lemmas about the summability of the Eisenstein series E2 that will be used to prove how it transforms under the slash action.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.E2.Transform
nodes.description: This file proves how the weight-2 Eisenstein series E2 (and G2) transforms under the slash action of SL₂(ℤ). Unlike modular forms of weight k ≥ 4, the functions G2 and E2 are not modular forms because they acquire a correction term under the action of S = [[0, -1], [1, 0]].

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.IsBoundedAtImInfty
nodes.description: We show that Eisenstein series of weight k and level Γ(N) with congruence condition a : Fin 2 → ZMod N are bounded at infinity.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.MDifferentiable
nodes.description: We show that Eisenstein series of weight k and level Γ(N) with congruence condition a : Fin 2 → ZMod N are holomorphic on the upper half plane, which is stated as being MDifferentiable.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.QExpansion
nodes.description: We give the q-expansion of Eisenstein series of weight k and level 1. In particular, we prove EisensteinSeries.q_expansion_bernoulli which says that for even k with 3 ≤ k Eisenstein series can be written as 1 - (2k / bernoulli k) ∑' n, σ_{k-1}(n) q^n where q = exp(2πiz) and σ_{k-1}(n) is the sum of the (k-1)-th powers of the divisors of n. We need k to be even so that the Eisenstein series are non-zero and we require k ≥ 3 so that the series converges absolutely.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.Summable
nodes.description: We gather results about the summability of Eisenstein series, particularly the summability of the Eisenstein series summands, which are used in the proof of the boundedness of Eisenstein series at infinity.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.EisensteinSeries.UniformConvergence
nodes.description: We show that the sum of eisSummand converges locally uniformly on ℍ to the Eisenstein series of weight k and level Γ(N) with congruence condition a : Fin 2 → ZMod N.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Identities
nodes.description: Collection of useful identities of modular forms.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.JacobiTheta.Bounds
nodes.descriptionTitle: Asymptotic bounds for Jacobi theta functions
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to establish some technical lemmas about the asymptotics of the sums

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.JacobiTheta.Manifold
nodes.descriptionTitle: Manifold differentiability of the Jacobi theta function
nodes.description: In this file we reformulate differentiability of the Jacobi theta function in terms of manifold differentiability.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.JacobiTheta.OneVariable
nodes.description: This file defines the one-variable Jacobi theta function

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.JacobiTheta.TwoVariable
nodes.description: This file defines the two-variable Jacobi theta function

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.LevelOne
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.LevelOne.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains results specific to modular forms of level one, i.e. modular forms for SL(2, ℤ).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.LevelOne.DimensionFormula
nodes.descriptionTitle: Dimension formula and Sturm bound for level 1 modular forms
nodes.description: This file proves the dimension formula and the Sturm bound for the space of modular forms for 𝒮ℒ (= SL(2, ℤ)) of even weight.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.LevelOne.GradedRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: The graded ring of level-1 modular forms
nodes.description: This file collects structural results about the graded ring ⨁ k, ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k of level-1 modular forms, beyond those that fall out of the dimension formula directly.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.NormTrace
nodes.description: Given two subgroups 𝒢, ℋ of GL(2, ℝ) with 𝒢.relindex ℋ ≠ 0 (i.e. 𝒢 ⊓ ℋ has finite index in ℋ), we define a trace map from ModularForm (𝒢 ⊓ ℋ) k to ModularForm ℋ k.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.Petersson
nodes.description: For f, f' functions ℍ → ℂ, we define petersson k f f' to be the function τ ↦ conj (f τ) f' τ τ.im ^ k.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.ProperlyDiscontinuous
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for NumberTheory.ModularForms.ProperlyDiscontinuous.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.QExpansion
nodes.descriptionTitle: q-expansions of functions on the upper half plane
nodes.description: We show that a function on the upper half plane with strict period n can be written as τ ↦ F (𝕢 n τ) where F is analytic on the open unit disc, and 𝕢 n is the parameter τ ↦ exp (2 I π τ / n). As an application, we show that cusp forms decay exponentially to 0 as im τ → ∞.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.SlashActions
nodes.description: This file defines a class of slash actions, which are families of right actions of a group on an a additive monoid, parametrized by some index type. This is modeled on the slash action of GL (Fin 2) ℝ on the space of modular forms.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ModularForms.SlashInvariantForms
nodes.description: This file defines functions that are invariant under a SlashAction which forms the basis for defining ModularForm and CuspForm. We prove several instances for such spaces, in particular that they form a module over ℝ, and over ℂ if the group is contained in SL(2, ℝ).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.MulChar.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multiplicative characters of finite rings and fields
nodes.description: Let R and R' be commutative rings. A multiplicative character of R with values in R' is a morphism of monoids from the multiplicative monoid of R into that of R' that sends non-units to zero.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.MulChar.Duality
nodes.description: Let M be a finite commutative monoid and R a ring that has enough nth roots of unity, where n is the exponent of M. Then the main results of this file are as follows.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.MulChar.Lemmas
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for NumberTheory.MulChar.Lemmas.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Multiplicity
nodes.description: This file contains results in number theory relating to multiplicity.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Niven
nodes.description: This file proves Niven's theorem, stating that the only rational angles _in degrees_ which also have rational cosines, are 0, 30 degrees, and 90 degrees - up to reflection and shifts by π. Equivalently, the only rational numbers that occur as cos(π p / q) are the five values {-1, -1/2, 0, 1/2, 1}.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.AdeleRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: The adele ring of a number field
nodes.description: This file contains the formalisation of the adele ring of a number field as the direct product of the infinite adele ring and the finite adele ring.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines a number field and the ring of integers corresponding to it.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CMField
nodes.description: A CM-extension K/F of fields is an extension where K is totally complex, F is totally real and K is a quadratic extension of F. In this situation, the totally real subfield F is (isomorphic to) the maximal real subfield K⁺ of K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CanonicalEmbedding.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Canonical embedding of a number field
nodes.description: The canonical embedding of a number field K of degree n is the ring homomorphism K →+ ℂ^n that sends x ∈ K to (φ_₁(x),...,φ_n(x)) where the φ_i's are the complex embeddings of K. Note that we do not choose an ordering of the embeddings, but instead map K into the type (K →+ ℂ) → ℂ of ℂ-vectors indexed by the complex embeddings.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CanonicalEmbedding.ConvexBody
nodes.description: The file contains the definitions of several convex bodies lying in the mixed space ℝ^r₁ × ℂ^r₂ associated to a number field of signature K and proves several existence theorems by applying Minkowski Convex Body Theorem to those.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CanonicalEmbedding.FundamentalCone
nodes.description: Let K be a number field of signature (r₁, r₂). We define an action of the units (𝓞 K)ˣ on the mixed space ℝ^r₁ × ℂ^r₂ via the mixedEmbedding. The fundamental cone is a cone in the mixed space that is a fundamental domain for the action of (𝓞 K)ˣ modulo torsion.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CanonicalEmbedding.NormLeOne
nodes.descriptionTitle: Fundamental Cone: set of elements of norm ≤ 1
nodes.description: In this file, we study the subset NormLeOne of the fundamentalCone of elements x with mixedEmbedding.norm x ≤ 1.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.CanonicalEmbedding.PolarCoord
nodes.descriptionTitle: Polar coordinate change of variables for the mixed space of a number field
nodes.description: We define two polar coordinate changes of variables for the mixed space ℝ^r₁ × ℂ^r₂ associated to a number field K of signature (r₁, r₂). The first one is mixedEmbedding.polarCoord and has value in realMixedSpace K defined as ℝ^r₁ × (ℝ ⨯ ℝ)^r₂, the second is mixedEmbedding.polarSpaceCoord and has value in polarSpace K defined as ℝ^(r₁+r₂) × ℝ^r₂.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.ClassNumber
nodes.description: This file defines the class number of a number field as the (finite) cardinality of the class group of its ring of integers. It also proves some elementary results on the class number.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.FinitePlace
nodes.description: This file defines finite places of a number field K as absolute values coming from an embedding into a completion of K associated to a non-zero prime ideal of 𝓞 K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.InfinitePlace
nodes.descriptionTitle: The completion of a number field at an infinite place
nodes.description: This file contains the completion of a number field at an infinite place. This is ultimately achieved by applying the UniformSpace.Completion functor, however each infinite place induces its own UniformSpace instance on the number field, so the inference system cannot automatically infer these. A common approach to handle the ambiguity that arises from having multiple sources of instances is through the use of type synonyms. In this case, we use the type synonym WithAbs of a semiring.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.LiesOverInstances
nodes.descriptionTitle: LiesOver instances for completions of number fields
nodes.description: If L and K are number fields such that Algebra K L then this algebra extends naturally to the completions of K and L at places, whenever the place of L lies over the place of K. This file contains the relevant instances and properties of this extension as scoped instances. These are scoped because they create non-defeq instance diamonds when K = L.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.Ramification
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ramification theory of completions of number fields
nodes.description: This file studies the ramification of completions of number fields.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ring of integers of cyclotomic fields
nodes.description: We gather results about cyclotomic extensions of ℚ. In particular, we compute the ring of integers of a cyclotomic extension of ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.Embeddings
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cyclotomic extensions of ℚ are totally complex number fields.
nodes.description: We prove that cyclotomic extensions of ℚ are totally complex, meaning that NrRealPlaces K = 0 if IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ K and 2 < n.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.Galois
nodes.description: In this file, we study the Galois theory of cyclotomic extensions of ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.Ideal
nodes.description: In this file, we prove results about ideals in cyclotomic extensions of ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.PID
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cyclotomic fields whose ring of integers is a PID.
nodes.description: We prove that ℤ [ζₚ] is a PID for specific values of p. The result holds for p ≤ 19, but the proof is more and more involved.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Cyclotomic.Three
nodes.description: We gather various results about the third cyclotomic field. The following notations are used in this file: K is a number field such that IsCyclotomicExtension {3} ℚ K, ζ is any primitive 3-rd root of unity in K, η is the element in the units of the ring of integers corresponding to ζ and λ = η - 1.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.DedekindZeta
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Dedekind zeta function of a number field
nodes.description: In this file, we define and prove results about the Dedekind zeta function of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Discriminant.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the discriminant of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Discriminant.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines the discriminant of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Discriminant.Different
nodes.description: The norm of differentIdeal ℤ 𝒪 is the absolute discriminant. Formula for the absolute discriminant of L in terms of that of K in an extension L/K. Assume that K₁ and K₂ are two linear disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals. Then, the absolute value of the discriminant of their compositum is equal to |discr K₁| ^ [K₂ : ℚ] |discr K₂| ^ [K₁ : ℚ].

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.EquivReindex
nodes.description: This file introduces an equivalence between the set of embeddings of K into ℂ and the index set of the chosen basis of the ring of integers of K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.ExistsRamified
nodes.descriptionTitle: Every number field has a ramified prime over ℚ
nodes.description: This is a trivial corollary of NumberField.not_dvd_discr_iff_forall_mem and NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two but is placed in a separate file to avoid large imports.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.FinitePlaces
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.FractionalIdeal
nodes.description: Prove some results on the fractional ideals of number fields.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.House
nodes.description: This file defines the house of an algebraic number α, which is the largest of the modulus of its conjugates.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Ideal.Asymptotics
nodes.descriptionTitle: Asymptotics on integral ideals of a number field
nodes.description: We prove several asymptotics involving integral ideals of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Ideal.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic results on integral ideals of a number field
nodes.description: We study results about integral ideals of a number field K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Ideal.KummerDedekind
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kummer-Dedekind criterion for the splitting of prime numbers
nodes.description: In this file, we give a specialized version of the Kummer-Dedekind criterion for the case of the splitting of rational primes in number fields.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfiniteAdeleRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: The infinite adele ring of a number field
nodes.description: This file contains the formalisation of the infinite adele ring of a number field as the finite product of completions over its infinite places.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Infinite places of a number field
nodes.description: This file defines the infinite places of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.Embeddings
nodes.description: This file defines the embeddings of a number field and, in particular, the embeddings into the field of complex numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.Ramification
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ramification of infinite places of a number field
nodes.description: This file studies the ramification of infinite places of a number field.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.TotallyRealComplex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Totally real and totally complex number fields
nodes.description: This file defines the type of totally real and totally complex number fields.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Norm
nodes.description: Given a finite extension of number fields, we define the norm morphism as a function between the rings of integers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.ProductFormula
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Product Formula for number fields
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Product Formula for number fields: for any non-zero element x of a number field K, we have ∏ |x|ᵥ=1 where the product runs over the equivalence classes of absolute values of K. The |⬝|ᵥ are normalized as follows: embedding in ℂ and the usual absolute value on ℂ; ideal of 𝓞 K raised to the power of the v-adic valuation of x.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Units.Basic
nodes.description: We prove some basic results on the group (𝓞 K)ˣ of units of the ring of integers 𝓞 K of a number field K and its torsion subgroup.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Units.DirichletTheorem
nodes.descriptionTitle: Dirichlet theorem on the group of units of a number field
nodes.description: This file is devoted to the proof of Dirichlet unit theorem that states that the group of units (𝓞 K)ˣ of units of the ring of integers 𝓞 K of a number field K modulo its torsion subgroup is a free ℤ-module of rank card (InfinitePlace K) - 1.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.NumberField.Units.Regulator
nodes.description: We define and prove basic results about the regulator of a number field K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Ostrowski
nodes.description: Ostrowski's Theorem for the field ℚ: every absolute value on ℚ is equivalent to either a p-adic absolute value or to the standard Archimedean (Euclidean) absolute value.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.AddChar
nodes.description: We show that for any complete, ultrametric normed ℤ_[p]-algebra R, there is a bijection between continuous additive characters ℤ_[p] → R and topologically nilpotent elements of R, given by sending κ to the element κ 1 - 1. This is used to define the Mahler transform for p-adic measures.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.Complex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The field ℂ_[p] of p-adic complex numbers.
nodes.description: In this file we define the field ℂ_[p] of p-adic complex numbers as the p-adic completion of an algebraic closure of ℚ_[p]. We endow ℂ_[p] with both a normed field and a valued field structure, induced by the unique extension of the p-adic norm to ℂ_[p].

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.HeightOneSpectrum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Isomorphisms between adicCompletion ℚ and ℚ_[p]
nodes.description: Let R have field of fractions ℚ. If v : HeightOneSpectrum R, then v.adicCompletion ℚ is the uniform space completion of ℚ with respect to the v-adic valuation. On the other hand, ℚ_[p] is the p-adic numbers, defined as the completion of ℚ with respect to the p-adic norm using the completion of Cauchy sequences. This file constructs continuous ℚ-algebra isomorphisms between the two, as well as continuous ℤ-algebra isomorphisms for their respective rings of integers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.Hensel
nodes.description: This file proves Hensel's lemma on ℤ_p, roughly following Keith Conrad's writeup:

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.MahlerBasis
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Mahler basis of continuous functions
nodes.description: In this file we introduce the Mahler basis function mahler k, for k : ℕ, which is the unique continuous map ℤ_[p] → ℤ_[p] agreeing with n ↦ n.choose k for n ∈ ℕ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.PadicIntegers
nodes.description: This file defines the p-adic integers ℤ_[p] as the subtype of ℚ_[p] with norm ≤ 1. We show that ℤ_[p]

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.PadicNorm
nodes.description: This file defines the p-adic norm on ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.PadicNumbers
nodes.description: This file defines the p-adic numbers (rationals) ℚ_[p] as the completion of ℚ with respect to the p-adic norm. We show that the p-adic norm on ℚ extends to ℚ_[p], that ℚ is embedded in ℚ_[p], and that ℚ_[p] is Cauchy complete.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.PadicVal.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the p-adic valuation on ℕ, ℤ, and ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.PadicVal.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines the p-adic valuation on ℕ, ℤ, and ℚ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.ProperSpace
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that ℤ_[p] is totally bounded and compact, and that ℚ_[p] is proper.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.RingHoms
nodes.descriptionTitle: Relating ℤ_[p] to ZMod (p ^ n), aka ℤ/p^nℤ.
nodes.description: In this file we establish connections between the p-adic integers ℤ_[p] and the integers modulo powers of p, ℤ/p^nℤ, implemented as ZMod (p^n).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.ValuativeRel
nodes.descriptionTitle: p-adic numbers with a valuative relation
nodes.description: p-adic, p adic, padic, norm, valuation, cauchy, completion, p-adic completion

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Padics.WithVal
nodes.description: The p-adic numbers are isomorphic as a field to the completion of the rationals at the p-adic valuation. This is implemented via Valuation.Completion using Rat.padicValuation, which is shorthand for UniformSpace.Completion (WithVal (Rat.padicValuation p)).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Pell
nodes.description: Pell's Equation is the equation $x^2 - d y^2 = 1$, where $d$ is a positive integer that is not a square, and one is interested in solutions in integers $x$ and $y$.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.PellMatiyasevic
nodes.description: This file solves Pell's equation, i.e. integer solutions to x ^ 2 - d y ^ 2 = 1 in the special case that d = a ^ 2 - 1. This is then applied to prove Matiyasevic's theorem that the power function is Diophantine, which is the last key ingredient in the solution to Hilbert's tenth problem. For the definition of Diophantine function, see NumberTheory.Dioph.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.PowModTotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: Modular exponentiation with the totient function
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about modular exponentiation. In particular, it contains lemmas showing that an exponent can be reduced modulo the totient function when the base is coprime to the modulus.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.PrimeCounting
nodes.description: In this file we define the prime counting function: the function on natural numbers that returns the number of primes less than or equal to its input.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.PrimesCongruentOne
nodes.description: We prove that, for any positive k : ℕ, there are infinitely many primes p such that p ≡ 1 [MOD k].

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Primorial
nodes.description: This file defines the primorial function (the product of primes less than or equal to some bound), and proves that primorial n ≤ 4 ^ n.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.PythagoreanTriples
nodes.description: The main result is the classification of Pythagorean triples. The final result is for general Pythagorean triples. It follows from the more interesting relatively prime case. We use the "rational parametrization of the circle" method for the proof. The parametrization maps the point (x / z, y / z) to the slope of the line through (-1, 0) and (x / z, y / z). This quickly shows that (x / z, y / z) = (2 m n / (m ^ 2 + n ^ 2), (m ^ 2 - n ^ 2) / (m ^ 2 + n ^ 2)) where m / n is the slope.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.Basic
nodes.description: Given P : Ideal S lying over p : Ideal R for the ring extension f : R →+ S (assuming P and p are prime or maximal where needed), the ramification index Ideal.ramificationIdx f p P is the multiplicity of P in map f p, and the inertia degree Ideal.inertiaDeg f p P is the degree of the field extension (S / P) : (R / p).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.Galois
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ramification theory in Galois extensions of Dedekind domains
nodes.description: In this file, we discuss the ramification theory in Galois extensions of Dedekind domains, which is also called Hilbert's Ramification Theory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.HilbertTheory
nodes.description: In this file, we develop Hilbert Theory on the splitting of prime ideals in a Galois extension.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.Inertia
nodes.description: Given P : Ideal S lying over p : Ideal R for the ring extension f : R →+ S (assuming P and p are prime or maximal where needed), the inertia degree Ideal.inertiaDeg p P is the degree of the field extension (S / P) : (R / p).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.Ramification
nodes.description: Given P : Ideal S lying over p : Ideal R for the ring extension f : R →+ S (assuming P and p are prime or maximal where needed), the ramification index Ideal.ramificationIdx p P is the multiplicity of P in map f p.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RamificationInertia.Unramified
nodes.description: We connect Ideal.ramificationIdx to the commutative algebra notion predicate of IsUnramifiedAt.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.RatFunc.Ostrowski
nodes.description: This file proves Ostrowski's theorem for the field of rational functions K(X), where K is any field: if v is a discrete valuation on K(X) which is trivial on elements of K, then v is equivalent to either the I-adic valuation for some I : HeightOneSpectrum K[X], or to the valuation at infinity FunctionField.inftyValuation K.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Rayleigh
nodes.description: This file proves Rayleigh's theorem on Beatty sequences. We start by proving compl_beattySeq, which is a generalization of Rayleigh's theorem, and eventually prove Irrational.beattySeq_symmDiff_beattySeq_pos, which is Rayleigh's theorem.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Real.GoldenRatio
nodes.descriptionTitle: The golden ratio and its conjugate
nodes.description: This file defines the golden ratio φ := (1 + √5)/2 and its conjugate ψ := (1 - √5)/2, which are the two real roots of X² - X - 1.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Real.Irrational
nodes.description: In this file we define a predicate Irrational on ℝ, prove that the n-th root of an integer number is irrational if it is not integer, and that √(q : ℚ) is irrational if and only if ¬IsSquare q ∧ 0 ≤ q.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SelbergSieve
nodes.description: We set up the working assumptions of the Selberg sieve, define the notion of an upper bound sieve and show that every upper bound sieve yields an upper bound on the size of the sifted set. We also define the Λ² sieve and prove that Λ² sieves are upper bound sieves. We then diagonalise the main term of the Λ² sieve.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SiegelsLemma
nodes.description: In this file we introduce and prove Siegel's Lemma in its most basic version. This is a fundamental tool in diophantine approximation and transcendence and says that there exists a "small" integral non-zero solution of a non-trivial underdetermined system of linear equations with integer coefficients.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SmoothNumbers
nodes.description: For s : Finset ℕ we define the set Nat.factoredNumbers s of "s-factored numbers" consisting of the positive natural numbers all of whose prime factors are in s, and we provide some API for this.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SumFourSquares
nodes.description: The main result in this file is sum_four_squares, a proof that every natural number is the sum of four square numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SumPrimeReciprocals
nodes.descriptionTitle: The sum of the reciprocals of the primes diverges
nodes.description: We show that the sum of 1/p, where p runs through the prime numbers, diverges. We follow the elementary proof by Erdős that is reproduced in "Proofs from THE BOOK". There are two versions of the main result: not_summable_one_div_on_primes, which expresses the sum as a sub-sum of the harmonic series, and Nat.Primes.not_summable_one_div, which writes it as a sum over Nat.Primes. We also show that the sum of p^r for r : ℝ converges if and only if r < -1; see Nat.Primes.summable_rpow.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.SumTwoSquares
nodes.description: Fermat's theorem on the sum of two squares. Every prime p congruent to 1 mod 4 is the sum of two squares; see Nat.Prime.sq_add_sq (which has the weaker assumption p % 4 ≠ 3).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Lindemann.AnalyticalPart
nodes.descriptionTitle: Analytic part of the Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for NumberTheory.Transcendental.Lindemann.AnalyticalPart.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Liouville.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of Liouville's theorem stating that all Liouville numbers are transcendental.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Liouville.LiouvilleNumber
nodes.description: This file contains a construction of a family of Liouville numbers, indexed by a natural number $m$. The most important property is that they are examples of transcendental real numbers. This fact is recorded in transcendental_liouvilleNumber.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Liouville.LiouvilleWith
nodes.descriptionTitle: Liouville numbers with a given exponent
nodes.description: We say that a real number x is a Liouville number with exponent p : ℝ if there exists a real number C such that for infinitely many denominators n there exists a numerator m such that x ≠ m / n and |x - m / n| < C / n ^ p. A number is a Liouville number in the sense of Liouville if it is LiouvilleWith any real exponent, see forall_liouvilleWith_iff.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Liouville.Measure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Volume of the set of Liouville numbers
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the set of Liouville numbers with exponent (irrationality measure) strictly greater than two is a set of Lebesgue measure zero, see volume_iUnion_setOf_liouvilleWith.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Transcendental.Liouville.Residual
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the set of Liouville numbers form a dense Gδ set. We also prove a similar statement about irrational numbers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.TsumDivisorsAntidiagonal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas on infinite sums over the antidiagonal of the divisors function
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the antidiagonal of the divisors function. It defines the map from Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal n to ℕ+ × ℕ+ given by sending n = a b to (a, b).

nodes.label: NumberTheory.TsumDivsorsAntidiagonal
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.VonMangoldt
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in NumberTheory.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.WellApproximable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Well-approximable numbers and Gallagher's ergodic theorem
nodes.description: Gallagher's ergodic theorem is a result in metric number theory. It thus belongs to that branch of mathematics concerning arithmetic properties of real numbers which hold almost everywhere with respect to the Lebesgue measure.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Wilson
nodes.description: This file contains a proof of Wilson's theorem.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.ZetaValues
nodes.descriptionTitle: Critical values of the Riemann zeta function
nodes.description: In this file we prove formulae for the critical values of ζ(s), and more generally of Hurwitz zeta functions, in terms of Bernoulli polynomials.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Zsqrtd.Basic
nodes.description: The ring of integers adjoined with a square root of d : ℤ.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Zsqrtd.GaussianInt
nodes.description: The Gaussian integers are complex integer, complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are both integers.

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Zsqrtd.QuadraticReciprocity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Facts about the Gaussian integers relying on quadratic reciprocity.
nodes.description: prime_iff_mod_four_eq_three_of_nat_prime A prime natural number is prime in ℤ[i] if and only if it is 3 mod 4

nodes.label: NumberTheory.Zsqrtd.ToReal
nodes.description: This file defines Zsqrtd.toReal and related lemmas. It is in a separate file to avoid pulling in all of Data.Real into Data.Zsqrtd.

nodes.label: Order.Antichain
nodes.description: This file defines antichains. An antichain is a set where any two distinct elements are not related. If the relation is (≤), this corresponds to incomparability and usual order antichains. If the relation is G.Adj for G : SimpleGraph α, this corresponds to independent sets of G.

nodes.label: Order.Antisymmetrization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Turning a preorder into a partial order
nodes.description: This file allows to make a preorder into a partial order by quotienting out the elements a, b such that a ≤ b and b ≤ a.

nodes.label: Order.Atoms
nodes.description: This module defines atoms, which are minimal non-⊥ elements in bounded lattices, simple lattices, which are lattices with only two elements, and related ideas.

nodes.label: Order.Atoms.Finite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Atoms, Coatoms, Simple Lattices, and Finiteness
nodes.description: This module contains some results on atoms and simple lattices in the finite context.

nodes.label: Order.Basic
nodes.description: This file proves basic results about orders, provides extensive dot notation, defines useful order classes and allows to transfer order instances.

nodes.label: Order.Birkhoff
nodes.description: This file proves two facts which together are commonly referred to as "Birkhoff representation": 1. Any nonempty finite partial order is isomorphic to the partial order of sup-irreducible elements in its lattice of lower sets. 2. Any nonempty finite distributive lattice is isomorphic to the lattice of lower sets of its partial order of sup-irreducible elements.

nodes.label: Order.BooleanAlgebra.Basic
nodes.description: This file provides some basic definitions, functions as well as lemmas for functions and type classes related to Boolean algebras as defined in Mathlib/Order/BooleanAlgebra/Defs.lean.

nodes.label: Order.BooleanAlgebra.Defs
nodes.description: This file sets up the theory of (generalized) Boolean algebras.

nodes.label: Order.BooleanAlgebra.Set
nodes.description: This file proves that Set α is a Boolean algebra, and proves results about set difference and complement.

nodes.label: Order.BooleanGenerators
nodes.description: In this file, we provide an alternative constructor for Boolean algebras.

nodes.label: Order.BooleanSubalgebra
nodes.description: This file defines Boolean subalgebras.

nodes.label: Order.Booleanisation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adding complements to a generalized Boolean algebra
nodes.description: This file embeds any generalized Boolean algebra into a Boolean algebra.

nodes.label: Order.Bounded
nodes.description: We prove miscellaneous lemmas about bounded and unbounded sets. Many of these are just variations on the same ideas, or similar results with a few minor differences. The file is divided into these different general ideas.

nodes.label: Order.BoundedOrder.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines top and bottom elements (greatest and least elements) of a type, the bounded variants of different kinds of lattices, sets up the typeclass hierarchy between them and provides instances for Prop and fun.

nodes.label: Order.BoundedOrder.Lattice
nodes.description: This file contains miscellaneous lemmas about lattices with top or bottom elements.

nodes.label: Order.BoundedOrder.Monotone
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Order.BoundedOrder.Monotone.

nodes.label: Order.Bounds.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we prove various lemmas about upper/lower bounds of a set: monotonicity, behaviour under ∪, ∩, insert, and provide formulas for ∅, univ, and intervals.

nodes.label: Order.Bounds.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define: (resp., lower) bounds of s is nonempty; for a partial order, it is unique if exists; of s; for a partial order, it is unique if exists.

nodes.label: Order.Bounds.Image
nodes.descriptionTitle: Images of upper/lower bounds under monotone functions
nodes.description: In this file we prove various results about the behaviour of bounds under monotone/antitone maps.

nodes.label: Order.Bounds.Lattice
nodes.description: Some results about upper and lower bounds over collections of sets.

nodes.label: Order.Bounds.OrderIso

nodes.label: Order.Completion

nodes.label: Order.ConditionallyCompleteLattice.Basic

nodes.description: Suppose α β are linear orders, with α countable and β dense, nontrivial. Then there is an order embedding α ↪ β. If in addition α is dense, nonempty, without endpoints and β is countable, without endpoints, then we can upgrade this to an order isomorphism α ≃ β.

nodes.label: Order.Cover
nodes.description: This file proves properties of the covering relation in an order. We say that b covers a if a < b and there is no element in between. We say that b weakly covers a if a ≤ b and there is no element between a and b. In a partial order this is equivalent to a ⋖ b ∨ a = b, in a preorder this is equivalent to a ⋖ b ∨ (a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ a)

nodes.label: Order.DirSupClosed
nodes.description: We say that a set s is closed under directed suprema whenever it contains all least upper bounds for nonempty, directed subsets. Conversely, a set s is inaccessible by directed suprema whenever its complement is closed under directed suprema. Equivalently, if the least upper bound of a nonempty directed set t is contained in s, then t and s must have nonempty intersection.
