nodes.label: Order.Filter.Bases.Basic
nodes.description: A filter basis B : FilterBasis α on a type α is a nonempty collection of sets of α such that the intersection of two elements of this collection contains some element of the collection. Compared to filters, filter bases do not require that any set containing an element of B belongs to B. A filter basis B can be used to construct B.filter : Filter α such that a set belongs to B.filter if and only if it contains an element of B.

nodes.label: Order.Filter.Bases.Finite

nodes.label: Order.Filter.Basic
nodes.description: A filter on a type α is a collection of sets of α which contains the whole α, is upwards-closed, and is stable under intersection. They are mostly used to abstract two related kinds of ideas: at a point or at infinity, etc... a point x, or for close enough pairs of points, or things happening almost everywhere in the sense of measure theory. Dually, filters can also express the idea of things happening often: for arbitrarily large n, or at a point in any neighborhood of given a point etc...

nodes.label: Order.UpperLower.Relative
nodes.description: This file proves results on IsRelUpperSet and IsRelLowerSet.

nodes.label: Order.WellFounded
nodes.description: A relation is well-founded if it can be used for induction: for each x, (∀ y, r y x → P y) → P x implies P x. Well-founded relations can be used for induction and recursion, including construction of fixed points in the space of dependent functions Π x : α, β x.

nodes.label: Order.WellFoundedSet
nodes.description: This file introduces versions of WellFounded and WellQuasiOrdered for sets.

nodes.label: Order.WellQuasiOrder
nodes.description: A well quasi-order (WQO) is a relation such that any infinite sequence contains an infinite subsequence of related elements. For a preorder, this is equivalent to having a well-founded order with no infinite antichains.

nodes.label: Order.WithBot
nodes.description: Adding a bot or a top to an order.

nodes.label: Order.WithBotTop
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adding both ⊥ and ⊤ to a type
nodes.description: This files defines an abbreviation WithBotTop ι for WithBot (WithTop ι). We also introduce an abbreviation EInt for WithBotTop ℤ.

nodes.label: Order.Zorn
nodes.description: This file proves several formulations of Zorn's Lemma.

nodes.label: Order.ZornAtoms
nodes.description: In this file we use Zorn's lemma to prove that a partial order is atomic if every nonempty chain c, ⊥ ∉ c, has a lower bound not equal to ⊥. We also prove the order dual version of this statement.

nodes.label: Probability.BorelCantelli
nodes.description: This file contains the second Borel-Cantelli lemma which states that, given a sequence of independent sets (sₙ) in a probability space, if ∑ n, μ sₙ = ∞, then the limsup of sₙ has measure 1. We employ a proof using Lévy's generalized Borel-Cantelli by choosing an appropriate filtration.

nodes.label: Probability.CDF
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cumulative distribution function of a real probability measure
nodes.description: The cumulative distribution function (cdf) of a probability measure over ℝ is a monotone, right continuous function with limit 0 at -∞ and 1 at +∞, such that cdf μ x = μ (Iic x) for all x : ℝ. Two probability measures are equal if and only if they have the same cdf.

nodes.label: Probability.CentralLimitTheorem
nodes.description: We prove the central limit theorem in dimension 1.

nodes.label: Probability.Combinatorics.BinomialRandomGraph.Defs
nodes.description: This file constructs the binomial distribution with parameter p on simple graphs with vertices V. This is the law G(V, p) of binomial random graphs with probability p.

nodes.label: Probability.CondVar
nodes.description: This file defines the variance of a real-valued random variable conditional to a sigma-algebra.

nodes.label: Probability.ConditionalExpectation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Probabilistic properties of the conditional expectation
nodes.description: This file contains some properties about the conditional expectation which does not belong in the main conditional expectation file.

nodes.label: Probability.ConditionalProbability
nodes.description: This file defines conditional probability and includes basic results relating to it.

nodes.label: Probability.Decision.Risk.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic properties of the risk of an estimator
nodes.description: prior: if we compose the data generating kernel P with a Markov kernel, then the Bayes risk increases.

nodes.label: Probability.Decision.Risk.Defs
nodes.description: An estimation problem is defined by a parameter space Θ, a data generating kernel P : Kernel Θ 𝓧 and a loss function ℓ : Θ → 𝓨 → ℝ≥0∞. A (randomized) estimator is a kernel κ : Kernel 𝓧 𝓨 that maps data to estimates of a quantity of interest that depends on the parameter. Often the quantity of interest is the parameter itself and 𝓨 = Θ. The quality of an estimate y when data comes from the distribution with parameter θ is measured by the value of the loss function ℓ θ y (lower is better).

nodes.label: Probability.Density
nodes.description: This file defines the probability density function of random variables, by which we mean measurable functions taking values in a Borel space. The probability density function is defined as the Radon–Nikodym derivative of the law of X. In particular, a measurable function f is said to the probability density function of a random variable X if for all measurable sets S, ℙ(X ∈ S) = ∫ x in S, f x dx.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Beta
nodes.description: Define the beta distribution over the reals.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Binomial
nodes.description: This file defines the binomial distribution and binomial random variables, and computes their expectation and variance.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Cauchy
nodes.description: Define the Cauchy distribution with location parameter x₀ and scale parameter γ.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Exponential
nodes.description: Define the Exponential measure over the reals.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Fernique
nodes.description: Let μ be a finite measure on a second-countable normed space E such that the product measure μ.prod μ on E × E is invariant by rotation of angle -π/4. Then there exists a constant C > 0 such that the function x ↦ exp (C ‖x‖ ^ 2) is integrable with respect to μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gamma
nodes.description: Define the gamma measure over the reals.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Basic
nodes.description: We introduce a predicate IsGaussian for measures on a Banach space E such that the map by any continuous linear form is a Gaussian measure on ℝ.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.CharFun
nodes.description: In this file we prove that Gaussian measures over a Banach space E are exactly those measures μ such that there exist m : E and f : StrongDual ℝ E →L[ℝ] StrongDual ℝ E →L[ℝ] ℝ positive semidefinite (satisfying f.toBilinForm.IsPosSemidef) such that charFunDual μ L = exp (L m I - f L L / 2). We also prove that such m and f are unique and equal to ∫ x, x ∂μ and covarianceBilinDual μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Fernique
nodes.description: We show that the product of two identical Gaussian measures is invariant under rotation. We then deduce Fernique's theorem, which states that for a Gaussian measure μ, there exists C > 0 such that the function x ↦ exp (C ‖x‖ ^ 2) is integrable with respect to μ. As a consequence, a Gaussian measure has finite moments of all orders.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.HasGaussianLaw.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we prove basic properties of Gaussian random variables.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.HasGaussianLaw.Def
nodes.description: In this file we define a predicate HasGaussianLaw X P, which states that under the probability measure P, the random variable X has a Gaussian distribution, i.e. IsGaussian (P.map X).

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.HasGaussianLaw.Independence
nodes.description: In this file we prove some results linking Gaussian random variables and independence. It is a well known fact that if (X, Y) is Gaussian, then X and Y are independent if their covariance is zero. We prove many versions of this theorem in different settings: in Banach spaces, Hilbert spaces, and for families of real random variables.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.IsGaussianProcess.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic properties of Gaussian processes. In particular, in IsGaussianProcess.of_isGaussianProcess, we show that if a stochastic process Y : S → Ω → F is such that for each s : S, Y s can be written as a linear map applied to finitely many values of a certain Gaussian process, then Y is itself a Gaussian process.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.IsGaussianProcess.Def
nodes.description: In this file we define a Gaussian process as a stochastic process whose finite dimensional distributions are Gaussian.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.IsGaussianProcess.Independence
nodes.description: This file contains properties about independence of Gaussian processes. More precisely, we prove different versions of the following statement: if some stochastic processes are jointly Gaussian, then they are independent if their marginals are uncorrelated.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
nodes.description: In this file we define the standard Gaussian distribution over a Euclidean space and multivariate Gaussian distributions over EuclideanSpace ℝ ι.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Real
nodes.description: We define a Gaussian measure over the reals.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Geometric
nodes.description: We define the geometric distributions over natural numbers. For 0 < p ≤ 1, geometricMeasure p is the measure which to {n} associates (1 - p) ^ n n.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Pareto
nodes.description: Define the Pareto measure over the reals.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Poisson.Basic
nodes.description: Define the Poisson measure over the natural numbers. For r : ℝ≥0, poissonMeasure r is the measure which to {n} associates exp (-r) r ^ n / (n)!.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Poisson.PoissonLimitThm
nodes.description: This file proves a Poisson limit theorem.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.SetBernoulli
nodes.descriptionTitle: Product of bernoulli distributions on a set
nodes.description: This file defines the product of bernoulli distributions on a set as a measure on sets. For a set u : Set ι and p between 0 and 1, this is the measure on Set ι such that each i ∈ u belongs to the random set with probability p, and each i ∉ u doesn't belong to it.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.TwoValued
nodes.description: This file proves a few lemmas about random variables that take at most two values.

nodes.label: Probability.Distributions.Uniform
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniform distributions and probability mass functions
nodes.description: This file defines two related notions of uniform distributions, which will be unified in the future.

nodes.label: Probability.HasLaw
nodes.description: We introduce a predicate HasLaw X μ P stating that the random variable X has law μ under the measure P. This is expressed as P.map X = μ. We also require X to be P-almost-everywhere measurable. Indeed, if X is not almost-everywhere measurable then P.map X is defined to be 0, so that HasLaw X 0 P would be true. The measurability hypothesis ensures nice interactions with operations on the codomain of X. See for instance HasLaw.comp, IndepFun.hasLaw_mul and IndepFun.hasLaw_add.

nodes.label: Probability.HasLawExists
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas that state the existence of random variables with given distributions and a given dependency structure (currently only mutual independence is considered).

nodes.label: Probability.IdentDistrib
nodes.description: Two random variables defined on two (possibly different) probability spaces but taking value in the same space are identically distributed if their distributions (i.e., the image probability measures on the target space) coincide. We define this concept and establish its basic properties in this file.

nodes.label: Probability.IdentDistribIndep
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about identically distributed random variables and independence
nodes.description: independent random variables on Ω', such that X and Z are identically distributed and Y and W are identically distributed, then the pairs (X, Y) and (Z, W) are identically distributed. a countable type ι, such that for each i, X i and Y i are identically distributed, then the products X and Y are identically distributed.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Independence of sets of sets and measure spaces (σ-algebras)
nodes.description: any finite set of indices s = {i_1, ..., i_n}, for any sets f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n, μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i). It will be used for families of π-systems. measure μ (typically defined on a finer σ-algebra) if the family of sets of measurable sets they define is independent. I.e., m : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω is independent with respect to a measure μ if for any finite set of indices s = {i_1, ..., i_n}, for any sets f i_1 ∈ m i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ m i_n, then μ (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ (f i).

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.BoundedContinuousFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Characterizing independence via bounded continuous functions
nodes.description: Given two random variables X : Ω → E and Y : Ω → F such that E and F are Borel spaces satisfying HasOuterApproxClosed, X and Y are independent if for any real bounded continuous functions f and g, ∫ ω, f (X ω) g (Y ω) ∂P = (∫ ω, f (X ω) ∂P) (∫ ω, g (Y ω) ∂P).

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.CharacteristicFunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Links between independence and characteristic function
nodes.description: Two random variables are independent if and only if their joint characteristic function is equal to the product of the characteristic functions. More specifically, prove this in Hilbert spaces for two variables and a finite family of variables. We prove the analogous statements in Banach spaces, with an arbitrary Lp norm, for the dual characteristic function.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Conditional
nodes.description: We define conditional independence of sets/σ-algebras/functions with respect to a σ-algebra.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.InfinitePi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Independence of an infinite family of random variables
nodes.description: In this file we provide several results about independence of arbitrary families of random variables, relying on Measure.infinitePi.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Integrable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Independence of functions implies that the measure is a probability measure
nodes.description: If a nonzero function belongs to ℒ^p (in particular if it is integrable) and is independent of another function, then the space is a probability space.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Integration
nodes.description: Integration results for independent random variables. Specifically, for two independent random variables X and Y over the extended non-negative reals, E[X Y] = E[X] E[Y], and similar results.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Kernel
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Probability.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Kernel.Indep
nodes.descriptionTitle: Independence of families of sets with respect to a kernel and a measure
nodes.description: A family of sets of sets π : ι → Set (Set Ω) is independent with respect to a kernel κ : Kernel α Ω and a measure μ on α if for any finite set of indices s = {i_1, ..., i_n}, for any sets f i_1 ∈ π i_1, ..., f i_n ∈ π i_n, then for μ-almost every a : α, κ a (⋂ i in s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, κ a (f i).

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Kernel.IndepFun
nodes.descriptionTitle: Independence of random variables with respect to a kernel and a measure
nodes.description: A family of random variables is independent if the corresponding σ-algebras are independent. Independence of families of sets and σ-algebras is covered in the Indep file. This file deals with independence of random variables specifically.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Process.Basic
nodes.description: We prove that a stochastic process $(X_s)_{s \in S}$ is independent from a random variable $Y$ if for all $s_1, ..., s_p \in S$ the family $(X_{s_1}, ..., X_{s_p})$ is independent from $Y$.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Process.HasIndepIncrements
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Probability.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Process.HasIndepIncrements.Basic
nodes.description: A stochastic process X : T → Ω → E has independent increments if for any n ≥ 1 and t₁ ≤ ... ≤ tₙ, the random variables X t₂ - X t₁, ..., X tₙ - X tₙ₋₁ are independent. Equivalently, for any monotone sequence (tₙ), the random variables (X tₙ₊₁ - X tₙ) are independent.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.Process.HasIndepIncrements.IsGaussianProcess
nodes.descriptionTitle: A stochastic process with independent increments and Gaussian marginals is Gaussian
nodes.description: We prove that a stochastic process with independent increments and Gaussian marginals is Gaussian. To do so, we first define I.orderEmbOfFinWithBot : Fin (#I + 1) → T, which is the map (⊥, t₁, ..., tₙ), where t₁ < ... < tₙ are the elements of I and ⊥ is the smallest element of T.

nodes.label: Probability.Independence.ZeroOne
nodes.description: Let s : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω be an independent sequence of sub-σ-algebras. Then any set which is measurable with respect to the tail σ-algebra limsup s atTop has probability 0 or 1.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic results about kernels in general and definitions of some particular kernels.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Category.SFinKer
nodes.description: The category of measurable spaces with s-finite kernels is a copy-discard category.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Category.Stoch
nodes.description: The category of measurable spaces with Markov kernels is a positive Markov category.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.CompProdEqIff
nodes.descriptionTitle: Condition for two kernels to be equal almost everywhere
nodes.description: We prove that two finite kernels κ, η : Kernel α β are μ-a.e. equal for a finite measure μ iff the composition-products μ ⊗ₘ κ and μ ⊗ₘ η are equal. The result requires α to be countable or β to be a countably generated measurable space.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.AbsolutelyContinuous
nodes.descriptionTitle: Absolute continuity of the composition of measures and kernels
nodes.description: This file contains some results about the absolute continuity of the composition of measures and kernels which use an assumption CountableOrCountablyGenerated α β on the measurable spaces.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.Comp
nodes.description: We define the composition η ∘ₖ κ of kernels κ : Kernel α β and η : Kernel β γ, which is a kernel from α to γ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.CompMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about compositions and maps of kernels
nodes.description: This file contains results that use both the composition of kernels and the map of a kernel by a function.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.CompNotation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Notation for the composition of a measure and a kernel
nodes.description: This operation, for which we introduce the notation ∘ₘ, takes μ : Measure α and κ : Kernel α β and creates κ ∘ₘ μ : Measure β. The integral of a function against κ ∘ₘ μ is ∫⁻ x, f x ∂(κ ∘ₘ μ) = ∫⁻ a, ∫⁻ b, f b ∂(κ a) ∂μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.CompProd
nodes.description: We define the composition-product κ ⊗ₖ η of two s-finite kernels κ : Kernel α β and η : Kernel (α × β) γ, a kernel from α to β × γ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.IntegralCompProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bochner integral of a function against the composition and the composition-products of two kernels
nodes.description: We prove properties of the composition and the composition-product of two kernels.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.KernelLemmas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas relating different ways to compose kernels
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the composition of kernels that involve several types of compositions/products.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.Lemmas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas relating different ways to compose measures and kernels
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the composition of measures and kernels that do not fit in any of the other files in this directory, because they involve several types of compositions/products.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.MapComap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Map of a kernel by a measurable function
nodes.description: We define the map and comap of a kernel along a measurable function, as well as some often useful particular cases.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.MeasureComp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about the composition of a measure and a kernel
nodes.description: Basic lemmas about the composition κ ∘ₘ μ of a kernel κ and a measure μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.MeasureCompProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Composition-Product of a measure and a kernel
nodes.description: This operation, denoted by ⊗ₘ, takes μ : Measure α and κ : Kernel α β and creates μ ⊗ₘ κ : Measure (α × β). The integral of a function against μ ⊗ₘ κ is ∫⁻ x, f x ∂(μ ⊗ₘ κ) = ∫⁻ a, ∫⁻ b, f (a, b) ∂(κ a) ∂μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.ParallelComp
nodes.description: Two kernels κ : Kernel α β and η : Kernel γ δ can be applied in parallel to give a kernel κ ∥ₖ η from α × γ to β × δ: (κ ∥ₖ η) (a, c) = (κ a).prod (η c).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.Prod
nodes.description: We define the product κ ×ₖ η of s-finite kernels κ : Kernel α β and η : Kernel α γ, which is a kernel from α to β × γ.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Composition.RadonNikodym
nodes.descriptionTitle: Radon-Nikodym derivative of a composition product
nodes.description: We compute the Radon-Nikodym derivative of a composition product μ ⊗ₘ κ with respect to another composition product ν ⊗ₘ η in terms of the Radon-Nikodym derivatives ∂μ/∂ν and ∂(μ ⊗ₘ κ)/∂(μ ⊗ₘ η).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.CondDistrib
nodes.description: We define the regular conditional probability distribution of Y : α → Ω given X : α → β, where Ω is a standard Borel space. This is a Kernel β Ω such that for almost all a, condDistrib evaluated at X a and a measurable set s is equal to the conditional expectation μ⟦Y ⁻¹' s | mβ.comap X⟧ evaluated at a.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Condexp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Kernel associated with a conditional expectation
nodes.description: We define condExpKernel μ m, a kernel from Ω to Ω such that for all integrable functions f, μ[f | m] =ᵐ[μ] fun ω => ∫ y, f y ∂(condExpKernel μ m ω).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Defs
nodes.description: A kernel from a measurable space α to another measurable space β is a measurable map α → MeasureTheory.Measure β, where the measurable space instance on measure β is the one defined in MeasureTheory.Measure.instMeasurableSpace. That is, a kernel κ verifies that for all measurable sets s of β, a ↦ κ a s is measurable.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Deterministic
nodes.description: This file defines the class IsDeterministic of deterministic kernels, and proves some properties about them.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines predicates for a kernel to "disintegrate" a measure or a kernel. This kernel is also called the "conditional kernel" of the measure or kernel.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.CDFToKernel
nodes.descriptionTitle: Building a Markov kernel from a conditional cumulative distribution function
nodes.description: Let κ : Kernel α (β × ℝ) and ν : Kernel α β be two finite kernels. A function f : α × β → StieltjesFunction ℝ is called a conditional kernel CDF of κ with respect to ν if it is measurable, tends to 0 at -∞ and to 1 at +∞ for all p : α × β, fun b ↦ f (a, b) x is (ν a)-integrable for all a : α and x : ℝ and for all measurable sets s : Set β, ∫ b in s, f (a, b) x ∂(ν a) = (κ a).real (s ×ˢ Iic x).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.CondCDF
nodes.description: Given ρ : Measure (α × ℝ), we define the conditional cumulative distribution function (conditional cdf) of ρ. It is a function condCDF ρ : α → ℝ → ℝ such that if ρ is a finite measure, then for all a : α condCDF ρ a is monotone and right-continuous with limit 0 at -∞ and limit 1 at +∞, and such that for all x : ℝ, a ↦ condCDF ρ a x is measurable. For all x : ℝ and measurable set s, that function satisfies ∫⁻ a in s, ENNReal.ofReal (condCDF ρ a x) ∂ρ.fst = ρ (s ×ˢ Iic x).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.Density
nodes.description: Let κ : Kernel α (γ × β) and ν : Kernel α γ be two finite kernels with Kernel.fst κ ≤ ν, where γ has a countably generated σ-algebra (true in particular for standard Borel spaces). We build a function density κ ν : α → γ → Set β → ℝ jointly measurable in the first two arguments such that for all a : α and all measurable sets s : Set β and A : Set γ, ∫ x in A, density κ ν a x s ∂(ν a) = (κ a).real (A ×ˢ s).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lebesgue and Bochner integrals of conditional kernels
nodes.description: Integrals of ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.condKernel and MeasureTheory.Measure.condKernel.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.MeasurableStieltjes
nodes.description: We provide tools to build a measurable function α → StieltjesFunction ℝ with limits 0 at -∞ and 1 at +∞ for all a : α from a measurable function f : α → ℚ → ℝ. These measurable parametric Stieltjes functions are cumulative distribution functions (CDF) of transition kernels. The reason for going through ℚ instead of defining directly a Stieltjes function is that since ℚ is countable, building a measurable function is easier and we can obtain properties of the form ∀ᵐ (a : α) ∂μ, ∀ (q : ℚ), ...

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.StandardBorel
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of disintegration of measures and kernels for standard Borel spaces
nodes.description: Let κ : Kernel α (β × Ω) be a finite kernel, where Ω is a standard Borel space. Then if α is countable or β has a countably generated σ-algebra (for example if it is standard Borel), then there exists a Kernel (α × β) Ω called conditional kernel and denoted by condKernel κ such that κ = fst κ ⊗ₖ condKernel κ. We also define a conditional kernel for a measure ρ : Measure (β × Ω), where Ω is a standard Borel space. This is a Kernel β Ω denoted by ρ.condKernel such that ρ = ρ.fst ⊗ₘ ρ.condKernel.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Disintegration.Unique
nodes.description: We prove that the conditional kernels ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.condKernel and MeasureTheory.Measure.condKernel are almost everywhere unique.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Integral
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Probability.Kernel.Integral.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Invariance
nodes.descriptionTitle: Invariance of measures along a kernel
nodes.description: We say that a measure μ is invariant with respect to a kernel κ if its push-forward along the kernel μ.bind κ is the same measure.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.IonescuTulcea.Maps
nodes.description: This file contains auxiliary maps which are used to prove the Ionescu-Tulcea theorem.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.IonescuTulcea.PartialTraj
nodes.description: This file is the first step towards Ionescu-Tulcea theorem, which allows for instance to construct the product of an infinite family of probability measures. The idea of the statement is as follows: consider a family of kernels κ : (n : ℕ) → Kernel (Π i : Iic n, X i) (X (n + 1)). One can interpret κ n as a kernel which takes as an input the trajectory of a point started in X 0 and moving X 0 → X 1 → X 2 → ... → X n and which outputs the distribution of the next position of the point in X (n + 1).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.IonescuTulcea.Traj
nodes.description: This file proves the Ionescu-Tulcea theorem. The idea of the statement is as follows: consider a family of kernels κ : (n : ℕ) → Kernel (Π i : Iic n, X i) (X (n + 1)). One can interpret κ n as a kernel which takes as an input the trajectory of a point started in X 0 and moving X 0 → X 1 → X 2 → ... → X n and which outputs the distribution of the next position of the point in X (n + 1). If a b : ℕ and a < b, we can compose the kernels, and κ a ⊗ₖ κ (a + 1) ⊗ₖ ...

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Irreducible
nodes.description: A kernel κ : Kernel α α is φ-irreducible, for a given measure φ on α, if for every measurable set A with positive measure under φ, and for every a : α, there exists a positive integer n such that we have (κ ^ n) a A > 0.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.MeasurableIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability of the integral against a kernel
nodes.description: The Bochner integral of a strongly measurable function against a kernel is strongly measurable.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.MeasurableLIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Measurability of the integral against a kernel
nodes.description: The Lebesgue integral of a measurable function against a kernel is measurable.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Posterior
nodes.description: For μ : Measure Ω (called prior measure), seen as a measure on a parameter, and a kernel κ : Kernel Ω 𝓧 that gives the conditional distribution of "data" in 𝓧 given the prior parameter, we can get the distribution of the data with κ ∘ₘ μ, and the joint distribution of parameter and data with μ ⊗ₘ κ : Measure (Ω × 𝓧).

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Proper
nodes.description: This file defines properness of measure kernels.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.RadonNikodym
nodes.descriptionTitle: Radon-Nikodym derivative and Lebesgue decomposition for kernels
nodes.description: Let α and γ be two measurable spaces, where either α is countable or γ is countably generated. Let κ, η : Kernel α γ be finite kernels. Then there exists a function Kernel.rnDeriv κ η : α → γ → ℝ≥0∞ jointly measurable on α × γ and a kernel Kernel.singularPart κ η : Kernel α γ such that

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.Representation
nodes.description: This file contains results about isolation of kernels randomness. In particular, it shows that, when the target space is a standard Borel space, any Markov kernel can be represented as the image of the uniform measure on [0,1] by a deterministic map. It corresponds to Lemma 4.22 in Foundations of Modern Probability.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.SetIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral against a kernel over a set
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about the integral against a kernel and over a set.

nodes.label: Probability.Kernel.WithDensity
nodes.description: For an s-finite kernel κ : Kernel α β and a function f : α → β → ℝ≥0∞ which is finite everywhere, we define withDensity κ f as the kernel a ↦ (κ a).withDensity (f a). This is an s-finite kernel.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.Basic
nodes.description: A family of functions f : ι → Ω → E is a martingale with respect to a filtration ℱ if every f i is integrable, f is strongly adapted with respect to ℱ and for all i ≤ j, μ[f j | ℱ i] =ᵐ[μ] f i. On the other hand, f : ι → Ω → E is said to be a supermartingale with respect to the filtration ℱ if f i is integrable, f is strongly adapted with respect to ℱ and for all i ≤ j, μ[f j | ℱ i] ≤ᵐ[μ] f i.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.BorelCantelli
nodes.description: This file proves Lévy's generalized Borel-Cantelli lemma which is a generalization of the Borel-Cantelli lemmas. With this generalization, one can easily deduce the Borel-Cantelli lemmas by choosing appropriate filtrations. This file also contains the one-sided martingale bound which is required to prove the generalized Borel-Cantelli.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.Centering
nodes.description: Any ℕ-indexed stochastic process which is strongly adapted and integrable can be written as the sum of a martingale and a predictable process. This result is also known as Doob's decomposition theorem. From a process f, a filtration ℱ and a measure μ, we define two processes martingalePart f ℱ μ and predictablePart f ℱ μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.Convergence
nodes.description: The martingale convergence theorems are a collection of theorems characterizing the convergence of a martingale provided it satisfies some boundedness conditions. This file contains the almost everywhere martingale convergence theorem which provides an almost everywhere limit to an L¹ bounded submartingale. It also contains the L¹ martingale convergence theorem which provides an L¹ limit to a uniformly integrable submartingale. Finally, it also contains the Lévy upwards theorems.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.OptionalSampling
nodes.description: If τ is a bounded stopping time and σ is another stopping time, then the value of a martingale f at the stopping time min τ σ is almost everywhere equal to μ[stoppedValue f τ | hσ.measurableSpace].

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.OptionalStopping
nodes.description: The optional stopping theorem states that a strongly adapted integrable process f is a submartingale if and only if for all bounded stopping times τ and π such that τ ≤ π, the stopped value of f at τ has expectation smaller than its stopped value at π.

nodes.label: Probability.Martingale.Upcrossing
nodes.description: Given a discrete real-valued submartingale $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, denoting by $U_N(a, b)$ the number of times $f_n$ crossed from below $a$ to above $b$ before time $N$, Doob's upcrossing estimate (also known as Doob's inequality) states that $$(b - a) \mathbb{E}[U_N(a, b)] \le \mathbb{E}[(f_N - a)^+].$$ Doob's upcrossing estimate is an important inequality and is central in proving the martingale convergence theorems.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.Basic
nodes.description: measure μ, μ[X^p] μ[(X - μ[X])^p] μ[exp(tX)] function

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.ComplexMGF
nodes.description: The moment-generating function (mgf) is t : ℝ ↦ μ[fun ω ↦ rexp (t X ω)]. It can be extended to a complex function z : ℂ ↦ μ[fun ω ↦ cexp (z X ω)], which we call complexMGF X μ. That function is holomorphic on the vertical strip with base the interior of the interval of definition of the mgf. On the vertical line that goes through 0, complexMGF X μ is equal to the characteristic function.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.Covariance
nodes.description: We define the covariance of two real-valued random variables.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.CovarianceBilin
nodes.description: Given a measure μ defined over a Banach space E, one can consider the associated covariance bilinear form which maps L₁ L₂ : StrongDual ℝ E to cov[L₁, L₂; μ]. This is called covarianceBilinDual μ and is defined in the CovarianceBilinDual file.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.CovarianceBilinDual
nodes.description: We define the covariance of a finite measure in a Banach space E, as a continuous bilinear form on Dual ℝ E.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.IntegrableExpMul
nodes.description: For X a real random variable and μ a finite measure, the set {t | Integrable (fun ω ↦ exp (t X ω)) μ} is an interval containing zero. This is the set of points for which the moment-generating function mgf X μ t is well defined. We denote that set by integrableExpSet X μ.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.MGFAnalytic
nodes.description: The moment-generating function mgf X μ of a random variable X with respect to a measure μ is analytic on the interior of integrableExpSet X μ, the interval on which it is defined.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.SubGaussian
nodes.description: This presentation of sub-Gaussian random variables is inspired by section 2.5 of [vershynin2018high]. Let X be a random variable. Consider the following five properties, in which Kᵢ are positive reals,

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.Tilted
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results relating Measure.tilted to mgf and cgf
nodes.description: For a random variable X : Ω → ℝ and a measure μ, the tilted measure μ.tilted (t X ·) is linked to the moment-generating function (mgf) and the cumulant-generating function (cgf) of X.

nodes.label: Probability.Moments.Variance
nodes.description: We define the variance of a real-valued random variable as Var[X] = 𝔼[(X - 𝔼[X])^2] (in the ProbabilityTheory locale).

nodes.label: Probability.Notation
nodes.description: This file defines the following notations, for functions X,Y, measures P, Q defined on a measurable space m0, and another measurable space structure m with hm : m ≤ m0, measurable space m. The similar P[X|m] for a measure P is defined in MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic.

nodes.label: Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Basic
nodes.description: This file is about probability mass functions or discrete probability measures: a function α → ℝ≥0∞ such that the values have (infinite) sum 1.

nodes.label: Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Binomial
nodes.description: This file defines the probability mass function of the binomial distribution.

nodes.label: Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Specific Constructions of Probability Mass Functions
nodes.description: This file gives a number of different PMF constructions for common probability distributions.

nodes.label: Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Integrals
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integrals with a measure derived from probability mass functions.
nodes.description: This file connects PMF with integral. The main result is that the integral (i.e. the expected value) with regard to a measure derived from a PMF is a sum weighted by the PMF.

nodes.label: Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Monad
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monad Operations for Probability Mass Functions
nodes.description: This file constructs two operations on PMF that give it a monad structure. pure a is the distribution where a single value a has probability 1. bind pa pb : PMF β is the distribution given by sampling a : α from pa : PMF α, and then sampling from pb a : PMF β to get a final result b : β.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.Adapted
nodes.description: This file defines the related notions of a process u being (strongly) Adapted or Progressive (progressively measurable) with respect to a filtration f, and proves some basic facts about them.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.Filtration
nodes.description: This file defines filtrations of a measurable space and σ-finite filtrations.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.FiniteDimensionalLaws
nodes.descriptionTitle: Finite-dimensional distributions of a stochastic process
nodes.description: For a stochastic process X : T → Ω → 𝓧 and a finite measure P on Ω, the law of the process is P.map (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)), and its finite-dimensional distributions are P.map (fun ω ↦ I.restrict (X · ω)) for I : Finset T.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.HittingTime
nodes.description: Given a stochastic process, the hitting time provides the first time the process "hits" some subset of the state space. The hitting time is a stopping time in the case that the time index is discrete and the process is strongly adapted (this is true in a far more general setting however we have only proved it for the discrete case so far).

nodes.label: Probability.Process.Kolmogorov
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stochastic processes satisfying the Kolmogorov condition
nodes.description: A stochastic process X : T → Ω → E on an index space T and a measurable space Ω with measure P is said to satisfy the Kolmogorov condition with exponents p, q and constant M if for all s, t : T, the pair (X s, X t) is measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra on E × E and the following condition holds: ∫⁻ ω, edist (X s ω) (X t ω) ^ p ∂P ≤ M edist s t ^ q.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.LocalProperty
nodes.description: This file defines local and stable properties of stochastic processes with respect to a filtration. This is notably useful for local martingales.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.PartitionFiltration
nodes.descriptionTitle: Filtration built from the finite partitions of a countably generated measurable space
nodes.description: In a countably generated measurable space α, we can build a sequence of finer and finer finite measurable partitions of the space such that the measurable space is generated by the union of all partitions. This sequence of partitions is defined in MeasureTheory.MeasurableSpace.CountablyGenerated.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.Predictable
nodes.description: This file defines the predictable σ-algebra associated to a filtration, as well as the notion of predictable processes. We prove that predictable processes are progressively measurable and adapted. We also give an equivalent characterization of predictability for discrete processes.

nodes.label: Probability.Process.Stopping
nodes.descriptionTitle: Stopping times, stopped processes and stopped values
nodes.description: Definition and properties of stopping times.

nodes.label: Probability.ProductMeasure
nodes.description: This file provides a definition for the product measure of an arbitrary family of probability measures. Given μ : (i : ι) → Measure (X i) such that each μ i is a probability measure, Measure.infinitePi μ is the only probability measure ν over Π i, X i such that ν (Set.pi s t) = ∏ i ∈ s, μ i (t i), with s : Finset ι and such that ∀ i ∈ s, MeasurableSet (t i) (see eq_infinitePi and infinitePi_pi). We also provide a few results regarding integration against this measure.

nodes.label: Probability.StrongLaw
nodes.descriptionTitle: The strong law of large numbers
nodes.description: We prove the strong law of large numbers, in ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae: If X n is a sequence of independent identically distributed integrable random variables, then ∑ i ∈ range n, X i / n converges almost surely to 𝔼[X 0]. We give here the strong version, due to Etemadi, that only requires pairwise independence.

nodes.label: Probability.UniformOn
nodes.description: The classical formulation of probability states that the probability of an event occurring in a finite probability space is the ratio of that event to all possible events. This notion can be expressed with measure theory using the counting measure. In particular, given the sets s and t, we define the probability of t occurring in s to be |s|⁻¹ |s ∩ t|. With this definition, we recover the probability over the entire sample space when s = Set.univ.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Action
nodes.description: This file is the preliminary for the linearize functor from Action (Type w) G to Rep k G, constructing the functor from the Representation would reduce the amount of DefEq abuses that we currently are doing in the Rep file.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.AlgebraRepresentation.Basic
nodes.description: This file collects basic general facts about algebra representations. The purpose of this file is to have general results so that when we prove a corresponding fact about group representations (or Lie algebra representations etc), we can deduce them as special cases of facts from this file.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Basic
nodes.description: This file introduces monoid representations and their characters and defines a few ways to construct representations.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Character
nodes.description: This file introduces characters of representation and proves basic lemmas about how characters behave under various operations on representations.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Coinduced
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k, a monoid homomorphism φ : G → H, and a k-linear G-representation A, this file introduces the coinduced representation $Coind_G^H(A)$ of A as an H-representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Coinvariants
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a monoid G, this file introduces the coinvariants of a k-linear G-representation (V, ρ).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Continuous.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines continuous representations of a monoid G on a R-module V and related basic results.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Equiv
nodes.description: This file is a preliminary file for the Isos in Rep, we build all the isomorphisms from representation level to avoid abusing defeq.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.FDRep
nodes.descriptionTitle: FDRep k G is the category of finite-dimensional k-linear representations of G.
nodes.description: If V : FDRep k G, there is a coercion that allows you to treat V as a type, and this type comes equipped with Module k V and FiniteDimensional k V instances. Also V.ρ gives the homomorphism G → (V →ₗ[k] V).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.FinGroupCharZero
nodes.description: This proves some properties of representations that follow from Maschke's theorem.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.FiniteIndex
nodes.descriptionTitle: (Co)induced representations of a finite index subgroup
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k, a finite index subgroup S ≤ G, and a k-linear S-representation A, this file defines an isomorphism $Ind_S^G(A) ≅ Coind_S^G(A)$. Given g : G and a : A, the forward map sends ⟦g ⊗ₜ[k] a⟧ to the function G → A supported at sg by ρ(s)(a) for s : S and which is 0 elsewhere. Meanwhile, the inverse sends f : G → A to ∑ᵢ ⟦gᵢ ⊗ₜ[k] f(gᵢ)⟧ for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, where g₁, ..., gₙ is a set of right coset representatives of S.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.FiniteCyclic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projective resolution of k as a trivial k-linear representation of a finite cyclic group
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring and G a finite commutative group. Given g : G and A : Rep k G, we can define a periodic chain complex in Rep k G given by ... ⟶ A --N--> A --(ρ(g) - 𝟙)--> A --N--> A --(ρ(g) - 𝟙)--> A ⟶ 0 where N is the norm map sending a : A to ∑ ρ(g)(a) for all g in G.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The group cohomology of a k-linear G-representation
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring and G a group. This file defines the group cohomology of A : Rep k G to be the cohomology of the complex $$0 \to \mathrm{Fun}(G^0, A) \to \mathrm{Fun}(G^1, A) \to \mathrm{Fun}(G^2, A) \to \dots$$ with differential $d^n$ sending $f: G^n \to A$ to the function mapping $(g_0, \dots, g_n)$ to $$\rho(g_0)(f(g_1, \dots, g_n))$$ $$+ \sum_{i = 0}^{n - 1} (-1)^{i + 1}\cdot f(g_0, \dots, g_ig_{i + 1}, \dots, g_n)$$ $$+ (-1)^{n + 1}\cdot f(g_0, \dots, g_{n - 1})$$ (where ρ is the representation...

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.FiniteCyclic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Group cohomology of a finite cyclic group
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring, G a group and A a k-linear G-representation. Given endomorphisms φ, ψ : A ⟶ A such that φ ∘ ψ = ψ ∘ φ = 0, denote by Chains(A, φ, ψ) the periodic chain complex ... ⟶ A --φ--> A --ψ--> A --φ--> A --ψ--> A ⟶ 0 and by Cochains(A, φ, ψ) the periodic cochain complex 0 ⟶ A --ψ--> A --φ--> A --ψ--> A --φ--> A ⟶ ....

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.Functoriality
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k, a group homomorphism f : G → H, a k-linear H-representation A, a k-linear G-representation B, and a representation morphism Res(f)(A) ⟶ B, we get a cochain map inhomogeneousCochains A ⟶ inhomogeneousCochains B and hence maps on cohomology Hⁿ(H, A) ⟶ Hⁿ(G, B). We also provide extra API for these maps in degrees 0, 1, 2.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.Hilbert90
nodes.description: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. Then this file proves Noether's generalization of Hilbert's Theorem 90: that the 1st group cohomology $H^1(Aut_K(L), L^\times)$ is trivial. We state it both in terms of $H^1$ and in terms of cocycles being coboundaries.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.LongExactSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Long exact sequence in group cohomology
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a group G, this file shows that a short exact sequence of k-linear G-representations 0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0 induces a short exact sequence of complexes 0 ⟶ inhomogeneousCochains X₁ ⟶ inhomogeneousCochains X₂ ⟶ inhomogeneousCochains X₃ ⟶ 0.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.LowDegree
nodes.descriptionTitle: The low-degree cohomology of a k-linear G-representation
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring and G a group. This file contains specialised API for the cocycles and group cohomology of a k-linear G-representation A in degrees 0, 1 and 2.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupCohomology.Shapiro
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a subgroup S ≤ G, the file Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Coinduced.lean proves that the functor Coind_S^G : Rep k S ⥤ Rep k G preserves epimorphisms. Since Res(S) : Rep k G ⥤ Rep k S is left adjoint to Coind_S^G, this means Res(S) preserves projective objects. Since Res(S) is also exact, given a projective resolution P of k as a trivial k-linear G-representation, Res(S)(P) is a projective resolution of k as a trivial k-linear S-representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The group homology of a k-linear G-representation
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring and G a group. This file defines the group homology of A : Rep k G to be the homology of the complex $$\dots \to \bigoplus_{G^2} A \to \bigoplus_{G^1} A \to \bigoplus_{G^0} A$$ with differential $d_n$ sending $a\cdot (g_0, \dots, g_n)$ to $$\rho(g_0^{-1})(a)\cdot (g_1, \dots, g_n)$$ $$+ \sum_{i = 0}^{n - 1}(-1)^{i + 1}a\cdot (g_0, \dots, g_ig_{i + 1}, \dots, g_n)$$ $$+ (-1)^{n + 1}a\cdot (g_0, \dots, g_{n - 1})$$ (where ρ is the representation attached to A).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.FiniteCyclic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Group homology of a finite cyclic group
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring, G a group and A a k-linear G-representation. Given endomorphisms φ, ψ : A ⟶ A such that φ ∘ ψ = ψ ∘ φ = 0, denote by Chains(A, φ, ψ) the periodic chain complex ... ⟶ A --φ--> A --ψ--> A --φ--> A --ψ--> A ⟶ 0.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.Functoriality
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k, a group homomorphism f : G → H, a k-linear G-representation A, a k-linear H-representation B, and a representation morphism A ⟶ Res(f)(B), we get a chain map inhomogeneousChains A ⟶ inhomogeneousChains B and hence maps on homology Hₙ(G, A) ⟶ Hₙ(H, B).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.LongExactSequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Long exact sequence in group homology
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a group G, this file shows that a short exact sequence of k-linear G-representations 0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0 induces a short exact sequence of complexes 0 ⟶ inhomogeneousChains X₁ ⟶ inhomogeneousChains X₂ ⟶ inhomogeneousChains X₃ ⟶ 0.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.LowDegree
nodes.descriptionTitle: The low-degree homology of a k-linear G-representation
nodes.description: Let k be a commutative ring and G a group. This file contains specialised API for the cycles and group homology of a k-linear G-representation A in degrees 0, 1 and 2. In Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupHomology/Basic.lean, we define the nth group homology of A to be the homology of a complex inhomogeneousChains A, whose objects are (Fin n →₀ G) → A; this is unnecessarily unwieldy in low degree.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.GroupHomology.Shapiro
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a subgroup S ≤ G, the file Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Coinduced.lean proves that the functor Coind_S^G : Rep k S ⥤ Rep k G preserves epimorphisms. Since Res(S) : Rep k G ⥤ Rep k S is left adjoint to Coind_S^G, this means Res(S) preserves projective objects. Since Res(S) is also exact, given a projective resolution P of k as a trivial k-linear G-representation, Res(S)(P) is a projective resolution of k as a trivial k-linear S-representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Homological.Resolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: The standard and bar resolutions of k as a trivial k-linear G-representation
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k and a group G, this file defines two projective resolutions of k as a trivial k-linear G-representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Induced
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring k, a group homomorphism φ : G → H, and a k-linear G-representation A, this file introduces the induced representation $Ind_G^H(A)$ of A as an H-representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Intertwining
nodes.description: This file gives defines intertwining maps of representations (aka equivariant linear maps).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Invariants
nodes.descriptionTitle: Subspace of invariants a group representation
nodes.description: This file introduces the subspace of invariants of a group representation and proves basic results about it. The main tool used is the average of all elements of the group, seen as an element of k[G]. The action of this special element gives a projection onto the subspace of invariants. In order for the definition of the average element to make sense, we need to assume for most of the results that the order of G is invertible in k (e. g. k has characteristic 0).

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Irreducible
nodes.description: This file defines irreducible monoid representations.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Maschke
nodes.description: We prove Maschke's theorem for finite groups, in the formulation that every submodule of a k[G] module has a complement, when k is a field with Fintype.card G invertible in k.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Rep.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rep k G is the category of k-linear representations of G.
nodes.description: Given a G-representation ρ on a module V, you can construct the bundled representation as Rep.of ρ. Conversely, given a bundled representation A : Rep k G, you can get the underlying module as A.V and the representation on it as A.ρ.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Rep.Iso
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equivalence between Rep k G and ModuleCat k[G]
nodes.description: In this file we show that the category of k-linear representations of a monoid G is equivalent to the category of modules over the monoid algebra k[G].

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Rep.Res
nodes.description: Given a group homomorphism f : H → G, we have the restriction functor resFunctor f : Rep k G ⥤ Rep k H which sends a G-representation ρ to the H-representation ρ.comp f.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Semisimple
nodes.description: This file defines the typeclass IsSemisimpleRepresentation for semisimple monoid representations.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Submodule
nodes.descriptionTitle: Invariant submodules of a group representation
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RepresentationTheory.Submodule.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Subrepresentation
nodes.description: This file defines subrepresentations of a monoid representation.

nodes.label: RepresentationTheory.Tannaka
nodes.description: In this file we prove Tannaka duality for finite groups.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Algebra
nodes.description: In this file we provide an algebra instance on the adic completion of a ring. Then the adic completion of any module is a module over the adic completion of the ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.AsTensorProduct
nodes.description: In this file we examine properties of the natural map

nodes.descriptionTitle: Completion of a module with respect to an ideal.
nodes.description: In this file we define the notions of Hausdorff, precomplete, and complete for an R-module M with respect to an ideal I:

nodes.descriptionTitle: Completeness of the Adic Completion for Finitely Generated Ideals

nodes.description: In this file we establish exactness properties of adic completions. In particular we show:

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Functoriality
nodes.description: In this file we establish functorial properties of the adic completion.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.LocalRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic Properties of Complete Local Ring
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a ring that is adic complete with respect to a maximal ideal ia a local ring (complete local ring).

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Noetherian
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Noetherian.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.RingHom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lift of ring homomorphisms to adic completions
nodes.description: Let R, S be rings, I be an ideal of S. In this file we prove that a compatible family of ring homomorphisms from a ring R to S ⧸ I ^ n can be lifted to a ring homomorphism R →+ AdicCompletion I S. If S is I-adically complete, then this compatible family of ring homomorphisms can be lifted to a ring homomorphism R →+ S.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdicCompletion.Topology
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connection between adic properties and topological properties
nodes.description: IsPrecomplete I R is equivalent to CompleteSpace R in the adic topology. IsAdicComplete I R is equivalent to CompleteSpace R and T2Space R in the adic topology.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Adjoin.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic results on Algebra.adjoin.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Adjoin.Dimension
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some results on dimensions of algebra adjoin
nodes.description: This file contains some results on dimensions of Algebra.adjoin.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Adjoin.FG
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of finitely-generated subalgebras.

nodes.descriptionTitle: Finitely generated subalgebras of a base change obtained from an element
nodes.description: R-algebras A and B, there exists a finitely generated subalgebra C of B such that x is contained in C ⊗[R] B.

nodes.description: Some lemmas on the ring generated by adjoining an element to a field.

nodes.description: adjoining an element to a commutative (semi)ring gives a commutative (semi)ring proving a fact about a : adjoin R {x} is the same as proving it for aeval x p where p is an arbitrary polynomial

nodes.label: RingTheory.Adjoin.Polynomial.Bivariate
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bivariate polynomials and adjoining transcendental elements
nodes.description: Given two transcendental elements a, b over R, if one of them, say a, is algebraic over R[b] then b is algebraic over R[a].

nodes.description: This file defines the canonical power basis on R[x], where x is an integral element over R.

nodes.description: This file contains basic results on Algebra.adjoin, specifically on adjoining singletons.

nodes.description: then A is finitely generated as R-algebra C is algebra-finite over A, and C is module-finite over B, then B is algebra-finite over A.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AdjoinRoot
nodes.description: This file defines the commutative ring AdjoinRoot f, the ring R[X]/(f) obtained from a commutative ring R and a polynomial f : R[X]. If furthermore R is a field and f is irreducible, the field structure on AdjoinRoot f is constructed.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraTower
nodes.description: We set up the basic theory of algebra towers. An algebra tower A/S/R is expressed by having instances of Algebra A S, Algebra R S, Algebra R A and IsScalarTower R S A, the later asserting the compatibility condition (r • s) • a = r • (s • a).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.Basic
nodes.description: An element of an R-algebra is algebraic over R if it is the root of a nonzero polynomial. An R-algebra is algebraic over R if and only if all its elements are algebraic over R. The main result in this file proves transitivity of algebraicity: a tower of algebraic field extensions is algebraic.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.Cardinality
nodes.description: This file contains results on cardinality of algebraic extensions.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.Defs
nodes.description: An element of an R-algebra is algebraic over R if it is the root of a nonzero polynomial. An R-algebra is algebraic over R if and only if all its elements are algebraic over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.Integral
nodes.description: This file relates algebraic and integral elements of an algebra, by proving every integral element is algebraic and that every algebraic element over a field is integral.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.LinearIndependent
nodes.description: then {(x - a)⁻¹ | a : F} is linearly independent over F.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.MvPolynomial
nodes.description: This file lists some results on some elements in MvPolynomial σ R being transcendental over the base ring R and subrings MvPolynomial.supported of MvPolynomial σ R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.Pi
nodes.description: This file defines algebraic functions as the image of the algebraMap R[X] (R → S).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Algebraic.StronglyTranscendental
nodes.description: In this file, we provide basic properties for strongly transcendental elements in an algebra. This is a relatively niche notion, but is useful for proving Zariski's main theorem.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.Adjoin
nodes.description: This file concerns adjoining an algebraic independent family to a field.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.AlgebraicClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Algebraic independence persists to the algebraic closure
nodes.description: then a family of elements in A that are algebraically independent over R remains algebraically independent over S, provided that S has no zero divisors.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic results on algebraic independence of a family of elements of an R-algebra

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines algebraic independence of a family of elements of an R algebra.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.RankAndCardinality
nodes.description: This file concerns the cardinality of a transcendence basis.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.TranscendenceBasis
nodes.description: This file defines the transcendence basis as a maximal algebraically independent subset.

nodes.label: RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.Transcendental
nodes.description: This file relates algebraic independence and transcendence (or algebraicity) of elements.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Artinian.Algebra
nodes.description: In this file we collect results about algebras over Artinian rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Artinian.Defs
nodes.description: A module satisfying these equivalent conditions is said to be an Artinian R-module if every decreasing chain of submodules is eventually constant, or equivalently, if the relation < on submodules is well founded.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Artinian.Instances
nodes.description: We show that every reduced Artinian ring and the polynomial ring over it are decomposition monoids, and every reduced Artinian ring is semisimple.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Artinian.Module
nodes.description: A module satisfying these equivalent conditions is said to be an Artinian R-module if every decreasing chain of submodules is eventually constant, or equivalently, if the relation < on submodules is well founded.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Artinian.Ring
nodes.description: A ring is said to be left (or right) Artinian if it is Artinian as a left (or right) module over itself, or simply Artinian if it is both left and right Artinian.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bezout
nodes.description: A Bézout ring (Bezout ring) is a ring whose finitely generated ideals are principal. Notable examples include principal ideal rings, valuation rings, and the ring of algebraic integers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define Bialgebras.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.Convolution
nodes.description: This file constructs the ring structure on algebra homs C → A where C is a bialgebra and A an algebra, and also the ring structure on bialgebra homs C → A where C and A are bialgebras. Both multiplications are given by diagrammatically, where μ stands for multiplication and δ for comultiplication.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.Equiv
nodes.description: This file defines bundled isomorphisms of R-bialgebras. We simply mimic the early parts of Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Equiv.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.GroupLike
nodes.description: This file proves that group-like elements in a bialgebra form a monoid.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.Hom
nodes.description: This file defines bundled homomorphisms of R-bialgebras. We simply mimic Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Hom.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.MonoidAlgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: The bialgebra structure on monoid algebras
nodes.description: Given a monoid M, a commutative semiring R and an R-bialgebra A, this file collects results about the R-bialgebra instance on A[M] inherited from the corresponding structure on its coefficients, building upon results in Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/MonoidAlgebra.lean about the coalgebra structure.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.SymmetricAlgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bialgebra structure on SymmetricAlgebra R M
nodes.description: SymmetricAlgebra R M is the cocommutative commutative R-bialgebra on M in which each generator ι x is primitive: Δ(ι x) = ι x ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ ι x and ε(ι x) = 0.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Bialgebra.TensorProduct
nodes.description: We define the data in the monoidal structure on the category of bialgebras - e.g. the bialgebra instance on a tensor product of bialgebras, and the tensor product of two BialgHoms as a BialgHom. This is done by combining the corresponding API for coalgebras and algebras.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Binomial
nodes.description: In this file we introduce the binomial property as a mixin, and define the multichoose and choose functions generalizing binomial coefficients.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ChainOfDivisors
nodes.description: The results in this file show that in the monoid Associates M of a UniqueFactorizationMonoid M, an element a is an n-th prime power iff its set of divisors is a strictly increasing chain of length n + 1, meaning that we can find a strictly increasing bijection between Fin (n + 1) and the set of factors of a.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ClassGroup
nodes.description: This file defines the ideal class group ClassGroup R of fractional ideals of R inside its field of fractions.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define Coalgebra, and provide instances for:

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.CoassocSimps
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tactic to reassociate comultiplication in a coalgebra
nodes.description: coassoc_simps is a simp set useful to prove tautologies on coalgebras.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.Convolution
nodes.descriptionTitle: Convolution product on linear maps from a coalgebra to an algebra
nodes.description: This file constructs the ring structure on linear maps C → A where C is a coalgebra and A an algebra, where multiplication is given by (f g)(x) = ∑ f x₍₁₎ g x₍₂₎ in Sweedler notation or diagrammatically, where μ stands for multiplication and δ for comultiplication.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.Equiv
nodes.description: This file defines bundled isomorphisms of R-coalgebras. We largely mirror the basic API of Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Defs.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.GroupLike
nodes.description: This file defines group-like elements in a coalgebra, i.e. elements a such that ε a = 1 and Δ a = a ⊗ₜ a.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.Hom
nodes.description: This file defines bundled homomorphisms of R-coalgebras. We largely mimic Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Hom.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.MonoidAlgebra
nodes.descriptionTitle: The coalgebra structure on monoid algebras
nodes.description: Given a type X, a commutative semiring R and a semiring A which is also an R-coalgebra, this file collects results about the R-coalgebra instance on A[X] inherited from the corresponding structure on its coefficients, defined in Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.MulOpposite
nodes.description: Suppose R is a commutative semiring, and A is an R-coalgebra, then Aᵐᵒᵖ is an R-coalgebra, where we define the comultiplication and counit maps naturally.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coalgebra.TensorProduct
nodes.description: Suppose S is an R-algebra. Given an S-coalgebra A and R-coalgebra B, we can define a natural comultiplication map Δ : A ⊗[R] B → (A ⊗[R] B) ⊗[S] (A ⊗[R] B) and counit map ε : A ⊗[R] B → S induced by the comultiplication and counit maps of A and B.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Complex
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about Algebra.trace and Algebra.norm on ℂ
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Complex.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Conductor
nodes.description: This file defines the conductor ideal of an element x of R-algebra S. This is the ideal of S consisting of all elements a such that for all b in S, the product a b lies in the R-subalgebra of S generated by x.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Congruence.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic results concerning congruence relations on rings, which extend Con and AddCon on monoids and additive monoids.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Congruence.BigOperators
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Congruence.BigOperators.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Congruence.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines congruence relations on rings, which extend Con and AddCon on monoids and additive monoids.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Congruence.Hom
nodes.description: This file contains elementary definitions involving congruence relations and morphisms for rings and semirings

nodes.label: RingTheory.Congruence.Opposite
nodes.description: This file defines the order isomorphism between the congruences on a ring R and the congruences on the opposite ring Rᵐᵒᵖ.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coprime.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Coprime elements of a ring or monoid
nodes.description: that a x + b y = 1. Note that elements with no common divisors (IsRelPrime) are not necessarily coprime, e.g., the multivariate polynomials x₁ and x₂ are not coprime. The two notions are equivalent in Bézout rings, see isRelPrime_iff_isCoprime.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coprime.Ideal
nodes.descriptionTitle: An additional lemma about coprime ideals
nodes.description: This lemma generalises exists_sum_eq_one_iff_pairwise_coprime to the case of non-principal ideals. It is on a separate file due to import requirements.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Coprime.Lemmas
nodes.descriptionTitle: Additional lemmas about elements of a ring satisfying IsCoprime
nodes.description: and elements of a monoid satisfying IsRelPrime

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.AdicValuation
nodes.description: Given a Dedekind domain R of Krull dimension 1 and a maximal ideal v of R, we define the v-adic valuation on R and its extension to the field of fractions K of R. We prove several properties of this valuation, including the existence of uniformizers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the notion of a Dedekind ring (domain), as a Noetherian integrally closed commutative ring (domain) of Krull dimension at most one.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Different
nodes.description: If L = K[x], with x integral over A, then 𝔣 𝔇 = (f'(x)) with f being the minimal polynomial of x. If L = K[x], with x integral over A, then f'(x) ∈ 𝔇 with f being the minimal polynomial of x. (in the sense of Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt).

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Dvr
nodes.description: This file defines an equivalent notion of a Dedekind domain (or Dedekind ring), namely a Noetherian integral domain where the localization at every nonzero prime ideal is a DVR.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Factorization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Factorization of ideals and fractional ideals of Dedekind domains
nodes.description: Every nonzero ideal I of a Dedekind domain R can be factored as a product ∏_v v^{n_v} over the maximal ideals of R, where the exponents n_v are natural numbers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.FiniteAdeleRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: The finite adèle ring of a Dedekind domain
nodes.description: We define the ring of finite adèles of a Dedekind domain R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.GaussLemma
nodes.description: This file contains Gauss's Lemma for Dedekind Domains, which states that the content ideal of a polynomial is the whole ring if and only if the v-adic Gauss norms of the polynomial are equal to 1 for all v.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Ideal.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we show a ring is a Dedekind domain iff all fractional ideals are invertible, and prove instances such as the unique factorization of ideals. Further results on the structure of ideals in a Dedekind domain are found in Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Lemmas.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Ideal.Lemmas
nodes.description: In this file, we prove some results on the unique factorization monoid structure of the ideals. The unique factorization of ideals and invertibility of fractional ideals can be found in Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Instances
nodes.description: This file contains various instances to work with localization of a ring extension.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.IntegralClosure
nodes.description: This file shows the integral closure of a Dedekind domain (in particular, the ring of integers of a number field) is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.LinearDisjoint
nodes.descriptionTitle: Disjoint extensions with coprime different ideals
nodes.description: Let A ⊆ B be a finite extension of Dedekind domains and assume that A ⊆ R₁, R₂ ⊆ B are two subrings such that Frac R₁ ⊔ Frac R₂ = Frac B, Frac R₁ and Frac R₂ are linearly disjoint over Frac A, and that 𝓓(R₁/A) and 𝓓(R₂/A) are coprime where 𝓓 denotes the different ideal and Frac R denotes the fraction field of a domain R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.PID
nodes.descriptionTitle: Criteria under which a Dedekind domain is a PID
nodes.description: This file contains some results that we can use to test whether all ideals in a Dedekind domain are principal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.SInteger
nodes.descriptionTitle: S-integers and S-units of fraction fields of Dedekind domains
nodes.description: Let K be the field of fractions of a Dedekind domain R, and let S be a set of prime ideals in the height one spectrum of R. An S-integer of K is defined to have v-adic valuation at most one for all primes ideals v away from S, whereas an S-unit of Kˣ is defined to have v-adic valuation exactly one for all prime ideals v away from S.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DedekindDomain.SelmerGroup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Selmer groups of fraction fields of Dedekind domains
nodes.description: Let $K$ be the field of fractions of a Dedekind domain $R$. For any set $S$ of prime ideals in the height one spectrum of $R$, and for any natural number $n$, the Selmer group $K(S, n)$ is defined to be the subgroup of the unit group $K^\times$ modulo $n$-th powers where each element has $v$-adic valuation divisible by $n$ for all prime ideals $v$ away from $S$.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Derivation.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines derivation. A derivation D from the R-algebra A to the A-module M is an R-linear map that satisfy the Leibniz rule D (a b) = a D b + D a b.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Derivation.DifferentialRing
nodes.description: This file defines derivations from a commutative ring to itself as a typeclass, which lets us use the x′ notation for the derivative of x.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Derivation.Lie

nodes.label: RingTheory.Derivation.MapCoeffs
nodes.description: In this file we define applying a derivation on the coefficients of a polynomial, show this forms a derivation, and prove apply_eval_eq, which shows that for a derivation D, D(p(x)) = (D.mapCoeffs p)(x) + D(x) p'(x). apply_aeval_eq and apply_aeval_eq' are generalizations of that for algebras. We also have a special case for DifferentialAlgebras.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Discriminant
nodes.descriptionTitle: Discriminant of a family of vectors
nodes.description: Given an A-algebra B and b, an ι-indexed family of elements of B, we define the discriminant of b as the determinant of the matrix whose (i j)-th element is the trace of b i b j.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowerAlgebra.Init
nodes.description: Let R be a (commutative) semiring and M be an R-module. In this file we define Γ_R(M), the universal divided power algebra of M, as the ring quotient of the polynomial ring in the variables ℕ × M by the relation DividedPowerAlgebra.Rel.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowers.Basic
nodes.description: Let A be a commutative (semi)ring and I be an ideal of A. A divided power structure on I is the datum of operations a n ↦ dpow a n satisfying relations that model the intuitive formula dpow n a = a ^ n / n ! and collected by the structure DividedPowers. The list of axioms is embedded in the structure: To avoid coercions, we rather consider DividedPowers.dpow : ℕ → A → A, extended by 0.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowers.DPMorphism
nodes.description: Let A and B be commutative (semi)rings, let I be an ideal of A and let J be an ideal of B. Given divided power structures on I and J, a ring morphism A →+ B is a divided power morphism if it is compatible with these divided power structures.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowers.Padic
nodes.description: Given a divided power algebra (B, J, δ) and an injective ring morphism f : A →+ B, if I is an A-ideal such that I.map f = J and such that for all n : ℕ, x ∈ I, the preimage of hJ.dpow n (f x) under f belongs to I, we get an induced divided power structure on I.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowers.RatAlgebra
nodes.description: In this file we show that, for certain choices of a commutative (semi)ring A and an ideal I of A, the family of maps ℕ → A → A given by fun n x ↦ x^n/n! is a divided power structure on I.

nodes.label: RingTheory.DividedPowers.SubDPIdeal
nodes.description: Let A be a commutative (semi)ring and let I be an ideal of A with a divided power structure hI. A subideal J of I is a sub-dp-ideal of (I, hI) if, for all n ∈ ℕ > 0 and all x ∈ J, hI.dpow n x ∈ J.
