nodes.label: RingTheory.Etale.Basic
nodes.description: An R-algebra A is formally etale if Ω[A⁄R] and H¹(L_{A/R}) both vanish. This is equivalent to the standard definition that "for every R-algebra B, every square-zero ideal I : Ideal B and f : A →ₐ[R] B ⧸ I, there exists exactly one lift A →ₐ[R] B". An R-algebra A is étale if it is formally étale and of finite presentation.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Etale.Locus
nodes.description: Let A be a R-algebra. D(f) is contained in the etale locus if and only if A_f is formally etale over R. The etale locus is the whole spectrum if and only if A is formally etale over R. If A is of finite type over R, then the etale locus is open.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Etale.Weakly

nodes.label: RingTheory.EuclideanDomain
nodes.description: Various about Euclidean domains are proved; all of them seem to be true more generally for principal ideal domains, so these lemmas should probably be reproved in more generality and this file perhaps removed?

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Basic
nodes.description: A hom between P and P' is a ring homomorphism that makes the two squares commute.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Cotangent.BaseChange

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Cotangent.Basic

nodes.description: 1. ι: The type of variables. 2. val : ι → S: The assignment of each variable to a value. 3. σ: A set-theoretic section of the induced R-algebra homomorphism R[X] → S, where we write R[X] for R[ι].

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Presentation.Basic
nodes.description: A presentation of an R-algebra S is a distinguished family of generators and relations.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Presentation.Core

We define a property HasCoeffs R₀ for a presentation P to mean the (sub)ring R₀ contains the coefficients of the relations of P. subring R₀ of R that contains the coefficients of the relations In this case there exists a model of S over R₀, i.e., there exists an R₀-algebra S₀ such that S is isomorphic to R ⊗[R₀] S₀.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Extension.Presentation.Submersive
nodes.description: In this file we define PreSubmersivePresentation. This is a presentation P that has fewer relations than generators. More precisely there exists an injective map from σ to ι. To such a presentation we may associate a Jacobian. P is then a submersive presentation, if its Jacobian is invertible.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FilteredAlgebra.Basic

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Basic
nodes.description: A module M over a commutative semiring R is mono-flat if for all monomorphisms of modules (i.e., injective linear maps) N →ₗ[R] P, the canonical map N ⊗ M → P ⊗ M is injective (cf. [Katsov2004], [KatsovNam2011]). To show a module is mono-flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated submodules N into finitely generated modules P, and P can be further assumed to lie in the same universe as R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.CategoryTheory
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tensoring with a flat module is an exact functor
nodes.description: In this file we prove that tensoring with a flat module is an exact functor.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Domain
nodes.description: We show that the tensor product of two injective linear maps is injective if the sources are flat and the ring is an integral domain.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Equalizer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Base change along flat modules preserves equalizers
nodes.description: We show that base change along flat modules (resp. algebras) preserves kernels and equalizers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.EquationalCriterion
nodes.description: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring $R$. Let us say that a relation $\sum_{i \in \iota} f_i x_i = 0$ in $M$ is trivial (Module.IsTrivialRelation) if there exist a finite index type $\kappa$ = Fin k, elements $(y_j)_{j \in \kappa}$ of $M$, and elements $(a_{ij})_{i \in \iota, j \in \kappa}$ of $R$ such that for all $i$, $$x_i = \sum_j a_{ij} y_j$$ and for all $j$, $$\sum_i f_i a_{ij} = 0.$$

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Algebra
nodes.description: An A-algebra B is faithfully flat if B is faithfully flat as an A-module. In this file we give equivalent characterizations of faithful flatness in the algebra case.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Basic
nodes.description: A module M over a commutative ring R is faithfully flat if it is flat and IM ≠ M whenever I is a maximal ideal of R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Descent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties satisfying faithfully flat descent for rings
nodes.description: We show the following properties of ring homomorphisms descend under faithfully flat ring maps:

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.IsBaseChange
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about IsBaseChange under exact sequences
nodes.description: In this file, we show that if S is a flat R-algebra, taking kernels commutes with base change of modules from R to S.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Localization
nodes.description: In this file we show that localizations are flat, and flatness is a local property.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Rank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results for the rank of a finite flat algebra
nodes.description: In this file we study a finite, flat R-algebra S and relate injectivity and bijectivity of R → S with the rank of S over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Stability
nodes.descriptionTitle: Flatness is stable under composition and base change
nodes.description: We show that flatness is stable under composition and base change.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.Tensor
nodes.description: M is flat if · ⊗ M preserves finite limits (equivalently, pullbacks, or equalizers). If R is a ring, an R-module M is flat if and only if it is mono-flat, and to show a module is flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated ideals into R. See .

nodes.label: RingTheory.Flat.TorsionFree
nodes.description: We show that flat implies torsion-free, and that they're the same concept for rings satisfying a certain property, including Dedekind domains and valuation rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FormalGroup.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Formal group laws over commutative ring
nodes.description: Let R be a commutative ring, a one dimensional formal group law is a formal power series F(X,Y) ∈ R⟦X,Y⟧ such that · F(X,Y) = X + Y + higher order terms. · F(F(X,Y),Z) = F(X,F(Y,Z)).

nodes.label: RingTheory.FractionalIdeal.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines fractional ideals of an integral domain and proves basic facts about them.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FractionalIdeal.Extended
nodes.description: This file defines the extension of a fractional ideal along a ring homomorphism.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FractionalIdeal.Inverse
nodes.description: This file defines the notation I⁻¹ where I is a not necessarily invertible fractional ideal. Note that this is somewhat misleading notation in case I is not invertible. The theorem that all nonzero fractional ideals are invertible in a Dedekind domain can be found in Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FractionalIdeal.Norm
nodes.description: This file defines the absolute ideal norm of a fractional ideal I : FractionalIdeal R⁰ K where K is a fraction field of R. The norm is defined by FractionalIdeal.absNorm I = Ideal.absNorm I.num / |Algebra.norm ℤ I.den| where I.num is an ideal of R and I.den an element of R⁰ such that I.den • I = I.num.

nodes.label: RingTheory.FractionalIdeal.Operations
nodes.description: Let K be the localization of R at R⁰ = R \ {0} (i.e. the field of fractions). the ideal quotient I / J (typically written $I : J$, but a : operator cannot be defined)

nodes.label: RingTheory.FreeCommRing
nodes.description: The theory of the free commutative ring generated by a type α. It is isomorphic to the polynomial ring over ℤ with variables in α

nodes.label: RingTheory.FreeRing
nodes.description: The theory of the free ring over a type.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Frobenius
nodes.description: In algebraic number theory, if L/K is a finite Galois extension of number fields, with rings of integers 𝓞L/𝓞K, and if q is prime ideal of 𝓞L lying over a prime ideal p of 𝓞K, then there exists a Frobenius element Frob p in Gal(L/K) with the property that Frob p x ≡ x ^ #(𝓞K/p) (mod q) for all x ∈ 𝓞L.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.AlgHom
nodes.description: This file defines bundled R-linear homomorphisms of graded R-algebras.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the typeclass GradedAlgebra 𝒜, for working with an algebra A that is internally graded by a collection of submodules 𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A. See the docstring of that typeclass for more information.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.FiniteType
nodes.description: We show that graded rings of finite type (over the 0-th component) are generated by homogeneous elements of positive degree.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Homogeneous.Ideal

nodes.description: This file defines homogeneous ideals of GradedRing 𝒜 where 𝒜 : ι → Submodule R A and operations on them.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Homogeneous.Maps
nodes.description: In this file we define HomogeneousIdeal.map and HomogeneousIdeal.comap.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Homogeneous.Submodule

nodes.description: This file defines homogeneous submodule of a graded module ⨁ᵢ ℳᵢ over graded ring ⨁ᵢ 𝒜ᵢ and operations on them.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Homogeneous.Subsemiring
nodes.descriptionTitle: Homogeneous subsemirings of a graded semiring
nodes.description: This file defines homogeneous subsemirings of a graded semiring, as well as operations on them.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.HomogeneousLocalization
nodes.description: This file constructs the subring of Aₓ where the numerator and denominator have the same grading, i.e. {a/b ∈ Aₓ | ∃ (i : ι), a ∈ 𝒜ᵢ ∧ b ∈ 𝒜ᵢ}.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Noetherian

nodes.description: This file proves that the 0-th grade of a Noetherian ring is also a Noetherian ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.Radical
nodes.description: This file contains a proof that the radical of any homogeneous ideal is a homogeneous ideal

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.RingHom
nodes.description: This file defines bundled homomorphisms of graded (semi)rings. We use the same structure GradedRingHom 𝒜 ℬ, a.k.a. 𝒜 →+ᵍ ℬ, for both types of homomorphisms.

nodes.label: RingTheory.GradedAlgebra.TensorProduct
nodes.description: In this file we show that if 𝒜 is a graded R-algebra, and S is any R-algebra, then S ⊗[R] 𝒜 is a graded S-algebra with the grading fun i ↦ (𝒜 i).baseChange S.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Grassmannian

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Addition
nodes.description: If Γ is ordered and R has zero, then R⟦Γ⟧ consists of formal series over Γ with coefficients in R, whose supports are partially well-ordered. With further structure on R and Γ, we can add further structure on R⟦Γ⟧. When R has an addition operation, R⟦Γ⟧ also has addition by adding coefficients.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Basic
nodes.description: If Γ is ordered and R has zero, then the type HahnSeries Γ R, which we denote as R⟦Γ⟧, consists of formal series over Γ with coefficients in R, whose supports are partially well-ordered. With further structure on R and Γ, we can add further structure on R⟦Γ⟧, with the most studied case being when Γ is a linearly ordered abelian group and R is a field, in which case R⟦Γ⟧ is a valued field, with value group Γ.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Binomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Binomial expansions of powers of Hahn Series
nodes.description: We introduce binomial expansions using embDomain.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Cardinal
nodes.description: We define HahnSeries.cardSupp as the cardinality of the support of a Hahn series, and find bounds for the cardinalities of different operations. We also build the subgroups, subrings, etc. of Hahn series bounded by a given infinite cardinal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.HEval
nodes.descriptionTitle: Evaluation of power series in Hahn Series
nodes.description: We describe a class of ring homomorphisms from formal power series to Hahn series, given by substitution of the generating variable to an element of strictly positive order.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.HahnEmbedding
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the Hahn embedding theorem: every linearly ordered abelian group can be embedded as an ordered subgroup of Lex ℝ⟦Ω⟧, where Ω is the type of finite Archimedean classes of the group. The theorem is stated as hahnEmbedding_isOrderedAddMonoid.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Lex
nodes.description: In this file, we define lexicographical ordered Lex R⟦Γ⟧, and show this is a LinearOrder when Γ and R themselves are linearly ordered. Additionally, it is an ordered group or ring whenever R is.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Multiplication
nodes.description: If Γ is ordered and R has zero, then R⟦Γ⟧ consists of formal series over Γ with coefficients in R, whose supports are partially well-ordered. This module introduces multiplication and scalar multiplication on Hahn series. If Γ is an ordered cancellative commutative additive monoid and R is a semiring, then we get a semiring structure on R⟦Γ⟧.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.PowerSeries
nodes.descriptionTitle: Comparison between Hahn series and power series
nodes.description: If Γ is ordered and R has zero, then R⟦Γ⟧ consists of formal series over Γ with coefficients in R, whose supports are partially well-ordered. With further structure on R and Γ, we can add further structure on R⟦Γ⟧. When R is a semiring and Γ = ℕ, then we get the more familiar semiring of formal power series with coefficients in R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Summable
nodes.description: We introduce a notion of formal summability for families of Hahn series, and define a formal sum function. This theory is applied to characterize invertible Hahn series whose coefficients are in a commutative domain.

nodes.label: RingTheory.HahnSeries.Valuation
nodes.description: If Γ is a LinearOrderedCancelAddCommMonoid and R is a domain, then the domain R⟦Γ⟧ admits an additive valuation given by orderTop.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Henselian
nodes.description: In this file we set up the basic theory of Henselian (local) rings. A ring R is Henselian at an ideal I if the following conditions hold: there exists a lift a : R of a₀ that is a root of f.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Ideal.Cotangent
nodes.description: In this file, we provide special API support for the module I ⧸ I ^ 2. The official definition is a quotient module of I, but the alternative definition as an ideal of R ⧸ I ^ 2 is also given, and the two are R-equivalent as in Ideal.cotangentEquivIdeal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Ideal.CotangentBaseChange
nodes.description: Given an R-algebra S, an ideal I of S and a flat R-algebra T, we show that the base change T ⊗[R] I/I² of the cotangent space of I is naturally isomorphic to the cotangent space of the extended ideal I · (T ⊗[R] S).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Ideal.GoingDown
nodes.description: In this file we define a predicate Algebra.HasGoingDown: An R-algebra S satisfies Algebra.HasGoingDown R S if for every pair of prime ideals p ≤ q of R with Q a prime of S lying above q, there exists a prime P ≤ Q of S lying above p.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Ideal.Pure

nodes.label: RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IntegrallyClosed
nodes.description: An integrally closed ring R contains all the elements of Frac(R) that are integral over R. A special case of integrally closed rings are the Dedekind domains.

nodes.label: RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IsIntegral.AlmostIntegral

nodes.label: RingTheory.Localization.Defs
nodes.description: We characterize the localization of a commutative ring R at a submonoid M up to isomorphism; that is, a commutative ring S is the localization of R at M iff we can find a ring homomorphism f : R →+ S satisfying 3 properties: 1. For all y ∈ M, f y is a unit; 2. For all z : S, there exists (x, y) : R × M such that z f y = f x; 3. For all x, y : R such that f x = f y, there exists c ∈ M such that x c = y c. (The converse is a consequence of 1.)

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.Basic
nodes.description: The following are equivalent for a module M over a ring R: 1. Every increasing chain of submodules M₁ ⊆ M₂ ⊆ M₃ ⊆ ⋯ eventually stabilises. 2. Every submodule is finitely generated.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.Defs
nodes.description: The following are equivalent for a module M over a ring R: 1. Every increasing chain of submodules M₁ ⊆ M₂ ⊆ M₃ ⊆ ⋯ eventually stabilises. 2. Every submodule is finitely generated.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.Filter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Noetherian modules and finiteness of chains
nodes.description: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.Nilpotent
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Noetherian.Nilpotent.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.OfPrime
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Noetherian.OfPrime.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.Orzech
nodes.descriptionTitle: Noetherian rings have the Orzech property
nodes.description: (not necessarily commutative), M is Noetherian, i : N →ₗ[R] M is injective, f : N →ₗ[R] M is surjective, then f is also injective.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Noetherian.UniqueFactorizationDomain
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Noetherian.UniqueFactorizationDomain.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NonUnitalSubring.Basic
nodes.description: Let R be a non-unital ring. We prove that non-unital subrings are a complete lattice, and that you can map (pushforward) and comap (pull back) them along ring homomorphisms.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NonUnitalSubring.Defs
nodes.description: Let R be a non-unital ring. This file defines the "bundled" non-unital subring type NonUnitalSubring R, a type whose terms correspond to non-unital subrings of R. This is the preferred way to talk about non-unital subrings in mathlib.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NonUnitalSubsemiring.Basic
nodes.description: We define the CompleteLattice structure, and non-unital subsemiring map, comap and range (srange) of a NonUnitalRingHom etc.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NonUnitalSubsemiring.Defs
nodes.description: We define bundled non-unital subsemirings and some standard constructions: subtype and inclusion ring homomorphisms.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Norm.Basic
nodes.description: Suppose we have an R-algebra S with a finite basis. For each s : S, the determinant of the linear map given by multiplying by s gives information about the roots of the minimal polynomial of s over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Norm.Defs
nodes.description: Suppose we have an R-algebra S with a finite basis. For each s : S, the determinant of the linear map given by multiplying by s gives information about the roots of the minimal polynomial of s over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Norm.Transitivity
nodes.description: Suppose we have an R-algebra S with a finite basis. For each s : S, the determinant of the linear map given by multiplying by s gives information about the roots of the minimal polynomial of s over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NormTrace
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.NormTrace.

nodes.label: RingTheory.NormalClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Normal closure of an extension of domains
nodes.description: We define the normal closure of an extension of domains R ⊆ S as a domain T such that R ⊆ S ⊆ T and the extension Frac T / Frac R is Galois, and prove several instances about it.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Nullstellensatz
nodes.description: This file establishes a version of Hilbert's classical Nullstellensatz for MvPolynomials. The main statement of the theorem is MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal_zeroLocus_eq_radical.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OrderOfVanishing.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines the order of vanishing of an element of a ring as the length of the quotient of the ring by the ideal generated by that element. We also define the extension of this notion to the field of fractions

nodes.label: RingTheory.OrderOfVanishing.Noetherian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Order of vanishing in Noetherian rings.
nodes.description: In this file we define various properties of the order of vanishing in Noetherian rings, including some API for computing the order of vanishing in discrete valuation rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OreLocalization.Basic
nodes.description: This file proves results on the localization of rings (monoids with zeros) over a left Ore set.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OreLocalization.Cardinality
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cardinality of Ore localizations of rings
nodes.description: This file contains some results on cardinality of Ore localizations of rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OreLocalization.NonZeroDivisors
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ore Localization over nonZeroDivisors in monoids with zeros.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.OreLocalization.NonZeroDivisors.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OreLocalization.OreSet
nodes.description: This file contains results on left Ore sets for rings and monoids with zero.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OreLocalization.Ring
nodes.descriptionTitle: Module and Ring instances of Ore Localizations
nodes.description: The Monoid and DistribMulAction instances and additive versions are provided in Mathlib/RingTheory/OreLocalization/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.OrzechProperty
nodes.description: In this file we define the following property of rings:

nodes.label: RingTheory.Perfection
nodes.description: In this file we define the perfection of a ring of characteristic p, and the tilt of a field given a valuation to ℝ≥0.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Perfectoid.BDeRham
nodes.descriptionTitle: The de Rham Period Ring $\mathbb{B}_{dR}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{dR}$
nodes.description: In this file, we define the de Rham period ring $\mathbb{B}_{dR}^+$ and the de Rham ring $\mathbb{B}_{dR}$. We define a generalized version of these period rings following Scholze. When R is the ring of integers of ℂₚ (PadicComplexInt), they coincide with the classical de Rham period rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Perfectoid.FontaineTheta
nodes.description: In this file, we define Fontaine's θ map, which is a ring homomorphism from the Witt vector 𝕎 R♭ of the tilt of a perfectoid ring R to R itself. Our definition of θ does not require that R is perfectoid in the first place. We only need R to be p-adically complete.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Perfectoid.Untilt
nodes.description: In this file, we define the untilt function from the pretilt of a p-adically complete ring to the ring itself. Note that this is not the untilt functor.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PiTensorProduct
nodes.descriptionTitle: Tensor product of R-algebras and rings
nodes.description: If (Aᵢ) is a family of R-algebras then the R-tensor product ⨂ᵢ Aᵢ is an R-algebra as well with structure map defined by r ↦ r • 1.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PicardGroup
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Picard group of a commutative ring
nodes.description: This file defines the Picard group CommRing.Pic R of a commutative ring R as the type of invertible R-modules (in the sense that M is invertible if there exists another R-module N such that M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R) up to isomorphism, equipped with tensor product as multiplication.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Basic
nodes.description: If a ring is an integral domain, then so is its polynomial ring over finitely many variables. Hilbert basis theorem, that if a ring is Noetherian then so is its polynomial ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Bernstein
nodes.description: The definition of the Bernstein polynomials and the fact that for ν : Fin (n+1) these are linearly independent over ℚ.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Chebyshev
nodes.description: The Chebyshev polynomials are families of polynomials indexed by ℤ, with integral coefficients.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Content
nodes.description: Definitions and basic results about polynomials over GCD domains, particularly their contents and primitive polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.ContentIdeal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The content ideal of a polynomial
nodes.description: In this file we introduce the content ideal of a polynomial p : R[X] as the ideal generated by its coefficients, and we prove some basic properties about it.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Cyclotomic.Basic
nodes.description: For n : ℕ and an integral domain R, we define a modified version of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial with coefficients in R, denoted cyclotomic' n R, as ∏ (X - μ), where μ varies over the primitive nth roots of unity. If there is a primitive nth root of unity in R then this is the standard definition. We then define the standard cyclotomic polynomial cyclotomic n R with coefficients in any ring R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Cyclotomic.Eval
nodes.description: This file states some results about evaluating cyclotomic polynomials in various different ways.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Cyclotomic.Expand
nodes.description: We gather results relating cyclotomic polynomials and expand.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Cyclotomic.Factorization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Factorization of cyclotomic polynomials over finite fields
nodes.description: We compute the degree of the irreducible factors of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial over a finite field of characteristic p, where p and n are coprime.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Cyclotomic.Roots
nodes.description: We gather results about roots of cyclotomic polynomials. In particular we show in Polynomial.cyclotomic_eq_minpoly that cyclotomic n R is the minimal polynomial of a primitive root of unity.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.DegreeLT
nodes.descriptionTitle: Polynomials with degree strictly less than n
nodes.description: This file contains the properties of the submodule of polynomials of degree less than n in a (semi)ring R, denoted R[X]_n.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Dickson
nodes.description: The (generalised) Dickson polynomials are a family of polynomials indexed by ℕ × ℕ, with coefficients in a commutative ring R depending on an element a∈R. More precisely, the they satisfy the recursion dickson k a (n + 2) = X (dickson k a n + 1) - a (dickson k a n) with starting values dickson k a 0 = 3 - k and dickson k a 1 = X. In the literature, dickson k a n is called the n-th Dickson polynomial of the k-th kind associated to the parameter a : R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.Basic
nodes.description: Given an ideal 𝓟 of a commutative semiring R, we say that a polynomial f : R[X] is Eisenstein at 𝓟 if f.leadingCoeff ∉ 𝓟, ∀ n, n < f.natDegree → f.coeff n ∈ 𝓟 and f.coeff 0 ∉ 𝓟 ^ 2. In this file we gather miscellaneous results about Eisenstein polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.Criterion
nodes.description: Let R be an integral domain and let K an R-algebra which is a field Let q : R[X] be a monic polynomial which is prime in K[X]. Let f : R[X] be a polynomial of strictly positive degree satisfying the following properties:

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.Distinguished
nodes.description: In this file we define the predicate Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt and develop the most basic lemmas about it.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.IsIntegral
nodes.description: In this file we gather more miscellaneous results about Eisenstein polynomials

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.GaussLemma
nodes.description: Gauss's Lemma is one of a few results pertaining to irreducibility of primitive polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.GaussNorm
nodes.description: This file defines the Gauss norm for polynomials. Given a polynomial p in R[X], a function v : R → ℝ and a real number c, the Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of the set of all values of v (p.coeff i) c ^ i for all i in the support of p.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Hermite.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines Polynomial.hermite n, the nth probabilists' Hermite polynomial.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Hermite.Gaussian
nodes.description: This file shows that the Hermite polynomial hermite n is (up to sign) the polynomial factor occurring in the nth derivative of a Gaussian.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.HilbertPoly
nodes.description: In this file, we formalise the following statement: if F is a field with characteristic 0, then given any p : F[X] and d : ℕ, there exists some h : F[X] such that for any large enough n : ℕ, h(n) is equal to the coefficient of Xⁿ in the power series expansion of p/(1 - X)ᵈ. This h is unique and is denoted as Polynomial.hilbertPoly p d.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Ideal
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Polynomial.Ideal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.IntegralNormalization
nodes.description: We define integralNormalization, which relate arbitrary polynomials to monic ones.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.IrreducibleRing
nodes.description: This file contains results about the polynomials over an irreducible ring (i.e. a ring with only one minimal prime ideal, equivalently, whose spectrum is an irreducible topological space).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.IsIntegral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results about coefficients of polynomials being integral
nodes.description: with integral coefficients, then the coefficients of p are themselves integral. p : S[X] is integral over R[X] iff the coefficients of p are integral over R. MvPolynomial σ R iff the coefficients of p are integral over R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Morse
nodes.description: This file proves that Morse polynomials have Galois group S_n. A Morse polynomial is a polynomial whose roots have at most one collision modulo each maximal ideal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Nilpotent
nodes.description: This file is a place for results related to nilpotency in (single-variable) polynomial rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Opposites
nodes.description: This file contains the basic API for "pushing through" the isomorphism opRingEquiv : R[X]ᵐᵒᵖ ≃+ Rᵐᵒᵖ[X]. It allows going back and forth between a polynomial ring over a semiring and the polynomial ring over the opposite semiring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Pochhammer
nodes.description: We define and prove some basic relations about ascPochhammer S n : S[X] := X (X + 1) ... (X + n - 1) which is also known as the rising factorial and about descPochhammer R n : R[X] := X (X - 1) ... (X - n + 1) which is also known as the falling factorial. Versions of this definition that are focused on Nat can be found in Data.Nat.Factorial as Nat.ascFactorial and Nat.descFactorial.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Quotient
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Polynomial.Quotient.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Radical
nodes.description: This file proves some theorems on radical and divRadical of polynomials. See Mathlib.RingTheory.Radical.Basic for the definition of radical and divRadical.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.RationalRoot
nodes.descriptionTitle: Rational root theorem and integral root theorem
nodes.description: This file contains the rational root theorem and integral root theorem. The rational root theorem (num_dvd_of_is_root and den_dvd_of_is_root) for a unique factorization domain A with localization S, states that the roots of p : A[X] in A's field of fractions are of the form x / y with x y : A, x ∣ p.coeff 0 and y ∣ p.leadingCoeff. The corollary is the integral root theorem isInteger_of_is_root_of_monic: if p is monic, its roots must be integers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Resultant.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains basic facts about resultant of two polynomials over commutative rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.ScaleRoots
nodes.descriptionTitle: Scaling the roots of a polynomial
nodes.description: This file defines scaleRoots p s for a polynomial p in one variable and a ring element s to be the polynomial with root r s for each root r of p and proves some basic results about it.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Selmer
nodes.description: This file proves irreducibility of the Selmer polynomials X ^ n - X - 1.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.SeparableDegree
nodes.description: This file contains basics about the separable degree of a polynomial.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.ShiftedLegendre
nodes.description: In this file, we define the shifted Legendre polynomials shiftedLegendre n for n : ℕ as a polynomial in ℤ[X]. We prove some basic properties of the Legendre polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.SmallDegreeVieta
nodes.descriptionTitle: Vieta's Formula for polynomial of small degrees.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Polynomial.SmallDegreeVieta.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Subring
nodes.description: Given a ring K with a subring R, we construct a map from polynomials in K[X] with coefficients in R to R[X]. We provide several lemmas to deal with coefficients, degree, and evaluation of Polynomial.toSubring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Tower
nodes.description: This file proves some basic results about the algebra tower structure for the type R[X].

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.UniqueFactorization
nodes.descriptionTitle: Unique factorization for univariate and multivariate polynomials
nodes.description: If an integral domain is a WFDvdMonoid, then so is its polynomial ring. If an integral domain is a UniqueFactorizationMonoid, then so is its polynomial ring (of any number of variables).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing
nodes.description: Let R be a commutative ring and p : R[X] be monic of degree n and let n = m + k. We construct the universal ring of the following functors on R-Alg: Represented by R[X₁,...,Xₙ]. See MvPolynomial.mapEquivMonic. Represented by an R-algebra (Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing) that is finitely-presented as an R-module. See Polynomial.UniversalFactorizationRing.homEquiv. Represented by an etale R-algebra (Polynomial.UniversalCoprimeFactorizationRing). See Polynomial.UniversalCoprimeFactorizationRing.homEquiv.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Vieta
nodes.description: The main result is Multiset.prod_X_add_C_eq_sum_esymm, which shows that the product of linear terms X + λ with λ in a Multiset s is equal to a linear combination of the symmetric functions esymm s.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Polynomial.Wronskian
nodes.descriptionTitle: Wronskian of a pair of polynomial
nodes.description: This file defines Wronskian of a pair of polynomials, which is W(a, b) = ab' - a'b. We also prove basic properties of it.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PolynomialAlgebra
nodes.description: Given [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] we show A[X] ≃ₐ[R] (A ⊗[R] R[X]).

nodes.label: RingTheory.PolynomialLaw.Basic
nodes.description: Let M and N be a modules over a commutative ring R. A polynomial law f : PolynomialLaw R M N, with notation f : M →ₚₗₗ[R] N, is a “law” that assigns a natural map PolynomialLaw.toFun' f S : S ⊗[R] M → S ⊗[R] N for every R-algebra S.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerBasis
nodes.description: This file defines a structure PowerBasis R S, giving a basis of the R-algebra S as a finite list of powers 1, x, ..., x^n. For example, if x is algebraic over a ring/field, adjoining x gives a PowerBasis structure generated by x.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines (univariate) formal power series and develops the basic properties of these objects.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Binomial
nodes.description: We introduce formal power series of the form (1 + X) ^ r, where r is an element of a commutative binomial ring R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Catalan
nodes.description: We introduce the Catalan generating function as a formal power series over ℕ: catalanSeries = ∑_{n ≥ 0} catalan n X^n

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.CoeffMulMem
nodes.descriptionTitle: Some results on the coefficients of multiplication of two power series
nodes.description: PowerSeries.coeff_mul_mem_ideal_mul_ideal_of_coeff_mem_ideal': if for all i ≤ n (resp. for all i), the i-th coefficients of power series f and g are in ideals I and J, respectively, then for all i ≤ n (resp. for all i), the i-th coefficients of f g are in I J.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Derivative
nodes.description: In this file we define an operation derivative (formal differentiation) on the ring of formal power series in one variable (over an arbitrary commutative semiring).

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Evaluation
nodes.description: Power series in one indeterminate are the particular case of multivariate power series, for the Unit type of indeterminates. This file provides a simpler syntax.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Exp
nodes.description: This file defines the exponential power series exp A = ∑ Xⁿ/n! over ℚ-algebras and develops its key properties, including the fundamental differential equation (exp A)' = exp A, a uniqueness characterization, and the functional equation for multiplication.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Expand
nodes.description: Given a power series φ, one may replace every occurrence of X i by X i ^ n, for some nonzero natural number n. This operation is called PowerSeries.expand and it is an algebra homomorphism.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.GaussNorm
nodes.description: This file defines the Gauss norm for power series using the gaussNorm for multivariate power series. Given a power series f in R⟦X⟧, a function v : R → ℝ and a real number c, the Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of the set of all values of v (f.coeff i) c ^ i for all i : ℕ.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Ideal
nodes.description: We gather miscellaneous results about prime ideals in R⟦X⟧. More precisely, we prove that, given a prime ideal I of R⟦X⟧, if the ideal generated by the constant coefficients of the f ∈ I is generated by n elements, then I is generated by at most n + 1 elements (actually it is generated by n elements if X ∉ I and n + 1 elements otherwise). This implies immediately that R⟦X⟧ is noetherian if R is. The proof of eq_of_le_of_X_notMem_of_fg_of_isPrime is inspired by [zbMATH05171613].

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Inverse
nodes.description: If the constant coefficient of a formal (univariate) power series is invertible, then this formal power series is invertible. (See the discussion in Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Inverse.lean for the construction.)

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Log
nodes.description: This file defines the logarithmic power series log A = ∑ (-1)^(n+1)/n · Xⁿ over ℚ-algebras and establishes its key properties.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.NoZeroDivisors
nodes.descriptionTitle: Power series over rings with no zero divisors
nodes.description: This file proves, using the properties of orders of power series, that R⟦X⟧ is an integral domain when R is.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Order
nodes.descriptionTitle: Formal power series (in one variable) - Order
nodes.description: The PowerSeries.order of a formal power series φ is the multiplicity of the variable X in φ.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.PiTopology
nodes.description: Let R be with Semiring R and TopologicalSpace R In this file we define the topology on PowerSeries σ R that corresponds to the simple convergence on its coefficients. It is the coarsest topology for which all coefficients maps are continuous.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Restricted
nodes.description: IsRestricted : We say a power series over a normed ring R is restricted for a parameter c if ‖coeff R i f‖ c ^ i → 0.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Schroder
nodes.description: This file defines lemmas and theorems about the power series for large and small Schröder numbers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Substitution
nodes.description: A (possibly multivariate) power series can be substituted into a (univariate) power series if and only if its constant coefficient is nilpotent.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.Trunc
nodes.descriptionTitle: Formal power series in one variable - Truncation
nodes.description: PowerSeries.trunc n φ truncates a (univariate) formal power series to the polynomial that has the same coefficients as φ, for all m < n, and 0 otherwise.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.WeierstrassPreparation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Weierstrass preparation theorem for power series over a complete local ring
nodes.description: In this file we define Weierstrass division, Weierstrass factorization, and prove Weierstrass preparation theorem.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PowerSeries.WellKnown
nodes.description: In this file we define the following power series:

nodes.label: RingTheory.Prime
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about prime elements of commutative rings.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PrincipalIdealDomain
nodes.descriptionTitle: Principal ideal rings, principal ideal domains, and Bézout rings
nodes.description: A principal ideal ring (PIR) is a ring in which all left ideals are principal. A principal ideal domain (PID) is an integral domain which is a principal ideal ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.PrincipalIdealDomainOfPrime
nodes.descriptionTitle: Principal ideal domains and prime ideals
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.PrincipalIdealDomainOfPrime.

nodes.label: RingTheory.QuasiFinite.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define the notion of quasi-finite algebras and prove basic properties about them

nodes.label: RingTheory.QuasiFinite.Polynomial
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.QuasiFinite.Polynomial.

nodes.label: RingTheory.QuasiFinite.Weakly
nodes.description: The definition Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt is equivalent to the usual definition "isolated in fibers" mathematically for algebras of finite type, but this requires Zariski's main theorem to prove. Hence we introduce a weaker notion of being Algebra.WeaklyQuasiFiniteAt that we shall state Zariski's main theorem in terms of, and deduce from this that Algebra.WeaklyQuasiFiniteAt is equivalent to Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt under all relevant scenarios.

nodes.label: RingTheory.QuotSMulTop
nodes.descriptionTitle: Reducing a module modulo an element of the ring
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring R and an element r : R, the association M ↦ M ⧸ rM extends to a functor on the category of R-modules. This functor is isomorphic to the functor of tensoring by R ⧸ (r) on either side, but can be more convenient to work with since we can work with quotient types instead of fiddling with simple tensors.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Radical
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in RingTheory.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Radical.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Radical of an element of a unique factorization normalization monoid
nodes.description: This file defines the radical of an element a in a unique factorization normalization monoid as the product of normalized prime factors of a without duplication. This is different from the radical of an ideal.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Radical.NatInt
nodes.descriptionTitle: The radical in ℕ and ℤ
nodes.description: are the same as the prime factors defined in Nat.primeFactors.

nodes.label: RingTheory.RamificationInertia.Inertia
nodes.description: Given a prime ideal q of an R-algebra S, the inertia degree of q over R is defined to be the degree of the residue field of q over the residue field of its preimage p in R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.RamificationInertia.Ramification
nodes.description: Let S/R be an extension of rings, and let q be a prime ideal of S lying over a prime ideal p of R. Let Sq be the localization of S and q, and let pSq be the image of p in Sq. Then the ramification index of q over R is defined to be the length of the quotient Sq/pSq as an Sq-module.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ReesAlgebra
nodes.description: The Rees algebra of an ideal I is the subalgebra R[It] of R[t] defined as R[It] = ⨁ₙ Iⁿ tⁿ. This is used to prove the Artin-Rees lemma, and will potentially enable us to calculate some blowup in the future.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Regular.Category
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Regular.Category.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Regular.Depth
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in RingTheory.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Regular.Flat
nodes.descriptionTitle: RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular is stable under flat base change
nodes.description: M be an R-module, S be a flat R-algebra, N be the base change of M to S. If [r₁, …, rₙ] is a weakly regular M-sequence, then its image in N is a weakly regular N-sequence.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Regular.IsSMulRegular
nodes.description: For modules over a ring the proposition IsSMulRegular r M is equivalent to r being a non-zero-divisor, i.e. r • x = 0 only if x = 0 for x ∈ M. This specific result is isSMulRegular_iff_smul_eq_zero_imp_eq_zero. Lots of results starting from this, especially ones about quotients (which don't make sense without some algebraic assumptions), are in this file. We don't pollute the Mathlib/Algebra/Regular/SMul.lean file with these because it's supposed to import a minimal amount of the algebraic hierarchy.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Regular.LinearMap

nodes.description: Let R be a local ring, A be a local R-algebra essentially of finite type. Then A/R is unramified if and only if κA/κR is separable, and m_R S = m_S. Let A be an essentially of finite type R-algebra, q be a prime over p. Then A is unramified at p if and only if κ(q)/κ(p) is separable, and pS_q = qS_q.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Unramified.LocalStructure
nodes.description: In this file, we will prove that if S is a finite type R-algebra unramified at Q, then there exists f ∉ Q and a standard etale algebra A over R that surjects onto S[1/f]. Geometrically, this says that unramified morphisms locally are closed subsets of etale covers.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Unramified.Locus
nodes.description: D(f) is contained in the unramified locus if and only if A_f is unramified over R. The unramified locus is the whole spectrum if and only if A is unramified over R. If A is (essentially) of finite type over R, then the unramified locus is open.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Unramified.Pi
nodes.descriptionTitle: Formal-unramification of finite products of rings
nodes.description: if and only if each A i is R-formally-smooth.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.AlgebraInstances
nodes.description: This file contains several Algebra and IsScalarTower instances related to extensions of a field with a valuation, as well as their unit balls.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Archimedean
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ring of integers under a given valuation in a multiplicatively archimedean codomain
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Valuation.Archimedean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Basic
nodes.description: The basic theory of valuations (non-archimedean norms) on a commutative ring, following T. Wedhorn's unpublished notes “Adic Spaces” ([wedhorn_adic]).

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Discrete.Basic
nodes.description: Given a linearly ordered commutative group with zero Γ, a valuation v : A → Γ on a ring A is discrete, if there is an element γ : Γˣ that is < 1 and generated the range of v, implemented as MonoidWithZeroHom.valueGroup v. When Γ := ℤₘ₀ (defined in Multiplicative.termℤₘ₀), γ = ofAdd (-1) and the condition of being discrete is equivalent to asking that ofAdd (-1 : ℤ) belongs to the image, in turn equivalent to asking that 1 : ℤ belongs to the image of the corresponding additive valuation.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Discrete.RankOne
nodes.description: a discrete valuation in ℤᵐ⁰ that contains exp (-1) in its range is equal to exp (-1). a surjective discrete valuation in ℤᵐ⁰ is equal to exp (-1). between the ValueGroup₀ of a discrete valuation and ℤᵐ⁰.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.DiscreteValuativeRel
nodes.description: Discrete valuative relations have a maximal element less than one in the value group.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.ExtendToLocalization
nodes.description: We show that, given a valuation v taking values in a linearly ordered commutative group with zero Γ, and a submonoid S of v.supp.primeCompl, the valuation v can be naturally extended to the localization S⁻¹A.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Extension
nodes.description: In this file, we define the typeclass for valuation extensions and prove basic facts about the extension of valuations. Let A be an R algebra, equipped with valuations vA and vR respectively. Here, the extension of a valuation means that the pullback of valuation vA to R is equivalent to the valuation vR on R. We only require equivalence, not equality, of valuations here.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.FiniteField
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in RingTheory.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Integers
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ring of integers under a given valuation
nodes.description: The elements with valuation less than or equal to 1.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Integral
nodes.descriptionTitle: Integral elements over the ring of integers of a valuation
nodes.description: The ring of integers is integrally closed inside the original ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.IsTrivialOn
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic lemmas on valuations that are trivial over a base ring
nodes.description: This file contains additional results about Valuation.IsTrivialOn which is defined in Mathlib.RingTheory.Valuation.Basic.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.LocalSubring
nodes.descriptionTitle: Valuation subrings are exactly the maximal local subrings
nodes.description: See LocalSubring.isMax_iff. Note that the order on local subrings is not merely inclusion but domination.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Minpoly
nodes.description: We prove some results about valuations of zero coefficients of minimal polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.PrimeMultiplicity
nodes.descriptionTitle: multiplicity of a prime in an integral domain as an additive valuation
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.Valuation.PrimeMultiplicity.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.Quotient
nodes.descriptionTitle: The valuation on a quotient ring
nodes.description: The support of a valuation v : Valuation R Γ₀ is supp v. If J is an ideal of R with h : J ⊆ supp v then the induced valuation on R / J = Ideal.Quotient J is onQuot v h.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.RamificationGroup
nodes.description: The decomposition subgroup and inertia subgroups.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.RankOne
nodes.description: We define rank one valuations.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.ValuationRing
nodes.description: A valuation ring is a domain such that for every pair of elements a b, either a divides b or vice-versa.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.ValuationSubring
nodes.description: The order structure on ValuationSubring K.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.ValuativeRel.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we introduce a class called ValuativeRel R for a ring R. This bundles a relation vle : R → R → Prop on R which mimics a preorder on R arising from a valuation. We introduce the notation x ≤ᵥ y for this relation.

nodes.label: RingTheory.Valuation.ValuativeRel.Trivial
nodes.description: Trivial valuative relations relate all non-zero elements to each other. Equivalently, all elements are related to 1: the relation is equal to the relation induced by the trivial valuation which sends all non-zero elements to 1.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Basic
nodes.description: This file verifies that the ring operations on WittVector p R satisfy the axioms of a commutative ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Compare
nodes.descriptionTitle: Comparison isomorphism between WittVector p (ZMod p) and ℤ_[p]
nodes.description: We construct a ring isomorphism between WittVector p (ZMod p) and ℤ_[p]. This isomorphism follows from the fact that both satisfy the universal property of the inverse limit of ZMod (p^n).

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Complete
nodes.descriptionTitle: The ring of Witt vectors is p-torsion free and p-adically complete
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that the ring of Witt vectors 𝕎 k is p-torsion free and p-adically complete when k is a perfect ring of characteristic p.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define the type of p-typical Witt vectors and ring operations on it. The ring axioms are verified in Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.DiscreteValuationRing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Witt vectors over a perfect ring
nodes.description: This file establishes that Witt vectors over a perfect field are a discrete valuation ring. When k is a perfect ring, a nonzero a : 𝕎 k can be written as p^m b for some m : ℕ and b : 𝕎 k with nonzero 0th coefficient. When k is also a field, this b can be chosen to be a unit of 𝕎 k.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Domain
nodes.description: This file builds to the proof WittVector.instIsDomain, an instance that says if R is an integral domain, then so is 𝕎 R. It depends on the API around iterated applications of WittVector.verschiebung and WittVector.frobenius found in Identities.lean.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Frobenius
nodes.description: If R has characteristic p, then there is a ring endomorphism frobenius R p that raises r : R to the power p. By applying WittVector.map to frobenius R p, we obtain a ring endomorphism 𝕎 R →+ 𝕎 R. It turns out that this endomorphism can be described by polynomials over ℤ that do not depend on R or the fact that it has characteristic p. In this way, we obtain a Frobenius endomorphism WittVector.frobeniusFun : 𝕎 R → 𝕎 R for every commutative ring R.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.FrobeniusFractionField
nodes.descriptionTitle: Solving equations about the Frobenius map on the field of fractions of 𝕎 k
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to prove WittVector.exists_frobenius_solution_fractionRing, which says that for an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p and a, b in the field of fractions of Witt vectors over k, there is a solution b to the equation φ b a = p ^ m b, where φ is the Frobenius map.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Identities
nodes.descriptionTitle: Identities between operations on the ring of Witt vectors
nodes.description: In this file we derive common identities between the Frobenius and Verschiebung operators.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.InitTail
nodes.description: Given a Witt vector x, we are sometimes interested in its components before and after an index n. This file defines those operations, proves that init is polynomial, and shows how that polynomial interacts with MvPolynomial.bind₁.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.IsPoly
nodes.description: WittVector.IsPoly is a (type-valued) predicate on functions f : Π R, 𝕎 R → 𝕎 R. It asserts that there is a family of polynomials φ : ℕ → MvPolynomial ℕ ℤ, such that the nth coefficient of f x is equal to φ n evaluated on the coefficients of x. Many operations on Witt vectors satisfy this predicate (or an analogue for higher arity functions). We say that such a function f is a polynomial function.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Isocrystal
nodes.description: When k is an integral domain, so is 𝕎 k, and we can consider its field of fractions K(p, k). The endomorphism WittVector.frobenius lifts to φ : K(p, k) → K(p, k); if k is perfect, φ is an automorphism.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.MulCoeff
nodes.descriptionTitle: Leading terms of Witt vector multiplication
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to study the leading terms of the formula for the n+1st coefficient of a product of Witt vectors x and y over a ring of characteristic p. We aim to isolate the n+1st coefficients of x and y, and express the rest of the product in terms of a function of the lower coefficients.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.MulP
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multiplication by n in the ring of Witt vectors
nodes.description: In this file we show that multiplication by n in the ring of Witt vectors is a polynomial function. We then use this fact to show that the composition of Frobenius and Verschiebung is equal to multiplication by p.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.StructurePolynomial
nodes.description: In this file we prove the main theorem that makes the whole theory of Witt vectors work. Briefly, consider a polynomial Φ : MvPolynomial idx ℤ over the integers, with polynomials variables indexed by an arbitrary type idx.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Teichmuller
nodes.description: This file defines WittVector.teichmuller, a monoid hom R → 𝕎 R, which embeds r : R as the 0-th component of a Witt vector whose other coefficients are 0.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.TeichmullerSeries
nodes.description: Let R be a characteristic p perfect ring. In this file, we show that every element x of the Witt vectors 𝕎 R can be written as the (p-adic) summation of Teichmuller series, namely ∑ i, (teichmuller p (((frobeniusEquiv R p).symm ^ i) (x.coeff i)) p ^ i)

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Truncated
nodes.description: The ring of truncated Witt vectors (of length n) is a quotient of the ring of Witt vectors. It retains the first n coefficients of each Witt vector. In this file, we set up the basic quotient API for this ring.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.Verschiebung
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for RingTheory.WittVector.Verschiebung.

nodes.label: RingTheory.WittVector.WittPolynomial
nodes.description: To endow WittVector p R with a ring structure, we need to study the so-called Witt polynomials.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ZMod
nodes.description: We collect a few facts about ZMod n that need some ring theory to be proved/stated.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ZMod.Torsion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Torsion group of ZMod p for prime p
nodes.description: This file shows that the ZMod p has p - 1 roots-of-unity.

nodes.label: RingTheory.ZMod.UnitsCyclic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cyclicity of the units of ZMod n
nodes.description: ZMod.isCyclic_units_iff : (ZMod n)ˣ is cyclic iff one of the following mutually exclusive cases happens: (with 1 ≤ e).

nodes.label: RingTheory.ZariskisMainTheorem
nodes.description: The statement of Zariski's main theorem is the following: Given a finite type R-algebra S, and p a prime of S such that S is quasi-finite at R, then there exists a f ∉ p such that S[1/f] is isomorphic to R'[1/f] where R' is the integral closure of R in S.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Aleph
nodes.description: This file defines the ω, ℵ, and ℶ functions which enumerate certain kinds of ordinals and cardinals. Each is provided in two variants: the standard versions which only take infinite values, and "preliminary" versions which include finite values and are sometimes more convenient.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Arithmetic
nodes.description: Arithmetic operations on cardinals are defined in Mathlib/SetTheory/Cardinal/Order.lean. However, proving the important theorem c c = c for infinite cardinals and its corollaries requires the use of ordinal numbers. This is done within this file.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Basic
nodes.description: We provide a collection of basic results on cardinal numbers, in particular focusing on finite/countable/small types and sets.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Cofinality.Basic
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of the cofinality Order.cof α of an order. This is the smallest cardinality of a cofinal subset.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Cofinality.Club
nodes.description: A subset of a well-ordered type α is called a club set when it is closed in the order topology and cofinal. If α has no maximum, then an equivalent condition is that α is closed and unbounded; hence the name.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Cofinality.Enum
nodes.description: We define a typeclass IsRegularCardinalOrder for well-ordered types, whose order type equals (the initial ordinal of) their cofinality. This notion does not appear in the literature, but intends to generalize the properties of intervals Iio c.ord, wherever c is a regular cardinal. Other instances of this typeclass include ℕ, Ordinal, and Cardinal.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Cofinality.Ordinal
nodes.description: This file contains the definition of the cofinality Ordinal.cof o of an ordinal. This is the cofinality of the ordinal o when viewed as a linear order.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Continuum
nodes.description: In this file we define Cardinal.continuum (notation: 𝔠, localized in Cardinal) to be 2 ^ ℵ₀. We also prove some simp lemmas about cardinal arithmetic involving 𝔠.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.CountableCover
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cardinality of a set with a countable cover
nodes.description: Assume that a set t is eventually covered by a countable family of sets, all with cardinality ≤ a. Then t itself has cardinality at most a. This is proved in Cardinal.mk_subtype_le_of_countable_eventually_mem.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Defs
nodes.description: We define cardinal numbers as a quotient of types under the equivalence relation of equinumerosity (i.e., existence of a bijection).

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Divisibility
nodes.description: We show basic results about divisibility in the cardinal numbers. This relation can be characterised in the following simple way: if a and b are both less than ℵ₀, then a ∣ b iff they are divisible as natural numbers. If b is greater than ℵ₀, then a ∣ b iff a ≤ b. This furthermore shows that all infinite cardinals are prime; recall that a b = max a b if ℵ₀ ≤ a b; therefore a ∣ b c = a ∣ max b c and therefore clearly either a ∣ b or a ∣ c.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.ENat
nodes.description: In this file we define a coercion Cardinal.ofENat : ℕ∞ → Cardinal and a projection Cardinal.toENat : Cardinal →+o ℕ∞. We also prove basic theorems about these definitions.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Embedding
nodes.descriptionTitle: Existence of embeddings from finite types
nodes.description: Let s : Set α be a finite set.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Finite
nodes.description: If α is infinite, Nat.card α = 0. If α is infinite, ENat.card α = ⊤.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Finsupp
nodes.descriptionTitle: Results on the cardinality of finitely supported functions and multisets.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for SetTheory.Cardinal.Finsupp.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Free
nodes.description: This file shows that all the free constructions over α have cardinality max #α ℵ₀, and are thus infinite, and specifically countable over countable generators.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.HasCardinalLT
nodes.descriptionTitle: The property of being of cardinality less than a cardinal
nodes.description: Given X : Type u and κ : Cardinal.{v}, we introduce a predicate HasCardinalLT X κ expressing that Cardinal.lift.{v} (Cardinal.mk X) < Cardinal.lift κ.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.NatCount
nodes.description: This file provides lemmas about the relation of Nat.count with cardinality functions.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Order
nodes.description: We define the order on cardinal numbers and show its basic properties, including the ordered semiring structure.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Ordinal
nodes.description: This file collects results about the cardinality of different ordinal operations.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Pigeonhole
nodes.description: This file proves variants of the infinite pigeonhole principle.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Regular
nodes.description: This file defines regular, singular, and inaccessible cardinals.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.SchroederBernstein
nodes.description: This file proves the Schröder-Bernstein theorem (see schroeder_bernstein), the well-ordering of cardinals (see min_injective) and the totality of their order (see total).

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.Subfield
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cardinality of the division ring generated by a set
nodes.description: Subfield.cardinalMk_closure_le_max: the cardinality of the (sub-)division ring generated by a set is bounded by the cardinality of the set unless it is finite.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.ToNat
nodes.descriptionTitle: Projection from cardinal numbers to natural numbers
nodes.description: In this file we define Cardinal.toNat to be the natural projection Cardinal → ℕ, sending all infinite cardinals to zero. We also prove basic lemmas about this definition.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Cardinal.UnivLE
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for SetTheory.Cardinal.UnivLE.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Descriptive.Tree
nodes.descriptionTitle: Trees in the sense of descriptive set theory
nodes.description: This file defines trees of depth ω in the sense of descriptive set theory as sets of finite sequences that are stable under taking prefixes.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Lists
nodes.descriptionTitle: A computable model of ZFA without infinity
nodes.description: In this file we define finite hereditary lists. This is useful for calculations in naive set theory.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Arithmetic
nodes.description: Ordinals have an addition (corresponding to the disjoint union) that turns them into an additive monoid, and a multiplication (corresponding to the lexicographic order on the product) that turns them into a monoid. One can also define (truncated) subtraction and division operators.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Basic
nodes.description: Ordinals are defined as equivalences of well-ordered sets under order isomorphism. They are endowed with a total order, where an ordinal is smaller than another one if it embeds into it as an initial segment (or, equivalently, in any way). This total order is well founded.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.CantorNormalForm
nodes.description: The Cantor normal form of an ordinal is generally defined as its base ω expansion, with its non-zero exponents in decreasing order. Here, we more generally define a base b expansion Ordinal.CNF in this manner, which is well-behaved for any b ≥ 2.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Commute
nodes.description: Results on the commutativity of ordinal arithmetic operations.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Enum
nodes.descriptionTitle: Enumerating sets of ordinals by ordinals
nodes.description: The ordinals have the peculiar property that every subset bounded above is a small type, while themselves not being small. As a consequence of this, every unbounded subset of Ordinal is order isomorphic to Ordinal.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Exponential
nodes.description: In this file we define the power function and the logarithm function on ordinals. The two are related by the lemma Ordinal.opow_le_iff_le_log : b ^ c ≤ x ↔ c ≤ log b x for nontrivial inputs b, c.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Family
nodes.description: This file proves basic results about the suprema of families of ordinals.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.FixedPoint
nodes.description: We prove various statements about the fixed points of normal ordinal functions. We state them in two forms: as statements about indexed families of normal functions, and as statements about a single normal function.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.FixedPointApproximants
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ordinal Approximants for the Fixed points on complete lattices
nodes.description: This file sets up the ordinal-indexed approximation theory of fixed points of a monotone function in a complete lattice [Cousot1979]. The proof follows loosely the one from [Echenique2005].

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.FundamentalSequence
nodes.description: A fundamental sequence for a countable limit ordinal o is a strictly monotone function ℕ → Iio o with cofinal range. We can generalize this notion to arbitrary ordinals by setting the domain as Iio o.cof.card. Note that for a countable limit ordinal, one has o.cof.card = ω.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Notation
nodes.description: Constructive ordinal arithmetic for ordinals below ε₀.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Principal
nodes.description: If op is a binary operation on ordinals, we say that an ordinal o is op-principal (or op-indecomposable) whenever a < o and b < o imply op a b < o. Most commonly, one talks of additive and multiplicative principal ordinals.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Rank
nodes.description: For r a well-founded relation, IsWellFounded.rank r a is recursively defined as the least ordinal greater than the ranks of all elements below a.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Topology
nodes.description: We prove some miscellaneous results involving the order topology of ordinals.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Univ
nodes.description: Cardinal.univ is the cardinality of the cardinals themselves. Likewise, Ordinal.univ is the order type of the ordinals. These are related via Cardinal.univ.ord = Ordinal.univ and Ordinal.univ.card = Cardinal.univ.

nodes.label: SetTheory.Ordinal.Veblen
nodes.description: We define the two-arguments Veblen function, which satisfies veblen 0 a = ω ^ a and that for o ≠ 0, veblen o enumerates the common fixed points of veblen o' for o' < o.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we model Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory (+ choice) using Lean's underlying type theory, building on the pre-sets defined in Mathlib/SetTheory/ZFC/PSet.lean.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.Cardinal
nodes.description: In this file, we define the cardinalities of ZFC sets as ZFSet.{u} → Cardinal.{u}.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.Class
nodes.description: Classes in set theory are usually defined as collections of elements satisfying some property. Here, however, we define Class as Set ZFSet to derive many instances automatically, most of them being the lifting of set operations to classes. The usual definition is then definitionally equal to ours.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.Ordinal
nodes.description: This file works towards the development of von Neumann ordinals, i.e. transitive sets, well-ordered under ∈.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.PSet
nodes.description: A pre-set is inductively defined by its indexing type and its members, which are themselves pre-sets.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.Rank
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ordinal ranks of PSet and ZFSet
nodes.description: In this file, we define the ordinal ranks of PSet and ZFSet. These ranks are the same as IsWellFounded.rank over ∈, but are defined in a way that the universe levels of ranks are the same as the indexing types.

nodes.label: SetTheory.ZFC.VonNeumann
nodes.description: This file defines the von Neumann hierarchy of sets V_ o for ordinal o, which is recursively defined so that V_ a = ⋃ b < a, powerset (V_ b). This stratifies the universal class, in the sense that ⋃ o, V_ o = univ.

nodes.label: Tactic
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Tactic.

nodes.label: Tactic.Abel
nodes.description: Evaluate expressions in the language of additive, commutative monoids and groups.

nodes.label: Tactic.AdaptationNote
nodes.description: This file defines a #adaptation_note command. Adaptation notes are comments that are used to indicate that a piece of code has been changed to accommodate a change in Lean core. They typically require further action/maintenance to be taken in the future.

nodes.label: Tactic.Algebra.Basic
nodes.description: A suite of three tactics for solving equations in commutative algebras over commutative (semi)rings, where the exponents can also contain variables.

nodes.label: Tactic.Algebra.Lemmas
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Tactic.Algebra.Lemmas.

nodes.label: Tactic.Algebraize
nodes.description: This file defines the algebraize tactic. The basic functionality of this tactic is to automatically add Algebra instances given RingHoms. For example, algebraize [f, g] where f : A →+ B and g : B →+ C are RingHoms, will add the instances Algebra A B and Algebra B C corresponding to these RingHoms.

nodes.label: Tactic.ApplyAt
nodes.description: A tactic for applying functions at hypotheses.

nodes.label: Tactic.ApplyCongr
nodes.descriptionTitle: Introduce the apply_congr conv mode tactic.
nodes.description: apply_congr will apply congruence lemmas inside conv mode. It is particularly useful when the automatically generated congruence lemmas are not of the optimal shape. An example, described in the doc-string is rewriting inside the operand of a Finset.sum.

nodes.label: Tactic.ApplyFun
nodes.description: Apply a function to an equality or inequality in either a local hypothesis or the goal.

nodes.label: Tactic.ApplyWith
nodes.description: The applyWith tactic is like apply, but allows passing a custom configuration to the underlying apply operation.

nodes.label: Tactic.ArithMult
nodes.description: We define the arith_mult tactic using aesop

nodes.label: Tactic.ArithMult.Init
nodes.description: This module defines the IsMultiplicative Aesop rule set which is used by the arith_mult tactic. Aesop rule sets only become visible once the file in which they're declared is imported, so we must put this declaration into its own file.

nodes.label: Tactic.Attr.Core
nodes.description: In Lean 4, an attribute declared with register_simp_attr cannot be used in the same file. So, we declare all simp attributes used in Mathlib in Mathlib/Tactic/Attr/Register and tag lemmas from the core library and the Batteries library with these attributes in this file.

nodes.label: Tactic.Attr.Register
nodes.description: In this file we define all simp-like and label-like attributes used in Mathlib. We declare all of them in one file for two reasons:

nodes.label: Tactic.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Basic tactics and utilities for tactic writing
nodes.description: This file defines some basic utilities for tactic writing, and also and explicitly name the non-dependent hypotheses, context).

nodes.label: Tactic.Bound
nodes.description: bound is an aesop wrapper that proves inequalities by straightforward recursion on structure, assuming that intermediate terms are nonnegative or positive as needed. It also has some support for guessing where it is unclear where to recurse, such as which side of a min or max to use as the bound or whether to assume a power is less than or greater than one.

nodes.label: Tactic.Bound.Attribute
nodes.description: Any lemma tagged with @[bound] is registered as an apply rule for the bound tactic, by converting it to either norm apply or safe apply . The classification is based on the number and types of the lemma's hypotheses.

nodes.label: Tactic.Bound.Init
nodes.description: This module defines the Bound Aesop rule set which is used by the bound tactic. Aesop rule sets only become visible once the file in which they're declared is imported, so we must put this declaration into its own file.

nodes.label: Tactic.ByCases

nodes.label: Tactic.Linarith.Oracle.SimplexAlgorithm.SimplexAlgorithm

nodes.label: Tactic.Linarith.Parsing
nodes.descriptionTitle: Parsing input expressions into linear form
nodes.description: linarith computes the linear form of its input expressions, assuming (without justification) that the type of these expressions is a commutative semiring. It identifies atoms up to ring-equivalence: that is, (y3)x will be identified 3(xy), where the monomial xy is the linear atom.

nodes.label: Tactic.Linarith.Verification
nodes.description: linarith uses an untrusted oracle to produce a certificate of unsatisfiability. It needs to do some proof reconstruction work to turn this into a proof term. This file implements the reconstruction.

A Syntax.Tactic object can also be passed into the tactic, allowing the user to specify a normalization tactic.

nodes.label: Tactic.Module
nodes.descriptionTitle: A tactic for normalization over modules
nodes.description: This file provides the two tactics match_scalars and module. Given a goal which is an equality in a type M (with M an AddCommMonoid), the match_scalars tactic parses the LHS and RHS of the goal as linear combinations of M-atoms over some semiring R, and reduces the goal to the respective equalities of the R-coefficients of each atom. The module tactic does this and then runs the ring tactic on each of these coefficient-wise equalities, failing if this does not resolve them.

While in simple cases it might be possible to use congr_arg or congr_fun, congruence quotations are more general, since for example f could have implicit arguments, complicated dependent types, and subsingleton instance arguments such as Decidable or Fintype.

nodes.label: Tactic.Translate.TagUnfoldBoundary

nodes.description: This file defines a procedure for inserting casts into (proof) terms in order to make them well typed in a setting where certain constants aren't allowed to be unfolded.

nodes.label: Tactic.TryThis
nodes.description: This is a convenient shorthand intended for macro authors to be able to generate "Try this" recommendations. (It is not the main implementation of 'Try this', which is implemented in Lean core, see Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.)

nodes.label: Tactic.UnsetOption

For example, inputting set_option blah 7 and then unset_option blah returns the user to the default state before any set_option command is called. This is helpful when the user does not know the default value of the option or it is cleaner not to write it explicitly, or for some options where the default behaviour is different from any user set value.

nodes.label: Tactic.Use

nodes.label: Tactic.WLOG
nodes.description: The tactic wlog h : P will add an assumption h : P to the main goal, and add a new goal that requires showing that the case h : ¬ P can be reduced to the case where P holds (typically by symmetry). wlog! h : P is a variant that will also call push Not at h : ¬ P.
