nodes.description: We define basic notions of partially defined linear operators, which we call unbounded operators for short. In this file we prove all elementary properties of unbounded operators that do not assume that the underlying spaces are normed.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.LocallyConvex
nodes.description: A LocallyConvexSpace is a topological semimodule over an ordered semiring in which any point admits a neighborhood basis made of convex sets, or equivalently, in which convex neighborhoods of a point form a neighborhood basis at that point.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.ModuleTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: A "module topology" for modules over a topological ring
nodes.description: If R is a topological ring acting on an additive abelian group A, we define the module topology to be the finest topology on A making both the maps • : R × A → A and + : A × A → A continuous (with all the products having the product topology). Note that - : A → A is also automatically continuous as it is a ↦ (-1) • a.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Multilinear.Basic
nodes.description: We define continuous multilinear maps as maps from (i : ι) → M₁ i to M₂ which are multilinear and continuous, by extending the space of multilinear maps with a continuity assumption. Here, M₁ i and M₂ are modules over a ring R, and ι is an arbitrary type, and all these spaces are also topological spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Multilinear.Bounded
nodes.descriptionTitle: Images of (von Neumann) bounded sets under continuous multilinear maps
nodes.description: In this file we prove that continuous multilinear maps send von Neumann bounded sets to von Neumann bounded sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Multilinear.Topology
nodes.description: In this file we define TopologicalSpace and UniformSpace structures on ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 E F, where E i is a family of vector spaces over 𝕜 with topologies and F is a topological vector space.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.PerfectPairing
nodes.description: This file defines continuous perfect pairings.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.PerfectSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Vector spaces over nontrivially normed fields are perfect spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Module.PerfectSpace.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Simple
nodes.descriptionTitle: The kernel of a linear function is closed or dense
nodes.description: In this file we prove (LinearMap.isClosed_or_dense_ker) that the kernel of a linear function f : M →ₗ[R] N is either closed or dense in M provided that N is a simple module over R. This applies, e.g., to the case when R = N is a division ring.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.CharacterSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Character space of a topological algebra
nodes.description: The character space of a topological algebra is the subset of elements of the weak dual that are also algebra homomorphisms. This space is used in the Gelfand transform, which gives an isomorphism between a commutative C⋆-algebra and continuous functions on the character space of the algebra. This, in turn, is used to construct the continuous functional calculus on C⋆-algebras.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.CompactConvergenceCLM
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology of compact convergence on the space of continuous linear maps
nodes.description: In this file, we define a type alias CompactConvergenceCLM for E →L[𝕜] F, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.ContinuousLinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology of bounded convergence on the space of continuous linear map
nodes.description: In this file, we endow E →L[𝕜] F with the "topology of bounded convergence", or "topology of uniform convergence on bounded sets". This is declared as an instance.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.PointwiseConvergenceCLM
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology of pointwise convergence on continuous linear maps
nodes.description: topology on finite sets. as a continuous linear map. E →SLₚₜ[σ] F as a continuous linear map. This is the statement that bounded convergence is stronger than pointwise convergence. WeakDual 𝕜 E.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.UniformConvergenceCLM
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topologies of uniform convergence on the space of continuous linear maps
nodes.description: In this file, we define the "topology of 𝔖-convergence" on E →L[𝕜] F, where 𝔖 : Set (Set E). It is the topology of uniform convergence on the elements of 𝔖. Similarly to UniformOnFun, we define a type synonym UniformConvergenceCLM for E →L[𝕜] F endowed with this topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.WeakBilin
nodes.description: This file defines the weak topology given two vector spaces E and F over a commutative semiring 𝕜 and a bilinear form B : E →ₗ[𝕜] F →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜. The weak topology on E is the coarsest topology such that for all y : F every map fun x => B x y is continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Spaces.WeakDual
nodes.description: We continue in the setting of Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/WeakBilin.lean, which defines the weak topology given two vector spaces E and F over a commutative semiring 𝕜 and a bilinear form B : E →ₗ[𝕜] F →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜. The weak topology on E is the coarsest topology such that for all y : F every map fun x => B x y is continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.Star
nodes.descriptionTitle: The star operation, bundled as a continuous star-linear equiv
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Module.Star.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.StrongTopology
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.TopDualPairing
nodes.description: This file proves that topDualPairing 𝕜 E is a continuous perfect pairing when E is a finite-dimensional Hausdorff space over a complete nontrivially normed field.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.TransferInstance
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfer topological algebraic structures across Equivs
nodes.description: In this file, we construct a continuous linear equivalence α ≃L[R] β from an equivalence α ≃ β, where the continuous R-module structure on α is the one obtained by transporting an R-module structure on β back along e. We also specialize this construction to Shrink α.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Module.UniformConvergence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Algebraic facts about the topology of uniform convergence
nodes.description: This file contains algebraic compatibility results about the uniform structure of uniform convergence / 𝔖-convergence. They will mostly be useful for defining strong topologies on the space of continuous linear maps between two topological vector spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Monoid
nodes.description: In this file we define mixin classes ContinuousMul and ContinuousAdd. While in many applications the underlying type is a monoid (multiplicative or additive), we do not require this in the definitions.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Monoid.AddChar
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Monoid.AddChar.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Monoid.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define three mixin typeclasses:

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Monoid.FunOnFinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuity of the functoriality of X → M when X is finite
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Monoid.FunOnFinite.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.MulAction
nodes.description: In this file we define class ContinuousSMul. We say ContinuousSMul M X if M acts on X and the map (c, x) ↦ c • x is continuous on M × X. We reuse this class for topological (semi)modules, vector spaces and algebras.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.MvPolynomial
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following lemma:

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.NonUnitalAlgebra
nodes.description: A non-unital topological algebra over a topological semiring R is a topological (non-unital) semiring with a compatible continuous scalar multiplication by elements of R. We reuse typeclass ContinuousSMul to express the latter condition.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.NonUnitalStarAlgebra
nodes.description: A non-unital topological star algebra over a topological semiring R is a topological (non-unital) semiring with a compatible continuous scalar multiplication by elements of R and a continuous star operation. We reuse typeclasses ContinuousSMul and ContinuousStar to express the latter two conditions.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Nonarchimedean.AdicTopology
nodes.description: Given a commutative ring R and an ideal I in R, this file constructs the unique topology on R which is compatible with the ring structure and such that a set is a neighborhood of zero if and only if it contains a power of I. This topology is non-archimedean: every neighborhood of zero contains an open subgroup, namely a power of I.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Nonarchimedean.Bases
nodes.descriptionTitle: Neighborhood bases for non-archimedean rings and modules
nodes.description: This file contains special families of filter bases on rings and modules that give rise to non-archimedean topologies.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Nonarchimedean.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we set up the theory of nonarchimedean topological groups and rings.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Nonarchimedean.Completion
nodes.descriptionTitle: The completion of a nonarchimedean additive group
nodes.description: The completion of a nonarchimedean additive group is a nonarchimedean additive group.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Nonarchimedean.TotallyDisconnected
nodes.description: In this file, we prove that a nonarchimedean group is a totally separated topological space. The fact that a nonarchimedean group is a totally disconnected topological space is implied by the fact that a nonarchimedean group is totally separated.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.OpenSubgroup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Open subgroups of a topological group
nodes.description: This file builds the lattice OpenSubgroup G of open subgroups in a topological group G, and its additive version OpenAddSubgroup. This lattice has a top element, the subgroup of all elements, but no bottom element in general. The trivial subgroup which is the natural candidate bottom has no reason to be open (this happens only in discrete groups).

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Archimedean
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on archimedean groups and fields
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following theorems:

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.ArchimedeanDiscrete
nodes.descriptionTitle: Discreteness of subgroups in archimedean ordered groups
nodes.description: This file contains some supplements to the results in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Order/Archimedean.lean, involving discreteness of subgroups, which require heavier imports.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Field
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a linear ordered field with order topology has continuous multiplication and division (apart from zero in the denominator). We also prove theorems like Filter.Tendsto.mul_atTop: if f tends to a positive number and g tends to positive infinity, then f g tends to positive infinity.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Floor
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological facts about Int.floor, Int.ceil and Int.fract
nodes.description: This file proves statements about limits and continuity of functions involving floor, ceil and fract.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Group
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on a linear ordered commutative group
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a linear ordered commutative group with order topology is a topological group. We also prove continuity of abs : G → G and provide convenience lemmas like ContinuousAt.abs.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.LiminfLimsup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about liminf and limsup in an order topology.
nodes.description: The same lemmas are true in ℝ, ℝ × ℝ, ι → ℝ, EuclideanSpace ι ℝ. To avoid code duplication, we provide an ad hoc axiomatisation of the properties we need.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Module
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Order.Module.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.Support
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topological support of sup and inf of functions
nodes.description: In a topological space X and a space M with Sup structure, for f g : X → M with compact support, we show that f ⊔ g has compact support. Similarly, in β with Inf structure, f ⊓ g has compact support if so do f and g.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Order.UpperLower
nodes.description: The topological closure and interior of an upper/lower/order-connected set is an upper/lower/order-connected set (with the notable exception of the closure of an order-connected set).

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Polynomial
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following lemmas.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.PontryaginDual
nodes.description: This file defines the Pontryagin dual of a topological group. The Pontryagin dual of a topological group A is the topological group of continuous homomorphisms A → Circle with the compact-open topology. For example, ℤ and Circle are Pontryagin duals of each other. This is an example of Pontryagin duality, which states that a locally compact abelian topological group is canonically isomorphic to its double dual.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ProperAction.AddTorsor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The action underlying a topological additive torsor is proper.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.ProperAction.AddTorsor.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ProperAction.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define proper action of a group on a topological space, and we prove that in this case the quotient space is T2. We also give equivalent definitions of proper action using ultrafilters and show the transfer of proper action to a closed subgroup.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ProperAction.CompactlyGenerated
nodes.descriptionTitle: When a proper action is properly discontinuous
nodes.description: This file proves that if a discrete group acts on a T2 space X such that X × X is compactly generated, and if the action is continuous in the second variable, then the action is properly discontinuous if and only if it is proper. This is in particular true if X is first-countable or weakly locally compact.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ProperAction.ProperlyDiscontinuous
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ProperConstSMul
nodes.description: In this file we define ProperConstSMul M X to be a mixin Prop-value class stating that (c • ·) is a proper map for all c.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.RestrictedProduct.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Restricted products of sets, groups and rings
nodes.description: We define the restricted product of R : ι → Type of types, relative to a family of subsets A : (i : ι) → Set (R i) and a filter 𝓕 : Filter ι. This is the set of all x : Π i, R i such that the set {j | x j ∈ A j} belongs to 𝓕. We denote it by Πʳ i, [R i, A i]_[𝓕].

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.RestrictedProduct.TopologicalSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Restricted products of topological spaces, topological groups and rings
nodes.description: We endow a restricted product of topological spaces with a natural topology, which we describe below. We also show various compatibility results when we change filters, and extend the construction of restricted products of algebraic structures to the topological setting.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.RestrictedProduct.Units
nodes.description: This file contains results about the units of a restricted product. The restricted product Πʳ i : ι, [R i, B i]_[𝓕] of a family of types R with respect to a family of subsets B along a filter 𝓕 is defined in Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.RestrictedProduct.Basic. Here, we give conditions that characterize when an element of the restricted product is a unit, and provide an isomorphism between the units of the restricted product and the restricted product of the units.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Ring.Basic
nodes.description: A topological (semi)ring is a (semi)ring equipped with a topology such that all operations are continuous. Besides this definition, this file proves that the topological closure of a subring (resp. an ideal) is a subring (resp. an ideal) and defines products and quotients of topological (semi)rings.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Ring.Compact
nodes.description: Compact Hausdorff Artinian rings are finite (and thus discrete). Maximal ideals are open in compact Hausdorff Noetherian rings. An ideal in a compact Hausdorff Noetherian local ring is open iff it has finite index. An ideal in a compact Hausdorff Dedekind domain (that is not a field) is open iff it is non-zero.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Ring.Ideal
nodes.descriptionTitle: Ideals and quotients of topological rings
nodes.description: In this file we define Ideal.closure to be the topological closure of an ideal in a topological ring. We also define a TopologicalSpace structure on the quotient of a topological ring by an ideal and prove that the quotient is a topological ring.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Ring.Real
nodes.description: This file defines topological field/(semi)ring structures on the (extended) (nonnegative) reals and shows the algebraic operations are (uniformly) continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Semigroup
nodes.description: This file provides a sufficient condition for a semigroup M to contain an idempotent (i.e. an element m such that m m = m ), namely that M is a nonempty compact Hausdorff space where right-multiplication by constants is continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.SeparationQuotient.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define algebraic operations (multiplication, addition etc) on the separation quotient of a topological space with corresponding operation, provided that the original operation is continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.SeparationQuotient.FiniteDimensional
nodes.descriptionTitle: Separation quotient is a finite module
nodes.description: In this file we show that the separation quotient of a finite module is a finite module.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.SeparationQuotient.Hom
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lift of MonoidHom M N to MonoidHom (SeparationQuotient M) N
nodes.description: In this file we define the lift of a continuous monoid homomorphism f from M to N to SeparationQuotient M, assuming that f maps two inseparable elements to the same element.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.SeparationQuotient.Section
nodes.description: In this file we construct a section of the quotient map E → SeparationQuotient E as a continuous linear map SeparationQuotient E →L[K] E.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Star
nodes.description: This file defines the ContinuousStar typeclass, along with instances on Pi, Prod, MulOpposite, and Units.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Star.LinearMap
nodes.descriptionTitle: Intrinsic star operation on continuous linear maps
nodes.description: This file defines the star operation on continuous linear maps: (star f) x = star (f (star x)). This corresponds to a map being star-preserving, i.e., a map is self-adjoint iff it is star-preserving.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Star.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological properties of conjugation on ℝ
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Star.Real.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Star.Unitary
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Algebra.Star.Unitary.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.StarSubalgebra
nodes.description: A topological star algebra over a topological semiring R is a topological semiring with a compatible continuous scalar multiplication by elements of R and a continuous star operation. We reuse typeclass ContinuousSMul for topological algebras.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Support
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topological support of a function
nodes.description: In this file we define the topological support of a function f, tsupport f, as the closure of the support of f.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.TopologicallyNilpotent
nodes.description: Let M be a monoid with zero M, endowed with a topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.UniformConvergence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Algebraic facts about the topology of uniform convergence
nodes.description: This file contains algebraic compatibility results about the uniform structure of uniform convergence / 𝔖-convergence. They will mostly be useful for defining strong topologies on the space of continuous linear maps between two topological vector spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.UniformField
nodes.description: The goal of this file is to prove the main part of Proposition 7 of Bourbaki GT III 6.8 :

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.UniformFilterBasis
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniform properties of neighborhood bases in topological algebra
nodes.description: This file contains properties of filter bases on algebraic structures that also require the theory of uniform spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.UniformMulAction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Multiplicative action on the completion of a uniform space
nodes.description: In this file we define typeclasses UniformContinuousConstVAdd and UniformContinuousConstSMul and prove that a multiplicative action on X with uniformly continuous (•) c can be extended to a multiplicative action on UniformSpace.Completion X.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.UniformRing
nodes.description: This file endows the completion of a topological ring with a ring structure. More precisely, the instance UniformSpace.Completion.ring builds a ring structure on the completion of a ring endowed with a compatible uniform structure in the sense of IsUniformAddGroup. There is also a commutative version when the original ring is commutative. Moreover, if a topological ring is an algebra over a commutative semiring, then so is its UniformSpace.Completion.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.ValuativeRel.ValuativeTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topology on a ring induced by a valuation
nodes.description: In this file, we define the non-Archimedean topology induced by a valuation on a ring.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.LocallyCompact
nodes.descriptionTitle: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a locally compact valued field
nodes.description: it is totally bounded iff the residue field is finite.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.NormedValued
nodes.descriptionTitle: Correspondence between nontrivial nonarchimedean norms and rank one valuations
nodes.description: Nontrivial nonarchimedean norms correspond to rank one valuations.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.ValuationTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topology on a valued ring
nodes.description: In this file, we define the non-Archimedean topology induced by a valuation on a ring. The main definition is a Valued type class which equips a ring with a valuation taking values in a group with zero. Other instances are then deduced from this.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.ValuativeRel
nodes.description: In this temporary file, we provide a helper instance for Valued R Γ derived from a ValuativeRel R, so that downstream files can refer to ValuativeRel R, to facilitate a refactor.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.ValuedField
nodes.description: In this file we study the topology of a field K endowed with a valuation (in our application to adic spaces, K will be the valuation field associated to some valuation on a ring, defined in valuation.basic).

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithVal
nodes.description: For a given valuation v : Valuation R Γ₀ on a ring R taking values in Γ₀, this file defines the type synonym WithVal v of R. By assigning a Valued (WithVal v) Γ₀ instance, WithVal v represents the ring R equipped with the topology coming from v. The type synonym WithVal v is in isomorphism to R as rings via WithVal.equiv v. This isomorphism should be used to explicitly map terms of WithVal v to terms of R.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.Valued.WithZeroMulInt
nodes.description: This file contains topological results for valuation rings taking values in the multiplicative integers with zero adjoined. These are useful for cases where there is a Valued R ℤₘ₀ instance but no canonical base with which to embed this into NNReal.

nodes.label: Topology.Algebra.WithZeroTopology
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topology on linearly ordered commutative groups with zero
nodes.description: Let Γ₀ be a linearly ordered commutative group to which we have adjoined a zero element. Then Γ₀ may naturally be endowed with a topology that turns Γ₀ into a topological monoid. Neighborhoods of zero are sets containing { γ | γ < γ₀ } for some invertible element γ₀ and every invertible element is open. In particular the topology is the following: "a subset U ⊆ Γ₀ is open if 0 ∉ U or if there is an invertible γ₀ ∈ Γ₀ such that { γ | γ < γ₀ } ⊆ U", see WithZeroTopology.isOpen_iff.

nodes.label: Topology.ApproximateUnit
nodes.description: An approximate unit is a filter l such that multiplication on the left (or right) by m : α tends to 𝓝 m along the filter, and additionally l ≠ ⊥.

nodes.label: Topology.Baire.BaireMeasurable
nodes.descriptionTitle: Baire category and Baire measurable sets
nodes.description: This file defines some of the basic notions of Baire category and Baire measurable sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Baire.CompleteMetrizable
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a completely pseudometrizable topological space is a Baire space.

nodes.label: Topology.Baire.Lemmas
nodes.description: A topological space is called a Baire space if a countable intersection of dense open subsets is dense. Baire theorems say that all completely metrizable spaces and all locally compact regular spaces are Baire spaces. We prove the theorems in Mathlib/Topology/Baire/CompleteMetrizable and Mathlib/Topology/Baire/LocallyCompactRegular.

nodes.label: Topology.Baire.LocallyCompactRegular
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a locally compact regular topological space has Baire property.

nodes.label: Topology.Bases
nodes.description: A topological basis on a topological space t is a collection of sets, such that all open sets can be generated as unions of these sets, without the need to take finite intersections of them. This file introduces a framework for dealing with these collections, and also what more we can say under certain countability conditions on bases, which are referred to as first- and second-countable. We also briefly cover the theory of separable spaces, which are those with a countable, dense subset.

nodes.label: Topology.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Openness and closedness of a set
nodes.description: This file provides lemmas relating to the predicates IsOpen and IsClosed of a set endowed with a topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.Absorbs
nodes.description: Let M act on α, let A and B be sets in α. We say that A absorbs B if for sufficiently large a : M, we have B ⊆ a • A. Formally, "for sufficiently large a : M" means "for all but a bounded set of a".

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.Basic
nodes.description: We develop the basic theory of bornologies. Instead of axiomatizing bounded sets and defining bornologies in terms of those, we recognize that the cobounded sets form a filter and define a bornology as a filter of cobounded sets which contains the cofinite filter. This allows us to make use of the extensive library for filters, but we also provide the relevant connecting results for bounded sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.BoundedOperation
nodes.description: This file introduces type classes for bornologically bounded operations.

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bornology structure on products and subtypes
nodes.description: In this file we define Bornology and BoundedSpace instances on α × β, Π i, X i, and {x // p x}. We also prove basic lemmas about Bornology.cobounded and Bornology.IsBounded on these types.

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.Hom
nodes.description: This file defines locally bounded maps between bornologies.

nodes.label: Topology.Bornology.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: The reals are equipped with their order bornology
nodes.description: This file contains results related to the order bornology on (non-negative) real numbers. We prove that ℝ and ℝ≥0 are equipped with the order topology and bornology.

nodes.label: Topology.CWComplex.Abstract.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines (relative) CW-complexes using a categorical approach.

nodes.label: Topology.CWComplex.Classical.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines (relative) CW complexes and proves basic properties about them using the classical approach of Whitehead.

nodes.label: Topology.CWComplex.Classical.Finite
nodes.description: In this file we define what it means for a CW complex to be finite dimensional, of finite type or finite. We define constructors with relaxed conditions for CW complexes of finite type and finite CW complexes.

nodes.label: Topology.CWComplex.Classical.Graph
nodes.description: In this file we define the 1-skeleton of a CW complex as a graph.

nodes.label: Topology.CWComplex.Classical.Subcomplex
nodes.description: In this file we discuss subcomplexes of CW complexes. The definition of subcomplexes is in the file Mathlib/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Born
nodes.description: This defines Born, the category of bornologies.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHaus.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of Compact Hausdorff Spaces
nodes.description: We construct the category of compact Hausdorff spaces. The type of compact Hausdorff spaces is denoted CompHaus, and it is endowed with a category instance making it a full subcategory of TopCat. The fully faithful functor CompHaus ⥤ TopCat is denoted compHausToTop.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHaus.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: This file proves that EffectiveEpi, Epi and Surjective are all equivalent in CompHaus. As a consequence we deduce from the material in Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/EffectiveEpi.lean that CompHaus is Preregular and Precoherent.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHaus.Frm
nodes.descriptionTitle: The forgetful functor from TopCatᵒᵖ to Frm.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Category.CompHaus.Frm.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHaus.Limits
nodes.description: This file applies the general API for explicit limits and colimits in CompHausLike P (see the file Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/Limits.lean) to the special case of CompHaus.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHaus.Projective
nodes.description: In this file we show that CompHaus has enough projectives.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHausLike.Basic
nodes.description: We construct the category of compact Hausdorff spaces satisfying an additional property P.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHausLike.Cartesian
nodes.description: If the predicate P is preserved under taking type-theoretic products and PUnit satisfies it, then CompHausLike P is a cartesian monoidal category.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHausLike.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: In any category of compact Hausdorff spaces, continuous surjections are effective epimorphisms.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHausLike.Limits
nodes.description: This file collects some constructions of explicit limits and colimits in CompHausLike P, which may be useful due to their definitional properties.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompHausLike.SigmaComparison
nodes.description: This file defines the map CompHausLike.sigmaComparison associated to a presheaf X on CompHausLike P, and a finite family S₁,...,Sₙ of spaces in CompHausLike P, where P is stable under taking finite disjoint unions.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.CompactlyGenerated
nodes.description: This file defines the category of compactly generated topological spaces. These are spaces X such that a map f : X → Y is continuous whenever the composition S → X → Y is continuous for all compact Hausdorff spaces S mapping continuously to X.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Compactum
nodes.description: Recall that, given a monad M on Type, an algebra for M consists of the following data:

nodes.label: Topology.Category.DeltaGenerated
nodes.description: The category of delta-generated spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.FinTopCat
nodes.description: Definition of the category of finite topological spaces with the canonical forgetful functors.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.AsLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Light profinite sets as limits of finite sets.
nodes.description: We show that any light profinite set is isomorphic to a sequential limit of finite sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Basic
nodes.description: We construct the category LightProfinite of light profinite topological spaces. These are implemented as totally disconnected second countable compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Cartesian
nodes.description: This file defines the cartesian monoidal structure on LightProfinite given by the type-theoretic product.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: This file proves that EffectiveEpi and Surjective are equivalent in LightProfinite. As a consequence we deduce from the material in Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/EffectiveEpi.lean that LightProfinite is Preregular and Precoherent.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Extend
nodes.description: Let (Sₙ)_{n : ℕᵒᵖ} be a sequential inverse system of finite sets and let S be its limit in Profinite. Let G be a functor from LightProfinite to a category C and suppose that G preserves the limit described above. Suppose further that the projection maps S ⟶ Sₙ are epimorphic for all n. Then G.obj S is isomorphic to a limit indexed by StructuredArrow S toLightProfinite (see LightProfinite.Extend.isLimitCone).

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Injective
nodes.description: This file establishes that non-empty light profinite sets are injective in the category of profinite sets, and thus also in the category of light profinite sets. This is used in the proof that the null sequence module is internally projective in light condensed abelian groups.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Limits
nodes.description: This file applies the general API for explicit limits and colimits in CompHausLike P (see the file Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/Limits.lean) to the special case of LightProfinite.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.LightProfinite.Sequence
nodes.descriptionTitle: The light profinite set classifying convergent sequences
nodes.description: This file defines the light profinite set ℕ∪{∞}, defined as the one point compactification of ℕ.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Locale
nodes.description: This file defines Locale, the category of locales. This is the opposite of the category of frames.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.AsLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: Profinite sets as limits of finite sets.
nodes.description: We show that any profinite set is isomorphic to the limit of its discrete (hence finite) quotients.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Basic
nodes.description: We construct the category of profinite topological spaces, often called profinite sets -- perhaps they could be called profinite types in Lean.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.CofilteredLimit
nodes.description: This file contains some theorems about cofiltered limits of profinite sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: This file proves that EffectiveEpi, Epi and Surjective are all equivalent in Profinite. As a consequence we deduce from the material in Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/EffectiveEpi.lean that Profinite is Preregular and Precoherent.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Extend
nodes.description: Let (Sᵢ)_{i : I} be a family of finite sets indexed by a cofiltered category I and let S be its limit in Profinite. Let G be a functor from Profinite to a category C and suppose that G preserves the limit described above. Suppose further that the projection maps S ⟶ Sᵢ are epimorphic for all i. Then G.obj S is isomorphic to a limit indexed by StructuredArrow S toProfinite (see Profinite.Extend.isLimitCone).

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Limits
nodes.description: This file applies the general API for explicit limits and colimits in CompHausLike P (see the file Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/Limits.lean) to the special case of Profinite.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Nobeling.Basic
nodes.description: This file constructs basic objects and results concerning them that are needed in the proof of Nöbeling's theorem, which is in Mathlib/Topology/Category/Profinite/Nobeling/Induction.lean. See the section docstrings for more information.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Nobeling.Induction
nodes.description: This file proves Nöbeling's theorem. For the overall proof outline see Mathlib/Topology/Category/Profinite/Nobeling/Basic.lean.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Nobeling.Span
nodes.description: Most of the argument is developing an API for π C (· ∈ s) when s : Finset I; then the image of C is finite with the discrete topology. In this case, there is a direct argument that the good products span. The general result is deduced from this.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Nobeling.Successor
nodes.descriptionTitle: The successor case in the induction for Nöbeling's theorem
nodes.description: Here we assume that o is an ordinal such that contained C (o+1) and o < I. The element in I corresponding to o is called term I ho, but in this informal docstring we refer to it simply as o.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Nobeling.ZeroLimit
nodes.descriptionTitle: The zero and limit cases in the induction for Nöbeling's theorem
nodes.description: This file proves the zero and limit cases of the ordinal induction used in the proof of Nöbeling's theorem. See the section docstrings for more information.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Product
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compact subsets of products as limits in Profinite
nodes.description: This file exhibits a compact subset C of a product (i : ι) → X i of totally disconnected Hausdorff spaces as a cofiltered limit in Profinite indexed by Finset ι.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Profinite.Projective
nodes.description: In this file we show that Profinite has enough projectives.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Sequential
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of sequential topological spaces
nodes.description: We define the category Sequential of sequential topological spaces. We follow the usual template for defining categories of topological spaces, by giving it the induced category structure from TopCat.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Stonean.Adjunctions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjunctions involving the category of Stonean spaces
nodes.description: This file constructs the left adjoint typeToStonean to the forgetful functor from Stonean spaces to sets, using the Stone-Cech compactification. This allows to conclude that the monomorphisms in Stonean are precisely the injective maps (see Stonean.mono_iff_injective).

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Stonean.Basic
nodes.description: This file develops some of the basic theory of extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Stonean.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: This file proves that EffectiveEpi, Epi and Surjective are all equivalent in Stonean. As a consequence we deduce from the material in Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/EffectiveEpi.lean that Stonean is Preregular and Precoherent.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.Stonean.Limits
nodes.description: This file applies the general API for explicit limits and colimits in CompHausLike P (see the file Mathlib/Topology/Category/CompHausLike/Limits.lean) to the special case of Stonean.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Adjunctions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjunctions regarding the category of topological spaces
nodes.description: This file shows that the forgetful functor from topological spaces to types has a left and right adjoint, given by TopCat.discrete, resp. TopCat.trivial, the functors which equip a type with the discrete, resp. trivial, topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Basic
nodes.description: We introduce the bundled category TopCat of topological spaces together with the functors TopCat.discrete and TopCat.trivial from the category of types to TopCat which equip a type with the corresponding discrete, resp. trivial, topology. For a proof that these functors are left, resp. right adjoint to the forgetful functor, see Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Adjunctions.lean.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.EffectiveEpi
nodes.description: This file proves the result TopCat.effectiveEpi_iff_isQuotientMap: The effective epimorphisms in TopCat are precisely the quotient maps.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.EpiMono
nodes.description: This file shows that a continuous function is an epimorphism in the category of topological spaces if and only if it is surjective, and that a continuous function is a monomorphism in the category of topological spaces if and only if it is injective.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.GrothendieckTopology
nodes.description: In this file we define the standard Grothendieck topology on TopCat. This is the topology generated by families of jointly surjective open embeddings.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of topological spaces has all limits and colimits
nodes.description: Further, these limits and colimits are preserved by the forgetful functor --- that is, the underlying types are just the limits in the category of types.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Cofiltered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cofiltered limits in the category of topological spaces
nodes.description: Given a compatible collection of topological bases for the factors in a cofiltered limit which contain Set.univ and are closed under intersections, the induced naive collection of sets in the limit is, in fact, a topological basis.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Konig
nodes.description: A topological version of Kőnig's lemma is that the inverse limit of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces is nonempty. (Note: this can be generalized further to inverse limits of nonempty compact T0 spaces, where all the maps are closed maps; see [Stone1979] --- however there is an erratum for Theorem 4 that the element in the inverse limit can have cofinally many components that are not closed points.)

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Products
nodes.descriptionTitle: Products and coproducts in the category of topological spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Products.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Pullbacks
nodes.descriptionTitle: Pullbacks and pushouts in the category of topological spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Category.TopCat.Limits.Pullbacks.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Monoidal
nodes.descriptionTitle: The cartesian monoidal structure on TopCat
nodes.description: We define the cartesian monoidal category structure on TopCat. We also introduce the unit interval as an object TopCat.I of TopCat.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.OpenNhds
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of open neighborhoods of a point
nodes.description: Given an object X of the category TopCat of topological spaces and a point x : X, this file builds the type OpenNhds x of open neighborhoods of x in X and endows it with the partial order given by inclusion and the corresponding category structure (as a full subcategory of the poset category Set X). This is used in Topology.Sheaves.Stalks to build the stalk of a sheaf at x as a limit over OpenNhds x.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Opens
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of open sets in a topological space.
nodes.description: We define toTopCat : Opens X ⥤ TopCat and map (f : X ⟶ Y) : Opens Y ⥤ Opens X, given by taking preimages of open sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Sphere
nodes.description: This file defines the n-sphere 𝕊 n, the n-disk 𝔻 n, its boundary ∂𝔻 n and its interior 𝔹 n as objects in TopCat.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.ULift
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lifting topological spaces to a higher universe
nodes.description: In this file, we construct the functor uliftFunctor.{v, u} : TopCat.{u} ⥤ TopCat.{max u v} which sends a topological space X : Type u to a homeomorphic space in Type (max u v).

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCat.Yoneda
nodes.descriptionTitle: Yoneda presheaves on topologically concrete categories
nodes.description: This file develops some API for "topologically concrete" categories, defining universe polymorphic "Yoneda presheaves" on such categories.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopCommRingCat
nodes.description: We introduce the category TopCommRingCat of topological commutative rings together with the relevant forgetful functors to topological spaces and commutative rings.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.TopPair
nodes.description: In this file we introduce TopPair, the category of topological pairs. It is defined as the category of arrows in TopCat which are topological embeddings.

nodes.label: Topology.Category.UniformSpace
nodes.description: We construct the category of uniform spaces, show that the complete separated uniform spaces form a reflective subcategory, and hence possess all limits that uniform spaces do.

nodes.label: Topology.Clopen
nodes.description: A clopen set is a set that is both closed and open.

nodes.label: Topology.ClopenBox
nodes.description: In general, a clopen subset in a Cartesian product of topological spaces cannot be written as a union of "clopen boxes", i.e. products of clopen subsets of the components (see [buzyakovaClopenBox] for counterexamples).

nodes.label: Topology.Closure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Interior, closure and frontier of a set
nodes.description: This file provides lemmas relating to the functions interior, closure and frontier of a set endowed with a topology.

nodes.label: Topology.ClusterPt
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas on cluster and accumulation points
nodes.description: In this file we prove various lemmas on cluster points (also known as limit points and accumulation points) of a filter and of a sequence.

nodes.label: Topology.Coherent
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology generated by its restrictions to subsets
nodes.description: We say that restrictions of the topology on X to sets from a family S generates the original topology, if either of the following equivalent conditions hold:

nodes.label: Topology.CompactOpen
nodes.description: In this file, we define the compact-open topology on the set of continuous maps between two topological spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactification.OnePoint.Basic
nodes.description: We construct the one-point compactification of an arbitrary topological space X and prove some properties inherited from X.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactification.OnePoint.ProjectiveLine
nodes.description: We construct a set-theoretic equivalence between OnePoint K and the projectivization ℙ K (Fin 2 → K) for an arbitrary division ring K.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactification.OnePoint.Sphere
nodes.descriptionTitle: One-point compactification of Euclidean space is homeomorphic to the sphere.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Compactification.OnePoint.Sphere.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactification.StoneCech
nodes.description: Construction of the Stone-Čech compactification using ultrafilters.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.Bases
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological bases in compact sets and compact spaces
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Compactness.Bases.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.Compact
nodes.description: with a subbasis S and s is a subset of X, then s is compact if for any open cover of s with all elements taken from S, there is a finite subcover.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.CompactSystem
nodes.description: This file defines compact systems of sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.CompactlyCoherentSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compactly coherent spaces and the compact coherentification
nodes.description: In this file we will define compactly coherent spaces and the compact coherentification and prove basic properties about them. This is a weaker version of CompactlyGeneratedSpace. These notions agree on Hausdorff spaces. They are both referred to as compactly generated spaces in the literature while the compact coherentification is often called the k-ification.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.CompactlyGeneratedSpace
nodes.description: This file defines compactly generated topological spaces. A compactly generated space is a space X whose topology is coinduced by continuous maps from compact Hausdorff spaces to X. In such a space, a set s is closed (resp. open) if and only if for all compact Hausdorff space K and f : K → X continuous, f ⁻¹' s is closed (resp. open) in K.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.CountablyCompact
nodes.description: A set A in a topological space is countably compact if every countably generated proper filter contained in A has a cluster point in A. Equivalently, every sequence in A has a cluster point in A, and every countable open cover of A admits a finite subcover.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.DeltaGeneratedSpace
nodes.description: This file defines delta-generated spaces, as topological spaces whose topology is coinduced by all maps from Euclidean spaces into them. This is the strongest topological property that holds for all CW-complexes and is closed under quotients and disjoint unions; every delta-generated space is locally path-connected, sequential and in particular compactly generated.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.HilbertCubeEmbedding
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.Lindelof
nodes.description: We define the following properties for sets in a topological space:

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.LocallyCompact
nodes.description: This file contains basic results about locally compact spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.LocallyFinite
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compact sets and compact spaces and locally finite functions
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.Compactness.LocallyFinite.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.NhdsKer
nodes.descriptionTitle: Compactness of the neighborhoods kernel of a set
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the neighborhoods kernel of a set (defined as the intersection of all of its neighborhoods) is a compact set if and only if the original set is a compact set.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.Paracompact
nodes.description: A topological space X is said to be paracompact if every open covering of X admits a locally finite refinement.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.PseudometrizableLindelof
nodes.description: Full Mathlib source module in Topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Compactness.SigmaCompact
nodes.description: of a countable collection of compact subspaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define connected subsets of a topological spaces and various other properties and classes related to connectivity.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.CardComponents
nodes.descriptionTitle: Cardinality of connected components under open and closed maps
nodes.description: Let f : X → Y be an open and closed map.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.Clopen
nodes.descriptionTitle: Connected subsets and their relation to clopen sets
nodes.description: In this file we show how connected subsets of a topological space are intimately connected to clopen sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.LocPathConnected
nodes.description: This file defines LocPathConnectedSpace X, a predicate class asserting that X is locally path-connected, in that each point has a basis of path-connected neighborhoods.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.LocallyConnected
nodes.description: A topological space is locally connected if each neighborhood filter admits a basis of connected open sets. Local connectivity is equivalent to each point having a basis of connected (not necessarily open) sets --- but in a non-trivial way, so we choose this definition and prove the equivalence later in locallyConnectedSpace_iff_connected_basis.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.PathComponentOne
nodes.descriptionTitle: The path component of the identity in a locally path connected topological group
nodes.description: This file defines the path component of the identity is an OpenNormalSubgroup when the ambient topological group is locally path connected. We place this in a separate file to avoid importing additional algebra into the topology hierarchy.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.PathConnected
nodes.description: Continuing from Mathlib/Topology/Path.lean, this file defines path components and path-connected spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.Separation
nodes.descriptionTitle: Separation and (dis)connectedness properties of topological spaces.
nodes.description: This file provides an instance T2Space X given TotallySeparatedSpace X.

nodes.label: Topology.Connected.TotallyDisconnected
nodes.descriptionTitle: Totally disconnected and totally separated topological spaces
nodes.description: We define the following properties for sets in a topological space:

nodes.label: Topology.Constructible
nodes.description: This file defines constructible sets, which are morally sets in a topological space which we can make out of finite unions and intersections of open and closed sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructions of new topological spaces from old ones
nodes.description: This file constructs pi types, subtypes and quotients of topological spaces and sets up their basic theory, such as criteria for maps into or out of these constructions to be continuous; descriptions of the open sets, neighborhood filters, and generators of these constructions; and their behavior with respect to embeddings and other specific classes of maps.

nodes.label: Topology.Constructions.SumProd
nodes.descriptionTitle: Disjoint unions and products of topological spaces
nodes.description: This file constructs sums (disjoint unions) and products of topological spaces and sets up their basic theory, such as criteria for maps into or out of these constructions to be continuous; descriptions of the open sets, neighborhood filters, and generators of these constructions; and their behavior with respect to embeddings and other specific classes of maps.

nodes.label: Topology.Continuous
nodes.description: For topological spaces X and Y, a function f : X → Y and a point x : X, ContinuousAt f x means f is continuous at x, and global continuity is Continuous f. There is also a version of continuity PContinuous for partially defined functions.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Algebra
nodes.description: In this file we define instances of algebraic structures over the type ContinuousMap α β (denoted C(α, β)) of bundled continuous maps from α to β. For example, C(α, β) is a group when β is a group, a ring when β is a ring, etc.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define the type ContinuousMap of continuous bundled maps.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.ArzelaAscoli
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Arzelà–Ascoli theorem for bounded continuous functions
nodes.description: Arzelà–Ascoli asserts that, on a compact space, a set of functions sharing a common modulus of continuity and taking values in a compact set forms a compact subset for the topology of uniform convergence. This file proves the theorem and several useful variations around it.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.Basic
nodes.description: The type of bounded continuous functions taking values in a metric space, with the uniform distance.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.Normed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Inheritance of normed algebraic structures by bounded continuous functions
nodes.description: For various types of normed algebraic structures β, we show in this file that the space of bounded continuous functions from α to β inherits the same normed structure, by using pointwise operations and checking that they are compatible with the uniform distance.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.Star
nodes.descriptionTitle: Star structures on bounded continuous functions
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded.Star.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.BoundedCompactlySupported
nodes.description: The two-sided ideal of compactly supported bounded continuous functions taking values in a metric space, with the uniform distance.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.CocompactMap
nodes.description: The type of cocompact continuous maps are those which tend to the cocompact filter on the codomain along the cocompact filter on the domain. When the domain and codomain are Hausdorff, this is equivalent to many other conditions, including that preimages of compact sets are compact.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Compact
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous functions on a compact space
nodes.description: Continuous functions C(α, β) from a compact space α to a metric space β are automatically bounded, and so acquire various structures inherited from α →ᵇ β.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.CompactlySupported
nodes.description: In this file, we define the type C_c(α, β) of compactly supported continuous functions and the class CompactlySupportedContinuousMapClass, and prove basic properties.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.ContinuousMapZero
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous maps sending zero to zero
nodes.description: This is the type of continuous maps from X to R such that (0 : X) ↦ (0 : R) for which we provide the scoped notation C(X, R)₀. We provide this as a dedicated type solely for the non-unital continuous functional calculus, as using various terms of type Ideal C(X, R) were overly burdensome on type class synthesis.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.ContinuousSqrt
nodes.description: This provides the instances of ContinuousSqrt for ℝ, ℝ≥0, and ℂ, thereby yielding instances of StarOrderedRing C(α, R) and StarOrderedRing C(α, R)₀ for any topological space α and R among ℝ≥0, ℝ, and ℂ.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Defs
nodes.description: In this file we define the type ContinuousMap of continuous bundled maps.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Ideals
nodes.description: For a topological semiring R and a topological space X there is a Galois connection between Ideal C(X, R) and Set X given by sending each I : Ideal C(X, R) to {x : X | ∀ f ∈ I, f x = 0}ᶜ and mapping s : Set X to the ideal with carrier {f : C(X, R) | ∀ x ∈ sᶜ, f x = 0}, and we call these maps ContinuousMap.setOfIdeal and ContinuousMap.idealOfSet. As long as R is Hausdorff, ContinuousMap.setOfIdeal I is open, and if, in addition, X is locally compact, then ContinuousMap.setOfIdeal s is closed.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Interval
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few results about ContinuousMap when the domain is an interval.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Lattice
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous maps as a lattice ordered group
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.Lattice.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.LocallyConstant
nodes.descriptionTitle: The algebra morphism from locally constant functions to continuous functions.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.LocallyConstant.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.LocallyConvex
nodes.descriptionTitle: The space of continuous maps is a locally convex space
nodes.description: In this file we prove that the space of continuous maps from a topological space to a locally convex topological vector space is a locally convex topological vector space.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Ordered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Bundled continuous maps into orders, with order-compatible topology
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.Ordered.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Periodic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Sums of translates of a continuous function is a period continuous function.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.Periodic.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Polynomial
nodes.descriptionTitle: Constructions relating polynomial functions and continuous functions.
nodes.description: as a bundled continuous function in C(X, R). the polynomial functions separate points.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: Second countable topology on C(X, Y)
nodes.description: In this file we prove that C(X, Y) with compact-open topology has second countable topology, if

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Sigma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equivalence between C(X, Σ i, Y i) and Σ i, C(X, Y i)
nodes.description: If X is a connected topological space, then for every continuous map f from X to the disjoint union of a collection of topological spaces Y i there exists a unique index i and a continuous map from g to Y i such that f is the composition of the natural embedding Sigma.mk i : Y i → Σ i, Y i with g.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Star
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.ContinuousMap.Star.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.StarOrdered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Continuous functions as a star-ordered ring
nodes.description: The type class ContinuousSqrt gives a sufficient condition on R to make C(α, R) and C(α, R)₀ into a StarOrderedRing for any topological space α, thereby providing a means by which we can ensure C(α, R) has this property. This condition is satisfied by ℝ≥0, ℝ, and ℂ, and the instances can be found in the file Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/ContinuousSqrt.lean.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.StoneWeierstrass
nodes.description: If a subalgebra A of C(X, ℝ), where X is a compact topological space, separates points, then it is dense.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.T0Sierpinski
nodes.descriptionTitle: Any T0 space embeds in a product of copies of the Sierpinski space.
nodes.description: We consider Prop with the Sierpinski topology. If X is a topological space, there is a continuous map productOfMemOpens from X to Opens X → Prop which is the product of the maps X → Prop given by x ↦ x ∈ u.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Units
nodes.description: This file concerns itself with C(X, M)ˣ and C(X, Mˣ) when X is a topological space and M has some monoid structure compatible with its topology.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.Weierstrass
nodes.descriptionTitle: The Weierstrass approximation theorem for continuous functions on [a,b]
nodes.description: We've already proved the Weierstrass approximation theorem in the sense that we've shown that the Bernstein approximations to a continuous function on [0,1] converge uniformly.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousMap.ZeroAtInfty
nodes.description: The type of continuous functions vanishing at infinity. When the domain is compact C(α, β) ≃ C₀(α, β) via the identity map. When the codomain is a metric space, every continuous map which vanishes at infinity is a bounded continuous function. When the domain is a locally compact space, this type has nice properties.

nodes.label: Topology.ContinuousOn

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.Category
nodes.description: Let X i be a family of topological spaces. In this file, we define the category GeneratedByTopCat X of X-generated spaces: this is defined as a full subcategory of TopCat.

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.ContinuousMapGeneratedBy
nodes.description: Given a family X i of topological spaces, we introduce a predicate ContinuousGeneratedBy X on maps g : Y ⟶ Z saying that g is X-continuous, i.e. for any continuous map f : X i → Y, the composition g ∘ f is continuous.

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.GeneratedBy
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topology that is generated by a family of topological spaces
nodes.description: Let X : ι → Type u be a family of topological spaces. Let Y be a topological space. We introduce a type synonym WithGeneratedByTopology X Y for Y. This type is endowed with the X-generated topology, which is coinduced by all continuous maps X i → Y. When the bijection WithGeneratedByTopology X Y ≃ Y is a homeomorphism, we say that Y is X-generated (typeclass IsGeneratedBy X Y).

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.HomSpace
nodes.descriptionTitle: The topological space of X-continuous maps
nodes.description: Let X i be a family of topological spaces. Let Z and T be topological spaces. In this file, we endow the type ContinuousMapGeneratedBy X Z T of X-continuous maps Z → T with the coarsest topology which makes the precomposition maps ContinuousMapGeneratedBy X Z T → C(X i, T) continuous for any continuous map X i → Z, where C(X i, T) is endowed with the compact-open topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.Localization
nodes.descriptionTitle: The category of X-generated spaces, as a localization
nodes.description: Let X i be a family of topological spaces. In this file, we introduce a property of morphisms morphismPropertyWithGeneratedByTopologyEquiv X in the category TopCat: it consists of the morphisms corresponding to the canonical continuous maps WithGeneratedByTopology X Z → Z for all topological spaces Z. We show that the functor TopCat.toContinuousGeneratedByCat X : TopCat ⥤ ContinuousGeneratedByCat X makes ContinuousGeneratedByCat X the localized category of TopCat with respect to this class of morphisms.

nodes.label: Topology.Convenient.OpenClosed
nodes.descriptionTitle: Open or closed subsets that are also X-generated spaces
nodes.description: Let X : ι → Type be a family of topological spaces. If all the opens (resp. closed) subsets of the X i are X-generated, then any open (resp. closed) subset of an X-generated space is X-generated.

nodes.label: Topology.EMetricSpace.BoundedVariation
nodes.description: We study functions of bounded variation. In particular, we show that a bounded variation function is a difference of monotone functions, and differentiable almost everywhere. This implies that Lipschitz functions from the real line into finite-dimensional vector space are also differentiable almost everywhere.

nodes.label: Topology.EMetricSpace.Defs
nodes.description: This file is devoted to the definition and study of EMetricSpaces, i.e., metric spaces in which the distance is allowed to take the value ∞. This extended distance is called edist, and takes values in ℝ≥0∞.

nodes.label: Topology.EMetricSpace.Diam
nodes.descriptionTitle: Diameters of sets in extended metric spaces
nodes.description: In this file we define the diameter of a set in the extended metric space as an extended nonnegative real number.

nodes.label: Topology.EMetricSpace.Lipschitz
nodes.description: A map f : α → β between two (extended) metric spaces is called Lipschitz continuous with constant K ≥ 0 if for all x, y we have edist (f x) (f y) ≤ K edist x y. For a metric space, the latter inequality is equivalent to dist (f x) (f y) ≤ K dist x y. There is also a version asserting this inequality only for x and y in some set s. Finally, f : α → β is called locally Lipschitz continuous if each x : α has a neighbourhood on which f is Lipschitz continuous (with some constant).

nodes.descriptionTitle: Extending a function from a subset
nodes.description: The main definition of this file is extendFrom A f where f : X → Y and A : Set X. This defines a new function g : X → Y which maps any x₀ : X to the limit of f as x tends to x₀, if such a limit exists.

nodes.label: Topology.ExtremallyDisconnected
nodes.description: An extremally disconnected topological space is a space in which the closure of every open set is open. Such spaces are also called Stonean spaces. They are the projective objects in the category of compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.FiberBundle.Basic
nodes.description: Mathematically, a (topological) fiber bundle with fiber F over a base B is a space projecting on B for which the fibers are all homeomorphic to F, such that the local situation around each point is a direct product.

This is an abstraction which is occasionally convenient in showing that a map is open, a quotient map, etc.

nodes.label: Topology.GDelta.MetrizableSpace

nodes.label: Topology.Germ

nodes.description: In this file we define a class ContinuousEval F X Y saying that F is a bundled morphism class (in the sense of FunLike) with a topology such that fun (f, x) : F × X ↦ f x is a continuous function.

nodes.label: Topology.Hom.ContinuousEvalConst

nodes.label: Topology.Hom.Open

nodes.label: Topology.Homeomorph.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines homeomorphisms between two topological spaces. They are bijections with both directions continuous. We denote homeomorphisms with the notation ≃ₜ.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Affine
nodes.descriptionTitle: Affine homotopy between two continuous maps
nodes.description: In this file we define ContinuousMap.Homotopy.affine f g to be the homotopy between f and g such that affine f g (t, x) = AffineMap.lineMap (f x) (g x) t.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Basic
nodes.description: In this file, we define a homotopy between two functions f₀ and f₁. First we define ContinuousMap.Homotopy between the two functions, with no restrictions on the intermediate maps. Then, as in the formalisation in HOL-Analysis, we define ContinuousMap.HomotopyWith f₀ f₁ P, for homotopies between f₀ and f₁, where the intermediate maps satisfy the predicate P. Finally, we define ContinuousMap.HomotopyRel f₀ f₁ S, for homotopies between f₀ and f₁ which are fixed on S.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Contractible
nodes.description: In this file, we define ContractibleSpace, a space that is homotopy equivalent to Unit.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Equiv
nodes.description: In this file, we define homotopy equivalences between topological spaces X and Y as a pair of functions f : C(X, Y) and g : C(Y, X) such that f.comp g and g.comp f are both homotopic to ContinuousMap.id.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.HSpaces
nodes.description: This file defines H-spaces mainly following the approach proposed by Serre in his paper Homologie singulière des espaces fibrés. The idea beneath H-spaces is that they are topological spaces with a binary operation ⋀ : X → X → X that is a homotopy-theoretic weakening of an operation that would make X into a topological monoid. In particular, there exists a "neutral element" e : X such that fun x ↦ e ⋀ x and fun x ↦ x ⋀ e are homotopic to the identity on X, see the Wikipedia page of H-spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.HomotopyGroup
nodes.description: We define the nth homotopy group at x : X, π_n X x, as the equivalence classes of functions from the n-dimensional cube to the topological space X that send the boundary to the base point x, up to homotopic equivalence. Note that such functions are generalized loops GenLoop (Fin n) x; in particular GenLoop (Fin 1) x ≃ Path x x.

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Lifting

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.LocallyContractible

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Path

nodes.label: Topology.Homotopy.Product
nodes.description: In this file, we introduce definitions for the product of homotopies. We show that the products of relative homotopies are still relative homotopies. Finally, we specialize to the case of path homotopies, and provide the definition for the product of path classes. We show various lemmas associated with these products, such as the fact that path products commute with path composition, and that projection is the inverse of products.

nodes.label: Topology.KrullDimension

nodes.description: The Krull dimension of a topological space is the order-theoretic Krull dimension applied to the collection of all its subsets that are closed and irreducible. Unfolding this definition, it is the length of longest series of closed irreducible subsets ordered by inclusion.

nodes.label: Topology.LocallyClosed
nodes.description: A set s is locally closed if one of the equivalent conditions below hold 1. It is the intersection of some open set and some closed set. 2. The coborder (closure s \ s)ᶜ is open. 3. s is closed in some neighborhood of x for all x ∈ s. 4. Every x ∈ s has some open neighborhood U such that U ∩ closure s ⊆ s. 5. s is open in the closure of s.

nodes.label: Topology.Maps.OpenQuotient
nodes.description: An open quotient map is an open map f : X → Y which is both an open map and a quotient map. Equivalently, it is a surjective continuous open map. We use the latter characterization as a definition.

nodes.label: Topology.Maps.Proper.Basic
nodes.description: This file develops the basic theory of proper maps between topological spaces. A map f : X → Y between two topological spaces is said to be proper if it is continuous and satisfies the following equivalent conditions: 1. f is closed and has compact fibers. 2. f is universally closed, in the sense that for any topological space Z, the map Prod.map f id : X × Z → Y × Z is closed. 3. For any ℱ : Filter X, all cluster points of map f ℱ are images by f of some cluster point of ℱ.

nodes.label: Topology.Maps.Proper.CompactlyGenerated
nodes.descriptionTitle: A map is proper iff preimage of compact sets are compact
nodes.description: This file proves that if Y is a Hausdorff and compactly generated space, a continuous map f : X → Y is proper if and only if preimage of compact sets are compact.

The intended use case is to abstract certain properties shared by normed groups and by R≥0.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Antilipschitz

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.BundledFun
nodes.description: This file defines a pseudometric as a bundled function. This allows one to define a semilattice on them, and to construct families of pseudometrics.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.CantorScheme
nodes.description: In topology, and especially descriptive set theory, one often constructs functions (ℕ → β) → α, where α is some topological space and β is a discrete space, as an appropriate limit of some map List β → Set α. We call the latter type of map a "β-scheme on α".

nodes.description: Various results on Cauchy sequences in (pseudo-)metric spaces, including

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Closeds

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Completion

nodes.description: Completion of uniform spaces are already defined in Topology.UniformSpace.Completion. We show here that the uniform space completion of a metric space inherits a metric space structure, by extending the distance to the completion and checking that it is indeed a distance, and that it defines the same uniformity as the already defined uniform structure on the completion

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Congruence
nodes.description: This file defines Congruent, i.e., the equivalence between indexed families of points in a metric space where all corresponding pairwise distances are the same. The motivating example are triangles in the plane.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Contracting
nodes.description: A Lipschitz continuous self-map with Lipschitz constant K < 1 is called a contracting map. In this file we prove the Banach fixed point theorem, some explicit estimates on the rate of convergence, and some properties of the map sending a contracting map to its fixed point.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Cover
nodes.description: This file defines covers, aka nets, which are a quantitative notion of compactness in a metric space.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.CoveringNumbers
nodes.description: We define covering numbers of sets in a pseudo-metric space, which are minimal cardinalities of ε-covers of sets by closed balls. We also define the packing number, which is the maximal cardinality of an ε-separated set.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines metric spaces and shows some of their basic properties.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Dilation
nodes.description: We define dilations, i.e., maps between emetric spaces that satisfy edist (f x) (f y) = r edist x y for some r ∉ {0, ∞}.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.DilationEquiv
nodes.description: In this file we define DilationEquiv X Y, a type of bundled equivalences between X and Y such that edist (f x) (f y) = r edist x y for some r : ℝ≥0, r ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Equicontinuity
nodes.description: This file contains various facts about (uniform) equicontinuity in metric spaces. Most importantly, we prove the usual characterization of equicontinuity of F at x₀ in the case of (pseudo) metric spaces: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x, dist x x₀ < δ → ∀ i, dist (F i x₀) (F i x) < ε, and we prove that functions sharing a common (local or global) continuity modulus are (locally or uniformly) equicontinuous.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.GromovHausdorff
