nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.GromovHausdorffRealized
nodes.description: In this file, we construct of a good coupling between nonempty compact metric spaces, minimizing their Hausdorff distance. This construction is instrumental to study the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between nonempty compact metric spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffAlexandroff
nodes.description: In this file, we prove the Hausdorff–Alexandroff theorem, which states that every nonempty compact metric space is a continuous image of the Cantor set.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDimension
nodes.description: The Hausdorff dimension of a set X in an (extended) metric space is the unique number dimH s : ℝ≥0∞ such that for any d : ℝ≥0 we have

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDistance
nodes.description: The Hausdorff distance on subsets of a metric (or emetric) space.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Holder
nodes.description: In this file we define Hölder continuity on a set and on the whole space. We also prove some basic properties of Hölder continuous functions.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.HolderNorm
nodes.description: This file defines the Hölder (semi-)norm for Hölder functions alongside some basic properties. The r-Hölder norm of a function f : X → Y between two metric spaces is the least non-negative real number C for which f is r-Hölder continuous with constant C, i.e. it is the least C for which WithHolder C r f is true.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Infsep
nodes.description: This file defines the extended infimum separation of a set. This is approximately dual to the diameter of a set, but where the extended diameter of a set is the supremum of the extended distance between elements of the set, the extended infimum separation is the infimum of the (extended) distance between distinct elements in the set.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.IsometricSMul
nodes.description: In this file we define two typeclasses:

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Isometry
nodes.description: We define isometries, i.e., maps between emetric spaces that preserve the edistance (on metric spaces, these are exactly the maps that preserve distances), and prove their basic properties. We also introduce isometric bijections.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Kuratowski
nodes.description: Any separable metric space can be embedded isometrically in ℓ^∞(ℕ, ℝ). Any partially defined Lipschitz map into ℓ^∞ can be extended to the whole space.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Lipschitz
nodes.description: A map f : α → β between two (extended) metric spaces is called Lipschitz continuous with constant K ≥ 0 if for all x, y we have edist (f x) (f y) ≤ K edist x y. For a metric space, the latter inequality is equivalent to dist (f x) (f y) ≤ K dist x y. There is also a version asserting this inequality only for x and y in some set s. Finally, f : α → β is called locally Lipschitz continuous if each x : α has a neighbourhood on which f is Lipschitz continuous (with some constant).

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.MetricSeparated
nodes.description: This file defines a few notions of separations of sets in a metric space.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.PartitionOfUnity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about (e)metric spaces that need partition of unity
nodes.description: The main lemma in this file (see Metric.exists_continuous_real_forall_closedBall_subset) says the following. Let X be a metric space. Let K : ι → Set X be a locally finite family of closed sets, let U : ι → Set X be a family of open sets such that K i ⊆ U i for all i. Then there exists a positive continuous function δ : C(X, ℝ) such that for any i and x ∈ K i, we have Metric.closedBall x (δ x) ⊆ U i. We also formulate versions of this lemma for extended metric spaces and for different codomains (ℝ, ℝ≥0, and ℝ≥0∞).

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Perfect
nodes.description: In this file we define properties of Perfect subsets of a metric space, including a version of the Cantor-Bendixson Theorem.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.PiNat
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topological study of spaces Π (n : ℕ), E n
nodes.description: When E n are topological spaces, the space Π (n : ℕ), E n is naturally a topological space (with the product topology). When E n are uniform spaces, it also inherits a uniform structure. However, it does not inherit a canonical metric space structure of the E n. Nevertheless, one can put a noncanonical metric space structure (or rather, several of them). This is done in this file.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Polish
nodes.description: A topological space is Polish if its topology is second-countable and there exists a compatible complete metric. This is the class of spaces that is well-behaved with respect to measure theory. In this file, we establish the basic properties of Polish spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace.Lemmas
nodes.description: This file contains some more involved results about ProperSpaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace.Real
nodes.description: We prove that EReal, ℝ≥0 and ℝ≥0∞ are second countable. In the process, we also provide the instance ProperSpace ℝ≥0.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Basic
nodes.description: Further results about pseudo-metric spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Constructions
nodes.descriptionTitle: Products of pseudometric spaces and other constructions
nodes.description: This file constructs the supremum distance on binary products of pseudometric spaces and provides instances for type synonyms.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines pseudo-metric spaces: these differ from metric spaces by not imposing the condition dist x y = 0 → x = y. Many definitions and theorems expected on (pseudo-)metric spaces are already introduced on uniform spaces and topological spaces. For example: open and closed sets, compactness, completeness, continuity and uniform continuity.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Lemmas

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Pi
nodes.description: This file constructs the infinity distance on finite products of pseudometric spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Real
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about distances between points in intervals in ℝ.
nodes.description: Module documentation is present for Topology.MetricSpace.Pseudo.Real.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Sequences
nodes.description: In this file we prove 2 versions of Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem for proper metric spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.ShrinkingLemma
nodes.descriptionTitle: Shrinking lemma in a proper metric space
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few versions of the shrinking lemma for coverings by balls in a proper (pseudo) metric space.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Similarity
nodes.description: This file defines Similar, i.e., the equivalence between indexed sets of points in a metric space where all corresponding pairwise distances have the same ratio. The motivating example is triangles in the plane.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Snowflaking
nodes.description: Given a (pseudo) (extended) metric space X and a number 0 < α ≤ 1, one can consider the metric given by d x y = (dist x y) ^ α. The metric space determined by this new metric is said to be the α-snowflaking (or α-snowflake) of X. In this file we define Metric.Snowflaking X α hα₀ hα₁ to be a one-field structure wrapper around X with metric given by this formula.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.ThickenedIndicator
nodes.description: This file is about thickened indicators of sets in (pseudo e)metric spaces. For a decreasing sequence of thickening radii tending to 0, the thickened indicators of a closed set form a decreasing pointwise converging approximation of the indicator function of the set, where the members of the approximating sequence are nonnegative bounded continuous functions.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.TransferInstance
nodes.descriptionTitle: Transfer metric space structures across Equivs
nodes.description: In this file, we transfer a distance and (pseudo-)metric space structure across an equivalence.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Ultra.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines ultrametric spaces, implemented as a mixin on the Dist, so that it can apply on pseudometric spaces as well.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Ultra.ContinuousMaps

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Ultra.Pi
nodes.description: This file contains results on the behavior of ultrametrics in products of ultrametric spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.Ultra.TotallySeparated
nodes.description: In a metric space with an ultrametric, the space is totally separated, hence totally disconnected.

nodes.label: Topology.MetricSpace.UniformConvergence
nodes.descriptionTitle: Metric structure on α →ᵤ β and α →ᵤ[𝔖] β for finite 𝔖
nodes.description: When β is a (pseudo, extended) metric space it is a uniform space, and therefore we may consider the type α →ᵤ β of functions equipped with the topology of uniform convergence. The natural (pseudo, extended) metric on this space is given by fun f g ↦ ⨆ x, edist (f x) (g x), and this induces the existing uniformity. Unless β is a bounded space, this will not be a (pseudo) metric space (except in the trivial case where α is empty).

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.Basic
nodes.description: In this file we define metrizable topological spaces, i.e., topological spaces for which there exists a metric space structure that generates the same topology. We define it without any reference to metric spaces in order to avoid importing the real numbers. For the proof that metrizable spaces admit a compatible metric, see Mathlib/Topology/Metrizable/Uniformity.lean.

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.CompletelyMetrizable
nodes.description: A topological space is completely (pseudo)metrizable if one can endow it with a (Pseudo)MetricSpace structure which makes it complete and gives the same topology. This typeclass allows to state theorems which do not require a (Pseudo)MetricSpace structure to make sense without introducing such a structure. It is in particular useful in measure theory, where one often assumes that a space is a PolishSpace, i.e. a separable and completely metrizable space.

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.ContinuousMap
nodes.description: If X is a weakly locally compact σ-compact space and Y is a (pseudo)metrizable space, then C(X, Y) is a (pseudo)metrizable space.

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.Real
nodes.description: This file currently only contains results on ENNReal but is named Real.lean to make it clear we can accept more (E)(NN)Real results.

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.Uniformity
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a uniform space with countably generated uniformity filter is pseudometrizable: there exists a PseudoMetricSpace structure that generates the same uniformity. The proof follows Sergey Melikhov, Metrizable uniform spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Metrizable.Urysohn
nodes.description: In this file we prove Urysohn's Metrization Theorem: a T₃ topological space with second countable topology X is metrizable.

nodes.label: Topology.NatEmbedding
nodes.description: In this file we prove several properties of infinite Hausdorff topological spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Neighborhoods
nodes.description: Each point x of X gets a neighborhood filter 𝓝 x.

nodes.label: Topology.NhdsKer
nodes.description: In Mathlib/Topology/Defs/Filter.lean, nhdsKer s is defined to be the intersection of all neighborhoods of s. Note that this construction has no standard name in the literature.

nodes.label: Topology.NhdsSet
nodes.description: In this file we define the filter 𝓝ˢ s or nhdsSet s consisting of all neighborhoods of a set s.

nodes.label: Topology.NhdsWithin
nodes.description: This file develops API on the relative versions nhdsWithin and nhdsSetWithin of nhds and nhdsSet, which are defined in previous definition files.

nodes.label: Topology.OpenPartialHomeomorph.Defs
nodes.description: This file defines homeomorphisms between open subsets of topological spaces. An element e of OpenPartialHomeomorph X Y is an extension of PartialEquiv X Y, i.e., it is a pair of functions e.toFun and e.invFun, inverse of each other on the sets e.source and e.target. Additionally, we require that these sets are open, and that the functions are continuous on them. Equivalently, they are homeomorphisms there.

nodes.label: Topology.Order
nodes.description: Topologies on a fixed type α are ordered, by reverse inclusion. That is, for topologies t₁ and t₂ on α, we write t₁ ≤ t₂ if every set open in t₂ is also open in t₁. (One also calls t₁ finer than t₂, and t₂ coarser than t₁.)

nodes.label: Topology.Order.AtTopBotIxx
nodes.descriptionTitle: Filter.atTop and Filter.atBot for intervals in a linear order topology
nodes.description: Let X be a linear order with order topology. Let a be a point that is either the bottom element of X or is not isolated on the left, see Order.IsSuccPrelimit. Then the Filter.atTop filter on Set.Iio a and 𝓝[<] a are related by the coercion map via pushforward and pullback, see map_coe_Iio_atTop and comap_coe_Iio_nhdsLT.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Basic
nodes.descriptionTitle: Theory of topology on ordered spaces
nodes.description: The order topology on an ordered space is the topology generated by all open intervals (or equivalently by those of the form (-∞, a) and (b, +∞)). We define it as Preorder.topology α. However, we do not register it as an instance (as many existing ordered types already have topologies, which would be equal but not definitionally equal to Preorder.topology α).

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Bornology
nodes.description: This file relates the notion of bornology-boundedness (sets that lie in a bornology) to the notion of order-boundedness (sets that are bounded above and below).

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Category.AlexDisc
nodes.description: This defines AlexDisc, the category of Alexandrov-discrete topological spaces with continuous maps, and proves it's equivalent to the category of preorders.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Category.FrameAdjunction
nodes.descriptionTitle: Adjunction between Locales and Topological Spaces
nodes.description: This file defines the point functor from the category of locales to topological spaces and proves that it is right adjoint to the forgetful functor from topological spaces to locales.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Compact
nodes.description: In this file we prove that a closed interval in a conditionally complete linear ordered type with order topology (or a product of such types) is compact.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.CountableSeparating
nodes.descriptionTitle: Countably many infinite intervals separate points
nodes.description: In this file we prove that in a linear order with second countable order topology, the points can be separated by countably many infinite intervals. We prove 4 versions of this statement (one for each of the infinite intervals), as well as provide convenience corollaries about Filter.EventuallyEq.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.DenselyOrdered
nodes.descriptionTitle: Order topology on a densely ordered set

nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about extendFrom in an order topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.ExtrClosure
nodes.descriptionTitle: Maximum/minimum on the closure of a set
nodes.description: In this file we prove several versions of the following statement: if f : X → Y has a (local or not) maximum (or minimum) on a set s at a point a and is continuous on the closure of s, then f has an extremum of the same type on Closure s at a.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Filter
nodes.descriptionTitle: Topology on filters of a space with order topology
nodes.description: In this file we prove that 𝓝 (f x) tends to 𝓝 Filter.atTop provided that f tends to Filter.atTop, and similarly for Filter.atBot.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Hom.Basic
nodes.description: This file defines continuous order homomorphisms, that is maps which are both continuous and monotone. They are also called Priestley homomorphisms because they are the morphisms of the category of Priestley spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Hom.Esakia
nodes.description: This file defines pseudo-epimorphisms and Esakia morphisms.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.HullKernel
nodes.description: Let α be a CompleteLattice and let T be a subset of α. The pair of maps S → sInf (Subtype.val '' S) and a → T ↓∩ Ici a are often referred to as the kernel and the hull respectively. They form an antitone Galois connection between the subsets of T and α. When α can be generated from T by taking infs, this becomes a Galois insertion and the relative topology (Topology.lower) on T takes on a particularly simple form: the relative-open sets are exactly the sets of the form (hull T a)ᶜ for some a in α.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.IntermediateValue
nodes.description: In this file we prove the Intermediate Value Theorem: if f : α → β is a function defined on a connected set s that takes both values ≤ a and values ≥ a on s, then it is equal to a at some point of s. We also prove that intervals in a dense conditionally complete order are preconnected and any preconnected set is an interval. Then we specialize IVT to functions continuous on intervals.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.IsLUB
nodes.descriptionTitle: Properties of LUB and GLB in an order topology

nodes.label: Topology.Order.IsLocallyClosed
nodes.description: We prove that the intervals on a topological ordered space are locally closed.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.IsNormal
nodes.descriptionTitle: A normal function is strictly monotone and continuous
nodes.description: We defined the predicate Order.IsNormal in terms of IsLUB, which avoids having to import topology in order theory files. This file shows that the predicate is equivalent to the definition in the literature, being that of a strictly monotonic function, continuous in the order topology.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Lattice
nodes.description: In this file we define mixin classes ContinuousInf and ContinuousSup. We define the class TopologicalLattice as a topological space and lattice L extending ContinuousInf and ContinuousSup.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LawsonTopology
nodes.description: This file introduces the Lawson topology on a preorder.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LeftRightLim
nodes.description: We define the (strict) left and right limits of a function.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LeftRightNhds
nodes.descriptionTitle: Neighborhoods to the left and to the right on an OrderTopology
nodes.description: We've seen some properties of left and right neighborhood of a point in an OrderClosedTopology. In an OrderTopology, such neighborhoods can be characterized as the sets containing suitable intervals to the right or to the left of a. We give now these characterizations.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LiminfLimsup
nodes.descriptionTitle: Lemmas about liminf and limsup in an order topology.
nodes.description: The same lemmas are true in ℝ, ℝ × ℝ, ι → ℝ, EuclideanSpace ι ℝ. To avoid code duplication, we provide an ad hoc axiomatisation of the properties we need.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LocalExtr
nodes.descriptionTitle: Local extrema of functions on topological spaces
nodes.description: This file defines special versions of IsFilter f a l, =Min/Max/Extr, from Mathlib/Order/Filter/Extr.lean for two kinds of filters: nhdsWithin and nhds. These versions are called IsLocalOn and IsLocal, respectively.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.LowerUpperTopology
nodes.description: This file introduces the lower topology on a preorder as the topology generated by the complements of the left-closed right-infinite intervals.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Monotone
nodes.descriptionTitle: Monotone functions on an order topology
nodes.description: This file contains lemmas about limits and continuity for monotone / antitone functions on linearly-ordered sets (with the order topology). For example, we prove that a monotone function has left and right limits at any point (Monotone.tendsto_nhdsLT, Monotone.tendsto_nhdsGT).

nodes.label: Topology.Order.MonotoneContinuity
nodes.description: In this file we prove the following fact: if f is a monotone function on a neighborhood of a and the image of this neighborhood is a neighborhood of f a, then f is continuous at a, see continuousWithinAt_of_monotoneOn_of_image_mem_nhds, as well as several similar facts.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.MonotoneConvergence
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few theorems of the form “if the range of a monotone function f : ι → α admits a least upper bound a, then f x tends to a as x → ∞”, as well as version of this statement for (conditionally) complete lattices that use ⨆ x, f x instead of IsLUB.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.NhdsSet

nodes.label: Topology.Order.PartialSups

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Priestley
nodes.description: This file defines Priestley spaces. A Priestley space is an ordered compact topological space such that any two distinct points can be separated by a clopen upper set.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.ProjIcc

nodes.label: Topology.Order.Rolle

nodes.label: Topology.Order.ScottTopology

nodes.description: In this file we prove that a linear order with order topology is a completely normal Hausdorff topological space.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.UpperLowerSetTopology
nodes.description: This file introduces the upper set topology on a preorder as the topology where the open sets are the upper sets and the lower set topology on a preorder as the topology where the open sets are the lower sets.

nodes.label: Topology.Order.WithTop
nodes.description: When ι is a topological space with the order topology, we also endow WithTop ι with the order topology. If ι is second countable, we prove that WithTop ι also is.

nodes.label: Topology.Partial
nodes.description: In this file we prove properties of Filter.PTendsto etc. in topological spaces. We also introduce PContinuous, a version of Continuous for partially defined functions.

nodes.label: Topology.Perfect

nodes.label: Topology.QuasiSeparated
nodes.description: A topological space is quasi-separated if the intersections of any pairs of compact open subsets are still compact. Notable examples include spectral spaces, Noetherian spaces, and Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Sets.VietorisTopology
nodes.description: This file defines the Vietoris topology on the types of compact subsets and nonempty compact subsets of a topological space. The Vietoris topology is generated by sets of the form $\{K \mid K \subseteq U\}$ and $\{K \mid K \cap U \ne \emptyset\}$, where $U$ is an open subset of the underlying space.

nodes.label: Topology.Sheaves.Skyscraper
nodes.description: A skyscraper (pre)sheaf 𝓕 : (Pre)Sheaf C X is the (pre)sheaf with value A at point p₀ that is supported only at open sets contain p₀, i.e. 𝓕(U) = A if p₀ ∈ U and 𝓕(U) = if p₀ ∉ U where is a terminal object of C. In terms of stalks, 𝓕 is supported at all specializations of p₀, i.e. if p₀ ⤳ x then 𝓕ₓ ≅ A and if ¬ p₀ ⤳ x then 𝓕ₓ ≅ .

nodes.label: Topology.Sheaves.Stalks
nodes.description: For a presheaf F on a topological space X, valued in some category C, the stalk of F at the point x : X is defined as the colimit of the composition of the inclusion of categories (OpenNhds x)ᵒᵖ ⥤ (Opens X)ᵒᵖ and the functor F : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C. For an open neighborhood U of x, we define the map F.germ x : F.obj (op U) ⟶ F.stalk x as the canonical morphism into this colimit.

nodes.label: Topology.ShrinkingLemma
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few versions of the shrinking lemma. The lemma says that in a normal topological space a point finite open covering can be “shrunk”: for a point finite open covering u : ι → Set X there exists a refinement v : ι → Set X such that closure (v i) ⊆ u i.

nodes.label: Topology.Sion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Formalization of Sion's version of the von Neumann minimax theorem
nodes.description: Sion.exists_isSaddlePointOn : Let X and Y be convex subsets of topological vector spaces E and F, X being moreover compact, and let f : X × Y → ℝ be a function such that Then ⊓ x, ⊔ y, f (x, y) = ⊔ y, ⊓ x f (x, y).

nodes.label: Topology.SmallInductiveDimension
nodes.description: The small inductive dimension of a space is inductively defined as follows. Empty spaces have small inductive dimension less than 0, and a topological space has dimension less than n + 1 if it has a topological basis whose elements have frontiers of dimension strictly less n.

nodes.label: Topology.Sober
nodes.description: A quasi-sober space is a topological space where every irreducible closed subset has a generic point. A sober space is a quasi-sober space where every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. This is if and only if the space is T0, and thus sober spaces can be stated via [QuasiSober α] [T0Space α].

nodes.label: Topology.Specialization

nodes.label: Topology.Spectral.Basic
nodes.description: A topological space is spectral if it is T0, compact, sober, quasi-separated, and its compact open subsets form an open basis. Prime spectra of commutative semirings are spectral spaces.

nodes.label: Topology.Spectral.ConstructibleTopology
nodes.description: In this file we define the constructible topology on a topological space. This is the topology generated by compact open subsets and their complements.

nodes.label: Topology.Spectral.Hom
nodes.description: This file defines spectral maps. A map is spectral when it's continuous and the preimage of a compact open set is compact open.

nodes.label: Topology.Spectral.Prespectral
nodes.description: In this file, we define prespectral spaces as spaces whose lattice of compact opens forms a basis.

nodes.label: Topology.Subpath
nodes.description: This file defines Path.subpath as a restriction of a path to a subinterval, reparameterized to have domain [0, 1] and possibly with a reverse of direction. It then defines Path.concat as a way to concatenate finite sequences of paths with compatible endpoints.

nodes.label: Topology.TietzeExtension
nodes.description: In this file we prove a few version of the Tietze extension theorem. The theorem says that a continuous function s → ℝ defined on a closed set in a normal topological space Y can be extended to a continuous function on the whole space. Moreover, if all values of the original function belong to some (finite or infinite, open or closed) interval, then the extension can be chosen so that it takes values in the same interval.

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.AbsoluteValue
nodes.descriptionTitle: Uniform structure induced by an absolute value
nodes.description: We build a uniform space structure on a commutative ring R equipped with an absolute value into a linear ordered field 𝕜. Of course in the case R is ℚ, ℝ or ℂ and 𝕜 = ℝ, we get the same thing as the metric space construction, and the general construction follows exactly the same path.

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.AbstractCompletion
nodes.descriptionTitle: Abstract theory of Hausdorff completions of uniform spaces
nodes.description: This file characterizes Hausdorff completions of a uniform space α as complete Hausdorff spaces equipped with a map from α which has dense image and induces the original uniform structure on α. Assuming these properties we "extend" uniformly continuous maps from α to complete Hausdorff spaces to the completions of α. This is the universal property expected from a completion. It is then used to extend uniformly continuous maps from α to α' to maps between completions of α and α'.

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.Ascoli

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.Completion
nodes.description: The goal is to construct a left-adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform spaces into all uniform spaces. Any uniform space α gets a completion Completion α and a morphism (i.e. uniformly continuous map) (↑) : α → Completion α which solves the universal mapping problem of factorizing morphisms from α to any complete Hausdorff uniform space β. It means any uniformly continuous f : α → β gives rise to a unique morphism Completion.extension f : Completion α → β such that f = Completion.extension f ∘ (↑).

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.Dini
nodes.description: This file proves Dini's theorem, which states that if F n is a monotone increasing sequence of continuous real-valued functions on a compact set s converging pointwise to a continuous function f, then F n converges uniformly to f.

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.DiscreteUniformity

nodes.label: Topology.UniformSpace.Equicontinuity
nodes.descriptionTitle: Equicontinuity of a family of functions
nodes.description: Let X be a topological space and α a UniformSpace. A family of functions F : ι → X → α is said to be equicontinuous at a point x₀ : X when, for any entourage U in α, there is a neighborhood V of x₀ such that, for all x ∈ V, and for all i, F i x is U-close to F i x₀. In other words, one has ∀ U ∈ 𝓤 α, ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 x₀, ∀ i, (F i x₀, F i x) ∈ U. For maps between metric spaces, this corresponds to ∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x, ∀ i, dist x₀ x < δ → dist (F i x₀) (F i x) < ε.

Under uniform convergence, many properties of the Fₙ pass to the limit, most notably continuity.
